name: Associate Degree in Arts Studies
description: Adelaide University's Associate Degree in Arts Studies is the two-year pathway exit award within the Bachelor of Arts, covering the same first two years of study and giving students a recognised qualification if they choose not to continue to the full degree, or a direct credit pathway back into it. The Bachelor of Arts at Adelaide University runs on a two-major structure: every student picks two of the 26 available majors, from long-standing options like English, History, and Politics to newer additions such as Digital Humanities and Criminology. Each major is built from eight courses across three years (two in first year, three in second, three in third), so switching or adding a major stays a genuine option rather than paperwork.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — 1 course from Major 1; 1 course from Major 2; SOCI1007 Professional Pathways and Destinations 1; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — 1 course from Major 1; 1 course from Major 2; University Common Core course 1; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — 1-2 courses from each major; University Common Core course 2 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — 1-2 courses from each major; SOCI2019 Professional Pathways and Destinations 2 (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 70.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.0, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Associate Degree in Building Studies
description: Adelaide University's Associate Degree in Building Studies is the two-year pathway exit award within the Bachelor of Construction Management, covering the same first two years of study and giving students a recognised qualification if they choose not to continue to the full degree, or a direct credit pathway back into it. Adelaide University's Bachelor of Construction Management is a three-year degree (144 units) covering the construction process end to end: low-rise and high-rise construction, structures, construction science and materials, economics and procurement, quantity surveying and cost estimating, contract administration, planning and safety, building codes, building services, and scheduling. Digital construction tools are taught from first year.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Structures (6 units); Construction Economics and Procurement (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Construction Science and Materials (6 units); Construction Communication and Digital Construction Fundamentals (6 units); Program electives; Common core courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — High-rise Construction (6 units); Construction Planning and Safety (6 units); Building Services (6 units); Quantity Surveying Fundamentals and Cost Estimating (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Construction Contract Administration (6 units); Infrastructure Construction (6 units); Program electives; Common core courses.
admission_requirements: Guaranteed entry ATAR 70 (or equivalent secondary qualification); no prerequisite subjects; IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Associate Degree in Business Studies

A three-year degree (144 units) at Adelaide University's city campus. The structure is a common core (ethics, data literacy, First Nations knowledges, responsible AI), a program core (accounting for decision makers, management and leadership, emerging technologies and business analytics, marketing principles), one 48-unit major, a work-integrated learning block, and electives.

name: Associate Degree in Creative Arts Studies
description: Adelaide University's Associate Degree in Creative Arts Studies is the two-year pathway exit award within the Bachelor of Creative Arts, covering the same first two years of study and giving students a recognised qualification if they choose not to continue to the full degree, or a direct credit pathway back into it. Adelaide University's Bachelor of Creative Arts is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide. Students choose two major areas across the creative industries and build a portfolio through collaborative projects with students from other creative disciplines. Core courses cover the contemporary arts and cultural sector and the business and entrepreneurial side of creative work. Graduates move into production, design, arts management and freelance creative practice.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Major; Second Major.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Major; Second Major; Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Major; Major; Second Major; Second Major.

name: Associate Degree in Cyber Security
description: Adelaide University's Associate Degree in Cyber Security is the two-year pathway exit award within the Bachelor of Cyber Security, covering the same first two years of study and giving students a recognised qualification if they choose not to continue to the full degree, or a direct credit pathway back into it. Adelaide University Bachelor of Cyber Security lets students build their own program from a range of cyber courses, from technical subjects such as malware and attack technologies to information assurance and risk management, rounded out with professional communication, business and teamwork courses and an ICT capstone project on a real-world security problem. Students use their first- and second-year electives to complete mathematics prerequisites suited to their background. The program is provisionally accredited by the Australian Computer Society at the level of cyber security professional; subject to full accreditation, graduates will be eligible for ACS membership and recognition under the Seoul Accord. Entry is competitive and international students must meet Adelaide academic and English requirements. Graduates work as security analysts, incident responders, ethical hackers, data privacy officers and IT risk managers. International tuition is about A$53,300 per year.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Structured Data (6 units); Human-Centred Design of Digital Innovations (6 units); Information Technology Systems (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — System Requirements (6 units); Security Foundations (6 units); Elective; Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Cyber Law, Policy and Privacy (6 units); Human, Organisational and Societal Aspects (6 units); Discipline courses; Elective.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Professional Communication and Teamwork (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Elective.
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 75 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Associate Degree in Data Analytics
description: Adelaide University's Associate Degree in Data Analytics is the two-year pathway exit award within the Bachelor of Information Technology: Data Analytics, covering the same first two years of study and giving students a recognised qualification if they choose not to continue to the full degree, or a direct credit pathway back into it. The data analytics specialisation of Adelaide University's Bachelor of Information Technology: a three-year degree (144 units) with a 66-unit IT core and a common first year that lets students change major, then a specialisation in turning data into decisions, covering data management, analysis, visualisation and the tools used across industry.

Year 1, Semester 2 — System Requirements (6 units); Security Foundations (6 units); Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Cloud Platforms (6 units); Unstructured Data (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses.

english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Associate Degree in Information Technology
description: Adelaide University's Associate Degree in Information Technology is the two-year pathway exit award within the Bachelor of Information Technology, covering the same first two years of study and giving students a recognised qualification if they choose not to continue to the full degree, or a direct credit pathway back into it. Adelaide University's Bachelor of Information Technology runs a 72-unit, three-year structure split cleanly into thirds: 27 core units, a 27-unit major, and 18 units of free electives. The major choice does most of the work differentiating graduates: Software Development, Networking and Cyber Security, and Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning are the most commonly taken.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Programming; IT Systems Fundamentals; Business Analysis (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Database Systems; Networking Fundamentals; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Systems Analysis and Design; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — IT Project Management; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).

name: Associate Degree in Legal Studies
description: Adelaide University's Associate Degree in Legal Studies is the two-year pathway exit award within the Bachelor of Laws, covering the same first two years of study and giving students a recognised qualification if they choose not to continue to the full degree, or a direct credit pathway back into it. Adelaide University's single Bachelor of Laws is a 96-unit, four-year AQF Level 7 degree: half core, half elective, but with real constraints on when students can take the elective half. No more than 9 units can be taken at Level I, and a minimum of 12 units is reserved for Level III, so students can't front-load easy electives early and coast.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Legal Method and Reasoning; Criminal Law; Torts; 1 broadening elective (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Contracts; Constitutional Law; 1 law elective; 1 broadening elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Property Law; Equity and Trusts; 2 law electives (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Administrative Law; Evidence; 2 law electives (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 90.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Associate Degree in Mathematical Studies
description: Adelaide University's Associate Degree in Mathematical Studies is the two-year pathway exit award within the Bachelor of Mathematics, covering the same first two years of study and giving students a recognised qualification if they choose not to continue to the full degree, or a direct credit pathway back into it. Adelaide University's Bachelor of Mathematics is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide covering the theory and technical skills of the mathematical sciences, including statistical modelling. Students work on real business problems in the university's Maths Clinic and on industry projects, and can add an honours year for research training. Graduates work as analysts, modellers and statisticians across finance, technology, health, environmental management and research.
curriculum:

Year 1, Semester 2 — Calculus 2 (6 units); Linear Algebra (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Communication and Research Skills in Mathematics (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Statistical Practice (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline electives Level 2; Common core.

name: Associate Degree in Media Studies
description: Adelaide University's Associate Degree in Media Studies is the two-year pathway exit award within the Bachelor of Media and Communication, covering the same first two years of study and giving students a recognised qualification if they choose not to continue to the full degree, or a direct credit pathway back into it. The Bachelor of Media and Communication at Adelaide University is a flexible three-year degree that teaches students to create impactful media and communications content for any career context. Students understand the issues, trends and technologies shaping how we interact, and learn to produce well-informed and targeted media and communication strategies for a range of organisations, audiences and platforms, using words, images and sound to tell powerful stories. Graduates work in public relations, social media, design, immersive media, film, gaming and entertainment, and communication roles across industries.

Year 1, Semester 2 — Media and Communication Professional Identities (6 units); Discipline courses.

name: Associate degree in Psychology Studies
description: Adelaide University's Associate degree in Psychology Studies is the two-year pathway exit award within the Bachelor of Psychology, covering the same first two years of study and giving students a recognised qualification if they choose not to continue to the full degree, or a direct credit pathway back into it. Adelaide University's Bachelor of Psychology builds on twelve core psychology courses common to every specialisation in the suite (Cognitive Neuroscience, Counselling and Interpersonal Skills, and the general stream), meaning students can defer choosing a specialisation without falling behind, since the differentiation mostly happens in fourth-year honours options.

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Sciences
description:
A three-year, 144-unit degree (102 core + 18 work-integrated learning + 24 elective units) taught across Waite, Adelaide City, and Roseworthy campuses, with February and July intakes. Combines crop and livestock science, soil and water management, agricultural genetics and biochemistry, agribusiness, and precision-agriculture technology (GPS, sensors, drones) rather than focusing narrowly on farm operation.

Includes at least 240 hours of industry placement across three dedicated work-integrated-learning courses. Waite Campus (about 7km from the Adelaide CBD, ~184 hectares) is a major agricultural research precinct with laboratories, greenhouses, orchards, and vineyards; Roseworthy Campus (about 50km north of Adelaide) focuses on dryland agriculture and animal production.

Adelaide University lists graduate career paths including agronomist, agricultural scientist, soil scientist, livestock scientist, horticultural manager, biosecurity officer, sustainability officer, and agribusiness roles.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — AGRI1002 Agricultural Systems; BIOL1004 Biology 1B: Evolution and Diversity of Organisms; CHEM1000 Foundations in Chemistry (or CHEM1002 Chemistry 1A); STAT1000 Data Skills for Scientists (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — AGRI1000 Agricultural Production; AGRI1003 Soils and Landscapes; BIOL1003 Biology 1A: Molecules, Genes and Cells; AGRI1910 Introduction to Professional Skills in Agriculture (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — AGRI2004 Soil and Water Resources; AGRI2006 Agricultural Biochemistry; AGRI2013 Microbiology and Invertebrate Biology; AGRI2011 Foundations in Plant Science (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — AGRI2005 Crop and Pasture Production; AGRI2910 Agricultural Science Work Experience; ANIM2006 Livestock Production 2; AGRI2017 Agricultural Genetics (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — AGRI3003 Agricultural Economics and Policy; AGRI3007 Agricultural Experimental Design and Analysis; 2 electives (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — AGRI3004 Professional Skills in Agricultural Science 3; AGRI2010 Agribusiness; 2 electives (24 units).
admission_requirements: Secondary education equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE); no formal prerequisite, but assumed knowledge of SACE Stage 2 Chemistry and Mathematical Methods (or equivalent) is expected. Country-specific academic benchmarks apply for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Architectural Design
description:
A three-year, 144-unit foundation degree (90 core + a 36-unit major/discipline stream + 18 elective units) at Adelaide City Campus, with February and July intakes. Covers design studio work, technical drawing and construction, digital modelling, sustainability, and architectural history/theory. No prerequisites or assumed knowledge required.

Adelaide University frames this as the first stage toward architectural registration rather than a standalone qualification: it feeds into the Master of Architecture, with a packaged Bachelor + Master of Architecture pathway offered at 5 years full-time; this bachelor's degree alone does not qualify a graduate as a registered architect. Students can also specialise via a major in Urban Planning, with a combined Bachelor of Architectural Design (Urban Planning) + Master of Urban and Regional Planning pathway at 4 years, or a Bachelor of Architectural Design + Master of Landscape Architecture pathway at 5 years.

Adelaide University lists graduate career paths including architect (with further study), landscape architect (with further study), architectural graduate, draftsperson, urban designer, environmental designer, architectural technician, and heritage consultant.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — ARCH1000 Design Studio (Principles); ARCH1002 Design Communication (Principles); ARCH1003 Design Construction (Principles); 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — ARCH1004 Architectural Design Studio (Home); ARCH1005 Architectural Design Cultures; ARCH1006 Environmental Design and the Sensory Body; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — ARCH2004 Architectural Design Studio (Urban Landscapes); ARCH2007 Digital Design Communications; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — ARCH2011 Architectural Design Studio (Communication); ARCH2000 Contemporary Architectural Theory; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — ARCH3001 Architectural Design Studio (Tectonics); ARCH3003 Multi-storey Technologies; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — ARCH3013 Architectural Design Studio (Context and Cultures); ARCH3014 Environmental Ecologies and Systems in Architecture; 1 elective (24 units).
admission_requirements: Secondary education equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE) or higher; no formal prerequisites and no assumed knowledge required.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
The Bachelor of Arts at Adelaide University runs on a two-major structure: every student picks two of the 26 available majors, from long-standing options like English, History, and Politics to newer additions such as Digital Humanities and Criminology. Each major is built from eight courses across three years (two in first year, three in second, three in third), so switching or adding a major stays a genuine option rather than paperwork.

Running alongside the majors is a University Common Core: three interdisciplinary courses spread across the degree rather than front-loaded, plus three Work Integrated Learning courses (Professional Pathways and Destinations 1 and 2, and a final-year Internship in Society and Culture) that push students into placements, portfolio work, or applied projects tied to their chosen field.

No two Arts degrees look quite the same in practice; a History/Politics combination reads very differently to a Creative Writing/Film Studies one, and the university markets that flexibility as the point rather than a limitation. Career paths span journalism, policy and government, publishing, and education, with a meaningful share of graduates going on to postgraduate study in law, teaching, or their chosen discipline.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — 1 course from Major 1; 1 course from Major 2; SOCI1007 Professional Pathways and Destinations 1; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — 1 course from Major 1; 1 course from Major 2; University Common Core course 1; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — 1-2 courses from each major; University Common Core course 2 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — 1-2 courses from each major; SOCI2019 Professional Pathways and Destinations 2 (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — 1-2 courses from each major; University Common Core course 3 (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — 1-2 courses from each major; SOCI3903 Internship: Society and Culture (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 70.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.0, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Bachelor of Aviation: Management
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Aviation (Management) is a three-year degree (144 units) at the Mawson Lakes campus, on the business and operational side of aviation rather than flying: airline finance and operations, airport administration, aviation safety, supply chain and logistics, and strategic planning. Students get about five hours of flying and five hours of observational flying for context but do not train for a licence.

The third year includes two aviation project courses applying the material to real problems. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits people who want a management career in airlines, airports or the wider aviation sector, in roles such as operations manager, fleet planner, safety manager or airport manager.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Human Performance and Limitations in Aviation (6 units); Aviation Law (6 units); Introduction to Aviation (6 units); Program electives.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Introduction to Aviation Management (6 units); Aviation Safety Fundamentals (6 units); Flight Training Theory 1 (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Humans in Aviation: People, Systems and Safety (6 units); Data Analytics (6 units); Foundations of Airline Finance (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Principles of Logistics and Supply Chain Management (6 units); Aviation Economics (6 units); Airline Operations Management (6 units); Project Management Fundamentals (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Program electives; Safety and Risk Management for Aviation Professionals (6 units); Airport Management (6 units); Common core.
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (or equivalent secondary qualification) (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Aviation: Pilot
description:
A three-year degree (144 units) that shares its first year with the aviation management major before specialising. It combines aviation coursework with flight training delivered in partnership with Flight Training Adelaide, including single and multi-engine aircraft and A320 and 737 simulators.

Students can take a concurrent Graduate Diploma in Aviation that carries the Commercial Pilot Licence, command instrument rating and multi-engine class rating; the flight training is an additional cost on top of tuition and follows CASA's integrated-course timeline. Entry is an ATAR of about 70, and an aviation medical is required to fly. It suits students set on an airline or commercial flying career who want a degree alongside the licences.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Human Performance and Limitations in Aviation (6 units); Aviation Law (6 units); Introduction to Aviation (6 units); Program electives.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Introduction to Aviation Management (6 units); Aviation Safety Fundamentals (6 units); Flight Training Theory 1 (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Humans in Aviation: People, Systems and Safety (6 units); Commercial Pilot Theory (18 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Aviation Physics 1 (6 units); Advanced Pilot Theory (6 units); Program electives; Common core.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Data Analytics (6 units); Aviation Project 1 (6 units); Safety and Risk Management for Aviation Professionals (6 units); Large Aircraft Flight Operations (Part 1) (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Aviation Project 2 (6 units).
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 (Australian applicants); country-specific secondary-qualification equivalents for international applicants (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Biomedical and Health Sciences
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Biomedical and Health Sciences is a three-year science degree (144 units) about how the human body works in health and disease, with a choice of eight majors: biochemistry, clinical trials, genetics, medical science, microbiology and immunology, neuroscience, public health, or reproductive and childhood health, and the option of two majors.

Students use dedicated anatomy laboratories with real human specimens and complete a final-year work placement or research project. Entry is an ATAR of about 80 with no specific prerequisites. It prepares graduates for research and health-industry work and is a common foundation for postgraduate study, including graduate-entry medicine.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Health Research (6 units); Human Anatomy and Physiology A (6 units); Majors; Elective.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Common core; Majors; Elective.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Majors; Majors; Elective.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Common core; Majors; Elective; Elective.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Majors; Majors; Elective; Elective.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Common core; WIL in Biomedical and Health Sciences (6 units).
admission_requirements: ATAR 90 (competitive health-science entry) (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Biotechnology (Honours)
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Biotechnology (Honours) stay current with emerging trends in the biotech field with our Bachelor of Science (Honours) majoring in Biotechnology. Develop your foundational knowledge and technical skills while learning how to adapt to current and emerging trends. Stay current in a constantly evolving industry with a comprehensive and diverse educational experience. Combine traditional science with engineering and computer science to take discoveries from the lab to the market and broader community. Explore areas such as drug development, gene therapy and the identification of biomarkers for cancers. Expand your critical thinking skills and analytical approaches to problem-solving and evidence-based decision making. Our Honours year will allow you to explore biotechnology in greater depth, encouraging exploration across the field, and providing a pathway for entry into a research degree at either a master’s or doctoral (PhD) level. You’ll be supported by experts and researchers through your final year honours thesis. In the first two years of your degree, you’ll explore molecular, genetic animal and plant biology. You’ll learn how to produce food, drugs and other products, while discovering microbial technology and bioprocess engineering. You’ll investigate how to modify living things while also focusing on broadening your understanding of scientific process and advancements. Gain a competitive edge by studying an Honours year. Undertake 80+ hours of placement or project work alongside industry. Engage with experts and academics currently in the field. Expand your knowledge through new research techniques and skills.
curriculum: No fixed course sequence; students choose electives across areas including: Biology; Chemistry; Biochemistry; Microbiology; Principles of Biotechnology; Molecular and structural biology; Molecular basis of cancer; Molecular and biomedical science practical skills; Analytical Chemistry; Animal Behaviour; Animal Science; Biotechnology; Chemistry; Computational Physics; Ecology; Environmental Science; Environmental and Geospatial Science; Evolutionary Biology; Evolutionary Biology and Palaeontology; Experimental Physics; Food Science and Technology; Genetics; Geology; Geology and Earth Resources; Geology and Palaeontology; Geophysics; Marine and Wildlife Conservation; Medicinal and Biological Chemistry; Microbiology and Immunology; Nuclear Chemistry; Nuclear and Radiation Physics; Physics and Geophysics; Plant Biology; Pure and Applied Chemistry; Soil Science; Space Science and Astrophysics; Theoretical Physics.
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 85 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
A three-year degree (144 units) at Adelaide University's city campus. The structure is a common core (ethics, data literacy, First Nations knowledges, responsible AI), a program core (accounting for decision makers, management and leadership, emerging technologies and business analytics, marketing principles), one 48-unit major, a work-integrated learning block, and electives.

Students choose one major from 13 options, including Digital Business, International Business, Management, Marketing, Project Management, Human Resource Management, Real Estate, Sport Management, Procurement and Supply Chain Management, and Tourism, Events and Hospitality Management. The work-integrated learning courses provide internships, practicums, or industry projects as part of the degree rather than as an add-on.

english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Digital Business
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Business, digital business major, is a three-year degree (144 units). Alongside the shared business core it focuses on how organisations run and compete online: digital strategy, e-commerce, digital marketing, data-informed decision-making and the management of technology-driven change.

Work-integrated learning is built in, with February and July intakes at the city campus and an ATAR of about 70 for entry. It is less technical than an IT degree and suits students who want to lead digital projects and transformation from the business side, in roles such as digital coordinator, e-commerce officer or business analyst.
curriculum:

Year 1, Semester 2 — Marketing Principles (6 units); Major; Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Emerging Technologies, Data and Business Analytics (6 units); Negotiation, Conflict Management and Resolution (6 units); Major; Major.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Major; WIL/ Profession (6 units); Common core.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Strategic Management (6 units); Major; Major; Major.

english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Business: Human Resource Management
description:

name: Bachelor of Clinical Exercise Physiology (Honours)
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Clinical Exercise Physiology (Honours) is a four-year, 192 unit allied health degree with integrated honours, training clinical exercise physiologists who prescribe exercise for chronic disease, injury and rehabilitation. The structure is 150 core units, 30 work-integrated learning units and 12 electives, with more than 500 hours of clinical placement (about 140 in third year and 360 in fourth) across South Australian clinical facilities and the university's community clinics. Core study covers exercise physiology, biomechanics, motor control, nutrition, pain management and chronic disease assessment, using equipment such as metabolic carts and ECG. The degree is accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia, so graduates are eligible for accreditation as Accredited Exercise Physiologists and Exercise Scientists. Entry requires IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. It suits students committed to a registered allied health career in exercise-based treatment.

Year 1, Semester 1 — Physiology Essentials 100 (6 units); Human Anatomy 100 (6 units); Aboriginal Health: Culture, Community and Country (6 units); Physical Activity and Health (6 units).

Year 2, Semester 1 — Motor Control and Learning (6 units); Exercise Physiology 1 (6 units); Human Nutrition (6 units); Exercise Prescription and Delivery 1 (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Biomechanics of Human Movement (6 units); Exercise Physiology 2 (6 units); Health, Exercise and Sport Psychology (6 units); Exercise Prescription and Delivery 2 (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Practice Education in Exercise Delivery (6 units); Pain Mechanisms and Management (6 units); Clinical Exercise Honours Project Design (6 units); Elective.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Advanced Exercise Assessment and Reasoning (6 units); Clinical Basis of Chronic Disease Management (6 units).

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description: Adelaide University Bachelor of Commerce is a three-year degree that builds foundational knowledge in accounting, finance, economics and commercial law before students focus through a major or double major. Majors include Accounting, Banking and Finance, Financial Planning, Property, and Business Analytics, the last covering industry-standard analytical tools, artificial intelligence and interpreting complex data for business decisions. The degree is built toward professional accreditation: an accounting major meets the entry requirements of CPA Australia and CA ANZ, the finance major aligns with the CFA Institute, and the marketing major is accredited by the Australian Marketing Institute. Entry requires a completed secondary qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education, a Certificate IV or higher from a registered training organisation, or at least six months of full-time higher education study. International tuition is about A$52,200 per year.

name: Bachelor of Commerce: Accounting
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Commerce (Accounting major) sits within the standard 144-unit, three-year commerce structure: a common core shared across all commerce degrees, an accounting major built from financial and management accounting, auditing, and taxation law courses, plus electives students can use to add a second major or take free-standing units in business, management, or a language. February and July intakes, delivered mainly at Adelaide City Campus with occasional online options.

The accounting major is built to satisfy the accreditation requirements of both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, a distinction not every accounting degree in the state carries, and one that matters for graduates aiming at Big Four or mid-tier firm graduate programs. Coursework goes beyond bookkeeping mechanics into the professional judgement calls accountants actually make: revenue recognition disputes, audit independence questions, and the ethical grey areas around tax minimisation.

Career paths the university lists include auditor, tax accountant, management accountant, financial analyst, and forensic accountant. Many students pair the major with Finance or Business Analytics for a double major rather than taking accounting alone.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — ACCTING 1006 Financial Accounting; COMMERC 1004 Data Analysis for Business; ECON 1002 Introductory Microeconomics; COMMERC 1006 Business, Society and the Planet (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — ACCTING 1007 Management Accounting; COMMERC 1005 Marketing Principles; ECON 1004 Introductory Macroeconomics; COMMLAW 1004 Business Law (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — ACCTING 2005 Financial Accounting and Reporting; ACCTING 2008 Cost Management; COMMLAW 2101 Corporations Law; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — ACCTING 2006 Accounting Information Systems; ACCTING 3014 Auditing and Assurance Services; TAXATION 2000 Taxation Law; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — ACCTING 3007 Advanced Financial Accounting; ACCTING 3009 Contemporary Issues in Accounting; 2 electives (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — ACCTING 3010 Strategic Management Accounting; COMMERC 3005 Business Capstone; 2 electives (24 units).
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 80.

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description:
At 72 units across three years, Adelaide University's Bachelor of Computer Science front-loads breadth: first year covers programming fundamentals, IT systems, structured data, and security foundations, before requiring a major from second year on: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Distributed Systems and Networking, or Programming Languages, among others.

Unlike some computing degrees that treat security as a bolt-on elective, security foundations sit in first year here, reflecting a program design that assumes cybersecurity literacy is baseline rather than a later specialisation. The AI major benefits from Adelaide's strength in machine learning research, and feeds directly into the university's Master of Computer Science for students who want to continue rather than enter the workforce at three years.

Like its postgraduate counterpart, the degree carries provisional accreditation from the Australian Computer Society at the Professional level and is recognised under the Seoul Accord. Career paths listed include software engineer, systems analyst, data engineer, and cybersecurity analyst, with February and July intakes.

Year 1, Semester 1 — Programming; Introduction to Computer Systems; Discrete Mathematics; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Object-Oriented Programming; Security Foundations; Structured Data and Databases; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Algorithms and Data Structures; Software Engineering; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Operating Systems; Requirements and User Experience; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — 2 major courses; 2 electives (24 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Capstone Project; 1 major course; 1 elective (24 units).

name: Bachelor of Computer Science (Honours)
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Computer Science (Honours) is a four-year degree (the honours is built in, not a separate year) with a fourth-year thesis run across three courses, where students define a research topic and work with academic staff. First year covers programming, structured data, object-oriented programming, mathematics, and security; later years add theory of computation, operating systems, algorithms, distributed computing, and language models.

Students take one major from Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Human-Centred Computing, or Programming Languages, and complete 12 to 24 units of work-integrated learning through an intensive computing project or ICT internships. The degree is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society and recognised internationally through the Seoul Accord. Part-time study is not available to international students.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Structured Data (6 units); Human-Centred Design of Digital Innovations (6 units); Information Technology Systems (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Object-Oriented Programming (6 units); System Requirements (6 units); Security Foundations (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Ethical and Legal Challenges in Technology (6 units); Discrete Mathematics (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Language Models, Translation and Execution (6 units); Operating Systems (6 units); Data Structures and Algorithms (6 units); Professional Communication and Teamwork (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Theory of Computation and Formal Verification (6 units); Grand Challenges (6 units); Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms (6 units); Cyber Security Application (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — ICT Internship 1 (6 units); ICT Internship 4 (24 units).
admission_requirements: Guaranteed entry ATAR 75 (or equivalent secondary qualification); no assumed knowledge or prerequisite subjects; IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Computer Science: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
description:
The artificial intelligence and machine learning major of Adelaide University's Bachelor of Computer Science: a three-year degree (144 units) with a 66-unit computing core in programming, data structures, security and mathematics, then a 54-unit major concentrating on machine learning algorithms, data analytics and the systems that put models into production, finishing with a team capstone project for a real client.

The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society and recognised internationally through the Seoul Accord. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students who want to build AI systems rather than just use them, heading into machine learning engineering, data science or research roles across defence, health, finance and agriculture.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Structured Data (6 units); Information Technology Systems (6 units); Human-Centred Design of Digital Innovations (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Object-Oriented Programming (6 units); Security Foundations (6 units); System Requirements (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Discrete Mathematics (6 units); Ethical and Legal Challenges in Technology (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Language Models, Translation and Execution (6 units); Data Structures and Algorithms (6 units); Operating Systems (6 units); Professional Communication and Teamwork (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms (6 units); Cyber Security Application (6 units); Theory of Computation and Formal Verification (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — ICT Capstone Project 1 (6 units); ICT Capstone Project 2 (6 units).
admission_requirements: Guaranteed entry ATAR 75 (or equivalent secondary qualification); no assumed knowledge or prerequisite subjects; IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Computer Science: Human-Centred Computing
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Computer Science, human-centred computing major, is a three-year degree (144 units). It keeps the full computing core, programming, data structures, security and mathematics, and directs the 54-unit major toward how people actually use software: interaction design, user experience, usability testing and accessible interfaces, ending in a team capstone project for an external client.

The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society and recognised under the Seoul Accord. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students who want to stay technical but work at the boundary between engineering and design, moving into UX engineering, product roles or front-end and interaction development.

Year 1, Semester 1 — Structured Data (6 units); Information Technology Systems (6 units); Human-Centred Design of Digital Innovations (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Object-Oriented Programming (6 units); Security Foundations (6 units); System Requirements (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Discrete Mathematics (6 units); Ethical and Legal Challenges in Technology (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Language Models, Translation and Execution (6 units); Data Structures and Algorithms (6 units); Operating Systems (6 units); Professional Communication and Teamwork (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Advanced Data Structures and Algorithms (6 units); Cyber Security Application (6 units); Theory of Computation and Formal Verification (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — ICT Capstone Project 1 (6 units); ICT Capstone Project 2 (6 units).

name: Bachelor of Computer Science: Programming Languages
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Computer Science, programming languages major, is a three-year degree (144 units). On top of the shared computing core it focuses the 54-unit major on the design, semantics and implementation of programming languages, compilers and translators, and the theory that underpins reliable software, finishing with a client capstone project.

The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society and recognised under the Seoul Accord. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It is the most theoretical of the three computer science majors and suits students drawn to compilers, language design, formal methods and systems programming, or planning postgraduate research.

name: Bachelor of Construction Management
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Construction Management is a three-year degree (144 units) covering the construction process end to end: low-rise and high-rise construction, structures, construction science and materials, economics and procurement, quantity surveying and cost estimating, contract administration, planning and safety, building codes, building services, and scheduling. Digital construction tools are taught from first year.

Work-integrated learning is one mandatory professional practice course. On accreditation: as of 2026 the Australian Institute of Building Surveyors has accredited years 1 and 2 at Level 2, with year 3 accreditation being pursued, and the page does not list quantity surveying accreditation, so applicants who need a specific professional pathway should confirm the current status with the university.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Structures (6 units); Construction Economics and Procurement (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Construction Science and Materials (6 units); Construction Communication and Digital Construction Fundamentals (6 units); Program electives; Common core courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — High-rise Construction (6 units); Construction Planning and Safety (6 units); Building Services (6 units); Quantity Surveying Fundamentals and Cost Estimating (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Construction Contract Administration (6 units); Infrastructure Construction (6 units); Program electives; Common core courses.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Development Regulations and Building Codes (6 units); Risk, Quality and People Management (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Commercial Management (6 units); Construction Management Research Methods (6 units); Construction Management Professional Practice (6 units).
admission_requirements: Guaranteed entry ATAR 70 (or equivalent secondary qualification); no prerequisite subjects; IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Creative Arts
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Creative Arts is a three-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide. Students choose two major areas across the creative industries and build a portfolio through collaborative projects with students from other creative disciplines. Core courses cover the contemporary arts and cultural sector and the business and entrepreneurial side of creative work. Graduates move into production, design, arts management and freelance creative practice.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Major; Second Major.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Major; Second Major; Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Major; Major; Second Major; Second Major.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Creative Solutions: Reimagining Projects (6 units); Major; Second Major; Common core.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Major; Major; Second Major; Second Major.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Major; Second Major; Common core.
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 70 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Criminology (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Criminology (Honours) at Adelaide University builds on the Bachelor of Criminology, in which students learn how crime is shaped by social, psychological and economic factors and how criminologists collect and analyse data to understand where, when and why crimes occur and develop crime prevention strategies. The honours year adds advanced coursework and an independent research project. Graduates work in crime analysis and research, policy development, community advocacy, crime prevention, corrections and youth justice, and are prepared for a research higher degree.

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
description: The Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice at Adelaide University is a three-year degree that prepares students to contribute to debate on criminal behaviour and societal responses to it. Students explore the complex causes and nature of crime and its impact on communities, learning how crime is shaped by social, psychological and economic factors, how criminologists collect and analyse data to understand where and why crimes occur, and how to develop crime prevention strategies. Graduates work in crime analysis and research, policy development, community advocacy, crime prevention, corrections, victim support and youth justice.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Crime Problems in Australia (6 units); Introduction to Criminal Justice (6 units); Common core.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Fundamentals of Social Research (6 units); Explaining Crime and Deviance (6 units); Majors; Majors.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Majors; Policing and Crime Control (6 units); Professional Pathways and Destinations 2 (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Penology and Corrections (6 units); Majors; Majors.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Majors; Criminology and Criminal Justice Internship (6 units); Contemporary Issues in Criminology (6 units); Common core.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Criminal Law and Criminal Process (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 75 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Cyber Security
description: Adelaide University Bachelor of Cyber Security lets students build their own program from a range of cyber courses, from technical subjects such as malware and attack technologies to information assurance and risk management, rounded out with professional communication, business and teamwork courses and an ICT capstone project on a real-world security problem. Students use their first- and second-year electives to complete mathematics prerequisites suited to their background. The program is provisionally accredited by the Australian Computer Society at the level of cyber security professional; subject to full accreditation, graduates will be eligible for ACS membership and recognition under the Seoul Accord. Entry is competitive and international students must meet Adelaide academic and English requirements. Graduates work as security analysts, incident responders, ethical hackers, data privacy officers and IT risk managers. International tuition is about A$53,300 per year.
curriculum:

Year 1, Semester 2 — System Requirements (6 units); Security Foundations (6 units); Elective; Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Cyber Law, Policy and Privacy (6 units); Human, Organisational and Societal Aspects (6 units); Discipline courses; Elective.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Professional Communication and Teamwork (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Elective.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Security Operations and Incident Response (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Business for IT Professionals (6 units); Discipline courses; ICT Capstone Project 1 (6 units); ICT Capstone Project 2 (6 units).
admission_requirements: Completion of a secondary education qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education (SACE), with a minimum ATAR of approximately 75 (or equivalent via VET Certificate IV+ or prior higher education study).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Dental Surgery
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Dental Surgery is a five-year undergraduate degree in Adelaide with a preventive, patient-centred approach to oral health care. It integrates biological and medical science with clinical training, and students undertake compulsory placements from first year across hospital, community, rural and interstate clinics. Graduates are prepared to register and practise as dentists.

Year 1, Semester 1 — Dental Science and Practice I Part 1.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Dental Science and Practice I Part 2 (48 units); First Annual B.D.S. Examination.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Dental Science and Practice II Part 1.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Dental Science and Practice II Part 2 (48 units); Second Annual B.D.S. Examination.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Dental Science and Practice III Part 1.
Year 3, Semester 2 — Dental Science and Practice III Part 2 (48 units); Third Annual B.D.S. Examination.
Year 4, Semester 1 — Dental Science and Practice IV Part 1.
Year 4, Semester 2 — Dental Science and Practice IV Part 2 (48 units); Fourth Annual B.D.S. Examination.
Year 5, Semester 1 — Dental Science and Practice V Part 1.

name: Bachelor of Economics
description: Adelaide University Bachelor of Economics is a three-year degree of 72 units, half compulsory courses in economic principles, applied economics and econometrics and half optional. First year covers economic principles, data analytics and mathematical economics; second year adds applied econometrics, microeconomics, macroeconomics and global economic history; and in third year students run their own economic policy investigation. Common core courses include data, ethics, artificial intelligence, entrepreneurship and design thinking. Students can major in Financial Economics, Public Policy, International Economic Development or Advanced Analysis. Entry requires a completed secondary qualification equivalent to the South Australian Certificate of Education, a Certificate IV or higher, or at least six months of full-time higher education study. Graduates work as economists, economic researchers, policy and trade advisers, bankers and business data analysts across banks, government, consultancies and international organisations. International tuition is about A$52,200 per year.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) (Honours)
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) (Honours) is a four-year AQF Level 8 degree built around a common first two years of mathematics, mechanics, and design fundamentals shared with other engineering streams, before students specialise into civil-specific coursework in structures, geotechnics, water engineering, and transportation.

From third year, students choose a major (Construction Management, Environmental Engineering, Renewable Energy, or Structures and Infrastructure) or add a minor in Defence Systems, Entrepreneurship, or Humanitarian Engineering, so the same base degree can point toward quite different careers: site engineer on a construction crew, dam safety analyst, or renewables project developer.

Fourth year centres on an honours research project run more like a live consulting engagement than a purely theoretical thesis. A real client, either an industry partner or an academic researcher, sets the brief, and students work through feasibility, concept design, and detailed design stages. Adelaide University lists graduate destinations including structural engineer, geotechnical engineer, water resources engineer, transport engineer, and construction manager, and the degree is accredited by Engineers Australia to Washington Accord standard for professional registration.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — ENG 1001 Engineering Mechanics; MATHS 1011 Mathematics IA; CIVIL 1002 Introduction to Civil Engineering; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — ENG 1003 Engineering Modelling and Problem Solving; MATHS 1012 Mathematics IB; CIVIL 1004 Statics and Dynamics; 1 common core course (24 units).
Year 2 — CIVIL 2001 Structural Analysis; CIVIL 2002 Fluid Mechanics; CIVIL 2003 Geomechanics; CIVIL 2004 Construction Materials; CIVIL 2005 Surveying; MATHS 2107 Engineering Mathematics IIA; 1 elective.
Year 3 — CIVIL 3001 Structural Design; CIVIL 3002 Water Engineering; CIVIL 3003 Geotechnical Engineering; CIVIL 3004 Transport Engineering; CIVIL 3005 Construction Management; CIVIL 3006 Environmental Engineering; ENG 3004 Engineering Practice; ENG 3005 Project Management, plus major/minor electives.
Year 4 — CIVIL 4050 Honours Research Project (year-long, industry- or academic-supervised); ENG 4002A/ENG 4002B Engineering Practice Capstone; remaining major specialisation courses.
admission_requirements: SACE (or equivalent) completion with an ATAR of approximately 85, including Mathematical Methods and a recommended study of Physics.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Electrical) (Honours)
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Engineering (Electrical) (Honours) is a four-year, 192 unit electrical and electronic engineering degree in which honours is integrated throughout rather than added as a separate year. After a common engineering first year, students specialise in areas including circuit analysis, digital systems, electromagnetics, electrical machines, control systems and power systems, with electives in machine learning, RF engineering, robotics and renewable energy. The degree includes up to 12 weeks of industry placement and a major honours research project in the final year. It holds provisional professional engineer accreditation from Engineers Australia and is aligned with the Washington Accord for international recognition. Entry requires SACE Stage 2 Mathematical Methods or equivalent and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work across power and energy, telecommunications, electronics, automation and manufacturing. It suits students set on becoming a professional electrical engineer.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Engineering Programming (6 units); Electrical and Electronic Systems (6 units); Engineering Physics (6 units); Engineering Mathematics (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Engineering Design and Prototyping (6 units); Engineering Materials (6 units); Professional Engineering Practice (6 units); Engineering Modelling 1 (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Circuit Analysis (6 units); Digital Fundamentals (6 units); Signals and Systems (6 units); Engineering Modelling 2 (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Electronic Devices and Circuits (6 units); Electrical and Electronic Engineering Design (6 units); Engineering Project Management (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Control Systems (6 units); Electromagnetic Engineering (6 units); Systems Engineering and Professional Practice (6 units); Professional Engineer Career Preparation (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Electrical Machines (6 units); Digital Systems Design (6 units); Digital Signal Processing (6 units).
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Environmental) (Honours)
description: Adelaide University's Bachelor of Engineering (Environmental) (Honours) is a four-year, 192 unit engineering degree focused on environmental problems, combining engineering with chemistry, mathematics and environmental science to address water quality, waste, contamination and climate risk. Honours is integrated across the degree. Core subjects include water engineering, wastewater treatment, soil remediation, environmental systems and sustainability, and climate risk analysis, with electives in green infrastructure, hydrology and renewable energy systems, and stackable diploma and associate degree exit points. The program includes up to 12 weeks of industry placement and a major honours research and design project, and holds provisional professional engineer accreditation from Engineers Australia. Entry requires SACE Stage 2 Mathematical Methods or equivalent and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work in environmental consulting, water utilities, remediation, renewable energy and government. It suits students who want to apply engineering to environmental and sustainability challenges.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Engineering Programming (6 units); Professional Engineering Practice (6 units); Engineering Chemistry (6 units); Engineering Mathematics (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Construction Materials (6 units); Engineering Design and Prototyping (6 units); Engineering Modelling 1 (6 units); Environmental Systems and Sustainability (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Introduction to Water Engineering (6 units); Engineering Modelling 2 (6 units); Environmental Modelling and Management (6 units); Environmental Pollution and Monitoring (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Engineering Project Management (6 units); Environmental and Climate Risk Analysis (6 units); Integrated Natural Hazard Risk Management (6 units); Level 2 electives.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Systems Engineering and Professional Practice (6 units); Soil and Groundwater Remediation (6 units); Water Resources Planning and Management (6 units); Professional Engineer Career Preparation (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Water Treatment and Reuse Applications (6 units); Hydrology and Flood Management (6 units).
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Mechanical) (Honours)
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Engineering (Mechanical) (Honours) is a four-year degree (132 core units) with honours built in. Core courses cover solid mechanics, dynamics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, acoustics and vibrations, control systems, manufacturing processes, and computer-aided design, and year four is a major industry research project.

Students complete up to 450 hours of supervised industry work experience through professional practice courses and internships of up to 12 weeks. The degree is provisionally accredited at Professional Engineer level by Engineers Australia, which on full accreditation gives Washington Accord international recognition. Entry requires IELTS 6.5 and a Stage 2 mathematical methods prerequisite. Indicative international fee is around A$57,100 per year.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Engineering Design and Prototyping (6 units); Engineering Materials (6 units); Introduction to Engineering Mechanics (6 units); Engineering Mathematics (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Engineering Programming (6 units); Electrical and Electronic Systems (6 units); Engineering Modelling 1 (6 units); Professional Engineering Practice (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Engineering Project Management (6 units); Mechanics of Materials (6 units); Mechanical Engineering Practice and Design Project (6 units); Mechatronics Foundations (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Engineering Modelling 2 (6 units); Dynamics (6 units); Fluid Mechanics (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Acoustics and Vibrations (6 units); Thermodynamics (6 units); Common core; Professional Engineer Career Preparation (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 2 — Mechanical Systems and Design Project (6 units); Applied Control Systems (6 units).
admission_requirements: ATAR 80 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Environmental Policy and Management
Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science is a three-year degree accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia, so graduates are eligible to register as an Accredited Exercise Scientist. Students complete more than 140 hours of industry placement across sporting clubs, gyms, fitness centres and schools.

Facilities are a strength: exercise testing labs, a high-performance sport centre, exercise physiology clinics, an environmental chamber, and a sport science hub at the South Australian Sports Institute. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students heading into strength and conditioning, performance analysis or exercise science, and it is the standard first step toward postgraduate clinical exercise physiology.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Human Anatomy 100 (6 units); Foundations in Human Movement, Exercise and Sports Science (6 units); Physical Activity and Health (6 units); Physiology Essentials 100 (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Group and Team Leadership (6 units); Functional Anatomy (6 units); Introduction to Evidence Based Practice and Research in Health Sciences (6 units); Motor Development and Ageing (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Exercise Prescription and Delivery 1 (6 units); Exercise Physiology 1 (6 units); Motor Control and Learning (6 units); Human Nutrition (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Exercise Prescription and Delivery 2 (6 units); Exercise Physiology 2 (6 units); Health, Exercise and Sport Psychology (6 units); Biomechanics of Human Movement (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Professional Practice in Exercise Science (6 units); Exercise and Sport Science Project Design (6 units); Elective; Elective.
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Film and Television
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Film and Television is a three-year degree (144 units) covering the full production cycle from script to post, across screenwriting, cinematography, directing, editing, sound design and visual effects, with technical strands in digital compositing, 3D design and motion capture, plus film theory courses on world cinema, genre and documentary.

Facilities include a virtual production and TV studio, cinema cameras and industry-standard software, and students complete two work-integrated learning courses, an industry placement and a professional experience component, with partners such as Channel 44. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits people aiming at directing, cinematography, editing, screenwriting or content production.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Cinematic Design (6 units); Introduction to Film and Television (6 units); Introduction to 3D (6 units); Common core.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Screen Sound (6 units); Cinematography and Editing (6 units); Global Art Cinemas (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Digital Compositing (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Australian Film and Television (6 units); Screenwriting: Theory and Practice (6 units); Common core.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Experimental Production (6 units).
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Fine Arts
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Fine Arts is a three-year studio degree that starts broad, sampling painting, drawing, printmaking, photography, sculpture, ceramics, jewellery, glass, and time-based work in video, sound and performance, then narrows to chosen disciplines in years two and three.

Work-integrated learning runs through partnerships with the Samstag Museum, JamFactory and the Art Gallery of South Australia, and students build a portfolio and exhibit publicly. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits students who want to build a practice as a working artist, or move into curatorial, gallery, education or arts administration roles.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Materials and Processes for Fabrication (6 units); Foundation Studio: Ground (6 units); Everyday Materials Workshop (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Common core; Foundation Studio: Form (6 units); Everyday Technologies Workshop (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Expanded Studio: Field (12 units); Program electives - Art History and Visual Culture 1; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Art (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Expanded Studio: Exchange (12 units); Common core; Art and Critical Thinking (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Specialisation 3: Fine Arts (12 units); Fine Art Practice and Research (6 units); Common core.
admission_requirements: ATAR 65, or portfolio/interview for non-ATAR applicants (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Food and Nutrition Science (Honours)
Bachelor of Graphic Communication Design
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Graphic Communication Design is a three-year studio-based degree (144 units) taught across the city and Magill campuses, covering identity and branding, typography, interactive and digital design, UX design and packaging, with diploma and associate-degree exit points.

Much of the assessment is real client work, competitions and a final-year industry placement, so students graduate with a professional portfolio. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits students heading into graphic design, branding, web and UX design, or visual communication roles across advertising, tech and corporate settings.

Year 1, Semester 1 — Thinking By Design (6 units); Drawing for Art and Design (6 units); Design Perspectives (6 units); Digital Design Principles and Methods (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Graphic and Communication Design Studio 1 (6 units); Typography Studio 1 (6 units); Graphic and Communication Design Studio 2 (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Principles of UX Design (6 units); Graphic Communication Design Studio 3 (12 units); Typography Studio 2: Advanced Design for Reading (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Critical Design Issues (6 units); Graphic Communication Design Studio 4 (12 units); Common core.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Integrated Studio A (6 units); Graphic Communication Design Studio 5 (6 units); Design for Digital Interaction (6 units).

name: Bachelor of Health and Medical Science (Honours)
Bachelor of Health and Medical Sciences (Advanced)
Bachelor of Human Movement
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Human Movement is a three-year degree (144 units) built on anatomy, exercise physiology, biomechanics and motor control, paired with practical coaching and teaching skills and a human movement practicum.

Students choose one major: sport coaching, secondary health and physical education, or human nutrition, so the degree ranges from athlete development through to a pathway toward teaching health and PE. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits people aiming at coaching, sport development, physical education or community health and fitness roles, and it differs from the Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science, which is the ESSA-accredited exercise science pathway rather than a coaching and education one.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Common core; Physiology Essentials 100 (6 units); Physical Activity and Health (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Human Anatomy 100 (6 units); Motor Development and Ageing (6 units); Teaching and Coaching (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Active Lifestyles (6 units); Exercise Physiology 1 (6 units); Motor Control and Learning (6 units); Sport Practice (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Biomechanics of Human Movement (6 units); Exercise Physiology 2 (6 units); Common core.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Human Nutrition (6 units); Human Movement Practicum (6 units); Performance Analysis and Player Monitoring (6 units).

english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Human Nutrition
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Human Nutrition is a three-year science degree grounded in anatomy, physiology, chemistry and biochemistry, with applied courses in nutrition across the lifespan, sports nutrition, public health nutrition and food science, and up to 200 hours in an industry or research setting in the final year.

It is a nutrition science degree rather than a dietetics qualification: it does not by itself make graduates dietitians. Entry is an ATAR of about 75. It suits students interested in designing diet and lifestyle programs for individuals and communities, working as nutritionists, sports nutritionists, community health workers or food industry advisers, or continuing to a postgraduate dietetics degree.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Foundations in Chemistry (6 units); Human Anatomy and Physiology A (6 units); Introduction to Health Research (6 units); Aboriginal Health, Culture, Community, and Country (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Biology 1A: Molecules, Genes and Cells (6 units); Human Anatomy and Physiology B (6 units); Introduction to Nutrition (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Integrative Nutritional Physiology (6 units); Human Nutrition (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Biochemistry 2: Metabolism (6 units); Lifespan Nutrition Physiology (6 units); Culinary Nutrition (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Nutrition Assessment and Behaviour Change (6 units); Public Health and Community Nutrition (6 units).
admission_requirements: ATAR 75 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Illustration and Animation
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Illustration and Animation is a three-year studio degree covering drawing, traditional and digital illustration, 2D and 3D animation, stop-motion, motion capture and visual effects, along with character design and visual storytelling.

Students work in industry-standard studios with visual effects software and AR and VR tools, and build a professional portfolio through real project work. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. It suits people aiming at careers as animators, illustrators, concept artists or visual effects artists in film, games, publishing and advertising.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to 3D (6 units); Digital Design Principles and Methods (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Cinematic Design (6 units); Thinking By Design (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Character Performance (6 units).
Year 3, Semester 1 — Advanced Life Drawing (6 units); Illustration Studio 3 (6 units).
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 (secondary-qualification equivalents apply for international applicants)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Bachelor of Industrial Design
description:
Adelaide University's Bachelor of Industrial Design is a three-year studio-based degree (144 units) in designing physical products, systems and services, with an explicit emphasis on ethical, social and environmental responsibility alongside CAD, digital visualisation and materials.

Students work in purpose-built studios with CNC machines, 3D printers, laser cutters and VR and AR systems, and the third year includes a capstone design project and an industrial design practice course run with industry partners. Entry is an ATAR of about 70. Graduates work as industrial and product designers across consumer goods, furniture, packaging, assistive technology and related fields.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Digital Design Principles and Methods (6 units); Industrial Design Studio 1 - Foundation (12 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Industrial Design Studio 2 - Aesthetics and Meaning (6 units); Introduction to Industrial Design Visualisation (6 units); Common core.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Design Perspectives (6 units); Industrial Design Studio 3a - Human Centred Design (6 units); Industrial Design Studio 3B - Human Factors and Usability (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Industrial Design Studio 4a - Production and Structures (6 units); Industrial Design Studio 4b - Production and Sustainability (6 units); Common core.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Industrial Design Production Technology (6 units); Industrial Design Studio 5a - Systems (6 units).
