Year 1, Semester 2 — Ethics in the Counselling Workplace (6 units); Counselling Skills 2 (6 units); Nature of Grief (6 units); Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; AND; OR Undertake the Casper Situational Judgement Test (CSJT); AND; OR Attend an interview, if invited.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Master of Curatorial and Museum Studies
description: Adelaide University's Master of Curatorial and Museum Studies is a two-year degree in Adelaide delivered in partnership with cultural institutions including the South Australian Museum and the History Trust of South Australia. It challenges existing museum theory and practice, with a focus on ethical collection and exhibition development, First Nations truth-telling, and international cultural exchange. Graduates work as curators and museum professionals.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Making a museum (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
Year 1, Semester 2 — The Secret Life of Objects: Museums in Practice (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Museum Studies Minor Research Project (12 units); Program electives; Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Curatorial and Museum Studies Research Thesis (24 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Cyber Security
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) in Adelaide University's Master of Information Technology family, which share a common first four courses so students can switch specialisation early. It is open to graduates without an IT background, starting from foundational IT before moving into security principles, networking, governance risk and compliance, cloud security, security architecture, enterprise security, cyber law and critical infrastructure protection.

Three work-integrated learning courses, including an industry research project and two capstones, give applied experience. Entry needs a bachelor's degree with a GPA equivalent to 4.5 on Adelaide's 7-point scale. It suits people moving into roles such as cybersecurity analyst, security consultant, IT auditor or compliance specialist, in a market with a well-documented skills shortage.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Information Technology and Systems Concepts (6 units); Security Principles (6 units); Data in Information Technology Systems (6 units); Problem Solving and Programming Foundations (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Project Management for IT Professionals (6 units); Cyber Law, Ethics and Professional Practice in Cyber (6 units); Computer Networking (6 units); Industry Research Project (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Human Factors and Cyber Criminal Behaviour (6 units); Cloud Security (6 units); Security Architecture and Engineering (6 units); Security Operations and Risk Management (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Enterprise Security (6 units); Critical Infrastructure and Control System Security (6 units); ICT Master Capstone Project 1 (6 units); ICT Master Capstone Project 2 (6 units).
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Data Science
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Data Science combines computer science, mathematics, and statistics with a significant capstone project (either research-based or industry-based) sitting alongside a flexible mix of core and elective courses that lets students lean toward machine learning, AI, or data engineering depending on background.

Unlike the more AI/cybersecurity-heavy Master of Computer Science, the Data Science degree keeps a stronger statistics and mathematics backbone throughout, useful for students coming from an analytics or actuarial background rather than straight software engineering. Electives can be drawn from programming, systems programming, algorithms, and distributed systems courses shared with the Computer Science program, so the two degrees overlap more than their names suggest.

Adelaide runs three intakes a year for this degree, in January, May, and September, which is unusual outside the standard February/July starts, and well suited to international students whose home academic calendars don't line up with the Australian one. Career paths include data scientist, data engineer, machine learning engineer, and business intelligence analyst.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Statistical Learning; Programming for Data Science; Data Management and Databases; 1 elective.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Machine Learning; Big Data Analytics; 2 electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Data Science Capstone Project (Research or Industry-based); 1 elective.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Advanced Topics in Data Science; 1 elective.
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a quantitative discipline (mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering, or similar) with a GPA equivalent to 4.5/7.0.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Master of Design
description: Adelaide University's Master of Design is a two-year degree in Adelaide that pairs technical design expertise with professional practice skills. It is mostly studio-based, with collaboration, real-time feedback and access to current tools, and project-based courses connect students with industry professionals. Students also study the legal and ethical side of design. Some courses are offered online.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Art and Design Interdisciplinary Studio (12 units); Nature, Culture and Sustainability (6 units); Art and Design Advanced Theory (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Art and Design Masters Foundation Studio (12 units); Art and Design Business Practices (6 units); Art and Design Research Methods (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Art and Design Masters Project 1 (12 units); Art and Design Masters Report (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Arts and Design Masters Project 2 (12 units); Art and Design Professional Experience (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution. This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 4.0 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Economics and Resource Policy
description: Adelaide University's Master of Economics and Resource Policy is a two-year degree in Adelaide covering global food and agricultural markets, international trade and development, and cost-benefit analysis. Students develop specialised knowledge aligned to their career goals and can open a pathway to a PhD. Graduates advise on economic and resource policy across government, industry and international organisations.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Economic Principles (6 units); Global Food and Agricultural Markets (6 units); Principles of International Trade and Development (6 units); Program electives.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Cost-Benefit Analysis (6 units); Program electives; Program electives; Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Research Methods and Development (6 units); Program electives; Program electives; Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 2 — MERP Research Project (12 units); Program electives; Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution. This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 5.0 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Education
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Education is a two-year degree for people already working in education, not a route to initial teacher registration. It can be shortened to one to 1.5 years for applicants with a teaching qualification and experience.

Students choose one of ten focus areas, including education leadership and innovation, digital learning, early childhood, the brain and learning, TESOL, wellbeing and inclusion, First Nations cultures and perspectives, and a research stream with a two-part dissertation. Research methods coursework and a major project run through the degree. It is offered on campus or online (international students study mainly on campus). It suits teachers, school leaders, trainers and consultants wanting a specialisation or a research pathway.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Wellbeing in Education (6 units); International Comparative Studies in Education (6 units); Education Policies and Systems (6 units); Research Communications (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Evidence-Informed Practice in Education (6 units); Education Leadership in Diverse Contexts (6 units); Mixed Methods Research (6 units); Assessment and Evaluation (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Research Design in Education (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Program electives.
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (AQF Level 7) or higher in any discipline; advanced standing available for education-specific backgrounds
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Education Studies
description: Adelaide University's Master of Education Studies is a two-year degree in Adelaide for school leaders, teachers, consultants and trainers moving toward leadership, or preparing for higher education teaching or research. Adelaide ranks 89th in the world for education in the Times Higher Education 2026 subject rankings. Students study leadership strategy and education policy and complete a major research project.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Wellbeing in Education (6 units); International Comparative Studies in Education (6 units); Education Policies and Systems (6 units); Research Communications (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Evidence-Informed Practice in Education (6 units); Education Leadership in Diverse Contexts (6 units); Mixed Methods Research (6 units); Assessment and Evaluation (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Research Design in Education (6 units); Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Discipline courses.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Discipline courses; Discipline courses; Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Engineering
description: Adelaide's Master of Professional Engineering is a two-year, 96 unit degree offered across nine specialisations: Chemical, Civil, Electrical, Energy Resources, Mechanical, Mechatronic, Mining, Structural, and Telecommunications. It is a professional qualification pathway, taking graduates who hold a four-year bachelor or bachelor honours degree in a relevant field through to practice-ready engineer level, with credit available for prior learning. The structure is stackable, with a graduate certificate exit at six months and a graduate diploma at one year. Study combines advanced technical coursework with up to 450 hours of industry placement, capstone design projects and research, plus engineering management and data analytics. The program holds provisional accreditation from Engineers Australia, with full accreditation expected after the first cohort graduates, and aligns with the Washington Accord for international recognition. It suits engineering graduates seeking a formally accredited professional qualification.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Environmental Policy and Management
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) taught at the city campus with February and July intakes, with a coursework or research route in the second year. The core covers research design and methods and environmental planning and governance, with electives in sustainable cities, environmental economics, impact assessment and resource management.

Students complete a dissertation or research project on a real environmental problem. Entry needs a bachelor's degree with a GPA equivalent to 5.0 on Adelaide's 7-point scale. It suits people moving into environmental consulting, policy advice, sustainability management or conservation roles.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Program electives; Program electives.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Program electives; Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Dissertation Env Pol & Mgt (Applied) Part 1 (24 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Dissertation Env Pol & Mgt (Applied) Part 2 (24 units).
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Finance
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Finance is a two-year degree (96 units) open to graduates from any background, with mathematics knowledge recommended. Year one covers accounting, finance principles, business statistics, economics, fixed-income securities, equity valuation and ethics; year two moves into derivatives, advanced investment management and financial statement analysis, with two industry projects and electives in areas like blockchain, fintech, behavioural finance and real estate investment.

Students use a Financial Lab with the simulated trading platforms used by banks and investment firms, and the curriculum is developed with industry. A graduate certificate or diploma exit is available. It suits people targeting specialist roles in finance, investment banking or corporate finance.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Accounting Concepts and Methods (6 units); Principles of Finance (6 units); Business Statistics (6 units); Economic Principles (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Fixed Income Securities (6 units); Equity Valuation and Analysis (6 units); Ethical Principles in Finance and Accounting (6 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Program electives; Advanced Investment Management (6 units); Derivatives (6 units); Financial Statement Analysis (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Program electives; Program electives; Finance Industry Project 1 (6 units); Finance Industry Project 2 (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent), open to graduates from any background; senior-secondary or tertiary mathematics is recommended. GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Finance and Business Analytics
description:
A two-year master's (96 units: 30 core, 66 specialisation) that pairs finance, equity valuation, fixed income, derivatives and investment management, with analytics, predictive modelling, customer and text analytics, big data and AI tools.

Year two includes two capstones, a finance industry project and a business analytics project, done with industry input. Entry needs a bachelor's degree with a GPA equivalent to 4.5 on Adelaide's 7-point scale. It suits people targeting quantitative and data-heavy roles in banking, investment, risk analysis or consulting, where both financial judgement and analytics skills are expected.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Business Statistics (6 units); Economic Principles (6 units); Accounting Concepts and Methods (6 units); Principles of Finance (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Fixed Income Securities (6 units); Equity Valuation and Analysis (6 units); Fundamentals of Business Analytics (6 units); Customer Analytics (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Ethical Principles in Finance and Accounting (6 units); Predictive and Visual Analytics (6 units); Advanced Investment Management (6 units); Derivatives (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Chatbots and Text Analytics for Business (6 units); Managing with Big Data Analytics (6 units); Business Analytics Project 1 (6 units); Finance Industry Project 1 (6 units).
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Finance and Business Economics
Master of Financial Planning
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Financial Planning is a two-year degree approved under the Financial Adviser Standards, so graduates meet the qualification requirement to give personal financial advice in Australia (a Professional Year and the ASIC adviser exam still follow separately).

Foundation courses in business statistics, economics, accounting and finance lead into advanced investment management, risk and insurance, estate planning, taxation law, superannuation strategy and the practice of delivering financial advice. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree with no specific prerequisites. It suits career changers and finance professionals moving specifically into financial planning and wealth advice.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Business Statistics (6 units); Economic Principles (6 units); Accounting Concepts and Methods (6 units); Principles of Finance (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Personal Financial Advice (6 units); Ethics and Professionalism (Financial Planning) (6 units); Superannuation Strategy and Advice (6 units); Fundamentals of Financial Planning (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Managing Personal Risk (6 units); Estate Planning Fundamentals (6 units); Advanced Investment Management (6 units); Commercial and Business Law (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Delivering Financial Advice (6 units); Taxation Law and Policy (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline (cognate discipline preferred)
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Health Services Management
discontinued_note: No longer marketed as a standalone on-campus program; Adelaide University now offers this content via the online Master of Business Administration (Health Management).

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Human Resource Management is a two-year degree (96 units) with a stackable structure allowing a graduate certificate or diploma exit. The curriculum covers strategic HR, talent acquisition and development, performance and rewards, people analytics, industrial relations, employment law and managing global workforces, alongside business foundations in accounting, marketing and negotiation.

An industry-based project runs through two courses, Applied Challenge and Integrated Learning, turning coursework into practice. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree in any field. It suits people moving into or up within HR, toward roles such as HR business partner, talent specialist, chief people officer or organisational consultant.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Marketing (6 units); Entrepreneurial Thinking (6 units); Accounting Principles for Decision Makers (6 units); People, Leadership and Organisational Performance (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Talent Acquisition and Development (6 units); Managing Employee Performance and Rewards (6 units); People Analytics (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Applied Challenge (6 units); Strategic Management of Human Resources (6 units); Integrated Learning (6 units); Managing the Global Workforce (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Australian Industrial Relations (6 units); Negotiation (6 units); Foundations of Employment Law (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent). GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Immersive Media Technologies
description: Adelaide University's Master of Immersive Media Technologies is a two-year degree in Adelaide focused on virtual, augmented and mixed reality and other immersive media. It is deliberately practical, with hands-on projects and real-world briefs throughout. Graduates work in immersive content, interaction design and applied media roles across the creative, training and technology sectors.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 2 — Immersive Media Asset Generation (12 units); Immersive Media Development (12 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Core selective courses; Elective; Elective.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Information Technology (Applied Artificial Intelligence)
description: This two-year masters at Adelaide University teaches the practical side of artificial intelligence rather than pure theory. The first year covers programming, data systems and core IT concepts before the degree moves into AI subjects: computer vision, deep learning architectures, generative AI, natural language processing, network modelling, and robotics and autonomous systems. Students finish with an industry-based project. Entry requires a bachelor degree with a grade point average of about 4.5 on a 7-point scale and IELTS 6.5. Study is split across the Adelaide City and Mawson Lakes campuses. The program is provisionally accredited at professional level by the Australian Computer Society and is recognised internationally through the Seoul Accord, so graduates are eligible for ACS membership. Career paths include AI consultant, AI data analyst, digital strategist and AI policy specialist across healthcare, finance, technology and research. Indicative international tuition is around A$55,400 per year.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Problem Solving and Programming Foundations (6 units); Data in Information Technology Systems (6 units); Information Technology and Systems Concepts (6 units); Security Principles (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Industry Research Project (6 units); Business Intelligence (6 units); Project Management for IT Professionals (6 units); Statistical Foundations for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Data Taming and Prediction (6 units); Applied Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (6 units); Entrepreneurial Thinking (6 units); Business Process Management (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Innovative and Emerging Technologies (6 units); Applied Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning 2 (6 units); ICT Master Capstone Project 1 (6 units); ICT Master Capstone Project 2 (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution. This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 4.5 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of International and Security Law
description: Adelaide University's Master of International and Security Law is a two-year degree in Adelaide covering international law and security in a period of emerging threats and shifting geopolitical dynamics. Students study the legal frameworks that govern armed conflict, defence, and international cooperation. Graduates work in government, defence, international organisations and legal practice.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Australian Law (6 units); Elective; Elective; Elective; Introduction to Australian Law (6 units); Elective; Elective; Elective.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Public International Law (UoA) (PG) (6 units); Elective; Elective; Elective.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Elective; Elective; Elective; Elective.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Elective; Elective; Elective; Elective.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution with a competitive Grade Point Average (GPA); OR A completed Graduate Diploma in Law or Graduate Certificate in Law. This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 5.0 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 6.5.

name: Master of International Business
description:
A two-year master's (96 units) taught at the Adelaide city campus with February and July intakes. Foundation courses in marketing, accounting, management and entrepreneurship lead into international business strategy, managing multinational corporations, cross-cultural management and negotiation, and global business analysis.

Students complete an internship with a global business, NGO or government organisation, plus a two-semester industry research project. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree or graduate certificate in any field. It suits people aiming at leadership roles in multinational firms, international consulting or development work, or planning to run a business across borders.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Marketing (6 units); People, Leadership and Organisational Performance (6 units); Accounting Principles for Decision Makers (6 units); Entrepreneurial Thinking (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Foundations of International Business (6 units); Managing Multinational Corporations (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — International Trade: Strategies and Opportunities (6 units); Research in International Business Part A (6 units); Cross-Cultural Management and Negotiation (6 units); International Entrepreneurship and Innovation (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Global Business Analysis (6 units); Research in International Business Part B (6 units); International Business Strategy (6 units); Global Marketing (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree or graduate certificate in any discipline (or equivalent). GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Landscape Architecture
description: Adelaide University's Master of Landscape Architecture is a two-year degree in Adelaide focused on designing landscapes for community health and wellbeing, diversity and sustainability. Students develop their understanding of ecology, prepare planting plans, and work across urban and regional contexts with an emphasis on respecting Aboriginal knowledge, culture and connection to land. Graduates work as landscape architects.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Landscape Architecture Creative Cultures Studio (12 units); Designed Ecologies (6 units); Case Studies in Landscape Architecture (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Landscape Architecture Urbanism Studio (12 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Landscape Architecture Nature by Design Studio (12 units); Landscape Architecture Technologies (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Landscape Architecture Capstone Studio (18 units); Program electives.
admission_requirements: To be eligible, an applicant must have achieved at least one of the following minimum entry requirements and demonstrate they fulfil any prerequisite and essential criteria for admission. In cases where there are more eligible applicants than available places, admission will be competitive with ranks based on the entry criteria. Eligible pathways include additional requirements: A design portfolio must be submitted. The portfolio should include the applicant's own creative works from previous degrees, professional, and/or personal background, showing design skills, knowledge, and familiarity with a range of design tools and media. In addition to final outcomes, it should comprise evidence of design process, development and drawing documentation. The portfolio may include material developed with others if clearly referenced and the applicant's contribution explained.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Laws
description: Adelaide University's Master of Laws is a one-year degree in Adelaide for law graduates and practising lawyers building deep discipline knowledge and intellectual breadth. Students select from a range of specialist option courses and connect with an international network of peers. Graduates advance their careers in legal practice, government, business and the not-for-profit sector.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Australian Law (6 units); Elective; Elective; Elective; Introduction to Australian Law (6 units); Elective; Elective; Introduction to Australian Law (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Elective; Elective; Elective; Elective; Elective; Elective; Elective; Elective.
admission_requirements: A completed Bachelor of Laws (Honours) (or equivalent); OR A completed Bachelor of Laws (or equivalent), plus a completed Graduate Diploma in Legal Practice ; OR A completed Bachelor of Laws (or equivalent), plus substantial professional experience within the profession; OR A completed Bachelor of Laws (or equivalent), plus substantial research experience within the profession. This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 5.0 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 6.5.

name: Master of Management
description: Adelaide University's Master of Management is a two-year degree in Adelaide, co-designed with industry, that combines core business courses with specialised management study and an industry placement. It suits professionals upskilling, changing careers or moving into senior roles. Graduates leave with a strong grounding in business and management and a network of industry partners.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Marketing (6 units); People, Leadership and Organisational Performance (6 units); Accounting Principles for Decision Makers (6 units); Entrepreneurial Thinking (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Managing Organisational Development and Change (6 units); Managing the Global Workforce (6 units); Project Management Fundamentals (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Ethics, Sustainability and Governance (6 units); Business Analytics for Managers (6 units); Negotiation (6 units); Business Decision Making and Problem-Solving (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Strategy Concepts (6 units); Applied Challenge (6 units); Integrated Learning (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Maritime Engineering
description: The Master of Maritime Engineering at Adelaide University is designed to extend engineers ready to take their career to the next level, and is delivered in collaboration with ASC, Australia's builder and sustainer of the Navy's Collins Class submarines. Students study higher-level courses in advanced systems engineering, submarine design, naval architecture and shipbuilding programs, and deepen their project management expertise through engineering management and data analytics courses. A wide range of electives lets students tailor their studies to interests such as defence leadership, autonomous robotic systems, or advanced mechanics and materials. Graduates work across South Australia's significant maritime industry base and the growing global sector.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Engineering Data Analytics (6 units); Principles of Systems Engineering (6 units); Acoustics and Vibrations (6 units); Masters Professional Engineer Career Preparation (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Professional Engineering Management (6 units); Submarine Design and Construction (6 units); Principles of Submarine Design (6 units); Masters Professional Engineer Engagement with Professional Practice (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Masters Engineering Research Project A (6 units); Engineering Systems Design Project (6 units); Submarine Naval Architecture Maritime Engineering (6 units); Elective.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Masters Engineering Research Project B (12 units); Shipbuilding Programs for Industry and Defence Managers (6 units); Naval Nuclear Propulsion and Stewardship (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed four year bachelor (AQF7) or bachelor honours (AQF8) degree or equivalent in science, engineering, technology or a related field from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Marketing
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Marketing is a two-year degree (96 units) with a stackable structure: students can exit after six months with a graduate certificate or after a year with a graduate diploma. Year one covers advertising, digital marketing, consumer behaviour, marketing analytics, and leadership and entrepreneurship; year two moves into brand management, global marketing and services marketing, ending with a capstone marketing research project done as work-integrated learning.

Advanced digital marketing and advanced marketing analytics sit in the core, reflecting where the field is heading. Entry is a completed bachelor's degree in any field. It suits people deepening an existing marketing career or moving into marketing from another discipline, with graduate roles such as brand manager, campaign manager, digital marketing specialist and marketing analyst.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Marketing (6 units); People, Leadership and Organisational Performance (6 units); Accounting Principles for Decision Makers (6 units); Entrepreneurial Thinking (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Advertising: Theory and Practice (6 units); Advanced Digital Marketing (6 units); Consumer Behaviour and Insights (6 units); Advanced Marketing Analytics (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Global Marketing (6 units); Services Marketing (6 units); Marketing Research Project Part A (6 units); Marketing for Society (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Strategic Brand Management (6 units); Marketing Strategy and Planning (6 units); Marketing Research Project Part B (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent). GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Midwifery
description: Adelaide University's Master of Midwifery is a two-year degree in Adelaide for registered midwives advancing their practice, knowledge and leadership. Students tailor their study with a wide range of electives, and from second year choose a clinical or research stream, finishing with a clinical application project or an original research publication or thesis.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Program electives; Program electives.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Program electives; Research for Advancing Nursing, Midwifery and Health Care (12 units); Program electives; Research for Advancing Nursing, Midwifery and Health Care (12 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Clinical Project (12 units); Program electives; Minor Thesis A (12 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Program electives; Minor Thesis B (12 units); Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor degree (AQF level 7) or higher from a recognised higher education institution in the field of Midwifery; AND; OR Hold or be eligible to hold registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA). This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 5.0 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Master of Music (Performance and Pedagogy)
description: Adelaide University's Master of Music (Performance and Pedagogy) is a two-year degree in Adelaide that develops advanced performance technique and stage presence alongside teaching practice through supervised music education projects. Students perform regularly and learn to teach and mentor others. It suits musicians working toward careers as soloists, ensemble members and music teachers, and in the wider music community.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Pedagogy Research Seminar IV (12 units); Performance and Pedagogy IV A (12 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Pedagogy Practicum IV (12 units); Performance and Pedagogy IV B (12 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Pedagogy Research Seminar V (12 units); Pedagogy Practicum V (12 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Performance and Pedagogy V (24 units).
admission_requirements: To be eligible, an applicant must have achieved the following minimum entry requirement and demonstrate they fulfil any prerequisite and essential criteria for admission. In cases where there are more eligible applicants than available places, admission will be competitive with ranks based on the entry criteria. Eligible pathways include additional requirements: Applicants must submit a high-quality DVD of varying and contrasting work of 25 minutes duration to the Elder Conservatorium of Music. The DVD should include four or more music pieces of different styles or by different composers and a letter of verification from the music teacher or qualified person confirming that the performance is a true representation of the applicant's own work. Classical voice applicants must present works in four languages: English, French, German and Italian. The recording must clearly state the date on which the recording was made and whether it represents a live performance, commercial release or radio broadcast.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Nursing
description: Adelaide University's Master of Nursing is a post-registration degree for nurses who already hold, or are eligible to hold, registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. It is not a qualifying degree for people who are not already nurses. The two-year program at the Adelaide City campus runs to 96 units and offers either a clinical project pathway or a research thesis pathway, with specialist interest areas including critical care, oncology, mental health, perioperative nursing, primary health care and women's health. The qualification is stackable, so students can exit with a graduate certificate after six months or a graduate diploma after one year. Entry requires a bachelor degree, a grade point average around 5.0 on a 7-point scale, and a high IELTS result of 7 overall. Graduates move into senior clinical, leadership, management and research roles. Indicative international tuition is around A$54,900 per year.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Program electives; Program electives.
Year 1, Semester 2 — Research for Advancing Nursing, Midwifery and Health Care (12 units); Program electives; Research for Advancing Nursing, Midwifery and Health Care (12 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Clinical Project (12 units); Program electives; Minor Thesis A (12 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Program electives; Minor Thesis B (12 units); Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor degree (AQF level 7) or higher from a recognised higher education institution; AND; OR Hold or be eligible to hold registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australi a (NMBA). This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 5.0 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Master of Occupational Therapy (Graduate Entry)
description: Adelaide University's Master of Occupational Therapy (Graduate Entry) is a two-year degree in Adelaide that prepares graduates from other fields to register as occupational therapists. It takes a holistic view of health, covering human neuroanatomy, neurophysiology and pathology, how the environment shapes occupational performance, and how to design interventions for individual needs. Students complete 1,000 hours of field placements across settings and the lifespan.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Introduction to Occupational Therapy Practice GE (6 units); Enabling Occupation 1 (6 units); Occupational Therapy Field Practice 1 (6 units); Evidence Based Practice Skills (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Human Neuroscience GE (6 units); Enabling Occupation 2 (6 units); Occupational Science (GE) (6 units); Occupational Therapy Field Practice 2 (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Enabling Occupation 3 (6 units); Enabling Occupation 4 (6 units); Participatory Community Practice GE: Planning (6 units); Evidence Based Practice GE (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Enabling Occupation 5 (6 units); Participatory Community Practice GE: Implementation (6 units); Occupational Therapy Field Practice 4 (12 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor degree (AQF level 7) or higher from a recognised (CRICOS) Australian higher education institution with a highly competitive GPA; AND; OR Satisfactory completion of prerequisite courses at a bachelor level (AQF level 7) or higher within the last 10 years.*. This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 5.0 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Master of Pharmacy
description: Adelaide University's Master of Pharmacy is a one-year degree in Adelaide that builds advanced knowledge of pharmaceutical science and practice, covering how medicines work, how they are used safely and effectively, and the role of the pharmacist in patient care. It suits pharmacy and health graduates deepening their expertise.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Internship Studies 1 (6 units); Pharmacy Practice Research and Inquiry (6 units); Pharmacist Internship Supervised Practice 1 (12 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Internship Studies 2 (6 units); Pharmacy Practice Leadership and Management (6 units); Pharmacist Internship Supervised Practice 2 (12 units).
admission_requirements: A completed Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) from a recognised higher education institution that has provisional or full Australian Pharmacy Council (APC) accreditation in Australia or New Zealand.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Master of Physiotherapy (Graduate Entry)
description: Adelaide University's Master of Physiotherapy (Graduate Entry) is a two-year intensive degree in Adelaide for graduates from a related field. The curriculum is contemporary and culturally informed, with hands-on learning, and covers how to assess, treat and prevent a range of health conditions. Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a physiotherapist with the Physiotherapy Board of Australia.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Physiotherapy Professional Practice (6 units); Evidence Informed Clinical Reasoning in Physiotherapy (6 units); Musculoskeletal Skills in Physiotherapy (12 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Acute Care Skills in Physiotherapy (12 units); Rehabilitation Skills in Physiotherapy (12 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Pain Science (GE) (6 units); Acute Care in Physiotherapy Practice (6 units); Physiotherapy Practice in Rehabilitation (6 units); Applied Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy Practice (GE) (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Clinical Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy GE (6 units); Physiotherapy Practice with Children and Families (6 units); Advanced Practice in Physiotherapy GE (12 units).
admission_requirements: To be eligible, an applicant must have achieved the following minimum entry requirements and demonstrate they fulfil any prerequisite and essential criteria for admission. In cases where there are more eligible applicants than available places, admission will be competitive with ranks based on the entry criteria. Eligible pathways include approved fields of education: Medical Studies Rehabilitation Therapies Human Biology Medical Science Human Movement Public Health; prerequisite courses: Statistics and Research Methods (at least one course equivalent); AND Human Anatomy (at least two courses equivalent); AND Human Physiology (at least two courses equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0.

name: Master of Procurement and Supply Chain Management
description: Adelaide University's Master of Procurement and Supply Chain Management is a two-year degree in Adelaide with strong industry connections. Students review real company case studies and develop ethical, sustainable solutions to common challenges, and study digital supply chains across manufacturing, warehousing, logistics and procurement, including how AI and robotics are changing service businesses. Graduates work in procurement and supply chain roles across industry and government.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Marketing (6 units); People, Leadership and Organisational Performance (6 units); Accounting Principles for Decision Makers (6 units); Managing Sustainable Supply Chains (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Digital Supply Chains (6 units); Global Supply Chain Management (6 units); Strategic Procurement (6 units); Entrepreneurial Thinking (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Integrated Logistics Management (6 units); Managing Operations in Supply Chains (6 units); Service Management in Supply Chains (6 units); Supply Chain Design and Analytics (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Integrated Learning (6 units); Program Electives; Program Electives; Program Electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: The Master of Professional Accounting at Adelaide University is a 1.5-year degree at the Adelaide City campus for graduates from any discipline who want to qualify as accountants. It is accredited by both Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand and CPA Australia, so graduates are eligible to begin either professional program. The first year covers analytical tools for business, economics, accounting, finance principles, accounting information systems and corporate law, and the final six months consolidate financial accounting, auditing and assurance. Entry requires a bachelor degree with a grade point average of about 4.5 on a 7-point scale and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work in audit, business advisory, financial reporting, management accounting, forensic accounting and corporate tax. Indicative international tuition is around A$54,300 per year.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Accounting Concepts and Methods (6 units); Principles of Finance (6 units); Business Statistics (6 units); Economic Principles (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Management Accounting Concepts and Techniques (6 units); Accounting Information Production and Analytics (6 units); Intermediate Financial Reporting (6 units); Commercial and Business Law (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Auditing and Assurance Services (6 units); Advanced Financial Accounting (6 units); Taxation Law and Policy (6 units); Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution. This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 4.5 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Professional Engineering
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Professional Engineering is a two-year degree (96 units) that is the accredited professional qualification for people who already hold an engineering bachelor's degree and want the credential recognised for practice. It is offered in discipline streams such as electrical, mechanical, and civil. Core courses cover professional engineering management, discipline-specific technical subjects, engineering data analytics, a design project, and a two-part masters research project, plus about 450 hours of industry placement.

Entry requires a four-year bachelor's or honours degree in a relevant engineering field and IELTS 6.5. Early exit points exist (graduate certificate at six months, graduate diploma at one year). The program holds provisional Engineers Australia accreditation with Washington Accord recognition expected after the first cohort graduates. Some courses run across the city and Mawson Lakes campuses.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Professional Engineering Management (6 units); Electrical Power Systems (6 units); Control Systems (6 units); Masters Professional Engineer Career Preparation (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Electrical Machines (6 units); Renewable Energy Systems (6 units); Engineering Data Analytics (6 units); Masters Professional Engineer Engagement with Professional Practice (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Masters Engineering Research Project A (6 units); Electrical and Electronic Engineering Design Project (6 units); Program electives; Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Masters Engineering Research Project B (12 units); Program electives; Program electives.
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 4.5/7.0; bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL)

name: Master of Project and Program Management
Master of Project Management
description: Adelaide University Master of Project Management is a 1.5-year AQF Level 9 degree, available in online or intensive mode, accredited by the Project Management Institute Global Accreditation Center. Students can weight the degree toward portfolio and program management, enterprise transformation and innovation, project governance or complex decision-making, and toward the end complete an industry project on a topic of their choice plus a choice of internship, career development or research-skills course. It is part of a stackable set: students can exit after six months with a graduate certificate or after a year with a graduate diploma. Indicative international tuition is around A$50,500 per year. Graduates work across defence, construction, healthcare, information technology and government as project managers, project officers, business analysts and consultants.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Project Management Fundamentals (6 units); Project Control Methods (6 units); Risk Assessment and Management (6 units); Project Leadership (6 units); Project Management Fundamentals (6 units); Project Control Methods (6 units); Risk Assessment and Management (6 units); Project Leadership (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Research Methods and Development (6 units); Project Procurement and Contract Management (6 units); Program electives - Group A; Program electives - Group C.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Project Governance (6 units); Enterprise Transformation Project Management (6 units); Systems Design for Projects (6 units); Program and Portfolio Management (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Integrated Learning (6 units); Complex Project Management (6 units); Industry Project in Project Management (12 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Psychology
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Psychology (Clinical) is a highly competitive two-year master's accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council. It combines coursework, three placement courses totalling 24 units, and two research projects in the second year.

Graduates are eligible for general registration as a psychologist and can then complete a supervised registrar program for clinical endorsement. Entry requires an APAC-accredited four-year psychology honours sequence with an upper second class result or better, plus the Casper situational test, referee reports and an interview; selection weights the interview at 50 percent and Casper at 40 percent. It suits psychology graduates set on clinical practice in mental health assessment and evidence-based therapy.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Evidence Based Practice; Psychological Assessment (Clinical and Health) (6 units); Clinical Neuropsychology & Disability (6 units); Psychopathology and Clinical Practice (6 units); Interviewing and Intervention (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Advanced Child & Adult Intervention (6 units); Health Psychology (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Master of Psychology (Clinical) Placement II (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Research Project in Clinical Psychology II (18 units); Master of Psychology (Clinical) Placement III (12 units).
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 5.0/7.0; APAC-accredited psychology honours degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Master of Public Health
description:
Adelaide University's Master of Public Health runs three distinct end points on the same 96-unit, two-year frame: a Professional Practice pathway built around a 24-unit placement for people wanting applied, workplace-ready public health skills; a Dissertation pathway (60 core units, a 24-unit dissertation, and 12 electives) for students weighing a PhD later; and a Research Thesis pathway that swaps in a 48-unit thesis for those committed to a research career from the outset.

Core content covers epidemiology, biostatistics, health promotion, and communicable disease control. A Translational Health Sciences specialisation is delivered entirely online for students who want to keep working while they study, a genuinely different format from the on-campus-and-online Public Health specialisation.

Adelaide has a long track record in this field through its School of Public Health, building on established South Australian public health research in areas like Indigenous health and chronic disease epidemiology. Graduates go into state and federal health departments, NGOs, and international agencies, with the Professional Practice placement often functioning as an unofficial foot in the door at SA Health or a similar employer.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Epidemiology 1; Biostatistics for Public Health; Health Promotion: Principles and Practice; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Communicable Disease Control; Health Systems and Policy; Research Methods in Public Health; 1 elective (24 units).
Year 2 (Professional Practice pathway) — Public Health Placement (24 units); Global Public Health; 2 electives.
Year 2 (Dissertation pathway) — Public Health Dissertation (24 units); 2 electives.
Year 2 (Research Thesis pathway) — Public Health Thesis (48 units).
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in any discipline (health-related background preferred but not required).
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with 6.0 minimum in each band.

name: Master of Research (Computer and Information Science)
Master of Social Work
description:
A two-year qualifying master's (96 units) that leads to eligibility for practice as a social worker. It includes up to 1,000 hours of supervised field placement across two practicum courses, typically 3 to 5 days a week including outside teaching weeks, so it is difficult to combine with heavy outside work.

Entry needs a bachelor's degree with at least one year full-time equivalent study in social and behavioural sciences, a GPA around 5.0 on a 7-point scale, and IELTS 7 across all bands. A criminal history check and Working with Children clearance are required within the first six months. One caveat: as of 2026 Adelaide University is working with the Australian Association of Social Workers on reaccreditation of the program for 2027, which applicants should confirm before enrolling.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Social Work and Policy Practice (6 units); Contemporary Practice Theories for Social Work (6 units); Social Work Practice Skills (6 units); Aboriginal Health and Wellbeing (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Social Work Practicum 1 (18 units); Ethical Decision Making (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Innovation and Research (6 units); Innovative Social Work Practice with Children and Families (6 units); Mental Health and Social Work Practice (6 units); Human Rights Based Practice and Community Development (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Leadership in Social Work (6 units); Social Work Practicum 2 (18 units).
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 5.0/7.0; minimum one year full-time study in social/behavioural sciences
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Master of Statistics
description: Adelaide University's Master of Statistics is a two-year degree in Adelaide combining statistical theory with practical application. Students work in teams on group projects and a major statistical project in the final year, and build programming skills in languages such as R. Graduates turn data into evidence for decision-making across industry, government and research.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Data Visualisation (6 units); Calculus for Statisticians (6 units); Probability and Statistics (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Linear Algebra (6 units); Design of Experiments (6 units); Statistical Practice (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Statistical Methodology (6 units); Program electives; Program electives; Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 2 — Program electives; Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution. This degree requires a Grade Point Average (GPA) equivalent to an Adelaide University 5.0 on a 7-point scale for entry.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Strategic Communication
description: Adelaide University's Master of Strategic Communication is a two-year degree in Adelaide covering how organisations plan and deliver communication across strategy, messaging, channels and audiences. Students apply their learning through an industry project or a communication research project. Graduates work in corporate communication, public relations and campaign roles.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Strategic Communication Contexts (6 units); Social Media Management (6 units); Campaign Planning (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Transmedia Storytelling (6 units); Managing Digital Design (6 units); Risk, Issues and Crisis Communication (6 units); Media Management (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Researching Strategic Communication and Media (12 units); Leadership in Strategic Communication (12 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Strategic Communication Extended Research Project (24 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Teaching
description:
A two-year initial teacher education master's (96 units) that leads to eligibility for teacher registration. Adelaide University offers it in primary (Reception to Year 6) and secondary streams. The primary program includes 520 hours of supervised placement (about 60 days) across two professional experience courses.

It is accredited by the Teachers Registration Board of South Australia; recognition in other states and countries varies. Entry requires a bachelor's degree with a GPA around 5.0 on a 7-point scale, IELTS 7 across all bands, and a Working With Children Check, and students must pass the national LANTITE literacy and numeracy test before their final placement. Primary is taught mainly at the Magill campus, with Mount Gambier and Whyalla options.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Language and Learning (6 units); Primary Mathematics Education 1 (6 units); Effective Pedagogical Practices for Primary Contexts; Classroom Management and Inclusive Education (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Professional Experience 1: Planning, Teaching, Assessing and Managing the Classroom Environment (6 units); Reading and Literacies (6 units); Arts and Technologies Education (6 units); Neuroscience, Cognition and Learning (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Primary Science Education (6 units); Primary Health and Physical Education (6 units); Humanities and Social Science Education (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Learning about Literacies and Text Production (6 units); Professional Experience 2: Inquiry into Practice (12 units); Languages Education and First Nations Knowledges (6 units).
admission_requirements: GPA equivalent to Adelaide University 5.0/7.0; bachelor's degree in any discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, no band below 7.0 (or equivalent PTE/TOEFL), required for health/education placements

name: Master of Technology, Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: Adelaide University's Master of Technology, Innovation and Entrepreneurship is a two-year degree in Adelaide combining business insight with technological capability. Students develop advanced skills in innovation management, commercialisation and entrepreneurial thinking, learning to turn ideas into ventures and to lead change in existing organisations. Graduates launch startups, drive transformation in established companies or consult on technology strategy and trends.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Marketing (6 units); People, Leadership and Organisational Performance (6 units); Accounting Principles for Decision Makers (6 units); Entrepreneurial Thinking (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Leading New Product Innovation (6 units); Entrepreneurial Business Development (6 units); Strategic Innovation Management (6 units); Navigating Commercialisation Pathways (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — AI for Business (6 units); Program Electives - Technology; Program Electives - Business; Tech eChallenge (Advanced) (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Program Electives - Technology; Program Electives - Technology; Program Electives - Business; eChallenge (Advanced) (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Tourism, Events and Hospitality Management
description: Adelaide University's Master of Tourism, Events and Hospitality Management is a two-year degree in Adelaide covering sustainable tourism, destination management and festival and event management, with real projects alongside industry partners. It suits working professionals and newcomers to the sector, and graduates move into roles such as event director, destination manager and hotel manager.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Marketing (6 units); People, Leadership and Organisational Performance (6 units); Accounting Principles for Decision Makers (6 units); Entrepreneurial Thinking (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Foundations of Tourism and Hospitality (6 units); Tourism and Hospitality Enterprise Management (6 units); Festival and Event Management (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Managing Tourism and Hospitality Operations (6 units); Tourism, Event and Hospitality Practicum (6 units); Marketing for Tourism, Events and Hospitality (6 units); Managing Venues and EventScapes (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Event Leveraging and Legacy (6 units); Digital Innovations in Tourism, Events and Hospitality (6 units); Sustainable Destination Management (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Urban and Regional Planning
description: Adelaide University's Master of Urban and Regional Planning is a two-year degree in Adelaide covering planning history, policy, finance, ethics, climate and society. Students learn to prepare proposals, assess feasibility and balance competing interests, with fieldwork inspecting regenerated urban spaces, and complete an original research project. Graduates work as planners across government, consultancies and property organisations.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1 — Theory and Practice in Urban and Regional Planning (6 units); Planning Governance, Stakeholders, Politics and Policy (6 units); Integrated Transport and Infrastructure Planning (6 units).
Year 1, Semester 2 — Urban Design for Health and Sustainability (6 units); Development Economics (6 units); Environmental Planning, Climate Change and Sustainability (6 units); Program electives.
Year 2, Semester 1 — Planning Law (6 units); Development Assessment (6 units); Social Planning and Community Issues (6 units); Research Methods in Planning (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Urban Design and Master Planning Studio (6 units); Research Project in Planning (12 units); Urban Planning Professional Experience (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Viticulture and Oenology
description: Adelaide University's Master of Viticulture and Oenology is a two-year degree in Adelaide, recognised internationally, in a wine industry adapting to environmental, technological and consumer change. Students study grapegrowing and winemaking including organic and biodynamic cultivation, and can complete a research dissertation on a topic of choice. Graduates work as winemakers, viticulturists and wine industry specialists.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 2 — Sensory Studies (6 units); Introductory Winemaking (6 units); Viticultural Methods and Procedures (6 units); Sensory Studies (6 units); Introductory Winemaking (6 units); Viticultural Methods and Procedures (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Program electives; Winemaking at Vintage (6 units); Viticultural Science B (6 units); Winemaking at Vintage (6 units); Viticultural Science B (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 2 — Advances in Wine Science (6 units); Program electives; Program electives; Program electives.
Year 3, Semester 1 — Experience & Perspectives in the Wine Industry (12 units); Program electives.
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) degree or equivalent in a science field from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Wine and Food Business
description: Adelaide University's Master of Wine and Food Business is a two-year degree in Adelaide covering marketing, branding, global markets, tourism and the legal side of the wine and food sectors. Students build practical skills in market analysis, entrepreneurial thinking and project management, and take part in a study tour and industry networking. Graduates work in marketing, retail management and export strategy.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 2 — Wine and Food Retailing (6 units); Entrepreneurial Thinking (6 units).
Year 2, Semester 1 — Accounting Principles for Decision Makers (6 units); Foundations of Wine Science (6 units).
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor (AQF level 7) or bachelor honours (AQF level 8) degree or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution; OR A completed nested or related graduate certificate (AQF level 8) or higher or equivalent from a recognised higher education institution.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
At 240 credit points, ACU's Bachelor of Arts gives students room to build a genuine major (80cp in one discipline) plus a minor (40cp) or a second major, drawing from disciplines that range from history and philosophy to global studies and theology. Because ACU runs Arts alongside so many double-degree combinations (Arts/Laws, Arts/Commerce, Psychological Science/Arts), the standalone BA tends to attract students who want breadth rather than a professional accreditation attached to the degree itself.

One quirk worth knowing: students aren't restricted to units badged under "Arts." They can draw from units across ACU's Schedule of Unit Offerings, campus and prerequisites permitting, which in practice means a philosophy major can pick up business or education units as electives without switching degrees.

It's a degree that rewards students who already have a direction in mind (further study, teaching, writing, policy work) since it doesn't come with the built-in professional pathway of, say, nursing or paramedicine. The value is in the major chosen and what's built around it.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory units in chosen major (e.g. History, Philosophy, English, Global Studies), breadth electives
Year 2: 200-level major units (minimum 40cp at this level across the degree), elective units from other Arts disciplines or ACU schools
Year 3: 300-level major units, minor sequence or second major, capstone or research-based unit in the major discipline
Structure: 80cp major, 40cp minor (or second major), remaining credit points as electives
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science (Honours)
description:
This is an 80-credit-point add-on year for students who've already completed a relevant bachelor's degree and hold at least a 5.0 GPA on ACU's seven-point scale, not a standalone four-year degree. The structure splits into coursework (including HLSC406 Research Methods in Biomedical and Health Sciences Research) and a research component worth either 20 or 40 credit points depending on the pathway chosen, with prerequisite units like SCIE403 or SCIE405 gating entry into the higher-research-weighted option.

The point of the year is to pair students with an academic supervisor and have them contribute to an actual area of research rather than complete another year of taught units, a deliberate bridge toward higher degree research (Masters by Research, PhD) for students who discover during their undergraduate degree that they want a research career in biomedical or health science rather than a purely clinical one.

Because it's a single honours year rather than a full degree, applicants are typically ACU biomedical science graduates staying on, though the pathway is open to graduates of equivalent degrees from other universities.
curriculum:
Coursework component: HLSC406 Research Methods in Biomedical and Health Sciences Research, plus discipline-specific advanced units
Research component: independent research project (20cp or 40cp depending on pathway) under academic supervision, culminating in a thesis
Prerequisites for higher-research pathway: completion of SCIE403 or SCIE405
Total: 80 credit points, combining coursework and supervised research
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (Birth to Five Years)
Bachelor of Education (Primary and Secondary)
description:
Most initial teacher education degrees pick a lane, primary or secondary, but this ACU course runs 320 credit points to give graduates both: a broad primary teaching qualification plus one specialist secondary teaching area. It's a longer, more demanding structure, but it produces a graduate who can move between a Year 4 classroom and a Year 10 specialist subject, which matters in regional and outer-suburban schools where staffing flexibility counts.

The unit structure separates education theory (the EDES-coded units, including a mandatory unit on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledges, histories and cultures) from discipline-specific curriculum and pedagogy units, and from the EDET-coded "effective teaching" sequence that runs across all four years, tying theory back to classroom practice each semester rather than leaving it until the practicum blocks.

Professional experience is substantial: a minimum of 80 days of supervised placement, plus a required 25 hours of direct service delivered through a dedicated social justice and community engagement unit (EDES206). Graduates come out eligible for provisional teacher registration and, given the primary-and-secondary combination, tend to have an easier time picking up early-career roles in schools that need coverage across both bands.
curriculum:
Year 1: EDES100 Understanding Learning and Teaching, EDES103 Understanding Learners and Their Contexts, EDES104 Digital Cultures and Capabilities, EDEN100 Foundations of Literacy, EDET100
Year 2: EDES105 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Knowledges, Histories and Cultures, EDMA291 Mathematics Curriculum Pedagogy and Assessment 2, EDSI290 Science Curriculum Pedagogy and Assessment, EDET200, first professional experience placements
Year 3: Secondary discipline studies units (100- and 300-level in chosen specialist area), EDES206 Social Justice and Community Engagement for Educators (25 hours), EDET300
Year 4: Advanced primary curriculum units, final secondary discipline units, EDET400/EDET401, capstone professional experience block
Total professional experience: minimum 80 days across the four years
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent (teaching registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sports Science
description:
The course is aligned to Exercise and Sports Science Australia (ESSA) standards for Accredited Exercise Scientist registration, and ACU has built in a checkpoint most competitor programs don't: a strengthened Exercise Assessment and Conditioning unit that functions as a secure, skills-based gate students must pass before they're allowed into practicum. It's there to make sure students can actually design and justify a safe, evidence-based exercise program before they're let loose on real clients.

Placement is a two-stage structure: Professional Experience 1 runs internally with heavy support, Professional Experience 2 is external, across a minimum of two placement sites and 140 total hours, 90 of which must be exercise testing, prescription and delivery specifically. The degree finishes with an Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE), the same kind of practical, station-based assessment used in medical and allied health training, which is a more rigorous capstone than many exercise science degrees use.

Depending on which electives students choose, graduates can also become eligible for Level 1 accreditation with the Australian Strength and Conditioning Association, giving the degree a foothold in both clinical exercise science and performance/strength coaching pathways.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Anatomy, Exercise Physiology, Biomechanics, Functional Anatomy
Year 2: Exercise Assessment and Conditioning (checkpoint unit — secure skills-based assessment), Nutrition for Exercise and Sport, Motor Learning and Control
Year 3: Professional Experience 1 (internal, supported placement), Clinical Exercise Prescription, Strength and Conditioning electives (ASCA Level 1 pathway)
Year 4: Professional Experience 2 (external placement, across minimum two sites, 140 hours including 90 hours exercise testing/prescription/delivery), capstone Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE)
Accreditation: aligned to ESSA Exercise Scientist standards; ASCA Level 1 eligible depending on electives
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
ACU's IT degree is built around a deliberately broad first year (ITEC100 Information Technology in Action, ITEC105 Cybersecurity For Everyone, ITEC201 Fundamentals of Information Technology) before students specialise, and it lets students borrow electives from any other ACU bachelor degree, so a student leaning toward health informatics could pick up health science units, or one leaning toward fintech could add business units, without a formal double degree.
