The coursework is the same, covering event planning, organisational behaviour and financial decision-making, then marketing, sport as a product and service, data analytics, and a final block on sport law, governance, elite athlete management and stakeholder relations, taught by people from professional and Olympic sport organisations. The Professional version formalises Bond's placement connections, with football codes and the World Surf League among them, into a compulsory 20-week Work Integrated Learning component in the final semester: a supervised placement plus a professional portfolio taken after coursework, adding about one semester. The Bond Business School holds AACSB and EQUIS accreditation. It is open to international students only; domestic students take the standard degree. It suits students building a sport administration career who want an Australian placement in the program.
curriculum: Required Subjects: BUSN71-201 Event Management, FINC71-101 Fundamentals of Finance, LAWS77-521 Global Sports Law and Governance, MGMT71-104 Managing People, MKTG71-100 Marketing Fundamentals, SPMT71-124 International Sport Business, SPMT71-125 Managing High Performance Sport, STAT71-111 Business Statistics Professional Option: BUSN71-701 Professional Portfolio, BUSN71-705 Professional Development Sport Management Option: ENFB71-104 Entrepreneurship and Innovation, MGMT71-311 Leading Innovation and Change
admission_requirements: Successful completion of a recognised Bachelor degree (or equivalent qualification) in any field.
english_requirements: International English Language Testing System (IELTS) Academic Overall score 6.5 with no sub score less than 6.0. Pearson Test of English (PTE) Academic Overall score 58 with no Communicative Scores below 50. Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test (TOEFL iBT) Overall score 79 (no scores below 21 in Writing, 18 in Speaking, and 16 in Reading and Listening)

name: Master of Sport Management / Master of Project Management
admission_requirements: A completed bachelor's degree in a related discipline (or equivalent) with a competitive GPA; some programs consider relevant professional experience in place of a directly related degree.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 6.5, with no band below 6.0.

name: Master of Valuation and Property Development
description:
A four-semester master's (about 16 months), also available part-time, covering property finance and taxation, corporate portfolio management, risk, feasibility analysis, property law, and valuation and market analysis, with electives that lean toward either property valuation or city planning.

It is accredited by the Australian Property Institute, the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors and the Valuers Registration Board of Queensland, so it supports the pathway toward registration as a valuer. Classes are taught in Bond's Built Environment Precinct, which includes Australia's first 6-Star Green Star education building. The degree is designed both for people already working in property who want to formalise and extend their skills and for graduates moving in from finance, law or another field, with graduates working in valuation, investment, asset management and property research.
curriculum: Required Subjects: SSUD71-101 Understanding Buildings, SSUD71-106 Real Estate Property Rights, SSUD71-107 Property Investment and Valuation, SSUD71-109 Commercial Valuation, SSUD71-124 Property Development, SSUD71-125 Feasibility Analysis, SSUD71-126 Property Finance and Investment, SSUD71-216 Corporate Property and Asset Management, SSUD71-300 Planning and Assessment Processes
admission_requirements: Successful completion of a recognised Bachelor degree (or equivalent qualification) in any field (Note - This program is not available to graduates of Bond's Bachelor of Property, students may consider either the Master of City Planning or the Master of Project Management as an alternative.)
english_requirements: International English Language Testing System (IELTS) Academic Overall score 6.5 with no sub score less than 6.0. Pearson Test of English (PTE) Academic Overall score 58 with no Communicative Scores below 50. Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test (TOEFL iBT) Overall score 79 (no scores below 21 in Writing, 18 in Speaking, and 16 in Reading and Listening)

name: Master of Valuation and Property Development (Professional)
description: The work-integrated learning version of Bond's Master of Valuation and Property Development. The coursework is the same, covering property finance and taxation, corporate portfolio management, risk, feasibility analysis, property law, and valuation and market analysis, with electives leaning toward either valuation or city planning, and it carries the same accreditation from the Australian Property Institute, the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors and the Valuers Registration Board of Queensland. The Professional version adds a compulsory 20-week Work Integrated Learning component in the final semester, a supervised placement in an Australian property organisation plus a professional portfolio, taken after coursework, adding about one semester. It is open to international students only; domestic students take the standard degree. It suits students on the pathway toward registration as a valuer who want Australian industry experience in the qualification.

name: Medical Program* Bachelor of Medical Studies, Doctor of Medicine
description:
Bond's Medical Program is the shortest path to a medical doctorate in Australasia: students complete two consecutive degrees, the Bachelor of Medical Studies and the Doctor of Medicine, in four years and eight months total rather than the five to six years most Australian medical degrees take. The Bachelor of Medical Studies runs for two years and eight months (eight trimesters) and builds foundational clinical knowledge and skills, after which the Doctor of Medicine runs for a further two years (six trimesters); both degrees are conferred together on completion of the MD.

Teaching in the first two years is problem-based: each week opens with a clinical case that the week's learning is built around, worked through in small interactive groups rather than large lectures. From the third year, students relocate to the Bond University Clinical Education and Research Centre at Robina Hospital for a full year immersed in a genuine hospital environment before moving into the MD's more advanced clinical phases. The MD is accredited at AQF level 9 as an Extended Masters Degree, and graduates meet the requirements for provisional medical registration, allowing them to begin accredited intern training toward full registration.
curriculum:
Bachelor of Medical Studies (8 trimesters, 2 years 8 months):
Years 1-2 (5 trimesters): case-based small-group learning covering foundational biomedical science, clinical skills, and population health, structured around a weekly clinical case
Year 3: full-year clinical immersion at the Bond University Clinical Education and Research Centre, Robina Hospital
Doctor of Medicine (6 trimesters, 2 years):
Advanced clinical rotations across medicine, surgery, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynaecology, and general practice
Elective clinical placement, including options for rural or international rotations
Final trimesters: capstone clinical practicum and preparation for provisional registration
MD accredited at AQF level 9 (Extended Masters Degree); meets requirements for provisional medical registration
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (or equivalent) with strong results in Chemistry and Biology, plus a competitive score on an approved medical admissions test (e.g. UCAT) and interview.
english_requirements: IELTS Overall 7.0, with no band below 7.0 (registration-board English requirement).

name: Professional Doctorate of Occupational Therapy
description: Bond University's Professional Doctorate of Occupational Therapy is a four-year program that is both an entry-to-practice qualification and a research doctorate. The first two years are an accelerated Master of Occupational Therapy, an entry-level clinical degree, and the final two years add a doctoral research component and a capstone internship. It includes more than 1,600 hours of practice-based education. Graduates of the master's component are eligible to apply for registration as an occupational therapist with the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia, so a graduate from another field can use this pathway to enter the profession. The program is also accredited in the United States by ACOTE, supporting eligibility for NBCOT certification and practice in the US and Canada. Graduates work as clinician-researchers and move into leadership roles. It suits people who want to qualify as an occupational therapist and complete a doctorate in one continuous program.
curriculum: Required subjects: OCTY71-108 Occupational Therapy: Work, OCTY71-109 Occupational Therapy: Learn, Play, Connect, OCTY71-111 The New Global Occupational Therapist, OCTY71-113 The Occupational Therapy Professional: Practice, Standards and Quality, OCTY71-402 Health Professional Research Internship A, OCTY71-403 Health Professional Research Internship B, OCTY73-700 Professional Practice in Occupational Therapy I, OCTY73-701 Professional Practice in Occupational Therapy II
admission_requirements: Students who are enrolled in Bond's Master of Occupational Therapy and who meet the requirements below may apply to progress to the Professional Doctorate of Occupational Therapy at the completion of Bond's Master of Occupational Therapy program. Students applying to progress must meet the following criteria: Successful completion of all requirements of Bond's Master of Occupational Therapy, including the Clinically-focused research pathway, AND. be in good academic standing, AND. have a minimum weighted average mark of 75%, AND. successful completion of all practice education fieldwork experiences on the first attempt. Admission is on the basis of an approved research proposal and successful completion of a Confirmation of Candidature presentation. Further information on how to apply can be found on the Research Degrees web pages. See compulsory Health Sciences & Medicine compliance requirements
english_requirements: International English Language Testing System (IELTS) Academic Overall score 7.0 with no sub score less than 7.0. Pearson Test of English (PTE) Academic Overall score 65 with no Communicative Scores below 65. Test of English as a Foreign Language Internet-Based Test (TOEFL iBT) Overall score 94, no scores below 27 Writing, 23 Speaking, 24 for Reading and Listening

name: Professional Doctorate of Physiotherapy
description: A post-professional doctorate, not an entry-to-practice degree. It builds on Bond's two-year Doctor of Physiotherapy, which is the qualification that leads to registration as a physiotherapist with the Physiotherapy Board of Australia. The professional doctorate adds a further two years of advanced research coursework, a doctoral thesis and an industry-based capstone internship, for four years in total, with up to one year of credit for prior learning. It develops advanced clinical research capability, leadership and specialised expertise for clinician-researchers. Graduates work across clinical practice, research, education, management and industry. It suits registered physiotherapists, or students continuing directly from the Doctor of Physiotherapy, who want a research doctorate anchored in professional practice.
curriculum: Required subjects: PHTY71-001 Clinical Practice of Physiotherapy: Unit 1, PHTY71-002 Clinical Practice of Physiotherapy: Unit 2, PHTY71-003 Clinical Practice of Physiotherapy: Unit 3, PHTY71-004 Clinical Practice of Physiotherapy: Unit 4, PHTY71-005 Clinical Practice of Physiotherapy: Unit 5, PHTY71-006 Clinical Practice of Physiotherapy: Unit 6, PHTY71-007 Clinical Practice of Physiotherapy: Unit 7, PHTY71-406 Transition to Professional Practice, PHTY72-419 Physiotherapy: Evidence Based Practice Research - Part 1, PHTY73-423 Physiotherapy: Evidence Based Practice Research - Part 2, PHTY73-424 Physiotherapist: Work Ready
admission_requirements: Successful completion of a Doctor of Physiotherapy degree from Bond University or equivalent qualification from another university, with a minimum GPA requirement of 3 (on a 4-point scale where 1 = pass). Must also meet subject prerequisites (see additional requirements) and undertake an interview. See compulsory Health Sciences & Medicine compliance requirements

name: Bachelor of Commerce (Applied)
description:
Box Hill Institute's Bachelor of Commerce (Applied) splits its three years into 12 core subjects (72 points), 8 major subjects (48 points), and 4 electives (24 points): accounting, finance, management, marketing, business ethics, and law all sit in the core before students specialise.

As a dual-sector provider, Box Hill teaches this degree the way it teaches its TAFE diplomas: smaller cohorts than a large university commerce school, and a direct line into the institute's own vocational accounting and business programs for students who want to start at certificate or diploma level and build up rather than enrolling in a bachelor's straight away.

The degree carries accreditation from both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, which matters more than it might for a similarly-titled degree elsewhere. Box Hill isn't a research university trading on reputation, so professional body accreditation is the credential that does the work of assuring employers the accounting training meets the same bar as a larger institution's.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Foundations of Accounting; Economics for Business; Business Law; Marketing Principles; 2 further core subjects.
Year 2 — Financial Accounting; Management Accounting; Taxation Law; Corporations Law; 2 further core subjects; major subjects begin.
Year 3 — Auditing and Assurance; Strategic Management; Contemporary Issues in Accounting; remaining major subjects; 4 electives across the degree.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall (Box Hill's own published bachelor-entry bar)

name: Bachelor of Computer Systems (Networking)
description:
This degree runs 19 core units plus 5 electives drawn from a choice of majors (cyber security, networking, or cloud and virtualisation), with the Networking major itself sitting inside a broader Computer Systems degree rather than being sold as a standalone qualification.

First year is deliberately generalist: basic networking, cloud computing, and introductory programming, so students don't have to commit hard to networking specifically before they've seen the alternatives. Second year gets specific fast: operating systems, cyber security, network security, systems security, virtualisation, and programming for web applications, alongside business and communication units that a purely technical program often skips. Third year moves into emerging ICT technologies, advanced security or virtualisation techniques, and entrepreneurship and innovation.

Box Hill delivers this in partnership with Cisco, VMware, and Microsoft, which shows up in the practical, vendor-relevant skills the networking major targets. Those skills sit closer to what a network administrator or systems engineer does day to day than a purely theoretical computer science curriculum, and they're useful for students aiming at Cisco or Microsoft certifications alongside the degree itself.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Introduction to Networking; Cloud Computing Fundamentals; Introductory Programming; IT Systems Fundamentals; foundational core units.
Year 2 — Operating Systems; Cyber Security Fundamentals; Network Security; Systems Security; Virtualisation; Programming for Web Applications; Business and Communication Skills.
Year 3 — Emerging ICT Technologies; Advanced Networking/Virtualisation Techniques; Entrepreneurship and Innovation; 5 electives (networking, cyber security, or cloud/virtualisation stream).
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education
description:
Box Hill's Bachelor of Early Childhood Education is built for people already working while they study, the program runs as blended delivery with classes on evenings and occasional Saturdays, and each core subject pairs 30 hours of face-to-face lecture, tutorial, and workshop time with around 5 hours of online activity rather than a standard daytime timetable.

The degree comprises 28 core subjects and 4 practicum subjects, totalling 80 days of supervised placement across a range of early childhood settings, deliberately including services other than the student's own workplace, so students already working in childcare still have to demonstrate their skills somewhere unfamiliar rather than only in a setting where staff already know them.

The program is recognised by the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority and meets Victorian Institute of Teaching standards for Early Childhood Teacher registration, meaning graduates come out eligible to register as qualified early childhood teachers, not just educators, in Victoria.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Child Development; Foundations of Early Childhood Pedagogy; Health, Safety and Wellbeing in Early Childhood Settings; Practicum 1.
Year 2 — Curriculum Design for Early Learning; Language and Literacy Development; Working with Families and Communities; Practicum 2.
Year 3 — Leadership in Early Childhood Settings; Inclusive Practice and Additional Needs; Professional Practice and Ethics; Practicum 3.
Year 4 — Research and Reflective Practice in Early Childhood Education; Transition to Teaching; Practicum 4 (final placement block).
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent (teaching registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Fashion
description:
Box Hill Institute has run fashion design and merchandising training out of its Box Hill campus for decades, well before it offered bachelor's degrees at all, and the Bachelor of Fashion sits on top of that vocational base rather than starting from scratch as a purely academic program. The broader fashion degree family here splits 12 core units, 10 major units, and 6 electives across three years: pattern-making, garment construction, and textiles knowledge sit alongside business, marketing, and enterprise units rather than treating design as a purely creative pursuit separate from the commercial reality of running a label.

Students work with industry-standard equipment and, depending on the trimester, contribute to Box Hill's own fashion parades and graduate showcases, a public, portfolio-building event that functions as an informal industry pitch rather than a purely internal assessment.

Career paths lean toward fashion design, garment technology, buying and merchandising, and small-label entrepreneurship, reflecting Box Hill's applied, business-aware take on fashion education rather than a purely runway-focused design school model.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Fashion Design Fundamentals; Pattern-Making and Garment Construction 1; Textiles and Materials; Introduction to the Fashion Industry; core business unit.
Year 2 — Pattern-Making and Garment Construction 2; Fashion Illustration and Communication; Fashion Marketing; Sustainable Fashion Practice; major units begin.
Year 3 — Fashion Enterprise and Business Planning; Collection Development (culminating in graduate showcase); remaining major and elective units.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; portfolio may be required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Hospitality Management
description:
The Bachelor of Hospitality Management at Box Hill covers accounting, marketing, business and hospitality law, workplace communications, strategic project management, and human resources management: a management-focused degree built for people planning to run hospitality operations rather than work the front line of them, though Box Hill's parallel commercial cookery and hospitality certificate programs mean many students arrive with genuine kitchen or floor experience already.

Small class sizes and direct lecturer contact are emphasised more than at a typical large university business school, consistent with Box Hill's TAFE-scale delivery model even at bachelor's level. A work-based hospitality management project gives students a real venue or business problem to solve rather than a hypothetical case study, drawing on Box Hill's existing industry relationships across Melbourne's hospitality sector.

Career paths include hotel and venue management, event management, hospitality operations, and food and beverage management, with the strategic project management and contemporary issues coursework aimed at people expected to run a shift, a venue, or eventually a business rather than simply staff one.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Introduction to Hospitality Management; Accounting for Hospitality; Workplace Communications; Marketing Principles.
Year 2 — Business and Hospitality Law; Human Resource Management; Contemporary Issues in Hospitality; Financial Management.
Year 3 — Strategic Project Management; Work-Based Hospitality Management Project; electives.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
Box Hill's Bachelor of Information Technology follows the same 12 core / 8 major / 4 elective structure as several of its other applied degrees, with specialisation streams in cyber security, data analytics and AI, cloud computing and IoT, and software engineering. It's TEQSA-accredited and pitched at AQF Level 7, the standard bachelor's level, despite Box Hill's identity as a TAFE first and university-level provider second.

That dual-sector status is arguably the more interesting fact about the degree: students can move between Box Hill's certificate and diploma-level IT courses and this bachelor's with credit transfer arrangements that a stand-alone university IT school doesn't usually offer as smoothly, useful for students who started in vocational IT training and want to step up without repeating content.

Career paths include software developer, cyber security analyst, data analyst, cloud engineer, and IT support/systems roles, with the elective structure letting students weight the final year toward whichever of the four specialisation areas matches where they want to work.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Introduction to Programming; IT Systems Fundamentals; Networking Basics; Database Fundamentals; core units.
Year 2 — Software Development; Cyber Security Principles; Cloud Computing Fundamentals; Data Analytics Foundations; major units begin.
Year 3 — Advanced specialisation units (cyber security, data analytics and AI, cloud and IoT, or software engineering); capstone IT project; 4 electives.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Music Industry (Major in Performance)
description:
Box Hill structures its Bachelor of Music Industry around six possible majors (Performance is one, alongside options like Audio Production and Composition), with a combined common core running through the first two years covering the music industry from multiple angles: innovation, creativity, entrepreneurship, and preparing for where the industry is heading rather than where it's been.

Once the major is chosen, it accounts for roughly half the remaining coursework, and students fill the rest by picking from a pool of more than sixty subjects, adding either two minors, a minor plus electives, or straight electives, a genuinely open structure compared to a fixed-major conservatoire degree. Full-time study runs at 16 contact hours a week plus an expected 16 hours of personal practice and study time, delivered face to face on weekdays.

Box Hill also builds in formal exit points most bachelor's degrees don't offer: a Diploma in Music Industry after one year and an Associate Degree in Music Industry after two, useful for students who want a credential if their circumstances change partway through, or who are testing whether a full three-year commitment is right for them.
curriculum:
Year 1 — Music Industry Foundations (common core); Performance Major 1; Innovation and Creativity in Music; electives.
Year 2 — Music Industry Perspectives (common core); Performance Major 2; entrepreneurship unit; electives or minor units. (Diploma exit available after Year 1; Associate Degree exit available after Year 2.)
Year 3 — Performance Major 3 (advanced); electives from the 60+ subject pool; capstone performance project.
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; audition required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Diploma of Aviation (Commercial Pilot Licence - Aeroplane)
Associate Degree of Engineering
description: The Associate Degree of Engineering at Charles Darwin University provides a sound basis of fundamental engineering concepts followed by the application of civil and structural, electrical and electronics, or mechanical engineering theory and practice. Students develop skills for solving common engineering problems and prepare for further study in the Bachelor of Engineering Science and Bachelor of Engineering Honours. Civil and structural associates contribute to the design, operation and maintenance of structures such as water resources, roads, bridges and marine structures, while electrical and electronics associates assist with the design, automation and control of devices.

name: Associate Degree of Information and Communication Technology
description: The Associate Degree of Information and Communication Technology at Charles Darwin University prepares students to be part of a rapidly evolving field, developing knowledge of the principles and applications of ICT and strengthening problem-solving, decision-making, communication and teamwork skills. The course was developed with ICT industry leaders and aligns with industry requirements. Graduates may work as an information technology specialist in government, private companies and non-government organisations, in roles such as analyst, technician, web designer, developer or system administrator.

name: Associate Degree of Legal Studies
description: The Associate Degree of Legal Studies at Charles Darwin University is for people interested in broadening their understanding of the legal system without committing to a full law degree. It gives a broad understanding of the law, legal processes and legal principles and introduces practical areas such as torts, contracts, criminal law and transnational law. It suits those with a general interest in legal issues and those gauging their interest before a full law degree. After completing the first year, students may seek admission to the Bachelor of Laws with credit transfer. The course does not lead to professional accreditation.

name: Associate Degree of Network Engineering
description: The Associate Degree of Network Engineering at Charles Darwin University provides the skills, knowledge and confidence to design, operate and maintain the networks that underpin the infrastructure of industry and government organisations. The course has a strong practical emphasis with extensive opportunities to put theory into practice, and can be studied part-time or full-time, fully online for domestic students or on campus. Graduates may work as a technician, in helpdesk support, or as a network and systems administrator.

name: Bachelor of Accounting
description:
The value proposition of CDU's Bachelor of Accounting is almost entirely about the accreditation stack: graduates meet the educational requirements for CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand (CAANZ), and the broader accounting suite at CDU also carries CIMA (UK) and ACCA recognition. For a degree at a regional Australian university, that's a fairly comprehensive set of professional pathways, and it means graduates aren't limited to local NT employers if they want to sit CPA or CA exams interstate or move to accounting roles in the UK or elsewhere in the Commonwealth.

Content-wise it's a fairly standard accounting core (financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation, commercial law), but CDU frames electives around the resources and government sectors that dominate the Territory economy: mining royalties, public sector financial management, and small-business advisory work show up more than in accounting degrees oriented toward corporate finance in a capital-city CBD. A combined Bachelor of Accounting/Diploma of Laws option exists for students who want commercial law grounding without committing to a full LLB.

Delivery is flexible (on campus, online, or blended) and the degree can be taken part-time, which suits the number of students working in bookkeeping or para-accounting roles while they complete the qualification.
curriculum:
Core units: Financial Accounting, Management Accounting, Company Accounting, Auditing and Assurance, Taxation Law, Commercial Law, Corporations Law, Accounting Information Systems, Business Finance, Economics for Business
Electives: choose from public sector accounting, small business advisory, resources sector accounting, or a business minor
Capstone: integrated case study or professional practice unit in final year
Professional accreditation built into course design: meets CPA Australia and CAANZ requirements
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Architectural Design
description: The Bachelor of Architectural Design at Charles Darwin University places the design studio at the centre of the curriculum, supported by history and theory, communication, materials and construction, and environmental design units. The course develops theoretical knowledge, design proficiency and communication techniques applicable to architecture and the built environment, including computer-aided design for preparing architectural drawings. Each semester builds on the previous one across projects of increasing complexity, with particular emphasis on environmental design for tropical, desert and temperate climates. Graduates work as building designers and technicians, and can continue to the Master of Architecture.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
CDU pitches its Bachelor of Arts around a genuinely distinctive regional angle: rather than being a generic humanities degree, it's built around issues facing Northern Australia, Indigenous communities, and South-East Asia, which makes sense given Darwin sits closer to Dili and Denpasar than to Sydney. Students choose from nine majors, including options rarely paired together at one institution: Digital Communication and Indigenous Studies sit alongside more familiar choices, and an Architecture major (unusual for a BA) covers representation, spatial design, and industry-standard drafting tools with a tropical-north focus.

The Indigenous Studies major is arguably the strongest reason to choose CDU specifically over an east-coast university for this degree; it's taught by staff embedded in Northern Territory Aboriginal communities and covers philosophy, sociology, and Indigenous perspectives in a way that's hard to replicate somewhere without that geographic and cultural proximity. The Digital Communication major, meanwhile, tracks social media, media ethics, and multi-screen communication, practical skills for content and comms roles rather than a literary-criticism-heavy media studies track.

As with most CDU undergraduate degrees, the BA is available fully online, on campus, or mixed, and can be taken part-time, which matters given a meaningful chunk of the student body balances study with work or family responsibilities in regional NT towns.
curriculum:
Foundation year: core arts units in critical thinking, research methods, and an introductory unit in the chosen major
Majors offered (choose one, minor optional): Digital Communication, Indigenous Studies, Architecture, Creative Writing, History, Politics and International Relations, Society and Culture, Asian Studies, Screen and Media
Years 2-3: major-specific sequence plus free electives, culminating in a capstone or independent research project
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus, online, or blended
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Arts Honours
description: The Bachelor of Arts Honours at Charles Darwin University provides an initiation into independent research. Through core units, students gain an understanding of research and fundamental knowledge and learn to conduct ethical research, foster positive working relationships and acknowledge intellectual property rights. Students work closely with a research supervisor to develop a high-quality research thesis, industry project or sustained creative work, with one-on-one support and the flexibility to design a bespoke project aligned with their talents and interests. Graduates develop expertise in a number of key disciplinary areas.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science at Charles Darwin University is a three-year degree that develops fundamental knowledge in cell biology, anatomy and physiology, microbiology, biochemistry and pathophysiology, providing an understanding of the structure and function of the healthy and diseased body at the system, cellular and molecular level. Students also gain knowledge in research design and methodology and in Indigenous, rural and remote health, enabling them to consider health issues from global, regional and societal perspectives, and choose a specialisation to develop specific knowledge and skills in an area aligned with their interests.

name: Bachelor of Business
description: The Bachelor of Business at Charles Darwin University is a flexible qualification that develops knowledge, skills and understanding of business and commerce within global and local contexts, supporting students to be innovative thinkers able to meet the challenges of a changing business world. Communication, presentation and problem-solving skills are emphasised throughout. Students develop fundamental business knowledge and can major in marketing, international management, entrepreneurship, human resource management, accounting or financial management. The course is fully flexible, with full-time or part-time study.

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description: The Bachelor of Computer Science at Charles Darwin University prepares students to be part of a continually evolving field, developing skills and knowledge in the technical principles and applications of computer science and strengthening problem-solving, decision-making and communication skills. Graduates may work as a computer scientist in government, private companies and non-government organisations, in areas such as web design and development, games development, networking, application development, analysis, consulting, UX, programming, database administration or business analysis.

name: Bachelor of Creative Arts
description: The Bachelor of Creative Arts at Charles Darwin University is a comprehensive program in contemporary creative arts, offering a transformative learning experience in making, performing and presenting creative work, leading to creative, managerial and leadership roles in the sector. Students develop their unique creative voice through studio practice units with guidance from experienced teachers who are creative professionals, collaborate with each other, and connect with the creative sector. Delivery is internal and external for flexibility, with the opportunity to study online depending on unit and major choices, and optional field trips in the Northern Territory.

name: Bachelor of Digital Enterprise
description: The Bachelor of Digital Enterprise at Charles Darwin University combines business and information technology to prepare students for careers shaped by innovation and rapid digital change. Students develop a foundation in management, marketing, digital product development and data-driven decision-making, alongside core IT capabilities in web development, systems, networking and applications. The mix enables students to understand how organisations operate, create value and compete in digital environments. The degree is flexible, with a wide selection of business and IT units and online or on-campus study.

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
CDU trains a disproportionate share of the Northern Territory's primary teachers, and the Bachelor of Education (Primary) is shaped by that reality: a strong First Nations education thread runs through the coursework because so many graduates end up teaching in schools with significant Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander student populations, including remote community schools where CDU-trained teachers are often the most viable local supply pipeline.

The course covers Transition through Year 6/7 and is structured around 30 core units plus two specialist elective areas chosen from English, humanities, science, technology and mathematics, health and PE, or the Arts, letting students build some depth in a curriculum area they want to specialise in, without turning the degree into a secondary-style single-subject major. Professional experience placements run throughout the degree rather than being backloaded into final year, and online students complete placements at schools near where they live rather than having to relocate to Darwin, which is a meaningful accessibility factor given how spread out the NT population is.

Graduates meet the Australian Professional Standards for Graduating Teachers and are eligible for provisional registration with the Teacher Registration Board of the Northern Territory, with mutual recognition arrangements applying interstate.
curriculum:
Core sequence (30 units) across child development, curriculum and pedagogy, inclusive education, classroom management, and First Nations education
Specialist elective areas (choose 2): English, Humanities and Social Sciences, Science, Technology and Mathematics, Health and Physical Education, The Arts
Professional experience: staged placements from first year through to a final-year extended practicum block
Capstone: final professional experience placement with formal competency assessment against the Australian Professional Standards for Graduating Teachers
Total: 4 years full-time, on campus or online with local placements
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent (teaching registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Education Birth to Five Years
description: The Bachelor of Education Birth to Five Years at Charles Darwin University prepares students to become an early childhood teacher, exploring issues, concepts and practices common and specific to early childhood education. Students learn about play and learning sciences, language and literacy, preparation for teaching, health and physical education, science in education, curriculum and programming, mathematics, leadership and advocacy in early childhood contexts, and humanities, social science and the environment. The course develops professional knowledge and skills, reflective practice, and an awareness of environmental and cultural influences on teaching and learning.

name: Bachelor of Education Early Childhood and Primary
description: The Bachelor of Education Early Childhood and Primary at Charles Darwin University prepares students to become an early childhood teacher and a primary school teacher, offering flexible and versatile employment options. Students explore issues, concepts and practices common and specific to both early childhood education, including before-school settings, and primary school education, learning about play and learning sciences, language and literacy, health and physical education, science in education, technology and design, curriculum and programming, mathematics, and leadership and advocacy. It is an initial teacher education qualification covering children from birth to the end of primary school.

name: Bachelor of Education in Early Childhood Teaching (Birth-12 Years)
Bachelor of Education Primary
description: The Bachelor of Education Primary at Charles Darwin University prepares students to guide and develop primary school students' skills through the key learning areas of education during their early years at school. Students learn about the school curriculum, contemporary approaches to issues such as inclusivity, child and adolescent development, classroom management and student wellbeing, improving the teaching and learning relationship, First Nations education, and developing an evidence-based approach to learning and teaching in primary settings. Study is available online or on campus, part-time or full-time, with online students completing placements close to home.

name: Bachelor of Education Secondary
description: The Bachelor of Education Secondary at Charles Darwin University prepares students to become a secondary school teacher, eligible to teach in middle, secondary and senior colleges. The course combines discipline-specific curriculum and pedagogical studies, general education studies and professional experience, and on graduating students are qualified to register as a teacher anywhere in Australia. It focuses on the skills and knowledge needed to teach in high schools as outlined by the Australian National Curriculum, and meets the national and local need for teachers committed to improving educational outcomes for children in years 7 to 12.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Engineering at CDU is explicitly oriented toward the infrastructure and resources challenges of northern Australia: remote power and water systems, tropical building performance, and the mining and gas projects that dominate NT industry. Students pick one of three specialisations (civil and structural, electrical and electronic, or mechanical engineering), and the course was developed with industry input specifically so graduates come out with skills that map onto what Territory employers (and the broader northern Australia resources sector) are actually hiring for, rather than a generic engineering curriculum transplanted from a southern capital city.

It's a four-year Honours-embedded degree (not a separate add-on year like some Group of Eight universities do it), accredited to meet Engineers Australia's requirements for professional engineer registration, and available fully online for students who can't relocate to Darwin. That's a genuinely unusual offering, since most accredited engineering degrees in Australia require substantial on-campus lab and workshop time. CDU manages this partly through intensive on-campus blocks for lab-heavy units combined with remote delivery for the more theory-based content.

Because Darwin's engineering employment market is smaller and more resources-and-government-heavy than Sydney's or Melbourne's, a good chunk of the practical/work-integrated learning component connects students directly with NT infrastructure and utilities employers rather than a broad national graduate market.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Engineering Mathematics, Mechanics, Materials Science, Engineering Design, Thermodynamics, Electrical Fundamentals, Professional Practice in Engineering
Specialisation streams (choose one): Civil and Structural, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical
Year 3: specialisation core units plus Project Management, Fluid Mechanics or Power Systems (depending on stream), industry-linked design project
Year 4 (Honours): capstone engineering project, advanced specialisation electives, professional experience placement
Total: 4 years full-time, accredited by Engineers Australia; on campus or online with intensive lab blocks
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Engineering Honours
description: The Bachelor of Engineering Honours at Charles Darwin University provides advanced science, in theory and practice, to qualify students as an engineer able to solve problems in infrastructure, the environment or technology. Students specialise in civil and structural, electrical and electronics, or mechanical engineering, and can study fully online or on campus, full-time or part-time, qualifying as an engineer in Australia and internationally. The course provides an advanced understanding of the scientific and technical principles of engineering, 12 weeks of industry placement, and teamwork and management skills for engineering projects or research.

name: Bachelor of Engineering Science
description: The Bachelor of Engineering Science at Charles Darwin University encourages independent thinking and creative, logical solutions for real-world challenges, providing the scientific knowledge that underpins each discipline along with hands-on practical experience in civil and structural, electrical and electronics, or mechanical engineering. Study is available fully online or on campus, full-time or part-time, learning from award-winning engineers and lecturers. The course was developed with industry leaders so graduates leave with engineering skills that align with international industry requirements, working as an engineering technologist in their chosen discipline.

name: Bachelor of Environmental Science
description: The Bachelor of Environmental Science at Charles Darwin University combines academic study with practical experience, enabling students to play an active role in the protection and conservation of the environment. Foundation knowledge in biology, ecology and spatial analysis is the base from which students learn to solve complex environmental problems, exploring human impacts, social and cultural perspectives, and how to communicate information for positive environmental outcomes. Training in critical and systems thinking prepares graduates to work in government, private companies or community organisations in areas including environment and heritage and biodiversity conservation.

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description:
CDU's Exercise and Sport Science degree gets students into practical, sport-specific coursework earlier than many equivalent programs, which tend to spend most of first year on generic science prerequisites before students see anything resembling their actual field. Anatomy, physiology, psychology, coaching, and nutrition units appear from early in the course, and the program builds toward supervised placements rather than treating practical experience as an afterthought bolted onto the final semester.

A five-day compulsory residential intensive at the Casuarina campus plus 80 hours of practicum placement are built in specifically to satisfy Exercise and Sport Science Australia (ESSA) accreditation requirements: this matters for online and remote students, who make up a meaningful share of enrolments given the Territory's dispersed population, because it means even fully online students have to travel to Darwin at some point for the intensive component. Graduates come out eligible for ESSA accreditation as an Exercise Scientist (via the non-accredited pathway track) and can also seek membership with the Australian Strength and Conditioning Association, Sports Medicine Australia, and Fitness Australia.

Given the NT's demographics and remoteness, several placement partners work in community sport and remote/Indigenous health and physical activity settings, which is a different practicum flavour than the elite-sport or metro gym placements more common in programs at east-coast universities.
curriculum:
Core units: Human Anatomy, Exercise Physiology, Biomechanics, Sport and Exercise Psychology, Nutrition for Performance, Motor Learning and Control, Strength and Conditioning, Exercise Prescription for Health and Disease
Practical components: compulsory 5-day residential intensive (Casuarina campus) and 80 hours of supervised practicum
Capstone: applied placement project in a community, clinical, or sport-performance setting
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus or online with mandatory on-campus components
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Health Honours
description: The Bachelor of Health Honours at Charles Darwin University is a one-year full-time program for students who have completed a bachelor degree in a health-related discipline. The honours program builds on students' knowledge and develops specialised skills in their area of interest, covering research design, data collection, critical analysis and data interpretation, and the ethical and professional issues of research. Students complete coursework in research methods and writing plus an independent research project and thesis, working under supervision and meeting regularly with their supervisor.

name: Bachelor of Health Science
description: The Bachelor of Health Science at Charles Darwin University provides the skills to work in a multidisciplinary health industry, with strong health industry connections and diverse content leading to work in health policy and research, health and wellbeing, health promotion and public health. The degree is a pathway into master's-level study in occupational therapy, nutrition, speech and language pathology, physiotherapy, health research and public health. A core part of the course is community engagement and a community project that provides the opportunity to put knowledge into practice, supported by CDU academic staff.

name: Bachelor of Health Services Management
description: The Bachelor of Health Services Management at Charles Darwin University offers units across health, business and information technology to prepare students to contribute to the health service management industry. Graduates gain an understanding of business management and of the diversity of health clients, the importance of cultural safety, health promotion, and local and global health issues influencing the health care system. The course explores the challenges of working in urban, rural and remote communities and offers scholarships, international study tours and student exchange, with students studying alongside peers from business, social work and other allied health areas.

name: Bachelor of Humanitarian Aid and Development
description: The Bachelor of Humanitarian Aid and Development at Charles Darwin University is an interdisciplinary degree that teaches students to understand, critically analyse and apply concepts of community development, humanitarian practice and development aid. Students explore culture studies, sociology, ethics, Indigenous knowledge, community development, international humanitarian assistance and development, project management and language studies, learning from academics and industry practitioners focused on national and international community work, disaster relief and development. Students complete a two-week compulsory intensive at the Casuarina campus, and Human Services major students undertake 400 hours of community placement.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description: The Bachelor of Information Technology at Charles Darwin University prepares students to develop creative and innovative technologies, building knowledge and skills in web design and development, networking, application development and systems, and encouraging open-minded problem solving, creative thinking and engaging communication. Students can undertake sought-after industry modules including Cisco and Microsoft certificates. Graduates may work as an information technology specialist in government, private companies and non-government organisations, as a web designer and developer, among other roles.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
Studying law at CDU means studying it in a jurisdiction most Australian law schools barely touch: the Northern Territory has its own quirks in areas like Indigenous land rights, mining and resources law, and criminal sentencing that don't come up the same way in a Sydney or Melbourne law degree. Students get exposure to that Territory-specific context alongside the standard Priestley 11 subjects the profession requires everywhere in Australia.

The LLB runs 240 credit points across three years full-time, with a maximum of 100 credit points able to come from first-year (100-level) units and at least 60 credit points required at 300-level or above, a structure meant to stop students front-loading easy units and coasting. Most of the core sequence (contracts, torts, criminal law, property, equity, evidence, civil procedure) is prescribed by the legal profession's admission requirements, so there's not much room to swap those out; the flexibility shows up in the specialist electives, where students can lean toward family law, international law, or competition and consumer law depending on where they want to end up.

CDU offers full online delivery for the whole degree, which is unusual for a law program and reflects the practical reality that a lot of NT residents live hours from Darwin. Graduates wanting Honours can roll straight into the one-year Bachelor of Laws Honours add-on rather than restarting a separate degree.
curriculum:
Year 1: Legal Process, Contracts A & B, Criminal Law, Legal Research and Writing, foundational electives
Year 2: Torts, Property Law, Equity and Trusts, Administrative Law, Constitutional Law
Year 3: Evidence, Civil Procedure, Company Law, Professional Conduct, capstone/clinical elective
Specialist electives across the degree: family law, international law, competition and consumer law, Indigenous legal issues
Structure: 240 credit points total, max 100 credit points at 100-level, minimum 60 credit points at 300-level or above
Optional: Bachelor of Laws Honours (1 additional year) for eligible graduates
Delivery: on campus, fully online, or blended; 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Laws Honours
description: The Bachelor of Laws Honours at Charles Darwin University is a one-year course for high-achieving Bachelor of Laws graduates. It may provide a pathway to a PhD, enhance career prospects and advance legal research and writing skills. Students undertake a substantial legal research project in an area relevant to their career, deeply exploring a legal topic and developing an understanding of research methodologies relevant to law and legal scholarship, with support from CDU academic staff and a research supervisor to produce work to a publishable level. Successful completion may make graduates eligible for admission to a PhD.

name: Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science Honours
description: The Bachelor of Medical Laboratory Science Honours at Charles Darwin University provides the knowledge and skills to work as a medical scientist in diagnostic pathology, in areas such as haematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, histology and molecular pathology. Students are taught by industry professionals and learn to test samples, interpret results and make recommendations for improved patient health, with placements that let students apply their skills in the workplace. In the final year students can undertake a research project or advanced professional practice alongside medical scientists and researchers in accredited laboratories.

name: Bachelor of Midwifery
description: The Bachelor of Midwifery at Charles Darwin University is a professionally accredited degree that qualifies graduates to register as a midwife, recognised by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. Students study online with intensive clinical teaching blocks or on campus, full-time or part-time, learning from experts in the field. Graduates provide woman-centred, evidence-based care for women, babies and families throughout the childbearing journey in a variety of settings, with a particular focus on rural, remote and First Nations Australians, supporting women's childbearing choices across pregnancy, birth, postnatal and newborn periods.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Remote and Indigenous health placements are the defining feature of nursing at CDU in a way they simply aren't at most Australian nursing schools, because the Northern Territory has some of the most acute rural and remote health workforce shortages in the country. Students complete 800 hours of clinical placement across metropolitan and rural/remote settings, and those who've finished second-year scope-of-practice units plus the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health unit can apply for a four-week remote placement, run in partnership with NT Top End Health Service, that puts them into genuinely remote clinical settings most nursing graduates elsewhere never experience before registration.

That partnership-driven remote placement track is a real point of difference for students who know they want a career in remote area nursing, a distinct, higher-paid, higher-autonomy specialisation within Australian nursing that's hard to break into without exactly this kind of exposure during training. Indigenous students undertaking placements also have access to 'away from base' funding support, recognising that a lot of NT students are commuting from communities well outside Darwin.

The degree meets registration requirements set by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, so graduates can register as Registered Nurses nationally; the remote and Indigenous health specialisation is additive, not a trade-off against the standard national scope of practice.
curriculum:
Core sequence: Anatomy and Physiology, Pathophysiology, Pharmacology, Nursing Practice (foundational through advanced), Mental Health Nursing, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health, Community and Primary Health Care
Clinical placement: 800 hours total across metropolitan and rural/remote settings
Elective pathway: 4-week remote placement (Northern Territory) available to eligible 3rd-year students, delivered with NT Top End Health Service
Capstone: transition-to-practice placement in final semester
Total: 3 years full-time, registration-ready under Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia standards
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 6.5) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nutrition
description: The Bachelor of Nutrition at Charles Darwin University provides the knowledge and skills to work in the food and nutrition sector to positively influence health, leading to work in health policy and research, health and wellbeing, and health promotion across local, rural and remote Australia and beyond. The course is a pathway into master's-level study in dietetics. Graduates may work in community health centres, health promotion organisations, government and non-government organisations, the food industry, sporting organisations, universities and research organisations, in roles such as nutrition consulting.

name: Bachelor of Oral Health Therapy
description: The Bachelor of Oral Health Therapy at Charles Darwin University prepares graduates for a career as an oral health therapist, meeting the oral health needs of communities in the Northern Territory and across Australia with an emphasis on being adaptable, culturally safe, fair and sustainable. Students develop skills in health promotion, communication, clinical decision-making, problem-solving and critical thinking for person-centred care, with a focus on social and professional responsibility, leadership, and scientific and clinical knowledge. Work-ready skills are developed through simulation and clinic-based learning, including treatments such as fillings, tooth removals and periodontal care.

name: Bachelor of Paramedicine
description: The Bachelor of Paramedicine at Charles Darwin University qualifies graduates to work as a paramedic in Australia, with guaranteed clinical placements in the Northern Territory across a range of health care providers. Graduates are ready to work in emergency ambulance and out-of-hospital environments in regional, remote and urban settings. Over the three years, students gain clinical decision-making, problem-solving and critical thinking skills and learn about anatomy and physiology, human development and Australia's health-care systems, developing knowledge in clinical science areas including trauma and emergency response, with a strong focus on First Nations health and mental health.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
This is CDU's APAC-accredited entry point into psychology: the degree that has to exist before an Honours year, before provisional registration, before any of the postgraduate paths toward clinical or organisational psychology. Because that accreditation constrains the curriculum tightly (APAC dictates a lot of the sequencing and content to meet national competency standards), CDU's version looks broadly similar to psych degrees at other Australian universities, but it opens with a Year 1 that explicitly folds in Indigenous protocols and intercultural sensitivity content alongside the usual introduction to psychology and research methods, a reflection of the practicum and research contexts students are likely to work in around Darwin and remote NT communities.

Across the degree, students work through roughly 24 standard subjects covering biological, cognitive, developmental, and social psychology, plus a heavy research methods and statistics load that culminates in an independent research project in third year. Graduates who want to continue toward registration as a psychologist need the Honours year (also APAC-accredited at CDU) or an equivalent postgraduate qualifying program; this bachelor's alone doesn't get you registration, which surprises some students who assume otherwise.

Students can also join the Australian Psychological Society as student members while still completing this degree, which gives earlier access to networking and CPD content than waiting until after graduation.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods and Design, Psychology Ethics, Indigenous protocols and intercultural sensitivity, Biological Bases of Behaviour
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Statistics for Psychology, Personality and Individual Differences
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Advanced Research Methods, independent research project, specialist electives
Pathway: Bachelor of Psychological Science Honours (1 additional year, APAC-accredited) required before provisional psychologist registration
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science Honours
description: The Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours) at Charles Darwin University is an Australian Psychology Accreditation Council accredited fourth-year program designed to equip students with an in-depth understanding of the application of psychological theories to practice and to advance their capacity to design, conduct, interpret and communicate impactful research. It suits high-achieving psychology students who want to distinguish themselves and advance their knowledge of psychological assessment and intervention, and provides in-demand interdisciplinary skills valued by employers in human-centred professions.

name: Bachelor of Public Health
description: The Bachelor of Public Health at Charles Darwin University teaches students how to connect with communities and develop innovative, evidence-based health strategies, with a focus on addressing health disparities experienced by populations and communities at a local, national and global level. The qualification prepares graduates to work in health promotion, policy making, research and disease prevention, and is available online or on campus. Units cover topics such as epidemiology, cultural safety, social media, and global and environmental health, and CDU offers scholarships and international study tours.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
CDU's plain Bachelor of Science is the flexible, build-your-own-major sibling to its more structured Environmental Science degree, and its real drawcard is what's on the university's doorstep: Kakadu, Litchfield, the Timor Sea, and some of the most intact tropical savanna and monsoon ecosystems left in the world. Research project options in the final year regularly draw on this: aquaculture, marine and freshwater ecology, botany, and zoology projects here look genuinely different from equivalent projects at a temperate-climate university, because the field sites and species are different.

Unlike a lot of generalist BSc degrees that are essentially a menu of first-year science subjects with no strong identity, CDU leans into its geography: field intensives take students into Northern and Central Australia and parts of the Asia-Pacific for hands-on data collection, which becomes a differentiator on a CV compared to lab-only science degrees. Students without a settled major can still keep options open through first year before choosing a direction.

It's worth being clear-eyed that CDU is not a large research-intensive science faculty compared to a Go8 university, so students chasing a narrow specialisation in, say, particle physics or advanced biochemistry will find the depth of elective offerings thinner than at a bigger institution. The strength here is specifically in field-based, tropical and environmental science.
curriculum:
Year 1: foundational units across two or more of Biology, Chemistry, Earth Science, Mathematics, Physics
Year 2: discipline deepening in chosen area(s), plus statistics and research design
Year 3: advanced electives and an independent or supervised research project (options include aquaculture, marine ecology, freshwater and terrestrial ecology, botany, zoology)
Field components: optional field intensives in Northern and Central Australia and the Asia-Pacific region
Total: 3 years full-time / 6 years part-time, on campus or online (lab units require on-campus attendance)
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion, ATAR approx 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Science and Technology
description: The Bachelor of Science and Technology at Charles Darwin University is an interdisciplinary degree that lets students tailor their studies across science, engineering and information technology, blending theoretical knowledge with practical, hands-on experience. Students build analytical, technical and problem-solving skills through lab work, collaborative projects and industry-focused learning, applying technology to real challenges alongside experts. Graduates are prepared to collaborate across disciplines, adapt to emerging technologies, and work in careers that drive industry, research and innovation.

name: Bachelor of Science Honours
description: The Bachelor of Science Honours at Charles Darwin University is a one-year course that includes a major research project, advanced-level coursework and research skills training across science disciplines including environmental science, health and clinical science, and information technology. Research areas include biology, ecology, hydrological science, spatial science, analytical chemistry and molecular modelling, exercise and sports science, medical laboratory science, pharmacy, information systems, mobile networking and software development. The honours qualification prepares graduates for professional positions requiring higher-level project management, communication, analysis, problem-solving and research skills, under the guidance of experienced researchers.

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description: The Bachelor of Social Work at Charles Darwin University is a professionally recognised degree that prepares graduates to work as a social worker, using principles of social justice, human rights and cultural safety to promote social change and empowerment through skills in counselling, case management and community development. The course incorporates knowledge from social work, psychology, social policy, research and First Nations Peoples perspectives, and prepares students to work with individuals, families, groups and communities, including those in crisis or affected by poverty and social disadvantage. It includes 20 days of face-to-face intensive classes prior to placements.

name: Bachelor of Software Engineering Honours
description: The Bachelor of Software Engineering Honours at Charles Darwin University develops an understanding of the underlying principles and applications of software engineering along with professional knowledge and skills for the digital world. Students can undertake sought-after industry modules including Cisco and Microsoft certification. Graduates are prepared to move into small and large organisations, consultancy, startups, and government and private companies. The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society at the level of professional practice in ICT and is recognised internationally under the Seoul Accord.

name: Diploma of Alcohol and Other Drugs Practice
Diploma of Arts
description: The Diploma of Arts at Charles Darwin University offers specialist and interdisciplinary thematic knowledge across areas including media studies, literature and creative writing, society and digital culture, Australian Indigenous knowledges, languages, linguistics and culture, interdisciplinary studies, and justice studies, peace and truth-telling. Students develop core communication, critical and creative thinking skills to participate in a multidisciplinary and global workforce. The diploma suits anyone who wants a taste of studying arts and a qualification without committing to a full bachelor's degree, and can lead into a bachelor program.

name: Diploma of Business Studies
description: The Diploma of Business Studies at Charles Darwin University is designed to reflect general business degree objectives and build toward the University's graduate attributes of creative, flexible and socially responsible graduates with skills in communication, leadership and team work. Delivered with UP Education, it parallels the existing first-year business course with the added dimensions of academic English development, increased contact time with staff, and a focus on the linguistic and cultural gaps that many students face in first-year units, providing a supported pathway into a business bachelor degree.

name: Diploma of Counselling
description: The Diploma of Counselling at Charles Darwin University is a first step for people seeking a career in counselling, wanting to increase their qualifications, or with an interest in psychology, social work and counselling. It prepares students with the knowledge and skills required for progression into the Bachelor of Psychological Science. Graduates may work in fields including counsellor, counselling support worker, case worker and case manager.

name: Diploma of Digital Enterprise
description: The Diploma of Digital Enterprise at Charles Darwin University is a flexible one-year qualification that combines business and information technology to prepare students for careers shaped by innovation and rapid digital change. Students develop a foundation in management, marketing, digital product development and data-driven decision-making, alongside core IT capabilities in web development, systems, networking and applications. The course can be tailored with a wide selection of business and IT units and studied online or on campus, and on completion students are eligible to transfer into the Bachelor of Digital Enterprise, Bachelor of Business or an IT bachelor degree.

name: Diploma of Engineering
description: The Diploma of Engineering at Charles Darwin University is ideal for people curious about studying engineering who are unsure about committing to a full undergraduate degree. Students explore general concepts, principles and practices of engineering, develop technical skills and build on their maths and science knowledge. The diploma qualifies students for entry-level engineering roles, or they can continue to CDU's Associate Degree in Engineering, Bachelor of Engineering Science, or Bachelor of Engineering Honours.

name: Diploma of Health Science
description: The Diploma of Health Science at Charles Darwin University equips students with essential skills and knowledge applicable to the Australian health care system, covering health promotion, effective communication and cultural safety in healthcare, with content focused on improving the health and wellbeing of individuals and communities. Graduates are well-prepared for further study, with completed units aligning with higher education pathways in fields such as occupational therapy, public health and nutrition. Graduates may work in health promotion, primary and community health centres, non-government organisations, social services, and project or therapy support roles.

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: The Diploma of Information Technology at Charles Darwin University is designed to reflect general degree objectives and build toward the University's graduate attributes of creative, flexible and socially responsible graduates with skills in communication, leadership and team work. Delivered with UP Education, it parallels the existing first-year IT course with the added dimensions of academic English development, increased contact time with staff, and a focus on the linguistic and cultural gaps that many students face in first-year units, providing a supported pathway into an IT bachelor degree.

name: Diploma of Laws
description: The Diploma of Laws at Charles Darwin University offers a general understanding of the law, legal processes and legal principles, along with the opportunity to gain specialist knowledge needed for work or other reasons. It is also suitable for internationally qualified lawyers who need to complete some Australian subjects to qualify for admission to legal practice in Australia, and is a recognised pathway to the Bachelor of Laws with up to 80 credit points of credit transfer. The course does not lead to professional accreditation, though students can transfer to the accredited Bachelor of Laws.

name: Diploma of Network Engineering
description: The Diploma of Network Engineering at Charles Darwin University prepares students for entry-level network engineering roles by providing the skills and knowledge to design, operate and maintain the networks that underpin the infrastructure of industry and government organisations. Coursework covers key areas including data networks and their implementation, combining academic study with practical experience. The qualification can be used to move into the Bachelor of Information Technology or Bachelor of Software Engineering Honours, and students can undertake sought-after industry modules including Microsoft certification.

name: Diploma of Psychology
description: The Diploma of Psychology at Charles Darwin University is a first step for people considering a career in psychology, wanting to increase their qualifications, or with an interest in the field. It prepares students with the knowledge and skills required for progression into the APAC-approved Bachelor of Psychological Science, though the diploma itself is not APAC-approved. Graduates may be prepared for career opportunities in various psychology-related fields in government, private companies, non-government organisations and community groups, and the course may complement an existing professional career.

name: Diploma of Science
description: The Diploma of Science at Charles Darwin University is ideal for people curious about studying science who are unsure about committing to a degree, or those already working in the sciences who want to upskill in another discipline. Students explore science concepts, theories and principles across fields such as general science, biology, chemistry, environmental science, geographic information science, physics and mathematics, developing logical and critical thinking and problem-solving from a scientific and technological perspective. After completing the diploma, students can move into the Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Environmental Science.

name: Doctor of Pharmacy
description: The Doctor of Pharmacy at Charles Darwin University prepares graduates for entry into the pharmacy profession, where pharmacists have an expanding scope of practice that includes advising prescribers, improving health literacy and access to vaccinations, contributing to the discovery of new medicines, and tailoring medicines to individuals. This graduate-entry, coursework extended master's program is offered both face-to-face and externally, with teaching commencing in an intensive block early in January so that unit prerequisites are met and units are studied in the correct sequence.

name: Graduate Certificate of Arts
description: The Graduate Certificate of Arts at Charles Darwin University is designed to diversify and expand knowledge in cultural and creative spheres, with unit choices across social sciences, Indigenous knowledges and engagement, Indigenous languages and contemporary social issues, Indigenous research practice, and creative arts. Whether consolidating expertise or moving into a new career path, students develop the analytical and critical thinking skills for success, exploring unique perspectives on contemporary issues facing Indigenous Australia, Northern Australia and South-East Asia, guided by lecturers who are leaders in their fields.

name: Graduate Certificate of Business
description: The Graduate Certificate of Business at Charles Darwin University equips professionals with the knowledge and practical skills to navigate today's evolving business landscape, exploring strategic decision-making, leadership, financial literacy and organisational management, and how to drive business success while balancing operational efficiency and stakeholder engagement. It offers a flexible learning experience for those seeking to upskill, pivot careers or lay the foundation for further study, and completion provides a pathway into the Master of Business Administration.

name: Graduate Certificate of Health Services Management
Graduate Certificate of Infectious Disease Prevention and Control
