If you’ve completed a different English test or qualification, you may be able to use it to meet this requirement. Check accepted English tests, qualifications and required scores on our English language requirements page. IELTS Academic (International English Language Testing System) Writing 6 Speaking 6 Reading 6 Listening 6 Overall band score 6

name: Bachelor of Actuarial Science

This course is designed to provide a graduate with a foundation in Actuarial Science, applied statistics and quantitative finance. This could set them on the pathway for a career as an actuary, data scientist, quants trader, or other related fields. Bachelor Degrees prepare students to develop broad and coherent knowledge and skills in a discipline for professional work and further learning corresponding to AQF level 7 qualifications.

name: Bachelor of Advanced Biomedical Sciences (Honours)

name: Bachelor of Agribusiness
description: Curtin University's Bachelor of Agribusiness degree. This course enables students to undertake a combined program of Agribusiness and agricultural science. Students will use chemistry and biology to develop an understanding of production systems and to apply problem-solving techniques to management strategies. Students will be introduced to satellite-based technologies including precision agriculture for crop, pasture and livestock management systems. The course will have a strong focus on broadacre systems in mediterranean and low-rainfall environments of southern Australia, and these will be discussed in the context of global issues such as food security, changing markets, sustainability and climate change. Graduates of this course have a combination of a strong scientific and critical thinking approach and employment-ready skills. This understanding of agricultural production systems is combined with the business skills associated with production, processing, marketing and distribution of food. Students who undertake this course will benefit from gaining a qualification that offers a comprehensive understanding of a primary production system, in combination with a key emphasis on the business environment. The future for the agriculture industry is very attractive and the skills gained in this course are in high demand across agricultural food chain industries. Highly educated, creative people are needed to develop new methods and technologies to produce food sustainably throughout developed and emerging economies. Bachelor Degrees prepare students to develop broad and coherent knowledge and skills in a discipline for professional work and further learning corresponding to AQF level 7 qualifications.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Sciences
description: Curtin University's Bachelor of Biomedical Sciences degree. The Bachelor of Biomedical Sciences (B-BIOMED) is a highly flexible degree that will allow you to tailor your studies and pursue your interest in the biology of human health and disease. In first year, you will complete foundation studies in areas of biomedical science including human biology, genetics, cell biology, microbiology, and immunology. In second and third year, you can major in: Human Biomedicine, the application of biological and physiological principles to clinical practice; Molecular Genetics, in which you will learn about new advances in genetics and genomics, and how these can be applied to improve health outcomes; or Pharmacology, in which you will gain an in-depth understanding of pharmacological principles, essential to the safe and effective development and application of medicines aimed to prevent or treat disease. You may also undertake a second major, or choose one or more specialisations in Human Pathology, Immunology and Cell Biology, Microbiology, Human Genetics and Genomics, and Pharmacology. Additional option units allow you to explore your interest in areas such as Reproductive Technologies, Bioinformatics, Forensics, Psychology, and more. You are also able to complete specialisations in others disciplines such as Corporate Governance, Professional Writing, or Digital and Social Media. The choice is yours! Throughout this course, you will gain valuable hands-on experience in our high-quality laboratories using specialised technology that will prepare you for a variety of careers or further study in clinical health services, biomedical research, or drug discovery and development.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Commerce runs on a build-it-yourself model: a major is a fixed set of eight units, and students choose the first one in their opening semester with guidance from an advisor rather than being locked in at application. A second major can come from the rest of the Commerce list or, less obviously, from the Arts or Creative Arts major lists, which is how a Curtin commerce student ends up graduating with, say, Marketing paired with Screen Arts rather than a strictly business-only transcript.

The final-year capstone is framed around international business exposure specifically, applying entrepreneurial and critical-thinking skills to something closer to a live workplace problem than a standard assessed group project, which reflects Curtin's broader push to make its business degrees read as job-ready to Perth's resources, logistics, and professional services employers rather than purely theoretical.

Given Curtin's business school accreditation (AACSB) and its physical size, one of the largest commerce cohorts in Western Australia, the major combinations available (Accounting, Banking and Finance, Economics, Human Resource Management, International Business, Management, Marketing, among others) are broader than most WA competitors offer inside a single degree.

Year 1: Introductory business units across accounting, economics, and management, first major selection, foundational quantitative unit
Year 2: Core major units (four of eight), second major or minor units, electives
Year 3: Remaining major units, capstone experience (international business focus, applied workplace-style project), electives
Structure: one major minimum (8 units), optional second major from Commerce, Arts, or Creative Arts lists

name: Bachelor of Creative Arts
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Creative Arts narrows the choice to three majors (Fine Art, Screen Arts, or Theatre Arts) rather than the sprawling major list attached to the Bachelor of Arts, which makes it a more deliberately practice-focused degree from day one. Students build a thorough grounding in both the theory and the practice of their chosen discipline, then layer on a specialisation drawn from a different Creative Arts area or effectively any other field they meet the prerequisites for, so a Theatre Arts major might specialise in Screen Arts, or step entirely outside Creative Arts for something like marketing or writing.

The capstone unit is where the degree's practical bent shows most clearly: Fine Art students mount an exhibition, Theatre Arts students stage a performance, Screen Arts students complete a screen project, all functioning as a public-facing portfolio piece rather than a written exam or essay.

Curtin's location gives Screen Arts students in particular a practical edge. Perth's screen production sector has grown considerably with state government screen incentives drawing international productions to WA, and Curtin has leaned into that with industry-facing production units.

Year 2: Core major units, specialisation units (Fine Art, Screen Arts, or Theatre Arts, or another discipline), electives
Year 3: Advanced major units, capstone project (exhibition, performance, or screen project depending on major), remaining electives
Majors offered: Fine Art, Screen Arts, Theatre Arts

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Curtin runs its engineering degree through a common Engineering Foundation Year before anyone commits to a discipline. First-year students cover fundamentals shared across all engineering areas and only choose their major (from Chemical, Petroleum, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mechatronic, Civil and Construction, Metallurgical, Mining, Industrial and Systems, or Environmental Engineering) heading into second year, which gives students who arrive unsure between, say, mechanical and mechatronic engineering a genuine trial period rather than forcing a decision at enrolment.

The major list itself is a tell for what Curtin is known for regionally: Metallurgical, Mining, and Petroleum Engineering majors sit alongside the more universally-offered options, a direct reflection of Perth's position as headquarters city for most of Australia's mining and resources companies, and Curtin's engineering graduates in those majors tend to move directly into WA's resources sector rather than needing to relocate.

Final year is a genuine honours research project done independently within the chosen major, and students can add a four-unit specialisation or minor on top of their major to sharpen the degree toward a specific career direction, pairing Mechanical Engineering with a renewable energy specialisation, for instance.

Year 1: Engineering Foundation Year — common units across all disciplines (engineering mathematics, mechanics, computer-aided design, introductory programming)
Year 2: Major-specific core units (Chemical, Petroleum, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mechatronic, Civil and Construction, Metallurgical, Mining, Industrial and Systems, or Environmental Engineering)
Year 3: Advanced major units, specialisation or minor units (four units), professional practice exposure
Year 4: Honours-level independent research project, remaining advanced major units
Structure: pre-major foundation year, one Engineering major, optional four-unit specialisation or minor

name: Bachelor of Mine and Engineering Surveying
description: The Bachelor of Mine and Engineering Surveying is an industry connected course that ensures that graduates are job ready through a mix of theoretical and practical content. The first 2 years of the Bachelor of Mine and Engineering Surveying are delivered in Bentley with the 3rd year delivered at Curtin University’s W.A. School of Mines campus in Kalgoorlie. Studying in Kalgoorlie in the final year, students receive real-world practical fieldwork experience in working mines in one of the most significant mining regions in Australia. Mine and Engineering Surveying is a specialist area of modern-day surveying. Mine surveyors are responsible for the measurement, representation and management of data associated with a mining operation. The core responsibilities of the mine surveyor include the marking out, measurement and maintenance of direction for all surface and underground workings on a mine site. A mine surveyor is also legally responsible, under government regulations, for the preparation and updating of all mine surveying plans for open pit and underground workings. The engineering surveyor plays a key role in the construction industry to ensure that the locations, in three dimensions, of all civil engineering works are placed in their correct position and orientation. Engineering surveying generally precedes all types of construction associated with roads and bridges, tunnels, buildings, industrial plants and hydraulic engineering. Students study the use of advanced technology and scientific principles to provide practical solutions and services to industry, in land development, construction, mining and mapping.

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description:
Curtin's Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) is APAC-accredited and runs as a combined four-year sequence rather than a standard three-year degree with honours bolted on afterward. The honours stream is embedded as an expected continuation for students who hit the mark, not a separate application most students won't get into. That said, entry to the honours stream itself is competitive: a minimum 70% average across the 14 core second- and third-year psychology units is required, and offers go out by invitation rather than automatic progression.

The APAC accreditation is the whole point structurally: it's what makes graduates eligible for associate membership of the Australian Psychological Society and sets up the standard Australian pathway toward provisional registration and eventual practice, which distinguishes this from a psychological-science degree that stops short of the accredited sequence.

Because the honours year functions as a genuine research year within the four-year structure rather than an optional fifth year, students plan their thesis topic and supervisor arrangements earlier than they would in a bolt-on honours model, and Curtin's psychology school covers a fairly broad research spread from clinical and health psychology through to forensic and organisational applications.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory Psychology (Level One sequence), foundational science or statistics unit, electives
Year 2: Core psychology units (part of the 14-unit core sequence) — social, developmental, biological psychology
Year 3: Remaining core units — cognition, research methods, psychopathology, personality; honours stream invitation based on 70% average across core units
Year 4 (Honours): independent research thesis, advanced seminars
APAC accredited; graduates eligible for APS associate membership

name: Bachelor of Science (Nursing)
description:
Curtin's undergraduate nursing degree runs 840 hours of clinical placement across the course (hospitals, private practices, aged care, rural health settings, and mental health services), which starts as early as second semester of first year, meaning students are shadowing real clinical environments well before most other health degrees would send them out. Placements can involve shift work including night duty and weekends by design, since the point is exposure to how hospitals actually run rather than a sanitised nine-to-five version of nursing.

The course structure leans heavily on simulation before fieldwork: Curtin's simulated practice labs are used to build competency in a controlled setting first, so that clinical placement time is spent applying skills rather than learning them cold in front of a patient. Given Curtin's status as WA's largest nursing school by intake, the simulation infrastructure (mock wards, standardised patients) is a genuine scale advantage over smaller providers.

Students are pushed toward interprofessional learning throughout, working alongside pharmacy, physiotherapy, and medical students in shared units rather than training in a nursing-only bubble, which mirrors how WA Health actually staffs its wards and is meant to make the transition into a graduate nurse year less of a culture shock.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Introduction to Professional Nursing, simulated practice units; clinical placement begins second semester
Year 2: Adult Health Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology for Nursing, interprofessional learning units, clinical placements (hospital and community settings)
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Rural and Remote Health placement option, Aged Care Nursing, capstone clinical placement block, Transition to Professional Practice
Total: 840 hours clinical placement, 216 hours simulated practice across the course; registration pathway with Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia

name: Bachelor of Science (Science)
description:

Mineral Processing and Space and Planetary Science in particular are majors you won't find at most Australian universities, tied respectively to WA's mining sector and Curtin's own astronomy research group (home to some of the country's radio astronomy and remote sensing work).

Students pick at least one science major and can double up, with extension specialisations layered on for those wanting to go deeper into a sub-area without adding a whole second major, plus minors that don't carry first-year prerequisites for students who want breadth without planning it out from day one.

Honours is a genuine one-year add-on rather than an embedded final-year component, which means students finishing the standard three years and wanting a research-track future need to apply separately and typically need a strong average across their major units.

Year 2: Core major units, laboratory or fieldwork components, extension specialisation or minor units
Year 3: Advanced major units, capstone or research-methods unit within major, remaining minor or elective units
Optional Year 4 (Honours): independent research thesis, separate application required, competitive entry

name: Bachelor of Surveying
description: Curtin University offers the only comprehensive surveying degree in Western Australia. Surveying is a highly specialised discipline within Engineering and Science (sometimes called Geomatics Engineering or Geomatics) and is a long-established profession, having played a crucial role in the development of Australia since settlement. Furthermore, the evolution of Australian infrastructure will depend upon the skills that surveyors and spatial scientists provide. Surveyors use advanced technology and scientific principles to provide practical solutions and services to many areas of industry, such as land development, construction, mining and mapping. Surveying will give you the opportunity to work as a Land Surveyor, Cadastral Surveyor, Engineering Surveyor, Mine Surveyor and offers further career opportunities. It includes modern techniques with total stations, levels, satellite positioning (GPS/GNSS), laser scanning, photogrammetry (drone surveying), airborne and marine navigation, digital mapping, satellite and airborne remote sensing, specialised alignment mine and engineering surveying, and geographic information systems (GIS). The research focus of an Honours degree provides a pathway for career advancement. Students are required to complete at least three months' employment in their field during the course of their degree . Additionally, students must hold an approved first aid certificate before graduating. Bachelor Degrees prepare students to develop broad and coherent knowledge and skills in a discipline for professional work and further learning corresponding to AQF level 7 qualifications. The honours component prepares students to develop advanced knowledge and skills for professional work, research and further learning corresponding to AQF level 8 qualifications.

name: Bachelor of Technology (Computer Systems and Networking)
description:
This Bachelor of Technology sits in the more hands-on end of Curtin's ICT offerings: hardware, networking (LANs and WANs specifically), network management, and Internet of Things content, with Python and Linux taught progressively from basics through to advanced application rather than assumed as prior knowledge. It's a more infrastructure-and-systems-focused degree than a standard software-development-flavoured IT degree, aimed at students who want to end up managing networks and infrastructure rather than writing application code full-time.

The course is explicit about industry certification alignment: Cisco and Amazon Web Services certifications are named targets the curriculum is built to prepare graduates for, which matters in a job market where certifications often carry as much weight as the degree title itself for network engineering and cloud infrastructure roles.

The professional practice requirement (minimum 8 weeks, logged formally) pushes students into real workplace exposure before graduation, and Curtin frequently pairs this degree with a Bachelor of Information Technology as a double degree for students who want both the networking depth and the broader IT/software coverage on one transcript.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming (Python), Computer Systems Fundamentals, Networking Fundamentals, Linux Systems Administration (introductory)
Year 2: Network Programming and Distributed Computing, Security Fundamentals, LAN/WAN Design and Management, Linux Systems Administration (advanced)
Year 3: Internet of Things Systems, Network Management and Cloud Infrastructure, professional practice placement (minimum 8 weeks, logged), capstone networking project
Certification alignment: prepares students for industry certifications including Cisco and AWS
admission_requirements: WACE/Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide

description: Curtin University's Doctor of Education degree. The Doctor of Education caters for those educators seeking doctoral level studies with a view to becoming leaders in classroom teaching, curriculum development, educational leadership, school improvement, evaluation or school-based professional development. It will also be useful for educators already occupying positions of leadership in a variety of educational or training organisations, who need to upgrade their qualifications. This course targets educators seeking doctoral level study and will simultaneously provide them with advanced in-depth knowledge related to their profession, and involvement in research work which is closely related to the improvement of their professional practice. The course provides high-level inquiry and research skills for senior education professionals, enabling them to evaluate, commission, design, implement and administer research into different aspects of education provision, and to understand the policy implications of such research. The research focus which underpins the Doctor of Education is closely related to the professional world of the students, with a distinctive orientation towards practical research that contributes to the growth of the profession and the discipline itself.

description: Curtin University's Graduate Certificate in Development Planning degree. This course provides an introduction to the planning principles, practices and techniques used by urban and regional planners. Examples and applications draw on local, national and international examples. It can be seen as a stand-alone qualification in its own right, or as the first step towards the Master of Urban and Regional Planning, which is a full professional qualification. It can also provide mid-career training for practising planners. name: Graduate Diploma in Agriculture and Food Security
description: Curtin University's Master of Science (Agriculture and Food Security) degree. This master program will allow candidates to acquire knowledge and skills for agricultural systems and food security. Candidates will study farming systems and ensuring a secure food supply in Australia and globally. These systems have relevance to mediterranean environments around the world, and to areas where agricultural production is determined by rainfall during the cooler part of the year. The program will cover science and technology for crop, pasture, livestock and food production (including the roles of genetics and management in achieving sustainable production against environmental constraints), and their integration into viable farming systems. Special emphasis is placed on emerging technologies for precise management of crops and livestock, and the role of these technologies in ensuring sustainable and environmentally sound production systems into the future. A research project in an area relevant to agricultural systems or food security is an important component of the program. Master Degrees (Coursework) prepare students to apply advanced knowledge for professional practice, scholarship and further learning corresponding to AQF level 9 qualifications.

name: Master of Computing
description:
Curtin's Master of Computing is built for career-changers rather than CS undergrads looking to specialise further. The entry requirements assume a bachelor's degree plus some demonstrated programming, operating systems, and computing maths background, and the first stretch of the course deliberately re-teaches fundamentals before splitting into the three available majors: Computer Science, Cyber Security, or Artificial Intelligence.

What distinguishes it from a lot of one-size-fits-all computing conversion masters is the credit arrangement for Curtin's own graduates. Someone who already did a Bachelor of Technology or Bachelor of Computing at Curtin can be granted up to a full semester of credit, effectively turning this into an 18-month top-up for internal students while still running as a full two-year program for outsiders.

The major project in the final stage is where the specialisation actually gets tested. Students in the Cyber Security stream, for instance, end up doing something closer to an applied security research piece than a generic capstone, which matters given Perth's growing resources-sector demand for industrial cyber security skills specifically, an angle Curtin leans into given its mining and energy industry connections.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Programming Fundamentals, Computer Systems Fundamentals, Computing Mathematics, Database Systems
Semester 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Networks and Security Fundamentals, major-track foundation unit, elective
Semester 3: Major units (Computer Science, Cyber Security, or Artificial Intelligence stream) x3, elective
Semester 4: Advanced major units, Major Project (capstone, specialisation-specific)
Credit: up to one semester's credit available for Curtin Bachelor of Technology or Bachelor of Computing graduates
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree with demonstrated knowledge/skills in programming, operating systems, and computing mathematics (or equivalent); Master Qualifying Program pathway available for those who don't meet direct entry.

name: Master of Dietetics
description: Curtin University's Master of Dietetics degree. Dietetics involves the study of those medical aspects of disease that have a nutritional component in prevention or treatment. Dietetics is concerned with the science and art of providing nutritional care for patients, clients, communities and populations differing widely in economic, social, psychological and physiological conditions. Dietitians are recognised as a member of interprofessional teams in hospitals, primary health care, private practice, aged care, disability sectors and in the community or public health settings. Dietitians also work in food service and food industry and research teams. Master Degrees (Coursework) prepare students to apply advanced knowledge for professional practice, scholarship and further learning corresponding to AQF level 9 qualifications.

admission_requirements: Prospective applicants to Curtin’s Master of Dietetics need an undergraduate degree that meets Dietitians Australia’s requirements. Dietitians Australia requires that human sciences underpin the application of science in nutrition and dietetic practice. To meet these criteria, 50% of the first year of undergraduate study must be composed of introductory bioscience (examples include chemistry, biology, introductory physiology). Prospective applicants also need to have completed two units of biochemistry, two units of human physiology, and four units of nutrition at second- and third-year level. Eligible applicants must also submit a personal statement. External applicants must arrange for two academic referee reports to be submitted to the Course Coordinator. Eligible applicants will be invited to attend an interview to assess attributes that are considered essential for dietitians, particularly communication skills. Course entry is competitive, and applicants who pass the interview are ranked by course-weighted average. Prospective applicants who have a dietetic qualification that can be considered by the Dietitians Australia for recognition of overseas skills are not eligible for entry into this program. name: Master of Engineering Management
description:
Curtin's Master of Engineering Management is a genuinely fast program: 12 months full-time across three trimesters rather than the standard two years, jointly delivered by the Faculty of Science and Engineering and the Faculty of Business and Law, which shows up directly in the unit split: 125 credits of engineering units (choose five from six options) plus 125 credits of business units (four core plus one elective) plus a 50-credit engineering project capstone.

The business content isn't generic MBA filler bolted onto an engineering degree: strategic management, finance, projects and operations management, and human factors units are chosen specifically because they map onto what an engineer moving into a management or project-lead role actually needs, rather than a broad business-generalist curriculum. That combination is aimed at engineers already in the workforce who want to move from individual-contributor technical roles into managing engineering teams or projects, not new graduates.

Evening class availability is a deliberate accommodation for that same audience: working engineers studying part-time over a minimum 24 months rather than pausing a career for full-time study, which is a genuinely different student profile than most of Curtin's other engineering postgraduate offerings attract.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Engineering units (two of five chosen options), Strategic Management
Trimester 2: Engineering units (remaining chosen options), Finance for Engineers, Projects and Operations Management
Trimester 3: Human Factors in Engineering Management, business elective, Engineering Project (capstone, 50 credits)
Full-time: 12 months across three trimesters; part-time minimum 24 months, two units per trimester; evening classes available
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Environment and Climate Emergency
description: Curtin University's Master of Sustainability and Climate Leadership degree. The Master of Sustainability and Climate Leadership is an advanced practice and research-led degree that explores a transdisciplinary mix of specialist areas, including leadership for systems change, economics for sustainability, climate resilience, circular economy, sustainable development, and net-zero cities and regenerative urban design. Students will build their competence in strategic and systems thinking through analysing international perspectives on policy and practice, while developing their ability to learn and work collaboratively with others towards change. Students will learn to read social, cultural, and ecological systems, interpret complex evidence, and apply place-based approaches. Drawing on these insights, they will learn to design policies and social innovations that shift governance practices, resource flows, and urban environments towards justice, sustainability, and climate resilience. Learning blends immersive field work, studio and lab practice, and sustained partnership projects with industry, government, and community organisations. Graduates will be empowered to lead change towards sustainability and climate action in any environment, with the technical, practical, and collaboration skills to fill diverse professional roles. Master Degrees (Coursework) prepare students to apply advanced knowledge for professional practice, scholarship and further learning corresponding to AQF level 9 qualifications.

name: Master of Nursing Practice
description:
Curtin's Master of Nursing Practice is the graduate-entry pathway into nursing registration for people who already hold a degree in something else. It runs four semesters plus a summer coursework term, condensed but not shortcut, since it still carries 840 hours of professional practice experience and 216 hours of simulated practice, the same clinical hour benchmarks the undergraduate degree runs on, just compressed into two years instead of three.

Because the cohort is graduate-entry, the theory content moves faster than an undergraduate nursing unit would: physical, biological, psychological and social science content is treated as something students can absorb quickly given prior degree-level study skills, with more weight placed on advanced clinical development and interprofessional learning than on foundational science literacy.

Professional practice placements run full-time and include shift and night duty work, mirroring the undergraduate program's approach of exposing students to how wards actually operate rather than easing them in. It's a deliberate design choice given these students will be entering the workforce as registered nurses within two years rather than three, so the placement intensity compensates for the shorter timeline.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice (accelerated), Anatomy and Physiology, Pharmacology, simulated practice units
Semester 2: Adult Health Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, clinical placement block (professional practice hours begin)
Summer term: intensive coursework unit, additional simulated practice
Semester 3: Complex Care Nursing, interprofessional learning unit, clinical placement
Semester 4: Transition to Professional Practice, capstone clinical placement block
Total: 840 hours professional practice, 216 hours simulated practice; leads to eligibility for registration with Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia

name: Master of Occupational Therapy
description: Curtin University's Master of Occupational Therapy degree. The Graduate Entry Master of Occupational Therapy (GEM) course is a fast-track option to becoming an occupational therapist for those who already hold a bachelor degree, preferably in a health science or human service. Assisting people to participate in their diverse daily activities is what occupational therapists call ‘occupation’. Occupation can be as varied as cleaning your tattoo, socialising with friends, driving a car, blow-drying your hair, holding a pen, participating in work and sport and living in supported accommodation. There are many reasons why people cannot participate: such as illness, injury or disability, and these can occur at any age. Occupational therapists work with people, organisations, groups or communities to identify barriers that stop engagement in occupation and then find interventions, strategies and solutions. The barriers can be as diverse as physical, social, attitudinal or legislative, so occupational therapists need a broad education. Master Degrees (Coursework) prepare students to apply advanced knowledge for professional practice, scholarship and further learning corresponding to AQF level 9 qualifications.

name: Master of Professional Engineering
description:
Curtin's Master of Professional Engineering is aimed squarely at Engineers Australia Stage 1 competency accreditation: students graduate meeting the academic benchmark for professional engineer status, with a formal logbook requirement tracking at least 12 weeks of professional practice exposure alongside the coursework, which is a heavier practical documentation burden than a typical taught masters carries.

Major choice spans Chemical, Civil, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mining, Petroleum, and Software Engineering. The Mining and Petroleum options in particular reflect Curtin's position as the go-to engineering school for Western Australia's resources sector, with a research and industry-partnership base (WA School of Mines heritage feeds into some of this) that eastern-states universities generally can't match for those two majors specifically.

The final-year major research or design project is meant to genuinely integrate everything from the coursework rather than function as an add-on. Students draw on both the technical major content and a research methodology grounding, working alongside academic researchers rather than purely on an industry-sponsored brief, though industry-linked projects are common given Curtin's mining and energy sector ties.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics and Modelling, major-specific core units (Chemical, Civil, Electrical and Electronic, Mechanical, Mining, Petroleum, or Software), Research Methods, professional practice logbook commencement
Year 2: Advanced major units, engineering management or industry-context unit, Major Research or Design Project (capstone), completion of 12 weeks professional practice exposure
Accreditation: meets Engineers Australia Stage 1 competency requirements, subject to accreditation

name: Master of Psychology (Professional)
description:
Curtin's Master of Psychology (Professional) is a genuinely compressed program: one year full-time, integrating coursework, a research project, and supervised practical placements all within twelve months, which is unusually fast for a professional psychology masters and reflects Curtin's design choice to front-load the experiential placement work rather than spread it across a longer program. Part-time enrolment exists but is limited and offered mainly on equity grounds rather than as a standard option.

The placement component is where the degree earns its "professional" label specifically: students are taught and then supervised administering psychological assessments, conducting mental status examinations, and applying counselling skills in real placement settings, not just discussing these skills in seminar. That hands-on structure is what leads toward the practical competencies assessed in the National Psychology Examination.

Graduates who pass the National Psychology Examination become eligible for registration with the Psychology Board of Australia, making this one of the more direct routes from an accredited undergraduate psychology sequence into registered practice, compressed into a single intensive year rather than the two-year professional masters some other universities require.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Advanced Psychological Assessment, Psychopathology and Diagnosis, Counselling Skills, placement orientation and commencement
Semester 2: Research Project (professional application focus), supervised clinical placement (assessment and counselling practice), Ethics and Professional Practice in Psychology
Throughout: integrated placement hours across both semesters combining assessment, mental status examination, and counselling skill application
Outcome: eligibility to sit the National Psychology Examination and apply for registration with the Psychology Board of Australia
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in psychology or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

The Master of Sustainability and Climate Leadership is an advanced practice and research-led degree that explores a transdisciplinary mix of specialist areas, including leadership for systems change, economics for sustainability, climate resilience, circular economy, sustainable development, and net-zero cities and regenerative urban design. Students will build their competence in strategic and systems thinking through analysing international perspectives on policy and practice, while developing their ability to learn and work collaboratively with others towards change. Students will learn to read social, cultural, and ecological systems, interpret complex evidence, and apply place-based approaches. Drawing on these insights, they will learn to design policies and social innovations that shift governance practices, resource flows, and urban environments towards justice, sustainability, and climate resilience. Learning blends immersive field work, studio and lab practice, and sustained partnership projects with industry, government, and community organisations. Graduates will be empowered to lead change towards sustainability and climate action in any environment, with the technical, practical, and collaboration skills to fill diverse professional roles. Master Degrees (Coursework) prepare students to apply advanced knowledge for professional practice, scholarship and further learning corresponding to AQF level 9 qualifications.

name: Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence
description: The Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence at Deakin University equips students with the knowledge and skills to design, develop and evolve computational solutions that harness the latest advances in artificial intelligence. Students get hands-on experience building intelligent AI-driven software solutions that extend beyond software to systems and products, supported by academics who are leaders in this emerging field. Deakin's research in AI feeds directly into the curriculum. Graduates work as AI developers, machine learning engineers and data specialists across industry and research.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
Deakin's Bachelor of Arts is a genuinely flexible humanities degree: students pick two majors from a list spanning literature, history, politics, sociology, creative writing, and languages, rather than being funnelled into one fixed track, and the same degree structure runs across Burwood, Geelong and Cloud Campus online delivery. It's less a single defined program than a framework, which suits students who aren't sure yet which humanities discipline they want to specialise in.

A recurring theme in Deakin's arts teaching is linking coursework to employability early: most majors include at least one unit built around a real-world writing, research or communication project rather than purely essay-based assessment, and Deakin's careers-focused STP-coded employability units are compulsory across its degrees, arts included. Students can also add a diploma of languages or a study-abroad trimester without extending the degree, which is a genuine structural option rather than an add-on marketing line.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory units in two chosen majors (e.g. History, Literature, Politics, Sociology, Creative Writing); Academic and Career skills unit
Year 2: Major subjects continue (2 per major); Elective from a third discipline
Year 3: Advanced major subjects; capstone or research project unit in at least one major; remaining electives
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science at Deakin University develops a comprehensive understanding of human biology, giving students the expertise and practical skills to contribute to disease diagnosis and treatment across molecular, cellular and systems levels. Students become proficient in the biological sciences and disease mechanisms, and tailor their degree by choosing from a range of majors to specialise in an area of interest. Graduates work in medical research, laboratory science, pathology, and roles across the health and biotechnology sectors, or progress to postgraduate study in medicine and allied health.

name: Bachelor of Business (Sport Management)
description: The Bachelor of Business at Deakin University, redesigned for 2027, is for students who want to lead people, manage projects and develop creative solutions, with the option to focus on sport management. Students build adaptable skills in leadership, project work, entrepreneurship, marketing and people management, and a strong foundation in digital information, financial literacy, economics and management. The course tackles modern business challenges so students graduate ready for changing workforces. Graduates work across management, marketing, operations and the sport industry.

name: Bachelor of Business Analytics
description: The Bachelor of Business Analytics at Deakin University, the longest-running specialised business analytics course in the state of Victoria, teaches students how to turn raw data into meaningful evidence to guide decisions. Students build skills in data visualisation, business intelligence, artificial intelligence for business and predictive analytics while working on real projects with industry-standard tools. As part of at least 80 hours of practical experience, students apply these skills through work-integrated learning. Graduates work as business analysts, data analysts and insight specialists across industries.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
Deakin Business School holds triple accreditation (AACSB, EQUIS and AMBA), a status only a small number of business schools worldwide carry, and the Bachelor of Commerce is the school's broad flagship undergraduate degree: students choose from majors including accounting, finance, marketing, management, human resource management and business analytics, or combine more than one. It's offered at Burwood, Geelong Waurn Ponds, and online through Deakin's Cloud Campus, with the same majors generally available across delivery modes.

A distinguishing feature is Deakin's Work Integrated Learning unit requirement, which most commerce majors satisfy through an internship, consulting project with an external organisation, or a simulated business challenge rather than pure coursework. The university markets this heavily as differentiating its commerce graduates from those of pure-theory programs. Students with the accounting major who complete the right unit combination are also eligible for accreditation pathways with CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Principles; Economic Principles; Marketing Principles; Quantitative Methods for Business
Year 2: Business Law; Organisational Behaviour; core major subjects begin (1–2 units per major)
Year 3: Major subjects continue (3–4 units); Work Integrated Learning unit (internship, consulting project or business challenge)
Final trimester: Capstone major subject; remaining electives or second major units
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Communication (Public Relations)
description: The Bachelor of Communication at Deakin University teaches students how to craft content that resonates with audiences across print, digital, audio and video platforms, with the option to major in public relations. Whether breaking a news story, writing a press release, creating a national campaign or running a high-profile event, students learn to create persuasive messages that inspire action. The degree develops specialised industry skills through majors including advertising, digital media, journalism and public relations. Graduates work in communication, media, campaigns and events roles across sectors.

name: Bachelor of Communication and Creative Arts (Honours)
Bachelor of Computer Science
description: Deakin University Bachelor of Computer Science requires 24 credit points across eight units, taken as one major plus two electives, one minor plus four electives, or two minors. Major sequences include Computational Mathematics, Data Science covering data mining, machine learning, deep learning, software architecture and scalability, natural language processing and artificial intelligence, and Internet of Things covering data capture, embedded systems, data mining and machine learning. The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society and recognised internationally through the Seoul Accord, and includes a compulsory work placement with an approved host organisation. Applicants who do not meet the standard academic requirements may use the STAT test or be considered on work and life experience. Indicative international tuition is around A$43,600 per year. Graduates enter software, data and systems roles and can progress into project management.

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description:
Deakin's criminology program, taught mainly out of the Geelong Waurn Ponds and online cohorts within the School of Humanities and Social Sciences, has built a reputation partly around Australian-context research into policing, youth justice and cybercrime rather than importing a US-textbook criminology curriculum wholesale. Students move from foundational theories of crime and justice into applied units on policing, corrections, and increasingly cybercrime and digital forensics, an area Deakin has invested in given its parallel strength in cyber security.

The degree is commonly combined with a second degree: Deakin offers formal double-degree pairings with Criminology plus Laws, Psychological Science, or Cyber Security, which is a genuine structural feature rather than marketing, since students in those combined degrees take a blended unit set rather than simply two separate degrees end to end. A work placement or research project unit toward the end of the single degree lets students test interests in policing, youth services, or policy work before graduating.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Criminology; Crime, Justice and Society; Understanding Deviance; Introduction to Law
Year 2: Policing and Society; Youth and Crime; Research Methods for Criminology; Elective
Year 3: Corrections and Community Justice; Cybercrime and Digital Investigation; Criminal Justice Policy; Work placement or research project unit
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Cyber Security
description:
Deakin's cyber security degree runs out of its Centre for Cyber Security Research and Innovation, and the course structure reflects that research base: units on computer crime and digital forensics sit alongside more conventional network security content, and the degree can be paired as a double degree with Criminology or Laws for students aiming at policy, investigative or legal cyber roles rather than purely technical ones. That double-degree option is a genuinely distinctive structural feature compared with a standalone technical cyber security degree.

The standard single degree runs 24 credit points over three years full-time, split across foundational computing units, core security subjects, and later electives that let students lean toward penetration testing/technical security or governance and forensics. Deakin has also run national cyber security competitions and industry partnerships that regularly feed into student projects, giving students exposure to real incident-response style scenarios rather than only textbook case studies.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals; Networking Fundamentals; Introduction to Cyber Security; Systems Analysis
Year 2: Network Security; Digital Forensics; Cryptography; Elective
Year 3: Penetration Testing and Ethical Hacking; Security Governance and Risk; Cybercrime Investigation; Capstone Security Project
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Data Science
description: The Bachelor of Data Science at Deakin University explores the full lifecycle of data, from collection and storage to analysis and communication. Through more than 120 hours of hands-on placement with clients such as Singapore Airlines, ANZ and Barwon Water, students learn how data is used to generate insights and inform strategic decisions. The course content reflects current industry practice in a fast-growing field. Graduates work as data scientists, data analysts and machine learning practitioners across business, government and technology.

name: Bachelor of Design (Architecture)
description: The Bachelor of Design at Deakin University helps students harness creativity to solve complex problems and influence the world around them, with the option to focus on architecture. Students learn design-thinking tools used widely across industry, such as journey mapping, empathy maps and visualisation, and work with industry-standard tools in dedicated design facilities. By second year, students' work meets industry standards, giving them an understanding of professional practice, and they can major in communication design or interactive and UX design. Graduates work across design studios, agencies and in-house creative teams.

name: Bachelor of Digital Marketing and Advertising
description: The Bachelor of Digital Marketing and Advertising at Deakin University is the only degree of its kind offered by an Australian university. Students explore the full spectrum of brand communication where data, consumer relationships, creativity and technology meet, studying consumer psychology and business analytics while building advertising craft from copywriting and art direction to social media content and brand campaigns. Students learn to turn audience insights into creative brand stories that influence behaviour. Graduates work in digital marketing, advertising, brand and content roles.

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood and Primary Education
Bachelor of Early Childhood Education
description: The Bachelor of Early Childhood Education at Deakin University prepares students to become confident, capable educators of young children. Deakin is the only university to embed the Berry Street Education Model into its initial teaching degrees, so students graduate with practical skills to apply trauma-informed strategies that support every learner. Students also learn how to create safe, healthy and engaging learning environments while building positive classroom relationships, supported by placements. Graduates work as early childhood teachers in kindergartens, preschools and the early years of primary school.

name: Bachelor of Electrical and Electronics Engineering (Honours)
Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Deakin's engineering degree is taught almost entirely out of Waurn Ponds in Geelong, a campus purpose-built around applied engineering and manufacturing research. The adjacent Carbon Nexus facility, one of the few pilot-scale carbon fibre production lines in the world outside Japan and Germany, gives the mechanical and materials-leaning specialisations a genuine industry-research flavour that's hard to find elsewhere in Australia. Students choose a specialisation (civil, environmental, electrical, renewable energy, mechanical, or mechatronics) partway through the course.

The degree is accredited by Engineers Australia and includes compulsory professional practice units around safety and project-based learning from first year, plus a substantial industry-based capstone project in the final year. Deakin also runs a parallel Bachelor of Engineering (Industry) (Honours) with built-in paid industry placements for students who want workplace experience baked into the structure rather than left to a single work-integrated-learning unit.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics; Introduction to Engineering Practice; Mechanics; Materials Science; Safety and Project-Oriented Learning
Year 2: Thermodynamics; Circuits and Systems; specialisation-track subjects begin (Civil / Electrical / Mechanical / Mechatronics / Renewable Energy / Environmental)
Year 3: Advanced specialisation subjects; Engineering Management; Elective
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Project (industry-based); remaining specialisation subjects; professional practice unit
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion with strong mathematics; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Environmental Science and Sustainability
description: The Bachelor of Environmental Science and Sustainability at Deakin University explores ways to manage the interaction between people and the environment. Combining the latest research with extensive application of skills in professional, community, lab and field settings, students devise and implement innovative solutions to protect natural resources in local and global contexts. Fieldwork is a core part of the course, and students explore the role of science and society in achieving global sustainability. Graduates work in environmental management, conservation, sustainability and policy roles across government, industry and consulting.

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description: The Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science at Deakin University is a professionally recognised degree that provides a pathway to accreditation with Exercise and Sports Science Australia as an Accredited Exercise Scientist. Students build a strong foundation in the physiological, anatomical and behavioural principles of exercise and sport, and learn how these are applied across health, performance and participation. Hands-on experience takes place in specialist facilities including a climate chamber. Graduates work in strength and conditioning, sports performance, health and community fitness, and progress to clinical exercise physiology study.

name: Bachelor of Film, Television and Animation
description: The Bachelor of Film, Television and Animation at Deakin University helps students find their creative voice in a supportive, collaborative environment. Mentored by academics, students work on live-action, virtual production and animated films across narrative, documentary and episodic genres, learn emerging technologies, and develop cross-disciplinary critical and technical skills to work across multiple roles. Graduates work in screen production, animation, post-production and content creation across the film, television and digital media industries.

name: Bachelor of Fine Arts
description: The Bachelor of Fine Arts at Deakin University supports students to develop their creative practice under the guidance of experienced industry professionals. Students major in dance, photography, theatre, visual arts or writing, immerse themselves in their practice, and develop critical skills to become agile, versatile creatives. The degree can be personalised further with minors in complementary areas such as scriptwriting, theatre production and Indigenous studies. Graduates pursue practice, production and teaching roles across the creative and cultural industries.

name: Bachelor of Forensic Science (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Forensic Science at Deakin University is professionally accredited and exposes students to the full scope of modern forensic science, from simulated crime scenes to courtroom presentations. With a strong focus on practical training, students graduate with the skills to examine, interpret and present forensic evidence, and gain hands-on experience in a purpose-built crime scene training facility. The course covers disciplines including illicit drugs analysis and DNA analysis. Graduates work in forensic laboratories, police and government agencies, and related scientific roles.

name: Bachelor of Health and Medical Science (Honours)
Bachelor of Health and Physical Education
description: The Bachelor of Health and Physical Education at Deakin University develops the critical skills, specialised knowledge and practical classroom experience needed to become a secondary health and physical education teacher. Students access industry-standard equipment and facilities, including an Elite Sports Precinct, and explore the art of movement, specialist teaching methods, applied sports science, biomechanics and motor learning. Supervised school placements build classroom readiness. Graduates are qualified to teach health and physical education in secondary schools.

name: Bachelor of Health Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Health Sciences at Deakin University builds a strong foundation in health while letting students tailor their degree through at least two of 13 majors, with the option to take up to three majors or combine with electives. In Australia, over half a million new jobs are projected in the healthcare and social assistance sector over the next decade, creating strong demand for graduates. This flexible approach allows students to develop expertise across areas such as health promotion, physical activity, disability and family health. Graduates work across health promotion, community health, policy and program roles.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description: Deakin University Bachelor of Information Technology gives students the skills to launch an IT career while building specialist depth in a chosen area such as programming, networking, cyber security, cloud applications, entrepreneurship or user-centred design. Students complete nine units, taken as one major of six units plus three electives, one minor plus five electives, or two minors plus one elective; core units cover data science and artificial intelligence, responsive web apps, cyber security, software engineering and user-centred design. Entry needs a minimum ATAR of 50 plus the English requirement, with Trimester 1 in March and Trimester 2 in July intakes, and a Deakin College diploma pathway gives direct entry into second year. Indicative international tuition is around A$43,600 per year. Graduates work as network and IT security officers, programmers, database and web designers, analysts and consultants across health, education, finance, government, mining and agriculture.

name: Bachelor of International Studies
description:
International Studies at Deakin is built around a compulsory in-country component: students typically undertake a study period abroad or an international internship as part of the degree, not as an optional add-on, which reflects the university's positioning of the course as preparation for careers in diplomacy, international development, trade, or global business rather than as a generalist arts degree with an international flavour. Deakin has long-standing exchange partnerships across Asia, Europe and the Americas that this degree draws on directly.

Coursework blends international relations and global politics with a language stream (options have included Indonesian, Chinese, French, Spanish and others) and area-studies electives, and a research or professional placement unit toward the end lets students apply the language and policy background to something practical, typically a placement with an NGO, government department, or company with international operations.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to International Relations; Global Politics; Language stream unit 1; Global Issues
Year 2: International Political Economy; Comparative Politics; Language stream unit 2; Area Studies elective
Year 3: Study abroad trimester or international internship; Language stream unit 3; International Studies research project
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Laws
description: The Bachelor of Laws at Deakin University is delivered by one of the top three law schools in the state of Victoria, designed and taught by leading academics and practising lawyers. The degree builds strong academic foundations in law alongside vital skills in communication, problem solving and analytical thinking, with multiple opportunities for work-integrated learning in professional or international settings. An extensive list of law electives spans commercial, criminal, international and other areas. Graduates progress to practical legal training and careers as lawyers, and into government, business and policy roles.

name: Bachelor of Marine Science
description: The Bachelor of Marine Science at Deakin University is the state of Victoria's only dedicated marine science degree, with access to spectacular marine environments rich in biodiversity. Students become experts in ocean systems by exploring marine biology and ecology, oceanography, marine mapping, conservation, aquaculture, fisheries, and marine and coastal management. The course runs across two coastal campuses and equips students with the skills to create a sustainable future for the world's oceans. Graduates work in marine research, conservation, fisheries, aquaculture and coastal management.

name: Bachelor of Medical Imaging
description: The Bachelor of Medical Imaging at Deakin University prepares students for one of the strongest growth areas in the health sector. Students develop clinical skills in imaging modalities including general radiography and advanced techniques such as computed tomography, interventional imaging and magnetic resonance imaging. Deakin is the only Victorian university where clinical placements begin in the first semester and continue every semester across metropolitan, rural and regional settings. Graduates work as radiographers and medical imaging technologists in hospitals and imaging clinics.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Deakin runs nursing across multiple Victorian campuses (Burwood, Geelong Waurn Ponds, and previously Warrnambool) and puts real weight behind simulation-based learning before students ever hit a ward. Its clinical simulation labs are built to mirror real hospital environments, which the university uses to front-load confidence before the roughly 800+ hours of clinical placement required for national accreditation. The course is accredited by ANMAC and the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, with graduates eligible for RN registration.

The curriculum runs from bioscience and health assessment fundamentals into progressively more complex clinical subjects (medical-surgical nursing, mental health, aged care, and community nursing), with a placement block attached to nearly every trimester rather than one concentrated block, so students are in real clinical settings from relatively early in the course rather than only in their final year.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology; Foundations of Nursing Practice; Health Assessment; Pharmacology 1; clinical placement
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing 1 and 2; Mental Health Nursing; Pharmacology 2; clinical placement blocks
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing; Aged Care and Chronic Illness; Community and Primary Health Nursing; Transition to Professional Practice; extended clinical placement
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Nutrition Science (Dietetics Pathway)
description: The Bachelor of Nutrition Science at Deakin University is taught at a leading Australian university for nutrition research, with a dietetics pathway option for students planning postgraduate dietetics study. Students help tackle challenges from disease prevention and lifespan nutrition to sustainability, misinformation and the psychological and social impacts of food. Food preparation, analysis and sensory labs modelled on commercial laboratories provide hands-on experience, and students complete at least 75 hours of industry placement. Graduates work in public health nutrition, food industry, community health and research, or continue to dietetics study.

name: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy
description: The Bachelor of Occupational Therapy at Deakin University is accredited and develops the skills to support people to live more independently. Students learn to assess people's strengths and limitations, identify environmental and social barriers, and design personalised, evidence-based interventions that enable participation in meaningful activities across all stages of life. Learning from expert educators and working alongside other disciplines builds capability as part of an interdisciplinary team, with practice education embedded in every year. Graduates work as occupational therapists across hospitals, community health, rehabilitation, disability and aged care.

name: Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics
description: The Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics at Deakin University teaches how power, ethics, sustainability and economics converge to shape our lives. Built by leading academics and researchers, the course is designed for deep and creative thinkers who want to make an impact on society. Students learn the nature of public decision making, explore resource management issues, and gain the skills to analyse business problems in line with social justice, balancing a big-picture view of public problems with analytical skills. Graduates work in policy, government, research, advocacy, consulting and business.

name: Bachelor of Property and Real Estate
description: The Bachelor of Property and Real Estate at Deakin University is an accredited degree that develops the practical skills employers look for, preparing students for property roles in valuation, development and investment. Students gain a strong foundation in property valuation, development, finance and law while learning how market cycles, demographic trends and sustainability shape property decisions, with the ability to tailor study toward commercial or residential property and sustainable construction. Through more than 80 hours of work-integrated learning students gain industry experience. Graduates work as valuers, property analysts, developers and asset managers.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
Deakin's Bachelor of Psychological Science is APAC-accredited, which matters because it's the first step of the standard Australian pathway into registration as a psychologist: students who want to go further typically follow it with Deakin's own fourth-year honours and then a master's or provisional registration pathway, and Deakin markets the degree explicitly around that multi-year trajectory rather than as a terminal qualification.

The course covers the core content APAC requires (biological bases of behaviour, cognition, social psychology, developmental psychology, research methods and statistics) with a heavier-than-average statistics and research methods load in the final year, reflecting the discipline's accreditation requirements. Deakin also runs the degree online through its Cloud Campus alongside on-campus delivery at Burwood and Geelong, which is less common for a laboratory/research-methods-heavy science degree and requires the university to run virtual practical and statistics tutorials at scale.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology; Biological Psychology; Research Methods 1; Lifespan Development
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology; Social Psychology; Research Methods and Statistics 2; Personality and Individual Differences
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology; Research Methods and Statistics 3; Psychological Assessment; Advanced elective and research project unit
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Public Health and Health Promotion
description: The Bachelor of Public Health and Health Promotion at Deakin University builds the expertise to address the causes of poor health and improve wellbeing, combining community engagement, practice, policy development, epidemiology, research, education and communication. Practical learning is a core component: students complete at least 200 hours of practical experience, including a 120-hour placement in a health-related agency in their final year, applying their knowledge in professional settings. Graduates work in health promotion, prevention, policy and program roles across government and non-government organisations.

name: Bachelor of Science (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Science at Deakin University is designed for curious minds who want to explore diverse scientific disciplines and tailor their studies to their strengths and career goals. In the first year students build a strong foundation across key scientific fields before progressing into a specialised major, and develop transferable skills including critical thinking, problem solving, data analysis, teamwork and professional communication. Hands-on laboratory and field experience is a core part of the degree. Graduates work in research, laboratory, analytical and technical roles across science, industry and government.

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description: The Bachelor of Social Work at Deakin University is fully accredited and equips students to support individuals, families and communities through an understanding of policy, socioeconomic factors and social equity issues. Students develop the skills to address the underlying causes of inequality and contribute to lasting social change, learning contemporary approaches through student-centred teaching. Students undertake 1000 hours of supervised practice education across a range of community and professional settings. Graduates work in child protection, health, mental health, community development and policy, and are eligible for membership of the Australian Association of Social Workers.

name: Bachelor of Sport Development
description: The Bachelor of Sport Development at Deakin University teaches students how to grow participation, design programs and support safe, inclusive sport in schools, clubs and community organisations. Students build expertise in sport systems and pathways, coaching, and contemporary health and community development, developing the skills to create positive sporting experiences and strengthen communities through sport. A range of electives and practical placements with organisations such as Netball Victoria provide industry experience. Graduates work in sport development, participation, program and community roles across sporting bodies, clubs and government.

name: Bachelor of Zoology and Animal Science
description: The Bachelor of Zoology and Animal Science at Deakin University explores the social and economic impacts of human activity on animals and their ecosystems. Students investigate how animals respond and adapt to changes in climate and the environment, and apply the latest research techniques to test hypotheses in real-world settings, developing evidence-based decision-making skills valued by industry. Students work with live animals in the lab and field, gaining first-hand insight into animal form and function. Graduates work in wildlife and conservation, animal management, research and environmental roles.

name: Graduate Certificate of Business
description: The Graduate Certificate of Business at Deakin University is a flexible half-year postgraduate course designed for graduates from any discipline who want to build core business capability. Students explore strategy, finance, marketing, business technology, innovation and entrepreneurship, gaining insight into how organisations operate, adapt to change and grow. Learning is shaped by industry input, so theory is connected with real-world business challenges. The course can be taken as a standalone qualification or used as a pathway into Deakin's Master of Business and related masters degrees. Graduates use it to move into management roles or to change career direction.

name: Graduate Certificate of Business Analytics
description: The Graduate Certificate of Business Analytics at Deakin University is a half-year postgraduate course for professionals who want to develop practical analytics capability and open new career opportunities. Students build skills in data analysis, visualisation and evidence-based decision making, learning from industry-experienced academics. Through industry-shaped learning, students apply analytics tools to real datasets and business problems. The course provides a pathway into the Master of Business Analytics for those who continue their study. Graduates work in analyst and insight roles across marketing, finance, operations and consulting, helping organisations make confident, data-driven decisions.

name: Graduate Certificate of Communication
description: The Graduate Certificate of Communication at Deakin University is a half-year postgraduate course that helps professionals build the strategic communication and critical thinking skills needed to grow their career in the media and communication industry. Designed for people stepping into postgraduate study, it lets students tailor their learning to their goals through units in areas such as writing news, brand storytelling, public relations, media law and design strategy. It offers a flexible, supported study experience and a pathway into the Graduate Diploma and Master of Communication. Graduates work in public relations, content, journalism, marketing communication and corporate communication roles.

name: Graduate Certificate of Fine Arts
description: The Graduate Certificate of Fine Arts at Deakin University is a half-year postgraduate course that builds on undergraduate study to explore contemporary approaches to creativity. Students refine their practice through practical learning and collaboration while developing transferable skills such as imaginative thinking, problem solving and leadership. They learn alongside people from a range of backgrounds in a supportive environment, and complete electives that deepen existing strengths or build capability in a new area. Learning takes place in professional-standard creative facilities, including studios for visual arts, photography, dance, drama and design. Graduates pursue careers and further study across the creative industries.

name: Graduate Certificate of Health and Medical Research
Graduate Certificate of Information Systems
description: The Graduate Certificate of Information Systems at Deakin University is a half-year postgraduate course that develops skills in the design, evaluation and improvement of the information systems organisations depend on. Students build in-demand capability in business analysis, data management, digital innovation and IT-enabled change, guided by experts and working with current tools and practical case scenarios. The course is shaped by industry input and offers a pathway into the Master of Information Systems. Graduates work as business analysts, systems analysts and consultants, helping organisations use technology to improve decisions, operations and customer experience.

name: Graduate Certificate of Information Technology
description: The Graduate Certificate of Information Technology at Deakin University is a half-year postgraduate course developed in consultation with industry. Students gain essential, industry-relevant IT skills spanning software design and engineering, information retrieval and web development, and explore the critical role information technologies play in everyday business operations. The course suits students without a computing background as well as those who want to add a recognised academic qualification to their industry experience. It provides a pathway into the Master of Information Technology. Graduates move into IT support, development, systems and analyst roles across sectors.

name: Graduate Certificate of Professional Accounting
description: The Graduate Certificate of Professional Accounting at Deakin University is a half-year postgraduate course that builds accounting foundations and the skills to help inform business decision making. Students learn core accounting principles in areas such as financial reporting, management accounting, finance and business law, taught by industry-experienced academics. A flexible choice of units lets students align study to their background and goals, and the course provides a pathway into the Master of Professional Accounting for those seeking a professional accounting qualification. Graduates work in accounting, finance and analysis roles across a wide range of organisations.

name: Graduate Certificate of Writing and Literature
description: The Graduate Certificate of Writing and Literature at Deakin University is a half-year postgraduate course for aspiring authors and professionals who want to sharpen their voice. Students explore creative writing, professional writing, publishing and literary study while building their own writing practice.
