name: Graduate Diploma in Geospatial Information Systems
description: The only Geospatial Information Systems postgraduate courses in South Australia. The postgraduate program for Geospatial Information Systems (GIS) is the only GIS stream available in South Australia. Blending the disciplines of science, computer science, data analytics, geography and cartography, GIS is a fascinating and powerful area of study which allows you to impact the world around you - from using drones to survey and photograph potential areas for environmental conservation, using location intelligence and data to address racial inequities, to helping plan our future cities and genuinely improve lives. The program provides a theoretical and practical framework for graduates from a range of backgrounds, as well as those from the public sector and non-government organisations wishing to extend their choice of career path by acquiring knowledge and skills in the capture, analysis and communication of spatially referenced information. You will develop and implement GIS skills and knowledge applicable to a range of areas, such as environmental management, urban and regional planning, human geography and environmental health, land-use dynamics, natural resources management, ecosystem services, biological sciences and archaeology. Students completing the Master of Geospatial Information Systems will be able to undertake research and analysis using spatially-referenced data and prepare research reports. This course is delivered by Flinders University.
curriculum: You can select from a range of geospatial topics to build a study program that suits your interests and current or future employment requirements. The program is specifically designed to provide flexibility to students with different levels of GIS and remote sensing experience and skills. Specifically, the program allows students who have already completed undergraduate introductory topics in GIS.

The focus on Flinders University's strengths in the design, implementation and management of enterprise information technology and the application of information technology to information retrieval, analysis and visualisation characterise this program. The courses integrate with the strong and active research and development program in the College of Science and Engineering, carried out as externally funded research and development.

You will graduate with outstanding critical skills, public speaking skills, the ability to solve numerous challenges and understand the relationship between theory and practice. description: The Graduate Diploma in Maritime Archaeology at Flinders University is a one-year full-time program, described by the university as the leading named degree of its kind in Australia. Students learn practical maritime and underwater archaeology skills in the classroom and through field schools led by internationally recognised experts, working with digital technology including 3D recording, marine geophysics and conservation across topics from historic shipwrecks to submerged landscapes. Graduates work in maritime heritage, cultural resource management and research. Indicative international tuition is around 34,200 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 046437B.

name: Graduate Diploma in Media and Communication
description: The Graduate Diploma in Media and Communication at Flinders University is a one-year full-time program that develops the skills to work in a fast-changing digital communication field. Students learn the intricacies of digital communication and examine how disruptive technologies such as artificial intelligence are reshaping media, and can continue into the Master of Media and Communication. Graduates work in communications, content, journalism and digital media roles. Indicative international tuition is around 34,200 Australian dollars per year. name: Graduate Diploma in Nursing (Acute Care)
description: The Graduate Diploma in Nursing (Acute Care) at Flinders University is a one-year full-time program for registered nurses who want to build advanced skills in caring for acutely and critically ill patients. It covers nursing across environments including emergency, intensive care and paediatric settings, and sits within an articulated set of postgraduate nursing qualifications leading to the Master of Nursing. Graduates take on advanced clinical roles in acute care. Indicative international tuition is around 34,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 113748E.

name: Graduate Diploma in Palliative Care
description: The Graduate Diploma in Palliative and End-of-Life Care at Flinders University is a one-year full-time program that develops the knowledge and skills to support individuals and families through complex, compassionate care across health and community settings. Taught by a group with a long record in palliative care education, the course covers symptom management, communication, grief and loss, and coordinated care. Students complete eight topics and can progress into the Master of Palliative and End-of-Life Care, which prepares graduates for leadership roles. Graduates work across hospitals, hospices and community health services. Indicative international tuition is around 37,500 Australian dollars per year.

You will also learn to coordinate programs and portfolios, lead complex projects, and manage procurement and contracts throughout the project lifecycle. The course is structured around a trimester model, with topics delivered across three study periods. The course provides an alternative to Honours in Psychology. It covers links between knowledge, theory, research, and psychological practice, with an emphasis on how psychology informs our understanding of personal and social problems, and interventions to address them. Study at the university ranked #1 in Australia in Psychology for overall educational experience and teaching quality (The Good Universities Guide 2025 (undergraduate)).
curriculum: Students learn to interpret and evaluate applied psychological research across a range of contexts and problems. Under the guidance of their supervisor, they conduct an independent study using appropriate methods and data analysis techniques. Students also learn about a range of practical skills, including counselling, interviewing, assessment techniques, and critical thinking. Prospective.
admission_requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification in psychology or with a major in psychology, completed within the last 10 years, which is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC); and must normally have achieved a Grade Point Average of 5.00 or above in all second and third year psychology topics attempted including a third year research methodology topic. name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Up to 36 weeks of work-integrated learning across the two-year program is a lot for an MBA, and it signals what Flinders is actually trying to produce - not just credentialed managers but graduates who've spent real time embedded with industry partners. Specialisations run across Business Analytics, Marketing, Healthcare Management, Human Resource Management, Finance, International Business and Social Impact, letting students steer the generalist MBA core toward a specific sector or function.

One distinctive strand is the industry-focused entrepreneurial stream tied to Flinders' advanced manufacturing and Industry 4.0 capabilities, aimed at students working on small-to-medium enterprise problems using the university's own prototyping and manufacturing research infrastructure - a fairly unusual pairing for a business school MBA to have direct access to. Delivery is flexible: on-campus in the Adelaide CBD, blended online/on-campus, and part-time options for people continuing to work.

Healthcare Management as a named specialisation is worth flagging given Flinders' strong health sciences and medical faculty presence - it gives the MBA a genuine connection to the university's clinical and health services expertise rather than being a generic add-on specialisation borrowed from a template.

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
Flinders built this degree around the idea that computer science is now a broad enough field that a good master's should let students choose their own weighting between theory and application. You'll pull topics from computer science, information technology, digital media, software engineering and mathematics, so two graduates can come out with genuinely different skill sets depending on whether they leaned toward robotics, intelligent systems, or software engineering practice.

Accreditation from the Australian Computer Society at the professional level matters here because Flinders' course is also recognised through the Seoul Accord, which means the qualification carries weight for skilled migration and professional registration well beyond South Australia. That international recognition is a bigger deal for this degree than it sounds on paper, since a large share of the cohort is international students planning a career move to Australia or elsewhere.

The final two semesters shift from coursework to a supervised masters project, and Flinders explicitly frames it as a chance to dig into an advanced niche - robotics, video game technology, or biomedical computing among them - under a named supervisor rather than a generic capstone brief. For someone who already has an undergraduate degree in an unrelated field, the first year is where the real foundational catch-up happens; for those with a CS background already, it's more of an accelerant into a specialisation.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1: foundations in programming and data structures, discrete mathematics for computing, computer systems
Year 1, Semester 2: database systems, software engineering principles, choice of an elective stream (AI, networks, or digital media)
Year 2, Semester 1: advanced electives drawn from robotics, intelligent and interactive systems, or systems engineering
Year 2, Semester 2: masters project (part 1) plus specialised electives such as heuristic optimisation or advanced software engineering
Final semester: masters project (part 2) - independent supervised research or applied development in an area such as robotics, biomedical computing or game technology
72 units total, full accreditation from the Australian Computer Society at the professional level
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in computer science, information technology, ICT-based engineering, or a closely related discipline (or hold the Graduate Diploma in Computer Science); assumed knowledge of at least second-year undergraduate computer science.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall (Flinders postgraduate standard).

name: Master of Counselling (Behavioural Health)
description: Jobs for Counsellors are projected to grow by 27.7% through to 2033 * . As an accredited professional counsellor, you will support the changing needs of individuals, families, and communities. By engaging in our suite of articulated courses, you will build knowledge, understanding and skills that are sought after in a range of industry settings such as health care, not for profit, private-practice, educational settings. As an existing or emerging health professional, you bring personal values of integrity, curiosity, and compassion. Learn and develop alongside passionate Flinders experts, who will guide you to develop skills in evidence-based therapeutic approaches, for a diverse range of needs in areas such as youth and families, strengths-based wellbeing, digital care and telehealth, chronic conditions, addictions, grief and loss, interpersonal counselling, disability, and priority communities. Competency-based, supervised industry placements are embedded in the Diploma and Masters courses to demonstrate the application of skills. You will have opportunities to translate knowledge of chronic and mental health conditions, strengths-based models, motivational interviewing, as well as specific and transdiagnostic treatments. *Source: Jobs and Skills Australia 2024 Please note: The theoretical content of this course is delivered online and can be accessed anywhere within Australia with internet coverage, however.
curriculum: Students complete core and optional topics aimed at providing students with the understanding, and skills in person-centred behavioural health counselling to improve physical and mental health outcomes for individuals and populations. The courses aim to provide opportunities for individuals working in health and related areas to increase and develop their knowledge within a competency-based.
admission_requirements: Graduate Certificate Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification in a health-related area - e.g., behavioural science, counselling, medicine, midwifery, nursing, occupational therapy, psychology or social work; or hold an un-related bachelor degree or equivalent qualification and hold two years of full-time work experience in counselling, psychology or behavioural sciences; or hold an un-related bachelor degree or equivalent qualification and have evidence of continued professional development in counselling or hold a postgraduate degree in counselling; or hold three years of full-time work experience in counselling, psychology or behavioural sciences. Graduate Diploma Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree in a health-related area, eg behavioural science, counselling, medicine, midwifery, nursing, occupational therapy, psychology or social work, or hold the Graduate Certificate in Counselling (Behavioural Health) or equivalent qualification. Masters Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification in a health-related discipline such as behavioural science, counselling, medicine, midwifery, nursing, occupational therapy, psychology or social work; or hold the Graduate Diploma in Counselling (Behaviour Health) or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (writing 7.0); PTE Academic overall 65. name: Master of Data Science
description: If you are a graduate with a previous degree in information technology or computer science but are looking to upgrade and extend your knowledge and skills in this dramatically changing area, the Flinders Master of Data Science provides the perfect opportunity. Continuing advances in technology and the growing complexity of big data is leading us towards a world where an incredible amount of information is at our fingertips. It's also creating a need for specialists who can make sense of, and find new insights from all that information to create innovative solutions. Flinders Master of Data Science will give you the skills to analyse complex data, form powerful insights and communicate new ideas to help solve the myriad challenges faced by government and industry in the 21 st century.
curriculum: Flinders postgraduate Data Science program has been designed in close consultation with industry. You'll develop in-demand skills to help solve the challenges of today and tomorrow. You'll also learn soft skills that will help you navigate the world by working with multiple disciplines and cultures. You'll hone your leadership and problem-solving skills, and develop interpersonal skills that will.
admission_requirements: Graduate Diploma Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification in science, medical science, information technology, mathematics, statistics or a closely related discipline. Masters Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification in science, medical science, information technology, mathematics, statistics or a closely related discipline or hold the Graduate Diploma in Data Science.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. Flinders also accepts TOEFL iBT, Cambridge C1 Advanced, Duolingo English Test and LanguageCert Academic at equivalent levels, or completion of an approved English-medium secondary or tertiary qualification, or a Flinders University Academy / approved ELICOS pathway course.

name: Master of Digital Communications
description: The Master of Digital Communications at Flinders University is a two-year full-time degree built for a fast-changing digital communication field. Students learn the intricacies of communication in a digital world, how to adapt as new platforms emerge, and how disruptive technologies such as blockchain and artificial intelligence are reshaping the field. It suits journalists, entrepreneurs, creative practitioners and communication professionals. Graduates work in digital communications, content strategy, public relations and media roles. Indicative international tuition is around 38,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 119370H.

name: Master of Disability Practice and Leadership (Developmental Education)
description: Enhance your leadership in policy and practice as a Developmental Educator - an allied health professional that works alongside people with disability, their families, and advocates to promote their well-being. The Masters of Disability Practice and Leadership (Developmental Education) aims to provide senior practitioners with work-relevant knowledge and skills they can apply as developmental educators across a wide range of contexts in disability, health, and human services fields. Up to 80% off fees due to Government subsidies* *Government subsidies enable Flinders to offer Domestic applicants a reduction of up to 80% off full course fees through Commonwealth Supported Places. Offer subject to change. Learn more .
curriculum: First Year Topics in disability theory and practice; leading through change; facilitating accessible teaching and learning strategies; ethical issues in disability, design and evaluation of disability programs; inclusion, belonging and participation; disability, rights and embodiment; and policy in the lives of people with disability Second Year Core topics in positive behaviour support;.
admission_requirements: Masters Applicants must normally hold a Bachelors degree in an allied health or human services-related area (eg special education, education, teaching, behavioural science, counselling, medicine, nursing, occupational therapy, psychology or social work) and have not less than two years work experience in a relevant disability related field.

name: Master of Education
description: Flinders University's Master of Education - 2 years degree. The Master of Education - 2 years is an advanced level coursework degree that extends the knowledge and skills of educators and educational stakeholders for applications to workplace contexts and/or pathways to further and more specialist knowledge. The program of study is designed to meet the increasing demand for professional development for educators across a diverse range of specialist areas. It offers a cross-disciplinary program with a flexibility to enable breadth of study or a blend of specialised areas of study that enhance career opportunities. Up to two eligible Graduate Certificates can be credited towards this course. To graduate with the Master of Education, you must be admitted to the course and complete a further two Minors as prescribed below in the course rule. Eligible Graduate Certificates are: Graduate Certificate in Autism and Complex Disabilities Graduate Certificate in Digital Innovation and Artificial Intelligence in Education Graduate Certificate in Education Pedagogy and Practice Graduate Certificate in Education Research OR Graduate Certificate in Research and Evaluation for Practice Graduate Certificate in Leadership in Education Graduate Certificate in STEM Education Graduate Certificate in Student Inclusion Graduate Certificate in Student Wellbeing
curriculum: To qualify for the Master of Education - 2 years, a student must complete 72 units with a grade of P or NGP or better in each topic, according to the program of study below. Not all topics are necessarily available each year. Upon completion of an 18-unit Minor, a student may choose to exit with one of the following awards, subject to meeting the program of study for that award: Graduate Certificate in Autism and Complex Disabilities Graduate Certificate in Digital Innovation and Artificial Intelligence in Education Graduate Certificate in Education Pedagogy and Practice Graduate Certificate in Research and Evaluation for Practice Graduate Certificate in Indigenous Education, Pedagogy and Leadership Graduate Certificate in Leadership in Education Graduate Certificate in Leading Mental Health and Wellbeing (Workplace and Community) Graduate Certificate in STEM Education Graduate Certificate in Student Inclusion Graduate Certificate in Student Wellbeing
admission_requirements: Applicants must normally hold a degree or equivalent qualification from an approved tertiary institution. However, the Dean (Education), may under certain circumstances and subject to specific conditions admit others who can show evidence of fitness for candidature.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. name: Master of Engineering (Mechanical)
description: If you are a graduate with a previous degree in Mechanical Engineering (or a related field) and are looking to upgrade and extend your knowledge and skills in this high demand area, the Mechanical Engineering postgraduate program at Flinders provides you with the perfect study plan. Ranging from the Graduate Diploma , and Master of Engineering Science to this Master of Engineering, these courses offer a unique selection of advanced topics in various branches of Mechanical Engineering such as Solid Mechanics, Fluid Mechanics, Design and Manufacturing, Materials, and Control. The courses also integrate with the strong research and development programs in the College of Science and Engineering. With the demand for professional mechanical engineers with an advanced level of expertise and knowledge, these courses equip students with the latest theoretical and practical aspects of Mechanical Engineering to address high-level industry requirements such as research and development, advanced design and analysis of complex mechanical systems.
curriculum: The Master of Engineering (Mechanical) provides both core and optional advanced topics such as Solid Mechanics, Control Systems, Applied Thermo-Fluid Dynamics, Mechanics of Machines, Renewable Energy, Advanced Mechanical Design, Finite Element Methods, Fatigue and Fracture, Materials Selection, Project Management & Innovation and Standards and Ethics.
admission_requirements: Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification in engineering or closely related field; or hold the Graduate Diploma in Engineering Science (Mechanical stream) from Flinders University; or have completed a minimum of one year full-time equivalent in the Master of Engineering Science (Mechanical) or equivalent qualification. A knowledge of mathematics (equivalent to second year university mathematics including Fourier and Laplace Transforms) and a knowledge of Materials and Dynamics is assumed. Applicants without such a qualification should apply for the Master of Engineering Science (Mechanical) (2CM240).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. Flinders also accepts TOEFL iBT, Cambridge C1 Advanced, Duolingo English Test and LanguageCert Academic at equivalent levels, or completion of an approved English-medium secondary or tertiary qualification, or a Flinders University Academy / approved ELICOS pathway course.

name: Master of Engineering Management
description: Engineering Management combines the problem-solving and technical design ability of engineering and other scientific and technology focused disciplines with executive organisational skills and the planning power of business and management. Central to this are advanced project management skills (both for large-scale complex projects and for smaller-scale projects). Together they enable graduates to manage complex engineering driven enterprises across a range of discipline areas. Engineering managers are required across of range of industry sectors from traditional engineering operations (such as construction, manufacturing and energy), though to managing complex defence acquisition and large-scale software engineering projects. They oversee teams of engineers and work closely with other professionals to oversee the successful delivery of complex engineering projects. Up to 80% off fees due to Government subsidies* *Government subsidies enable Flinders to offer Domestic applicants a reduction of up to 80% off full course fees through Commonwealth Supported Places. Offer subject to change. Learn more . **Please note this only applies to the Master of Engineering Management.
curriculum: The Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma and Masters courses provide a structured pathway containing approximately equal amounts of business/management study and design/engineering study. First year (and the Graduate Diploma) contains study in human resource management, marketing strategy, decision making, accounting and engineering project management. It also has a focus on engineering design,.
admission_requirements: Graduate Certificate Applicants must either: hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification OR hold a Diploma in Engineering plus have at least three years' full-time equivalent experience in an engineering context. Graduate Diploma Applicants must either: hold a degree or equivalent qualification OR hold the Flinders University Certificate in Engineering Management OR hold a Diploma in Engineering plus have at least three years' full-time equivalent experience in an engineering context. Master Applicants must either hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification; or hold the Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Engineering Management from Flinders University or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. name: Master of Engineering Science (Specialisations)
description: The Master of Engineering Science gives you a comprehensive understanding of all of the theories - natural, physical, material, and mathematical - that make up the engineering industry ecosystem. You'll learn the skills to investigate, plan, design, manufacture and maintain engineering systems and equipment in a range of areas. In addition to being taken as a stand-alone degree, it can also be used as a pathway to Flinders' accredited Master of Engineering degrees.
curriculum: The first year will see you learn Engineering Mathematics, Advanced Professional Skills, and Engineering Materials and Systems. You'll also have the opportunity to select from a range of Majors that focus on a particular aspect of Engineering - Biomedical, Electrical and Electronic, Civil, Environmental, and Mechanical. The second year will focus on the Masters Project, with extra subjects in.
admission_requirements: Applicants must normally hold at least one of the following: A Bachelor degree in engineering or an equivalent qualification A Bachelor degree in science or an equivalent qualification An Australian TAFE Diploma or Advanced Diploma or Associate Degree or an equivalent qualification in an appropriate field plus 7 years of relevant work experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. name: Master of Environmental Health
description: Flinders University's Master of Environmental Health degree. The Master of Environmental Health gives you a strong foundation in environmental health science, risk assessment, and research methods. You will explore how toxicology, microbiology, and epidemiology are used to understand and manage risks that affect communities and the environment. If you choose the 27‑unit thesis pathway, you will work closely with industry or government partners and apply your knowledge to a real‑world problem. This research experience helps you build advanced skills in analysing data, interpreting evidence, and presenting your findings clearly and convincingly. Across the course, you will strengthen your problem‑solving abilities, deepen your understanding of environmental health issues, and learn to communicate effectively with community, government, and academic audiences. You will also build the confidence to direct your own learning and research as the field continues to evolve.
curriculum: Program: Sustainable Development - Health Issues, Public Health Microbiology, Risk Assessment and Management, Environmental Health Concepts, Public Health Toxicology, Environmental Health Law and Policy, Food Safety, Advanced Professional Skills, Masters Research Thesis (4.5/22.5 units), Research Methods for Science Masters, Masters Research Project (4.5/13.5 units), Environmental Impact Assessment GE, Geospatial Information Systems GE, NCGRT Australian Groundwater School GE, Introductory Biostatistics, Physical Hydrogeology GE, Advanced Spatial Analysis GE, Health Promotion in Public Health, Sustainable Regional Development GE, Ethics, Sustainability and Governance, Critical Perspectives on Global Health and Development, Caring as Country: Indigenous Environmental Management GE, Public Health, Climate Change and Disasters, Introduction to Epidemiological Research Methods, Smart, Liveable and Resilient Cities GE, Social Determinants of Health and Wellbeing, Economic Evidence for Health Care Decision Making, First Nations Health and Well-Being, Global Climate Change GE
admission_requirements: Applicants who do not hold the Graduate Diploma in Environmental Health Practice must normally hold an undergraduate degree or equivalent from an approved tertiary institution and have successfully completed a minimum of one semester full-time (18 units or equivalent) in basic sciences such as chemistry, physics, microbiology, physiology, biology and life sciences. However, the Dean (Education) may, under certain circumstances and subject to specific conditions, admit others who can show evidence of fitness for candidature.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. Flinders also accepts TOEFL iBT, Cambridge C1 Advanced, Duolingo English Test and LanguageCert Academic at equivalent levels, or completion of an approved English-medium secondary or tertiary qualification, or a Flinders University Academy / approved ELICOS pathway course.

name: Master of Environmental Management and Sustainability
description: The Master of Environmental Management and Sustainability at Flinders University is a two-year full-time degree that combines the social sciences and humanities with physical geography, earth sciences and biology to build the breadth expected of environmental managers. It focuses on environmental policy, strategy and management systems and the development of sustainable practice in urban and non-urban environments. Graduates work in environmental management, sustainability and policy roles across government, industry and consulting. Indicative international tuition is around 37,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 107182M.

name: Master of Forensic Science
description: Take your forensic and analytical skills to the next level and master the techniques to help you develop the most scientific and objective findings in any investigation. The Master of Forensic Science offers students with a background in science the opportunity to obtain new skills in forensic science and apply their knowledge and skills in a forensic context. Students will explore how chemical and biological techniques are used for forensic investigations. Students choose one of two areas of focus, depending on their entry qualifications: Forensic and Analytical Chemistry Minor requires a bachelor's degree in science containing a study of chemistry to at least second year level Forensic Biology Minor requires a bachelor's degree in science containing a study of biology to at least second year level. Graduates of this course will have completed a Masters thesis and coursework designed to address topical concerns in industry and society, preparing them for further enrolment in a research higher degree or employment in forensic-science related fields. This course is delivered by Flinders University.
curriculum: The Master in Forensic Science will enhance your knowledge of forensics by teaching you how to utilise the latest tools and techniques available in your field, and allowing you to choose the areas you want to specialise in through elective units. There is also a focus on professional skills development, preparing you for more senior career roles. Topics can include: Advanced Professional Skills.
admission_requirements: Forensic and Analytical Chemistry minor requires a bachelor's degree in science including chemistry topics to at least second year level. Applicants who hold an Honours degree in Chemistry or a closely related area are not eligible to apply for this degree. Forensic Biology minor requires a bachelor's degree in science including biology topics to at least second year level. Applicants who hold an Honours degree in Biology or a closely related area are not eligible to apply for this degree.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. name: Master of Geospatial Information Systems
description: The only Geospatial Information Systems postgraduate courses in South Australia. The postgraduate program for Geospatial Information Systems (GIS) is the only GIS stream available in South Australia. Blending the disciplines of science, computer science, data analytics, geography and cartography, GIS is a fascinating and powerful area of study which allows you to impact the world around you - from using drones to survey and photograph potential areas for environmental conservation, using location intelligence and data to address racial inequities, to helping plan our future cities and genuinely improve lives. The program provides a theoretical and practical framework for graduates from a range of backgrounds, as well as those from the public sector and non-government organisations wishing to extend their choice of career path by acquiring knowledge and skills in the capture, analysis and communication of spatially referenced information. You will develop and implement GIS skills and knowledge applicable to a range of areas, such as environmental management, urban and regional planning, human geography and environmental health, land-use dynamics, natural resources management, ecosystem services, biological sciences and archaeology. Students completing the Master of Geospatial Information Systems will be able to undertake research and analysis using spatially-referenced data and prepare research reports. This course is delivered by Flinders University.
curriculum: You can select from a range of geospatial topics to build a study program that suits your interests and current or future employment requirements. The program is specifically designed to provide flexibility to students with different levels of GIS and remote sensing experience and skills. Specifically, the program allows students who have already completed undergraduate introductory topics in GIS.
admission_requirements: The articulated graduate program in GIS is not available to graduates of the Bachelor of Applied Geographical Information Systems or of equivalent undergraduate courses from other tertiary institutions or significant relevant experience. Graduate Certificate Applicants must normally hold a degree or equivalent qualification. Graduate Diploma Applicants must normally hold a degree or equivalent qualification. Or hold the Graduate Certificate in Geospatial Information Systems. Masters Applicants must normally hold a degree or equivalent qualification. Or hold the Graduate Certificate in Geospatial Information Systems or the Graduate Diploma in Geospatial Information Systems.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. Flinders also accepts TOEFL iBT, Cambridge C1 Advanced, Duolingo English Test and LanguageCert Academic at equivalent levels, or completion of an approved English-medium secondary or tertiary qualification, or a Flinders University Academy / approved ELICOS pathway course.

name: Master of Health Administration
description: Course update for 2027 This course suite has been revised and will be offered as the Health Management and Leadership suite from 2027. The updated courses reflect a stronger focus on contemporary health management, leadership and the evolving needs of the health and aged care sectors. From 2027, the suite will include the Master of Health Management and Leadership, Graduate Diploma in Health Management and Leadership and Graduate Certificate in Health Management and Leadership. Courses Graduate Diploma in Health Administration This course is delivered by Flinders University.
curriculum: You will apply theory to management problems, use management tools and techniques, and reflect critically on your own practice as a manager. You are also able to pursue your personal interests by taking topics in public health, business, public administration, education and other disciplines at Flinders and other institutions. Topics cover areas such as health and aged care systems and policy,.
admission_requirements: Masters Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification and have a minimum of two years' full-time equivalent professional work experience in the aged care or health sector such as; but not limited to; nursing, midwifery, medicine or in health therapy; by the commencement date of the course; or hold either the Graduate Certificate or the Graduate Diploma in Health Administration from Flinders University or equivalent qualification and have a minimum of two years' full-time equivalent professional work experience in the health or aged care sector. All applicants will be asked to provide a 300-500 word statement detailing their relevant work experience. Graduate Diploma Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification and have a minimum of two years' full-time equivalent professional work experience in the aged care or health sector such as; but not limited to; nursing, midwifery, medicine or in health therapy; by the commencement date of the course; or hold the Graduate Certificate in Health Administration or equivalent from Flinders University Application requirements Applicants must provide an electronic copy of either their original or certified copy of their Official Academic Transcript for all qualifications relevant to their application. Unofficial academic transcripts, statement of results, exam slips, screen shots of grades, AHEGS etc. will not be accepted. If academic transcripts are in a language other than English, applicants must submit copies of both the original documents and full translations. Translations must show results for all subjects undertaken and be certified by an independent accredited translator. It is an applicant's responsibility to comply with requests to provide further documentation, either in the original language or English translation. Flinders graduates of a Bachelor degree or Flinders students currently completing their Bachelor degree at Flinders are not required to provide a copy of their official transcript for their Flinders course. An application can be made for up to 3 courses in order of preference. You will be assessed for entry to the course you are eligible for as per your preferences. Applicants must provide details of their professional work experience in their application.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. name: Master of Health Administration [2 years]
description: The Master of Health Administration at Flinders University, in its two-year full-time pathway, prepares professionals to manage healthcare systems and shape health policy. Students learn to navigate health systems, apply digital health technologies and use practical management strategies across leadership, financial management, ethics, policy, quality and safety. Graduates work in health service management, policy and quality roles across health and aged care. Indicative international tuition is around 42,100 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 023592C.
discontinued_note: Not admitting new students from 2025. Prospective students please refer to the MHADFP Master of Health Administration in the Handbook. Existing students please refer to the course rules.

name: Master of Health and Clinical Research
description: The Master of Health and Clinical Research at Flinders University is an 18-month full-time higher degree by research pathway for professionals in any health field. It combines advanced coursework topics with a supervised, time-based research project that culminates in an externally examined thesis, giving graduates specialised knowledge and skills in research methods. The program is a recognised pathway into PhD study. Graduates strengthen careers in government, private and corporate consulting, academia and research institutions. Indicative international tuition is around 37,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Health Management and Leadership 1.5 years
description: The Master of Health Management and Leadership at Flinders University, in its shorter pathway of around eighteen months full-time, is built around the university's MBA (Healthcare Management) specialisation. Students study core business principles with a healthcare focus and sustainability embedded across topics, preparing to apply contemporary management concepts in health and aged care settings. Graduates move into leadership roles in health and aged care organisations. Indicative international tuition is around 47,400 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 107691A.

name: Master of Health Management and Leadership 2 years
description: The Master of Health Management and Leadership at Flinders University, in its two-year full-time pathway, is built around the university's MBA (Healthcare Management) specialisation. Students study core business principles with a healthcare focus and sustainability embedded across topics, developing the capability to lead and improve performance in health and aged care organisations. Graduates take on management and leadership roles across the health sector. Indicative international tuition is around 47,900 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 107691A.

name: Master of Inclusive and Specialised Education
description: The Master of Inclusive and Specialised Education is designed for education professionals who aspire to provide leadership in inclusive and specialised education, and advocacy for children and young people with special needs. You'll have the opportunity to study a range of minors where you can develop expertise across a range of areas in inclusive and specialised education, or you can build a unique program of study featuring a broad selection of topics. Gain the creative, caring, ethical, critical thinking, problem-solving and research skills needed to analyse provisions and practices relating to children and young people with special needs. Upon graduation, you'll be equipped to design, implement and evaluate policies, programs and services relating to inclusive and specialised education. Advance your career and become a skilled professional who is able to thrive in a range of diverse settings, and communicate and collaborate effectively and ethically with children, parents, carers and educators. Your experience counts If you've studied at Flinders or another institution previously, or have time in teaching service, this could be recognised towards your Master of Inclusive and Specialised Education - meaning you could complete the degree in as little as 12 months! Find out more about how you can.
curriculum: Students can choose from: a range of option topics and minor programs of study to shape the degree according to your needs and interests.

This course acknowledges the diverse range of learners in preschools and schools and their entitlement to an equitable and appropriate education, and is designed to prepare educators and other professionals to build research-informed knowledge, skills and understandings that will enable them to implement and lead inclusive processes and practices in their schools and sites. The Master of Inclusive and Specialised Education offers a wide range of topics to enable students to tailor their studies to suit their particular learning goals and contexts. Up to two eligible Graduate Certificates can be credited towards this course. To graduate with the Master of Inclusive and Specialised Education, you must be admitted to the course and complete a further one or two Minors as prescribed below in the course rule. Eligible Graduate Certificates are: One or two of core focus areas: Graduate Certificate in Autism and Complex Disabilities Graduate Certificate in Education Research OR Graduate Certificate in Research and Evaluation for Practice Graduate Certificate in Student Inclusion One of optional focus area: Graduate Certificate in Digital Innovation and Artificial Intelligence in Education Graduate Certificate in Education Pedagogy and Practice Graduate Certificate in Leadership in Education Graduate Certificate in STEM Education Graduate Certificate in Student Wellbeing

name: Master of Information Technology (Network and Cybersecurity Systems)
description: If you are a graduate with a previous degree in an information technology or computer science related field, but are looking to specialise and extend your knowledge and skills in this dramatically changing area, the specialised networks and cybersecurity masters in information technology program at Flinders provides the perfect introduction. This coursework masters provides advanced studies in information technology, with particular emphasis on the techniques required to design, develop, secure and manage an enterprise's networked information systems. The course capitalises on the demand for professionals across a continually widening range of applications, from intelligent consumer goods such as mobile phones and cars through to electronic medical records. It addresses the profession's growing concern regarding the skills shortage in the area of cybersecurity. The focus on Flinders University's strengths in the design, implementation and management of enterprise information technology and the secure and interconnected application of information technology for information retrieval, analysis and visualisation characterise this program. The course integrates with the strong and active research and development program in the College of Science and Engineering, carried out as externally funded research and development.
curriculum: The coursework masters provides both core and advanced studies in information technology, with particular emphasis on the techniques required to design, develop and manage an enterprise's information systems. Topics cover areas such as the fundamentals of computing, software engineering, database and conceptual modelling, statistical science, and networks and cybersecurity.
admission_requirements: Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification in information technology or computer science or closely related area.

name: Master of International Relations
description: The Master of International Relations provides a comprehensive foundation to understand the dynamics that shape contemporary international relations, and critically analyse the major and political landscapes and security trends unfolding both regionally, (including Asia- Pacific) and globally. The program is designed for forward-thinking professionals aiming to develop an advanced set of knowledge and the core skills required to advance careers for managers and analysts working in foreign affairs, international trade, defence, national and international security and more. You will graduate with outstanding critical skills, public speaking skills, the ability to solve numerous challenges and understand the relationship between theory and practice. These courses are flexible, and designed for 100% online, in person, or blended learning (a combination of in person and online classes). This course is delivered by Flinders University.
curriculum: Students can choose from: a range of electives in public policy, public administration, and international law, or explore topics from other disciplines such as Global Feminist Activism or Adapting to Climate Change.

name: Master of Laws (Research)
description: The Master of Laws (Research) at Flinders University is a two-year full-time research degree in which students undertake independent research on an area of law of their choice under supervision. It develops advanced research, critical thinking, legal writing, communication and project management skills within a research community that spans established and emerging areas of legal scholarship. Graduates pursue careers in legal practice, policy, academia and research. Indicative international tuition is around 33,700 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 020070J.

name: Master of Maritime Archaeology
description: The Graduate Program in Maritime Archaeology at Flinders is the top named degree of its kind in Australia. You'll learn practical skills in the classroom and gain valuable, career-ready experience in the field, with field schools and training led by award-winning, internationally recognised experts in maritime and underwater archaeology. Get hands on in the lab with the latest digital technology, including 3D recording of artefacts and landscapes, marine geophsyics, conservation and diverse topics from historic shipwrecks to ancient submerged landscapes. Participate on archaeological projects interstate and overseas and obtain field experience through formal training in our field schools and practical topics. In the Masters Program, you'll graduate with theoretical and practical training with an option to become a qualified Scientific Diver enabling you to participate on many scientific and archaeological projects around the world. Careers in maritime archaeology are steadily growing, both in Australia and internationally. The Flinders program has drawn students from many countries (Australia, New Zealand, Brunei, Sri Lanka, Philippines, Indonesia, Thailand, Japan, UK, USA, Canada, South Africa, Italy and the Netherlands) and graduates now work professionally for underwater cultural heritage management agencies, museums and consultancy companies, as well as studying and teaching at universities all over the.
curriculum: The program enables you to select from a range of topics covering the theory and method of maritime and underwater archaeology. In addition, a broad selection of topics in archaeology and related disciplines, such as geophysics or heritage management, are available. You can undertake fieldwork in both maritime archaeology and a number of archaeological contexts. Students without a background in.

Masters (1.5 years) Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree or equivalent qualification in Archaeology; or hold a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Archaeology or Maritime Archaeology (or a closely related discipline); or hold a Honours degree in Archaeology (or a closely related discipline).

name: Master of Media and Communication (2 years)
description: The Master of Media and Communication at Flinders University is a two-year full-time degree designed for creative practitioners, journalists, entrepreneurs and other professionals working in a fast-growing field. Students learn the intricacies of communication in a digital world and how to adapt as new technologies and platforms emerge, examining the implications of digital disruption and technologies such as artificial intelligence. Graduates work in communications, content, journalism and digital media roles. Indicative international tuition is around 35,000 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 119370H.

name: Master of Nursing (Acute Care)
description: The Master of Nursing (Acute Care) at Flinders University is a program of around eighteen months full-time for registered nurses who want advanced skills in caring for acutely and critically ill patients. It covers nursing across environments including emergency, intensive care and paediatric settings, and sits within an articulated set of postgraduate nursing qualifications. Graduates take on advanced clinical and specialist roles in acute care. Indicative international tuition is around 34,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 113748E.

name: Master of Nutrition and Dietetics
description: Undertake advanced studies in nutrition and dietetics, the pathophysiology of nutrition-related illnesses, health promotion, communication skills, and clinical, food service and community and public health nutrition skills. This program aims to prepare students for professional practice as nutritionists or dietitians. Graduates will be able to work across a variety of settings to integrate and apply advanced theoretical knowledge, skills and attributes to promoting health, and preventing and treating diet-related illnesses. Graduates are able to use scientific principles and critical thinking skills to consider the wider environment affecting food supply and eating behaviours and to evaluate new developments in this rapidly evolving area. The course is offered by Flinders University's College of Nursing and Health Sciences and is founded on practices designed to encourage lifelong learning in the practice of nutrition and dietetics. A wide variety of teaching and learning strategies are employed, including lectures, tutorials, field placements, site visits, food practicals and student seminars and presentations. A variety of assessment methods is used, including peer and self-assessment and competency-based assessment of field placements. Particular emphasis is given to the provision of practice-focused learning strategies (eg. case studies, role-plays, simulated counselling and group sessions). Consistent with the postgraduate level of the.
curriculum: Your study program will include lectures, tutorials, field placements, site visits, food practicals, and student seminars and presentations. Topics cover areas such as the nutrition care process, food service and professional practice, research methods and critical thinking in human nutrition, communication and nutrition counselling, and clinical nutrition and dietetics. Students will undertake.
admission_requirements: Applicants must normally hold a bachelor degree or an equivalent qualification from an approved tertiary institution which includes: At least the equivalent of 13.5 Flinders units (0.375 EFTSL) across the course of their undergraduate program in human nutrition and food science topics in the areas of basic nutrition principles, life-cycle nutrition and food science At least the equivalent of 18 Flinders units (0.5 EFTSL) of introductory bioscience topics studied at first year level, including at least 9 Flinders units (0.25 EFTSL) of human biology and 4.5 Flinders units (0.125 EFTSL) of chemistry At least the equivalent of 9 Flinders units (0.25 EFTSL) in human biochemistry topics studied at second year undergraduate level At least the equivalent of 9 Flinders units (0.25 EFTSL) in human physiology topics studied at second year undergraduate level A Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least 5 Applicants will be ranked for admission on the basis of their GPA. Please refer to the pre-requisite flyer for further information about the topic pre-requisites. Applicants for the Master of Nutrition and Dietetics must also complete the Self-assessment form when submitting their SATAC application.

Emphasis is placed on preparing you to become a contemporary health professional who is able to work effectively across a range of settings in metropolitan and rural or remote locations. Our program has a strong clinical focus with teaching mainly embedded within clinical settings across South Australia and has close links with healthcare providers to best prepare you for professional practice as a physiotherapist. name: Master of Professional Psychology
description: Your pathway to registration as a general psychologist. The Master of Professional Psychology comprises a fifth-year qualification in Psychology training. It provides you with the theoretical knowledge, research skills development, and practical skills required to prepare you for professional practice in a wide variety of setting and with diverse populations. The degree forms part of a 5+1 pathway to general psychology registration. After completion of the degree, you will be required to undertake a one-year internship via the Psychology Board of Australia before being eligible for general registration as a psychologist. This course is delivered by Flinders University.
curriculum: The Master of Professional Psychology consists of 36 units. You must complete 27 units of coursework and 9 units (i.e., 300 hours) of supervised practicum. Coursework covers areas such as foundations of psychological practice, assessment across the lifespan, evidence based interventions, and applied research for practitioners.
admission_requirements: Applicants must normally have completed an APAC accredited fourth year of study in the field of Psychology conferred within 10 years of the commencement of the course. Candidates will be chosen based on interview, clinically relevant volunteer and paid work experience, 2nd and 3rd year Psychology topics sequence GPA, Honours year mark, referee reports and publications/grants. Applicants will be shortlisted for interview based on their Academic record, relevant clinical skills and experience and referee reports. Selection for a place in the course will be based on interview performance and the overall application. On completion of the course, graduates will be required to complete an approved one year internship of supervised practice to be eligible for general registration with the Psychology Board of Australia. The course aims to prepare you for professional work in a wide variety of settings, ranging across community mental health, hospital and health care facilities, community welfare and correctional service settings. It provides you with theoretical knowledge, research and clinical skills leading to professional registration. Experience is provided in both adult and child domains of clinical psychology. name: Master of Public Administration
description: The Master of Public Administration provides a comprehensive foundation in the core skills required to effectively manage the business of government, not-for-profit and international organisations, with a specialisation in public administration. This specialisation in public administration is designed to prepare leaders to learn the latest concepts and skills which can be applied to the workplace immediately. You will deepen your knowledge of governance in the global world, digital strategy, and sustainable development. Tailor your degree depending on your career goals. You can choose electives from public policy, international relations, or you can select two electives from anywhere across the university. These courses are flexible, and designed for 100% online, in person, or blended learning (a combination of in person and online classes). Flinders University also offers the Master of Public Policy which enables policy analysts and managers to become an expert on the fundamentals of public policy making, and the Master of International Relations, which enables leaders in foreign affairs, defence, or international trade to develop skills around security, trade and diplomacy.
curriculum: The study program includes core topics, elective topics, as well as individual research. These courses are flexible, and designed for 100% online, in person, or blended learning (a combination of in person and online classes). Flinders University also offers the Master of Public Administration which equips the managers and administrators with knowledge and skills required to effectively manage the business of the government, not-for profit and international organisations and the Master of International Relations, which enables leaders in foreign affairs, defence or international trade to develop skills around security, economics, trade and diplomacy.

name: Master of Science Mathematics/Statistics)

name: Master of Screen and Media Production
Master of Social Work
description:
Two placements, 500 hours each, four days a week for roughly 18 to 20 weeks apiece - that's the structural spine of Flinders' graduate-entry social work degree, and it's worth stating plainly because the placement load is what distinguishes a professional social work qualification from an adjacent human services degree. Students attend Monday to Thursday during placement blocks, which effectively means putting paid work or other commitments on hold for those stretches.

Coursework runs alongside and before the placements, covering practice with diverse populations, work with children and families in complex situations, mental health across the life course, and trauma and resilience - areas chosen to map onto where Flinders' placement partners in South Australia actually operate, from statutory child protection to community mental health services.

At 72 units across two years full-time (or four years part-time), this is the graduate-entry pathway for people who already hold a bachelor's degree in an unrelated field and want the professional social work qualification without repeating an undergraduate degree. The professional registration outcome - eligibility for Australian Association of Social Workers membership - is the whole point of the structure being this placement-heavy.
curriculum:
Year 1, Semester 1: foundations of social work practice, human behaviour and the social environment, social policy
Year 1, Semester 2: social work with diverse populations, complexities in work with children and families
Year 2, Semester 1: first field placement (500 hours, four days/week, approx. 18-20 weeks) plus mental health through the life course
Year 2, Semester 2: second field placement (500 hours) plus trauma and resilience, integrated practice seminar
72 units total; two supervised placements are required for AASW-eligible registration
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Speech Pathology
description: Become a competent, reflective and innovative practitioner in the field of speech pathology. Speech pathologists provide professional services for people across the lifespan whose educational, vocational, personal and social functioning is impaired by disorders of communication and swallowing. Communication and swallowing disabilities may severely impact people's quality of life and result from developmental difficulties, social disadvantage, illness or accident. This coursework program is founded on principles designed to encourage lifelong learning in the practice of speech pathology. It involves an innovative, integrated enquiry-based curriculum, incorporating a problem-based learning format. This approach is supported by a wide variety of teaching and learning strategies including lectures, workshops, clinical skills tutorials and practicum. A variety of assessment methods are used, including peer and self-assessment, performance within authentic tasks and competency-based assessment of practical work. This course is delivered by Flinders University.
curriculum: The Master of Speech Pathology consists of 72 units. The program is highly integrated and comprises three streams of study: professional studies and communication sciences speech pathology skills and practice research methods. In the professional studies and communication sciences stream, the content is delivered via problem-based learning tutorials. It involves working through a weekly case.
admission_requirements: Applicants must hold an approved bachelor degree or equivalent qualification, and typically have achieved a Flinders equivalent grade point average (GPA) of 5.00 or above to be considered. Applicants who did not achieve the minimum GPA in their completed approved bachelor degree or equivalent qualification, can also be considered on the basis of a second bachelor degree, graduate certificate, graduate diploma or masters degree of their choice, provided they have completed a minimum one semester of full-time equivalent study in one of these courses and they achieve a Flinders equivalent GPA is 5.00 or above in this study. Selection will be based on academic merit. Up to 4 places are reserved in the course for applicants who have completed the Bachelor of Health Sciences or the Bachelor of Medical Science at Flinders University.

name: Master of Teaching (Early Childhood)
description: Flinders University's Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) degree. The Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) is an initial teacher education degree that focuses on the play, learning, development and wellbeing of children from birth through to eight years of age. You'll explore how children grow, learn and express themselves in diverse and dynamic ways, and learn to design inclusive, challenging and meaningful learning experiences. With a strong focus on play, relationships and children's agency, you'll develop the knowledge and skills to support every child as a capable and active participant in their world. Throughout the course, you'll build your confidence in working with families, communities and interdisciplinary teams, and learn to use research, data and theory to inform your teaching. You'll also gain the tools to communicate effectively across a range of settings and embed Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives in your practice. Graduates are equipped to teach in a variety of early childhood settings, including preschools, kindergartens and the early years of primary school. You'll be ready to make a real difference in the lives of young children and their communities. For applicants who would benefit from further contextual preparation for study and teaching in Australia, completion of the Graduate Certificate in Teaching Studies should be considered as an initial introduction to the profession.

name: PhD (Geography and Population Studies)
description: The PhD (Geography and Population Studies) at Flinders University is a research doctorate, typically four years full-time, in which candidates pursue an advanced supervised research project on the cultural, social and political forces shaping the contemporary world, within the history, archaeology, geography and Indigenous studies discipline. Candidates produce a substantial thesis and build advanced analytical and communication skills valued across many careers. Graduates work in academic and applied research, policy and government. Indicative international tuition is around 34,100 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 106282D.

name: Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management
description:
The advanced diploma builds directly on Greenwich's Diploma of Hospitality Management, moving from shift-level operations into venue-level strategy: financial performance across a whole property, workforce planning, and strategic marketing and business planning for a hospitality operation rather than a single department.

Students typically arrive at this qualification either having completed Greenwich's standard hospitality diploma or with several years of unaccredited hospitality supervisory experience they want formally recognised. The strategic-planning units mean assessment shifts from the more operational, task-based work of the standard diploma toward business-planning documents and analysis.

It carries the strongest credit-transfer weighting among Greenwich's hospitality qualifications, letting graduates enter a partner university hospitality or business degree with a substantial head start, or move directly into venue or operations management roles.
curriculum:
Core units: Develop and Implement Business Plans, Manage Physical Assets, Manage Finance Within a Budget, Roster Staff, Manage Operational Plans, Lead and Manage People
Electives: Manage Ethical Business Practices, Manage Business Risk, Develop and Manage Marketing Strategies
Capstone: venue-level business plan or strategic management project
Pathway: credit toward advanced-standing entry into a partner university hospitality or business degree
admission_requirements: Diploma of Hospitality Management or equivalent industry experience
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Advanced Diploma of Information Technology
description:
This advanced diploma runs deeper than a first-year IT unit, covering network design, systems analysis, database design and project-based development work, and it's positioned specifically for students who want maximum credit transfer into a partner university's IT or computer science degree. Greenwich markets the advanced diploma route as the fastest legitimate way to reach second- or third-year standing in an IT bachelor's.

Because the field moves fast, Greenwich updates elective offerings between intakes to track current employer demand: cloud fundamentals and cybersecurity basics have become more prominent additions to the elective pool in recent years, alongside the more constant core of networking and database work.

Graduates either move directly into junior technical support, network administration or junior developer roles, or continue into a partner university IT degree with substantial advanced standing already banked.
curriculum:
Core units: Design Database Solutions, Design and Implement a Server Infrastructure, Automate Processes for Business Requirements, Design Enterprise Wireless Local Area Networks, Manage Data in the Database
Electives: Manage Network Security, Cloud Computing Fundamentals, Develop Advanced Web Applications
Capstone: applied systems or network design project
Pathway: credit toward second- or third-year entry into a partner university IT or computer science degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Advanced Diploma of Leadership and Management
description:
The advanced diploma sits a level above Greenwich's standard leadership and management diploma and assumes students either already hold that diploma or bring equivalent supervisory experience: the coursework moves quickly into strategic-level tasks (leading organisational change, strategic planning, developing workplace policy) rather than repeating first-line management basics.

Because it's pitched at people already functioning in, or close to, a team-leader role, Greenwich runs a fair amount of the assessment around each student's own workplace or a detailed case organisation, so two students in the same cohort can end up producing quite different portfolios depending on the industry they're aiming at.

The advanced diploma carries the strongest credit weighting of Greenwich's business-adjacent qualifications, and students most often use it to enter directly into the second or third year of a partner university's business or management degree, or to move straight into a team leader or supervisor role without continuing to a bachelor's at all.
curriculum:
Core units: Lead Strategic Planning Processes, Develop Organisational Systems, Lead and Manage Organisational Change, Manage Strategic Financial Resources, Undertake Strategic Workforce Planning
Electives: Manage Innovation and Continuous Improvement, Manage Business Risk, Manage Business Operational Plans
Capstone: workplace-based (or case-organisation) strategic management portfolio
Pathway: credit toward second- or third-year entry into a partner university business or management degree
admission_requirements: Diploma of Leadership and Management or equivalent industry experience
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Business
description:
Greenwich College's Diploma of Business is a nationally recognised VET qualification, not a taste of a university degree: the assessment is built around workplace tasks (drafting a business plan, running a budget, writing up a risk register) rather than essays, which suits students who learn better by producing something usable than by writing about theory. Most students enrol specifically because it converts into credit toward a partner university's business degree, shaving up to a year off a bachelor's when the pathway is followed through.

Class sizes at Greenwich's Sydney CBD campus are kept small by design, and a large share of the cohort is international students building English proficiency and local business fluency alongside the qualification itself. Group projects and presentations get more classroom time here than they typically would in a standard first-year university subject, which is deliberate scaffolding rather than a lighter workload.

Graduates either step straight into junior business, admin or coordinator roles or, more commonly, use the diploma's credit points to enter the second year of a partner university's Bachelor of Business.
curriculum:
Core units: Develop and Use Emotional Intelligence, Communicate in the Workplace, Undertake Project Work, Apply Business Risk Management Processes, Plan and Manage Budgets and Financial Plans, Contribute to Organisational Development
Electives: Marketing Principles, Human Resources Fundamentals, Workplace Health and Safety Processes (elective selection varies by intake)
Assessment: workplace-style tasks (business plans, budgets, case studies) rather than exams
Pathway: credit toward second-year entry into a partner university Bachelor of Business on successful completion
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, or Certificate IV in Business
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Community Services (Case Management)
description:
This is the more vocationally distinct qualification in Greenwich's diploma suite. It trains students directly in case management practice: needs assessment, care planning, working within legal and ethical frameworks, and coordinating services across the community sector rather than general business or management skills.

Given the sensitivity of the work, assessment leans heavily on scenario-based tasks and reflective practice, and the coursework spends real time on the legal and ethical obligations of case workers (duty of care, confidentiality, mandatory reporting contexts) rather than treating those as a single compliance module.

Students typically use this diploma either as a direct entry credential into community services, disability support or case-work roles, or as credit toward a partner university degree in social work, human services or community welfare. That latter pathway usually requires the student to complete additional units at the university end given how tightly regulated social work degrees are.
curriculum:
Core units: Undertake Case Management, Facilitate the Empowerment of People Receiving Services, Provide Loss and Grief Support, Work Legally and Ethically, Manage Legal and Ethical Compliance, Analyse Impacts of Sociological Factors, Work with Diverse People
Electives: Support Community Participation and Social Inclusion, Coordinate Complex Case Requirements
Assessment: scenario-based case studies, reflective practice tasks, placement-linked activities
Pathway: credit toward partner university community services, human services or social work degrees (subject to individual university credit assessment)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care
Diploma of Hospitality Management
description:
Greenwich runs this diploma with a genuine operations focus: rostering, cost control, service standards, compliance with liquor and food safety regulation, rather than treating hospitality as a soft add-on to a general business diploma. Sydney's hospitality and tourism sector gives students easy access to real venues for site visits and guest speakers, which the college leans on more than a college in a smaller city could.

Assessment mixes practical skills demonstration with the more conventional written case-study work found in other diplomas, since supervising a shift and managing a budget aren't skills that can be assessed purely on paper. International students make up a large share of this cohort, and the qualification doubles as an entry credential into the hospitality workforce for students not planning to continue into a degree at all.

On successful completion, students can use the diploma for credit into a partner university hospitality or business degree, or move directly into supervisory hospitality roles: duty manager, front office supervisor, functions coordinator.

Electives: Manage Physical Assets, Plan and Monitor In-House Food and Beverage Service, Coordinate Cost-Effective Services
Practical component: rostering, service and compliance tasks assessed via demonstration and workplace scenarios

name: Diploma of Leadership and Management
description:
This sits a level below Greenwich's Advanced Diploma of Leadership and Management and is aimed at students moving into a first management or team-leader role rather than those already operating at a senior level. The units cover the basics of leading a team, managing workplace relationships, and building operational plans rather than organisation-wide strategy.

It's one of Greenwich's more flexible diplomas in terms of who enrols: recent graduates aiming at their first supervisory job sit in the same classes as mid-career professionals from overseas whose existing management experience isn't formally recognised in Australia and who need a local, AQF-recognised credential to have that experience taken seriously by Australian employers.

Successful completion carries credit into a partner university business or management degree, typically at second-year entry, and graduates commonly step into team leader, supervisor or coordinator roles.
