name: Master of Catchment Science
description: The Master of Catchment Science at Griffith University teaches students to combine scientific, engineering and economic knowledge to plan ways to protect, restore and rehabilitate river basins and catchments that have been transformed by cities, land clearing and food production. Described by Griffith as the only catchment-dedicated postgraduate degree in the world, it is hosted by the International WaterCentre and covers natural sciences, monitoring, data analysis, modelling and economics. It runs one to two years full-time depending on entry point.

name: Master of Cinematic Arts
description: The Master of Cinematic Arts at Griffith University involves research and practical work in a chosen discipline of animation, film and screen production, or games, studied at Griffith Film School with its high-end equipment and studios. Students engage in research and professional development toward innovation and career acceleration, including studio projects supervised by discipline leads and, where applicable, industry partners, and produce creative works in collaboration with peers and external stakeholders. Practice-based work may take cross-disciplinary approaches exploring new and emerging platforms and media. It runs one to two years full-time.

name: Master of Civil Engineering
description: Griffith's Master of Civil Engineering is a 120-credit-point degree, one to 1.5 years full-time, taught at the Gold Coast, that extends an undergraduate civil engineering qualification with advanced study across the field's specialisations. It is aimed at practising civil engineers who want to develop their design skills and their ability to analyse and solve structural problems in real-world applications. Entry is a bachelor degree in a related discipline, with IELTS 6.5. Graduates take senior roles in the building, construction, infrastructure and mining industries, providing structural analysis and design for projects such as roads, bridges, tunnels, water networks and high-rise buildings. Indicative international tuition is around A$46,500 per year.

name: Master of Civil Engineering Advanced
description: Griffith University's Master of Civil Engineering Advanced degree. This program provides students with advanced study across the breadth of specialisations in Civil Engineering. It is designed to extend and deepen the knowledge and skills gained from an undergraduate degree in civil engineering. It is ideal for professional civil engineers who aspire to develop their design skills and advance their capabilities to analyse and solve structural problems and manage projects across a wide range of real-world civil engineering applications. The program provides a pathway to a research higher degree.
curriculum:
Compulsory courses: Advanced Topics in Engineering Management, Advanced Reinforced and Pre-stressed Concrete, Advanced Steel Structures, Advanced Geotechnical Engineering, Project Evaluation and Control, Advanced Foundation Engineering, Advanced Water Engineering Practice, Engineering Communication and Leadership
Plus 5 elective/flexible courses chosen from an approved list to complete the 160 credit-point program.

name: Master of Clinical Dentistry
description: Griffith's Master of Clinical Dentistry is an 80-credit-point degree, one year full-time, taught at the Gold Coast, for qualified dentists who want to strengthen advanced general-practice skills. Students choose one of three majors, implant dentistry, oral surgery or prosthodontics, and study through seminars, journal clubs, supervised clinical practice and a research project, applying the enhanced skills directly in practice. Entry is a bachelor degree in dentistry, current professional registration, clinical experience and an interview, and IELTS 7.0, so it is aimed at practising dentists rather than new graduates. The program integrates academic learning with extensive clinical experience so skills can be applied immediately in practice. Graduates deliver advanced procedures within general dental practice in their chosen area of implant dentistry, oral surgery or prosthodontics. Indicative international tuition is around A$77,000 per year.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: Prepare for a career as a clinical psychologist. Through a combination of rigorous coursework, applied research and extensive professional placements, you'll develop advanced assessment, intervention and therapeutic skills while building the professional confidence and ethical practice required of a registered clinical psychologist. Highlights of studying the Master of Clinical Psychology Complete over 1,000 hours of professional placements in Griffith University clinics and partner organisations, including rural, regional and external settings. Gain direct experience managing therapeutic caseloads, both individually and in groups. Develop expertise in assessment, diagnosis, formulation, neuropsychology and evidence-based interventions. Apply advanced research methods to clinical projects, building skills in critical evaluation and independent research. Learn from highly experienced academics and practising psychologists, with close supervision and mentoring. Prepare for eligibility for full registration with the Psychology Board of Australia or entry into the Registrar program for clinical psychology. Practical learning for clinical practice From your first placements in the Griffith University Psychology Clinic to external practicum experiences, you'll integrate theory and practice to develop competence in psychological assessment, therapy and professional decision-making. The degree's applied focus ensures you gain the clinical confidence, ethical awareness and practical expertise to provide high-quality care. Provisional registration as a psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia It is a requirement that students enrolled in this degree have and maintain either provisional or full registration as a Psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia via the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (Ahpra) for the duration of the program.
curriculum: Plus 15 elective/flexible courses chosen from an approved list to complete the 160 credit-point program.
admission_requirements: Accredited Bachelor of Psychology (Honours), professional registration, interview
english_requirements: English language requirements apply to International applicants and other applicants whose previous study was undertaken in a language other than English in a recognised country*. The English Language Requirements for this accredited program are HIGHER than the requirements stipulated in University policy. The minimum English language requirements for such applicants for entry to this program are as follows: - IELTS (Academic): Overall score of 7.0, with a minimum score of 7.0 in each of the listening, reading and speaking components, and a minimum score of 6.5 in writing; OR - Occupational English Test (OET): Minimum score of B in each of the listening, reading, and speaking components, and a minimum score of C+ in writing; OR - TOEFL iBT: Minimum overall score of 94, with a minimum score of 24 in each of the listening, reading and writing components, and a minimum score of 23 in speaking; OR - Pearson Test of English (Academic): Minimum overall score of 66, with a minimum score of 66 in each of the listening, reading, and speaking components, and a minimum score of 56 in writing; OR - Cambridge (C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency): Minimum overall score of 185, with a minimum score of 185 in each of the listening, reading, and speaking components, and a minimum score of 176 in writing; OR - Successful completion of at least two years of secondary education and your entire tertiary studies in psychology taught and assessed solely in English from a recognised country*; OR - Successful completion of at least six years (full time equivalent) education, including your tertiary qualifications in psychology, that were taught and assessed solely in English from a recognised country* prior to commencement. name: Master of Clinical Psychology Practice
description: Griffith's Master of Clinical Psychology Practice is an 80-credit-point degree, one year full-time, taught at the Gold Coast and Brisbane South, developed with industry to prepare psychologists and provisional psychologists for a sustainable career in clinical psychology. Students learn advanced techniques for clinical psychological assessment, case conceptualisation, and the implementation and evaluation of interventions, and complete 750 hours of supervised psychological practice under accredited clinical psychologist supervisors. The degree is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council. Entry requires provisional or general psychology registration, and IELTS 7.0. Graduates work in Queensland Health and child and youth mental health services, education, corrections, health psychology, non-government agencies, private hospitals and general practice, and private practice. Indicative international tuition is around A$37,500 per year.

name: Master of Cybersecurity
description: Griffith's Master of Cyber Security is a 160-credit-point degree, 1.5 to two years full-time, taught at Brisbane City, the Gold Coast and online. It combines core cyber security principles with management, governance and digital investigations, covering risk mitigation, data privacy protection and governance, and how to assess vulnerabilities and respond to attacks across business, government and infrastructure. The degree is professionally accredited by the Australian Computer Society. Entry is a recognised bachelor degree with a grade point average of at least 4.0, and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work in cyber security analysis, architecture and management, forensic computer analysis, security consultancy, and security and compliance auditing. Indicative international tuition is around A$43,000 per year.

name: Master of Data Science
description: Griffith's Master of Data Science is a 160-credit-point degree, one to two years full-time, taught online and at the Gold Coast and Brisbane South. Griffith is ranked Queensland's leading university for AI research in the 2025 ShanghaiRanking Global Ranking of Academic Subjects. Study develops advanced skills in analytics, machine learning and big data, including programming, data wrangling, statistical modelling and visualisation with tools such as Python and SQL, applied through industry-focused projects. Entry is a recognised bachelor degree, with IELTS 6.5. Graduates work as data scientists, machine learning engineers, data engineers, analytics consultants, business intelligence analysts, risk analysts and research scientists. Indicative international tuition is around A$45,000 per year.

name: Master of Dentistry
description: Take the final step towards a career as a registered dentist with the Master of Dentistry. Building on the knowledge and skills developed in the Bachelor of Dental Health Science, this program provides the professional training required to apply for registration as a dentist in Australia. Note: students can only enter this program if they have successfully completed the Bachelor of Dental Health Science (or the Bachelor of Oral Health in Dental Science) at Griffith University. Highlights of studying the Master of Dentistry Develop specialist skills in dentistry, including oral surgery, orthodontics, prosthodontics, periodontics, paediatrics and special needs dentistry. Refine clinical techniques and simulate private practice to build confidence managing patients in real-world settings. Lead innovation through a group research project, analysing and applying emerging knowledge in dental science. Exciting clinical placements Gain advanced clinical and research expertise in oral health through placements in metropolitan, regional and rural communities. You'll work in diverse community settings across Queensland, providing much-needed services while preparing for the realities of dental practice. You may also undertake extensive clinical work in our purpose-built Griffith Dental Clinic. Through a combination of simulated practice, applied learning and research, you'll graduate with the confidence and expertise to provide high-quality patient care across a wide range of clinical contexts. Build precision, compassion and confidence in dental care Dentistry involves blending clinical precision with compassionate patient care. Throughout your studies, you'll learn how to diagnose, manage and treat complex dental conditions while building strong communication and problem-solving skills essential for professional practice.
curriculum: Compulsory courses: Foundations of Research Inquiry, Professional Practice 2, Clinical Dental Sciences 7, Clinical Dental Sciences 8, Quantitative Research, Qualitative Research, Professional Practice 2, Clinical Dental Sciences 9, Clinical Dental Sciences 10, Professional Practice 3, Research Project, Professional Practice 3, Research Project
admission_requirements: Bachelor of Dental Health Science or Bachelor of Oral Health in Dental Science

name: Master of Design
description: The Master of Design at Griffith University is an exploration of 21st-century creative practice for current or emerging designers who want to become design leaders with social design skills. It equips designers with concepts, strategies and technologies to solve complex real-life problems while prioritising ethical and sustainable practice, respecting First Nations cultures and perspectives, and embracing environmental stewardship. Students advance their skills across strategic visual communication, experience and interaction design, and leadership and social design, and gain industry exposure through a placement course. It runs one to two years full-time.

name: Master of Education
description: Griffith's Master of Education is a 160-credit-point degree, one to two years full-time, taught at Brisbane South and online, for educators and professionals working across schools, tertiary settings, community organisations and government. Study deepens knowledge of contemporary education practice, research and reform, with majors in culturally responsive studies, digital learning, international studies, leading in education, or wellbeing in education. It is not designed to lead to initial teacher registration or early childhood accreditation. Entry is a recognised bachelor degree with relevant work experience, and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work as curriculum innovators, learning and teaching specialists, education administrators, and training and development managers. Indicative international tuition is around A$37,500 per year.

name: Master of Education and Professional Studies Research
description: The Master of Education and Professional Studies Research at Griffith University is designed for educators and professionals who want to deepen their expertise and advance their careers through research. Students build advanced knowledge in research design and methodology while completing a substantial dissertation of approximately 30,000 words on a topic of their choice, learning to apply both qualitative and quantitative research methods. Supported by expert supervisors, graduates gain the ability to influence policy and practice and can progress to doctoral study. It runs one year full-time.

name: Master of Engineering Project Management
description: Griffith University's Master of Engineering Project Management degree. Take your engineering career to the next level by combining technical expertise with advanced project management skills. This degree equips professional engineers with the knowledge to plan, manage and deliver complex projects across a range of industries, including civil infrastructure, energy, mining, built environment and facility management. Highlights of studying the Master of Engineering Project Management Gain advanced skills in project planning, evaluation, control and risk management. Develop the leadership and high-level communication skills essential for engineering management. Learn to integrate quality, safety and environmental management systems into projects. Apply research methods to solve practical engineering challenges and support evidence-based decision-making. Work through project simulations and industry case studies to build practical expertise. Optional advanced study prepares you for higher degree research (PhD) or specialised consultancy. Hands-on experience and industry relevance Guided by expert supervisors, you'll complete major projects that mirror contemporary engineering challenges. Through workshops, case studies and industry-focused assessments, you'll learn to apply advanced project management tools, evaluate project performance and implement solutions that meet regulatory, budgetary and sustainability requirements.

The program provides a pathway to a research higher degree.

name: Master of Environment
description: The Master of Environment at Griffith University builds expertise to engage with environmental decision-making, tackle complex sustainability challenges, contribute to policy, and guide organisations toward responsible environmental practice. Students learn from academics and industry experts across climate adaptation, environmental planning, business sustainability and conservation practice, build advanced skills in environmental economics, pollution assessment and water resource management, and gain research capability through training in research design and data analysis. Students can tailor study with a major. It runs one to two years full-time depending on entry point.

name: Master of Environmental Engineering
description: Griffith's Master of Environmental Engineering is a 120-credit-point degree, one to 1.5 years full-time, taught at Brisbane South and online. It develops understanding of complex environmental problems and the skills to design engineering solutions and manage projects in solid and hazardous waste management, air quality monitoring and control, and water and wastewater treatment. Entry is a bachelor degree plus relevant work experience, with IELTS 6.5. Graduates lead environmental engineering practice in the public sector, resource and infrastructure sectors, and consulting engineering, working with organisations dealing with waste, wastewater and air pollution control. Indicative international tuition is around A$46,500 per year.

name: Master of Environmental Engineering and Pollution Control
description: Griffith University's Master of Environmental Engineering and Pollution Control degree. The wants and needs of a rapidly expanding, global population means it has never been more important to shape our environmental future. Environmental engineering is your pathway to protecting the natural environment and its resources by ensuring that we minimise the adverse effect we may have on it. In this program you will develop an understanding of complex environmental problems and issues, and of the challenges facing environmental sustainability. You will learn to design creative engineering solutions and manage key projects associated with environmental protection in the area of solid and hazardous waste management, air quality monitoring and control, water and wastewater treatment, and renewable energy. You will develop the skills to incorporate sustainability concepts into engineering work practices from various discipline backgrounds.
curriculum:
Compulsory courses: Cleaner Production and Circular Economy, Industrial Water and Wastewater Treatment, Engineering Communication and Leadership, Hydrologic and Hydraulic Modelling, Air Quality Monitoring and Control, Renewable Energy Systems, Advanced Water and Wastewater Engineering, Environmental Management Systems
Plus 17 elective/flexible courses chosen from an approved list to complete the 160 credit-point program.

name: Master of Finance
description: Griffith's Master of Finance is a 160-credit-point degree, one to two years full-time, taught at Brisbane City, Brisbane South and online. It delivers advanced technical and quantitative capability for investment analysis, portfolio management and financial risk, for graduates entering finance or accelerating within it. The program is in the CFA Institute University Affiliation Program and its ESG Investing recognition program, and is an academic partner of the Global Association of Risk Professionals for the Financial Risk Manager credential. Entry is a bachelor degree in any discipline, with IELTS 6.5. Graduates work in banking, investment management and financial services, including with superannuation and mutual funds, insurers and consulting firms. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,000 per year.

name: Master of Financial Crime Investigation and Compliance
description: Griffith's Master of Financial Crime Investigation and Compliance is a 160-credit-point degree, one to two years full-time, taught online and at Brisbane South. It equips graduates to ensure compliance with local and global regulation and to investigate the illegal or inappropriate use of funds, covering money laundering, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorism financing frameworks, evolving regulatory requirements, and the risks created by new technology and inefficient operations. Entry is a bachelor degree in any discipline with a grade point average of at least 4.0, and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work in compliance, risk analysis, auditing and investigation, in high demand across the financial sector in risk management and crime prevention roles. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,000 per year.

name: Master of Financial Technology
description: Griffith's Master of Financial Technology is a 160-credit-point degree, one to two years full-time, taught at Brisbane South and online, for people with or without a background in IT or finance who want to work in fintech. Study spans big data analytics, artificial intelligence, blockchain, programming and cybersecurity alongside how financial markets function, with a strong applied and advanced-spreadsheet component. Entry is a bachelor degree in any discipline with a grade point average of at least 4.0, and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work as financial application developers, data and financial analysts, cybersecurity analysts, compliance specialists, risk analysts and financial services consultants with banks, funds, insurers and treasury teams. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,000 per year.

name: Master of Global Development
description: Griffith's Master of Global Development is a 160-credit-point degree, one to two years full-time, taught online and at Brisbane South, built around the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Study covers policy, politics, people and power across development contexts, and students choose one of six majors: climate change and disaster management, development economics, global health, human rights, politics and planning, or sustainable development. Entry is a recognised bachelor degree with a grade point average of at least 4.0, and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work with non-government and aid organisations, in international development, government policy, consultancy and research, with employers such as the United Nations, the World Bank, Oxfam and the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. Indicative international tuition is around A$38,500 per year.

name: Master of Global Public Health
description: Griffith University's Master of Global Public Health degree. This program helps you to develop and further your career in public health practice, research and/or management. It allows you to re-orient your work interests in health to disease prevention and health promotion and is widely recognised both nationally and internationally as the public health credential for careers in public health. The program focuses on the socio-ecological model of public health that emphasises and analyses the important interactions between the social, biological, economic and environmental determinants of health. It enables you to apply this analytical skill set to plan, implement and evaluate population-based interventions that protect and promote health. The program has a strong focus on global health and provides you with the opportunity to focus your public health studies by selecting from a range of electives in areas such as public health nutrition, health promotion, climate change, planetary health, and health services management.
curriculum:
Compulsory courses: Community Engagement in Health Promotion, Global Health and Human Rights, Epidemiology: Principles and Practices, Foundations of Research Inquiry, Public Health Practice, Global Health: Priorities and Interventions, Environment and Population Health

name: Master of Health and Medical Research
description: The Master of Health and Medical Research at Griffith University gives graduates the opportunity to undertake advanced study and research, providing training in applied research and methodology to prepare for higher degree by research studies and professional employment in research. The program combines coursework, which covers critical evaluation of research, statistical analysis techniques and research proposal design, with a major research project undertaken under the supervision of a leading researcher, culminating in a seminar and thesis. It runs about 1.5 years full-time.

name: Master of Health Services Management
description: Griffith's Master of Health Services Management is a 120-credit-point degree, one to 1.5 years full-time, taught at Brisbane City and online, for clinicians, health professionals and managers in the health, aged and community care sectors. Study covers healthcare management, health policy, governance and value-based care, along with health workforce planning, human resource management, and healthcare finance and budgeting. The degree is accredited by the Australasian College of Health Service Management. Entry is a bachelor degree, with IELTS 6.5. Graduates work as health service and clinical services managers, health policy advisers, quality and safety managers, and program managers in health and aged care. Indicative international tuition is around A$38,500 per year.

name: Master of Human Resource Management and Employment Relations
description: Griffith's Master of Human Resource Management and Employment Relations is a 120-credit-point degree, one to 1.5 years full-time, taught at the Gold Coast, Brisbane South and online. It covers HR strategy, evidence-based HRM, organisational change, international and comparative HRM, recruitment and selection, and performance and reward, alongside employment law, negotiation, dispute resolution and managing workplace equity. The degree is accredited by the Australian HR Institute. Entry is a bachelor degree in a related discipline with a grade point average of at least 4.0, and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work as HR managers, employment relations managers, HR business partners, and recruitment or training specialists. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,000 per year.

name: Master of Information Systems and Information Technology Management
description: Griffith's Master of Information Systems and Information Technology Management is a 160-credit-point degree, one to two years full-time, taught at Brisbane City. It combines technical and managerial content so graduates can both work with and manage information technology in organisations, with a grounding in IT principles and practice and an in-depth understanding of information and communication technologies and information systems. Students learn to manage the information technology function in an organisation while keeping enough technical depth to work directly with systems, covering systems analysis and design, databases, IT governance and the management of technology projects. Entry is a recognised bachelor degree, with IELTS 6.5. Graduates work as systems analysts and developers, web and e-commerce developers, database designers and administrators, and information technology managers across public and private sector organisations. Indicative international tuition is around A$43,500 per year.

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Griffith's Master of IT sits inside the university's Nathan campus tech precinct, a short walk from the Cyber Range that the School of ICT built with defence-industry funding. Students in the security specialisation actually run attack-and-defend exercises against simulated networks there rather than just reading about them. The degree is built for career-changers: roughly half of any given cohort arrives with an undergraduate degree in something unrelated (commerce, biology, the occasional music grad) and the first trimester is deliberately weighted toward programming fundamentals and systems thinking before the specialisations open up.

From second trimester students pick a track (software development, data science, network and cyber security, or enterprise systems), and the coursework gets noticeably more project-based, with several units assessed entirely on a working deliverable rather than exams. Griffith's industry ties in South-East Queensland (Telstra, Suncorp, various defence primes based near Amberley) mean the capstone project frequently comes with a real client brief attached, not a simulated one.

Graduates skew toward Brisbane's growing cyber security and fintech employers, though a decent slice go on to further study: Griffith runs a fairly well-used PhD pipeline out of this cohort for students who get hooked on a research problem during the capstone.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Programming Foundations, Systems Analysis and Design, Database Systems, Networking Principles
Trimester 2: Software Engineering, choice of specialisation stream begins (Software Development / Data Science / Cyber Security / Enterprise Systems)
Specialisation core units (varies by stream): Secure Systems Programming, Applied Machine Learning, Enterprise Architecture, or Advanced Web Development
Electives: two or three units drawn from the broader ICT school offering, including Cloud Computing and IT Project Management
Final trimester: industry-linked Capstone Project (client-brief based), plus one advanced elective
Non-IT-background entrants complete an additional foundation trimester before the above sequence

name: Master of Integrated Water Management
description: The Master of Integrated Water Management at Griffith University creates water leaders by drawing on international teaching and research across many fields to provide a trans-disciplinary, whole-of-water-cycle approach to water management. It builds the capacity of future leaders working in water, sanitation and hygiene, urban water management, and water finance for the achievement of sustainable development goals, equipping students with practical tools and skills to develop and manage innovative solutions to local, regional, national and international water issues. The program is led by the International WaterCentre. It runs one to two years full-time.

name: Master of International Business
description: Griffith's Master of International Business is a 120-credit-point degree, one to 1.5 years full-time, taught online and at Brisbane South and Brisbane City. It builds advanced international business knowledge, cross-cultural leadership and digital economy insight for graduates and professionals aiming to work in multinational environments. Study covers international trade and investment, cross-cultural management, global strategy, and doing business in emerging markets. Entry is a recognised bachelor degree, with IELTS 6.5. Griffith is based in Queensland with campuses in Brisbane and the Gold Coast. Graduates move into senior and specialist roles in multinational corporations, export and trade organisations, consulting firms, and public sector agencies engaged in international trade and investment, and the 120-credit-point structure lets those with a business background finish in a year. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,000 per year.

name: Master of International Law
description: Griffith's Master of International Law is a 120-credit-point degree, one to 1.5 years full-time, taught at the Gold Coast, Brisbane City and online. It develops expertise in international law, international relations and international dispute resolution, framed around global problems that require coordinated rather than purely national responses, such as pandemics, terrorism, and climate change. Study covers public international law, human rights, international trade and investment law, and the institutions that make and enforce global rules. Entry is a bachelor degree, with IELTS 6.5, and the 120-credit-point structure suits both law graduates and professionals from other fields who work across borders. Graduates work as legal and policy professionals across government, private practice and the not-for-profit sector, and in diplomacy and international organisations. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,000 per year.

name: Master of International Law Studies
description: Griffith University's Master of International Law Studies degree. This program is scheduled for delivery at the Treasury Building at our Brisbane City campus in 2027, as well as Gold Coast and Online. If the scheduled opening of Treasury Building is delayed, courses may be delivered all or in part at our other locations. Queensland's #1 university for law and criminology. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2025) The Master of International Law Studies is designed for ambitious professionals and emerging scholars who want to understand how law operates across borders, cultures and international systems. You'll explore how global rules are made, contested, enforced and applied in real legal, political and commercial contexts. Whether you're advancing your legal career or moving into an international-facing role, this degree will give you the expertise to operate effectively in a global environment. Highlights of studying the Master of International Law Studies Build strong foundations in public international law, global law principles and international negotiations. Examine issues like human rights, criminal justice, environmental law, trade, intellectual property and armed conflict. Develop practical skills for handling cross-border disputes, international family matters and global commercial litigation. Be guided by academics and industry experts with deep experience in international courts, tribunals and policy environments. Deepen your expertise through electives in global security, climate policy, international relations and cyber law. Strengthen your research capability with advanced research methods and the option to complete an independent research project.

name: Master of International Relations
description: The Master of International Relations at Griffith University builds advanced knowledge and analytical skills for navigating global politics, teaching students to critically assess global events, interpret international policy and contribute to informed decision-making. Students work with experienced lecturers to explore diplomacy and statecraft, international security, human rights, globalisation and international organisations, analyse power, justice, peace and order in world politics, examine Australia's foreign policy and engagement with Asia and the United States, and study terrorism, nuclear proliferation and environmental security. It runs one to two years full-time depending on entry point.

name: Master of International Tourism and Hospitality Management
description: Griffith's Master of International Tourism and Hospitality Management is a 160-credit-point degree, one to two years full-time, taught at the Gold Coast and online. It develops managerial capability for the global tourism and hotel industry, covering business acumen, strategic thinking, people management and leadership with an emphasis on sustainability, and deepens core skills in revenue management, finance, marketing and technology and digitisation. Entry is a recognised bachelor degree, with IELTS 6.5. Graduates work in hotel and resort management and the accommodation sector, and in convention and event organisations, government and destination marketing, theme parks and attractions, national park authorities and travel retail. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,000 per year.

name: Master of Marketing
description: Griffith's Master of Marketing is a 120-credit-point degree, one to 1.5 years full-time, taught at the Gold Coast, Brisbane City and online. It builds advanced expertise in digital marketing, brand strategy, consumer behaviour, marketing analytics and integrated marketing communication for people aiming at senior and specialist roles. The degree is accredited by the Australian Marketing Institute. Entry is a bachelor degree in any field with a grade point average of at least 4.0, and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work as marketing managers, brand managers, digital marketing strategists, marketing analytics specialists, communications managers and senior marketing consultants across fast-moving consumer goods, tourism, entertainment, public relations, advertising and the not-for-profit sector. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,000 per year.

name: Master of Materials Science
discontinued_note: The Master of Materials Science has been discontinued with no live listing or direct successor found in Griffith's current degree search.

name: Master of Music
description: The Master of Music at Griffith University lets students choose specialisations to suit their professional goals and collaborate with peers to develop creativity, learning independence and pedagogical agility. It is delivered by the Queensland Conservatorium, one of Australia's leading music and performing arts schools, with well-equipped facilities and experienced lecturers. Majors include pedagogy, with a focus on experiential cross-training design and knowledge across a range of styles, and the Conservatorium's particularly renowned vocal pedagogy for emerging and experienced singing teachers. It runs one to 1.5 years full-time.

name: Master of Nursing Science
description: Griffith University's Master of Nursing Science degree. Australia's #1 university for nursing and midwifery. (ShanghaiRanking's Global Ranking of Academic Subjects 2025) Designed for registered nurses, this postgraduate degree builds on your existing experience and provides the expertise needed to take on leadership, education, research and advanced practice roles in healthcare. With a strong focus on research, quality and safety and elevated clinical capability, this degree supports your progression into senior nursing positions. Highlights of studying the Master of Nursing Science Strengthen your understanding of research inquiry and evidence-informed practice. Build capability in quality and safety within complex healthcare environments. Prepare for advanced clinical practice through coursework focused on collaboration and critical decision-making. Develop the leadership skills to support innovation and improvement across healthcare services. Gain expertise in health education, curriculum design and student assessment. Design, refine and complete a small-scale research project through a structured dissertation pathway with guided academic supervision. Develop advanced skills for contemporary nursing practice Deepen your knowledge in areas essential to modern healthcare. Study core courses in research inquiry, transformation and leadership, advanced practice in chronic health conditions and learning and teaching for health professionals. You'll also tailor your research development through options in quantitative and/or qualitative research or clinical trials. Industry and expert connections Learn from highly awarded academics with strong professional networks across the health sector. Industry consultation ensures the program remains current, rigorous and aligned with employer expectations. Graduates are also eligible to apply for Higher Degree Research programs.

name: Master of Pharmacy
description: Griffith University's Master of Pharmacy degree. Take the next step to becoming a registered pharmacist with the Master of Pharmacy, an accredited graduate-entry degree designed to prepare you for a rewarding career improving health outcomes through the safe and effective use of medicines. Building on your undergraduate science or health science background, this degree delivers advanced knowledge in pharmaceutical science, clinical pharmacy practice and research to develop you into a confident, skilled healthcare professional. Highlights of studying the Master of Pharmacy Gain the academic qualification required for eligibility to register as a pharmacist in Australia. Develop clinical expertise through placements in community, hospital and specialist pharmacy settings. Learn from experienced pharmacists, clinicians and researchers actively shaping the future of medicine use and patient care. Build advanced communication, problem-solving and decision-making skills through simulated and collaborative learning experiences. Explore innovative drug delivery systems, quality use of medicines and evidence-based therapeutic management. Enhance your understanding of health leadership, ethics and pharmacy management to prepare for diverse career pathways. Graduate ready to make an impact in patient care Through a mix of classroom learning, clinical placements and professional simulations, you'll gain the knowledge and experience needed to support patients across all stages of care. You'll graduate prepared to enter an internship program with the skills to improve medication safety, promote health literacy and deliver person-centred care.

name: Master of Primary Teaching
description: Griffith University's Master of Primary Teaching degree. Make a difference in children's lives and contribute to the future of education. The Master of Primary Teaching offers an exciting pathway to becoming a qualified teacher, focusing on educating children from Prep to Year 6. This program is designed for those who hold a bachelor degree in another field and wish to transition into teaching. Highlights of studying the Master of Primary Teaching Combine theoretical knowledge with practical classroom experience to meet the diverse needs of young learners. Study foundational topics including childhood development, educational psychology, curriculum design and inclusive teaching practices. Focus on literacy, numeracy and strategies to foster positive student outcomes. Complete 60 days of supervised school placements, applying learning in real classrooms with guidance from experienced mentors. Develop skills to manage diverse classrooms, differentiate teaching, integrate technology and adopt innovative strategies. This postgraduate pre-service teacher education program is offered in intensive mode to enable completion in one and a half years or over two years full-time. Graduate ready to inspire the next generation This degree has a strong focus on ethical practice, cultural awareness, and understanding education systems and policies. With demand for qualified teachers continuing to grow, completing a Master of Primary Teaching opens rewarding career opportunities.

English test results must be no more than two years old. The Direct Entry Program (DEP) pathway is not accepted for this program. This program is accredited and language requirements have been set to ensure applicants meet both Griffith University language requirements and requirements for registration within Queensland. The Queensland College of Teachers requires graduating teachers to provide evidence of English Language Proficiency (ELP) with their application for registration unless they have completed the full four years of higher education study required for registration in English in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Republic of Ireland, United Kingdom or the United States of America. Further information is available on the Queensland College of Teachers website.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: Griffith University Master of Professional Accounting lets non-accounting university graduates gain an accounting qualification accredited by the Australian professional bodies. It runs 2.5 years full-time at the Nathan campus, with a Graduate Diploma of Professional Accounting available as an exit point after 120 credit points of Group A courses; the graduate diploma is accredited by Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand and CPA Australia. Griffith is a registered CPA Program tuition provider, so students can prepare for the CPA Program professional-level examinations during the degree. A Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting provides an entry pathway for graduates from non-accounting backgrounds. Indicative international tuition is around A$40,500 per year. Graduates work in accounting, auditing, managerial accounting, taxation, forensic accounting, government and treasury, corporate and private practice, and consulting.

name: Master of Professional Engineering
description: Griffith University's Master of Professional Engineering degree. The Master of Professional Engineering is for aspiring engineers who want to obtain accredited qualifications to practise as an engineer in Australia and overseas, or for existing professional engineers to move into a different field of engineering. The program focuses on the knowledge and skills required to design solutions and manage engineering projects in a holistic way.
curriculum: Compulsory courses: Research Methods for Engineers, Project Management, Industry Affiliates Program - Dissertation
admission_requirements: A recognised Bachelor of Engineering (or higher) in a related discipline A recognised three year Diploma of Engineering and a completed 40CP Masters Qualifying Program (Engineering) from Griffith College

name: Master of Professional Psychology
description: Griffith University's Master of Professional Psychology degree. This degree integrates supervised placement experiences and coursework focused on psychological practice. You will learn how to practice professionally and ethically and to communicate and collaborate effectively as you gain skills in evaluating client needs, designing and implementing evidence-based interventions and evaluating outcomes. This program has been designed to meet the requirements for the fifth year of a 5+1 pathway to general registration as a Psychologist. Enrolment in this program may allow you to register as a provisional Psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia as part of the requirements of a 5+1 pathway and prepares you for eligibility to complete a +1 internship as a provisional Psychologist.
curriculum: Compulsory courses: Professional and Ethical Skills, Assessment, Diagnosis and Formulation, Lifespan Psychopathology and Therapy 1, Practice Skills for Psychologists, Assessment and Evaluation, Lifespan Psychopathology and Therapy 2, Placement
admission_requirements: Accredited Bachelor (Honours) degree in Psychology, professional registration and interview

A maximum of two years break while obtaining your qualifications and advanced education will be accepted; OR - Successful completion of at least ten years of primary and secondary education taught and assessed solely in English in a recognised country* and your entire tertiary qualifications in psychology taught and assessed in any country solely in English. The Direct Entry Program (DEP) pathway is not accepted for this program.

name: Master of Public Health
description:
Griffith's MPH sits within the Menzies Health Institute Queensland research grouping, which gives the degree a noticeably strong lean toward chronic disease epidemiology and health services research relative to a public health program housed inside a standalone medical school. Griffith's public health researchers do a lot of work on obesity, diabetes, and Indigenous health outcomes specifically, and that shows up in elective choice and guest lecture content.

The cohort is genuinely international and mixed-career: working clinicians (nurses, allied health professionals, occasional doctors) doing the degree to move into policy or management roles sit alongside students coming straight from an undergraduate science or health degree with no clinical background at all, and Griffith structures the core sequence to be accessible to both without dumbing down the epidemiology and biostatistics content.

Students choose a specialisation stream (health promotion, epidemiology, or health management), and the practicum placement component, done with a health department, hospital, or NGO, is where the degree earns its practical reputation; Griffith's Queensland Health connections mean placements are relatively easy to secure compared to some interstate programs.
curriculum:
Core: Foundations of Public Health, Biostatistics, Epidemiology, Health Promotion Theory and Practice, Health Systems and Policy
Specialisation stream (choose): Epidemiology, Health Promotion, or Health Management
Research methods unit and choice of either a research minor-thesis or coursework-only pathway
Practicum placement with a health department, hospital, or community health organisation
Capstone: Public Health Project applying core skills to a real health issue
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Science
description: The Master of Science at Griffith University is a two-year full-time program providing advanced study and research training in applied scientific research and methodology, preparing graduates for higher degree studies and professional employment. The program combines theoretical and practical coursework with a research dissertation, with advanced coursework completed before the research component. Coursework covers critical evaluation of research, statistical analysis techniques and research proposal design, and students undertake a major research project under the supervision of a leading researcher.

name: Master of Secondary Teaching
description: Prepare for a fulfilling career in secondary education and help shape the minds of the next generation. With a growing demand for qualified teachers across Australia, Griffith's Master of Secondary Teaching focuses on educating children from Year 7 to 12. This program is designed for those who hold a bachelor degree in another field and wish to transition into teaching. Highlights of studying the Master of Secondary Teaching Combine theory and hands-on experience to teach subject areas and manage secondary classrooms effectively. Study adolescent development, curriculum design, assessment, and classroom management. Develop critical thinking and engage with contemporary issues in education. Complete 60 days of supervised school placements with mentorship from experienced teachers to refine your teaching skills and strategies. This degree has an emphasis on the importance of differentiated instruction to meet the diverse needs of secondary students. You will need to identify two of the following Teaching Areas to form your study: Biology# Business Chemistry# Design technologies Digital technologies Drama English Food and nutrition Geography Health and physical education History Instrumental music# Languages Mathematics Music Physics# Psychology# Visual arts # These teaching areas must be taken at a senior level and require a minimum of six subjects in each area in the undergraduate degree.

Plus 38 elective/flexible courses chosen from an approved list to complete the 160 credit-point program.

Further information is available on the Queensland College of Teachers website.

name: Master of Social Work
description: Make an impact in your community as a social work practitioner. At Griffith, we value your commitment to making a difference. This professional qualifying degree builds on your lived experiences, equipping you with the expertise, practical skills and ethical grounding to become a confident advocate for those most in need. You'll graduate ready to make an impact, support individuals, families and groups, strengthen communities and lead meaningful change across social and human services. Highlights of studying the Master of Social Work Study courses in social work practice, research, First Peoples and social justice, counselling, ethics and leadership, human rights, law, policy and group facilitation. Gain an Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW) accredited qualification, meeting Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards (ASWEAS). Develop as an ethical, innovative thinker, communicator and leader, ready to drive positive change in complex professional environments. Build practical skills through social work field placements Start making a difference while you study and apply your learning through two extensive field placements. You'll complete a minimum 1,000 hours of practice-based learning in human service organisations, guided by qualified social work supervisors. Across both placements, you'll progressively develop the skills, knowledge and professional mindset required for effective practice. The first 500-hour placement introduces you to the realities of the profession, while the second 500-hour placement builds on this foundation with more advanced responsibilities and deeper critical reflection. Placements are designed so you'll gain the confidence and capability to graduate as a skilled, socially responsible practitioner ready to make an impact in diverse social work settings.
curriculum: Compulsory courses: Foundations of Social Work Practice, Foundations of Research Inquiry, First Peoples and Social Justice (Advanced), Social Work Theory for Practice, Applied Counselling, Social Work Field Placement 1, Applied Skills and Knowledge for Social Work, Human Services : Law and Social Policy, Interdisciplinary Professional Ethics, Social Work Field Placement 2, Critical Reflective Practice and Leadership
admission_requirements: A recognised Bachelor degree (or higher) in a relevant discipline with at least one year of study in social and behavioural sciences.
english_requirements: English language requirements apply to International applicants and other applicants whose previous study was undertaken in a language other than English. The minimum English language requirements for such applicants for entry to this program are: - A minimum overall band score of 7.0 on IELTS (Academic) with no sub-score of less than 7.0 ; OR - an overall score of 65 in the Pearson Test of English (Academic) with no score less than 65; OR - a minimum score of 580 on TOEFL; OR - an internet-based (iBT) TOEFL score of 92 (no score less than 22); OR - no score less than 4 in each skill of the ISLPR (conducted by ISLPR Language Services only); OR - a minimum overall score of 185 (no score less than 176) on C2 Proficiency (formerly Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English) * The ISLPR test will only be accepted if it has been administered by ISLPR Language Services, 9 Gowrie Street, Mt Gravatt, Queensland. As these requirements may change from time to time, students should contact the AASW to confirm registration requirements. Please refer to the AASW website for further details: Australian Association of Social Workers .

name: Master of Speech Pathology
description: Griffith University's Master of Speech Pathology degree. Step into a rewarding career transforming lives with the Master of Speech Pathology. This program equips you with the advanced knowledge, clinical skills and professional experience required to become a competent, evidence-based speech pathologist. Designed for graduates from other disciplines, the Master of Speech Pathology facilitates the transition into this dynamic and in-demand profession. Highlights of studying the Master of Speech Pathology Develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills through small-group, problem-based learning. Build confidence and competence via hands-on, workplace-based placements in hospitals, schools, aged care and private practice. Explore communication and swallowing disorders across all age groups, from early childhood to older adulthood. Collaborate with allied health professionals, including occupational therapists, dietitians and physiotherapists, to deliver holistic, person-centred care. Gain strong research literacy, ensuring your practice is informed by the latest evidence and innovations in speech pathology. Practical, inquiry-based learning The Master of Speech Pathology uses an engaging, case-based learning model that combines theory with practical application. Through hands-on placements, you'll develop the skills to support the diverse speech pathology needs of children and adults across health, community and educational settings.
curriculum: Compulsory courses: Speech Pathology Skills and Practice 1, Foundations of Speech Pathology, Communication and Swallowing Disorders 1, Speech Pathology Skills and Practice 2, Communication and Swallowing Disorders 2, Foundations of Research Inquiry, Speech Pathology Skills and Practice 3, Communication and Swallowing Disorders 3, Evidence Based Practice and Clinical Research, Speech Pathology Skills and Practice 4, Transition to Professional Practice, Speech Pathology Practice Innovation Project
admission_requirements: A recognised Bachelor degree (5.0 GPA or higher) in a related discipline and interview

English test results must be no more than two years old. The Direct Entry Program (DEP) pathway is not accepted for this program.

name: Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
description: Griffith's Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages is a 120-credit-point degree, 1.5 years full-time, taught at Brisbane South and online. It combines academic knowledge with practical teaching skills for teaching English as a second or foreign language, with a strong focus on the Asia-Pacific region, an intercultural perspective, and the analysis of how second and foreign languages are learned. The degree is endorsed by the National ELT Accreditation Scheme. Entry is a recognised bachelor degree, with IELTS 6.5. Graduates work as language instructors and literacy educators and in directing studies, in TAFE and technical colleges, university language centres, private language schools and migrant language programs, in Australia and overseas. Indicative international tuition is around A$36,500 per year.

name: Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages and Leadership
description: Griffith University's Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages and Leadership degree. This degree is designed to empower you to excel in the global English language teaching field. Gain the skills to teach English to speakers of other languages effectively, and be prepared to step into leadership roles, guiding teams and shaping the future of language education worldwide. Highlights of studying the Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages and Leadership Study twelve TESOL courses (1.5 years) with a focus on teaching English, plus four additional courses (0.5 years) covering global business, educational leadership and international education-giving you a well-rounded skill set for success in the global teaching industry. Study courses like Wellbeing, Global Business Strategy, Corporate Entrepreneurship, and Marketing Foundations, preparing you for roles in diverse educational settings. Acquire skills in guiding educational initiatives, navigating global teaching challenges and integrating sustainable business practices. Understand how second and foreign languages are learned in a variety of contexts with a strong focus on the Asia-Pacific region. Undertake an internship, in which you'll practice English language classroom teaching. An alternative, shorter 1.5-year Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (5757) is also available. Please note that this program does not lead to teacher registration with the Queensland College of Teachers.
curriculum:
Compulsory courses: Global Englishes in TESOL, Technology Enhanced Language Learning and Teaching, Sociolinguistics for Second Language Teachers, Foundations of Research in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages, Second Language Acquisition: Theory and Application, Discourse Analysis, Language Testing and Assessment, Teaching English for Academic Purposes

name: Master of Urban and Environmental Planning
description: Griffith University's Master of Urban and Environmental Planning degree. Advance your career in urban and environmental planning, where strategic thinking meets development and sustainability challenges. You'll be prepared for both traditional planning and environmental practice roles, and equipped with the skills to influence the future of cities, regions and natural environments. With a strong focus on applied learning and multidisciplinary expertise, this program sets you up for a rewarding career addressing some of the most pressing issues facing communities today and into the future. Highlights of studying the Master of Urban and Environmental Planning This masters degree enables you to work as both a town planner and as an environmental planning professional. Learn from leading experts in urban, regional and environmental planning, transport, community development and tourism. Develop advanced skills in spatial analysis, policy development and strategic decision-making. Explore real development challenges through studio-based projects, feasibility studies and scenario planning. Build confidence using tools such as GIS, urban data analytics and evidence-based research methods. Examine contemporary issues including climate adaptation, transport systems, urban growth, housing, environmental protection and community engagement. Apply your knowledge through a research dissertation or work-integrated learning placement, building networks and strengthening your professional readiness. Hands-on experience in planning and development Across foundation, core and flexible modules, you'll work on complex planning problems, from preparing and analysing development proposals to crafting strategic regional plans. Through studio courses, you'll evaluate sites, negotiate constraints, balance environmental considerations and propose innovative solutions for future communities.

name: Master of Visual Arts
description: The Master of Visual Arts at Griffith University is designed for practising artists and graduates seeking to deepen their creative knowledge and produce an ambitious body of work for exhibition. Through studio-based learning and research-led practice, students develop advanced studio practice across media including drawing, jewellery, painting, photography, printmaking and sculpture, build visual literacy and critical analysis skills, and explore the philosophical, cultural and historical contexts that influence modern art practice. It runs one to two years full-time at the Queensland College of Art and Design.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
Holmes's Bachelor of Business is a 24-unit, three-year degree with four specialisation options (Management, Marketing, International Business and Hospitality Management), the last of which is a slightly unusual inclusion for a business-only private provider and reflects Holmes's history of teaching hospitality alongside its commerce offerings. Students complete a shared core of accounting, economics, law and management units in years one and two before specialising in year three.

As with most of Holmes's degrees, the cohort is heavily international, and the degree functions for a lot of students as the standard three-year pathway toward permanent residency via the skilled migration points test, rather than purely as an academic credential chosen on its own merits. That's not a criticism of the teaching: the core units are solid and cover the same ground as equivalent degrees at larger universities. But it's worth naming plainly rather than pretending every enrolment is driven by intellectual interest in business theory.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Economics for Business; Business Communication; Introduction to Management; Business Law; Quantitative Methods
Year 2: Marketing Principles; Organisational Behaviour; Finance for Business; Business Ethics and Sustainability; Human Resource Management; Business Statistics
Year 3: specialisation strand (four units in Management, Marketing, International Business or Hospitality Management) plus Strategic Management and a capstone business project
Capstone: industry-linked business project or case competition in the final trimester
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Fashion Business
description:
Bachelor of Fashion Business is Holmes's attempt to sit between a straight business degree and a design school program. It teaches merchandising, buying, retail management and fashion marketing rather than pattern-making or garment construction, so students who actually want to design clothes should look elsewhere (RMIT or Whitehouse Institute are the more obvious choices in that space). What this degree is for is the commercial side of the fashion industry: supply chain, brand management, retail analytics and marketing applied specifically to apparel and accessories categories.

It shares a business core with Holmes's other undergraduate business degrees in years one and two, then narrows into fashion-specific units (trend forecasting, fashion retail management, visual merchandising) in year three. Melbourne's retail and wholesale fashion sector gives students some access to local industry placements and guest lecturers, though the program is smaller and less established than Holmes's mainstream business and accounting degrees, and prospective students should treat it as a niche offering rather than a flagship one.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Introduction to Fashion Industry; Business Communication; Economics for Business; Marketing Principles; Business Law
Year 2: Fashion Retail Management; Consumer Behaviour; Finance for Business; Brand Management; Supply Chain Fundamentals; Organisational Behaviour
Year 3: Fashion Buying and Merchandising; Trend Forecasting and Product Development; Visual Merchandising; Digital Marketing for Fashion; Strategic Management; capstone fashion business project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Information Systems
description:
This is a three-year degree for students who want an IT qualification with a business faculty attached rather than an engineering one: the difference matters, because the emphasis throughout is on systems that support organisations (databases, ERP-adjacent platforms, business analytics) rather than low-level programming or hardware. Holmes teaches it out of its Melbourne CBD and Sydney campuses to a mostly international cohort, many of whom are using the degree as a stepping stone toward the 189/190 skilled migration occupation lists that include ICT business analyst and systems analyst roles.

The 24-unit structure moves from foundational programming and database units in year one through systems analysis and network fundamentals in year two, before a final year that includes an IT project unit where students build and document a working system end to end. It suits someone who wants employable IT skills without committing to a heavier computer science or software engineering load, though students aiming specifically at software development roles at larger tech employers may find a more technically dense degree from a research university better positioned for that path.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming; Database Systems; Business Information Systems; Foundations of Business Communication; Accounting for Business Decisions; Quantitative Methods
Year 2: Systems Analysis and Design; Network Fundamentals; Web Application Development; Operating Systems; Business Law; Project Management Principles
Year 3: IT Project Management; Enterprise Systems; Cybersecurity Fundamentals; Data Analytics for Business; two electives
Capstone: IT systems project — students design, build and document a working information system for a simulated or partner organisation
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Professional Accounting
description:
This is the undergraduate counterpart to Holmes's Master of Professional Accounting: a three-year, CPA Australia and CA ANZ accredited degree built around the mandated accounting core (financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, tax, corporate law) plus general business units in the earlier years. It's the more common entry point for school leavers or first-degree students who know from the outset that they want to sit for CPA or CA membership after graduating, rather than coming to accounting via a conversion master's later.

The degree's reputation rests less on Holmes's institutional prestige and more on the fact that accreditation requirements are set externally by the professional bodies, so the technical content lines up closely with what's taught at any accredited Australian accounting degree. Where Holmes differentiates is smaller cohort sizes in tutorials and, for many international students, direct progression pathways from Holmes's own diploma and foundation programs into this degree with credit.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Systems and Processes; Economics for Business; Business Law; Quantitative Methods; Business Communication; Introduction to Management
Year 2: Financial Accounting; Management Accounting; Corporations Law; Financial Management; Business Information Systems; Organisational Behaviour
Year 3: Auditing and Assurance Services; Taxation Law; Advanced Financial Accounting; Ethics and Governance in Accounting; Strategic Management Accounting; capstone accounting project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Australian Senior Secondary Certificate) or equivalent, ATAR approx. 65-75 (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Graduate Diploma of Business
description:
The Graduate Diploma of Business is Holmes's shorter, standalone postgraduate business qualification: eight units over roughly eight months full-time, sitting below the MBA in the institute's course ladder and often used either as a terminal qualification for someone wanting a fast credential upgrade, or as a stepping stone that later articulates into the MBA with advanced standing.

The unit mix covers the standard generalist ground (accounting, marketing, management, economics) without the specialisation and elective units that round out the full MBA, so it's a leaner degree by design. Students who complete it and want to continue can usually move into Holmes's MBA with credit for overlapping units, which is the more common path than treating the Graduate Diploma as a final destination.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Economics for Business; Marketing Management; Management and Organisations in a Global Environment
Trimester 2: Finance for Business; Statistics and Research Methods for Business Decisions; Human Resource Management; Business Law and Ethics
Assessment: case-based assignments and a group consulting-style report in place of a thesis or major capstone
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Holmes Institute's MBA runs across its Melbourne and Sydney campuses to a full-time cohort that's overwhelmingly international, and the teaching reflects that: small seminar-style classes rather than lecture halls, with a lot of case discussion drawn from Asia-Pacific trade and services examples rather than the US case studies that dominate most MBA texts. The core is twelve units, everything from Accounting for Business Decisions through to Competitive Strategy, completed in about eighteen months, after which students pick one specialisation and one elective to round out the degree.

Because Holmes is a smaller private provider rather than a sandstone university, the MBA doesn't carry the brand weight of a Group of Eight degree, and it's honest to say most graduates use it as a credential to move into management roles in mid-sized firms or to support a permanent migration pathway, not to break into top-tier consulting or investment banking. Where it does its job well is for someone who already has a business degree or several years of work experience and wants the generalist management toolkit (finance, strategy, people management, research methods) without relocating overseas or taking two years out of the workforce.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Economics for Business; Management and Organisations in a Global Environment; Marketing Management
Trimester 2: Finance for Business; Statistics and Research Methods for Business Decisions; Leveraging Information Technology for Business Advantage; Human Resource Management
Trimester 3: Competitive Strategy; Corporate Governance and Ethics; International Business; Project Management
Final trimester: one specialisation unit (Marketing, International Business, Management or Hospitality Management) plus one elective
Capstone: applied strategy project addressing a real organisational problem, presented to faculty and industry panel
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline) typically required; relevant work experience preferred (approximate, typical bar, not program-page-verified)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall (typical bar for postgrad at private AU providers, approximate)

name: Master of Business Administration (Professional)
description:
The Professional variant of Holmes's MBA swaps the standard version's single specialisation-plus-elective tail for a much broader elective bank: eight core units and eight electives, which can be taken all from one specialisation to produce a focused MBA (Professional) in, say, marketing or international business, or spread across areas for a generalist qualification. It's aimed at students who want more say over the back half of their degree than the standard MBA structure allows.

In practice the two MBA products at Holmes overlap heavily in their core content (accounting, finance, economics, management, strategy), and the choice between them usually comes down to how much a student already knows they want to specialise versus keep options open. Neither carries the recruiting pull of an MBA from a AACSB-accredited research university, so it suits people building a management career step by step rather than those chasing a brand-name credential for a lateral move into strategy consulting.
curriculum:
Core (8 units): Accounting for Business Decisions; Finance for Business; Economics for Business; Marketing Management; Management and Organisations in a Global Environment; Statistics and Research Methods for Business Decisions; Competitive Strategy; Corporate Governance and Ethics
Electives (8 units): chosen from Marketing, International Business, Management or Hospitality Management strands, or mixed across strands for a generalist profile
Capstone: applied business project drawing on the student's chosen elective focus
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description:
The Master of Professional Accounting at Holmes is built to satisfy the CPA Australia and CA ANZ accreditation requirements for entry into those professional bodies, which is really the whole point of the degree for most people enrolled in it: it's a conversion course for graduates whose undergraduate degree wasn't in accounting and who need the full suite of core accounting units to sit the CPA Program or CA exams. It runs over roughly two years full-time across twelve to sixteen units depending on how much credit a student's prior degree earns them.

Because it's an accreditation-driven degree, the unit list is fairly fixed by the professional bodies rather than by Holmes itself: financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation law, corporate law and finance all have to appear. What Holmes adds on top is smaller class sizes and, for many students, English-language academic support built into the first trimester, which matters given a large share of the cohort has come from non-English-medium undergraduate study.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Accounting Systems and Processes; Financial Accounting; Economics for Business; Quantitative Methods for Business
Trimester 2: Management Accounting; Corporations Law; Taxation Law; Financial Management
Trimester 3: Auditing and Assurance Services; Advanced Financial Accounting; Business Law; Research Methods in Accounting
Final trimester: Ethics and Governance in Accounting; Strategic Management Accounting; two accounting electives aligned to CPA Program entry requirements
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor's degree (or equivalent); some programs consider work experience in lieu (approximate, typical bar)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (approximate, typical bar)

name: Bachelor of Business (Accounting)
description:
The Accounting specialisation at ICMS sits on the same core 12-subject business spine as the college's other Bachelor of Business streams, then adds the technical accounting sequence (financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation and corporate finance) needed to satisfy the professional accreditation requirements of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ. Getting that accreditation lined up matters more for accounting than for most other business majors, since it directly gates the pathway into the CA or CPA program after graduation, and ICMS structures the specialisation units specifically against those bodies' unit requirements.

Like every ICMS undergraduate degree, the course folds in two Work Integrated Learning placements totalling up to 600 hours, which for accounting students commonly means time inside a mid-tier or boutique Sydney accounting firm rather than a classroom-only capstone.
