Graduates are ready for agricultural roles including agronomist, agribusiness manager, animal nutritionist, soil scientist and government policy adviser.

name: Bachelor of Animal and Veterinary Biosciences
description: The Bachelor of Animal and Veterinary Biosciences at La Trobe University lets students turn a love of animals into a career. Students study the basics of animal science including breeding, nutrition and animal welfare, and explore global issues such as food security, epidemics and pandemics, and the environmental impacts of animal agriculture. Later years cover animal physiology, biochemistry and immunology. Each year includes practical elements such as real-life animal case studies with industry partners, plus compulsory and elective placements. With further study graduates can pursue veterinary science, or careers as conservation scientists and in animal industries.

name: Bachelor of Archaeology
description: The Bachelor of Archaeology at La Trobe University has students explore the human past, learning from leading researchers and industry experts about ancient societies, Indigenous histories and archaeological discoveries from Australia and around the world. Students examine how people lived, adapted and transformed landscapes over thousands of years, and build specialist capabilities in archaeological investigation, scientific analysis and ethical community engagement. Practical skills in fieldwork, science and heritage management are developed through hands-on learning, including a second-year industry-partnered excavation subject. Graduates work in consultant archaeology, cultural heritage management, museum curation and research.

name: Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence Engineering (Honours) at La Trobe University explores how artificial intelligence is transforming engineering across health, manufacturing, robotics and industry. Students combine engineering design, AI software, embedded sensing, the Internet of Things, robotics, cloud data and automation. In third year students complete an industry management project investigating a real-world problem for an industry client, and in fourth year they complete a thesis applying research, design and technical skills to an AI engineering problem. Minors in manufacturing and medical applications are co-designed with industry. Graduates become AI engineers and machine learning engineers.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
La Trobe's Bachelor of Arts covers an unusually wide humanities and social sciences spread for a Melbourne university, with archaeology standing out as a genuine area of departmental strength. La Trobe has run archaeology programs and fieldwork opportunities (including Australian and international excavation sites) for decades, well before most other Victorian universities built comparable programs. Criminology, politics, sociology, history, creative writing, journalism and a suite of language majors round out the available options.

Students build the degree around a major (occasionally two) plus a broad elective spread, and the course sits within a university that also runs La Trobe's Australian Institute for Public Policy and Innovation, giving politics and public policy students some connection to genuine policy research happening on campus rather than a purely theoretical curriculum.
curriculum:
Major (typically 8 subjects) chosen from Archaeology, Criminology, History, Politics and Policy Studies, Sociology, Creative Writing, Journalism, Languages (including options such as Indonesian, Italian, Spanish), and others
Second major or minor from a related discipline
Core Arts foundation subjects in critical thinking and research methods
Work-integrated learning or fieldwork component (notably in Archaeology)
Elective subjects to complete the degree
Honours pathway available in most majors for students proceeding to postgraduate research
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Biological Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Biological Sciences at La Trobe University gives students a strong scientific grounding plus the flexibility to specialise. Students build foundational skills in biology, chemistry, ecology and biodiversity, and explore the impacts of infection, epidemics and pandemics. Practical classes start in first year, both in on-campus labs and out in the field, alongside industry-led workshops, seminars and opportunities for work placements. Students choose a major from areas including biochemistry, botany, ecology, genetics, human physiological sciences and microbiology. Graduates work in lab and field settings across private industry, research institutes and government.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science at La Trobe University has students explore human biology, disease processes and applied biomedical science, with open electives to shape the degree around their interests and goals. Students build core knowledge in anatomy, physiology, chemistry, bioscience, statistics, microbiology and epidemiology, then deepen their understanding of physiology, pharmacology and biochemistry in relation to body systems, health and disease. Knowledge is applied to clinically focused areas including pathophysiology, biotechnology and pharmacology, with elective placement options. Graduates work across the biomedical, biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries and medical settings.

name: Bachelor of Biomedicine (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Biomedicine (Honours) at La Trobe University builds on the Bachelor of Biomedicine, letting students enhance their employability skills or take a first step towards a career in research and academia. Students conduct their own research project under the mentorship of expert researchers, gaining exposure to current techniques and scientific advances. Honours can be undertaken in disciplines including animal physiology and health, agriculture, biochemistry and cell biology, chemistry, environment and genetics, human anatomy, physiology and pharmacology, and microbiology, with projects hosted at La Trobe campuses and external research institutes.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
La Trobe Business School's Bachelor of Business sits within a AACSB-accredited faculty, which puts it in a smaller group of Australian business schools holding that particular international accreditation. Majors span the standard commerce disciplines: accounting, finance, marketing, management, human resource management, and the degree is taught across multiple La Trobe campuses (Bundoora in Melbourne, plus regional delivery at Bendigo, Albury-Wodonga, Shepparton and Mildura), which matters for the practical experience, since placement opportunities and industry partners differ noticeably depending on which campus a student is based at.

Work-integrated learning runs through the degree via La Trobe's industry-based learning program, connecting students with real organisations rather than leaving professional experience to a single capstone unit. The accounting major in particular is accredited by CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ, giving graduates a direct line into the CA/CPA pathway.
curriculum:
Business core: Accounting for Managers, Economics for Business, Marketing Principles, Business Law, Management, Business Statistics
Major (choose one or two) from Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management, Human Resource Management
Industry-based learning/work-integrated learning subject
Elective subjects and a second major or minor
Capstone: Business Strategy or Consultancy Project
AACSB-accredited business school; Accounting major accredited by CPA Australia and CA ANZ
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Business Analytics
description: The Bachelor of Business Analytics at La Trobe University prepares students to drive data, analytics and artificial intelligence innovations for business, economic and social growth. Co-designed with leading industry experts, the degree develops knowledge and skills in the business value of data, data engineering and management, analytics technologies and application, responsible AI, and industry best practices. Students learn from instructors with industry and research expertise in small, interactive classes that use generative AI teaching tools. Graduates work across finance, cybersecurity, health and defence in roles such as data analyst.

name: Bachelor of Civil Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Civil Engineering (Honours) at La Trobe University builds knowledge across a wide range of engineering specialties, including geotechnics and hydraulic systems, structural and electrical engineering, and mechanical engineering. Students develop a specialised skill set focused on creating sustainable, efficient and durable systems, covering infrastructure design, civil construction and computer-aided design. Small classes provide close contact with leading academics, and students can undertake research in sustainability and urban systems. Graduates work across construction, natural resources, renewable energy, mining and government, with major employers including John Holland and Fulton Hogan.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description: The Bachelor of Commerce at La Trobe University gives students a mix of skills and knowledge employers are looking for. Students learn the latest in commercial technologies such as automation, AI and big data, then apply it through industry placements, work-integrated learning projects and overseas exchange, graduating with a work-ready portfolio. Students choose from six majors: accounting, business analytics, economics, finance, management and marketing, and can add a second major. Graduates work across industries in roles including business analyst, management consultant, policy adviser and marketing manager.

name: Bachelor of Commerce - Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
This combined degree pairs La Trobe Business School's commerce core with the university's APAC-accredited psychological science stream, aimed at students who want a genuine double credential rather than a psychology minor tacked onto a business degree. It runs longer than either component alone, and the pairing shows up in career outcomes that are less obvious than a straight psych or straight commerce path: organisational psychology, HR analytics, and consumer behaviour research roles draw specifically on graduates who can do both the statistics-heavy psychology research methods sequence and a genuine accounting or marketing major.

Because the psychological science component still needs to satisfy APAC's Level 1 competency requirements, students don't get to water down the psych side to make room for commerce. Both halves are taught to the same standard as the standalone degrees, which is why the combined degree takes longer to complete than either on its own.
curriculum:
Commerce component: Business core (Accounting, Economics, Marketing, Management) plus a commerce major (e.g. Marketing, HR Management, Finance)
Psychological Science component: full APAC Level 1 sequence — Introduction to Psychology, Biological and Cognitive Psychology, Developmental and Social Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics
Integrated capstone or research project drawing on both disciplines
Elective units to complete the combined degree's extended credit point total
APAC-accredited psychology component; pathway to Honours for registration-track students
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description: The Bachelor of Computer Science at La Trobe University builds the technical skills to design, develop and improve the digital systems that power today's world. Students gain hands-on experience in programming, algorithms, databases, networks, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, developing solutions for complex problems across industry and society. Developed in partnership with industry leaders including Cisco, Optus and ANZ, the course combines contemporary theory with project-based learning, culminating in a final-year capstone project that delivers a solution to a real-world problem. Graduates work as software developers, cybersecurity analysts and data analysts.

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description: The Bachelor of Criminology at La Trobe University helps students understand crime in its broader social context and how responses are shaped by gender, race, power and money. Students address real-world problems while building a deeper understanding of issues such as family violence, international crime, youth justice, imprisonment and deaths in custody. The degree investigates the complex causes of crime, principles of crime prevention and policy, and the role of courts, police and prisons, and teaches students to critically analyse the Australian legal system. Graduates work in corrections, crime prevention, intelligence, policy and juvenile justice.

name: Bachelor of Cybersecurity
description: The Bachelor of Cybersecurity at La Trobe University lets students step into the rapidly evolving digital world of cybersecurity. Students build a highly specialised technical skill set, learning the history of hacking, developing coding expertise, and accessing industry-based projects and mentoring with major corporations. Industry-focused learning can be complemented with advanced electives in IT, business, law, policy and strategic communication. The program covers cybersecurity fundamentals and ethical hacking and defence, including assessing the security of network configurations. Graduates work as cyber threat analysts and vulnerability assessors across technology, finance, government, defence and healthcare.

name: Bachelor of Dental Science (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Dental Science (Honours) at La Trobe University prepares students to practise dentistry after five years of study at Australia's largest rural health school. Students learn the foundations of dental science and gain hands-on experience in clinical placements across regional Victoria, treating patients under the supervision of experienced clinicians and working to improve oral health through prevention, education and clinical care. Students can also complete a community-based or research project that can lead to a doctorate. Graduates practise in public dental clinics, hospitals and private practice.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
La Trobe's engineering school is considerably younger than its Business or Science faculties. Its first engineering cohorts only began in the mid-2010s, and the course was built from the ground up around a project-based learning model rather than a traditional lecture-and-tutorial structure inherited from an older program. Students work through substantial team-based engineering projects in most years of the degree rather than treating design projects as a single capstone experience bolted onto a lecture-heavy course.

Majors are offered across the conventional engineering disciplines, and the course is run from the Bundoora campus with strong emphasis on industry partnerships for placements, reflecting the practical, employer-facing approach La Trobe has taken to differentiate a newer engineering school from long-established Group of Eight competitors in Melbourne.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Fundamentals, Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Mechanics, first team-based engineering project
Years 2–3: major-specific technical subjects (Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, or Mechatronic engineering), continued project-based subjects each year
Industry placement/work-integrated learning component
Year 4: capstone engineering design project, undertaken in industry-partnered teams
Accredited pathway to Engineers Australia professional recognition
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion with strong mathematics; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Food and Nutrition
description: The Bachelor of Food and Nutrition at La Trobe University teaches students to work with people, communities and organisations to help prevent chronic disease and optimise health. Designed by food and nutrition science experts with industry, the degree explores nutrition science and metabolism, the environmental sustainability of food systems and diets, food product development, culture and food, nutrition assessment, and individual and public health nutrition across the lifespan. Students can tailor their studies through electives or a minor. Graduates work across public and community health, government, the food industry, research and media.

name: Bachelor of Global Studies
description: The Bachelor of Global Studies at La Trobe University has students explore the global issues facing key regions and countries, studying international relations, geopolitics, contemporary security, American power, the rise of China, climate change, armed conflict, terrorism and human rights. The degree can be studied fully online or at the Melbourne (Bundoora) Campus, with majors and minors in areas including international relations, conflict and negotiation, Asian politics and security, government and policy, human rights, and language studies. In second year students undertake an industry experience. Graduates work in government, intergovernmental agencies and humanitarian organisations.

name: Bachelor of Health Information Management
description: The Bachelor of Health Information Management at La Trobe University combines the clinical and business sides of healthcare, using data to improve the quality of patient care. Students develop a comprehensive skill set covering anatomy and physiology, health classification, data analytics, health informatics and health systems management, and complete 55 days of supervised professional placement with health partners. Students learn the language of medicine, the structures and function of human anatomy and physiology, and how to implement and manage health information systems. Graduates work as health information managers, clinical coders and health data analysts.

name: Bachelor of Health Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Health Sciences at La Trobe University develops transferable skills for careers across diverse areas of health and postgraduate pathways into emerging and established health professions. Depending on campus and study mode, students choose from majors in allied health, digital health, environmental health, food and nutrition, health promotion, psychological science, public health, and rehabilitation, counselling and wellbeing, with the flexibility to study a major and minor or a double major. Students learn to apply scientific thinking and fieldwork skills to investigate health issues. Graduates work as public health officers, health promotion coordinators and health educators.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
The undergraduate Bachelor of Information Technology follows the same specialisation logic as La Trobe's postgraduate IT courses, with majors in areas like cybersecurity, software development, networking and data-oriented computing, delivered mainly from the Bundoora campus with a Sydney campus option for students in NSW. Core first-year subjects cover programming fundamentals, systems and networks, and database design before the major-specific content takes over from second year.

La Trobe has pushed cybersecurity hard as a growth area across both its undergraduate and postgraduate IT offerings, reflecting genuine industry demand in Melbourne's tech and finance sectors, and the degree carries ACS accreditation that gives graduates a recognised route into Australian Computer Society membership. A capstone industry project or placement unit in the final year is standard rather than optional, tying the technical major to an applied deliverable before graduation.
curriculum:
Year 1 core: Introduction to Programming, Computer Systems and Networks, Database Design, ICT Professional Practice
Major (from Year 2) chosen from Cybersecurity, Software Development, Networking, or Data-oriented computing streams
Elective units and a minor from a complementary discipline
Capstone: industry project or work placement in final year
ACS-accredited
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Languages and Linguistics
description: The Bachelor of Languages and Linguistics at La Trobe University builds proficiency in a chosen language alongside a deep understanding of how languages are structured, used and learned. Students study key areas of linguistics including phonetics, syntax, semantics and pragmatics, and examine how language varies across social and cultural contexts. Alongside the language major, students tailor their studies through electives or a minor, exploring additional languages including Auslan or complementary disciplines, and gain real-world experience through industry-based learning. Graduates pursue roles in international relations, education, translation, speech pathology and media.

name: Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Laws (Honours) at La Trobe University is a four-year law degree committed to social impact and community engagement. Students gain a strong academic and professional foundation and can match their legal career to their interests through specialised electives. Hands-on practical learning comes through the Legal Internship Program, work-based learning, the Law Clinic, overseas study programs and a leading mooting program, plus internships, clerkships and placements at legal firms, government bodies and community legal centres. The degree meets the academic requirements to practise law in Victoria.

name: Bachelor of Media and Communication
description: The Bachelor of Media and Communication at La Trobe University lets students tell stories across any medium and graduate with a portfolio of work, industry experience and specialised media knowledge. Students choose a first major in creative and professional writing, journalism, sports media or marketing, then tailor the degree with a second major, minor or electives. Hands-on production and broadcast experience comes through the industry-grade Upstart newsroom, which includes a three-camera television studio, professional radio broadcast spaces and audio and editing suites, alongside work-based learning with industry partners. Graduates work in news and media, sport, health and politics.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
La Trobe's standard Bachelor of Nursing places students into clinical environments from first year, drawing on the university's long-standing partnerships with major Victorian health providers, including Austin Health, the Royal Women's Hospital, and Bendigo Health, rather than waiting until later years to start placements. The 800 clinical placement hours run across acute care, chronic illness management, mental health, rehabilitation, community and emergency settings, and the course also carries a specific First Nations Health subject and an Indigenous health component woven into the broader curriculum, not treated as a standalone add-on.

Students are required to purchase a branded scrub top for placements, a small but telling detail of how seriously the clinical placement component is treated administratively. Since July 2025, eligible students on mandatory placements can access the Australian Government's Commonwealth Prac Payment, which matters in practice given how placement blocks affect a nursing student's ability to hold down paid work during those weeks.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Biosciences for Nursing, first clinical placement block
Year 2: Acute Care Nursing, Chronic Illness Management, Mental Healthcare in Nursing, Primary Healthcare, Research in Nursing, continued placements
Year 3: Rehabilitation and Community Nursing, Emergency Care, First Nations Health, capstone Transition to Professional Practice placement
800 hours of clinical placement across partner health services including Austin Health, Royal Women's Hospital, and Bendigo Health
Eligible for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse on completion; Commonwealth Prac Payment eligibility for placement periods from July 2025
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours) at La Trobe University teaches students to help people maximise their quality of life and reach their potential. Students discover the science behind human activity and learn to conduct evidence-based occupational therapy assessments and interventions for people of all ages and backgrounds. Learning combines face-to-face tutorials and workshops, online study and hands-on experience, including 1,000 hours of professional placements. The program covers occupational science, anatomy, physiology, psychology, communication and group theory. Graduates are in high demand across community health, government, mental health, and paediatric and aged care services.

name: Bachelor of Oral Health Science
description: The Bachelor of Oral Health Science at La Trobe University is an accredited program that teaches students to provide essential oral healthcare while studying in an inter- and intradisciplinary setting at Australia's largest rural health school. Students develop their understanding of oral health promotion and the prevention and treatment of oral diseases, and gain hands-on experience in clinical placements across regional Victoria, treating patients of all ages under the supervision of experienced clinicians. Graduates can register as oral health therapists and work in dental clinics, community health centres, and health promotion, education and policy roles.

name: Bachelor of Orthoptics (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Orthoptics (Honours) at La Trobe University teaches students to make a real impact on the vision and visual function of others. Students study the anatomy and physiology of the eye to understand vision, and learn how to help people with eye disorders such as strabismus, eye diseases and low vision. Clinical experience begins in second year, with placements in hospitals with dedicated eye clinics, private eye clinics, low vision rehabilitation organisations and the on-campus eye clinic. Graduates work as orthoptists in hospitals, specialist clinics, rehabilitation centres, and ocular pharmaceutical and device companies.

name: Bachelor of Outdoor and Sustainability Education
description: The Bachelor of Outdoor and Sustainability Education at La Trobe University takes students beyond the classroom for hands-on outdoor experience and a deeper understanding of sustainability and environmental education. Students can spend more than 70 days on field trips and extended outdoor journeys, building outdoor adventuring skills such as bushwalking and kayaking while developing an understanding of climate change research and experiential learning. Students also learn to lead groups exploring outdoor environments and to foster respect for the natural world. Graduates work in education, land and resource management, adventure tourism and environmental conservation.

name: Bachelor of Paramedic Practice with Honours
description: The Bachelor of Paramedic Practice with Honours at La Trobe University builds the knowledge, clinical skills and confidence to provide emergency healthcare. Students develop hands-on clinical skills from first year alongside a strong foundation in human biosciences and evidence-based paramedic practice. They learn to assess and manage patients across trauma, cardiac, respiratory, paediatric and obstetric emergencies while developing communication, critical thinking and clinical decision-making skills, building confidence in the Paramedicine Practical Laboratory with industry-standard equipment and realistic simulation. Graduates work as ambulance and community paramedics in Australia and overseas.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) at La Trobe University is an accredited degree that starts students on the path to a career as a pharmacist. Students build their understanding of how medicines treat disease and affect people's lives, and the importance of patient-centred, individualised care. They access an on-campus training pharmacy and participate in community and hospital placements, studying biochemistry, haematology and pharmacology and how systems of the body work. Graduates are eligible to apply for a one-year supervised internship and the Pharmacy Board of Australia exams before working in hospitals and community pharmacies.

name: Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours) at La Trobe University prepares students to become fully qualified physiotherapists who use exercise and movement to improve the lives of athletes, children, adults and people recovering from surgery, injury or illness. Students gain a detailed understanding of the human body and develop practical skills from first year, learning from industry leaders and active researchers. The four-year degree includes unique industry opportunities with a broad range of partners. Graduates work in private practice, hospitals and community health centres assessing and treating a wide variety of patients.

name: Bachelor of Podiatry (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Podiatry (Honours) at La Trobe University prepares students to help others maintain and improve their mobility and independence. It is the only podiatry program in Australia where graduates are qualified to prescribe scheduled medicines, enhancing their scope and impact in patient care. Students learn from experienced podiatrists and researchers in sports medicine, biomechanics, hospital-based podiatry, private practice, paediatrics and foot surgery, studying human anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, paediatrics and sport injuries. Broad clinical experience makes graduates job-ready for a workforce with strong demand for podiatrists across private practice, sports podiatry and public health.

name: Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics
description: The Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics at La Trobe University gives students a multidisciplinary perspective on the political and economic systems that shape our world. Students grasp the interconnections between the three disciplines, gaining a distinctive and well-rounded combination of transferable skills that can be applied across policy contexts. The degree expands students' understanding of politics and the evolution of governmental structures, helps them pinpoint opportunities for innovative policy-making, and engages them with foundational questions in philosophy. Graduates work as think-tank analysts, political communications advisers and public servants.

name: Bachelor of Prosthetics and Orthotics (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Prosthetics and Orthotics (Honours) at La Trobe University teaches students to treat the physical and functional limitations of others. Students explore anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, and prosthetic and orthotic prescription, design and fabrication, honing their skills through clinical teaching at the purpose-built onsite clinic before completing clinical placements at external facilities and with industry partners. Students choose an industry minor or a research minor. Graduates are qualified to work as prosthetists and orthotists in public health, private practice and research.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
La Trobe's Bachelor of Psychological Science is the university's APAC-accredited foundation pathway into professional psychology, and it benefits from a research environment that's genuinely notable in one specific area: the Olga Tennison Autism Research Centre (OTARC), based at La Trobe, is one of the country's leading autism research groups, and its work feeds directly into some of the developmental and clinical psychology content taught in the degree.

The course covers the standard APAC Level 1 competencies, including biological bases of behaviour, cognition, developmental and social psychology, and research methods and statistics, and sets students up for La Trobe's own fourth-year Honours program, the compulsory next step for anyone pursuing provisional psychologist registration or further clinical postgraduate training. Students who want a psychology qualification without the accreditation pathway typically choose the psychology major within the Bachelor of Arts or Science instead; this degree is specifically for those aiming at registration.
curriculum:
Core subjects: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics (sequence across years 1–3), Abnormal Psychology, Psychological Assessment
Minor or elective sequence outside psychology
Research project/capstone subject in final year
APAC-accredited, meeting Level 1 competencies for provisional psychologist registration pathway
Progression to Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours), the required fourth year for registration
admission_requirements: Year 12 completion or equivalent; ATAR as per current guide
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science with Honours
description: The Bachelor of Psychological Science with Honours at La Trobe University builds on the Bachelor of Psychological Science, giving students a deeper understanding of research theory, design and practice. Students study advanced theory in psychology and take part in a tailored psychology research methodology seminar, then undertake an original research project under the supervision of expert staff from the School of Psychology and Public Health to produce evidence-based solutions to current issues. Honours develops research abilities and employability skills and is the best foundation for a postgraduate career in psychology.

name: Bachelor of Science
description: The Bachelor of Science at La Trobe University builds a strong foundation in science while students explore disciplines, majors and career pathways. Students study scientific concepts and learn how scientists think, work, test ideas and share findings, exploring areas such as data analysis, research, sustainability and emerging technologies including artificial intelligence. Learning is applied through laboratories, fieldwork, industry projects and work-integrated learning. Students can shape the degree through majors, minors or a double major, with pathways into Honours, postgraduate study and research. Graduates work in roles requiring strong analytical thinking and problem solving, in and beyond science.

name: Bachelor of Social Work (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Social Work (Honours) at La Trobe University gives students the clinical knowledge and hands-on skills to support people and families in need. Students learn from academics about promoting human rights and the importance of social justice, with a diverse range of subjects providing foundations in both psychology and sociology. Two 14-week placements let students put their knowledge into practice and gain professional experience within leading health and welfare organisations in Victoria. Graduates find employment in community health centres, hospitals, government agencies and non-government organisations.

name: Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours) at La Trobe University prepares students to help people of all ages who experience difficulties with communication or with eating and drinking. Students develop an understanding of the anatomy behind speech and swallowing impairments and learn to provide therapeutic treatment and management options. They build hands-on skills through approximately 1,000 hours of placement on-campus and in clinics across Victoria, and complete a research project aimed at improving speech pathology services and policies. Graduates work in hospitals, health centres, rehabilitation centres, teaching and consultancy.

name: Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science
description: The Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science at La Trobe University explores the science behind human movement, training and physical performance, building strong foundations in physiology, anatomy and biomechanics. Students learn to apply scientific principles, techniques and data to support injury prevention, rehabilitation, strength development and athletic performance. Real-world experience comes through 150 placement hours with organisations such as Carlton Football Club, Rugby Victoria and Bendigo Spirit, using industry-standard teaching, research and athlete performance facilities at the La Trobe Sports Park. Graduates work as sport scientists, health and wellness officers and rehabilitation coaches.

name: Bachelor of Sport and Recreation Management
description: The Bachelor of Sport and Recreation Management at La Trobe University teaches students to manage community sport and recreation services. Students explore program design, sport coaching, human resource management, marketing, delivery and evaluation, government policy and funding, facility and venue management, sport law and professional communication, building the skills to engage with communities, work with volunteers and support physical activity and wellbeing. Learning is applied through placements with local councils, sport associations, community groups and clubs. Graduates work as sport administrators, officers and managers across community, government and events roles.

name: Bachelor of Sport Coaching and Development
Bachelor of Visual Arts
description: The Bachelor of Visual Arts at La Trobe University gives creative students the knowledge, experiences and connections to pursue an artistic career. Students gain skills across a range of visual mediums and develop their art practice in a professional environment, accessing specialised facilities including painting and drawing studios, a digital lighting studio, photographic darkrooms, and sculpture and printmaking workshops. Each student has their own personal studio space from day one through to graduation. Graduates work in art galleries and museums, government and council organisations, graphic design agencies and photography studios, including as gallery or museum curators.

name: Bachelor of Wildlife and Conservation Biology
description: The Bachelor of Wildlife and Conservation Biology at La Trobe University draws on botany, genetics and zoology to give students the skills to make a difference for the environment. Students learn to apply ecological concepts to the conservation of species and ecosystems and explore the legal framework for conservation. The curriculum covers biology fundamentals, including how organisms, the environment and human populations interact, as well as climate change and sustainability. As they progress, students learn to use different technologies to collect and process data and design their own research. Graduates work as conservation scientists and park rangers.

name: Diploma of Engineering Technology
description: The Diploma of Engineering Technology at La Trobe University builds a foundation in engineering technology, developing core skills in programming, modelling, engineering design, electrical and electronic engineering, and mechanics of solids. Students study across engineering, computer science, mathematics and physics while building early experience through project-based learning and practical activities. Students can choose from streams in civil engineering or artificial intelligence, exploring physics and introductory AI concepts or combining engineering physics with computer-aided design. Completed in one year of full-time study, the diploma leads to careers in technical support, design, modelling and applied AI contexts.

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: The Diploma of Information Technology at La Trobe University is a supported pathway into an IT degree or an entry-level role in the industry. Students build a strong foundation in core IT subjects such as programming and cybersecurity, studying alongside Bachelor's degree students from day one and getting a taste of university life. Depending on the subjects studied, students can graduate with up to one year of advanced standing, allowing them to transfer directly into the second year of the Bachelor of Computer Science, Bachelor of Cybersecurity or Bachelor of Information Technology. Graduates can also pursue entry-level ICT roles such as IT support worker.

name: Diploma of International Tourism and Hospitality Management
Diploma of Science
description: The Diploma of Science at La Trobe University is a supported pathway into the Bachelor of Science or a qualification for entry-level roles in the science industry. Students explore basic scientific concepts and learn how to collaborate in the laboratory, consolidating their knowledge through practical, laboratory-based classes with hands-on experience. Students also build skills in scientific communication for sharing outcomes with different audiences. A wide range of electives lets students take specialist subjects early, including biochemistry, zoology, physics, molecular biology and data science. With further study, graduates pursue a range of science-related careers.

name: Diploma of Teacher Education
description: The Diploma of Teacher Education at La Trobe University is a pathway to an accredited teaching degree. On successful completion students can progress to the Bachelor of Education in Primary, Secondary, or Early Childhood and Primary, with advanced standing for up to one year of full-time study. Students develop solid foundations in digital learning, literacy, numeracy and learning contexts, skills that serve them throughout a teaching career, and immerse themselves in the full university experience by studying alongside Bachelor students in the same subjects.

name: Doctor of Clinical Science (Clinical Speech Pathology, Clinical Vision Sciences, Family Therapy, Occupational Therapy, Prosthetics and Orthotics, Counselling and Psychotherapy)
Doctor of Nursing (Professional Doctorate)
description: The Doctor of Nursing at La Trobe University is a professional doctorate for experienced nursing practitioners who want to enrich and extend their professional practice and undertake research in professional or community settings. The degree offers an integrated program of research with supporting coursework in the first year, building knowledge and skills in research design, literature review techniques, critical analysis and writing for publication, with opportunities to apply these skills in clinical projects. Candidates pursue a sustained investigation culminating in a 60,000 word thesis and graduate ready for nursing management, education and research roles.

name: Doctor of Social Work (Professional Doctorate)
description: The Doctor of Social Work at La Trobe University is a professional doctorate for experienced practitioners in social work and human services who want to enrich their practice and undertake research in professional or community settings. Areas of study include social work practice, social policy, program evaluation, disability, ageing, youth and family welfare, and mental health. The degree offers an integrated program of research with supporting coursework in the first year, and candidates pursue a sustained investigation culminating in a thesis. Graduates move into academic research, higher education and public sector roles.

name: Global Master of Business Administration
description: La Trobe's Global Master of Business Administration is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree built for early-career and emerging professionals from international backgrounds, so it does not require the years of management experience a traditional executive MBA expects. It is taught in Melbourne and Sydney. The core covers global strategic thinking, global marketing and consumer behaviour, financial management, supply chain and operations, ethics and corporate social responsibility, leadership and organisational behaviour, and digital transformation with business analytics and AI tools. An industry placement is built in. Students choose one of six specialisations: data analytics, financial management, human resource management, international business, marketing, or project management. Entry is a bachelor degree in any discipline, or a bachelor plus two years of managerial work experience. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Indicative international tuition is around A$49,800 per year.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business at La Trobe University is a foundational postgraduate program for people who want to build core business knowledge or move into further postgraduate study. Over one semester of full-time study, students are introduced to key areas including management, economics, accounting and finance, and artificial intelligence for business. The program emphasises analytical thinking, problem solving and communication, skills valued across industries. It can act as a pathway into the Graduate Diploma in Business or the Global Master of Business Administration, and suits career changers and professionals looking to upskill.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business Administration
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business Administration at La Trobe University is a fully online, AI-first qualification for professionals building management capability for an AI-driven economy. Delivered in flexible six-week study blocks, it lets students study from anywhere while developing practical expertise in strategy, financial analysis, innovation and AI-enabled decision making. Students complete four subjects drawn from La Trobe's online MBA curriculum, studying alongside MBA students and gaining exposure to postgraduate-level management learning. The course provides a direct credited pathway into the La Trobe MBA and suits aspiring strategy managers, consultants and team leaders.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business Analytics
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business Analytics at La Trobe University helps students build smarter, more resilient business solutions with data. Designed in consultation with industry leaders, it covers how artificial intelligence is transforming business decision making, the fundamentals of cybersecurity, and hands-on prototyping and low-code development. Students develop an analytical mindset and learn to use business data to create real impact. The program prepares graduates for roles such as data analyst across a wide range of sectors, and provides a pathway into further postgraduate analytics study at La Trobe.

name: Graduate Certificate in Data Science Fundamentals
description: The Graduate Certificate in Data Science Fundamentals at La Trobe University introduces the mathematics, modelling and database design that underpin data science. Students learn from industry experts and work with real data sets from industry partners, building the skills to create complex models and use powerful tools for advanced analysis and problem solving. Suitable for people with or without prior data experience, the program is a pathway to start or progress a career in data science, with graduates suited to roles such as data scientist and business analyst across finance, health, education and sport.

name: Graduate Certificate in Digital Health
description: The Graduate Certificate in Digital Health at La Trobe University builds an in-demand skill set to design, implement and manage digital health solutions. Students advance their knowledge in emerging areas including health analytics, virtual care, the Internet of Medical Things, and health websites, apps and social media, examining the benefits, risks and ethical and legal implications of these technologies. The program develops a design-thinking mindset using data-driven, human-centred approaches. Graduates work across commercial and public sector organisations at the interface of healthcare and digital technology.

name: Graduate Certificate in Information Technology Fundamentals
description: The Graduate Certificate in Information Technology Fundamentals at La Trobe University is a first step towards an IT career and a pathway into a range of postgraduate IT degrees. With technology central to modern business, industries from media and government to health and education are recruiting specialists in computing, diagnosis, service and maintenance. Whether students already work in IT or are new to the field, the program provides a strong foundation for further study or entry-level roles such as network administrator, supporting network and computer systems.

name: Graduate Certificate in Logistics and Supply Chain Management
description: The Graduate Certificate in Logistics and Supply Chain Management at La Trobe University equips students with the knowledge and strategic skills to tackle real-world industry challenges in one semester of full-time study. It provides a working understanding of end-to-end supply chains and focuses on applied analytics and digitalisation, exploring how emerging technologies such as AI, digital twins and cloud computing unlock value. The course rapidly upskills professionals and provides a pathway to further postgraduate study in logistics and supply chain management, with graduates suited to procurement, supply chain and operations roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting
description: The Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting at La Trobe University is a first step into postgraduate accounting study, developing essential knowledge in accounting principles, finance and economics. Designed for students from non-accounting backgrounds, it offers a structured way to explore the discipline before committing to a longer qualification. Students learn to apply accounting principles to record transactions and prepare financial statements, interpret economic concepts and explain core finance ideas. The certificate acts as a direct pathway to the Master of Professional Accounting and suits finance officer and accounts officer roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Public Health
description: The Graduate Certificate in Public Health at La Trobe University gives students vital skills and up-to-date insights into public health, a field in high demand worldwide. Students explore public health practice and theory, learning how professionals provide health education, prevent disease outbreaks and protect and improve community health. The internationally recognised qualification can be built on with further study to expand career pathways into government organisations and community health services, with graduates suited to roles such as community health worker and health and welfare services manager.

name: Graduate Certificate in Sport Analytics
description: The Graduate Certificate in Sport Analytics at La Trobe University builds foundational knowledge of how data supports performance analysis and decision making in sport. Students explore the principles of sport analytics, including the growing role of artificial intelligence, while building foundations in database management and analytical methods. Studies can be tailored through electives in programming, sport data capture, probability and statistics, and applied sport analytics, using authentic sport datasets. The program is a pathway to the Graduate Diploma in Sport Analytics and Master of Sport Analytics, preparing graduates for sport analyst and data analyst roles.

name: Graduate Certificate of Archaeology
description: The Graduate Certificate of Archaeology at La Trobe University is a first step towards a career in archaeology and heritage management. Through theoretical and hands-on learning, students develop foundational skills in contemporary archaeological practice, exploring the archaeology of Australia's First Peoples, field and laboratory skills, and artefact analysis. Completed over one year of part-time study, it acts as a pathway to the Graduate Diploma of Archaeology or the Master of Archaeology, with graduates eligible to apply for advanced standing towards those courses and for roles such as professional archaeologist and heritage advisor.

name: Graduate Diploma in Artificial Intelligence
description: The Graduate Diploma in Artificial Intelligence at La Trobe University teaches students to apply AI technology across contexts including digital healthcare, smart manufacturing, smart cities, sustainable energy infrastructure and precision agriculture. Students learn from experienced lecturers and take a hands-on approach, using AI skills to solve real-world problems in an industry-based project with organisations such as Microsoft and Optus. The program covers problem solving with AI, research skills, deep learning algorithms and machine learning, preparing graduates for roles such as artificial intelligence architect and software engineer.

name: Graduate Diploma in Business Information Systems
Graduate Diploma in Cybersecurity
description: The Graduate Diploma in Cybersecurity at La Trobe University lets students study from anywhere with the flexibility to fit work and life commitments. Specialised subjects include the psychology behind cybercrime and how to prepare defensively, secure programming for the future, and database skills for cyber analytics. The program covers cybersecurity fundamentals and cyber risk management grounded in business strategy. Graduates may be eligible to continue into the Master of Cybersecurity, and can pursue roles such as database and systems administrator and cyber threat analyst across healthcare, finance, public administration and telecommunications.

name: Graduate Diploma in Early Childhood Education
description: The Graduate Diploma in Early Childhood Education at La Trobe University is delivered by the School of Education with an industry-connected curriculum. Students gain the skills and knowledge to support pre-school children across social, emotional, physical and academic development, studying core subjects in early childhood development, assessment and reporting, teaching strategies, and safety and ethics. Learning is applied through work-based learning, integrated placement and an embedded professional mentoring program. Graduates are eligible for teacher accreditation as early childhood educators and can advance into La Trobe's Master of Education.

name: Graduate Diploma in Education
description: The Graduate Diploma in Education at La Trobe University helps working educators stay current with best practice and grow their careers as educators and leaders. Students deepen their foundations with core subjects on educational leadership, how humans learn and digital technologies, then add a specialisation such as curriculum design or inclusion and diversity. Many subjects are delivered in intensive or blended modes, and students can study one to four subjects per semester. The diploma provides a fully credited pathway to the Master of Education and suits leading teacher and community development roles.

name: Graduate Diploma in Engineering Management
description: The Graduate Diploma in Engineering Management at La Trobe University gives practising engineers the advanced skills and commercial expertise to move into leadership. Students update their knowledge of modern engineering practice and study specialist subjects in management, innovation and sustainability designed for engineers, alongside core business principles in marketing, finance, organisational behaviour and business statistics. Taught by experienced engineers and business professionals, the interdisciplinary program prepares graduates for engineering manager roles across manufacturing, technology, telecommunications, government and construction.

name: Graduate Diploma in Information Technology
description: The Graduate Diploma in Information Technology at La Trobe University provides a general professional qualification in IT, broadening or deepening students' knowledge of computing. Core subjects give a foundation in information systems, software development and computer networking. Students learn to evaluate and select appropriate technology solutions, use research and technical skills to test IT solutions and prevent bugs, communicate professionally and ethically within the sector, and apply critical thinking. Completed in one year of full-time study, it prepares graduates for IT roles across technology, communications, education, finance, government, healthcare and energy.

name: Graduate Diploma in Logistics and Supply Chain Management
Graduate Diploma in Sport Analytics
description: The Graduate Diploma in Sport Analytics at La Trobe University develops advanced technical and analytical skills in using data, programming and artificial intelligence to generate insights in sport. Students build expertise in programming, probability, statistics, database management and sport analytics, then explore artificial intelligence, large language models and machine learning in contemporary sport analytics. Analytical processes are applied to authentic sport datasets using industry-standard tools including R, Python and SQL. Completed in one year of full-time study, the program is a pathway to the Master of Sport Analytics and prepares graduates for sport analyst and data scientist roles.

name: Graduate Diploma of Archaeology
description: The Graduate Diploma of Archaeology at La Trobe University builds specialist skills in contemporary archaeological practice through theoretical and hands-on learning. Students study Indigenous Australian archaeology, historic archaeology, field and laboratory skills, artefact analysis, and field techniques including survey and excavation methods. Electives are available in areas such as cross-cultural management, project management, historical and archival research and industry placements. Completed in one year of full-time study, the diploma is a pathway to the Master of Archaeology, with graduates suited to professional archaeology, cultural heritage management and research roles.

name: Graduate Diploma of Data Science
description: The Graduate Diploma in Data Science at La Trobe University gives students a solid foundation in computer science, statistics and applied data analysis. Students learn with real data sets from industry partners and gain practical experience with open-source software and platforms including Python, R and Hadoop. Core subjects cover database fundamentals, programming languages such as Java and Python, cloud-based services, and mathematics. Completed in one year of full-time study, the program prepares graduates for roles such as data scientist and business analyst as organisations seek to make sense of large volumes of data.

name: Juris Doctor
description: La Trobe's Juris Doctor is a 360-credit-point graduate-entry law degree, three years full-time, taught at the City campus in Melbourne's court and business precinct with small, flexible evening classes. Starting in the preceding November intake or taking summer electives can shorten it to 2.5 years. Core subjects and electives are designed with judges and senior lawyers, and students who finish their core subjects by the start of the final year can add practical legal training within the degree. Entry is a bachelor degree with a 60 percent average, or a bachelor plus three years of professional experience and a personal statement, with IELTS 6.5 and no band below 6.0. The degree meets the Victorian Legal Admissions Board academic requirements to be admitted as a lawyer in Victoria; admission also requires practical legal training. Graduates work as solicitors and barristers, policy advisers, in-house counsel and legal consultants. Indicative international tuition is around A$48,000 per year.

name: Master of Archaeology
description: The Master of Archaeology at La Trobe University develops advanced skills in archaeological research, interpretation and practice. Students explore Australian, Australian Indigenous and global archaeology while examining how evidence explains past societies, informs heritage decisions and supports engagement with contemporary communities. Studies are tailored through a specialisation in advanced research or professional archaeology, with electives in Australian archaeology, Indigenous archaeology, historic archaeology, and field and laboratory methods. Completed over two years of full-time study, the degree prepares graduates for professional archaeology, cultural heritage management and research careers.

name: Master of Art therapy
description: La Trobe's Master of Art Therapy is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree that La Trobe describes as the only specialist postgraduate art therapy degree of its kind in Australia. It combines art practice with counselling for clinical, therapeutic and community settings, taught through face-to-face workshops in a purpose-built studio with work-integrated learning at partners including the Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre and the Royal Children's Hospital. The degree is accredited by the Australian Counselling Association, and graduates may apply for registration with it. Entry is a bachelor degree, a portfolio of original artwork, a written application and at least one year of human services or community work, paid or voluntary. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as art therapists in hospitals, community and crisis services, schools, aged and palliative care, and correctional settings. Indicative international tuition is around A$44,800 per year.

name: Master of Artificial Intelligence
description: La Trobe's Master of Artificial Intelligence is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree that pairs core AI technical skills with professional practice. Study covers IT fundamentals, machine learning, data mining, computer vision, natural language processing and cybersecurity, along with deep-learning techniques for image recognition, machine translation and speech synthesis. Students learn to build AI solutions to real-world problems and to weigh the ethical and societal issues the technology raises, and rounds out the degree with subjects in entrepreneurship, professional practice and project management. Entry is a completed bachelor degree; applicants with a computing background may qualify for a shorter pathway. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as AI consultants, developers and solutions architects, machine learning engineers and software engineers, in fields from digital healthcare and smart manufacturing to precision agriculture. Indicative international tuition is around A$46,000 per year.

name: Master of Arts (Humanities & Social Sciences) (By Research)
Master of Biotechnology and Bioinformatics
description: The Master of Biotechnology and Bioinformatics at La Trobe University teaches students to harness new and emerging technologies across human health, diagnostics, sustainability, food security and renewable energy. Students develop technical expertise and professional skills for industries spanning biological products, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and nutrition. In the final year, students choose an advanced bioinformatics pathway or a research project pathway with 25 to 30 hours of laboratory time each week and access to industry networks. Graduates are suited to roles such as biotechnologist and bioinformatician.

name: Master of Biotechnology Management
description: The Master of Biotechnology Management at La Trobe University combines biotechnology and business management expertise for graduates seeking a global career. In the first year students learn the fundamentals of management and marketing across diverse organisational contexts, then move into bio-business management and learn how to produce and market a product. Taught by industry experts, the program examines molecular modelling software, proteomics and genomics, and advanced technologies including CRISPR-mediated gene editing, next generation sequencing and mass spectrometry. Graduates work in roles such as sales representative and project officer.

name: Master of Business Analytics
description: La Trobe's Master of Business Analytics is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree co-designed with industry that sits between data science and business. Students learn to build and use analytics dashboards, predictive models and cloud applications for real business problems, apply artificial intelligence to productivity and decision-making, and work through the regulatory, ethics and cybersecurity frameworks that govern enterprise data. Teaching is in small interactive classes and includes industry placements and business case studies. Entry is a bachelor degree in a related field such as data analytics, computer science, information systems or IT completed in the last five years, or a bachelor in any discipline. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as business and data analysts, analytics consultants, business intelligence developers and in AI solution roles. Indicative international tuition is around A$46,800 per year.

name: Master of Business Information Systems
description: La Trobe's Master of Business Information Systems is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree, co-designed with industry, for people who want to work at the point where business, technology and innovation meet. Core study covers modern information systems, artificial intelligence, design thinking and data analytics, alongside the analytical and business skills to translate organisational needs into working systems. A 1.5-year pathway is available with recognised prior study. Entry is a bachelor degree in any discipline, or completion of La Trobe's Postgraduate Qualifying Program. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as business analysts, systems and enterprise resource planning analysts, and in enterprise architecture roles across every industry sector. Indicative international tuition is around A$46,800 per year.

name: Master of Civil Engineering
description: La Trobe's Master of Civil Engineering is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree accredited by Engineers Australia and designed with industry leaders. Students learn to analyse real-world problems and design modern infrastructure with an emphasis on building faster, better and more sustainably, and can take an 800-hour work-integrated learning placement. Entry is a four-year bachelor degree in civil engineering or a related field, or a Sydney Accord accredited three-year Bachelor of Technology; applicants from other engineering fields with relevant industry experience are assessed case by case. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as consulting and contracting civil engineers, structural engineers, site engineers, construction engineers and estimators across the public and private sectors. Indicative international tuition is around A$48,200 per year.

name: Master of Clinical Audiology
description: La Trobe's Master of Clinical Audiology is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree that qualifies graduates to work as audiologists. Study covers the nature of sound, speech and auditory perception, and advanced diagnostic and rehabilitative audiology, taught in small classes with pre-clinical work and extensive supervised clinical placement. The degree is accredited by Audiology Australia, and graduates may apply for membership. Entry is a bachelor degree in the social, physical, biological or health sciences with a weighted average mark of at least 70 percent. IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0. Graduates work as clinical audiologists in major hospitals, private clinics and research facilities, running diagnostic hearing assessments and individualised rehabilitation programs. Indicative international tuition is around A$52,600 per year.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: La Trobe's Master of Clinical Psychology is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree that provides the professional training for a career in clinical psychology. Coursework covers cognitive behavioural therapy, child and adolescent mental health, psychopathology, counselling skills, psychological assessment and treatment, and advanced psychotherapy, alongside professional and ethical practice and report writing. A clinical placement practicum has students conduct intake assessments and casework with adults and children. Entry requires an accredited fourth-year psychology qualification with strong results, completed in the last ten years. IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0. The degree is accredited by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council and leads to general registration as a psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia and the pathway toward clinical endorsement. Indicative international tuition is around A$47,800 per year.

name: Master of Construction and Engineering Management
description: La Trobe's Master of Construction Engineering and Management is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree that combines construction engineering with project and people management. It is described by La Trobe as Australia's first master's degree in the construction engineering area accredited by Engineers Australia, currently at provisional accreditation. Students learn to manage complex projects while handling social, environmental and work health and safety challenges, complete 800 hours of work-integrated learning, and finish with a research-based unit or an industry capstone project. Entry is a four-year bachelor degree in engineering or a Sydney Accord accredited three-year Bachelor of Technology; an interview may be required. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as construction engineers and managers, engineering project managers, project engineers, estimators and quantity surveyors. Indicative international tuition is around A$47,800 per year.

name: Master of Counselling, Rehabilitation and Mental Health
description: La Trobe's Master of Counselling, Rehabilitation and Mental Health is a 240-credit-point degree, two years full-time, taught at the City campus in Melbourne in a multi-modal format, with a one-year pathway for holders of La Trobe's Graduate Diploma in Rehabilitation Counselling. It combines rehabilitation counselling and mental health subjects with hands-on practice, preparing graduates to work in rehabilitation counselling and in broader settings such as mental health and Employee Assistance Program counselling, supporting people through disability, disadvantage and injury to return to work and the community. Students can specialise in advanced practice or applied research. The degree is accredited by the Australian Society of Rehabilitation Counsellors and the Australian Counselling Association. Entry is a bachelor degree, ideally in health sciences, psychology or behavioural sciences, or relevant industry experience, with IELTS 6.5 and no band below 6.0. Graduates work as rehabilitation counsellors and counsellors across allied health, education, government and sport. Indicative international tuition is around A$44,800 per year.

name: Master of Cybersecurity
description: La Trobe's Master of Cybersecurity is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree taught in Melbourne, Sydney and online, open to applicants with or without an IT background. It builds skills in system design, implementation and testing, then technical depth in ethical hacking and network defence, secure coding, penetration testing, blockchain and cyber forensics, plus the psychology of cybercrime and approaches to governance and risk. Microsoft certifications and hands-on work in on-campus Cisco labs are built in, and students choose an industry development project or a work-based placement. A 1.5-year pathway is available for applicants with a computer science or IT bachelor degree, with early exit as a graduate certificate or diploma. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as security analysts, penetration testers, security consultants and security architects. Indicative international tuition is around A$45,600 per year.

name: Master of Data Science
description:
The Master of Data Science mirrors the IT masters' two-year, 240-credit-point structure, with a 1.5-year accelerated pathway for anyone holding a cognate degree in data science, AI or IT. Core subjects front-load the mathematical and programming groundwork (data exploration and analysis, database fundamentals, introductory programming, mathematics and probability/statistics for data science) before students branch into a genuinely varied elective list covering bioinformatics, sport analytics, big data and cloud computing, and business applications.

The sport analytics option is a distinctive inclusion tied to La Trobe's sport and exercise science strength (the university runs a well-regarded sport science program out of Bundoora), giving data science students a specialisation that isn't just a rebadged AI or business analytics track. Delivery is multi-modal, blending online and on-campus study, which suits the working-professional segment of the cohort who are retraining into data careers mid-career.
curriculum:
Core subjects: Data Exploration and Analysis, Database Fundamentals, Introduction to Programming, Mathematics for Data Science, Probability and Statistics for Data Science, Professional Practices and Entrepreneurship in IT
Elective/specialisation subjects in Artificial Intelligence, Bioinformatics, Sport Analytics, Big Data and Cloud Computing, or Business Applications and Data Modelling
Capstone data science project
240 credit points over 2 years standard; 180 credit points/1.5 years for cognate-entry applicants
Multi-modal (online and on-campus) delivery
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree with quantitative background
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent

name: Master of Dietetics
description: La Trobe's Master of Dietetics is a 1.5-year, 195-credit-point degree that qualifies graduates to practise as registered dietitians, building on La Trobe's long history in nutrition education. It takes a person-centred, evidence-based approach to nutrition science and applies research skills across clinical and community practice settings. The degree is accredited by Dietitians Australia. Entry is a bachelor degree in nutrition, or in a science or health field with a nutrition minor, completed in the last eight years and including set units in human biology, human physiology, chemistry and biochemistry. IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0. Graduates work in hospitals, private practice, community and public health, and research. Indicative international tuition is around A$52,600 per year for a full-time year.

name: Master of Digital Health
description: La Trobe's Master of Digital Health is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree for people who want to design, implement and manage digital health solutions. Study covers health analytics, virtual care, the Internet of Medical Things, and health apps and social media, along with the benefits, risks and legal and ethical implications of these technologies. Students tailor the degree with one of eight specialisations, from data analytics, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence to health management, strategy and policy, and public health, and can take a work-based project. Entry is a completed bachelor degree in any discipline. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as digital health analysts and consultants and digital health project managers across commercial and public sector organisations. Indicative international tuition is around A$43,000 per year.

name: Master of Education (By Coursework)
description: La Trobe's Master of Education is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree for experienced educators and related professionals moving into leadership or specialist roles. Core subjects cover educational leadership, psychology, research and digital technologies, with the option to specialise in inclusion and diversity, language and literacy, or leadership and management, and an emphasis on curriculum reform, program design and using data for evidence-based practice. This is not an initial teacher education course and does not lead to registration with the Victorian Institute of Teaching. Entry is a completed bachelor degree. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as school leaders, inclusive education coordinators, learning designers, education managers and education researchers. Indicative international tuition is around A$40,600 per year.

name: Master of Engineering
description: La Trobe's Master of Engineering is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree combining technical, research and management capability, with a specialisation in either electronics or telecommunications and networks. Students advance their engineering practice through design, research and innovation, build knowledge in engineering management, data and software, and examine how AI and robotics are changing the profession and how to work sustainably in the Australian industry. The Melbourne offering is accredited by Engineers Australia. Entry is a four-year bachelor degree in electronic or electrical engineering or a related field, or a Sydney Accord accredited three-year Bachelor of Technology. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work as electronics engineers, network and systems engineers, robotics engineers and telecommunications engineers across communications, defence, medical technology and public administration. Indicative international tuition is around A$48,200 per year.

name: Master of Engineering (by Research) Computer Systems, Biomedical
Master of Engineering Management
description: La Trobe's Master of Engineering Management is a two-year, 240-credit-point degree that adds commercial and leadership capability to an engineering qualification. Students take management, innovation and sustainability subjects designed for engineers, plus a business foundation in marketing, finance, organisational behaviour and business data analysis. The second year moves into risk and cost management, project management, strategic management and computer-aided engineering, and students deepen one engineering specialisation chosen from twelve disciplines. IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates move into engineering project management and technical leadership roles across manufacturing, technology, telecommunications, geotechnical, government and construction. Indicative international tuition is around A$50,000 per year; confirm the current figure on the La Trobe course page.

name: Master of Health Administration
