name: Master of Pharmaceutical Science
description: Monash's Master of Pharmaceutical Science covers the full arc of how a medicine gets from an idea to a patient, working through target identification, drug design, formulation, clinical trials and regulatory approval using case studies drawn from real pharmaceutical challenges. Students get hands-on experience with the analytical, formulation and modelling techniques used in industry research and development, rather than a purely theoretical treatment of pharmaceutical science, and the course closes with an extended industry or research placement and a capstone unit where students apply everything they've learned in a genuine professional setting. Sustainability and social responsibility are built into the curriculum's framing throughout, reflecting current pressure on the pharmaceutical industry to address both drug access and environmental impact. It suits science graduates aiming for roles in pharmaceutical research, drug development, regulatory affairs or the broader biotech and pharmaceutical industry, particularly those who want practical placement experience alongside their qualification rather than a purely academic pathway.

The course suits graduates from health, science or social science backgrounds moving into public health policy, health promotion, epidemiology or global health roles across government, NGOs and international health organisations.

name: Master of Transport and Mobility Planning
description: Monash's Master of Transport and Mobility Planning tackles the interrelated social, economic and environmental factors driving transport policy, infrastructure and land use decisions in modern cities, combining theoretical coursework with project-based real-world case studies. The course covers multi-modal traffic engineering and management, travel demand modelling, and the economic factors that shape transport infrastructure decisions, alongside a dedicated research methods component that builds the analytical skills needed to evaluate transportation projects rigorously. A strong emphasis on integrating new technology into urban planning reflects how much transport planning has changed with the arrival of ride-sharing, electric vehicles and changing commuting patterns since the pandemic. It suits graduates from planning, engineering, geography or related backgrounds aiming for careers as transportation planners, urban mobility consultants or policy analysts in government or the private sector, particularly those interested in the technology and sustainability dimensions of how cities move people and goods.

Through the Southeast University partnership, eligible students complete both the Monash qualification and a second transportation-focused master's degree from the Chinese institution, giving dual international recognition. name: Master of Urban Planning and Design
description: Monash's Master of Urban Planning and Design, accredited by the Planning Institute of Australia, combines planning practice and design theory to prepare graduates for genuine twenty-first-century city challenges including climate change, urban growth and technological transitions. Real-world project studios organised around themes like the Compact, Expanding, Transforming and Inclusive City have students develop practical planning and design solutions each semester, working alongside classmates from architecture, landscape architecture, engineering, law, economics and geography backgrounds. That deliberately multidisciplinary cohort mirrors how urban planning actually works in practice, where planners constantly collaborate with professionals from other built-environment disciplines rather than working in isolation. Career paths span statutory planning roles in local government, urban design positions in state agencies, and roles in firms specialising in community planning and affordable housing, both in Australia and internationally, and the course suits graduates from any of those contributing disciplines who want to move into urban planning and design specifically.

name: Accelerated Research Masters with Training
description: Our Accelerated Research Masters with Training is a globally recognised, 12-month alternative pathway for graduate students who wish to expand their knowledge and undertake research in any given area. The course has a deep focus on an interdisciplinary approach, where you will work collectively with your peers to address and provide answers to key United Nations Sustainable Development Goals through a tailored unit in design thinking. You will also learn about research methods, the importance of research impact and you will work with a supervisory team to undertake research in your chosen area of interest. Throughout your studies, you will: Gain high-level technical and creative skills to investigate, analyse and synthesise complex information, problems, concepts and theories. Apply theories to different bodies of knowledge or practice. Have the opportunity to plan and execute a substantial research-based project. Gain theoretical knowledge to reflect critically on theory and professional practice. The Bioplastics Innovation Hub (BIH) is a collaborative project between Murdoch University, CSIRO and industry partners. Together, we are researching and developing 100% compostable bioplastics using organic waste that will leave no plastic legacy on land or in water. This includes a Research Masters with Training Specialising in Advanced Biomanufacturing to help ensure that Australia has the skilled personnel needed to deliver the plastic revolution on the global stage. For further information.
curriculum: There is no unit-based curriculum. Candidates complete a supervised, independent research project in their chosen field, with milestones including a research proposal, a progress review, and submission of a thesis for examination.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission as a candidate into the M1315 Accelerated Research Masters with Training an applicant must: • have a Bachelor Degree in the same or cognate discipline (AQF level 7); or • have a Bachelor Degree in a different discipline (AQF level 7) and: 1. have successfully completed a graduate course incorporating research training of at least six months of equivalent full-time study (AQF level 8); or 2. satisfy the Dean of Graduate Research with evidence of significant scholarly or professional attainments equivalent to AQF level 8. And Satisfy the English language requirements for entry into a Higher Degrees by Research program at Murdoch University

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Science
description: Study agricultural science at Australia's only city-based university with an on-campus farm If you're passionate about food production, animal health and sustainable farming, our Bachelor of Agricultural Science gives you the scientific knowledge and practical experience to thrive in Australia's evolving agricultural sector. Across your undergraduate degree, you'll develop strong foundations in science, data analysis and farming systems. You can tailor your studies with one or two majors - Animal Health , Animal Science or Crop and Pasture Science - that align with your interests and career goals. With access to our unique on-campus farm, you'll apply your learning in real production environments from your first year. You'll learn from academics leading applied research in animal health, crop systems and sustainable production, gaining insights shaped by real industry challenges and emerging innovation. Over the course of the program, you'll also work with the latest agricultural technologies and tools used across modern farming, animal health and agribusiness settings. From laboratories and farms to paddocks and professional placements, our highly practical degree in agricultural science sees real-world experience is integrated into every year of your course. You'll graduate with a clear understanding of how agriculture operates at local, national and global levels - and the skills, industry insight and professional confidence employers value. Learn about student profiles for this course on our Admission Information page. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Develop analytical and technical skills to solve real-world agricultural and animal health challenges. Collaborate with scientists across agriculture, animal health and environmental science. Studying both Crop and Pasture and Animal Science gave me the opportunity to learn about all sectors of the industry. In my first year, I went on field trips, handled animals and spoke to people directly involved in agriculture. Brittany, Agricultural Science.

name: Bachelor of Applied Social Care
description:
A three-year degree in applied social care, developed with industry and community partners for roles across the care and community services sector. Students choose one major from Child and Family Studies, Human Behaviour, International Aid and Development, Sociology, or Foundations of Business Management, and build practical skills through internships and placements with community organisations, government agencies and not-for-profits.

One thing to be clear on: this is a social care degree, not an accredited social work qualification, so it does not by itself lead to registration as a social worker with the Australian Association of Social Workers. Students who want that should look at an accredited Bachelor of Social Work. Entry is an ATAR of about 70, with Murdoch RISE adjustments and other alternative pathways available. Graduates work as child, family and youth support workers, disability support workers, care coordinators and community services officers. It suits students headed for frontline community and care roles.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description: Study a Bachelor of Arts and tailor your degree to your interests and career goals Design a degree that reflects what you care about and what you want to do. Throughout your arts course, you'll develop critical thinking, communication and analytical skills while tailoring your studies to your interests. You could explore languages and cultures through Japanese , Indonesian or Asian Studies ; politics, society and global issues through Politics and International Studies , Sociology , International Aid and Development or Sustainable Development ; creativity and storytelling through English and Creative Writing or Theatre and Creative Production ; or people, ideas and communities through Community Development , History , Philosophy or Tourism and Events . You'll also gain practical experience through industry-led projects, internships or community-based opportunities, applying your skills in real-world contexts and building valuable professional experience before you graduate. Whether you want to work in media, government, international development, community services or the creative industries, our flexible arts degree gives you the freedom to shape your studies and build the skills needed for your future career. Discover where a Bachelor of Arts could take you through the experiences of our graduates. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

description: Study biomedical science in the heart of the Murdoch Health and Knowledge Precinct Biomedical science is central to understanding health, disease and medical innovation, driving advances in healthcare and research. Our Bachelor of Biomedical Science degree equips you with the knowledge and practical skills to explore how the human body works, diagnose disease and contribute to these advances. During your biomedical science course, you'll study areas such as human biology, disease processes, diagnostics and laboratory science. Guided by leading academics, you'll develop strong analytical and problem-solving skills while exploring leading-edge research and how scientific discoveries translate into real-world health outcomes and biomedical research. name: Bachelor of Business
description:
Murdoch's Bachelor of Business runs on a major-first model. The degree itself is broad, and the substance comes from choosing among majors including Accounting, Banking, Business Law, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Finance, Hospitality and Tourism Management, Human Resources Management (with AHRI accreditation available), Management, and Marketing. Because majors are tied to the degree rather than offered as standalone qualifications, students effectively pick their specialisation after enrolling rather than applying into it directly.

An elective Work Integrated Learning program is the degree's most concrete differentiator: students take on real projects and internships with organisations that have included local government bodies, Myer, and RAC Arena, giving business students the kind of client-facing experience that's usually reserved for professional-track degrees like law or engineering. It's optional rather than compulsory, so outcomes vary a lot depending on whether a given student opts in.

The core skill set the university emphasises (critical thinking, financial literacy, data-informed decision-making, ethics) reads as fairly standard business-school language, but the WIL placements are where the degree's actual differentiation from a generic business degree shows up in practice.
curriculum:
Year 1: business core (accounting principles, economics, business law, marketing fundamentals, quantitative methods for business)
Year 2: major sequence begins (choice of Accounting, Banking, Business Law, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Finance, Hospitality and Tourism Management, HR Management, Management, or Marketing), business analytics
Year 3: advanced major units, elective Work Integrated Learning placement (internship or industry project), capstone business strategy unit
Total: 3 years full-time; WIL placements available with employers including local government, retail and major venues

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description: Understand crime and uphold justice with a tailored criminology course Crime affects individuals, communities and institutions in complex ways. Our Bachelor of Criminology allows you to explore why offences occur, how they can be prevented and how the criminal justice system responds to victims and offenders. You'll examine crime from social, psychological, legal and scientific perspectives, developing a well-rounded understanding of contemporary justice issues. As part of your degree in criminology, you'll contribute to real homicide and missing persons investigations through our Major Crimes Review initiative - a unique opportunity to apply your skills to genuine cases in an industry-linked learning environment. Throughout your studies, you'll be mentored by experienced criminologists to analyse criminal cases and evaluate justice processes. Tailor your studies by specialising in Criminal Behaviour , Crime Science or Legal Studies - with the Crime Science major the only program of its kind in Australia. You can complete a double major or combine criminology with another discipline, such as biology, toxicology or psychology, to broaden your expertise. During your undergraduate criminology degree, you'll build strong analytical and critical thinking skills, preparing you to assess evidence, understand justice systems and contribute meaningfully to crime prevention and justice reform. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Examine the motives, methods and psychology behind serious offenders and complex criminal behaviour. Evaluate policing, judicial practices and the lived experiences of individuals within the criminal justice system. Interpret forensic evidence and assess criminal cases, using structured legal and investigative frameworks. Apply evidence-based approaches to analyse crime from social, legal and scientific perspectives. Develop creative and critical thinking to interpret complex information and support informed justice outcomes. I love the freedom to think and have opinions without criticism. The lecturers allow for discussion, understanding that everyone may have a different opinion, and allow for free-flowing conversation. name: Bachelor of Data Analytics
description:
This degree sits at the intersection of statistics, programming and business decision-making rather than treating data analytics as a pure computer science offshoot: students build up R and Python skills for analysis alongside database design and visualisation tools like Tableau and Power BI, but the course frames all of it around organisational and business problem-solving rather than algorithmic theory for its own sake.

Students choose a specialisation track, most commonly Data Science or Business Intelligence, and the course requires an industry internship or applied project as part of the structure rather than offering it as an optional extra. Murdoch runs this partly through its IT Innovation Hub, which houses a data centre reported at roughly $2 million in infrastructure investment, a relatively serious facility for an undergraduate-focused analytics degree at a mid-sized Australian university.

Scholarship pathways like the Westpac Young Technologists Program give some students early industry contact before graduation, which matters in a field where employers weight practical project experience heavily against a still-developing formal discipline. Graduates commonly move into business intelligence analyst, data analyst or junior data scientist roles depending on which specialisation track they followed.
curriculum:
Year 1: introduction to programming (Python/R), statistics for data analysis, database fundamentals, business and organisational context units
Year 2: data visualisation and reporting (Tableau, Power BI), database design and management, applied statistical modelling, specialisation choice (Data Science or Business Intelligence)
Year 3: advanced analytics/machine learning fundamentals (Data Science track) or business intelligence systems (Business Intelligence track), industry internship or capstone analytics project, research and communication skills
Total: 3 years full-time; industry internship or applied project embedded in final year

description: Graduate ready to teach from birth to Year 6 with our unique early childhood and primary teaching degree Combining early learning expertise with primary curriculum knowledge, our Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood and Primary Teaching) prepares you to support children at every stage of their development. The only one of its kind in WA, this teaching degree qualifies you to work in both early learning settings and primary school classrooms from the moment you graduate. Grounded in research and real-world practice, our undergraduate teaching degree explores how play shapes creativity, resilience and cognitive growth. Throughout your studies, caring and experienced educators will support you as you build practical skills using evidence-based approaches while discovering how young learners think, communicate and grow. You'll study key primary curriculum areas such as English, mathematics, science, humanities and social sciences, health and physical education and the arts, all while specialising in early childhood development. Designed as a future-focused early childhood education degree, the course blends theory, classroom simulation using SimLab™ virtual technology and professional experience, so you graduate confident, capable and ready to launch your teaching career. Through extensive teaching placements in early learning centres and schools, you'll apply what you've learned in real classrooms. name: Bachelor of Engineering Honours
description:
Murdoch's engineering degree is genuinely small in scope compared to the sprawling multi-discipline programs at the larger Group of Eight universities. It offers three specialisations (Electrical and Renewable Energy Engineering, Environmental Engineering, and Industrial Control and Automation Engineering) rather than a dozen, and leans into that focus with a facility the school describes as the only one of its kind at a Western Australian university: a real-world engineering plant with a dedicated control room, used for hands-on training rather than simulation alone.

Every student completes 450 hours of professional work placement as part of the degree, and honours is embedded rather than a separate bolt-on year students apply for separately. Everyone finishes with an individual research or industry project in year four, applying material from the first three years to a genuine open-ended problem. That focus on renewable energy and industrial automation tracks reasonably well with Western Australia's resources and energy sector employment base, which is a different emphasis than engineering programs oriented toward software or biomedical applications.

Given the specialisation is fixed early relative to some universities' common-first-year models, students choosing this course should have a reasonably clear sense already of whether they want electrical/renewables, environmental, or automation/control work.
curriculum:
Years 1–2: engineering mathematics, engineering mechanics and materials, electrical circuits and systems fundamentals, programming for engineers, specialisation core units begin
Year 3: specialisation deepening (Electrical and Renewable Energy, Environmental, or Industrial Control and Automation), control systems, sustainability and infrastructure units, 450 hours professional work placement (completed across the course)
Year 4 (Honours, embedded): advanced specialisation electives, individual research or industry-based honours project, professional practice and ethics
Total: 4 years full-time (Honours embedded, not a separate application); access to Murdoch's dedicated engineering plant and control room facility

By the time you graduate, you'll have practical experience, industry insight and the confidence to launch your engineering career. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

name: Bachelor of Food Science and Nutrition

Throughout your food science and nutrition course, you'll explore the relationship between food, nutrition and health while building expertise in areas such as food chemistry, microbiology, food safety and human nutrition. Your learning combines scientific theory with hands-on experience in laboratories and food production settings. With access to the Murdoch Health and Knowledge Precinct and specialised teaching facilities, you'll work with industry-standard equipment to analyse food composition, assess quality and safety, and develop food products that meet nutritional and regulatory standards. By the time you graduate, you'll be prepared to contribute to the development of safe, nutritious and innovative food products while supporting public health and the evolving global food industry. Discover how Bachelor of Food Science and Nutrition student Tahlia is shaping her future and career goals through her studies.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
Murdoch's IT degree is built around named majors rather than a single generalist stream, and Cyber Security and Forensics is the one the school markets hardest: it covers network security, software security, computer forensics and penetration testing, and it carries Australian Computer Society accreditation at the Professional level, which is a recognised bar for graduates entering security roles in Australia.

Students aren't locked to a single major either; the course structure explicitly supports a double major within IT, or pairing an IT major with a major from another Murdoch degree, which lets students build combinations like cyber security plus data science or IT plus criminology that a single-major degree wouldn't allow. Delivery mixes on-campus lectures with lab-based practical work and industry placement opportunities, which matters in a discipline where a lot of the actual skill (network configuration, exploit analysis) doesn't transfer well from lecture slides alone.

Career outcomes cited by the school for cyber-focused graduates include security consultant, forensic investigator and database administrator roles: a broader spread than "penetration tester" alone, reflecting that most entry-level security jobs in Australia are still generalist information-security roles rather than narrow specialisations.
curriculum:
Year 1: programming fundamentals, computer systems and networks, database fundamentals, introduction to information security
Year 2: network security, systems administration, software security principles, major-specific units (e.g. Cyber Security and Forensics, Data Science, Web and Mobile Development)
Year 3: computer forensics, penetration testing and vulnerability assessment, advanced major electives, industry placement or capstone project
Total: 3 years full-time; Cyber Security and Forensics major accredited by the Australian Computer Society at Professional level; double-major and cross-degree combinations available

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
The distinguishing feature of Murdoch's law degree is SCALES, its award-winning student law clinic: students earn academic credit working actual client matters in areas like human rights law, family law and community legal issues, under supervision, rather than working through hypothetical case studies for the whole degree. That's a genuine point of difference from law schools where "clinical experience" is a mooting exercise dressed up in different language.

The school also foregrounds a social-justice orientation more explicitly than many Australian law programs: human rights and access-to-justice framing shows up across the marketing and, by the school's account, in elective offerings, which shapes who tends to be drawn to Murdoch Law over a more corporate-commercial-focused program. Mooting runs through a purpose-built courtroom facility and is positioned as building advocacy and courtroom presence alongside the clinic work rather than replacing it.

Beyond the clinic, Murdoch's Work Integrated Learning internship program places law students with law firms, government agencies and not-for-profits, which is a fairly standard offering across Australian law schools but is run here with the same WIL infrastructure Murdoch uses for its business and other professional degrees.
curriculum:
Year 1: introduction to law and legal system, legal research and writing, contracts, torts
Year 2: property law, criminal law, constitutional law, equity, SCALES law clinic (credit-bearing clinical placement) or mooting unit
Year 3: evidence, administrative law, dispute resolution, WIL internship (law firms, government, not-for-profit), advanced electives (e.g. human rights law, family law)
Total: 3 years full-time (as a single degree) or extended when combined with another Murdoch degree; SCALES clinical placement credit-bearing and available to eligible students
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 80+ (or equivalent); completion of WACE or equivalent secondary qualification.

Throughout your Bachelor of Laws degree, you'll gain hands-on experience through practical learning opportunities, including working with real clients in our clinical legal program in partnership with organisations such as SCALES Community Legal Centre . These experiences give you valuable insight into legal practice while building your professional skills. You'll also refine your advocacy and courtroom skills through competitions in our internationally recognised mooting program, where you'll argue simulated cases in a purpose-built courtroom environment. Combined with real-world placements through our Work Integrated Learning program, these experiences ensure you graduate with both theoretical knowledge and practical capability. You can also develop a unique specialisation by combining law with your existing qualification. Whether your background is. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Murdoch's nursing degree puts 20 weeks of supervised work experience into the course, spread across hospitals, aged care and community health settings rather than concentrated in a single block. Students typically encounter several different care contexts before they graduate rather than specialising in one setting by default. The School of Nursing's placement partners span both metropolitan Perth hospitals and rural WA services, so students can end up doing a rotation somewhere quite different from where they studied.

Before students reach a real ward, the course leans on simulated clinical environments and case-based learning to build competence and confidence, a fairly standard approach in Australian nursing education now, but one Murdoch runs with dedicated simulation labs on its Perth campus. Specialty placement areas mentioned by the school include gerontology, mental health, paediatrics and critical care, giving students exposure to sub-specialties they might not otherwise encounter until postgraduate study.

On graduation, students are eligible to register with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia through AHPRA, and the degree is commonly used as a springboard into postgraduate specialisation: critical care, mental health nursing or midwifery graduate-entry programs are the usual next step for those who want to sub-specialise.
curriculum:
Year 1: foundations of nursing practice, anatomy and physiology, health assessment, introduction to professional communication and ethics
Year 2: pathophysiology and pharmacology, mental health nursing, chronic disease and complex care, clinical placement blocks in hospital and community settings
Year 3: acute and critical care nursing, aged care and rehabilitation, leadership and transition to practice, specialty placement rotations (e.g. paediatrics, mental health, critical care)
Total placement across the course: approximately 20 weeks of work experience in hospitals, aged care and community settings
Total: 3 years full-time; graduates eligible for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to clinical placement.

name: Bachelor of Psychology
description:
This is Murdoch's APAC-accredited undergraduate psychology sequence: three years that lead, for eligible students, into a fourth Honours year rather than being accredited as a stand-alone terminal qualification. Students who complete both years exit eligible for provisional registration with the Psychology Board of Australia, which is the credential that actually matters for anyone planning to practise.

The Honours year is where the degree's research emphasis becomes explicit: students negotiate an original empirical research topic with a supervisor, and the year culminates in both a written thesis and a poster presented at a research conference, a dual output that mirrors how psychology researchers actually communicate findings, rather than a thesis alone. Advanced coursework alongside the research project balances theoretical grounding with the practical and professional issues graduates will face applying psychology in clinical, organisational or community settings.

Because Honours places are typically limited relative to the number of students completing the pass degree, students planning to progress need to maintain competitive grades through years one to three, a standard feature of Australian psychology accreditation nationwide, not unique to Murdoch, but one that shapes how seriously students need to take GPA management from first year.
curriculum:
Year 1: introduction to psychology, biological psychology, cognitive psychology, introductory statistics and research methods
Year 2: developmental psychology, social psychology, personality and individual differences, intermediate research methods
Year 3: abnormal psychology, psychological assessment, advanced statistics, discipline electives
Year 4 (Honours, separate accredited course): advanced seminars in applied psychology, supervised original empirical research project, thesis and conference-style poster presentation
Total: 3 years full-time (pass degree); Honours (4th year) APAC-accredited and required for provisional psychologist registration eligibility

name: Bachelor of Psychology Honours
description: A Bachelor of Psychology Honours will provide you with an in-depth understanding of the principles and practice of psychology. This course is a step on the pathway to becoming a registered psychologist . Working closely with an academic, you'll undertake an individual research project of your choice. You'll also develop your research ability through coursework on psychological measurement and practice. An Honours qualification of 2A (or suitable equivalent) is normally required for admission to postgraduate coursework and research degrees. Pathway information for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander applicants Murdoch University aspires to be the first choice for First Nations peoples. We wholeheartedly welcome and encourage Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people to consider applying for our psychology programs. Across our psychology courses, places are reserved for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander students. While these applicants must meet the specified criteria for each course to gain admission, they will not go through the competitive selection process. These places are reserved under an exemption to the Equal Opportunity Act 1984 , which is applied to promote equality and aligns with Australian Indigenous Psychology Education Project (AIPEP) guidelines for creating equity pathways for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander applicants. If you would like more information, please contact Ann-Maree Vallence at ann-maree.vallence@murdoch.edu.au.

Clear and coherent communication of psychological knowledge. Fundamentals of psychological assessment and intervention. What I am enjoying the most about the course is the varied experience and expertise I am able to draw upon in my time here, both in the area of psychological research as well as clinical practice. Veena Singh, Psychology.

name: Bachelor of Science / Doctor of Veterinary Medicine
description:
Murdoch runs the only veterinary school in Western Australia, and this is its flagship pathway: a three-year Bachelor of Science (Veterinary Biology) that transitions directly into a two-year Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, with the DVM itself run across trimesters rather than standard semesters to compress five years of content into the combined structure. Students don't apply separately into the DVM. The two qualifications are integrated by design, though academic progression standards still apply at the transition point.

The degree gives access to genuinely rare undergraduate infrastructure for an Australian veterinary program: a working teaching hospital treating companion animals, exotics, farm animals and horses, plus an operational farm, all on the same Perth campus rather than split across satellite sites. Species-group electives ("streaming") let students start weighting their final years toward large animal, equine or small animal practice depending on where they see their career heading, and the final year is largely spent immersed in the teaching hospital rather than in lecture theatres.

Because the DVM sits at AQF level 9, a master's-equivalent qualification, this is one of the longer and more structured pathways in the Murdoch catalogue, and the tuition reflects the cost of running live-animal clinical training rather than being comparable to a standard science degree.
curriculum:
Years 1–3 (Bachelor of Science, Veterinary Biology): animal biology and physiology, biochemistry, animal husbandry, foundational veterinary science units, six semesters total
Years 4–5 (Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, trimester-based): clinical veterinary training, species-group elective streaming (large animal, equine, small animal), professional and business skills for veterinary practice, six trimesters total
Final year: primarily hands-on clinical rotations through the on-campus veterinary teaching hospital and farm
Total: 5 years full-time, integrated BSc + DVM (AQF level 9 for the DVM component)
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 90+ (or equivalent), plus completion of Murdoch's veterinary science aptitude assessment and/or interview; highly competitive limited-entry program.

description: Focus on a field of science which interests you - from Games Technology to Biomedical Science, Marine Biology, Forensic Biology & Toxicology, Animal Health, Conservation & Wildlife Biology, Chemistry, Physics & Nanotechnology, Genetics & Molecular Biology, Sport & Health Science and more. You can take your learning outside the classroom with opportunities to travel overseas or complete internships or get involved in industry or community projects as part of your studies. For example, if you study Marine Biology, you'll take part in field camps, field trips and projects along our iconic Western Australian coastline. You'll get valuable experience through professional placements, working on science-related projects for real organisations. For example, if you study Games Technology, you'll learn to apply scientific thinking to develop games, apps and artificial intelligence. Expand your career prospects even further with a double major in a complementary scientific area or a double degree in another discipline, such as law, business, management or communications. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

name: Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science
description: Turn your love of sport into a sport science career Interested in how exercise improves health, performance and recovery? Our Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science prepares you to understand how the human body moves and responds to physical activity, building the scientific knowledge and practical skills needed for a rewarding career in sports science. Throughout your sport and exercise science degree, you'll explore key areas such as exercise physiology, biomechanics, sport psychology and motor control. You'll learn how to assess physical performance, analyse movement and design exercise programs that support both athletic performance and general health. Your learning combines scientific theory with applied practice. With access to our purpose-built, facilities , specialised laboratories and industry-standard technology, you'll gain experience analysing movement, testing physical performance and developing evidence-based exercise programs through practical classes and work-based learning opportunities across sport, fitness and health settings. By the time you graduate, you'll have a strong understanding of how exercise supports health, rehabilitation and performance, preparing you for a wide range of opportunities across sport, fitness and health industries. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Apply exercise physiology principles to improve fitness, health and rehabilitation outcomes. Analyse human movement and performance through biomechanics and motor control. Design evidence-based exercise programs tailored to athletes and community populations. Investigate the psychological and behavioural factors influencing sport and physical activity. Use scientific research methods to evaluate sport and exercise performance. The thing I've enjoyed most about Murdoch University is the opportunities to work with teaching staff who have years of experience, allowing me to pick their brains and gain a greater understanding of the practical application in the field. Jake, Allied Health student.

name: Doctor of Philosophy
description: Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) gives you the opportunity to explore in depth a research project that you're passionate about. You will independently research a specific topic under the guidance of a supervisor and produce a thesis no more than 100,000 words. Your research will represent a significant, original contribution to human knowledge. In undertaking a PhD, you will develop independent research skills, including the capacity to formulate a problem, develop mastery of appropriate conceptual and methodological skills to address it, and relate the research topic to a broader framework of knowledge in a relevant discipline. The process of completing your thesis offers exciting opportunities to work with and be challenged by top academics and experts in your field, as well as attending national and international conferences. Candidature for research degrees is offered in all disciplines. Murdoch encourages research in interdisciplinary areas as well as in the basic disciplines. For further information on Graduate Research Degrees, see the Future Research Students page . name: Doctor of Psychology in Clinical Psychology
description: If you're working towards becoming a registered psychologist and have completed your fourth year, this course provides you with the education required to complete the doctoral degree pathway. If you are already working as a registered psychologist, you'll gain specialist skills in clinical practice combined with extensive research. Murdoch's clinical training adopts an integrative and critical approach to clinical practice with a strong emphasis on clinical competencies and preparation for clinical practice. You'll learn how to apply your skills and knowledge in prevention and psychological intervention. You will also become a proficient researcher with practical research skills and the ability to develop novel interventions and program evaluation at the individual and system levels. The Doctor of Psychology is an intensive three-and-a-half year professional research degree consisting of clinical and research seminars, supervised practical work and supervision of a major research project in clinical psychology. You'll learn through coursework, practicum, and the research components, undertaking at least three practical placements to hone your skills as a clinical psychologist. A Professional Doctoral Degree is a research-focussed qualification recognised and accredited by APAC that makes a significant and original contribution to knowledge in the context of professional practice. You'll achieve professional accreditation as a Clinical Psychologist via a program of structured learning with a comprehensive research program undertaken over at least two years.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Build essential skills and knowledge to meet your career or study goals. Topics you'll cover include: Applying the rigorous method and innovative findings of psychological science to practice Assessment and intervention with individuals, families and communities Developing professional capacity and identity through a process of building comprehensive skills and experience in the context of the ethical and personal development in a supported environment Assessment, diagnosis, treatment planning, the delivery of psychological therapy and mental health promotion and prevention Working with clients across all stages of the lifespan: pregnancy, infancy, family life and parenting, adulthood and older adulthood. What I am enjoying the most about the course is the varied experience and expertise I am able to draw upon in my time here, both in the area of psychological research as well as clinical practice. Veena Singh, Psychology.
admission_requirements: Students who complete the first year of the Master of Applied Psychology in Clinical Psychology (M1156) and who average grades of Distinction in their first year units may apply for transfer to the Doctor of Psychology in Clinical Psychology. Applicants for the Doctor of Psychology in Clinical Psychology are required to submit a synopsis of their intended research and the name of a supervisor on the staff of the University as part of their application. Applicants will be required to present their research plans to a panel of Psychology staff prior to admission. Students permitted to transfer from the Master of Applied Psychology in Clinical Psychology will be exempt from the units common to both degrees. Applicants who hold the equivalent of the relevant Master of Applied Psychology in Clinical Psychology and current AHPRA registration with endorsement in clinical psychology can apply for direct entry and are to complete the balance of units in the Doctor of Psychology in Clinical Psychology. In some circumstances, the degree may be undertaken on a part-time basis but requires attendance of on-campus seminars and, for parts of the course, full-day attendance on campus or at a practicum site.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0, no band below 6.0); PTE Academic overall 58. name: Doctor of Veterinary Medical Science
description: This comprehensive combined coursework and research program is the only one of its kind in Western Australia. You'll have access to our on-campus, highly regarded veterinary facilities for training in a broad range of disciplines within veterinary science, including epidemiology and public health, parasitology, and clinical specialities. If required, you will also have access to Whitby Falls Farm, our off-campus teaching and research facility. This 203-hectare heritage listed farm property, located 46 kilometres south of Perth, will offer you further experience in livestock research. You'll gain advanced academic preparation in applied research. The degree provides the opportunity for advanced study in analytical and research skills in veterinary science, applied to clinical and non-clinical disciplines. The DVetMedSc program culminates in the completion of a research thesis. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Build essential skills and knowledge to meet your career or study goals. Topics you'll cover include: research skills through elective coursework units in research methodology the disciplines of epidemiology and veterinary pathology tailoring a research project to an animal disease or condition relevant to your field of interest. I love that Murdoch University is the only city-based university in Australia with a farm on campus. It makes it so easy to do practical classes right on your doorstep with all the state-of-the-art veterinary equipment and technologies. Saba, Veterinary Medicine.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission as a candidate for a Doctor of Veterinary Medical Science, an applicant must have: *Bachelor Degree in Veterinary Science with at least a 2A Honours normally in the same discipline (AQF level 8); ora Bachelor Degree in Veterinary Science (AQF level 7) and satisfy the Dean of Graduate Research with evidence of substantive and significant scholarly or professional attainments including satisfactory research preparation the equivalent of AQF level 8 or 9.

name: FlexiTrack High
description: Murdoch University works with participating FlexiTrack High secondary schools to provide a structured and supportive learning experience for students seeking an alternative option to the ATAR entry pathway into university. This is a chance to gain essential skills, bolster confidence and get a tangible feel of university-style learning while studying in high school. The program is delivered as a blended program utilising both online independent study and dedicated class time at each partner school. Over a period of 30 weeks, FlexiTrack High focuses on developing a student's academic skills as well as the self-regulation and independent learning competencies needed to successfully undertake tertiary study. Dates: Week commencing 1 st February- 24 th September 2027. Cost: $300 (Fully funded scholarships are available to equity students) To succeed you must be committed to attending FlexiTrack High classes during Terms 1, 2 and 3 while you're completing Year 12 as well as studying independently and during the term breaks. You will be eligible to apply for an undergraduate course at Murdoch University if you successfully pass FlexiTrack High and meet attendance requirements. As FlexiTrack High attracts WACE points it is assumed that you will complete Year 12. How to apply If your school is participating in our FlexiTrack High program, they will need to chat with you about whether you meet the eligibility.
curriculum: FlexiTrack High is a pre-university enabling program at Murdoch University. It combines foundational academic skills units (academic writing, numeracy and study skills) with subject-area preparation units chosen to meet the entry requirements of a student's intended degree, delivered over one or two semesters.
admission_requirements: You must be concurrently enrolled and completing year 12 at a partner secondary school, and nominated by a school representative. Students on a humanitarian visa attending a partnership school may be nominated. To demonstrate English competence for entry into the program, you must demonstrate that you have achieved 'B' or higher in general English or a 'D' or higher in ATAR English in year 11.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0, no band below 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. Murdoch also accepts TOEFL iBT, Cambridge Advanced (CAE), Occupational English Test and Duolingo English Test at equivalent levels, plus completion of Year 11/12 in Australia or approved university preparation study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Advanced Wound Care
description: Are you a health professional seeking career development in the growing specialty of wound care and infection prevention? Advanced education in wound care is necessary to decrease healthcare acquired complications to improve outcomes for patients and our health service. You'll learn advanced theoretical concepts concerning the assessment and management of simple and complex wounds with course content developed and delivered by experts in the specialty of wound care and management. Students are expected to have some working experience in the care and management of wounds as unit discussions and assessment will require you to draw upon this experience. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: An understanding of the concepts and practices of wound assessment across a variety of different wound types. Contemporary wound assessment and diagnostic modalities and the role of the digital technologies for wound management. The concepts and practices of routine and advanced wound therapies. Strategic leadership in diverse healthcare environments I definitely wouldn't have chosen rural work if I didn't have the opportunity to do rural placements. A lot of the other universities don't really offer that as well as Murdoch do. Camille Talbott, Nursing Read full student story.

name: Graduate Certificate in Asian Language
description: Indonesia and Japan play an important role in contemporary political, economic and environmental global change. This six-month graduate certificate will provide students with the opportunity to advance their understanding of the Asian language through an immersive learning experience at one of our partner universities in Indonesia or Japan, or a combination of both overseas and on-campus study. To complement your studies, students will also have the options to study subjects such as literature, media, religion, history, politics, economics, sociology and anthropology of Japan or Indonesia in the relevant language. These areas combined will enable you to build a specialisation with a wealth of knowledge of the region and personal networks in the community. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Build the knowledge and skills you need to meet your career or study goals. In this course you will: Advance your knowledge of the Japanese or Indonesian language. Gain an understanding of the culture and society of Japan or Indonesia. Develop a strong understanding of politics, economics, sociology and religion in Japan or Indonesia Having completed three semesters and my honours research in Indonesia, I was able to get a much better idea of development on the ground. I found that when I graduated, I had a more realistic idea of what to expect in the workplace. Karis Erceg, Bachelor of Arts.
admission_requirements: AQF Level 7 (Bachelors) degree. Applicants must demonstrate independent user proficiency in the relevant language, sufficient to understand and produce spoken and written texts on general topics and to participate in sustained conversations with appropriate grammatical accuracy (subject to approval by the Academic Chair). All applicants will be required to participate in an interview (conducted in the target language) to assess language proficiency, communicative competence, and readiness for advanced postgraduate study prior to admission.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business Administration
description: If you are looking to increase your knowledge in business management, trial part of a Master of Business Administration (MBA) degree, connect with like-minded professionals, and develop business management skills to further your career, this course is for you. You'll study core units in financial decision-making, plus choose specialist units to create a personalised qualification that suits your goals and career aspirations. You can choose to specialise in two of the following areas: Organisational behaviour and management Strategic research in international markets Strategic marketing management Health policy and governance Strategic risks and projects Entrepreneurship and innovation Global business and Asia Human Resources Sustainability Economics Not-for-profit organisations Business, society and the environment Leading enterprises Growth strategies This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Build essential skills and knowledge to meet your career or study goals. Topics you'll cover include: Accounting for managers Business finance A specialist area of your choice Flexibility was key for me, and Murdoch University's diverse range of study options gave me the perfect fit. I love the blended learning format, and their small class sizes and supportive faculty mean I'm never lost in the crowd. I feel like I can really thrive here. Jasmin, Business.

name: Graduate Certificate in Cancer Nursing
description: This course will prepare you as a nurse to excel in diverse settings, ensuring you can provide compassionate and effective care to cancer patients. Over four specialised online units, you'll learn about the key areas of cancer nursing. You'll focus on the cultivation of safe, caring, respectful, and responsive therapeutic relationships, to empower patients across their care continuum. As a graduate, you will be adept at evaluating and integrating comprehensive information to provide holistic, evidence-based care, fostering collaborative interprofessional relationships to significantly enhance patient care and outcomes. You will be able to navigate complex health environments with confidence, adhering to professional, ethical, and legal standards, while applying a strengths-based approach to nursing care. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Build the knowledge and skills you need to meet your career or study goals. Specific areas you'll cover include: Foundational concepts in cancer care: Learn to engage critically with current challenges and future advancements in cancer research and treatment. Cancer therapies: Explore the latest advancements in cancer screening, diagnosis, and management, to enhance your understanding of current treatments and therapies for cancer. Supportive cancer care: Learn to develop patient-centred, comprehensive care plans, using evidence-based approaches to prevent and minimise the side effects of cancer treatments, optimising patient function and comfort. Strengths-based cancer care: Delve into the critical evaluation of evidence supporting complementary health choices that empower individuals to live well with cancer. I definitely wouldn't have chosen rural work if I didn't have the opportunity to do rural placements. A lot of the other universities don't really offer that as well as Murdoch do. Camille Talbott, Nursing Read full student story.
admission_requirements: A Bachelor of Nursing degree (AQF 7) or equivalent that qualifies the applicant for registration as a registered nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. All applicants must have a minimum of 12 months clinical experience as a registered nurse. This course is designed for nurses working with people with cancer and applicants are expected to have some working experience in the care and management of people living with cancer as unit discussions and assessment will require students to draw upon this experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (writing 6.0, no band below 6.0); PTE Academic overall 50. name: Graduate Certificate in Contemporary Mental Health
description: This graduate certificate is designed primarily for registered nurses who wish to develop specialist skills in the care of people with mental health issues. This course aims to develop excellence in contemporary mental health care to meet the professional development needs of graduates interested in specialist mental health practice and evidence-based therapeutic approaches to care. You'll work on formulating safe, caring, respectful, responsive, and therapeutic relationships with people with mental health issues across a range of healthcare contexts. This course is recommended for Registered Nurses wanting to expand their knowledge and skills in the care of patients requiring specialist, or immediate mental health care. It will also be of interest to allied health professionals and nurses working in general areas such as ED, who are in regular contact with patients receiving immediate and ongoing medical and nursing care for mental health conditions. Accreditation It is anticipated that the course will provide many of the criteria required for credentialed mental health nurse status with the Australian College of Mental Health Nurses. Discussions with the college are ongoing, so please contact for further details. 3 Reasons to study Contemporary Mental Health at Murdoch University Study at your own pace with flexible, online learning. Gain evidence-based skills and strategies that are immediately applicable to your work. Take a step towards specialising in mental health practice.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Build essential skills and knowledge to meet your career or study goals. Things you'll cover include: Learning to formulate safe, caring, respectful, responsive, and therapeutic relationships with people with mental health issues across a range of healthcare contexts. Working to evaluate all accessible evidence to establish person-centred, collaborative decisions that contribute towards providing optimum mental healthcare. Creating effective and collaborative interdisciplinary relationships that facilitate the implementation of evidence based mental health care. Adapting to practising in complex mental healthcare environments whilst acting within appropriate professional, ethical, and legal frameworks. I definitely wouldn't have chosen rural work if I didn't have the opportunity to do rural placements. A lot of the other universities don't really offer that as well as Murdoch do. name: Graduate Certificate in Counselling
description: Counsellors help people through difficult times of their lives, often when they are most vulnerable. If you are looking to begin your journey to become a professional counsellor, or need to develop counselling skills for your current role as a teacher, nurse or human services professional, this course will develop your professional competence and personal readiness for a career in counselling. You'll learn through experiential education, enabling you to focus on the quality of counselling relationships as a key feature of effective counselling practice. After graduating from this course you may apply for admission to the Graduate Diploma in Counselling , Graduate Diploma in Creative Arts Therapies or Master of Counselling and will be exempt from the units already completed which are common to both degrees. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Coached practice in small groups Case studies, role plays and guest lecturer Counselling adults Counselling children and adolescents Experiential learning in group counselling The thing I've enjoyed most about Murdoch University is the opportunities to work with teaching staff who have years of experience, allowing me to pick their brains and gain a greater understanding of the practical application in the field. Jake, Allied Health student.
admission_requirements: Completion of a bachelor degree (AQF Level 7) or equivalent in any discipline. Applications based on previous study or professional experience will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

name: Graduate Certificate in Criminology
description: Begin to explore criminal behaviour, crime policy and prevention as you upskill or reskill in the field of criminology. Examine the way society currently look at justice and use theory and methods to examine areas of ongoing and emerging criminological concern. You'll gain a clear understanding of the justice systems, and engage in topics of interest to local, national and global communities. Upon successful completion of this course, you can gain direct entry into the Master of Criminology or the Graduate Diploma in Criminology. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Build essential skills and knowledge to meet your career or study goals. Topics you'll cover include: How to evaluate criminal issues, theories and concepts in a range of contexts. Criminological theories, social science methodologies and research ethics associated with crime and criminal behaviour. Interdisciplinary and intercultural perspectives. I love the freedom to think and have opinions without criticism. The lecturers allow for discussion, understanding that everyone may have a different opinion, and allow for free-flowing conversation. name: Graduate Certificate in One Health
description: If you want to learn how to protect global health security, improve food safety and security or prevent outbreaks of zoonotic disease in animals and people, whilst working to achieve our sustainable development goals then this is the course for you. One Health is an ambitious concept seeking to enhance interdisciplinary collaborations across all aspects of health and ecology. It embraces traditionally separate fields including human medical health disciplines, veterinary medicine, public health and health administration, and the interactions of human and animal populations with the environment. You'll explore how complex health problems such as disease pandemics cannot be prevented or controlled by specialists in one discipline alone, but require contributions from multiple specialists working in collaborative teams. Please be aware that if you study this course as an international student, your studies will be entirely online and you will not be required to attend campus. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

name: Graduate Certificate in Plant Biosecurity
description: More people are moving around the world than ever, and trade between nations and regions always increasing. With this comes increased risk of spreading plant pests and diseases that are damaging to food crops and the natural environment. Plant biosecurity is fundamental to managing the threat posed by plant-affecting organisms, and is of vital importance to world trade, environmental protection, and agriculture. Learn how plant biosecurity measures such as risk analysis, quarantine and surveillance are used to stop the entry and spread of exotic organisms locally and internationally. You'll gain an in-depth knowledge of rapid emergency response to an incursion, and how to manage pest organisms if they become permanently established in a new region and start impacting trade. Biosecurity is a growing field of activity for many professionals involved in agriculture, the environment and international and domestic trade to maintain agricultural and environmental integrity. This course will also appeal to those wishing to pursue careers in food production and postharvest management, in both the private and public sectors. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Build essential skills and knowledge to meet your career or study goals. Topics you'll cover include: Key plant biosecurity pests and diseases New and emerging diagnostics and surveillance technologies Practical community engagement strategies International biosecurity agreements and obligations Studying both Crop and Pasture and Animal Science gave me the opportunity to learn about all sectors of the industry. In my first year, I went on field trips, handled animals and spoke to people directly involved in agriculture. Brittany, Agricultural Science.

name: Graduate Diploma in Asian Language (In-country)
description: For political, economic, environmental and cultural reasons, Japan and Indonesia will play an increasingly important role in contemporary global change. The Australian Government is seeking to make study in Asia a 'rite of passage', to enable Australians to develop a deep and engaged knowledge of the countries and languages of Asia. This qualification is the only course in Australia that offers a full year in-country experience for postgraduate credit. It is designed for students interested in developing an advanced knowledge of an Asian language, through a program of study at universities in Japan or Indonesia. This qualification requires full-time study overseas for two semesters. Immersed in the language every day for a full year, you will develop your Japanese or Indonesian skills to an advanced level. You can also study a variety of subjects such as the literature, media, religion, history, politics, economics, sociology and anthropology of Japan or Indonesia. These areas combined will make you a specialist of Japan or Indonesia with a wealth of knowledge of the region and personal networks in the community. Note - as teaching of this course is conducted at Murdoch's partner universities in Japan and Indonesia, it takes several months to process institutional arrangements. You will therefore need to apply well in advance before your intended commencement of this course. AQF Level 7.
curriculum: Core topics covered in this course include: Build essential skills and knowledge to meet your career or study goals. Topics you'll cover include: Advanced knowledge of the language (Japanese or Indonesian) Understanding the culture and society of Japan or Indonesia, both traditional and contemporary Understanding history, politics, economics and religions in Japan or Indonesia Having completed three semesters and my honours research in Indonesia, I was able to get a much better idea of development on the ground. I found that when I graduated, I had a more realistic idea of what to expect in the workplace. Karis Erceg, Bachelor of Arts.
admission_requirements: AQF Level 7 (Bachelors) degree. All applicants will be required to participate in an interview (conducted in the target language) to assess language proficiency, communicative competence, and readiness for advanced postgraduate study prior to admission.

name: Graduate Diploma in Australian Migration Law and Practice
description: With over 10 years of experience teaching migration law, Murdoch University offers the Graduate Diploma in Australian Migration Law and Practice, recognised by the Office of Migration Agents Registration Authority (OMARA) as satisfying the required entry-level course for registration as a migration agent (registration also requires the Capstone exam and other criteria). You don't need a law degree to get started - just the drive to make a difference. This course is open to all backgrounds, and equally valuable for legal practitioners ready to expand their practice. Led by leading academics and experienced practitioners, this course is practical, hands-on, and designed to prepare you for success in this challenging field. Murdoch had this beautiful culture where you were really able to absorb yourself in so many different opportunities. I certainly took up as many opportunities as I could. Zahra Al Hilaly, Bachelor of Laws / Bachelor of Communication Read full student story

name: Graduate Diploma in Clinical Exercise Physiology
description: If you're passionate about a profession that focuses on keeping people moving and helping to improve quality of life, this postgraduate course will give you the qualification you need to work as an accredited Exercise Physiologist. Develop, implement and manage physical activity and behavioural programs for healthy clients and clients living with a range of chronic conditions, as you explore how exercise can improve health and wellbeing. Learn about the delivery of exercise, lifestyle and behavioural modification programs to help prevent and manage chronic diseases and injury. You'll learn how to provide physical activity and behavioural programs for clients with conditions as diverse as cardiovascular disease, diabetes, osteoporosis, depression, cancer, arthritis, respiratory disease and many others. Plus, you'll learn leadership skills to work independently or collaboratively within healthcare teams. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

For Murdoch graduates completion of B1317 with a double major in Movement Science and Sport and Health Science OR, B1348 OR B1352 meets the requirements for point 2 above.

name: Graduate Diploma in Community Development
description: This course will introduce you to the community development ideas and practices used to create and foster community-led change in settings around Australia and beyond. This course is designed for community work practitioners and graduates with an interest in moving into emerging fields that embrace the ideas and practices of community development, and want to broaden their knowledge through further postgraduate studies. You'll study real and living community projects that build on cultural strength in remote areas, urban agriculture and sustainability projects, grassroots creative arts projects, activism work and much more. Combine case studies, documentaries, films and other creative digital forms that showcase examples of community work and attend workshops designed to teach creative ways of getting the community involved. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

name: Graduate Diploma in Counselling
description: Prepare for a career in counselling by strengthening both your personal and professional skills. You'll learn how to support people during vulnerable times in their lives and develop the relationship-building skills that are key to effective counselling practice. As a student, you'll explore the latest evidence-based counselling practices through immersive, hands-on learning. You'll develop core counselling skills, learn how to conceptualise cases and apply your knowledge in real-world settings, including in the area of mental health and Indigenous, multicultural and other diverse communities. After graduating from this course, you can apply for the Master of Counselling and complete it in one year. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

name: Graduate Diploma in Creative Arts Therapies
description: Artists have been using art to express themselves for centuries - Vincent Van Gogh famously used his art to cope with mental illness throughout his life, and Edvard Munch is widely regarded to have inspired a whole movement of expressionism in art connecting to mood and internal emotional life. Modern science and psychology has helped to uncover the benefits of creative arts in promoting positive mental health outcomes. There is growing evidence about the power the artistic process has to help us connect with emotions and experiences, and by doing so face life's dilemmas. Learn how expression through the arts can be used to enhance the therapeutic process by using a person-centred framework. You'll learn the newly-emerging theory in this area of counselling, combined with hands-on experience that will build your counselling skills. While this course has proven beneficial for counsellors to work with clients to express themselves, if you're a teacher, social worker, chaplain, psychologist, or youth worker, you'll also be able to apply the skills you learn in your current role. Students who complete the Graduate Diploma in Creative Arts Therapies may apply for admission to the Masters of Counselling and will be exempt from the units already completed which are common to both degrees. This course offers valuable benefits for counsellors in helping their clients express themselves.. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

name: Graduate Diploma in Criminology
description: Security surveillance, terrorism, policing, cybercrime and transnational crime are just a few of the areas you'll explore to help you understand the inner workings of criminal behaviour. You'll learn how to evaluate, think critically and apply theories and methods to real-world environments through work placements. Some of our students have previously undertaken internships within federal or state government agencies, including community safety departments or commercial providers including in domestic violence to inmate reintegration. Upon successful completion of this course, you can gain direct entry into the Master of Criminology . This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

Criminological methods, theoretical perspectives, techniques and strategies for real world demands. Interdisciplinary and intercultural perspective. I love the freedom to think and have opinions without criticism. The lecturers allow for discussion, understanding that everyone may have a different opinion, and allow for free-flowing conversation. Ashlyn, Law & Criminology.

name: Graduate Diploma in Design Thinking and Service Innovation
description: Design thinking and service innovation is applied within various sectors to deal with complex business and societal issues, with many corporations crediting the practice with the successful development and innovation of their products, services and business models. In this course, you will employ human-centred and co-design methods to reframe, employ insights and evaluate complex commercial and social service issues for improved consumer or user experiences. You will also apply practical skill sets by developing, prototyping and implementing the outcomes of these creative approaches through a face-to-face real-world client project as part of the course. This approach to learning sees students like Nina level up their career in a world where creative thinking is valuable currency. This course will increase and update the skill set of graduates and current professionals of business, community development, engineering, graphic design, health services, information technology, marketing, strategic communications and sustainable development. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

name: Graduate Diploma in Education (Tertiary and Workplace)
description: A teaching degree gives you the opportunity to help students gain the skills and ways of thinking they'll need to solve problems in the future. It allows you connect to people and inspire and support them to reach their potential. This course could suit you if you're interested in transitioning to education from another discipline or already working in an adult learning context. For example, you might be working or aspiring to work as a lecturer, adult educator, facilitator, professional development facilitator, instructor or professional trainer. You'll explore the concepts, theories and practice of adult education and build on your own areas of interest through your choice of electives, such as mentoring, teaching second/foreign languages and opportunities with e-learning among others. If you have a Bachelor (undergraduate) degree in an area that's not in Education, you could use this course as a pathway into the Masters of Education (coursework). This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

name: Graduate Diploma in Energy and Carbon Studies
description: The Paris Agreement on climate change, growing world populations and limited fossil fuel resources have all created increased demand for renewable energy. How we increase supply, and integrate renewable energy into the current energy supply sector is driving the demand for professionals with climate change skills across the Asia Pacific region and Australia to serve as leaders of the emerging "green" economy. Develop the critical skills needed for the energy and carbon industries, and apply them to the challenges of global environmental and social change. Our industry-focussed units will equip you with skills such as energy auditing, carbon accounting, designing renewable energy systems, preparing energy policy briefs for government and developing corporate carbon management strategies. Successful completion of this course provides a clear pathway to the final year of the Master of Renewable and Sustainable Energy degree. This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.

Rohit Bomma, Master of Renewable and Sustainable Energy Read full student story.

name: Graduate Diploma in Environmental Science
description: Effectively managing human interactions with the environment requires a thorough understanding of the inter-relationships between land, water, air, biota and people. As an environmental professional, you'll need a clear understanding of the procedures and skills involved in investigating complex environmental issues in different settings such as urban, mining, agriculture and aquatic. Upgrade your qualification in Environmental Science, or get the skills and knowledge you need to move into the field if you already work in geology, forestry, agriculture, zoology, botany or planning. You'll gain an in-depth understanding of the science, policies, procedures and techniques of environmental planning and management. When you graduate, you'll have a multidisciplinary understanding of Environmental Science, and be proficient in a range of techniques employed in environmental management. On completion of this course, you may be eligible for entry into our one-year Master of Environmental Science . This course is delivered by Murdoch University in Western Australia.
