description: The Master of Project Management at QUT is a transdisciplinary qualification accredited by the Australian Institute of Project Management and aligned with the Project Management Body of Knowledge. Students engage with industry practitioners and academics who are experts in their field, and the curriculum uses real-life case studies and scenarios. Professionals use it to advance their career, change sectors or improve their employability. Graduates work as project and program managers across construction, engineering, IT, infrastructure, health, events and government.

name: Master of Psychology (Educational and Developmental)
description: QUT's Master of Psychology (Educational and Developmental) is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with supervised placements. It is an accredited postgraduate program preparing psychologists to work with learning, development and wellbeing across childhood, adolescence and adulthood. Graduates work as educational and developmental psychologists, and in counselling, research and education policy.

name: Master of Public Health
description: QUT's Master of Public Health is a 192-credit-point degree, two years full-time or 1.5 years for graduates with a recognised health bachelor degree. It combines eight core units with a 48-credit-point major and a research component, taken as a dissertation or a shorter research project plus electives. Majors are emergency and disaster management, epidemiology and research methods, health promotion, and health, safety and environment, and students can also mix units across majors. Core units and most electives can be studied on campus or online. Graduates work in government health agencies, non-government organisations, community health, workplace health and safety, and research. Indicative international tuition is around A$41,300 per year.

name: Master of Renewable Energy
description: QUT's Master of Renewable Energy is an 18-month degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It covers solar, wind and storage technologies, grid integration and energy systems for the shift away from fossil fuels, and domestic full-time students are offered Commonwealth Supported Places. Graduates work as electrical and energy engineers, energy analysts, consultants and policy officers.

name: Master of Renewable Energy with Data Analytics
description: QUT's Master of Renewable Energy with Data Analytics is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It combines renewable energy engineering with data analytics as the city rebuilds infrastructure for the 2032 Olympic Games, and QUT ranks first in Australia for data mining and analysis. Graduates work as electrical and power engineers, energy analysts and consultants with an analytics focus.

name: Master of Renewable Energy with Project Management
description: QUT's Master of Renewable Energy with Project Management is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It pairs renewable energy engineering, covering solar, wind, storage and grid integration, with project management as Brisbane rebuilds infrastructure ahead of the 2032 Olympic Games. Graduates work as electrical and power engineers, energy analysts and consultants moving into project and delivery roles.

name: Master of Robotics and Artificial Intelligence
description: QUT's Master of Robotics and Artificial Intelligence is an 18-month degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. Students work on perception, control, machine learning and autonomous systems in a school home to robotics researchers Michael Milford and Peter Corke, and domestic full-time students are offered Commonwealth Supported Places. Graduates work as robotics and AI engineers, computer vision engineers and machine learning specialists.

name: Master of Social Work Qualifying
description: QUT's Master of Social Work (Qualifying) is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Health, taught at the Brisbane campuses with two supervised field placements totalling 1,000 hours. It is a graduate-entry qualifying degree for people with a related bachelor's degree, and is accredited by the Australian Association of Social Workers so graduates are eligible for AASW membership. They work in health, child and family services, mental health and community organisations.

name: Master of Sustainable Infrastructure
description: QUT's Master of Sustainable Infrastructure is an 18-month degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It covers the planning, delivery and operation of transport, water and civil infrastructure with a sustainability focus, and domestic full-time students are offered Commonwealth Supported Places. Graduates work as civil and transport engineers, and in logistics, supply chain and infrastructure planning.

name: Master of Sustainable Infrastructure with Data Analytics
description: QUT's Master of Sustainable Infrastructure with Data Analytics is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It combines sustainable infrastructure engineering with data analytics as Brisbane rebuilds its transport and civil networks for the 2032 Olympic Games, drawing on QUT's top-ranked data mining research. Graduates work as civil and transport engineers and infrastructure analysts.

name: Master of Sustainable Infrastructure with Project Management
description: QUT's Master of Sustainable Infrastructure with Project Management is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Engineering, taught at the Brisbane campuses. It pairs sustainable infrastructure engineering, covering transport, water and civil works, with project management as Brisbane prepares its networks for the 2032 Olympic Games. Graduates work as civil and transport engineers and infrastructure project managers.

name: Master of Teaching (Early Childhood)
description: QUT's Master of Teaching (Early Childhood) is a two-year degree in the Faculty of Creative Industries, Education and Social Justice, taught at the Kelvin Grove campus in Brisbane. It is a graduate-entry teaching qualification for the early years, combining coursework in child development and pedagogy with supervised placements in early learning and school settings. Graduates are eligible for teacher registration and work as early childhood teachers.

name: Advanced Diploma of Accounting
description: The Advanced Diploma of Accounting at RMIT University prepares students for a career as a tax agent or for further accounting study. Students apply skills in accounting systems and internal controls, undertake a work placement with an accounting entity, and develop the theoretical and technical skills for specialised work in the accounting and financial services industries. Skills covered include implementing and maintaining accounting systems, internal control and audit, preparing financial statements for corporate reporting entities, business performance reporting, and preparing tax returns and providing tax advice for legal entities. Study options include full-time and part-time blended delivery in Melbourne.
curriculum: Program code C6181 (CRICOS 113126B). Delivered at City Campus, Full Time 1 Years. This industry-facing advanced diploma is designed to advance your career as a specialised accounting professional, tax agent, or assistant accountant. Graduates will meet the educational requirements for registration as a tax agent as prescribed by the Tax Practitioners Board (TPB) under the Tax Agent Services Act (2009). There are other conditions to be met in order to register as a tax agent (including a supervised work experience component) and graduates seeking tax agent registration are urged to check current licensing requirements with the TPB. To become an accredited accountant, you must successfully complete the Bachelor of Accounting .

name: Associate Degree in Applied Science
description: The Associate Degree in Applied Science at RMIT University provides an entry point to the biomedical science and biotechnology industries. This hands-on program involves significant time in laboratory classes, with students working in small practical groups that support interaction with teachers and classmates. The lab is fitted with equipment used in biotechnology and biomedical applications, and graduates qualify for membership of the Australian Society for Microbiology and the Australian Institute of Medical Scientists. Before beginning, students choose a pathway in science, biomedicine or pharmacy. It is taught in Melbourne.

This degree provides broad-based training for a technical career in diagnostics, medical research, veterinary, biological research, biotechnology or chemical and food testing laboratories. We ensure our qualifications meet the current needs of industry through our industry advisory committees. These include the Laboratory Medicine Program Advisory Committee and the Biosciences Program Advisory Committee. Blending aviation theory with practical flying lessons, the program prepares students to undertake the Civil Aviation Safety Authority Commercial Pilot Licence theory and flight tests, and students may also undertake subjects in instrument and instructor ratings. Flight training takes place at RMIT's Point Cook campus.

name: Associate Degree in Business
description: The Associate Degree in Business at RMIT University develops professional skills across all aspects of the modern business environment, with subjects spanning marketing, human resources, accountancy and management. Blending the academic and the practical, students explore how these areas work together to enable effective management of a contemporary business, and graduate able to analyse and solve problems, work collaboratively and understand core business concepts, for immediate employment or as a basis for further study. Students work with partner companies on group projects and gain mentorship from senior industry figures. It is taught in Melbourne.
curriculum: Year 1 In your first year of study, you will undertake 8 core subjects. These span marketing principles, business law, decision-making in a business context, information systems, and integrated perspectives. Year 2 In the second year of this associate degree, you will undertake 7 core subjects, covering topics including logistics and supply chain management, human resources management, entrepreneurship, financial markets, buyer behaviour, and more. You will also choose one elective subject. All subjects in the Associate Degree in Business introduce you to the major streams in the Bachelor of Business.

Assignments are live industry briefs, and students can participate in global design and trade exhibitions. It is taught in Melbourne.

Students gain broad theoretical and technical knowledge of the underlying principles of engineering, learning to analyse and interpret complex problems, communicate with a range of stakeholders, and find effective solutions to industry issues. Five majors are offered: mechanical, aerospace, advanced manufacturing and mechatronics, electrical and electronics, and civil engineering. RMIT is ranked ninth in Australia and in the top 150 globally for engineering and technology in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.

name: Associate Degree in Fashion
description: The Associate Degree in Fashion at RMIT University is a stepping stone into the fashion industry, blending technical expertise with business knowledge. Students learn fundamental techniques such as design concepts, pattern development, construction and garment fitting, and develop business acumen in marketing communication strategies, trend forecasting, buying methodologies and supply chain management. A common first semester helps students choose between a Design and Technology or a Business and Retail option, and the course spotlights the circular economy and sustainability. RMIT is ranked number one in Australia and 19th in the world for art and design in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.
curriculum: Year 1 In your first year of study, you will undertake five of the required core subjects. These core subjects have been confirmed by industry to be key skills and knowledge areas needed across any industry position. You will also undertake the first three subjects of your chosen option— Design and Technology or Business and Retail . Year 2 In second year, you will complete the remaining core and chosen option subjects, plus one subject chosen from university-wide electives or course-specific options. A key focus is your capstone subject, which is a major project delivered in the final semester of the course. You will be given a design and production brief by an industry partner. Students work alongside peers passionate about reading and writing and learn from teachers and mentors who are leading practitioners, gaining a broad base of skills in fiction, creative nonfiction, professional communication, digital content, grammar and editing before specialising, with a focus on building a writing portfolio and engaging with industry and readers. By organising and attending industry forums and investigating a self-directed research topic, you will increase your broader professional knowledge, skills and networks.

You will also get to choose one university elective subject.

name: Bachelor of Accounting Professional Practice
description: The Bachelor of Accounting Professional Practice at RMIT University provides a strong theoretical and technical foundation in accounting and business, preparing students for professional practice and evolving industry demands. The curriculum focuses on core accounting principles and law, developing in-depth discipline knowledge and practical skills alongside professional skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving and communication, and combines technical expertise with real-world application through professional practice. RMIT is ranked ninth in Australia and in the top 100 globally for accounting and finance in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.
curriculum: Year 1 In your first year, you'll complete a series of introductory business foundation subjects to prepare for your specialised accounting studies. You'll take subjects such as Understanding the Business Environment and Integrated Perspective on Business Problems . These will provide a strong foundation in key business concepts and equip you with the insights and skills needed for the rest of your studies. Year 2 In your second year, you'll deepen your knowledge in accounting with subjects in accounting data analytics and validation, company and finance law, cost analysis, and managerial advisory finance. You'll also begin preparing for your professional practice year by undertaking studies that focus on developing essential professional skills. Subjects such as Developing Professionally and Work, Health, Safety, and Wellbeing will help you build the foundation for your one-year professional placement. Year 3 In your third year, you'll complete your one-year professional placement, which can be a long internship, multiple smaller placements, or any other combination available. Year 4 In your final year, you'll focus on specialised accounting and finance subjects, including financial accountability and reporting, strategic accounting and leadership, and taxation. You'll also complete a capstone subject in Strategic Accounting and Leadership , where you'll synthesise all your learnings. Additionally, you'll have the opportunity to choose 2 elective subjects.

name: Bachelor of Architectural Design
description:
Design studio work starts in the very first semester here rather than being held back until students have "earned" it through a year of theory - RMIT runs the studios like a working architecture practice from day one, and they typically make up half of each semester's workload. Groups stay small, and from second semester onward students actually choose which studio project and theme to follow rather than being assigned one, so the degree lets people specialise in interests (housing, urban design, materials experimentation) earlier than most architecture programs allow.

The supporting subjects - technology, communication, history - fill out the rest of the degree and are there specifically to give studio work real technical and historical grounding, not to function as separate academic silos. It's explicitly a pathway degree: this bachelor's alone isn't the endpoint, it feeds into RMIT's Master of Architecture and the accreditation that comes with it, so most students here already know they're in for five-plus years of study total before registration.

The appeal for prospective students is usually the intensity of the studio culture and the small-group, project-based teaching model over the sheer volume of design work produced by third year.
curriculum:
Year 1: Design Studio 1 and 2 (foundations), Architectural Communication, Introduction to Building Technology, History of Architecture
Year 2: Design Studio 3 and 4 (student-selected themes), Structures, Environmental Systems, Architectural Communication (advanced)
Year 3: Design Studio 5 and 6 (student-selected themes), Professional Practice, Digital Design Technology, capstone design project
Pathway continuation into Master of Architecture for professional accreditation

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
RMIT restructured its Bachelor of Business around what it calls an agile, non-traditional model, built to layer more hands-on industry work into a normally quite theoretical degree. Students choose from fourteen majors - Entrepreneurship, Finance, Global Business, Logistics and Supply Chain, Management and Change, Marketing, People and Organisation, Business Information Systems, Economics, Financial Planning and several others - plus an optional minor, or can leave without declaring a major at all if they want maximum flexibility.

That range of majors is genuinely wide for an undergraduate business degree; a lot of universities offer four or five majors and expect students to fit their interests into one of them, whereas here a student interested in blockchain-enabled business or social impact work has an actual named pathway rather than a generic elective. Programs run three years full-time or six part-time, with February, July and October intakes, giving mid-year starters and people restarting study after a break more entry points than the standard once-a-year model.

Industry integration runs through most majors via partnerships with named organisations rather than generic "real-world case studies," and RMIT frames the whole degree around solving actual problems for those partners as part of coursework.
curriculum:
Year 1: Business foundation courses - Accounting Fundamentals, Economic Principles, Marketing Foundations, Business Statistics, Business Communication
Year 2: major courses begin (from 14 available majors - e.g. Finance, Marketing, Business Information Systems, Logistics and Supply Chain), optional minor
Year 3: advanced major courses, industry-partnered capstone project, electives

description: The Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours) at RMIT University develops the theoretical knowledge and technical skills to work as a construction management professional. Students critically evaluate and apply construction management concepts and methodologies, extending their knowledge in building design, building services, construction methods and processes, procurement and supply chains, sustainability, economics and resource management, and build confidence in managing projects from start to finish. RMIT is ranked number one in Australia and in the top 15 globally for architecture and built environment in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026. You will also cover what is required to create sustainable structures. You will be given broader skills in areas such as law, economics and leadership to help you on your way to becoming an industry leader. Year 3 Third year subjects explore commercial construction in greater detail. You'll gain the skills you need to manage complex construction projects. A research methods subject will build the foundation for your research project in fourth year. Year 4 Your final year prepares you to move into industry. All your learnings will come together in a capstone project where you'll have the opportunity to apply your skills and knowledge to a realistic construction simulation. You will also complete a research project, including writing a thesis and producing poster presentations.

name: Bachelor of Criminal Justice
description: The Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice at RMIT University teaches students how crime is defined and measured, how law and human rights intersect, and how factors such as Indigeneity, race, gender, class and disability shape experiences of crime and justice. Learning is practical and connected to the real world, including working with real wrongful conviction cases, completing a 50-day placement, and learning alongside prisoners. Students build skills in research, policy analysis, critical thinking and communication, and can major in criminology, justice systems or legal studies, graduating ready to work across policing, courts, corrections, policy, advocacy, community services or further study.
curriculum: Year 1 Year 2 Year 3 Work integrated learning (WIL) Minors Learning outcomes Year 1 Year 1 In your first year, you build a solid understanding of how crime and justice work from legal, social and psychological perspectives. You'll be introduced to the role of law in society and its links to human rights, ethics and politics, learn the core principles of criminal law through real case examples, and explore how crime is defined, measured and represented in policy, media and public debate. You'll also examine crime through psychology and intersectionality, looking at how factors like Indigeneity, race, gender, class, disability and colonialism shape people's experiences of crime and justice. Throughout, you'll be encouraged to reflect on your own position in the world and start developing the analytical, research and problem‑solving skills you'll draw on across the rest of your degree. Year 2 Year 2 In second year, you will connect what you've learned to real policy, practice and career pathways. You'll take a closer look at how justice policy is made and changed, using real case studies to unpack who has power, whose voices are heard, and how ideas about fairness and equality play out in law and practice. You'll also build your research skills, learning how to design and carry out ethical criminological research using both data and stories, and how research feeds into policy and reform. Alongside this, you'll begin preparing for life after graduation by exploring different justice careers, understanding what employers are looking for, and mapping your own strengths and goals so you can make informed choices about future career direction. description: The RMIT Bachelor of Data Science develops skills in data analytics, statistics, computer science, machine learning, programming, mathematics and data wrangling, positioning students to contribute to business decision-making, corporate strategy and government planning. Students gain strong problem-solving skills and learn to communicate their work to technical and non-technical audiences and to consider relevant standards. Graduates work as data scientists and analysts, machine learning and analytics engineers, and research analysts.

The subjects include, mathematics for computing, artificial intelligence, data science, programming and cyber security. You will also complete two innovative programming bootcamp and studio subjects, which will allow you to develop your programming skills through practical, project-based work. Year 2 After you have completed your first year, the direction you take is in your hands as you choose which majors, minors and subjects you want to undertake. name: Bachelor of Design (Communication Design)
description:
Worth flagging up front: this course is being renamed Bachelor of Graphic Design from Semester 1 2026, so the current program on record reflects the last cohorts under the Communication Design name before the structural refresh. The content itself has always centred on studio learning taught by working designers rather than career academics - RMIT is explicit that all lecturers have design industry backgrounds, which shows up in how briefs get set and critiqued.

Course content spans corporate and brand identity, UX, digital convergence, print and digital publication design, packaging, and what RMIT calls "intercultural design" - working across cultural and linguistic contexts rather than assuming a single default audience. Assessment leans heavily on physical and digital artefacts - actual books, logos, packaging objects - reviewed by both academic staff and industry clients, so the critique culture mirrors what a junior designer would face in a studio job rather than a purely academic marking rubric.

Graduates go into graphic design, branding, advertising and illustration roles across consultancies as well as in-house design teams inside corporate, government and NGO settings.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) (Civil Engineering)
description:
This is a four-year honours degree (eight years part-time) run out of RMIT's Melbourne City campus, and unlike a lot of civil engineering programs that treat sustainability as one unit among many, RMIT built environmental sustainability into the degree's core framing from the start - students are explicitly being trained to plan and manage infrastructure with that lens built in, not bolted on later.

Specialisation choices span civil infrastructure, geotechnical engineering, structures, transport and water resources, selected via electives rather than a hard major declaration, which keeps students' options open until they've actually experienced enough of each area to know what they prefer. Work-integrated learning is a real feature rather than a token requirement: students can take part in the Engineers Without Borders Challenge, sustainable design-and-build projects, industry capstones, and placements both in Australia and overseas, giving genuine variety in how the "real-world experience" requirement gets satisfied.

RMIT also foregrounds communication, teamwork and leadership skills throughout the degree and has an active push on diversity in engineering enrolment, which shows up in how project teams get formed and assessed rather than just in marketing copy.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Engineering Mathematics, Mechanics of Solids, Fluid Mechanics, Surveying and Geospatial Science, Materials Engineering, Engineering Sustainability, Introduction to Structures
Years 3-4: electives toward chosen specialisation (Civil Infrastructure, Geotechnical, Structures, Transport, or Water Resources), Project Management, Professional Practice
Final year: Work Integrated Learning (industry placement, Engineers Without Borders Challenge, or sustainable design-and-build project), Honours capstone thesis/project
admission_requirements: ATAR ~80+ with Units 3/4 Maths Methods recommended

name: Bachelor of Fashion (Design)
description:
The fashion design degree at RMIT runs 13 core courses across three years, moving from conceptual, almost sculptural ideas about fashion in first year through to a fully resolved design project launch in the final semester. First-year units like Introduction to Fashion Design Practice deliberately don't ask students to make wearable, sellable clothes yet - the point is learning to explore and document ideas before technical constraints narrow things down.

By second year the brief tightens: students work with conventional fashion materials and construction methods and start producing genuinely transformative design work, and third year turns into presentation and industry-facing practice, culminating in a project launch that functions like a mini fashion show crossed with a thesis defence. RMIT pairs students with industry and external partners throughout, with sustainability and ethical production treated as a design constraint from day one rather than an add-on elective late in the course - which matters given how much scrutiny the fashion industry gets on exactly that front.

Graduates leave with an actual portfolio of practice and research, and RMIT produces a digital publication each year showcasing graduating cohorts to an international audience of industry scouts and press.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Fashion Design Practice, Fashion Expressions, Fashion Materials Studies, Design Drawing for Fashion
Year 2: Transform Fashion Design Materials, Fashion Communication Design, Pattern Making and Construction, Fashion Industry Contexts
Year 3: Fashion Presentation Design, Fashion Design Project Launch, professional practice and industry collaboration unit, capstone portfolio

Working on real-world problems in industry and community contexts, students complete a year-long honours design research project and choose from four majors. RMIT has offered industrial design for more than 75 years, and is ranked number one in Australia and 19th in the world for art and design in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.
curriculum: Year 1 First year provides foundational exposure to the methods and nature of the designed form, and the socio-cultural factors of design and designing. Common first-year units introduce the field before students specialise, and in third year they can take a programming capstone that simulates an industry software-engineering project under a professional project manager. Work-integrated learning is embedded throughout. Entry is competitive and requires the Victorian Certificate of Education or equivalent with the English and mathematics study-score prerequisites; completing the Associate Degree in Information Technology guarantees entry with four semesters of credit. name: Bachelor of Laboratory Medicine (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Laboratory Medicine (Honours) at RMIT University prepares students to work in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases, working alongside doctors, pathologists and scientists. Students gain fundamental knowledge of human anatomy and physiology, develop communication and professional skills, and are introduced to factors that impact the health of individuals and communities, particularly First Nations peoples. They build skills in molecular diagnostics and the application of biochemical and molecular biology techniques to the study of human diseases including infectious diseases, inherited conditions and cancer, and learn clinical immunology and pathology. It is taught in Melbourne.
curriculum: Year 1 You will undertake subjects designed to provide a strong academic grounding in biological sciences. These will instil fundamental knowledge of human anatomy and physiology, develop your communication and professional skills and introduce you to factors that impact the health of individuals and communities. You will be introduced to the professional field of laboratory medicine via a hospital laboratory visit and basic studies in clinical disciplines. Year 2 You will be introduced to the clinical disciplines of haematology, transfusion and transplantation science, clinical biochemistry, anatomical pathology, immunology and medical microbiology, in preparation for your specialisations. Year 3 You will prepare for professional practice by being introduced to professional skills in laboratory medicine and specialising in 2 clinical discipline streams. In the second half of the year, you will complete a full-time supervised professional practice placement. Organised by RMIT, this is an 80-day placement that provides you with hands-on diagnostic pathology work experience. Year 4 In your final year, you will develop skills in laboratory management, genomics medicine, integrative pathology and undertake subjects that consolidate and provide a holistic interdisciplinary learning experience in preparation for the workforce in diagnostic pathology or medical research or further postgraduate studies.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
RMIT's LLB is three years, which is notably compressed against the more common four-year law degree structure - it front-loads core subjects (contracts, torts, criminal law, constitutional law) into the early semesters and opens up elective room as students progress, with final-year core units covering evidence, and equity and trusts specifically.

It's fully accredited by the Victorian Legal Admissions Board, meaning it satisfies the academic requirement for legal practice admission in Victoria - graduates still need to complete Practical Legal Training afterward, but the degree itself isn't a partial or non-accredited qualification some cheaper alternatives turn out to be. Work-Integrated Learning subjects are built into the structure so students get supervised exposure to actual legal work - community legal centres, clinics, or placements - before they graduate, rather than facing their first real client interaction during PLT.

The three-year length combined with full VLAB accreditation is genuinely the degree's main selling point against competitors: most Victorian law schools require four years to cover the same accredited content.
curriculum:
Year 1: Contract Law, Criminal Law, Torts, Legal Research and Writing, Constitutional Law
Year 2: Property Law, Administrative Law, Corporations Law, electives begin
Year 3: Evidence, Equity and Trusts, Work Integrated Learning placement, capstone electives (e.g. Alternative Dispute Resolution, International Law)
Note: graduates require completion of Practical Legal Training (PLT) for admission to legal practice

name: Bachelor of Medical Radiation (Radiation Therapy)
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Medical Radiation prepares allied health professionals who use radiation for diagnostic examinations, radiation therapy treatment, functional imaging and supportive care. Students enrol directly into one of three specialised streams: diagnostic radiography, radiation therapy, or nuclear medicine, each with different roles and responsibilities, and become highly skilled, patient-centred practitioners. Graduates register and practise as medical radiation practitioners in hospitals, cancer centres and imaging services.
curriculum: Year 1 You'll study a general introduction to the practice and physical principles of clinical nuclear medicine, radiation therapy, and medical imaging. Common subjects include anatomy and physiology, communication and professional practice, and an introduction to physics and the professional streams of medical radiations practice. The second semester subjects focus on anatomy and physiology, imaging anatomy and physics, and you'll undertake your first clinical placement in your enrolled profession. Years 2 and 3 You'll specialise in your chosen discipline (stream), and study c ommon learning modules including imaging anatomy, pathology, psychology, evidence-based practice and research, and advanced medical physics relative to your stream. The third year is designed to explore the complementary nature of the medical radiation disciplines. You'll examine techniques and case studies that highlight the multidisciplinary approach to diagnosis and treatment, and future directions and advancements in technology occurring within the profession. You'll also learn the specialised areas of CT, MRI and ultrasound, and undertake more interdisciplinary learning to further enhance your understanding of the other professions (streams). Year 4 This is delivered during a Flex Semester, with your first 12 weeks of placement beginning in the second week of January and your final 12 weeks of placement concluding in July of the same year. On successful completion of this degree, you are eligible to apply for registration with AHPRA as a medical radiation practitioner, within your division of practice.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
RMIT's nursing degree is almost entirely core subjects - anatomy, physiology, mental health, community health - with just one elective slot across three years, and clinical placement hours dominate the structure: five separate placements (PEP 1 through PEP 5) totalling at least 800 hours, climbing from 120 hours in first year to 200 hours in the final semester of third year. That 800-hour minimum is the AHPRA registration threshold, so it's not a target RMIT chose arbitrarily - it's the floor for graduates to register as Registered Nurses at all.

Placements happen across major metropolitan and rural hospitals as well as community-sector settings, giving students exposure to acute care and mental health contexts specifically, since those are prearranged placement types built into the structure. Before placement, students work through RMIT's simulated learning facilities - high-fidelity mannequins and simulated wards - so the first time a student manages a real deteriorating patient isn't literally the first time they've done it at all.

Clinical supervision comes directly from healthcare agency staff rather than solely university academics, which keeps the assessment grounded in what hospitals actually expect from a new graduate, not just what a lecture theatre covered.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and Physiology, Foundations of Nursing Practice, Health Assessment, PEP 1 clinical placement (120 hours, semester 2)
Year 2: Mental Health Nursing, Community and Primary Health Care, Pharmacology for Nursing, PEP 2 (160 hours) and PEP 3 (160 hours, semester 2)
Year 3: Acute and Complex Care Nursing, Leadership in Nursing Practice, elective, PEP 4 (160 hours) and PEP 5 (200 hours, semester 2)
Total clinical placement requirement: minimum 800 hours for AHPRA registration eligibility
admission_requirements: ATAR ~65+ (or equivalent Year 12), plus health/immunisation and police checks

Through authentic real-world learning, human-centred design, technology and innovation, and work alongside communities and industry partners, students build professional reasoning and practical skills to create evidence-informed solutions across health, disability and education. Through practical classes, simulation and early work-integrated learning, you'll start applying your learning in authentic settings and discover the diverse role of occupational therapists across health, disability, education and community practice. name: Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Honours)
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Honours) teaches students about the human body, the action of drugs, and how the pharmaceutical industry can deliver more reliable, accessible and effective treatments. Alongside pharmacology and physiology, students study the development of new drugs, the clinical use of medications, and the legal and regulatory aspects of the industry. Graduates work in pharmaceutical and biotechnology research and development, drug formulation and analysis, regulatory affairs, and clinical trials.
curriculum: Year 1 In your first year of study, you will study several general science subjects to provide you with a sound scientific base. These will include chemistry and biochemistry, cell biology, and anatomy and physiology. You will also be introduced to the foundations of human health and begin developing skills in communication and professional practice. Year 2 In your second year, you will gain more in-depth education and training in the major discipline areas of physiology and pharmacology, and begin to learn about the process of how drugs are discovered, developed, and regulated. You will select and begin studies in your chosen specialist or cross-disciplinary minor to complement your core studies in pharmaceutical science. Options for minors: Biotechnology - Learn how genetic, cellular and biomolecular processes are harnessed to develop breakthrough technologies to combat disease and promote healthy ageing. Economics - Discover the issues affecting businesses and economies both locally and globally. Year 3 In your final year, your focus will be on how drugs are used to treat diseases along with pharmaceutical industry-related topics, including the design and management of clinical trials, drug regulations and medical information. You will also complete studies in your chosen minor. The degree will culminate in a capstone research project in medical sciences, which will develop and assess your professional skills via both project-based work and activities in a workplace setting (real or simulated).

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) at RMIT University is a selective-entry, research-oriented honours degree for capable and highly motivated students who want hands-on involvement in research projects. It prepares students for the compulsory one-year internship required for Australia-wide registration as a pharmacist, after which graduates are registered to practise in any area of pharmacy in Australia, including community or hospital pharmacy. The degree also provides a foundation for further study and other career opportunities. It is taught in Melbourne.
curriculum: Year 1 In first year, you'll study a selection of science subjects, to give you a sound scientific base. Subjects include biology, chemistry, biochemistry, genetics, microbiology, immunology. You'll also study pharmacy-specific subjects, engaging you in the development of professional skills and an understanding of the social factors that contribute towards health. Year 2 In your second year, you'll start to specialise in the biomedical sciences that contribute towards the pharmacy profession. As well as being introduced to pharmacology, physiology, and the physical characteristics of dosage forms, you'll study pharmacy-specific professional practice subjects and engage in your first work-integrated learning (WIL) experience in second semester. Year 3 In third year, you'll complete in-depth study of therapeutics, supported by more detailed pharmacology, and expand your knowledge and skills in pharmacy practice, with increased emphasis on work-integrated learning activities. You'll study advanced formulations, learn how to compound medicines for individual patients, and how the quality of medicines is regulated and assured. Year 4 In your fourth year, you will expand your pharmacy practice and therapeutics proficiency through integrated study and engage in further work-integrated learning (WIL) activities. You'll learn about recent developments in medicines, and complete a subject preparing you for a research project in your final semester of study.

name: Bachelor of Project Management (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Project Management (Honours) at RMIT University builds the skills to initiate, plan and execute complex projects across a range of industries. The degree provides theoretical knowledge and practical know-how to take projects from inception to completion, with tools to manage projects across a range of scales and complexities. Students can take a minor to enhance employability in a specific project management field, and the course is fully accredited. RMIT is ranked number one in Australia and in the top 15 globally for architecture and built environment in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026, and connects students to more than 250 industry partners.
curriculum: Year 1 In your first year of study, you will be introduced to project management in the construction and property industries, providing the context for the following three years. You will learn essential project management skills and gain an understanding of the different types of buildings and assets, how they are created, and how they are acquired. Year 2 In the second year, you will study project management processes and techniques in greater depth, learning how to plan, cost and schedule projects. Building broader skills in areas like law, economics and leadership will prepare you to become an industry leader. You will be able to choose a minor in this year, giving you the opportunity to specialise in a project management field. Year 3 The third year broadens your focus and looks at project management in other industries, building core knowledge and skills. You will gain a deeper understanding of how to manage complex projects, and undertake a research methods course which will build the foundation for your research project in year 4. Year 4 The theme of your final year is 'moving to practice', preparing you to be industry-ready. You will gain advanced skills and insights into the latest industry trends. A feature of your fourth year is a capstone project, where the skills and knowledge developed in the degree are applied to a project for social benefit. You will also conduct a research project, including writing a thesis and creating a poster to present your research to industry representatives.

The reputable, fully industry-accredited degree focuses on current technical skills while developing critical thinking, professional writing, research and analytical abilities. Students gain the ability to understand the factors around property ownership, management, investment, valuation and development, learning to understand property markets, analyse data, build value, manage assets and create property developments. It is taught in Melbourne.
curriculum: Year 1 Be introduced to the property industry, forming the framework for the next four years. You will also be taught an introduction to construction and project management to aid in your work and studies. Year 2 You will study the property industry in greater detail, with the introduction of property development and investment, along with principles of valuation. You will also gain broader skills in areas of applied law, property economics and leadership that will help you become an industry leader. Year 3 You will build on the material of the second year, and look in-depth at valuation procedures, asset management and the property investment markets. You will gain knowledge and skills relating to analysing the features and performance of individual properties and the associated marketplace, and undertake a research methods subject that will build the foundation for your research project in the fourth year. Year 4 The final year prepares you to be industry-ready and gives you an insight into the industry environment and its latest trends. The year culminates with the following three major projects: an industry-focused property research thesis an investment project an in-depth property development.

name: Bachelor of Psychology
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Psychology is the study of the science of human behaviour and the mental states that drive it. Alongside the principles of personality, psychopathology and psychotherapy, students explore social, developmental, biological and cognitive psychology and research methods. Completing the accredited sequence is the first stage toward registration as a psychologist. Graduates also work in research, human resources, health and community services, and policy.
curriculum: Year 1 In first year, you will study these foundation areas: biological bases of behaviour including brain behaviour relationships, sensation, perception and consciousness theories of learning, memory and cognition (including theories of intelligence) theories of emotion, motivation and stress. You will also study these principles of psychology: personality psychopathology social psychology. Year 2 You will study biological psychology, cognitive psychology, developmental psychology, research methods in psychology, social psychology and forensic psychology. Year 3 In your final year, you will study philosophy and methodology of psychology, psychological assessment and individual differences, professional practices and cross- cultural psychology, psychopathology and models of intervention, motivational and organisational psychology and psychology of gender. You will also have the choice of a psychology placement or working on a psychology research project.

description: The RMIT Bachelor of Social Science is a community-oriented, person-centred and hands-on degree exploring how society shapes people's lives and how students can be part of creating change. Students choose a specialisation in mental health and wellbeing, youth work or psychology, studying communication and practice skills with individuals, groups and families, ethics, mental health, youth work and First Nations perspectives. Graduates work in community services, youth work, mental health support, and social research and policy.

You'll explore how society works and how policies shape people's lives, so you can better understand the world your service users live in. You'll also take your first counselling courses, where you'll start to connect theory with real-world practice. Across these subjects, you'll begin developing the practical skills and confidence you need to start working with people in a thoughtful, safe and supportive way. You'll learn how to communicate with people from different backgrounds, think critically and act ethically in your work with young people. You'll also explore how society and policy shape young people's lives, so you can understand the bigger picture they're navigating. Alongside this, you'll take your first practice skills course, where you'll be introduced to the core ways youth workers support and work with young people in real-world settings. You can choose from areas such as counselling, mental health and wellbeing, youth work, inclusive education, or art and social sciences. name: Bachelor of Software Engineering
description: The Bachelor of Software Engineering at RMIT University equips students with a solid foundation in computer science and mathematics and deep expertise in software architecture, processes, methodologies and quality frameworks. The four-year degree comprises two years of study, a one-year industry placement, then a final year of study, with the placement providing an opportunity to develop professional and technical skills and build a professional network. Students work within complex software development environments covering operating systems, communications, web software, databases and applications, focusing on the software development life cycle. It is taught in Melbourne.
curriculum: Year 1 In the first year, you will have the opportunity to put theory into practice through our embedded programming bootcamps and studios. This will allow you to develop your programming skills, design and implement small-scale software systems and apply software development practices and standards through project-based work. Years 2 and 3 In your second year, you will dive deeper into software engineering disciplines covering process, software architecture and modern tools. You will learn to design and implement large-scale software systems, applying current software development methods and modern technologies required to work as a software engineer. Year 3 The third-year industry placement provides valuable practical experience. This experience is then integrated with your studies and completed through coursework. Year 4 In your fourth year, you will undertake a capstone project that simulates an industry environment. Here, you will apply your skills in large-scale software application development. Many students tackle real-world problems for their projects with close involvement and supervision by an industry mentor. Additionally, you will choose a minor, or just focus on the individual subjects and electives that interest you most. There are nine software engineering minors to choose from, providing you with the flexibility to plan your own study to achieve your study and career goals. Minor options include: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Blockchain Technologies Cloud Computing Creative Computing Cyber Assurance Data Science Enterprise Systems Development Bioinformatics Data Analysis

name: Bachelor of Space Science
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Space Science develops critical skills in space science and technology, connecting the upstream (build and launch) and downstream (application of space-related products and services) industries. Described as unlike any other degree in Australia, RMIT leads in space science and engineering research and provides a unique mix of physics, geospatial science, mathematics, statistics and specialised space studies. Graduates work in the space and satellite industry, Earth observation and geospatial services, research, and defence.
curriculum: Year 1 In your first year, you will study fundamental science concepts across our common first year and begin your space science foundations. You will gain knowledge of calculus, physics, space exploration, and physical sciences. Year 2 In your second year, you will enhance your understanding of mechanics, data preprocessing, rocket science, satellites and space debris, remote sensing, digital signal processing, programming and geodesy. You can also study some of RMIT's Future Technology Skills subjects. Options include: Foundations of AI for STEM STEM for Sustainable Development Innovation Ecosystem and Future of Work Cyber-Physical-Biological Systems Year 3 In your final year, you will complete a space science capstone project of your choosing. Working under the guidance of a professional scientist, you will have the opportunity to learn, apply and demonstrate professional science practice. You will study microgravity science, classical and quantum mechanics, electromagnetism, satellite remote sensing, data analysis, and astrophysics and cosmology. You will also be able to choose a cross disciplinary minor in geospatial science or mathematics for space science, or explore other topics of interest across STEM.

name: Bachelor of Surveying (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Surveying (Honours) at RMIT University prepares students for an in-demand career as a surveyor, with expertise in the measurement, processing, interpretation and presentation of information about the size, shape, nature and location of features of the physical environment. It is the only four-year surveying degree in Victoria, and more than 90 percent of graduates are employed within three months. The hands-on degree provides a strong link between theory and practice across surveying specialisations including engineering and topographic surveying, with an extensive range of industry-based practical learning experiences. It is taught in Melbourne.
curriculum: Year 1 In your first year, you will study the fundamentals of surveying, gaining skills in measurement science, cartography, geographic information systems (GIS) and spatial thinking. Other required skills in mathematics, statistics, and physics are also covered. Years 2 and 3 In your second and third years, you will study more specialised subjects in geodesy, map projections, spatial analysis, remote sensing, image analysis, and professional practice. Specialised studies in cadastral and engineering surveying, GPS, and advanced adjustment methods are central components of the degree. Minor options include: Civil Engineering Environmental Geospatial Science Planning and Urban Design Space Science. You will also participate in a field camp to reinforce theoretical learning and allow you to exercise your knowledge of real-world problems. Year 4 In your final year, you will carry out a capstone research project that is industry approved and reflects current best practice.

name: Bachelor of Sustainability and Environment
description: The RMIT Bachelor of Sustainability and Environment explores biodiversity, climate action and sustainable policy to help drive solutions to urgent environmental and social challenges. Students develop a deep understanding of climate change, environmental management, Indigenous perspectives, place-based analysis, and pathways to social and ecological justice, with an emphasis on the social elements of environmental issues and skills in communication and critical thinking. Graduates work in sustainability, environmental policy and management, community engagement and advocacy roles.
curriculum: Year 1 Year 2 Year 3 Work integrated learning (WIL) Learning outcomes Year 1 Year 1 In your first year, you build a big-picture understanding of how people and the planet are interconnected, and what that means for climate change, biodiversity and justice. You explore how Earth's systems work, how human activity drives environmental change, and how different cultures, histories and power structures shape the way we think and talk about "the environment". You develop core skills in social research, mapping and systems thinking so you can critically analyse land use, resource management and environmental decisions. You also examine how sustainability plays out in everyday life, communities, workplaces and cities, and you study real responses to climate change from local to global scales. Throughout, you engage with First Peoples' knowledge and responsibilities to Country and consider what it means to live and work respectfully on unceded land, preparing you to think and act thoughtfully in the face of complex environmental challenges. Year 2 Year 2 In your second year, you move from understanding environmental challenges to working out how to change systems in practice. You explore how policies are made, implemented and evaluated across different levels of government, and how these processes shape environmental decisions on the ground. You examine how organisations in government and business manage their environmental impacts, using practical tools such as management systems, auditing, reporting and impact assessment. You apply your research and analysis skills to real-world policy problems for external partners, building experience in teamwork and professional practice. name: Bachelor of Urban and Regional Planning (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Urban and Regional Planning (Honours) at RMIT University was the first degree of its kind in Victoria and is designed to enable students to understand, analyse, manage and shape the strategies that inform the future of cities for improved liveability, climate resilience and equitable, sustainable places. Through core subjects, integrated minors, a work placement and a capstone experience, students focus on sustainability and its place in urban planning policy, preparing for a career as a policy and planning leader. RMIT is ranked number one in Australia and in the top 15 globally for architecture and built environment in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026.
curriculum: Year 1 Year 2 Year 3 Year 4 Learning outcomes Year 1 Year 1 By studying Australian society, politics and economics, you will better understand the foundations of urban and regional planning. You will also cover the origins and development of planning principles and practices. Year 2 Year 2 You will focus on contemporary planning policies, as well as social science research methods, social planning, urban design and transport planning. Many students opt to study overseas for a semester in second year. Year 3 Year 3 You will specialise in different areas of practice: planning law, regional planning, climate change adaptation, urban economics, natural resource management, and planning at local government level. Year 4 Year 4 In your final year you will undertake a work placement, in addition to studying planning theory, planning research methods and structure planning. You will finish by writing an individual thesis or a major professional report on a chosen topic. name: Diploma of Conservation and Ecosystem Management
description: The Diploma of Conservation and Ecosystem Management at RMIT University introduces the skills used by land managers, park rangers, site assessors, water quality assessors and conservation staff. Students learn to survey animals and plants, monitor waterways, assess and restore natural sites, and undertake cultural studies relating to land management, with field trips around Melbourne and overnight excursions to locations such as Heywood and Barmah Forest. Students learn about cultural heritage and Indigenous land management with direct input from Aboriginal Elders and community organisations, and the course is developed with industry stakeholders including Melbourne Water and Parks Victoria.
curriculum: Year 1 You will study plant identification and ecology, and learn skills related to site assessment and industry-specific communication. You will be introduced to cultural heritage and aspects of Indigenous land management with input from Aboriginal Elders and community organisations. You'll also learn how to conduct wildlife surveys and interpret the data using the appropriate format. Year 2 You'll study revegetation and the management of water, and learn about pest management. You will also explore Indigenous and cultural heritage issues and how these relate to land management. These are taught in collaboration with Indigenous Elders and community members, and include an extended field trip to western Victoria, where you will have the opportunity to work alongside Indigenous land care workers.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
RMIT's MBA runs across three study periods a year rather than the usual two semesters - full-time students take four courses per period and can finish in 1.5 years, which is fast for an MBA with this level of accreditation. The full program is 16 courses (192 credit points), but anyone who already holds a business-related bachelor's completed within the last decade only needs 12 - a meaningful discount for people who did a business or commerce undergrad and are coming back for the MBA credential rather than a career pivot.

The genuinely distinctive feature is the international study tour option: intensive units delivered in Vietnam or France that count as a 12-credit-point elective, combining an actual overseas trip with coursework rather than treating international exposure as a marketing photo. Electives can otherwise be pulled from other RMIT postgraduate programs, so students can lean the degree toward tech, health, or design management depending on where they're headed.

Teaching mixes lectures, studio-style workshops, and syndicate (small-group) work, reflecting an emphasis on group project delivery that mirrors how most MBA-holders actually operate once employed - in cross-functional teams, not solo.

Advanced-standing entrants (recent business bachelor's): 12-course pathway skipping select foundation courses

name: Master of Data Science
description:
RMIT's data science master's spends its first year deliberately narrow - solid computer science and statistics foundations - before opening into advanced electives and an industry or research project in year two. That sequencing is a response to a common complaint about data science master's programs elsewhere: students arriving from non-CS backgrounds (commerce, biology, social science) who get thrown into advanced machine learning units without the linear algebra or programming grounding to keep up. RMIT's structure front-loads that grounding instead.

The 192-credit-point, two-year full-time program includes a Graduate Diploma exit point at 96 credit points for students who need to leave partway through with something to show for it - a genuine safety net rather than a marketing line, since a lot of comparable programs offer no formal mid-point qualification at all. Case studies threaded through the coursework bring in practising data scientists to walk through legal, ethical and policy questions - algorithmic bias, data privacy law - alongside the purely technical content, which matters given how much scrutiny data science work now attracts.

Delivery mixes lectures, tutorials, and heavy practical lab time, with the year-two project functioning as the main portfolio piece graduates take into job interviews.

Year 1: Programming for Data Science, Statistics for Data Science, Database Systems, Data Preprocessing and Wrangling, Introduction to Machine Learning, Data Visualisation
Graduate Diploma exit point available at 96 credit points
Year 2: Advanced Machine Learning, Big Data Processing, electives (e.g. Natural Language Processing, Deep Learning), Data Ethics and Policy, capstone industry or research project

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
RMIT's Master of IT gives students seven specialisations to choose from - big data analytics, cloud infrastructure, AI in systems and applications, mobile and IoT computing, security and blockchain, software systems architecture, and web systems and search technology - which is an unusually wide spread for a two-year master's. Most competitor programs pick two or three tracks and call it done; RMIT built this one with industry partners specifically so students could chase whichever corner of tech was actually hiring that year.

Teaching mixes pre-recorded short lectures with lectorials, hands-on lab classes and project work, which suits the many students juggling part-time work in Melbourne's CBD-adjacent tech scene - RMIT's city campus location isn't incidental to that. The 192-credit-point load (full load for someone without recent related study) runs across roughly two years, with a research or industry project toward the end that's meant to function as a portfolio piece for job applications, not just an assessment box to tick.

Because the specialisations map fairly directly onto ANZSCO-recognised IT occupations, it's a common choice for students building toward a skills assessment for Australian permanent residency, alongside those simply wanting a technical master's from a university with a strong industry reputation in tech.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals, Data Structures and Algorithms, Database Concepts, IT Research Methods, Software Engineering Fundamentals, Networking
Year 2: chosen specialisation core courses (e.g. Big Data Analytics, Cloud Computing Architecture, Applied Machine Learning, IoT Systems, Cyber Security Fundamentals, depending on stream) plus electives
Final semester: Capstone Project or Industry-Based Learning placement
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline, AU or equivalent overseas) with GPA 2.0/4.0, or 5+ years relevant IT work experience (programming, software engineering, systems/business analysis, ICT management, etc.) in lieu of a degree.

curriculum: Year 1 During the first year, you will undertake two industry-partnered interior design studios and two core subjects that will operate as a direct support to the partnered design studio project, providing opportunities to refine specific skills and design techniques. These include communication (written, verbal and visual), technologies (manufacturing, materials, and experiential) as they are relevant to the project, and provide a base for further extension. You will also choose from a suite of elective subjects from allied areas of business, communication, social science, environment and technology. Year 2 In the second year, you will continue to develop your design capabilities through the completion of two further industry-partnered interior design studios, as well as core subjects, and further electives. In your final semester, the design studio will be complimented by a portfolio-based subject that will support you in identifying, evaluating and communicating key areas of interest, skills and expertise which will together form a profile of your practice, enabling you to position yourself within the design profession. name: Advanced Diploma of Accounting
description:
This qualification (FNS60222) sits above the standard Diploma of Accounting as the next rung for people already working in accounting or bookkeeping roles who want to move into more senior positions without doing a full university degree. There's no work placement requirement built in, which reflects that most students taking this at South Metro TAFE are already employed in the industry and studying around their job rather than starting from zero.

Delivery leans heavily online with mandatory on-campus attendance for assessments, and the college is upfront that students should budget 10-15 hours a week of study outside class time: assignment prep, private study and research on top of scheduled contact hours. That's a meaningful time commitment for people who are often studying part-time while working full-time, which is the more common profile for this level of qualification than a straight-from-school student.

The practical payoff is Tax Practitioners Board recognition: complete the prescribed taxation units and pass them, and graduates become eligible to pursue registration as a Registered Tax Agent, a credential that opens up self-employed tax practice or more senior roles in accounting firms handling client tax affairs.
curriculum:
Core units: complex corporate reporting requirements, financial reports for corporate entities, management accounting systems, budgets and forecasts, tax documentation for legal entities
Elective units: audit and assurance practice, financial risk management, specialised tax practices (prescribed units required for Tax Practitioners Board pathway)
Delivery: predominantly online with mandatory on-campus attendance for scheduled assessments
No mandatory work placement; approximately 10-15 hours per week of self-directed study expected outside class
Pathway: eligible graduates (with prescribed taxation units) can pursue Registered Tax Agent recognition through the Tax Practitioners Board
admission_requirements: Diploma of Accounting or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

It shares the same no-mandatory-placement structure as the Advanced Diploma: the assumption is that competency is demonstrated through simulated business scenarios and assessment tasks rather than a supervised workplace stint.

Like its advanced counterpart, delivery is mostly online with scheduled on-campus attendance for assessments, and the college flags 10-15 hours a week of expected self-directed study on top of scheduled contact. Accounting coursework tends to be assignment-heavy and cumulative, so falling behind on one unit's calculations makes the next unit noticeably harder.

Graduates commonly move into bookkeeping, accounts assistant or accounts payable/receivable roles, and the diploma functions as a credit-bearing pathway into further study, either the Advanced Diploma for those wanting Tax Agent registration eligibility, or articulation into a related university accounting degree for students who decide partway through that they want the fuller qualification.

description:
The Diploma of Business at South Metro TAFE is the deliberately broad option in the college's business suite. Where the Diploma of Accounting and Diploma of Hospitality Management lock students into a named discipline from the start, this qualification builds general business administration, project coordination and leadership competencies that apply across office environments regardless of sector.

That breadth is the point rather than a shortcoming: students who aren't sure yet whether they want to specialise into accounting, marketing, HR or operations get a year to build transferable skills and figure out direction, and the qualification is commonly used as a stepping stone into supervisory or team-leader roles in whatever industry a student happens to already be working in, rather than requiring a career change to make use of it.

As with the other business-suite diplomas at the college, there's no mandatory industry placement; assessment relies on workplace simulations and, where students are already employed, real workplace projects and evidence drawn from their existing job.

Diploma of Community Services
description:
Entry into South Metropolitan TAFE's Diploma of Community Services (CHC52021) generally expects a Certificate IV in Community Services already completed, or equivalent industry experience: it's pitched at people who've already had some exposure to the sector rather than a first qualification for someone entirely new to community work. The approximately 240 hours of mandatory work placement is arranged by the college itself rather than left to students to source, and comes with its own logbook system that both the student and the host workplace need to complete.

Because placements put students into direct contact with vulnerable community members, the compliance requirements are more involved than for most other diplomas at this level: a Working With Children Check and National Police Clearance are required before placement starts, and students must be 18 or over to go on placement at all, an industry-wide requirement rather than something specific to this college.

Graduates typically move into case work, community support, disability services or youth work roles, and the diploma level is often the practical ceiling for direct-service roles before further specialisation (such as a related degree) becomes necessary for case management or supervisory positions.
curriculum:
Prerequisite: Certificate IV in Community Services (or equivalent industry experience)
Core units: case management, community services context and practice, client advocacy, work within a legal and ethical framework, trauma-informed practice
Elective units: selected in consultation with industry (options may include disability support, youth work, family and domestic violence response)
Mandatory work placement: approximately 240 hours, arranged/negotiated by South Metropolitan TAFE, documented via vocational placement logbook
Compliance requirements: Working With Children Check and National Police Clearance required before placement; students must be 18+
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 5.5 (no band below 5.0)

name: Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care
description:
This diploma only opens up once a student already holds the Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care. It's a deliberate two-stage pathway rather than a standalone entry qualification, which means every student arrives with at least some paid or supervised experience already in a childcare setting. The diploma itself runs across two stages, each carrying 360 hours of mandatory work placement, for a combined 720 hours of supervised field experience across the qualification, a substantial practical component relative to the classroom time.

South Metro TAFE structures the course to work around people already employed in the sector: full-time study runs at roughly two days a week (or one evening at the Rockingham campus for students working in a regulated childcare service), and those students can count their paid work hours toward the placement requirement rather than needing to find separate unpaid placement time on top of a job.

Graduates typically move into lead educator or room leader roles in long day care, and the diploma is also the recognised qualification level for meeting the "diploma-qualified educator" ratio requirements under the National Quality Framework, which is what makes it valuable to centres beyond just the individual's own skill development.
curriculum:
Prerequisite: Certificate III in Early Childhood Education and Care (CHC30121 or equivalent)
Stage 1: children's health, safety and wellbeing, curriculum planning for early learning, working with families and communities, 360 hours supervised work placement
Stage 2: leadership and program development, inclusive practice for children with additional needs, legal and ethical frameworks in ECEC, further 360 hours supervised work placement
Total placement: 720 hours across the diploma (working students may count paid hours in a regulated service)
Study load: approximately 2 days per week full-time (or evening delivery at Rockingham for employed students)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 5.5)

name: Diploma of Electronics and Communications Engineering
Diploma of Engineering - Technical

This diploma (MEM50222) sits in the engineering trades pathway rather than the professional engineering pathway: it's the technical-officer-level qualification that follows on from trade or apprenticeship training, not a route toward becoming a registered engineer, which is an important distinction for students weighing this against a university engineering degree. Full-time study runs at roughly three to four days a week.

South Metro TAFE also runs this as a traineeship option, meaning eligible students can be employed under a formal training contract with an engineering or manufacturing employer and earn a wage while working through the qualification. That's a genuinely different funding and career model from full-time classroom study, and one that suits people already in the trades workforce wanting to move up without stopping work entirely.

The qualification targets specific technical roles rather than a generic "engineering" outcome: the college names CAD operator, hydraulic fitter, mechanical technician and robotics technician as typical destinations, which gives a fairly concrete sense of the mechanical/automation trades employers actually hire this diploma's graduates into.

That's a genuinely different practical experience from hospitality courses that rely purely on mock service exercises.

There's no external work placement requirement, which is a little unusual for a hospitality qualification: the college's position is that the Bentley Pines operation already delivers the equivalent supervised, real-world management experience without students needing to source an outside venue and juggle two sets of rostering and assessment expectations.

Career outcomes the college points to include function manager, restaurant manager and front office manager roles, all management-track positions rather than entry-level service jobs, reflecting that this is the "management" diploma rather than the operational Certificate III/IV level that precedes it in the hospitality qualification ladder.
