description: A one-year honours year following the Bachelor of Business, Government and Policy or a related degree at the University of Canberra. It adds advanced coursework in research methods and a supervised thesis on a business, government, politics or public policy question. Entry requires a completed bachelor's degree with a strong grade average in the relevant discipline and a supervisor for the topic. The honours result is classified, and a first or upper second class is the usual requirement for a PhD and for competitive graduate and policy roles. It suits graduates heading toward research, policy analysis or the senior public service who want to demonstrate independent research ability.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Commerce (Business Economics)
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point commerce degree with a specialist major in business economics, combining core commerce units, the economics major and open electives. The major covers microeconomics, macroeconomics and econometrics, with an emphasis on working through ambiguous or incomplete information and communicating findings to non-specialists. A capstone project pulls the degree together, and authentic work integrated learning runs through internships, industry projects and case studies.

Graduates work as economists, economic and business analysts, forecasters and policy advisers across government, consulting and the private sector, which is a natural fit in Canberra given the concentration of federal departments and agencies. Delivery is flexible, with online and blended options and completion timeframes from three years part-time upward. It suits students who want quantitative economic training inside a broader business degree rather than a pure economics program.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Communication and Media
description:
A three-year degree (72 credit points) with a choice of six majors: journalism, sports media, media production, public relations and strategic communication, social media and content creation, or marketing communication, with a double-major option.

Up to 200 hours of professional experience is built in, including at least 100 hours of approved internship placement, with partners such as the ABC, Seven West Media, the Brumbies and the Australian Public Service. Students work with real facilities: the UCFM radio station, television studios and editing suites, and The Owl publishing platform. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 with no assumed knowledge. It suits students who want to build a portfolio and try several media disciplines before committing to one.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Creative Industries
description: A three-year creative arts degree delivered with TAFE Queensland at the Brisbane South Bank campus, so students take University of Canberra units alongside TAFE Queensland studio training. It is offered as a set of named specialisations rather than one generalist degree: Visual Arts, Contemporary Music Practice, Applied Fashion, Acting and Performance, and Drama and Performance. Each combines hands-on practice, industry-standard facilities and portfolio or repertoire development with the theory and professional context of the creative industries. Graduates work as practising artists, musicians, designers, actors and performers, and in adjacent production, teaching and arts-organisation roles, usually as portfolio careers. It suits students who want conservatoire-style or studio-based creative training and are based in or willing to study in Brisbane.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Design
description:
A three-year studio-based degree with five majors: interaction design, industrial design, visual communication design, game development, or a multidisciplinary design pathway. Learning is built around collaborative studio projects, with industry briefs from partners such as Breville, the National Film and Sound Archive and the National Gallery of Australia.

Work-integrated learning runs through all three years via internships, live briefs, field trips and international study tours, and students graduate with a reviewed portfolio. Entry is a selection rank of about 60, or a portfolio submission with no ATAR required. It suits people who want to solve problems through design across digital products, physical products, branding or games.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Digital Design (Digital Media)
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point digital media degree delivered jointly with TAFE Queensland at the South Bank campus in Brisbane, so students take University of Canberra units alongside TAFE Queensland electives and studio classes. Core study covers 3D media art production, animation, sound design, digital photography, interactive fiction and emerging virtual and augmented reality tools, together with professional practice and a work integrated learning placement.

Entry is by selection rank, with a portfolio pathway available, and strong students can progress to an honours year. Graduates work as digital media and motion designers, animators, videographers and VR or AR content specialists across games, screen, advertising and immersive media. It suits students who want a hands-on, technology-heavy creative production degree and are based in or willing to study in Brisbane rather than Canberra.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood and Primary Education
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Early Childhood and Primary Education is a four-year degree (96 credit points) that qualifies graduates to teach across the whole birth-to-year-6 span, from preschools and early learning centres to primary schools, which is a broader qualification than a primary-only or early-childhood-only degree.

Students complete at least 132.5 days of placement across early childhood and primary settings, pass both parts of the LANTITE test and a Teaching Performance Assessment, and the program is approved by ACECQA for early childhood and registered with the ACT Teacher Quality Institute for primary. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 plus a suitability statement and, for teacher registration, IELTS 7.5 with 8.0 in speaking and listening. It suits people set on early-years and primary teaching who want both credentials.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.5 with 8.0 in speaking and listening and no band below 7.0 (or equivalent), reflecting the teacher-registration English requirement.

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (Birth to Five)
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point initial teacher education degree that qualifies graduates to teach children from birth to five years, accredited by the Australian Children's Education and Care Quality Authority. Holders of an ACECQA-approved diploma can complete it in two years. Delivery is blended, on-campus or online, at the Bruce campus in Canberra and the Sydney Hills campus in New South Wales.

Study covers child development, early literacy, STEM, play-based learning, behaviour guidance, Indigenous pedagogies and leadership, with a minimum of 95 days of supervised placement across a range of early childhood settings. Working with Vulnerable People registration is required before placement. Graduates work as early childhood teachers and centre directors, and move into education leadership, curriculum and policy roles. It suits students committed specifically to the early years rather than primary or secondary teaching.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description: The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) is a four-year degree with honours built in, offered in two specialisations: Intelligent Robotics, covering control and dynamics of machines, industrial robotics and algorithms, and Network Engineering, covering the design and operation of software-based networked systems. It is accredited by Engineers Australia at professional engineer level and by the Australian Computer Society at professional level, and includes 450 hours of work-integrated learning through placements, site visits, fieldwork and the Engineers Without Borders Challenge. Entry is a minimum ATAR of 65 with Year 12 Mathematical Methods and IELTS 6.5. Graduates work as robotics engineers, network architects, cybersecurity engineers, data scientists and software engineers. It suits students who want an accredited engineering degree focused on robotics and networked systems rather than the traditional civil or mechanical streams.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Bachelor of Engineering in Network and Software Engineering (Honours)
Bachelor of Engineering Technology
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point degree that pairs a broad information and communication technology core with an engineering technology specialisation and open electives. Core units cover database design, systems analysis, software technology and professional IT practice, while the specialisation adds cloud computing, cybersecurity, mobile technologies and digital signal processing.

One point to be clear on: this degree is not accredited by the Australian Computer Society, and students who need ACS-accredited qualifications should look at UC's other IT degrees. Admission is generally through transfer from approved articulation partners rather than direct school-leaver entry. Graduates work in networking, system administration, software development and technical support roles that value applied ICT skills alongside communication and business awareness. It suits students articulating from a diploma who want a bachelor-level ICT qualification with an engineering-technology slant.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Event and Tourism Management
Bachelor of Exercise Physiology and Rehabilitation
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Exercise Physiology and Rehabilitation is a four-year degree accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia, so graduates are eligible to apply for accreditation as an exercise physiologist and, along the way, as an exercise scientist. Students complete at least 500 hours of placement across hospitals, clinical health services, sporting organisations, private practice and community health.

The program frames exercise as medicine, working with people across the lifespan on injury recovery, chronic disease, aged care and rehabilitation, with an emphasis on clinical reasoning and person-centred care. Entry is a selection rank of about 70 with assumed knowledge in biology and mathematical methods, and IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0. It suits students who want a clinical allied-health career rather than a fitness or coaching one.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 75-80 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to clinical placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Film Production
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Film Production is a three-year production-focused degree that takes students through the full pipeline from concept to delivery, with specialisation possible in directing, cinematography, editing, sound design or producing, and dedicated units in screenwriting, documentary and creative producing.

Students use film cameras, lighting, green screen, and industry-standard editing and colour grading software, and complete a 100-hour work-integrated learning placement. Past placements include Wildbear, Channel 9, the National Film and Sound Archive and ABC TV productions. Entry is a selection rank of about 60, or a portfolio. It suits people who want hands-on, collaborative filmmaking training with a real production network rather than a purely theoretical screen-studies degree.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Games and Interactive Design
Bachelor of Government
description:
UC's Bachelor of Government sits within the Canberra School of Government and Policy and is built around the university's location in the middle of the federal public service: something the course leans on hard, given how many of its students already work in or alongside government departments based in the ACT.

Core units introduce politics, economics, law and management before students choose a major in Economics, Politics and International Relations, or Public Policy and Administration. The emphasis is consistently on how decisions actually get made and implemented at each level of government, rather than abstract political theory.

The course is offered flexibly, with some units delivered entirely online, which suits students who are already in public-sector roles and studying part time toward a formal qualification in government and policy work rather than starting a graduate career from zero.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Australian Politics; Principles of Economics; Law and Society; Introduction to Public Administration; Foundations of Policy Analysis
Year 2: Comparative Government; Public Sector Economics; major units (Economics, Politics and International Relations, or Public Policy and Administration stream)
Year 3: Policy Implementation and Evaluation; Government and the Media; Professional Placement or Applied Policy Project; advanced major electives
Capstone: Applied Government and Policy Project
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Health Science
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Health Science is a three-year broad degree rather than a clinical registration pathway, pairing a health science core with an applied health major and electives in areas such as health promotion, global health and ecological public health practice.

Students complete a 120-hour work-integrated learning placement in the final year plus professional practice units throughout. The degree is designed as a foundation for honours and then a professional master's such as public health, occupational therapy or speech pathology, or for non-clinical work in health policy, promotion and research. Entry is a selection rank of about 60. It suits students who want a flexible entry into the health sector while deciding on a specialisation.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Health Sciences (Honours)
description: A one-year research honours year following a Bachelor of Health Sciences or a related degree at the University of Canberra. Students complete advanced research-methods coursework and a supervised honours thesis in an area of health science matched to a supervisor. Entry requires a completed bachelor's degree with a strong grade average in the relevant field. The honours result is classified, and a first or upper second class is the standard entry requirement for a PhD and for research scholarships. It suits health sciences graduates who want research training and a completed thesis before a higher degree, or a stronger application for competitive postgraduate health programs.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Human Nutrition
description:
A three-year science degree (72 credit points) on the role of nutrition in health across different societies, built on biochemistry, physiology and food science alongside the psychological, social and cultural drivers of what people eat.

It does not lead to dietitian registration. Graduates are eligible for registration as an Associate Nutritionist with the Nutrition Society of Australia, and those who want to practise as dietitians progress to a master's such as UC's Master of Nutrition and Dietetics, for which this degree is a direct pathway. A placement is required, with Working with Vulnerable People and sometimes police and vaccination checks. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 with assumed knowledge in chemistry and mathematics. It suits students interested in nutrition science, public health, the food industry, research or an allied-health graduate pathway.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
UC's Bachelor of Information Technology sits inside the Faculty of Science and Technology and lets students specialise in one of four areas: Cloud Computing and the Internet of Things, Cybersecurity and System Administration, Data Science, or Robotics and Artificial Intelligence. Only three majors total (core, specialist and breadth) can be completed across the degree, which keeps the structure from sprawling into an unfocused generalist qualification.

Students take at least 24 credit points as a breadth major, minor or set of individual units drawn from outside IT altogether, a deliberate design choice that pushes technical students into some contact with other disciplines rather than three years of pure computing units.

Graduates with a strong GPA can progress directly into a one-year Honours program in the ITS discipline, useful for anyone eyeing research or a PhD pathway in cybersecurity, data science or AI rather than heading straight into industry.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming; Computer Systems Fundamentals; Database Systems; Networking Fundamentals; Web Technologies; Discrete Mathematics for Computing
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms; Systems Analysis and Design; Operating Systems; specialist major units (Cloud/IoT, Cybersecurity, Data Science, or Robotics/AI stream); breadth units
Year 3: Advanced specialist major units; IT Project Management; Professional and Ethical Issues in IT; capstone IT project; breadth major or minor units
Optional: Honours year (research thesis) for eligible high-GPA graduates
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Justice Studies
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Justice Studies is a three-year degree (72 credit points) that takes a broad view of the justice sector rather than specialising narrowly in criminology or policing. Units span criminal justice, social justice, environmental justice, Indigenous justice and family law, with electives in human rights and judicial administration.

A 75-hour internship in a justice workplace is required, with past placements at community legal centres, courts, the Commonwealth Ombudsman, government departments and Legal Aid ACT, and a capstone that includes practical dispute management. Entry is a selection rank of about 65 with alternative pathways available. It suits students who want to work across the justice system as policy officers, probation and parole officers, police, corrections officers or public servants, without doing a full law degree.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
A four-year professional LLB (three years for graduate entry) accredited by the ACT Legal Practitioners Admission Board and, through mutual recognition, accepted for admission in every Australian state and territory. Graduates still complete separate practical legal training before they can be admitted.

Work-integrated learning is substantial: students take at least one law elective with a practical placement component, and UC runs a legal advice clinic for small business where students assist under supervision. Past internships have included community legal centres, courts, government departments and overseas placements. High-achieving students can add an embedded honours unit in the final year without extending the degree. Entry is a selection rank of 85, with alternative pathways including work experience and paralegal experience. The Canberra location gives good access to courts, government legal teams and policy work.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Medical Imaging
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Medical Imaging is a four-year, 96 credit point degree in diagnostic radiography, with first intake in Semester 1, 2027 at the Bruce campus. Study covers imaging anatomy, radiographic technique, the physical principles of imaging, CT, radiation dosimetry, image interpretation and research methods, taught in progressive levels.

Clinical work integrated learning is substantial, structured as four five-week blocks plus two 13-week residencies in metropolitan, regional and rural hospitals. Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as diagnostic radiographers with the Medical Radiation Practice Board of Australia; formal professional accreditation is expected to be assessed in 2028 after the first cohort begins. Entry assumes Year 12 biology, physics and mathematics, and requires police clearance, immunisation records and current first aid. Graduates work as radiographers and move into mammography, sonography, clinical education and research. It suits students set on a medical radiation career.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 85-90 (or equivalent); highly competitive limited-entry program with clinical placement compliance (National Police Certificate, immunisation).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Medical Radiation Science (Medical Imaging)
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Medical Radiation Science (Medical Imaging) is an accelerated 3.5-year degree in diagnostic radiography, six months shorter than the standard four-year qualification elsewhere. It is accredited through the Medical Radiation Practice Board of Australia, so graduates can apply for registration as a diagnostic radiographer and for membership of the Australian Society of Medical Imaging and Radiation Therapy.

Clinical training is four five-week placement blocks and two 13-week residencies across metropolitan, regional and rural hospitals and private practice, after simulation practice on campus. Entry is a selection rank of about 85 with assumed knowledge in biology, physics and mathematics, IELTS 7.0 in every band, and police, immunisation and first aid clearances. It suits school leavers who want the quickest accredited route into radiography.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 85-90 (or equivalent); highly competitive limited-entry program with clinical placement compliance (National Police Certificate, immunisation).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Medical Science
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Medical Science is a three-year degree built around two majors, pathological basis of disease and genetic basis of disease, covering anatomy, physiology, disease mechanisms, genetics, genomics and bioinformatics, with laboratory-based professional practice units and the option of a supervised research project.

It is a common preparation for graduate-entry medicine via the GAMSAT, as well as for research careers and an honours year. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 with assumed knowledge in biology, chemistry and mathematical methods. It suits students aiming at medical research or postgraduate medicine, or who want a strong grounding in human health and disease before deciding.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Midwifery
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Midwifery is a three-year degree accredited by the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Accreditation Council, leading to eligibility for registration as a midwife with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. It is built on a continuity-of-care model: each student follows 22 women through pregnancy, birth and the postnatal period, attending their regular appointments and being on call for labour, which requires real flexibility.

Students complete 1,310 clinical practice hours over the three years, more than at many comparable programs. Entry is a selection rank of about 70 plus police, immunisation, tuberculosis and Working with Vulnerable People clearances, with IELTS 7.0 and at least 6.5 in writing. It suits people committed specifically to midwifery and woman-centred maternity care rather than general nursing.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 75-80 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to clinical placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
UC's Bachelor of Nursing opens with a ten-day clinical placement in first semester specifically so students can test, early, whether nursing as a career matches what they expected. It's a deliberate design choice rather than easing students in slowly. Across the rest of the degree, students complete a minimum of 800 hours of clinical practice spanning community care, mental health, aged care, medical and surgical wards, rehabilitation, palliative care, operating theatre, emergency department and ICU.

Placements run through Canberra Hospital, North Canberra Hospital, Goulburn Base Hospital and a number of private clinics across the ACT, southern NSW and as far as Bega, giving students exposure to both metropolitan and regional health settings within the one degree.

On-campus preparation makes heavy use of high-fidelity simulation (manikins, emerging AI and VR tools, and even trained actors standing in for patients), so students rehearse clinical and communication skills repeatedly in a controlled setting before they're let loose on the placement hours that make up the bulk of their professional preparation.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice; Human Anatomy and Physiology; Health Assessment; Introduction to Professional Nursing; ten-day orientation clinical placement
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing; Mental Health Nursing; Pharmacology for Nurses; Aged Care Nursing; clinical placements in community and acute settings
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing; Emergency and Critical Care Nursing; Palliative Care; Perioperative Nursing; further clinical placement blocks (ED, ICU, operating theatre)
Throughout: minimum 800 hours of supervised clinical placement across metropolitan and regional healthcare settings; transition-to-practice unit ahead of registration as a nurse with AHPRA
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate and immunisation compliance required prior to clinical placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements for nursing.

name: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Occupational Therapy is a four-year, 96 credit point degree that prepares graduates to assess and support people's participation in everyday activities across health, disability, education and aged care settings. Study covers occupational therapy theory and practice, anatomy, mental health and research methods, with competencies built through structured clinical blocks totalling around 1,000 hours of supervised fieldwork in hospitals, clinics, schools and community organisations.

The course is accredited by the Occupational Therapy Council of Australia and approved by the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia, so graduates are eligible to apply for registration as occupational therapists, and it meets World Federation of Occupational Therapists standards. High-achieving students can transfer into an honours stream. Graduates work in public, private and community services including rehabilitation, forensic and community health settings. It suits students committed to a registered allied health profession with strong hands-on placement content.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 85-90 (or equivalent); highly competitive limited-entry program with clinical placement compliance (National Police Certificate, immunisation).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy
description:
The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Pharmacy is a four-year degree fully accredited by the Australian Pharmacy Council, combining laboratory and clinical training. Students take repeated two-week placements in community and hospital pharmacies over the winter periods, plus shorter placements through the teaching semesters.

The degree makes graduates eligible for the supervised internship year that leads to registration as a pharmacist. Entry is a selection rank of about 75 with prerequisites in mathematical methods, chemistry or physics, and biology or human movement, and IELTS 7.0 with no band below 7.0. It suits students who want a clinical, patient-facing health career centred on medicines, clinical reasoning and medication management.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 85-90 (or equivalent); highly competitive limited-entry program with clinical placement compliance (National Police Certificate, immunisation).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Physiotherapy
description:
UC's four-year Bachelor of Physiotherapy is shaped by a Course Advisory Group drawn from Canberra Hospital, Calvary Hospital and the Australian Institute of Sport, which keeps the curriculum tied to what those services actually need from new graduates rather than a purely academic syllabus.

Clinical placements run in blocks, often outside normal teaching weeks, and students treat patients across all age groups and genders under full supervision, including through the UC Health Clinic on campus, which doubles as a low-cost physiotherapy service for the Canberra community. Before any placement, students must complete an immunisation schedule, hold current First Aid/CPR certification, and pass an AFP check for ACT placements, with additional state-based police checks for interstate rotations.

The course is accredited by the Australian Physiotherapy Council and approved by the Physiotherapy Board of Australia, so graduates can apply directly for registration to practise. High-performing students can also apply for the Honours pathway via academic record, interview and application.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Anatomy; Human Physiology; Introduction to Physiotherapy Practice; Biomechanics; Foundations of Musculoskeletal Practice; Psychology for Health Sciences
Year 2: Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy; Neurological Physiotherapy; Cardiorespiratory Physiotherapy; Exercise Prescription; Clinical Placement Block 1
Year 3: Advanced Musculoskeletal Practice; Paediatric and Older Person Physiotherapy; Pain Science; Clinical Placement Blocks in hospital and community settings
Year 4: Complex Clinical Presentations; Professional Practice and Ethics; Clinical Placement Blocks (including UC Health Clinic rotation); Research Project
Optional: Bachelor of Physiotherapy Honours (additional research year) for eligible students
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 85-90 (or equivalent); highly competitive limited-entry program with clinical placement compliance (National Police Certificate, immunisation).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.0 (no band below 6.5), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 94, PTE 65), reflecting registration-body English requirements.

name: Bachelor of Politics and International Relations
description:
A three-year degree (72 credit points) pairing a core major in government and policy with a specialist major in politics and international relations, plus open electives, covering economics, political institutions, democracy, national security and Asia-Pacific geopolitics.

Work-integrated learning runs through internships and a capstone, with past placements at the Australian Border Force, the Centre for Defence and Strategic Studies and the Australian Institute of International Affairs, and exchange options are available with program approval. Being in Canberra puts students near Parliament, the public service and diplomatic missions. Entry is a selection rank of about 65 with no assumed knowledge. It suits students aiming at policy, diplomacy, intelligence, political journalism or international development work.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Primary Education
description:
The Bachelor of Primary Education is a four-year degree preparing graduates to teach Kindergarten through Year 6, and it treats professional placement as the spine of the course rather than an add-on: students complete a minimum of 80 days of practical placement across different school levels and settings, building to a 30-day teaching placement in the final year that functions as a genuine trial run at the job.

From second year onward, the course's Pedagogical Content Knowledge units are taught on-site in schools rather than in a lecture theatre, so students are regularly working with children of primary age well before their major placement blocks begin.

UC also offers several targeted variants of the same degree (with specialisations in Health and Physical Education, Creative Arts, or STEM), all following the same 80-day-plus-30-day placement structure but layering in subject-specific pedagogy for students who already know which curriculum area they want to teach into.
curriculum:
Year 1: Child Development; Introduction to Curriculum and Pedagogy; Literacy Education 1; Numeracy Education 1; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Education
Year 2: Literacy Education 2; Numeracy Education 2; Pedagogical Content Knowledge units (taught on-site in schools); inclusive education units; practicum placement block
Year 3: Science and Technology Education; Humanities and Social Sciences Education; Assessment and Reporting; further on-site Pedagogical Content Knowledge units; practicum placement block
Year 4: Classroom Management; Professional Studies; capstone research or project unit; final 30-day teaching placement
Throughout: minimum 80 days of practical school placement, building to the final-year teaching placement
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.5 (no band below 7.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 102, PTE 69), reflecting registration-body English requirements for teaching.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
A three-year, 72 credit point science degree with a required core major in Science plus one specialist major chosen from Biomedical Science, Biological Science, Chemical Science, Environmental Science, Human Movement or Nutrition Studies, and eight open electives that can add a second major or broaden the degree.

The curriculum emphasises scientific reasoning, data analysis and communication, with laboratory and field work integrated throughout and professional practice units that place students in industry and research settings using current equipment. Entry is a selection rank of about 60, with Year 12 biology, chemistry and mathematical methods as assumed knowledge and IELTS 6.0 for international students. Graduates work as laboratory and research officers, environmental and sustainability officers and biomedical scientists, or move into STEM teaching with further study. It suits students who want a flexible science degree with a clear applied and work-integrated focus.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
description:
A three-year APAC-accredited psychology sequence covering how and why people think, feel and behave, from research methods and statistics through the core areas of the discipline. The degree on its own does not qualify anyone to work as a psychologist.

Registration requires further study: an honours year followed by either a two-year clinical or professional master's and supervised practice. High-achieving students progress to that honours year at UC. Entry is a selection rank of about 60 with alternative pathways available. It suits students heading toward professional psychology, and it also works well as a second major alongside law, business or sport science for roles in HR, policy research, marketing, disability and community health.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Science in Psychology (Honours)
description: The APAC-accredited fourth year of psychology study at the University of Canberra, taken after a three-year accredited psychology sequence. It combines advanced coursework with a supervised empirical research thesis, and completing it to a sufficient standard is a required step on the path to registration as a psychologist: after the accredited fourth year, students go on to a professional master's or the 5+1 internship route. Entry is competitive and based on the grade average across the core third-year psychology subjects. The honours result is classified. It suits psychology graduates committed to the professional pathway, and it is also valued on its own for research and analytical roles.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Secondary Education
description: The University of Canberra's Bachelor of Secondary Education is a four-year degree that qualifies graduates to teach in secondary schools, in state and independent systems. Students prepare in two teaching areas within a chosen specialisation: Arts (from disciplines such as English, history, geography, business, legal studies, media and the creative arts), Science (two science disciplines), or Health and Physical Education paired with a second subject. Placement totals a minimum of 80 days across different secondary settings, ending with a 30-day placement in the final year. Applicants complete a written statement assessing suitability for teaching, and Working with Vulnerable People registration and the national LANTITE test apply before final placement. Graduates are eligible to apply for teacher registration. It suits students who know the subjects they want to teach and are committed to secondary teaching from the start of their degree.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); satisfactory National Police Certificate required prior to professional placement.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Social and Economic Policy (Economic Policy)
Bachelor of Software Engineering
description:
The Bachelor of Software Engineering runs over six semesters full-time and carries accreditation from the Australian Computer Society at the Professional level, which matters for graduates aiming at roles requiring formal ACS recognition, including some skilled migration pathways.

Rather than a single fixed syllabus, students tailor later years toward robotics and AI, computer security, network computing, games development, digital forensics or intelligent systems, overlapping with the same specialist streams (Cloud Computing/IoT, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Robotics and AI) offered across UC's broader IT course family in the Faculty of Science and Technology.

Work Integrated Learning is compulsory, giving students real or close-to-real workplace experience before graduation, and the degree places heavy emphasis on communication and critical systems analysis alongside coding, on the reasoning that engineers who can't explain a design decision to a non-technical stakeholder are only doing half the job.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals; Object-Oriented Software Development; Computer Systems Architecture; Discrete Mathematics; Database Systems; Web Application Development
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms; Software Requirements and Design; Operating Systems; Software Testing and Quality; specialisation stream units (Security, Networks, AI/Robotics, Games, Digital Forensics)
Year 3: Software Architecture; Software Project Management; Work Integrated Learning industry placement/project; Professional Practice in Engineering; capstone Software Engineering Project
Accreditation: Australian Computer Society (Professional level)
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science
description:
Canberra is the base of the Australian Institute of Sport, and UC's Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science leans on that geography directly: students complete 250 hours of Work Integrated Learning, with internship placements available through partners including the AIS itself, NRL and Super Rugby clubs, WNBL and W-League programs, and the ACT's community sport network via UC's on-campus Sporting Commons facility.

The course is accredited by Exercise and Sports Science Australia, so graduates can seek accreditation as an exercise scientist immediately on completion, rather than needing a further conversion year. Coursework covers biomechanics, exercise physiology, motor control and nutrition, building toward a research project students choose within their own area of interest in sport or exercise science.

UC reports that placement-to-employment conversion is unusually strong for this course, with some students securing ongoing roles with their placement organisation before they've even graduated, a reflection of how tightly the internship network is woven into the ACT's sporting institutions.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Anatomy; Human Physiology; Foundations of Sport and Exercise Science; Biomechanics of Human Movement; Nutrition for Health and Performance; Psychology of Sport and Exercise
Year 2: Exercise Physiology; Motor Control and Learning; Strength and Conditioning; Research Methods in Sport Science; Functional Anatomy; elective units
Year 3: Clinical Exercise Physiology; Sport Injury Prevention and Management; Applied Sport Science Practicum (Work Integrated Learning internship); Sport and Exercise Science Research Project; electives
Throughout: 250 hours of supervised Work Integrated Learning placement with community, professional or institute-of-sport partner organisations
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of the Built Environment
description: A three-year design degree in the built environment, offered as named specialisations in Architecture or Interior Architecture. It is the first step toward becoming an architect rather than a licence in itself: registration in Australia requires a further accredited master's and supervised practice. Study is studio-based, combining design projects with history, theory, technology and digital tools, and students use UC's Workshop7 facilities including 3D printing, robotics, laser cutting and a CNC router. Internships, simulated projects and practical work are embedded across the degree. Graduates continue to a master's toward architect registration, or move into architectural and design support, visualisation, project and interiors roles. It suits students starting a long architecture pathway or wanting a design-focused built-environment degree.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 65-70 (or equivalent); completion of a recognised secondary qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Bachelor of Vision Science
description:
A three-year science degree in the biology, optics and health of the visual system. It is the required first half of UC's optometry pathway: the degree on its own is not a clinical qualification, and graduates go on to the two-year Master of Optometry to become registered optometrists.

The final year includes an integrated eye care and ocular therapeutics unit with clinical and non-clinical placement, using the University of Canberra Hospital. Entry is a selection rank of about 80 with assumed knowledge in mathematical methods, chemistry and physics, plus immunisation, first aid and Working with Vulnerable People checks. It suits students committed to the full optometry pathway, or to vision research and the optical industry.
admission_requirements: ATAR of approximately 70-75 (or equivalent); Mathematics at a senior secondary level recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 60, PTE 50).

name: Diploma of Business
description: A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points. It combines first-year business units in management, economics, business decision-making and communication with a required Academic English unit and explicit academic-skills teaching. On completion, students progress directly into the second year of a range of University of Canberra bachelor's degrees, including Business majors, Politics and International Relations and Government. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported, English-strengthening first year. UC College runs the same model in Communication, Design, Health, Information Technology and Science.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no ATAR requirement, direct-entry pathway program.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 46, PTE 42).

name: Diploma of Communication
description: A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points, combining first-year communication and media units with a required Academic English unit and academic-skills teaching. On completion, students move directly into the second year of University of Canberra communication and media bachelor's degrees. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year with built-in English development. UC College runs the same model in Business, Design, Health, Information Technology and Science.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no ATAR requirement, direct-entry pathway program.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 46, PTE 42).

name: Diploma of Design
description: A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points, combining first-year design studio and theory units with a required Academic English unit and academic-skills teaching. On completion, students progress directly into the second year of University of Canberra design bachelor's degrees. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year while building English and studio skills. UC College runs the same model in Business, Communication, Health, Information Technology and Science.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no ATAR requirement, direct-entry pathway program.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 46, PTE 42).

name: Diploma of Health
description: A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points, combining first-year health science units with a required Academic English unit and academic-skills teaching. On completion, students move directly into the second year of a range of University of Canberra health bachelor's degrees. Progression into programs with their own selection process, such as nursing or medical imaging, may have additional requirements. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year. UC College runs the same model in Business, Communication, Design, Information Technology and Science.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no ATAR requirement, direct-entry pathway program.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 46, PTE 42).

name: Diploma of Information Technology
description: A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points, combining first-year information technology units in programming, systems and networks with a required Academic English unit and academic-skills teaching. On completion, students progress directly into the second year of University of Canberra IT and computing bachelor's degrees. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year with built-in English development. UC College runs the same model in Business, Communication, Design, Health and Science.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no ATAR requirement, direct-entry pathway program.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 46, PTE 42).

name: Diploma of Science
description: A one-year pathway diploma delivered by UC College over three trimesters at the Bruce campus, worth 24 credit points, combining first-year science units in biology, chemistry and quantitative methods with a required Academic English unit and academic-skills teaching. On completion, students move directly into the second year of University of Canberra science bachelor's degrees. Entry requires IELTS 5.5 or equivalent. It suits students, particularly international students, who do not meet direct entry or who want a supported first year while strengthening English and laboratory skills. UC College runs the same model in Business, Communication, Design, Health and Information Technology.
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no ATAR requirement, direct-entry pathway program.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 5.5 (no band below 5.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 46, PTE 42).

name: Doctor of Business Administration
description: A professional doctorate in business at the University of Canberra, four years full-time (up to eight years part-time), combining a year of coursework in research design and methods with a substantial thesis. It differs from a PhD by centring on professional practice and work-integrated learning, with candidates using their workplace expertise to investigate a real business problem in an area such as management, economics, accounting or organisational behaviour. Entry requires about five years of senior professional experience plus a relevant master's or honours qualification. Graduates move into executive and senior advisory roles. It suits experienced managers who want a doctorate focused on applied, workplace-relevant research rather than academic research.
admission_requirements: A relevant master's degree (e.g. MBA) plus substantial senior management experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Doctor of Philosophy
description: The University of Canberra's research doctorate, four years full-time (up to ten years maximum), worth 96 credit points. The first year includes up to 12 credit points of coursework in research theory, methodology and critical thinking, with the rest of candidature spent on the research. The output can be a written dissertation, a portfolio of published work, or a creative work with an exegesis. Admission requires suitable supervision plus first or upper-second class honours, a research master's, or a coursework master's with a substantial research component. UC emphasises industry engagement, with internships and partnered projects with government, industry and community organisations. Domestic candidates are typically covered by a Research Training Program fee offset. It suits people aiming at research careers in academia, government or industry.
admission_requirements: A relevant master's degree or honours bachelor's degree with a strong research component (or equivalent); admission also requires an approved research proposal and confirmed supervisor availability.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Doctor of Philosophy in Clinical Psychology
English Language Intensive Course for Overseas Students (ELICOS)
description: An intensive English language program delivered by UC College for students who need to improve their English before starting a University of Canberra course. Teaching is full-time in graded levels focused on academic English: reading, writing, listening, speaking, and the research and study skills used at university. The length of study depends on a student's current level and the level their intended course requires. On successfully completing the required level, students progress into their UC program without sitting a separate external English test. It suits international students who are close to but not yet at the English entry requirement for their degree.
admission_requirements: Open to international student visa holders aged 18+; no formal academic prerequisite, entry level set by an in-house English placement test.
english_requirements: No minimum IELTS/PTE required for entry, ELICOS is itself an English-proficiency preparation program with multiple level intakes.
intake_dates: Multiple intakes throughout the year (approximately every 5 weeks)

name: Graduate Certificate in Academic Foundations
description: The University of Canberra's Graduate Certificate in Academic Foundations is a short 12 credit point course that builds the academic skills needed for postgraduate study: academic writing, research and referencing, critical reading and study strategies. It is aimed at people returning to study or moving into a demanding postgraduate program who want a supported start. It suits students who meet the entry requirements for a master's but want to strengthen their academic skills first, or who need a bridging qualification into further study.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in education or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Building and Construction Information Management
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate, the entry stage of the University of Canberra's Building Information Modelling pathway. It covers the foundations of BIM and digital construction management and articulates with full credit into the Graduate Diploma and then the two-year Master of Building and Construction Information Management, which uses UC's BIM Hub with VR, AR and 3D scanning facilities. Entry normally requires an undergraduate qualification in architecture, construction or engineering, with recognition of prior learning for experienced applicants. It suits built-environment professionals who want a short BIM qualification or a staged route into the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in construction management, architecture, engineering or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Building and Construction Information Management29
Graduate Certificate in Business
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate, four units over about eight months, delivered fully online and part-time. Units are chosen from options such as data-driven decision making, financial management, talent management, marketing and behavioural insights, managerial economics and strategic management, introducing managers and aspiring leaders to the core functions of business. Entry requires a bachelor's degree in any field or three years of relevant work experience, plus IELTS 6.5. The units are credited toward UC's Graduate Diploma and Master of Business. It suits working professionals who want a short, flexible business qualification or a first step toward the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any field, or three years of relevant work experience; IELTS 6.5 overall (6.0 in each band) for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Business Informatics
description: The University of Canberra's Graduate Certificate in Business Informatics is a 12 credit point course that introduces the meeting point of business and information technology, covering systems analysis, IT security and aligning technology with business needs. No prior IT or business informatics background is assumed. It articulates with full credit into the Graduate Diploma and the two-year Master of Business Informatics, where students can specialise in Cybersecurity, Data Science or Project Management. Entry requires a bachelor's degree, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience. It suits people who want a short qualification bridging business and IT, or a staged entry into the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); no prior IT or informatics background is assumed, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Communication
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate covering the foundations of professional communication: strategy, writing, digital and social media and audience research. It articulates with full credit into UC's Graduate Diploma in Communication and Master of Communication. Entry is open to graduates from any field, or applicants with relevant experience. It suits people moving into communication, marketing or public relations roles who want a short qualification, or a low-commitment start on the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any field (or equivalent), or relevant work experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Counselling
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in counselling theory and skills, the entry stage of UC's counselling pathway. It articulates with full credit into the Graduate Diploma in Counselling and then the Master of Counselling, which is accredited by the Australian Counselling Association and includes 200 hours of supervised placement. The certificate on its own is an introductory qualification, not a route to practise as a counsellor. It suits people exploring a move into counselling who want to test the field before committing to the full master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in psychology, social science or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Creative Industries
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in the creative industries, covering the professional context of creative work, project practice and one or more discipline areas. It articulates with full credit into UC's Graduate Diploma and Master of Creative Industries. Entry is open to graduates from a range of backgrounds. It suits practising artists, designers and media workers who want a postgraduate credential, or people moving into the creative sector who want a short qualification before the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent), or relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Cyber Security
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in cyber security, covering network and system security, threats and defensive practice. It articulates with full credit into UC's Graduate Diploma and Master of Cyber Security. No prior computing degree is assumed for entry, though applicants should check the specific requirements, and a professional pathway is available for those with relevant experience. It suits IT and technical staff moving into security roles, or career changers who want a short security qualification and the option to continue to the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); no prior computing degree is assumed, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Data Science
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in data science, covering programming, data analysis, statistical methods and machine learning fundamentals. It articulates with full credit into UC's Graduate Diploma and Master of Data Science. Entry is open to graduates from a range of fields, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience; applicants without a quantitative background should check the requirements. It suits people who want a short data science qualification or a staged route into the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a quantitative discipline (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Digital Marketing
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in digital marketing, covering digital and social media strategy, content, analytics and campaign management. It articulates with full credit into UC's related graduate diploma and master's in marketing and communication. Entry is open to graduates from any field or applicants with relevant experience. It suits marketing and communication staff who want to formalise digital skills, or people moving into digital marketing who want a short qualification before a fuller degree.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any field (or equivalent), or relevant work experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Disability Leadership and Strategy
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate focused on leadership and strategy in the disability sector, covering rights-based practice, service design and organisational leadership in the context of the National Disability Insurance Scheme. It sits alongside UC's Graduate Certificate in Disability Policy and Advocacy and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study in disability and health leadership. Entry is open to graduates and experienced practitioners. It suits managers and team leaders in disability services who want a formal leadership qualification.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (professional experience in disability services well regarded) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Disability Policy and Advocacy
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate focused on disability policy, advocacy and systemic change, covering the policy environment around the National Disability Insurance Scheme, rights frameworks and advocacy practice. It sits alongside UC's Graduate Certificate in Disability Leadership and Strategy and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study. Entry is open to graduates and experienced practitioners, including people with lived experience of disability. It suits advocates, policy officers and sector workers who want a formal qualification in disability policy and advocacy.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Education
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate for people who already work in education, taken fully online with intakes every two months. It is not an initial teaching qualification. Units cover education theory, policy, curriculum and reflective practice, and can be taken as a generalist set or oriented toward a focus area. The units are credited in full toward UC's Master of Education. It suits practising teachers and school staff who want a short qualification to support progression, or a first step toward the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a related field (relevant for practising or aspiring educators) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Education Studies
description: The University of Canberra's Graduate Certificate in Education Studies is a 12 credit point course for people working on policy, curriculum and leadership rather than classroom teaching. Like the Master of Education Studies it feeds into, it is not accredited as a teaching qualification and does not lead to teacher registration. Units cover research methods, education policy and program design. The units are credited in full toward the Master of Education Studies. It suits education professionals building toward leadership and policy roles who want a short qualification first.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in education or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Educational Leadership
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in educational leadership, covering leadership and management theory, organisational change and educational futures. It is aimed at people already working in education who are moving toward formal leadership, and the units are credited in full toward UC's Master of Educational Leadership and Management. Entry normally requires a bachelor's degree plus relevant experience in education or public administration. It suits aspiring school and system leaders who want a short leadership qualification or a staged route into the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in education, with relevant teaching/leadership experience (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Gender Policy
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in gender policy, covering how gender shapes and is shaped by public policy, gender analysis of programs and budgets, and evidence for reform. It sits within UC's public policy suite and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study in policy and public administration. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in government, advocacy or the community sector. It suits policy officers and advocates who want a focused qualification in gender-responsive policy.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Heritage Materials Conservation
description: The University of Canberra's Graduate Certificate in Heritage Materials Conservation is a specialist 12 credit point course covering the science of deterioration, preventive conservation and the care of collections and objects. It provides a grounding for people entering conservation practice or working in museums, galleries, archives and collecting institutions, and can lead into further postgraduate cultural heritage study. Entry is open to graduates from relevant fields such as science, art history, archaeology or museum studies. It suits collection and heritage workers who want formal training in materials conservation.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in heritage, museum studies, art conservation or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Human Movement Science
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in the science of human movement, covering exercise physiology, biomechanics and motor control at postgraduate level. It articulates into UC's related graduate diploma and master's study in human movement and exercise science. Entry normally requires a bachelor's degree in a related field such as sport and exercise science, health or physiotherapy. It suits sport, fitness and allied health professionals who want to deepen their movement science knowledge, or a staged start toward a master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in exercise science, health science or a related field (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Information Technology
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in information technology for graduates from any field, with no prior IT study assumed. Units cover programming, systems, databases and networks. They are credited in full toward UC's Graduate Diploma in Information Technology and Master of Information Technology, and a professional pathway is available for applicants with relevant experience. It suits career changers who want a short IT qualification or a staged, lower-commitment route into the master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in any discipline (foundational IT conversion program) (or equivalent).
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in International Development
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in international development, covering development theory, aid and program practice, and the political and economic context of development work. It sits within UC's governance and policy offering and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in aid, NGOs or government. It suits people entering or working in international development who want a formal qualification, or a first step toward a master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Law
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate for non-law graduates who want working legal knowledge, delivered fully online and part-time over about eight months. It is not a qualification to practise law. Students take two foundation units, Legal Methods and Skills and Legal Systems, plus two electives such as Contract Law, Constitutional Law or Intellectual Property Law. Entry requires a bachelor's degree in a non-law field with a sound grade average and IELTS 6.5. Graduates can progress into UC's Graduate Diploma in Law or the Juris Doctor, which does lead toward admission to practise. It suits professionals in compliance, policy, government relations and business who need to understand the law without becoming a lawyer.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in a non-law field with a sound grade average; IELTS 6.5 overall (6.0 in each band) for international applicants.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in LGBTQIA+ Policy
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in LGBTQIA+ policy, covering how law and public policy affect LGBTQIA+ communities, policy analysis and the evidence base for reform. It sits within UC's public policy suite and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in government, advocacy or community organisations. It suits policy officers and advocates who want a focused qualification in LGBTQIA+ inclusive policy.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Policy and Data
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate that pairs public policy with data skills, covering policy analysis alongside data handling, visualisation and evidence use for decision-making. It sits within UC's policy and governance offering and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in government or research. It suits policy and program staff who want to work more confidently with data, or a short qualification before a fuller policy master's.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Policy Evaluation
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in policy evaluation, covering evaluation design, methods, and using findings to improve programs and inform decisions. It sits within UC's public policy suite, which is a natural fit in Canberra given the concentration of federal agencies, and articulates into related graduate diploma and master's study. Entry is open to graduates and to people working in government or the community sector. It suits program and policy staff who want formal training in evaluating what works.
admission_requirements: A bachelor's degree in any discipline (or equivalent); open to people working in government, advocacy, research or the community sector, with a professional pathway for applicants with relevant experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.5 (no band below 6.0), or equivalent (TOEFL iBT 79, PTE 58).

name: Graduate Certificate in Public Administration
description: A 12 credit point graduate certificate in public administration, covering how government works: policy processes, public sector management, governance and accountability.
