The Bachelor of Agriculture at the University of Melbourne, co-designed with industry, builds a foundation in agricultural science across biology, natural environments and agricultural production, starting with Agriculture Discovery Week at the University's Dookie campus. Students complete 24 subjects over three years, combining eight core subjects with major and elective subjects, along with labs, fieldwork and hands-on experience.
The degree connects to careers spanning farms, finance, fieldwork, policy, business, science and environment, preparing graduates for roles across the agricultural sector and beyond.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
The Bachelor of Arts at the University of Melbourne, ranked first in Australia for arts and humanities, offers a flexible approach to studying the humanities, social sciences and languages. Students choose from more than 40 majors spanning languages, psychology, economics and media and communication, with a multidisciplinary first year building a strong foundation for further study.
Graduates develop career-ready skills in creative and analytical thinking, communication and leadership, with opportunities to build an international perspective through language study and exchange.
curriculum:
Year 1: introductory subjects across two intended majors, plus one breadth subject from outside the arts faculty
Year 2: major sequence subjects deepen (choose from majors including History, Philosophy, English, Politics and International Relations, Psychology, Media and Communications, and area studies), continued breadth requirement
Year 3: capstone subject within the major, remaining major electives, final breadth subject
Breadth subjects (roughly a quarter of the degree) must be taken outside the Faculty of Arts
No formal honours year built in — a separate fourth-year Honours program is available by application for high-achieving students
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 80-90 typically competitive (no specific prerequisites beyond English).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Biomedicine
description:
The Bachelor of Biomedicine at the University of Melbourne immerses students in the Southern hemisphere's largest biomedical precinct, home to more than 40 hospitals, research institutes and biotechnology organisations. Students choose from 16 majors across biomedical disciplines, building knowledge of the body's normal structure and function alongside critical thinking, problem-solving and evidence analysis skills.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia for life sciences and medicine and for graduate employability. Graduates move into medicine, health sciences and biomedical research careers.
curriculum:
Year 1: Biomolecules and Cells, Genetics and the Evolution of Life, Human Structure and Function, Chemistry for Biomedicine
Year 2: major selection (Cell and Developmental Biology, Human Structure and Function, Immunology, Pathology, Pharmacology, Neuroscience, or others), Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
Year 3: advanced major subjects, research-methods subject, capstone research or laboratory project
Breadth subjects required outside the science faculty, consistent with the wider Melbourne Model structure
Strong emphasis throughout on preparation for graduate-entry professional degrees (MD, Doctor of Dental Surgery, Doctor of Physiotherapy)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 92-97, a common pathway toward Medicine/Dentistry postgraduate entry; prerequisite Units 3/4 Chemistry and Mathematical Methods recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (writing 6.5); PTE Academic 65. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
The Bachelor of Commerce at the University of Melbourne, Australia's number one ranked university for business and management, builds a strong foundation in first year through a curated pool of subjects and a compulsory quantitative requirement. Students complete 24 subjects across three years, choosing majors and electives to deepen their commerce knowledge alongside breadth subjects from across the University.
Melbourne commerce graduates are known for their strong understanding of business issues and processes, their resourcefulness, and their problem-solving and leadership skills, moving into challenging and rewarding careers in Australia and overseas.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introductory Microeconomics, Introductory Macroeconomics, Accounting Reports and Analysis, Quantitative Methods, Business Statistics
Year 2: major selection (Accounting, Actuarial Studies, Econometrics, Economics, Finance, Management, Marketing), core major subjects begin
Year 3: advanced major subjects, capstone subject within major, one elective outside the major
Actuarial Studies major carries direct accreditation recognition from the Actuaries Institute
Breadth subjects required outside the Faculty of Business and Economics, per the Melbourne Model structure
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 90-95 typically competitive, plus prerequisite Units 3/4 Mathematics (Any).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Dance (Degree with Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Fine Arts (Dance) at the Victorian College of the Arts, University of Melbourne, builds on the College's reputation for performance-focused dance education, developing kinetically strong, culturally and conceptually aware dance artists. The three-year, full-time degree centres on studio practice, expanded dance thinking and performance, covering contemporary dance practices, dance science, somatics, critical dance studies and choreography.
New works by professional Australian and international choreographers and repertory studies provide performance experience. Graduates move into careers as performers, choreographers, dance leaders and cultural partners across performance, community and arts management sectors.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Design
description:
The Bachelor of Design at the University of Melbourne develops practical skills and theoretical expertise across cities, buildings, transport networks, furniture, websites and landscapes, with Design Studio classes that mirror real workplace practice from the first semester. Students complete 23 to 24 subjects across 300 credit points, producing their own designs and learning a range of design techniques and thinking approaches.
Graduates apply design thinking across technology, architecture, business and other industries, in a job market where demand for creativity skills has risen sharply in recent years.
curriculum:
Year 1: Design Thinking and Ideas, Visual Communication, Digital Design Tools, common studio project across all design majors
Year 2: major selection (Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Construction Management, Property, Urban Design), studio-based major subjects begin
Year 3: advanced design studios within major, Sustainability in the Built Environment, capstone design project
Studio-based assessment (physical and digital models, design juries) dominates from second year onward
Pathway degree into Melbourne's Master of Architecture or other graduate professional design qualifications
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 80-88; pathway toward Master of Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Urban Planning or Construction Management.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Engineering
description: The University of Melbourne does not offer an undergraduate Bachelor of Engineering. Under the Melbourne Model, students who want to become engineers first complete a three-year bachelor's degree, usually the Bachelor of Science taking an engineering systems major (or the Bachelor of Design for some disciplines), then complete the two- to three-year Master of Engineering, which carries professional accreditation from Engineers Australia. The Bachelor of Science plus Master of Engineering pathway takes about five to six years in total. Prospective engineering students should apply for the Bachelor of Science and choose an engineering-focused major, or the Bachelor of Design. This page is kept for reference because a Bachelor of Engineering still appears in the CRICOS register. International tuition for the Bachelor of Science is around A$50,000 per year.
discontinued_note: The University of Melbourne does not offer a standalone undergraduate engineering degree; engineering is studied via the Bachelor of Science (with an engineering systems major) followed by the Master of Engineering in a chosen discipline.

name: Bachelor of Environments
discontinued_note: This award has been replaced by the University of Melbourne's Bachelor of Design.

name: Bachelor of Film and Television (Degree with Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Fine Arts (Film and Television) at the Victorian College of the Arts, University of Melbourne, develops writer-directors with distinctive creative voices and detailed practical knowledge of all stages of film and television production. The three-year, full-time degree offers production-based, practical filmmaking and screen-based storytelling, with students initiating, developing and realising short film projects in studio and production environments.
Students and graduates win industry awards at festivals including Berlin International, Cannes and the Academy Awards. Graduates move into cinematographer, director, editor, producer and screenwriter roles.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Fine Arts (Honours) at the University of Melbourne is a one-year program introducing candidates of proven ability to research training, developing critical thinking, creative drive and the capacity to manage a major creative research project. Visual Art students work from The Stables, a contemporary arts research hub, producing work under individual supervision that enters the annual VCA Graduate Exhibition.
Graduates continue into advanced practice or pathways into graduate research programs such as the Master of Fine Arts by Research or Doctor of Philosophy (Fine Arts and Music).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Medical Science (Degree with Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Medical Science (Degree with Honours) at the University of Melbourne develops skills in interpreting and applying scientific evidence to clinical practice, exploring the design, recording and ethical reporting of clinical research. Students complete 100 credit points across three compulsory subjects: Introduction to Medical Research, Advanced Medical Research, and a Project in Medical Research.
Graduates develop analytical reasoning and problem-solving skills to critically evaluate scholarly evidence, meeting entry requirements for a master's degree or PhD in a relevant discipline.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (writing 6.5); PTE Academic 65. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Music
description:
The Bachelor of Music (Honours) at the University of Melbourne is an intensive, one-year program rounding off undergraduate music study, with specialisations in composition, interactive composition, jazz and improvisation, musicology or ethnomusicology, and performance. Under a supervisor's guidance, students produce a major creative work or series of works and related research, building on and deepening the skills of their chosen specialisation.
The program creates a direct pathway to graduate coursework and research opportunities, including the Master of Music (Research) and Doctor of Philosophy (Fine Arts and Music), or a career as a professional practising artist.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Oral Health
description:
The Bachelor of Oral Health at the University of Melbourne prepares students to register as an oral health therapist, qualified to practise as both a dental therapist and dental hygienist, taught alongside dental students at the Melbourne Dental School. The three-year degree comprises eight compulsory year-long subjects spanning oral health sciences, social sciences and health promotion, and community oral health studies, with hands-on clinical experience in metropolitan and rural placements.
Graduates gain the practical skills to examine, diagnose and treat patients and qualify for registration as a dental practitioner with AHPRA upon graduation.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
The Bachelor of Science at the University of Melbourne offers more than 40 majors across science, engineering, IT and mathematics, with a flexible first year letting students explore before specialising. Students complete 24 subjects over three years, including the discovery subject Today's Science, Tomorrow's World in their first semester, building analytical, technical, practical and theoretical skills.
Graduates move into careers across science, engineering, health and technology, with the flexibility to add a specialisation building complementary expertise.
curriculum:
Year 1: common core across Chemistry, Biology, Physics, and Mathematics, plus breadth subject requirement
Year 2: major selection from a wide list (Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Genetics, Microbiology and Immunology, Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Statistics, Environmental Science, Computing and Software Systems, and others), major core subjects begin
Year 3: advanced major electives, capstone Science Research Project embedded in an active research group
Fourth-year Honours available by application for high-achieving students, often a prerequisite for research higher degrees
Breadth requirement (outside the science faculty) runs across all three years
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 85-93 typically competitive, plus prerequisite Units 3/4 Mathematical Methods.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Science Advanced (Honours)
description: The University of Melbourne's Bachelor of Science Advanced (Honours) is a four-year undergraduate degree with a flexible, student-directed structure supported by the Melbourne curriculum. Students build core scientific knowledge and practical skills across a wide range of fields and specialise once they are ready, with an embedded honours research year. Graduates work across science, research, industry and further study.
discontinued_note: This award now sits within the Bachelor of Science.

name: Diploma in Computing
description:
The Diploma in Computing at the University of Melbourne, open only to students already admitted to another University of Melbourne degree, teaches programming, online solution design and web application development alongside a primary undergraduate degree. Students complete 100 points of specified study, with up to 50 points cross-credited between the diploma and their bachelor's degree, completing two compulsory subjects including COMP10001.
The diploma equips students with IT knowledge valued across finance, economics, biology, engineering, health and communications industries.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Diploma in Languages
description:
The Diploma in Languages at the University of Melbourne, one of five concurrent diplomas available to bachelor's degree students, lets students study one of 12 languages alongside their primary degree, with or without prior language training. Students complete a 100-point program through a proficiency-based progression sequence across three levels, with a mix of compulsory and elective subjects at each stage.
Melbourne is ranked 19th in the world for language study. Graduates gain oral, aural, writing and reading mastery comparable to a language major, alongside cultural understanding of the societies associated with their chosen language.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Diploma in Mathematical Sciences
description:
The Diploma in Mathematical Sciences at the University of Melbourne, open only to students already admitted to another University of Melbourne degree, gives students a mathematics qualification alongside their undergraduate studies. Students specialise in applied mathematics, operations research, pure mathematics, or statistics and stochastic processes, completing up to 50 points of mathematics and statistics subjects alongside their primary degree.
Graduates gain numerical and modelling skills applicable across almost every area of employment, engaging in mathematical discourse across science, industry, technology and commerce.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Diploma in Music (Practical)
description:
The Diploma in Music (Practical) at the University of Melbourne, open only to students already admitted to another University of Melbourne degree, gives students access to the full curriculum at the Melbourne Conservatorium of Music alongside their main studies. Students focus on practical music training with individual instrumental or vocal tuition over a minimum three-year sequence, or complete the equivalent of a major in musicology or ethnomusicology.
Students study alongside Bachelor of Music students, building networks and friendships, and graduate with a music qualification that complements their primary degree or leads toward a music-focused career in education or performance.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Clinical Dentistry
description:
The Doctor of Clinical Dentistry at the University of Melbourne lets general dentists become specialists in a chosen dental field, fully accredited by the Australian Dental Council. Students complete 300 points, with 75 points of core research subjects and 225 points in their chosen specialisation, split roughly 50 per cent clinical training, 20 per cent coursework and 30 per cent research.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia and 41st in the world for dentistry. Graduates specialise across seven clinical dentistry fields including endodontics, oral medicine, orthodontics, paediatric dentistry, periodontics, prosthodontics and special needs dentistry.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) or equivalent in a cognate (relevant) discipline. Cognate (relevant) disciplines include: Dentistry or equivalent that qualifies the applicant to register and practice as a Dentist (in their country of origin or residence). And Have two years of documented relevant clinical work experience. And Have demonstrated proof of current dental registration (AHPRA or international equivalent). The University of Melbourne is committed to maintaining a transparent admissions policy by clearly communicating all entry scores to prospective students. Entry requirements to the University of Melbourne are regularly reviewed to ensure they align with the University's Selection and Admissions Policy . The entry requirements published for this course will apply from the start year 2027 intake onwards.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 91; PTE Academic 72. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Dental Surgery
description:
The Doctor of Dental Surgery at the University of Melbourne is a four-year, full-time program preparing students for registration as a general dentist in Australia and New Zealand, with eligibility to apply for certification in Canada. The curriculum integrates foundational scientific knowledge with progressively increasing clinical experience, culminating in a final year predominantly spent in clinical settings.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia and 41st in the world for dentistry. Graduates are equipped to provide comprehensive oral health care across a variety of settings, supported by modern clinical facilities.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must have: An undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in any discipline, with studies completed within 10 years of 1 January of the year in which you intend to commence this degree, OR An undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in any discipline AND a graduate diploma, master's degree or PhD (or equivalent) completed within 10 years of 1 January of the year in which you intend to commence this degree. AND Passed prerequisite university subjects * in anatomy, biochemistry and physiology at second year level (or equivalent), with prerequisite subjects to have been taken within 10 years of 1 January of the year in which you intend to commence this degree, AND either: The Graduate Australian Medical School Admissions Test ( GAMSAT ), OR For international students who are located overseas only, one of the following: The United States Dental Admission
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (writing 6.5); PTE Academic 65. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Education
description:
The Doctor of Education at the University of Melbourne is a research doctorate for experienced professionals with educational responsibilities, combining a tailored coursework program with research directly relevant to their professional role. Candidates complete 100 credit points of coursework across four doctoral-level subjects in research design and methodology, plus a 55,000-word thesis comprising a substantial piece of original research, over four years full-time or eight years part-time.
Melbourne's Faculty of Education is ranked first in Australia and 15th in the world, and candidates demonstrate academic leadership and originality in their contribution to knowledge.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 58. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Medicine
description:
The Doctor of Medicine at the University of Melbourne is a four-year, full-time course externally accredited by the Australian Medical Council, comprising a year of integrated bioscience and clinical learning, two core clinical training years, discovery subjects for exploring particular interests, and a capstone semester rehearsing the skills needed for safe clinical practice. Students can also complete an immersive research experience.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia and 20th in the world for medicine. Graduates are eligible to apply for registration with the Medical Board of Australia and move into clinical practice, research, health leadership and education roles.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into the Doctor of Medicine via the standard pathway , as an international applicant you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) or equivalent in any discipline with studies to have been completed within 10 years of 1 January in the year in which you intend to commence the Doctor of Medicine. Or Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) or equivalent in any discipline completed 10 or more years before 1 January of the year in which you intend to commence the Doctor of Medicine. And Have completed a graduate diploma (AQF8) or equivalent in any discipline completed within 10 years before 1 January of the year in which you intend to commence the Doctor of Medicine. And Complete the Graduate Australian Medical Schools Admission Test (GAMSAT) with a minimum of 50 in each section. For international students who are located overseas only, either complete the GAMSA
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 91; PTE Academic 72. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Optometry
description:
The Doctor of Optometry at the University of Melbourne, the first course of its kind in the southern hemisphere, covers the basic and applied optical, visual and biomedical sciences underpinning optometry, fully accredited by the Optometry Council of Australia and New Zealand. Students complete 400 credit points across four years, including a clinically relevant research project and clinical training at metropolitan, rural and overseas sites in the final year.
Melbourne is ranked 14th in the world for life sciences and medicine. Graduates access high employment rates across diverse optometry career pathways.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must have: an undergraduate degree (or equivalent) with studies to have been completed within 10 years of commencing this degree OR An undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in any discipline completed more than 10 years ago, AND a graduate diploma, master's degree or PhD (or equivalent) completed within 10 years of commencing this degree. Learn more about prerequisite subjects for the Doctor of Optometry . You must also have completed: Three subjects at level two or level three (or equivalent) from one or more relevant biological science disciplines, with subjects to have been completed within 10 years of commencing this degree. Weighted average mark (WAM) While there is no minimum WAM for this course, applicants with a WAM of 65+ are encouraged to apply. The Melbourne MBA at Melbourne Business School has a long record of producing senior executives able to lead across private, public and government organisations, with an integrated, skills-focused curriculum built for career impact. The Full-time Master of Business Analytics at Melbourne Business School is a one-year, advanced degree developing the computational, analytical and business skills to extract value from data as a strategic asset. name: Master of Commerce
description: The University of Melbourne's Master of Commerce is not a general coursework master's degree. It is a two-year research-training program that forms years one and two of the University's five-year doctoral programs, offered as Master of Commerce in Management, Economics, Marketing, Accounting, Finance, or Decision, Risk and Financial Sciences. Students take advanced disciplinary and research-methods subjects and a research report, and progress into the PhD only if they meet high grade thresholds, generally a 75 to 80 per cent average. Entry is highly competitive and aimed at students planning an academic or research career, with scholarships including fee waivers and a stipend for strong applicants. Graduates who want a professional coursework qualification should instead look at Melbourne's Master of Management, Master of Finance, or the Master of Commerce specialisation coursework alternatives.

The Master of Creative Arts Therapy at the University of Melbourne is a blended learning program with a specialisation in either drama or dance movement therapy, using creative modalities within a therapeutic relationship to improve physical, mental and emotional wellbeing. Students complete supervised industry placements in community, health and education settings over 24 months full-time, studying theory, methods, research and professional practice.
Graduates are eligible for professional registration with the Dance Movement Therapy Association of Australasia or the Australian, New Zealand and Asian Creative Arts Therapies Association.

name: Master of Engineering (Civil)
description:
Consistent with the Melbourne Model logic that pushed most professional training to graduate level, the Master of Engineering (Civil) is how Melbourne now delivers what used to be an undergraduate civil engineering degree: students typically arrive having done a Bachelor of Science or a broader engineering systems undergraduate degree first, then specialise here.

The Melbourne School of Engineering has particular research depth in geotechnical and structural engineering that traces back to long-standing relationships with major Victorian infrastructure projects: the West Gate Tunnel and Metro Tunnel projects, among others, have supplied case material and occasionally student placements over the years the projects have run. That gives the degree's design studios a distinctly Melbourne-infrastructure flavour compared to a program without that local pipeline.

Because the degree is graduate-entry, cohorts include a mix of straight-through Melbourne Model students and a genuine slice of international students who did an unrelated undergraduate engineering degree elsewhere and are using the Melbourne master's to specialise or requalify for the Australian market. Engineers Australia accreditation is a real driver of enrolment for that second group specifically.
curriculum:
Foundational subjects (for students without a civil-specific undergraduate background): Structural Analysis, Geotechnical Engineering, Fluid Mechanics
Core: Reinforced Concrete Design, Steel Structures, Transport Engineering, Water Engineering, Construction Management
Advanced electives: Earthquake Engineering, Advanced Geomechanics, Sustainable Infrastructure, Bridge Engineering
Capstone: Engineering Design Project, often linked to a real Victorian infrastructure case or partner organisation
Engineers Australia accreditation pathway built into the standard sequence
admission_requirements: Bachelor of Science or equivalent with an engineering systems major (or approved equivalent quantitative degree); minimum WAM typically 65%+.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent TOEFL/PTE)
discontinued_note: This award now sits within the Master of Civil Engineering.

Graduates gain an in-depth understanding of international contemporary practice and are in demand across all levels of government, in landscape architecture, planning, engineering and multidisciplinary consultancies.

description:
The Master of Management at Melbourne Business School develops foundational knowledge and specialist organisational management skills through hands-on practical experience with real companies, open to students from business and non-business backgrounds. The 200-point program comprises 16 subjects including four foundation subjects, with accelerated one-year and 1.5-year options available and the option to add a concurrent graduate certificate.
Graduates use evidence to inform management decisions and think critically about how business issues affect society more broadly. Melbourne is ranked first in Australia for business and economics and 19th in the world for management studies.

The course was developed with industry input to address current skills shortages in Victoria's expanding MedTech workforce, preparing graduates to innovate and lead in a fast-growing healthcare sector.

Graduates become highly employable, versatile candidates for language teaching jobs around the world, in a field the University describes as key to a plurilingual society.

Graduates are eligible for registration as music therapists with the Australian Music Therapy Association, working with clients from preschool age through to older adults.

The Master of Nursing Science at the University of Melbourne, accredited by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, prepares graduates to practise as registered nurses delivering compassionate, evidence-based care. Students complete 200 credit points over two years, including 12 compulsory subjects and one elective, exploring contemporary health issues such as mental health, cancer and cardiovascular disease through intensive teaching blocks and clinical placements at major metropolitan teaching hospitals.
Melbourne is ranked 29th in the world for nursing. Graduates gain a portable qualification enabling them to work locally, nationally or internationally.

Semester 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Pharmacology, first clinical placement

Final semester: capstone Transition to Professional Practice placement, Professional and Ethical Practice in Nursing

The Master of Philosophy (Biomedical Science) at the University of Melbourne is an internationally recognised research master's degree for students developing advanced skills in independent research, with projects available across cancer, cardio-respiratory science, cell signalling, infection and immunity, neuroscience, stem cells and systems biology. Candidates enrol in a thesis subject for a normal candidature of 18 months full-time, completing at least six months of full-time research at the University.
Graduates demonstrate an advanced and integrated understanding of recent developments in their chosen biomedical discipline, with the ability to independently investigate and synthesise complex information.

The Master of Private Law at the University of Melbourne develops a deep understanding of the core areas of law fundamentally important to commercial practice, including contract law, the law of torts, equity, restitution, trusts and remedies. Students complete 100 credit points, including Fundamentals of the Common Law for those without a common law degree, delivered flexibly for working professionals.
The course is part of the Melbourne Law Masters program and is open to both law and non-law graduates. Melbourne Law School is ranked first in Australia and eighth globally, and graduates work in commercial litigation and commercial transactions.

The Master of Property at the University of Melbourne, accredited by the Australian Property Institute and the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, prepares aspiring property professionals to identify development opportunities and build a successful investment portfolio. Students entering from a cognate discipline with 100 points of advanced standing complete the 200-point program, analysing market trends, property valuation and financial feasibility.
Graduates work at firms including CBRE, Colliers International, Cushman and Wakefield, and Development Victoria across international, corporate and sustainable real estate sectors.

name: Master of Psychiatry
description:
The Master of Psychiatry at the University of Melbourne is delivered wholly online by the Department of Psychiatry, giving medical practitioners an integrated understanding of the evidence-based aetiology, diagnosis, formulation, assessment, management and prognosis of major psychiatric disorders. Students develop an understanding of psychological and scientific theories alongside the genetic and psycho-social context of patient presentations, and the evolution of human behaviour across the life cycle.
The course prepares medical practitioners for professional exams and further study pathways toward consultant psychiatrist roles, delivering outstanding clinical care in mental health.

description:
The Master of Psychology (Clinical Psychology) at the University of Melbourne is a nationally recognised, APAC-accredited program preparing graduates for professional registration as clinical psychologists in Australia, with immersive clinical placements and research opportunities. Students build a strong knowledge base in psychopathology alongside culturally responsive assessment and evidence-based therapy skills, guided by faculty who are leaders in both practice and scholarship.
Melbourne is ranked first in Australia and 20th in the world for psychology. Graduates gain a working knowledge of the medical and mental health systems where clinical psychologists are employed, becoming registered psychologists post-graduation.

The Master of Public Health at the University of Melbourne builds breadth and depth in public health knowledge and practice, delivered flexibly on campus in Parkville, online, or a combination of both, over two years full-time or four years part-time. Six core subjects are combined with a wide range of elective subjects in special interest areas, work-based placements, research projects and independent study.
Melbourne is ranked second in Australia and 17th in the world for public health. Graduates move into roles across infectious disease epidemiology, biostatistics, gender and women's health, global health and health economics.

The Master of Public Policy and Management at the University of Melbourne, the premier degree of its kind with over 30 years of teaching, develops high-level analytic skills that meet the demands of complex public policy-making. Students choose a 200-point, two-year program or a 150-point, 1.5-year program for graduates with relevant professional experience, using theoretical and analytical perspectives on governance, institutions and policy processes.
Graduates move into roles including senior policy and arts officer, policy and planning manager, government investment adviser, policy analyst and government communications adviser.

The Master of Publishing and Communications at the University of Melbourne examines new business models and the expanded digital footprint of publishing, from eBooks to apps, through a digitally focused, internationally oriented curriculum connected to current publishing practice. The Master of Science (Bioinformatics) at the University of Melbourne combines genetics, biology and biochemistry with computer science and applied mathematics to decode complex biological data. Students complete a 200-point course tailored to their academic background in the first year, then broaden into advanced analysis techniques and a 50-point research project addressing real industry and academic challenges.

Graduates develop screenwriting skills for national and international industries, becoming confident writing and rewriting screenplays, with the option to continue into a research master's degree.

The Master of Social Policy at the University of Melbourne examines key developments in social policy through a global lens, with a strong emphasis on social justice and the ability to influence policy across employment, income support, education, health and climate change. Students choose a 200-point, two-year program or a 150-point, 1.5-year program for graduates of a relevant discipline, with compulsory, capstone and elective subjects.
Graduates move into roles across community, state and national government, policy design, social administration and welfare work, and policy analysis.

description:
The Master of Social Work at the University of Melbourne is one of the first master's degrees nationally accredited by the Australian Association of Social Workers, meeting the Australian Social Work Education and Accreditation Standards. Over two years, students complete 175 points of coursework and 50 points of field education, including two 500-hour supervised field placements, developing skills in casework, counselling, advocacy and community engagement.

The Master of Software Engineering at the University of Melbourne covers best practice for every stage of the software development cycle, from design and engineering to deployment, with specialisations in Artificial Intelligence, Business, Cyber Security, Distributed Computing or Human Computer Interaction. Students with a relevant undergraduate major complete the degree in two years, starting in second year with credit for foundation subjects.
Graduates work across banking and finance, human-computer interaction, technology consulting and health, with a skillset also valued in management consulting and project management.

The Master of Speech Pathology at the University of Melbourne develops the knowledge, clinical reasoning and professional skills to assess and support communication and swallowing across the lifespan, over two years of evidence-based learning and practical experience. Students complete approximately 400 hours of supervised clinical work across health-care and educational facilities in metropolitan and rural Victoria.
Graduates are eligible for membership of Speech Pathology Australia and work in partnership with families across diverse healthcare, education and community settings.

The Master of Teaching (Secondary) at the University of Melbourne prepares students to teach 12 to 18-year-olds through the University's clinical model of education, unique in Australia, with a new Health, Outdoor and Physical Education learning area available from 2026. Students become qualified to teach two learning areas and are introduced to a third, completing the most comprehensive teaching placement program in Victoria and a final-year Work Integrated Learning experience.
Graduates register with the Victorian Institute of Teaching and are sought after directly by schools across Melbourne's extensive network, known for producing some of the country's best teachers.

name: Master of TESOL

The Master of TESOL at the University of Melbourne teaches students to teach English as an Additional Language across mainstream schools, migrant language centres and international settings, gaining a rich understanding of TESOL research, methodology and assessment. The Master of Urban and Cultural Heritage at the University of Melbourne is a cross-disciplinary, industry-oriented program examining the interpretation, management and conservation of urban and cultural heritage amid rapid urbanisation and social change. Students complete 100 points, including 50 points of core subjects and 50 points of electives, choosing an industry internship or a minor research thesis after the core subject stream.
Heritage skills are in demand across Australia and the Asia-Pacific, and the course complements existing professional skills in architecture, planning, archaeology and history.

The course is recognised by the Planning Institute of Australia. Urban design skills are in strong demand throughout Australia and the Asia-Pacific region.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) in a cognate (relevant) discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 65%, or equivalent. Cognate (relevant) disciplines include: Urban design, landscape architecture, or architecture. This course also has selection tasks you must complete, see below in 'About selection'.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 81; PTE Academic 64. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Master of Urban Horticulture
description:
The Master of Urban Horticulture at the University of Melbourne, the only course of its kind in the Southern Hemisphere, prepares students to maintain and improve green spaces for liveable neighbourhoods, taught at the heritage-listed Burnley campus. Students complete 100 points of core subjects, at least 75 points of discipline electives, and professional skills subjects, with an optional horticulture industry internship and research project, exiting after one year with the graduate diploma or completing two years for the full master's.
Graduates work in horticulture and landscape management roles across local government, design and consultancy firms, and community organisations.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) in any discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 65%, or equivalent. Or Have completed a graduate certificate (AQF8) in any discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 65%, or equivalent. Or Have completed a bachelor honours degree (AQF8) or equivalent in any discipline. Or Have completed a graduate diploma (AQF8) or equivalent in any discipline.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 81; PTE Academic 64. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Master of Urban Planning
description:
The Master of Urban Planning at the University of Melbourne, recognised by the Planning Institute of Australia, focuses on Australian and international policy and planning for human settlements amid climate change, inequality and population growth. Students complete eight core subjects, four specialisation subjects, a capstone or minor thesis, and two multidisciplinary electives from areas such as economics, engineering or public health.
Graduates work in government departments and agencies, local councils, and private and public sector planning roles in Australia and internationally.
admission_requirements: To be considered for entry into this course, you must: Have completed a bachelor degree (AQF7) in any discipline with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 65%, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 81; PTE Academic 64. The University of Melbourne also accepts its Melbourne University English Language Testing Service and pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Agricultural and Resource Economics
Bachelor of Agriculture
description:
UNE has been teaching agriculture out of Armidale since the 1950s and the degree still runs on the assumption that graduates need paddock-ready skills, not just classroom theory. Students spend real hours on the university's own working farms in the New England region doing things like pregnancy-testing cattle, soil sampling, and pasture assessment as assessed coursework rather than optional add-ons.

Students pick a specialisation in animal production, plant production, or mixed farming systems, and the New England tablelands setting shapes which one tends to dominate enrolment: this is sheep and cattle country, so animal production and the various livestock genetics electives draw the biggest numbers, though UNE's plant production stream benefits from the same research strength that backs the university's long-running work in pasture agronomy.

Because a large share of UNE's agriculture cohort comes from farming families or rural NSW/Queensland towns rather than capital cities, the degree also runs fully online with 24/7 tutor support for exactly that demographic. Someone running a family property doesn't necessarily want to relocate to study, and UNE built its entire institutional identity around solving that problem for regional Australia decades before "online learning" became a mainstream option elsewhere.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Agricultural Systems, Soil Science, Plant Production Principles, Animal Production Principles, Agricultural Business
Year 2: specialisation begins (Animal Production, Plant Production, or Mixed Farming), Agricultural Economics, Pasture and Rangeland Management
Year 3: Livestock Genetics or Crop Physiology (depending on stream), Farm Business Management, capstone Agricultural Systems Project
Minors available in agricultural sustainability, climate resilience, or agribusiness
On-campus students complete practical blocks at UNE's teaching farms; distance students complete equivalent practicals through residential schools
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65 or equivalent; no prerequisite subjects required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
UNE's Bachelor of Arts carries the university's founding identity more than almost any other program on this list. UNE was Australia's first university to offer external (distance) study back in the 1950s, and the BA remains the degree most associated with that mission: a large share of the cohort studies fully online, often as mature-age students balancing the degree with work, farming, or family responsibilities in regional NSW and beyond.

The major list covers the expected humanities and social science range (History, English, Politics, Sociology), and UNE's history department in particular has a research niche in Australian rural and regional history that shows up in elective offerings you wouldn't necessarily find at a metropolitan university's arts faculty. Local and family history methods units draw directly on that strength and on UNE's own regional archives.

Because so much of the cohort is part-time and juggling other commitments, the degree is structured to be genuinely flexible on pacing. Students can move through majors across a longer timeframe than a standard three-year full-time load without it functioning as an afterthought accommodation, since UNE's whole institutional model assumes non-standard study patterns rather than treating them as the exception.
curriculum:
Year 1: introductory subjects across two chosen majors, Academic and Research Skills
Year 2: major sequence subjects (choose from History, English, Politics, Sociology, Philosophy, Classics and Ancient History, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies)
Year 3: advanced major electives, capstone research subject within primary major
Delivered on-campus at Armidale or fully online, with flexible part-time pacing genuinely built into the structure
Minor option available for students wanting a secondary area of study alongside their major
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 60 or equivalent; broad entry requirements
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Computer Science with Honours
Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood and Primary)
description:
UNE has trained a disproportionate share of regional NSW's teaching workforce for decades, largely because it was one of the first Australian universities to offer education degrees by distance study, and the Early Childhood and Primary combined degree reflects that regional-supply mission directly. A lot of graduates end up teaching in exactly the kind of small-town and rural schools that struggle hardest to recruit and retain staff.

The dual qualification (early childhood plus primary) is a deliberate structural choice: it widens graduates' employability across the birth-to-12 age range rather than locking them into one narrower registration category, which matters more in regional labour markets where a single small town might only have openings in one sector in a given year.

Professional placement blocks run through partner schools and early learning centres across the New England region and beyond for online students, and UNE's placement office has built relationships specifically geared toward regional and rural schools that a metropolitan education faculty's placement network wouldn't reach as naturally.
curriculum:
Year 1: Child Development, Foundations of Early Childhood Education, Introduction to Primary Curriculum, Literacy Education I
Year 2: Numeracy Education, Play-Based Learning, Inclusive Education, first extended school/centre placement
Year 3: Science and Technology Education, Assessment and Reporting, Behaviour Support, second placement block
Year 4: capstone Professional Practice placement (full teaching responsibility under supervision), Education Research Project
Placements span both early childhood settings and primary schools to satisfy the dual qualification
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65 or equivalent; satisfactory Working with Children Check required prior to placement
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (NESA professional teaching requirement)

name: Bachelor of Historical Inquiry and Practice
Bachelor of International Studies with Honours
Bachelor of Laws
description:
UNE's law school is small compared to the sandstone universities but it was a genuine pioneer in flexible legal education. UNE offers its LLB fully online, which for a long time was unusual among Australian law degrees given how heavily traditional legal pedagogy leaned on in-person Socratic seminar teaching, and the school built out video-based moot court and virtual tutorial infrastructure specifically to make that model work for law rather than treating online delivery as a lesser substitute.

The degree covers the Priestley 11 compulsory subjects like any accredited Australian LLB, but UNE's context (regional NSW, a large mature-age and rural cohort) shapes elective demand toward areas like agricultural and rural law, water rights, and native title, topics that carry direct professional relevance for graduates likely to end up practising in regional firms rather than capital-city commercial practice.

A meaningful share of UNE law students are combining the LLB with work or a farm business rather than studying full-time straight out of school, and the university's assessment scheduling (block intensives, flexible submission windows) reflects that reality more directly than a metropolitan law school's calendar would.
curriculum:
Compulsory Priestley 11 sequence: Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, Equity and Trusts, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, Corporations Law, Professional Conduct
Foundation: Legal Research and Writing, Introduction to Legal Reasoning
Electives (choose from): Agricultural and Natural Resources Law, Native Title Law, Family Law, International Law
Capstone: Legal Practice Skills unit incorporating negotiation and advocacy assessment
Delivered on-campus at Armidale or fully online with residential intensives for practical components
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 75 or equivalent; competitive entry
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Media and Communicationswith Honours
Bachelor of Nursing
description:
UNE's nursing degree is built specifically around the New England region's healthcare workforce needs. Regional NSW and Queensland have chronic nursing shortages, and clinical placements run through Armidale Rural Referral Hospital and a spread of smaller regional and rural facilities across the New England and North West, giving students exposure to rural generalist nursing practice that's genuinely different from a metropolitan hospital placement rotation.

The degree has a strong online delivery component for theory content, with clinical placement blocks completed in students' home regions where possible, a deliberate design choice that lets students already living in rural or regional communities study without relocating to a capital city, and one that UNE leans into because it also serves as a pipeline back into the same underserved communities once students graduate.

Because rural nursing practice often demands broader generalist skills than a specialised metropolitan ward role, UNE's curriculum places real weight on primary health care and community nursing content earlier than some urban nursing degrees do, reflecting the reality that a New England graduate is statistically more likely to end up working in a small regional hospital or community health setting than a large tertiary trauma centre.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, first clinical placement
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, Rural and Remote Health, extended placement block
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Primary Health Care Nursing, Aged Care Nursing, Transition to Professional Practice placement
Clinical placements delivered through Armidale Rural Referral Hospital and regional partner facilities across the New England and North West
Total placement hours meet AHPRA registration requirements across all three years
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 70 or equivalent; satisfactory National Police Check and immunisation requirements for clinical placement
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (NMBA registration standard)

name: Bachelor of Nutrition and Health Science
Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
UNE's psychological science degree is APAC accredited, putting graduates on the standard first-stage pathway toward provisional psychologist registration, and the program has built a genuinely strong distance-education infrastructure around psychology specifically. Statistics and research methods units, which are usually the hardest content to teach remotely, run with structured online tutorials and simulation-based data analysis exercises rather than just recorded lectures.

Because such a large share of the cohort studies externally, UNE has invested specifically in making the practical and lab-based components (things that would normally require in-person attendance) work at a distance: online experimental simulations and remote data collection exercises substitute for some of what an on-campus student elsewhere would do in a physical lab.

The honours pathway, required for provisional registration under the national accreditation scheme, is competitive on GPA like anywhere else, and UNE's smaller psychology department means the honours cohort each year is modest in size but gets correspondingly close supervision: students doing the honours thesis often work directly and consistently with the same academic across the full year rather than a more diffuse supervision arrangement.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Bases of Behaviour, Social Psychology, Research Methods and Statistics I
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Psychopathology, Research Methods and Statistics II
Year 3: Personality and Individual Differences, Psychological Assessment, capstone Research Project, elective in Health or Forensic Psychology
Honours (separate, competitive-entry fourth year): independent thesis with close individual supervision, required for provisional psychologist registration
Delivered on-campus or externally with online-adapted practical and lab components
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
UNE's Bachelor of Science is a flexible, major-driven degree that benefits from the university's genuine research strength in a handful of specific areas: animal genetics and agricultural science given UNE's long history in that space, and environmental and geospatial science given the university's location in the New England tablelands, which functions as a living field laboratory for students studying ecology, geology, or environmental management.

The major list covers the standard science range (biology, chemistry, mathematics, physics, environmental science) plus some options that reflect UNE's specific institutional history, like animal science and geospatial science, majors that a smaller or more generalist science faculty elsewhere might not offer with the same depth.

Field-based units take advantage of the region directly: students in ecology and environmental science majors do fieldwork in the surrounding New England tablelands and gorge country rather than relying purely on simulated data, and the university's rural setting, which can be a drawback for some degrees, is a genuine asset for this one.
curriculum:
Year 1: common core across Biology, Chemistry, Mathematics, and Earth Sciences
Year 2: major selection (Biology, Chemistry, Environmental Science, Animal Science, Geospatial Science, Mathematics), major core subjects begin
Year 3: advanced major electives, field-based units (ecology and environmental majors use the surrounding New England region directly), capstone Science Research Project
Fourth-year Honours available by application for students pursuing research higher degrees
Field trips and practical components embedded across majors reflecting UNE's regional setting
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Social Science with Honours
Bachelor of Urban and Regional Planning
Graduate Certificate in Cybersecurity and Computing
Graduate Diploma in Urban and Regional Planning
Master of Business Administration
description:
UNE's MBA is delivered through the UNE Business School and is squarely aimed at working professionals studying externally. The university doesn't run a full-time residential MBA cohort in the way a capital-city business school might, and the entire program is timetabled around people holding down a job while they study, with trimester-based online units rather than an assumption of daytime campus attendance.

A meaningful proportion of the cohort comes from regional and rural Australia, often in agribusiness, local government, or regional health and education management roles, and electives in agribusiness management and rural enterprise reflect that demand directly. It's a different elective mix than you'd see at an MBA program drawing mostly from metropolitan corporate and finance sectors.

Because UNE has run business education by distance for a long time, the online delivery infrastructure (structured discussion forums, recorded case discussions, group project tools for geographically dispersed teams) is genuinely mature rather than a pandemic-era retrofit, which matters practically for group assignments given that classmates might be scattered across several states and time zones.
curriculum:
Core: Managerial Economics, Financial Management, Strategic Marketing, Organisational Behaviour, Managerial Accounting, Business Analytics
Core continued: Strategic Management, Operations Management
Electives: Agribusiness Management, Rural Enterprise and Innovation, Human Resource Leadership, International Business
Capstone: Strategic Management Project, typically built around the student's own workplace or industry
Delivered fully online across trimesters, structured for working professionals
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree plus at least 3 years of professional work experience, or equivalent significant professional experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Data Science
description:
UNE's Master of Data Science is a newer addition to the university's course list, built to address the same skills gap every Australian university has been chasing over the past several years, but it's delivered with UNE's characteristic flexibility: fully online, structured for working professionals rather than assuming a full-time, on-campus cohort, which suits UNE's traditional student demographic of people studying alongside a job rather than instead of one.

The degree draws heavily on statistics staff from UNE's mathematics and applied statistics groups, which have a longstanding reputation in agricultural and environmental statistics given the university's history. That background shows up in the program's applied, data-heavy assessment style, and in a genuine (if not exclusive) lean toward agricultural, environmental, and regional-economics datasets in capstone project options, rather than the finance and tech-sector case studies a capital-city program might default to.

Entry doesn't require a prior computing degree. Students from a range of quantitative backgrounds (science, commerce, agriculture) are common, and the early units are structured to bring everyone up to a common programming and statistics baseline before the more specialised machine learning and analytics content opens up.
curriculum:
Foundational units (for non-quantitative entrants): Statistical Thinking, Introduction to Programming for Data Science
Core: Data Management and Databases, Statistical Modelling, Machine Learning, Data Visualisation
Electives: Big Data Analytics, Applied Time Series, Spatial Data Analysis (reflecting UNE's agricultural and environmental statistics strength)
Capstone: Data Science Project, often drawn from agricultural, environmental, or regional business datasets
Delivered fully online across trimesters for flexible completion
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Economic and Regional Development
Master of Education (Research)
description:
UNE's Master of Education (Research) is a smaller, more specialised degree than its coursework Master of Education sibling. It's aimed squarely at practising teachers and education professionals wanting to build a genuine research track record, often as a stepping stone toward a PhD or an EdD, rather than a general professional-development credential.

Given UNE's decades of investment in distance and flexible education, a lot of the research topics that graduate from this program are actually about education itself in regional, rural, and remote contexts, such as rural teacher retention, the effectiveness of distance and blended learning models, and small-school pedagogy, areas where UNE's own institutional history gives supervisors direct expertise most education faculties elsewhere simply don't have.

The degree is thesis-heavy from early on, with less coursework padding than a taught master's, and students work closely with an individual supervisor for the bulk of the program. UNE's education research group is modest in size, which in practice means more direct supervisor access than a larger faculty with the same degree spread across many more research students.
curriculum:
Semester 1: Research Design in Education, Advanced Qualitative or Quantitative Methods (student's choice of methodological focus)
Semester 2: Literature Review and Research Proposal development, supervised thesis planning
Semester 3-4: independent thesis research, regular supervisory meetings, progress seminars
Final semester: thesis completion and submission, oral defence/examination
Coursework component is minimal relative to a taught master's; the degree is thesis-driven throughout
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree with honours, or equivalent research experience in education
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Environmental Science and Management
Master of Information Technology
description: The University of New England Master of Information Technology has a strong technical focus for graduates who want to refresh their skills or change careers into IT, and can be entered with no IT background, graduating ready for roles in private industry, government or research. Most students study online across three study periods a year with 24/7 tutor support, though some units include a mandatory on-campus intensive school in Armidale. A Graduate Diploma in Information Technology is available as an early exit. One entry pathway accepts a graduate certificate, graduate diploma or honours degree at AQF level 8 or overseas equivalent in a relevant discipline; applicants may need to demonstrate they meet the English language requirements. Indicative international tuition is around A$33,300 per year. Graduates work across software, systems, data and IT support roles.

name: Master of Laws
description:
UNE's LLM draws a cohort that's noticeably different from a capital-city law school's postgraduate program: a lot of students are practising solicitors in regional and rural firms looking to specialise or requalify, rather than fresh law graduates going straight into a research-oriented master's, and the fully online delivery model is what makes that possible for someone running a small-town legal practice who can't take a year away to study on campus.

The elective bench leans into UNE's practical strengths: agricultural and natural resources law, water law, and property law get more real depth here than at a program without that regional client base to draw case material from, since UNE's law academics maintain active links with rural legal practice and policy work in ways that shape both teaching content and applied research output.

Students can typically choose between a coursework-only pathway and one that includes a research minor-thesis component, which matters for practitioners using the degree mainly for skills upgrading versus those considering an eventual move into legal academia or policy research.
curriculum:
Core: Legal Research Methods, Advanced Legal Theory
Electives (choose a specialisation focus): Agricultural and Natural Resources Law, Water Law, Property Law, Family Law, International Law, Native Title
Coursework pathway: additional electives plus a capstone research paper
Research pathway: reduced coursework load plus an extended minor-thesis component
Delivered fully online, structured for practising solicitors balancing study with legal practice
admission_requirements: A Bachelor of Laws or equivalent legal qualification
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Nursing Practice (Preregistration)
description:
This is UNE's graduate-entry nursing qualification for people who already hold a degree in something else and want to become registered nurses without repeating a full three-year undergraduate program. The compressed structure covers the same registration-standard content as the Bachelor of Nursing but assumes graduate-level academic maturity, so the pace through anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology content in the early units is noticeably faster than an undergraduate-entry program.

Clinical placements run through the same regional New England hospital and health service network as UNE's undergraduate nursing degree, Armidale Rural Referral Hospital and partner regional facilities, giving graduate-entry students the same exposure to rural and regional nursing practice that shapes UNE's whole nursing offering, rather than routing them through a separate, more metropolitan placement network.

Because the cohort already has a prior degree, UNE's program tends to attract a genuinely varied mix of career-changers, former teachers, allied health assistants, people coming out of unrelated science degrees, and the intensity of the compressed timeline means students describe it as demanding in a different way than the undergraduate degree, less about adjusting to university study and more about absorbing clinical content at speed.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, first clinical placement
Trimester 2: Pathophysiology, Pharmacology, Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, extended placement
Trimester 3: Complex Care Nursing, Rural and Remote Health Nursing, Aged Care Nursing, further placement block
Final trimester: capstone Transition to Professional Practice placement, Professional and Ethical Practice
Clinical placements delivered through Armidale Rural Referral Hospital and regional partner facilities to meet AHPRA registration requirements
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a non-nursing discipline; competitive entry with satisfactory National Police Check and immunisation compliance
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (NMBA registration standard)

name: Master of Urban and Regional Planning
Associate Degree in Health [Exit Only Award]
Bachelor of Arts
description: The Bachelor of Arts at the University of Newcastle builds skills in analysing and explaining ideas and their consequences. Students choose from a range of major and minor study areas across the arts, humanities and languages, developing their reading, evaluating and writing into career-based skills for critiquing, curating, communicating and shaping knowledge about people in the world. The degree explores ideas, theories and records of human interaction, and builds advanced knowledge in history, literature, language, politics, society and culture, preparing graduates for varied careers strengthened by their chosen specialisations.

name: Bachelor of Arts / Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
description:
Newcastle Law School runs its combined Arts/Law as a six-year honours program, letting students build a genuine arts major (history, politics, English, whatever they choose) alongside the professional law sequence rather than squeezing electives in around the edges. The law school is smaller than the Group of Eight competitors, which in practice means smaller seminar groups in the later law units and closer contact with individual academics, something the school leans on in its own promotional material and which alumni feedback generally backs up.

The Newcastle Legal Centre gives students access to genuine legal clinic experience: supervised casework for real clients, mostly in areas like tenancy, family violence, and social security, which is a more hands-on clinical legal education offering than a lot of comparable regional programs manage. Newcastle also has a strong environmental and natural resources law research group, unsurprising given the Hunter region's mix of mining, agriculture, and coastal development creates a steady stream of live legal issues on the doorstep.

Graduates need to complete Practical Legal Training after the degree (the JD or PLT year) before admission as a solicitor, same as anywhere else in NSW, but the combined degree's arts component is genuinely substantial rather than a token humanities gloss.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Arts major coursework (history, politics, English, or other approved major) alongside foundational law units — Legal Method, Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law
Years 3-4: Continued arts major units, Property Law, Equity, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Evidence
Years 5-6: Advanced law electives, Corporations Law, Legal clinic placement option (Newcastle Legal Centre), capstone law units, honours thesis or coursework honours component
Practical Legal Training required post-graduation for admission as a solicitor in NSW
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 / ATAR approximately 85-90, combined Arts/Law degree
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science at the University of Newcastle prepares students for careers across a wide range of biomedical fields by developing knowledge of the structure and function of the human body. Students gain hands-on, career-ready skills on campus in a dedicated medical science precinct with specialised laboratory spaces, and learn from active biomedical researchers. The degree provides a strong foundation for roles in research, diagnostics, biotechnology and pharmaceuticals, or for further study in health and medicine.

name: Bachelor of Biotechnology
description: The Bachelor of Biotechnology at the University of Newcastle draws on the biochemical processes and genetic diversity of living organisms to benefit the modern world. The degree covers genetic engineering, pharmaceuticals, and plant and animal science, with recent developments such as high-profile vaccines giving the field new prominence. Students develop laboratory and analytical skills for careers in research, product development and industry across health, agriculture and environmental biotechnology.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Newcastle Business School holds AACSB accreditation, which puts it in a smaller club of Australian business schools than the AQF-only crowd, and the Bachelor of Business leans on that with a first-year "business challenge" unit that has students working in cross-major teams on briefs set by local firms in the Hunter region, a lot of hospitality, mining services, and logistics companies rather than the finance-sector case studies that dominate at the Group of Eight schools.

Majors run from the standard accounting and marketing through to a sport business major that draws on Newcastle's genuine sporting culture (the Knights NRL club, Newcastle Jets) for placements and guest lectures, which is a distinctive offering most other regional business schools don't have. Students can also take a double major, and the degree has a well-used study-abroad exchange list skewed toward partner universities in Germany and the Netherlands, a legacy of the business school's earlier European exchange partnerships.

Class sizes in first year are large lecture-plus-tutorial format at Callaghan, but by third year most students are in seminar-sized major electives, and the degree includes an optional (unpaid but credit-bearing) 100-hour professional placement unit that many students use to lock in a graduate job before finishing.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Business, Accounting for Business, Economics for Business, Business Statistics, Business Law, Marketing Principles, Business Challenge (team project unit), Elective
Year 2: Major units begin (choose from Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management, Human Resource Management, International Business, Sport Business, Tourism), Organisational Behaviour, Business Analytics, Electives
Year 3: Advanced major units, Strategic Management, optional Professional Placement (100 hours), Capstone Business Project, Electives
Study abroad exchange available in Year 2 or 3 (partner universities include several in Germany and the Netherlands)
