admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 / ATAR approximately 65-75; choice of up to two majors from accounting, finance, marketing, management, HR and international business
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Business Analytics
description: The Bachelor of Business Analytics at the University of Newcastle develops the data skills needed to implement and oversee data-driven business decisions as industry demand for analytics specialists grows. Students learn to use artificial intelligence methodologies to analyse data and inform evidence-based decision-making and strategic direction. The degree combines statistics, data management, visualisation and business knowledge, preparing graduates for careers as business analysts and data specialists across a wide range of organisations.

name: Bachelor of Chemical Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Chemical Engineering (Honours) at the University of Newcastle trains engineers to apply the fundamental principles of physics and chemistry, along with specialised disciplines such as bio and nanotechnology, to key problems in the community. Students learn to analyse and design processes, plants and control systems for productivity, safety and sustainability. Chemical engineering is about designing efficient processes to produce, use and transform materials and energy, and graduates work across a vast range of industries including energy, resources, pharmaceuticals and manufacturing.

name: Bachelor of Civil Engineering (Honours)
description:
Newcastle earned its engineering reputation the old way, as a steel and coal town where the university's engineering faculty grew up alongside heavy industry, and the civil program still has that industrial-region character: final-year projects regularly come from Hunter Valley coal infrastructure, port and rail logistics (the Port of Newcastle is the world's largest coal export port), and increasingly renewable energy and offshore wind projects as the region transitions.

The Bachelor of Civil Engineering (Honours) is Engineers Australia accredited, four years, with the honours component built in rather than a separate add-on year. That structure suits students planning to go straight into industry with a Washington Accord-recognised qualification. Students complete a mandatory 12 weeks of Professional Engineering Practice (industry placement) before graduating, and Newcastle's placement office leans hard on its Hunter region industry ties to place students with firms like local engineering consultancies, Ausgrid, and Hunter Water rather than leaving it entirely to students to source their own.

Final-year thesis projects are supervised individually and often tie into the university's structural, geotechnical, or water engineering research groups, with some students publishing or presenting findings at student engineering conferences.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mechanics, Mathematics for Engineers A and B, Engineering Materials, Introduction to Engineering Design, Computer-Aided Engineering
Year 2: Structural Analysis, Fluid Mechanics, Geotechnical Engineering, Surveying, Engineering Mathematics, Construction Materials and Methods
Year 3: Structural Design (steel and concrete), Water Engineering, Transportation Engineering, Engineering Management, Professional Engineering Practice (12-week industry placement)
Year 4 (Honours): Advanced Structural Design, Geotechnical Design, Engineering Thesis (individual research project), technical electives
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 / ATAR approximately 75-85, including Mathematics Advanced recommended
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Climate Science and Adaptation
Bachelor of Coastal and Marine Science
description: The Bachelor of Coastal and Marine Science at the University of Newcastle has students learn from experts in marine, coastal and ecological fields, gaining practical skills to address issues such as climate change, pollution and urbanisation. Students engage with contemporary issues in the marine environment from day one, through skills-based courses and extensive fieldwork opportunities, developing an understanding of ecological, physical, conservation, societal and management issues. Graduates work in marine research, conservation, environmental consulting and coastal management.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description: The Bachelor of Commerce at the University of Newcastle is a practical and flexible degree whose core courses give a thorough overview of business and commerce environments. Students major in two commerce areas, such as accounting and finance, or choose a second major in a business area such as marketing, graduating in three years as a competitive candidate. The degree builds practical skills employers value, including problem-solving and critical thinking, to help students move smoothly from the classroom to the workplace.

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description: The Bachelor of Computer Science at the University of Newcastle gives students the technical foundation behind modern digital systems, from artificial intelligence and cyber security to software development. Students develop strong skills in algorithms, data structures and system design while building the problem-solving capability employers value in a rapidly evolving digital economy. Students can specialise in Artificial Intelligence, Cyber Security or Software Development, learning how complex systems are designed, built and improved.

name: Bachelor of Computer Systems Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Computer Systems Engineering (Honours) at the University of Newcastle teaches students to use digital and computing technologies to solve problems in industrial systems, combining creativity with advanced technology. Students develop both hardware and software for electronic, computer and ICT systems, skills essential in rapidly growing fields such as the Internet of Things, autonomous vehicles and machine learning. Graduates have a unique skill set spanning hardware design, software design and system architecture.

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description: The Bachelor of Criminology at the University of Newcastle is the study of crime, its causes, and its effects on individuals and society, exploring the social, cultural, biological and psychological factors that contribute to criminal behaviour. Students examine why crimes occur, the impact on victims, and the roles of criminal justice institutions in preventing and responding to crime. This practical, hands-on degree qualifies graduates to work in criminal justice and allied fields such as corrections, policy and crime prevention.

name: Bachelor of Data Science
description: The Bachelor of Applied Data Science at the University of Newcastle gives students a competitive edge in the job market by combining a primary discipline with in-demand data skills through one extra year of study and two degrees. Students from varied backgrounds learn data wrangling and visualisation, statistical analysis, machine learning and the skills to uncover insights, solve complex problems and make data-driven decisions in their field. Data is reshaping every industry, and graduates apply these skills across sectors.

name: Bachelor of Design (Architecture)
description: The Bachelor of Design (Architecture) at the University of Newcastle teaches students to design spaces that shape communities. From day one, students work in a collaborative studio with 24/7 access, creating and developing their ideas alongside peers. Through hands-on, project-based learning, students tackle real-world challenges, build a strong design portfolio and explore how architecture responds to climate challenges and supports diverse communities, providing a foundation for the Master of Architecture.

name: Bachelor of Development Studies
description: The Bachelor of Development Studies at the University of Newcastle provides the opportunity to study the causes and consequences of unequal development, addressing issues such as poverty, inequality, political instability and environmental sustainability. It is the only development studies program in Australia to include economics and Aboriginal studies as core courses, and students focus on key global issues in local, national and international contexts. Graduates work in government, international agencies, non-government organisations and community development.

name: Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood and Primary)
Bachelor of Education Studies [Exit Only Award]
Bachelor of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Electrical and Electronic Engineering (Honours) at the University of Newcastle trains engineers to design and build essential devices and equipment integral to modern life, including systems for electricity generation and distribution, electronic automation and control, and the transmission and reception of electromagnetic signals. Students develop the technical knowledge and problem-solving skills to tackle major global challenges, and graduates work across power, electronics, communications, automation and renewable energy industries.

name: Bachelor of Environmental Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Environmental Engineering (Honours) at the University of Newcastle trains engineers to combine knowledge of chemistry, geomechanics, hydrology and land surface processes to solve major environmental challenges. Graduates might help adapt infrastructure and ecosystems to climate change, rehabilitate land damaged by mining, or work on the clean-up of oil spills that threaten ecosystems. The degree develops the technical and design skills to protect and restore the natural environment while supporting sustainable development.

name: Bachelor of Environmental Science and Management
description: The Bachelor of Environmental Science and Management at the University of Newcastle is for students passionate about science and sustainability who want to help solve environmental problems. Students explore the science behind human-induced impacts and learn to understand and combat critical issues placing strain on the earth's natural resources, such as climate change and the biodiversity crisis. The degree combines scientific study with management-based experience, preparing graduates for roles in environmental consulting, government, conservation and resource management.

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sports Science (Honours)
Bachelor of Food Science and Human Nutrition
description: The Bachelor of Food Science and Human Nutrition at the University of Newcastle prepares students to meet new challenges in food production while demand for sustainable and healthy choices grows. Students learn to assess how novel ingredients and trends impact health, driven by curiosity and innovative thinking. Food and beverage processing is Australia's largest manufacturing industry, and the degree opens opportunities for food and nutrition scientists in areas including product development, quality assurance and research.

name: Bachelor of Global Indigenous Studies
description: The Bachelor of Global Indigenous Studies at the University of Newcastle, offered through the Wollotuka Institute, prepares students to challenge and develop policy affecting social justice in the Indigenous workforce and community. Students learn to engage with Indigenous knowledge systems to respond to ecological, social and economic challenges, and to work with local and global communities. The degree develops skills in social innovation, cultural competence and multimedia capabilities for a range of careers addressing pressing global issues.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description: The University of Newcastle Bachelor of Information Technology has three majors: ICT Developer, covering software, web, mobile and game development; ICT Business Analyst, covering business, data, systems and business intelligence analysis; and ICT Security Specialist, covering cyber security analysis, information security and network security. Students undertake a career-ready industry placement for hands-on experience and complete a major team IT project, ideally developed with an industry partner. Admission usually requires a senior secondary qualification similar to the NSW Higher School Certificate, and applicants whose first language is not English must meet the University English proficiency requirement. Indicative international tuition is around A$46,200 per year. Career paths depend on the major, spanning software development, business analysis and cyber security roles across many industries.

name: Bachelor of Mathematics (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Mathematics (Honours) at the University of Newcastle develops essential skills in logic, mathematical modelling, experimental design and data analysis. Mathematics is the language of science and technology and underpins many everyday systems and innovations. As artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies continue to grow, organisations need people who can interpret data, build models and support complex decision-making. The degree suits students who enjoy analysing problems and thinking critically, and opens doors to a wide range of careers.

name: Bachelor of Mechanical Engineering (Honours)
description:
Mechanical engineering at Newcastle shares the same industrial-region orientation as civil: a lot of the applied research and industry placement pipeline runs through mining equipment, heavy manufacturing, and increasingly renewable energy and hydrogen projects tied to the Hunter's economic transition away from coal. The program is Engineers Australia accredited and runs four years with honours embedded, following the Washington Accord structure that's recognised for professional registration overseas as well as in Australia.

Students get hands-on lab time that's unusually generous for a mid-sized engineering school. Newcastle's engineering labs include a combustion research facility and manufacturing workshops that undergraduates actually use rather than just observe, and final-year thesis topics often come directly out of the mechanical engineering research groups working on things like solar thermal energy and advanced manufacturing.

The mandatory 12-week Professional Engineering Practice placement functions as a genuine foot in the door for a lot of students. Hunter Valley mining services companies and manufacturers recruit directly out of the placement cohort, and it's common for students to receive a graduate offer from their placement employer before finishing their thesis year.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mechanics, Mathematics for Engineers A and B, Engineering Materials, Thermodynamics, Introduction to Engineering Design
Year 2: Fluid Mechanics, Dynamics of Machines, Manufacturing Processes, Electrical Engineering for Mechanical Engineers, Mathematics for Engineers C
Year 3: Heat Transfer, Machine Design, Control Systems, Mechanics of Solids, Professional Engineering Practice (12-week industry placement)
Year 4 (Honours): Advanced Design Project, Mechanical Vibrations, Engineering Thesis, technical electives (options include energy systems, mechatronics)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 / ATAR approximately 75-85, Mathematics Advanced strongly recommended
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Mechatronics Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Mechatronics Engineering (Honours) at the University of Newcastle brings together electrical, computer and mechanical technologies to create new solutions to industrial problems. Students study a diverse range of courses including technical design, automation and the operational performance of electromechanical systems. Mechatronics engineers work in industries such as defence, advanced manufacturing, mining and health, and graduates are prepared to design and build the robotic and automated systems that these sectors rely on.

name: Bachelor of Mechatronics Engineering (Honours)/B Electrical & Electronic Engineering (Honours)
Bachelor of Media and Communication
description: The Bachelor of Media and Communication at the University of Newcastle develops the skills to produce engaging, thought-provoking work in the current communication landscape. Course options prepare students to craft stories and create content for different audiences and contexts, including social media, radio, podcasting, broadcast, streaming and news platforms. Students can tailor their skills to areas of interest such as documentary and filmmaking, podcasting, multiplatform journalism and social media, graduating ready for diverse media and communication industries.

name: Bachelor of Medical Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Medical Engineering (Honours) at the University of Newcastle prepares students to make medical treatment more effective, efficient, safer and affordable. Medical engineering spans medicine, biomedical science and engineering, and graduates take technology and create better solutions for health and wellbeing. Students learn to improve human health through the development of medical devices and systems, and graduates work with healthcare providers, medical technology companies and research institutions.

name: Bachelor of Medical Radiation Science (Honours) (Diagnostic Radiography)
Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine (Joint Medical Program)
description:
The Joint Medical Program is run jointly with the University of New England, and it's the reason Newcastle's medical school gets cited in medical education literature well beyond Australia. It was one of the first programs in the country built entirely around problem-based learning, adapted from the McMaster model, rather than bolting PBL onto a traditional lecture-based curriculum. Students spend the first two preclinical years working in small PBL tutorial groups of eight to nine, using clinical case scenarios to drive their own learning of basic and clinical sciences rather than starting from anatomy and biochem lectures.

The five-year combined Bachelor of Medical Science / Doctor of Medicine structure means students exit with an accredited MD, and entry runs through UAC plus the UCAT (or GAMSAT for graduate-entry places) and an interview, with a meaningful chunk of places reserved for rural background and Indigenous applicants, reflecting the program's explicit rural workforce mission: a large share of clinical years are spent at rural and regional clinical schools in Tamworth, Port Macquarie, Taree, and other New England and mid-north-coast sites rather than concentrated in a single teaching hospital.

Because of that rural distribution model, students don't all have the same clinical experience: some spend years 3-5 largely in Newcastle at John Hunter Hospital, others are placed for extended rural terms. The university markets this as a strength (genuine rural medicine exposure), but prospective students should weigh it if they're set on a particular clinical environment.
curriculum:
Years 1-2 (preclinical): Problem-based learning tutorials in small groups, Personal and Professional Development strand, Clinical Skills, Population Medicine, integrated basic sciences delivered through case-based learning rather than standalone subjects
Years 3-4: Clinical rotations across major teaching hospitals and rural clinical schools (Tamworth, Port Macquarie, Taree, Newcastle), core rotations in medicine, surgery, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynaecology, paediatrics, general practice
Year 5: Sub-internship style clinical placements, electives (including option for overseas elective term), preparation for internship
Selection: UAC application, UCAT or GAMSAT (graduate entry stream), interview; reserved places for rural background and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants
admission_requirements: ATAR approximately 90+, UCAT score, and interview; delivered jointly with University of New England
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0

name: Bachelor of Music and Performing Arts
description: The Bachelor of Music and Performing Arts at the University of Newcastle offers a future within the evolving creative arts industries, helping students enhance their skills and fast-track their creative career through practical and creative learning. Practitioners in the creative and performing arts need to be collaborative, combining technical skills in creative thinking, design, music, performance, production and writing. The program develops the professional skills to work across the music and performing arts sector.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Newcastle was one of the first Australian universities to move nursing education fully into the tertiary sector back in the 1970s hospital-training-to-degree transition, and the School of Nursing and Midwifery still trades on that history: it's consistently ranked among the top nursing schools in the country, and sends students into clinical placement blocks from first year rather than holding placements back to the later years the way some competitor programs do.

Clinical placement hours (a minimum of 800, in line with NMBA requirements) are spread across the Hunter New England Local Health District, which is one of the largest health networks in NSW and gives students exposure to everything from John Hunter Hospital's tertiary trauma unit to small rural placements further out in the Hunter Valley and New England region. It's a genuine mix of urban and rural nursing experience that's harder to get in a Sydney-based program competing for the same city hospital placement spots as five other universities.

The degree can be taken at Callaghan, at the Central Coast (Ourimbah) campus, or partly online for the theory components, and there's a well-worn pathway from here into UON's postgraduate nurse practitioner and midwifery programs for graduates who want to specialise later.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Structure and Function, Foundations of Nursing Practice, Introduction to Professional Nursing, Psychology for Health Professionals, first clinical placement block
Year 2: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology, Mental Health Nursing, Acute Care Nursing, Nursing Research and Evidence-Based Practice, clinical placements in acute and community settings
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Aged Care and Chronic Disease, Leadership in Nursing, Transition to Professional Practice, final clinical placement block (extended immersion)
Minimum 800 clinical placement hours across Hunter New England Local Health District and partner sites, required for NMBA registration eligibility
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 / ATAR approximately 65-75; adjustment factors and portfolio pathways available
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall (no band below 7.0) or equivalent, reflecting nursing registration standards

name: Bachelor of Nutrition and Dietetics (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Nutrition and Dietetics (Honours) at the University of Newcastle prepares students to shape a healthier future for the community, as demand grows for graduates with specialised knowledge amid rising diet-related diseases such as heart disease, diabetes and obesity. Students have access to experienced researchers and educators and learn to use the latest evidence to manage patient health, discovering the science of human nutrition. Graduates work as accredited practising dietitians across clinical, community and food industry settings.

name: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours) at the University of Newcastle trains occupational therapists who work with people and communities to help them overcome challenges and participate in everyday activities. Occupational therapists promote health and wellbeing by enabling people to take part in activities important to them, such as caring for themselves and others, working, studying and social activities. Students learn to work with children to reach developmental milestones and to support recovery and inclusion, graduating ready for practice across health and community settings.

name: Bachelor of Oral Health Therapy
description: The Bachelor of Oral Health Therapy at the University of Newcastle has students graduate with dual qualifications in dental hygiene and dental therapy. The degree has a strong focus on disease prevention, simulation-based training and an advanced restorative scope. Students learn from professional dental practitioners and develop the skills to perform preventive and minor restorative tasks, educate their community and apply emerging methods for caring for the oral health of children and adults.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) at the University of Newcastle prepares students to become future-ready pharmacists, frontline healthcare professionals who work to improve medication safety, patient outcomes and community health. Throughout the degree students work directly with patients, healthcare teams and communities, learning to counsel people on the safe and effective use of medicines, help manage chronic disease, advise on common health conditions and contribute to preventive care.

name: Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours) at the University of Newcastle prepares students to work across many health settings and complex clinical problems involving the musculoskeletal, neurological and cardiorespiratory systems. The program integrates the clinical and basic sciences with a focus on evidence-based physiotherapy practice, using case-based learning with a strong interdisciplinary focus. Students gain hands-on experience through clinical placements and develop the communication and interpersonal skills needed to work one on one with patients.

name: Bachelor of Podiatric Medicine (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Podiatric Medicine (Honours) at the University of Newcastle is a four-year degree that helps people stay mobile, independent and pain-free. Podiatry is identified as a national skills shortage, and industry-informed training and strong clinical networks ensure graduates are job-ready. The degree equips students with the knowledge and clinical skills to meet the prescribing competencies required for registration with the Podiatry Board of Australia, preparing graduates for advanced clinical practice.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description:
Newcastle's Bachelor of Psychological Science is APAC accredited, which is the qualification students actually need if they want a clear run at postgraduate clinical training later. It's the first of the standard three-plus-two (or three-plus-one-plus-master's) pathway toward registration as a psychologist in Australia, so most students here are aiming past the bachelor's degree from day one rather than treating it as a terminal qualification.

The school runs its own on-campus research clinic and has active research groups in areas like addiction and cognitive neuroscience, giving students earlier access to research participation and honours supervision than at some larger, more anonymous psychology schools. Newcastle also has a notable strength in health and behavioural science more broadly, given the university's medical school and public health programs sit close by, so cross-disciplinary units and guest teaching from medical faculty aren't unusual.

Fourth-year (honours) places are competitive and GPA-gated, which students are told about clearly from second year, and the honours thesis is individually supervised with a genuine expectation of a publishable-quality piece of research by the end.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology (Individual and Social Behaviour, Biological and Cognitive Processes), Statistics for Psychology, Academic and Research Skills
Year 2: Developmental Psychology, Social Psychology, Cognitive Psychology, Biological Psychology, Research Methods and Design
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Personality, Psychological Assessment, Advanced Research Methods, electives
Year 4 (Honours, competitive entry): Advanced statistics, supervised empirical thesis, seminar units in specialised areas
APAC accredited — pathway toward provisional registration and postgraduate clinical training
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 / ATAR approximately 70-80
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Renewable Energy Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Renewable Energy Engineering (Honours) at the University of Newcastle prepares engineers with the specialised skills to lead the transition to a renewable energy economy, one of the biggest challenges humankind faces. Renewable energy engineering is a multidisciplinary field dedicated to developing, designing and operating systems and processes that harness energy from sustainable sources. Graduates work across solar, wind, energy storage, grid integration and clean technology industries.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
The Bachelor of Science at Newcastle is a flexible-major degree rather than a fixed program, letting students combine majors across biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology, and mathematics, which suits the university's genuine strength in earth and environmental sciences. Newcastle sits on the doorstep of the Hunter Valley's coal geology and coastal ecosystems, and a lot of the geology and environmental science teaching draws directly on that landscape for fieldwork rather than relying on textbook case studies from elsewhere.

Marine and coastal ecology is a particular strength given the campus's proximity to the coast, and students in relevant majors get regular field trips to sites like Port Stephens and the Hunter Wetlands rather than lab-only coursework. The degree also has a well-established pathway into UON's science honours year for students wanting to go on to research higher degrees, with placement into a research group typically arranged in third year based on a student's chosen major and demonstrated interest.

Because the degree is major-driven rather than following one fixed sequence, the actual course load varies a lot between, say, a physics-heavy student and one majoring in environmental science. The university's course advisors handle this individually rather than through a single rigid structure, which is worth knowing before assuming a uniform curriculum.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundational units across chosen majors (e.g. Chemistry 1, Biology 1, Physics 1, Mathematics 1, Earth Sciences 1), Introduction to Scientific Practice
Year 2: Major-specific core units (two majors typically selected), Research Methods in Science, electives
Year 3: Advanced major units, Field Studies (for environmental science, geology, marine biology majors), Capstone Science Project
Optional Year 4: Honours year with individual research thesis, entry based on GPA and available supervision
Common majors: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Environmental Science, Geology, Marine Science, Mathematics
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 / ATAR approximately 65-75, broad choice of science majors
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Social Science
description: The Bachelor of Social Science at the University of Newcastle is the study of social systems, institutions and cultures, equipping students to understand and analyse the social dynamics of the world around them and develop practical solutions to create positive change. Students learn to analyse and address key social issues and inequalities, using practical strategies and evidence-based methods to propose solutions that create better outcomes. The degree lets students pursue their interests across a range of social science disciplines.

name: Bachelor of Social Work (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Social Work (Honours) at the University of Newcastle is a purpose-driven degree grounded in social justice, human rights and collective wellbeing. Students learn how to support individuals and families while challenging the social, political and economic structures that shape people's lives, working alongside people experiencing marginalisation. Students analyse the structural forces behind poverty, gender inequality, racism and colonialism, and the accredited degree prepares graduates for professional social work practice.

name: Bachelor of Software Engineering (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Software Engineering (Honours) at the University of Newcastle focuses on how complex digital systems are designed, built and maintained, teaching students to develop reliable software that powers everyday technology from mobile apps and online banking to enterprise platforms and digital infrastructure. As artificial intelligence, cloud computing and connected systems grow, organisations need engineers who can build secure and scalable technology, and students develop strong skills in programming, system design and software engineering practice.

name: Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Speech Pathology (Honours) at the University of Newcastle is described as the most comprehensive degree of its kind in Australia, with highly specialised training, placements and flexible outcomes. Speech pathologists assess and treat children and adults with communication and swallowing needs, including developmental and acquired speech and language disorders, cognitive communication disorders, voice disorders and stuttering. Graduates are prepared for practice across health, education and community settings.

name: Bachelor of Surveying (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Surveying (Honours) at the University of Newcastle combines surveying expertise with emerging technologies in spatial data science, satellite positioning, remote sensing and digital mapping. Surveyors help plan, measure and manage the world around us, from infrastructure and land development to environmental monitoring and digital construction. Students learn how advanced technologies are used to capture, analyse and manage spatial data, and graduates work as licensed surveyors and spatial professionals.

name: Bachelor of Tourism, Hospitality and Events
description: The Bachelor of Tourism, Hospitality and Events at the University of Newcastle helps students transform a passion for experiences and travel into leadership of sustainable futures in tourism, hospitality and events. Students develop skills in experience design, project management, marketing strategy, stakeholder engagement, destination development, digital innovation and visitor management, learning through industry projects, work placements and internationally focused experiences. They also explore the environmental, social, cultural and economic impacts of the sector.

name: Bachelor of Visual Communication Design
description: The Bachelor of Visual Communication Design at the University of Newcastle develops creative skills in graphic communication, animation, illustration and interaction design. Students work in well-equipped studios, labs and maker spaces, guided by industry experts through practical, real-world tasks with a hands-on, future focus. Graduates leave with a portfolio reflecting their creative vision and diverse visual communication skills, ready for careers in the design industries.

name: Diploma in Languages
description: The Diploma in Languages at the University of Newcastle develops proficiency in another language alongside an undergraduate degree or as a sole enrolment. Language skills open doors to diverse careers involving travel, overseas postings and teaching, as well as opportunities in sectors with foreign language clients, markets and stakeholders. Students can study a range of languages including Australian Sign Language, Chinese, French, Indonesian and Japanese, learning to speak, read and write the chosen language.

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Research) by Prior Publication (High Cost)
Graduate Certificate in Business Administration
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business Administration at the University of Newcastle is a first step to expanding career opportunities, improving foundational skills in people and organisational management. Content focuses on advanced management capabilities that apply to organisations of all sizes across the public, private and not-for-profit sectors. Students can attend campus or study through a flexible online program, learning from experienced lecturers with industry connections, and can use the certificate as a pathway into further postgraduate management study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Clinical Epidemiology
description: The Graduate Certificate in Clinical Epidemiology at the University of Newcastle introduces the fundamental principles of clinical epidemiology and basic research skills. Students learn how to apply the principles of epidemiology and biostatistics to improve their clinical decision-making, graduating with an understanding of clinical and population-based health problems. The program offers flexible full-time and part-time study, and studies count towards continuing professional development points for clinicians.

name: Graduate Certificate in Disaster Risk and Resilience
description: The Graduate Certificate in Disaster Risk and Resilience at the University of Newcastle builds the essential skills and knowledge to work in disaster risk reduction and management as the frequency and intensity of disasters and other crises increase worldwide. With flexible study options, it suits professionals seeking to advance their careers in disaster management, policy development, community resilience and related fields, and can serve as a pathway into the master degree.

name: Graduate Certificate in Education
description: The Graduate Certificate in Education at the University of Newcastle is for practising teachers and educators looking to deepen their understanding of broader education issues. Students enhance their current skills, connect with the latest industry developments and research, and move beyond the classroom to examine system-level challenges. By improving their professional knowledge, students can fast-track their career and increase their employability, supported by flexible study options and international recognition.

name: Graduate Certificate in Fintech
description: The Graduate Certificate in Fintech at the University of Newcastle equips students with fundamental financial knowledge, analytical skills and digital capabilities to navigate the rapidly evolving finance landscape. The program provides a nexus between traditional financial knowledge and transformative digital technologies, and can serve as a foundation for further study in fintech or a career in the digital finance sector.

name: Graduate Certificate in Health Economics, Management and Policy
Graduate Certificate in Health Management and Policy
description: The Graduate Certificate in Health Management and Policy at the University of Newcastle can be completed in as little as six months and prepares graduates to become future health leaders. The program develops an understanding of the broader context of the health sector, preparing students to navigate complexities such as digital health, personalised medicine, and big data and analytics. Students learn from international leaders and industry experts, and the certificate can lead into the master degree.

name: Graduate Certificate in Human and Social Services
description: The Graduate Certificate in Human and Social Services at the University of Newcastle is a pathway to the Master of Social Work (Qualifying) for students interested in becoming qualified social workers who hold a bachelor's degree in an unrelated field. Students who have completed four social and behavioural sciences courses in their undergraduate degree are eligible for admission to the Master of Social Work (Qualifying) in the following semester upon completing this certificate.

name: Graduate Certificate in Human Resource Management
description: The Graduate Certificate in Human Resource Management at the University of Newcastle equips graduates with the essential knowledge and skills to launch or advance a career in human resource management. With HR skills ranking among the most critical areas of skill shortage for Australian businesses, the program helps students build expertise in a high-demand field. Study options are flexible: fully online, face-to-face at NUspace in the Newcastle CBD, or a blended combination of both.

name: Graduate Certificate in Information Technology
description: The Graduate Certificate in Information Technology at the University of Newcastle helps students enhance their career opportunities within the IT industry and develop the analytical skills essential to organisations adopting new technologies or processes. Students explore areas such as information systems, software engineering, multimedia or telecommunications, developing a solid foundation in relevant technologies and theoretical concepts. Different entry levels are offered based on previous experience, from foundational IT skills to advanced study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Laboratory Medicine
description: The Graduate Certificate in Laboratory Medicine at the University of Newcastle introduces laboratory medicine with an emphasis on practical laboratory skills that transfer to a modern pathology laboratory. It is designed for graduates of biology, biotechnology, biomedical science or related degrees interested in a career in diagnostic pathology. Students gain practical experience with the latest advances in diagnostic medicine and can progress into the graduate diploma or master degree.

name: Graduate Certificate in Marketing and Digital Strategy
description: The Graduate Certificate in Marketing and Digital Strategy at the University of Newcastle enhances students' strategic capabilities in the marketing field, a fast-changing and demanding business function. The program equips students with essential skills for evolving business sectors, blending marketing principles with advanced digital strategies and providing a foundation in marketing theory covering strategy, consumer psychology and behaviour, and digital marketing.

name: Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting
description: The Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting at the University of Newcastle is a pathway to a career in accounting for students with a degree in a field other than accounting. A career in accounting offers challenging, rewarding and versatile opportunities, and businesses value the superior analytical skills that accounting develops. The program provides an introduction to accounting concepts and procedures and can lead into the graduate diploma or master degree.

name: Graduate Certificate in Social Change and Development
description: The Graduate Certificate in Social Change and Development at the University of Newcastle equips students with foundational knowledge to work in social change and development. It suits people who want to work in the professional service of others. Students learn about the key areas of social change through theoretical and practical coursework, and develop an understanding of the implications of social and political changes at a global level, preparing them for careers in community and international development.

name: Graduate Certificate in Sports Analytics
description: The Graduate Certificate in Sports Analytics at the University of Newcastle provides the skills and knowledge essential to measuring and evaluating sport performance through data analysis. Focusing on practical applications and case studies from the sports industry, students learn how to effectively and ethically use data to make informed decisions, building a foundation for careers in performance analysis and sports business or for further study.

name: Graduate Diploma in Psychological Science
description: The Graduate Diploma in Psychological Science at the University of Newcastle is an alternative pathway into psychology, designed for graduates from any discipline and requiring no prior background in the field. Students can study full-time and complete the program in as little as one year, developing foundational skills in key areas of psychology. It suits people looking to change careers, build psychological knowledge to support their current role, or pursue further study in psychology.

name: Juris Doctor
description:
Newcastle's JD is the standard graduate-entry law degree for people with a non-law bachelor's wanting to qualify for legal practice, and the program's selling point is scale: small cohorts mean JD students get taught by the same academics teaching the undergraduate combined degrees, not a separated graduate-only faculty, and the Newcastle Legal Centre clinical placement option is open to JD students as well as undergrads.

Most JD students are career-changers in their late twenties to forties, and Newcastle's JD timetabling (with some units offered in intensive or evening formats) reflects that. It's noticeably more accommodating of students working full time than a lot of the fully daytime-timetabled JDs at bigger city law schools. The program covers the full set of "Priestley 11" core subjects required for admission in Australia, plus electives in areas like environmental and resources law where Newcastle's research strength is genuine given the Hunter region's mining and energy industry.

Graduates still need to complete Practical Legal Training before seeking admission as a solicitor, and the JD itself typically runs three years full-time.
curriculum:
Year 1: Legal Method and Reasoning, Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, Legal Research and Writing
Year 2: Equity and Trusts, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Corporations Law, Evidence, electives
Year 3: Civil and Criminal Procedure, Professional Responsibility and Ethics, capstone units, electives (options include Environmental and Resources Law, given regional relevance)
Covers Priestley 11 core subjects required for admission to legal practice in Australia; Practical Legal Training required post-graduation
admission_requirements: Completed bachelors degree in any discipline; non-law backgrounds welcome
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Master of Architecture
description: The Master of Architecture at the University of Newcastle is grounded and future-focused, preparing students for professional practice and the next step towards becoming a registered architect. The program is shaped by a commitment to Caring for Country and a focus on social and ecological responsibility. Students develop their own approach to architecture through design-led studio learning that engages with real-world challenges and communities, spending more time in the studio than any other NSW program.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Newcastle's MBA runs through the AACSB-accredited Newcastle Business School and is pitched squarely at working professionals. Most units are delivered in intensive block or evening/weekend format rather than assuming students can attend daytime classes, and the cohort skews toward regional NSW managers and public sector employees rather than the international-student-heavy MBA cohorts common at city business schools.

The program includes a capstone strategy consulting project where student teams work with a real regional organisation on an actual business problem, often drawing on the Hunter region's mix of health, mining services, manufacturing, and increasingly renewable energy employers for project partners, a genuinely local flavour compared to generic case-study capstones. Students can also tailor the degree with electives toward specific interests like health management, given the strong health-sector presence in the region through Hunter New England Health and the university's own medical faculty.

Entry typically requires several years of professional work experience alongside an undergraduate degree, consistent with most AACSB MBA admission standards, and the program can be completed part-time over a longer period for students not wanting to step away from full-time work.
curriculum:
Core units: Accounting for Managers, Managerial Economics, Marketing Management, Organisational Behaviour and Leadership, Strategic Management, Corporate Finance, Operations and Supply Chain Management, Business Analytics
Electives: choose from streams including Health Management, Human Resource Management, International Business, Innovation and Entrepreneurship
Capstone: Strategic Management Consulting Project (team-based, real client brief, often with a Hunter region organisation)
Delivery: intensive block and evening/weekend formats to suit working professionals; part-time completion available
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline plus 2+ years relevant work experience preferred
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Business Psychology
description: The Master of Business Psychology at the University of Newcastle is for graduates seeking to advance their leadership and management skills using insights from psychological science. Designed for graduates from a wide range of backgrounds, not limited to psychology qualifications, the program enhances understanding of human psychology across workplace contexts and provides novel, evidence-based leadership skills and insights for understanding, working within, and leading organisations.

name: Master of Clinical Epidemiology
description: The Master of Clinical Epidemiology at the University of Newcastle teaches students how to use epidemiologic methods to conduct health care research. Students learn to apply the principles of epidemiology and biostatistics, apply theoretical frameworks and develop a research study protocol. Graduates are ready to work in clinical epidemiology and healthcare, and studies count towards continuing professional development points for clinicians, with credit available for prior learning.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: The Master of Clinical Psychology at the University of Newcastle is a professional qualification for those who wish to practise as a clinical psychologist. The program offers expert supervision in the university psychology clinic and in local health care and community settings, giving students the skills to work in the assessment, diagnosis and treatment of a wide range of psychological disorders across the lifespan, and to apply advanced knowledge, principles and methods to practice.

name: Master of Cyber Security
description: The University of Newcastle Master of Cyber Security offers two specialisations, including a Cyber Security Analyst stream that emphasises the human dimensions of cyber security, cyber crime and the consequences of security breaches. Coursework spans data, system and network security, security attack analysis and mitigation, human factors, and elements of law, psychology and criminology. Students complete a hands-on industry project across two semesters, using industry-leading cyber security labs and taking part in hackathons and real application development in a controlled environment. A Graduate Certificate in Cyber Security is available as a pathway into the masters. International students must meet the University English proficiency requirement. Indicative international tuition is around A$49,400 per year. Graduates work as cyber security analysts and ICT security specialists across many sectors.

name: Master of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
description: The University of Newcastle's Master of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence is a two-year degree designed for both experienced professionals and people new to the field. It merges data science fundamentals, including data processing, visualisation and predictive modelling, with machine learning and Big Data technologies for storing and analysing large structured and unstructured datasets. Students choose one of two specialisations, Computational Intelligence or Health Data Analysis, and complete an industry or research project. Graduates work as data scientists, machine learning engineers, data analysts and analytics consultants across health, finance, government and technology. Indicative international tuition is around A$47,700 per year.

name: Master of Disaster Resilience and Sustainable Development
Master of Disaster Risk and Resilience
description: The Master of Disaster Risk and Resilience at the University of Newcastle equips graduates from diverse backgrounds with resilience and sustainable development skills to help build a more resilient future. Students learn to anticipate and reduce disaster risks and to handle the impacts of extreme events, so that organisations can mitigate disaster risks while protecting lives and revenue. Graduates work in disaster management, policy development and community resilience roles.

name: Master of Education
description: The Master of Education at the University of Newcastle is for practising educators looking to retrain in an additional teaching area or advance their professional skills. Students deepen their understanding of educational theory and practice, stay updated with industry trends and research, and apply a proven, evidence-supported teaching framework. The program lets students deepen their curriculum knowledge in specialised areas to enhance their teaching effectiveness and career prospects.

name: Master of Environmental Law
description: The Master of Environmental Law at the University of Newcastle provides legal and non-legal professionals with a deeper knowledge of environmental law in Australia and beyond. Students study a range of discipline areas taught by international industry experts, including environmental and life sciences, business, and architecture and built environment. It is the only postgraduate legal program in Australia offering the opportunity to obtain certification by the United Nations Institute for Training and Research.

name: Master of Fintech
description: The Master of Fintech at the University of Newcastle equips students with a comprehensive understanding of emerging financial technologies, along with advanced financial theory, principles and practices, to build a successful career in the finance sector in the digital era. The program provides a nexus between traditional financial knowledge and transformative financial technologies, and is offered through an AACSB and EQUIS accredited business school.

name: Master of Food Science and Technology
description: The Master of Food Science and Technology at the University of Newcastle provides advanced knowledge, skills and opportunities to work across the food industry as the world faces evolving challenges in food production, sustainability and nutrition. Food is a cornerstone of culture, global health and innovation, and demand for forward-thinking professionals in food science has never been greater. Graduates work in product development, food safety, quality assurance and research.

name: Master of Health Economics, Management and Policy
Master of Health Management and Policy
description: The Master of Health Management and Policy at the University of Newcastle prepares graduates to become leaders in the health sector, where effective leadership and a strong understanding of healthcare organisations and policy are crucial to navigating complex challenges. This multidisciplinary program meets the growing demand for expertise in healthcare leadership and management roles, and students learn directly from international industry experts about policy and governance.

name: Master of Human Resource Management
description: The Master of Human Resource Management at the University of Newcastle provides the skills and knowledge to manage people and efficient work practices within an organisation, and to develop and lead high-performing teams and workforces within complex organisational environments. It suits people looking to advance their career in human resource management, employment relations or consulting, and develops a deep, nuanced understanding of strategic human resource management.

name: Master of Information Technology
description:
Newcastle's Master of IT sits inside a school that grew out of the university's original computing and engineering strength rather than being bolted on as a later cash-generator, and it shows in the elective spread: alongside the expected software engineering and networking units there are dedicated strands in cybersecurity and data science that draw on the same research groups producing NURVsim and IoT security work out of Callaghan. Most cohorts run heavy with international students converting from other bachelor's degrees, so the program includes conversion-style foundation units in the first session for anyone without a CS undergrad background, then lets students specialise from session two.

Teaching is a mix of Callaghan campus and, for some intakes, Sydney's CBD campus at 350 George Street, which matters for students weighing proximity to internships at Sydney-based tech employers against lower living costs in Newcastle. The capstone is an industry project rather than a pure research thesis for most students, done in small teams with a real client brief: recent ones have included local government data dashboards and health-sector app prototypes tied to the Hunter New England health precinct next to the university.
curriculum:
Session 1: Programming Fundamentals, Database Systems, Networking Fundamentals, Systems Analysis and Design
Session 2: Software Engineering, Advanced Database Systems, Elective (Cybersecurity or Data Science stream)
Session 3: Cloud Computing, Elective, Elective, IT Project Management
Session 4: IT Capstone Project (industry-sponsored team project), Elective
Specialisation streams: Cybersecurity, Data Science, Software Engineering, Networking
Entry pathway: Graduate Certificate in IT available for students needing foundation coursework before full enrolment

name: Master of International Business
description: The Master of International Business at the University of Newcastle helps students deepen their understanding of international business and develop the strategic decision-making knowledge and skills required to be a successful manager for organisations with an international focus. Students learn to form and implement strategic decisions in the global business environment. The program is hosted at NUspace in the heart of the Newcastle CBD.

name: Master of International Sports Business
description: The Master of International Sports Business at the University of Newcastle is an interdisciplinary program that equips students with the advanced knowledge and skills to excel in the global sports industry. It prioritises the development of problem-solving skills, ethical decision-making and strategic perspectives, preparing students for diverse careers in sport business. The program is delivered on campus in Sydney in partnership with the Global Institute of Sport, using the Allianz Stadium and Sydney Cricket Ground precinct.

name: Master of Laboratory Medicine
description: The Master of Laboratory Medicine at the University of Newcastle prepares job-ready graduates with advanced expertise in diagnostic pathology and medical research, real clinical laboratory experience, and strong pathways into hospital, pathology and regional laboratories. Designed to meet Australia's growing demand for skilled laboratory professionals, it is ideal for graduates of biomedical science, biology, biotechnology or closely related disciplines. Students undertake supervised placements in clinical laboratories, gaining practical experience with current diagnostic techniques before entering the workforce.

name: Master of Laws
description: The Master of Laws at the University of Newcastle is for people who want to specialise in a specific area of law, with flexible study options tailored to career needs. Students choose from Dispute Resolution, Environmental Law, Employment and Labour Relations Law and International Law, engaging in advanced studies with a strong research focus and developing critical thinking skills to analyse complex legal issues. Classes are held at NUspace in the Newcastle CBD.

name: Master of Leadership and Management in Education
Master of Marketing and Digital Strategy
description: The Master of Marketing and Digital Strategy at the University of Newcastle is a comprehensive, contemporary and practical program that equips students with digital transformation skills and data-driven insights to promote socially responsible marketing and foster a strategic and entrepreneurial mindset. The program can be studied face-to-face at the Newcastle City Precinct, online, or a combination of the two, allowing students to balance professional and personal life.

name: Master of Materials Science and Engineering
description: The Master of Materials Science and Engineering at the University of Newcastle combines coursework and research, with access to specialised infrastructure at the Global Innovative Centre for Advanced Nanomaterials. Students undertake research related to the design and discovery of new materials, including advanced materials, nanomaterials, functional materials, drug carriers, photovoltaics and soft materials, preparing them for careers in materials research and engineering.

name: Master of Midwifery Studies
description: The Master of Midwifery Studies at the University of Newcastle offers registered midwives a pathway to broaden their scope beyond bedside care and move into leadership, education or specialist roles such as primary care and research. Today's midwives work in increasingly complex environments with growing workload pressures, and the program is designed with these realities in mind, supporting midwives who are balancing shift work and career development.

name: Master of Nursing
description: The University of Newcastle Master of Nursing is built for working registered nurses who want to progress into senior, specialist, leadership, educator or researcher roles without stepping away from practice, with flexible online learning and recognition of existing experience. It offers specialisations such as Advanced Practice and Leadership and Management, and develops the knowledge to lead teams, manage complex care and deliver evidence-based care. Entry requires registration as a registered nurse in the applicant own country, plus a postgraduate qualification at AQF level 8 or higher or at least one year of work experience as a registered nurse, evidenced by a CV and statement of service. Indicative international tuition is around A$47,600 per year. With a projected national shortfall of around 79,000 nurses by 2035, demand for advanced-practice nurses is strong.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: The University of Newcastle Master of Professional Accounting is a two-year conversion degree for graduates whose qualifications are in a field other than accounting, covering financial and management accounting, finance, taxation, business law and auditing. It is structured to satisfy the joint accreditation guidelines of CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand, so graduates can take up associate membership of CPA Australia and enrol in the CPA Program or the CA Program. Entry requires a bachelor degree in any discipline, or at least seven years of relevant organisational experience including two years in management, plus the University English proficiency requirement. Indicative international tuition is around A$42,600 per year. Graduates work in accounting, finance, tax and audit roles across commerce, professional practice and government.

name: Master of Professional Engineering (Geospatial Engineering and Surveying)
Master of Professional Psychology
description: The Master of Professional Psychology at the University of Newcastle is designed for those interested in a career as a registered psychologist. Students develop core counselling skills and competencies appropriate for an early career psychologist, and graduates are ready to commence their internship as part of the 5+1 pathway to general psychology registration. Students learn to assess, develop a case formulation and apply best practice with people who have a range of psychological presentations.

name: Master of Public Health
description: The University of Newcastle's Master of Public Health is an 80-unit degree, one year full-time or two years part-time, available on campus or online. It is built from 40 units of core courses and 40 units chosen from a wide course list, so students can focus on areas such as epidemiology, biostatistics, health promotion or health services management. The program gives a broad grounding in identifying, evaluating and responding to public health problems at both local and global scale, and can also be taken as a double degree with health management and policy or with social change and development. Graduates work in government health agencies, non-government organisations, community health and research. Indicative international tuition is around A$46,400 per year.

name: Master of Social Change and Development
description: The Master of Social Change and Development at the University of Newcastle teaches students to undertake projects in collaboration with community members and to influence positive outcomes through theoretical and applied knowledge. The global environment is rapidly changing, and students make immediate impact through hands-on learning opportunities. The program provides an opportunity to create original research work as part of study and to shape a career in local and international development.

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description: The Master of Social Work (Qualifying) at the University of Newcastle prepares graduates from unrelated fields to become qualified social workers, a profession in high demand. The program is practice-led and industry-engaged, with embedded fieldwork placements to prepare students for professional practice. Students can study full-time or part-time, with a flexible night-school approach to class times to suit work and home responsibilities.

name: Master of Special and Inclusive Education
description: The Master of Special and Inclusive Education at the University of Newcastle builds on students' existing education or health qualifications, blending theory, research, practice, reflection and innovation with an emphasis on applying best-practice, evidence-based approaches to support the learning and development of people with disability or additional needs. It is designed for educators working in inclusive and specialist settings, including practising and accredited teachers seeking additional qualifications.

name: Master of Sports Analytics
description: The Master of Sports Analytics at the University of Newcastle is delivered in partnership with the Global Institute of Sport and is a future-focused degree for data-driven students with aspirations towards careers in sports business or performance analysis. Both growth areas require evidence-based decision-making and research skills, which are fundamental learning outcomes of the degree. Students study at the heart of Sydney's business and sports precinct.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
Notre Dame's BA covers the usual humanities spread (history, English, philosophy, politics), but the university's smaller scale and Catholic mission mean genuinely small tutorial groups and a values and ethics thread running through core units, framed differently than at a secular university. Available across the Fremantle and Sydney campuses, with slightly different elective offerings depending on location.

It's commonly taken as a combined degree (Arts/Law, Arts/Education) rather than standalone, and the degree's smaller enrolment numbers mean students get real access to academic staff rather than being one of several hundred in a lecture theatre.
curriculum:
Year 1: two introductory subjects across chosen majors, Core Curriculum unit (a university-wide requirement covering ethics and philosophy foundations)
Years 2-3: major sequences (8 subjects per major), electives
Typical majors: History, English, Philosophy, Politics and International Relations, Theology
Capstone: independent research essay or internship subject, final year
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65-70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science (Assured Pathway to Medicine)
description:
This is Notre Dame's dedicated feeder degree into its own Doctor of Medicine program. Students who maintain the required GPA through the three years get a guaranteed interview and, on passing that, a confirmed place in the MD without sitting GAMSAT, which is largely why students choose this over a generic biomedical science degree elsewhere. It runs out of the Fremantle campus, sharing teaching space and some staff with the medical school itself.

Class sizes are genuinely small by Australian university standards. Notre Dame markets itself on this, and in the science labs it means more direct instructor time than at the larger biomedical cohorts nearby. The degree still stands on its own for anyone who doesn't proceed to medicine, but the assured pathway is the headline feature and shapes the entire cohort's expectations.
curriculum:
Year 1: Human Biology, Chemistry, Foundations of Anatomy, Introduction to Medical Sciences
Year 2: Physiology, Biochemistry, Pathophysiology, Pharmacology Foundations
Year 3: Advanced Systems Physiology, Research Project, electives, MD entry interview process
Pathway requirement: minimum cumulative GPA maintained through all three years, interview in final year
admission_requirements: Minimum ATAR of 92 (or IB/equivalent) for international school leavers; maintain GPA of 2.5+ each semester to remain on assured pathway to MD
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
A standard business generalist degree through Notre Dame's School of Law and Business, offering majors across accounting, finance, management, and marketing, with the accounting major carrying professional accreditation relevant to CPA and CAANZ pathways. Class sizes are notably smaller than at the larger Perth or Sydney business schools, and the degree's Core Curriculum requirement (shared across all Notre Dame undergraduate degrees) means commerce students also take ethics and philosophy units alongside their business coursework, a genuine point of difference from a purely vocational business degree.

Placement and internship opportunities lean on Notre Dame's local business community ties in Fremantle and Perth, or Sydney depending on campus.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Fundamentals, Economics, Business Statistics, Core Curriculum unit
Year 2: Corporate Finance, Marketing Principles, Management, first major subjects
Year 3: major specialisation, Business Law, Strategic Management, capstone/internship option
Majors: Accounting, Finance, Management, Marketing
Capstone: work-integrated learning or business project, final year
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65-75 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
Leads to registration as a primary school teacher in Australia, with a strong practicum emphasis: students are typically in schools on placement from first year, not just in a token block near the end, which the university uses as a selling point against programs that front-load theory before classroom exposure. The Catholic education sector across WA and NSW is a major employer of Notre Dame education graduates, and the degree includes specific preparation for teaching in faith-based schools alongside the standard curriculum and pedagogy content required for any teaching role.

Literacy and numeracy pedagogy get heavy emphasis given AITSL's national teaching standards, and students sit the mandatory literacy and numeracy test (LANTITE) during the degree, not as an afterthought at the end.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Education, Child Development, Introduction to Curriculum, early school placement block
Year 2: Literacy Pedagogy, Numeracy Pedagogy, Classroom Management, school placement
Year 3: curriculum specialisations (science, HASS, arts, health/PE), Inclusive Education, extended placement
Year 4: Professional Experience (extended final placement), capstone teaching portfolio, LANTITE completion
Registration: leads to provisional teacher registration in the relevant state or territory
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65-75 or equivalent; interview and personal statement often required for teaching entry
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0 (professional teacher registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
Bachelor of Health and Physical Education (Primary) (Honours)
Bachelor of Laws
description:
Notre Dame's standard-entry undergraduate LLB, distinct from the graduate-entry JD, is usually taken as a combined degree (Arts/Law and Commerce/Law are the common pairings) across four to five years depending on the combination. It covers the same Priestley 11 core required for practice, delivered in smaller classes than the large capital-city law schools, with the same values-based ethics emphasis that runs through Notre Dame's law teaching generally.

Clinical legal education and mooting programs give students supervised practical exposure before graduation, and the smaller cohort size means more direct access to teaching staff for mooting coaching and clinic supervision than at higher-enrolment law schools.
curriculum:
Core (Priestley 11): Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, Equity, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, Corporations Law, Professional Conduct
Electives: minimum 6-8 subjects depending on combined degree structure
Clinical option: supervised legal clinic placement
Capstone: moot or research subject, final year
Leads to: eligibility for Practical Legal Training and admission as a legal practitioner
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 80-85 or equivalent, or mature-age entry with relevant experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Marketing and Public Relations
Bachelor of Nursing
description:
The University of Notre Dame Australia's Bachelor of Nursing leads to registration eligibility with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, taught with a strong clinical placement structure across Fremantle-area hospitals and health services, and Sydney placements for that campus's cohort. The degree's Catholic institutional character shows up specifically in mandatory units on ethics and pastoral care within a health context, sitting alongside the standard clinical science curriculum required for any nursing accreditation.

Simulation-based learning happens on campus in dedicated clinical skills labs before students progress to live hospital and community placements, with placement blocks increasing in complexity and autonomy each year.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, Ethics and Pastoral Care in Health
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, clinical placement blocks
Year 3: Acute and Critical Care, Community and Primary Health Care, Aged Care Nursing, final capstone placement
Placement: clinical hours across acute, community, aged care, and mental health settings, AHPRA-aligned
admission_requirements: Indicative ATAR of 70 with a minimum score of 50 in ATAR English/Literature/EALD, or equivalent; interview may be required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5 (higher requirement due to clinical placements)

name: Bachelor of Philosophy
description:
A distinctive offering shaped by Notre Dame's Catholic identity: unlike a standard philosophy major bolted onto a BA, this is a dedicated degree with a strong grounding in the history of philosophy, from ancient through medieval to modern, alongside contemporary ethics, metaphysics, and philosophy of religion. The faculty includes specialists in Thomistic and Catholic intellectual tradition scholarship structured in a way you won't find at a secular university.

It draws a genuinely small cohort (this isn't a high-enrolment degree), but that means seminar-style teaching rather than lectures for most of the degree, and students get close engagement with staff on primary texts rather than survey-level treatment.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Philosophy, Ancient Philosophy, Logic and Critical Thinking, Ethics
Year 2: Medieval Philosophy, Modern Philosophy, Philosophy of Religion, Metaphysics
Year 3: Contemporary Philosophy, Political Philosophy, independent research essay, electives
Capstone: extended research essay or thesis, final year
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with an ATAR of approximately 65-70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Physiotherapy
description:
A four-year professional degree accredited by the Australian Physiotherapy Council, leading to registration eligibility with AHPRA. Notre Dame runs this out of its Fremantle health sciences facilities, with clinical placement hours spread across public hospital, private practice, aged care, and sports settings. The degree emphasises hands-on clinical skills training in on-campus labs well before students go into placement, using the same anatomy and clinical skills facilities shared with the university's medical and nursing programs.

Given Notre Dame's smaller cohort compared to the bigger physiotherapy schools in the region, students get more individual attention in practical skills classes, which the school markets directly to prospective students.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy, Physiology, Biomechanics, Introduction to Physiotherapy Practice
Year 2: Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy, Neurological Physiotherapy, Cardiorespiratory Physiotherapy, clinical skills labs
Year 3: clinical placements begin (hospital, private practice), Exercise Physiology, Pain Science
Year 4: extended clinical placements (aged care, paediatrics, sports, community), Professional Practice, capstone case-based assessment
Placement: clinical hours across acute, community, private practice, and sports settings, AHPRA-aligned
admission_requirements: Indicative ATAR of approximately 85-90 or equivalent; interview and/or portfolio may be required due to clinical placements
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Bachelor of Sport and Recreation Management
Doctor of Medicine
description:
Notre Dame's MD is a four-year graduate-entry program taught at the Fremantle campus (Sydney also runs the degree), accredited by the Australian Medical Council.
