The first two years use problem-based learning as the backbone rather than traditional lecture-heavy pre-clinical teaching: small tutorial groups work through clinical cases collaboratively with a facilitator rather than being taught anatomy and physiology in isolation from clinical context.

The distinguishing feature is the rural and community health emphasis: third year is run jointly with UWA through the Rural Clinical School of Western Australia, and around a quarter of each cohort can opt into a full year-long placement in a rural WA clinical site instead of the standard rotation structure. Clinical years also include a compulsory rural or remote general practice placement for everyone, not just those on the extended rural track, a genuine point of difference from more metro-focused medical schools.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Problem-Based Learning case tutorials, basic clinical sciences, population and preventive health, bioethics, therapeutics, clinical skills training
Year 3: clinical rotations at Perth teaching hospitals, or Rural Clinical School of WA year-long placement for selected students
Year 4: discipline-based clinical rotations (medicine, surgery, paediatrics, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynaecology), rural/remote general practice placement, translational research or clinical audit project
Accreditation: AMC-accredited, leads to provisional registration and internship
admission_requirements: Completed bachelor degree in any discipline; GAMSAT average 52+ (min 50 per section) or equivalent, GPA 5.2+, CASPer situational judgement test, and interview
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0

name: Graduate Certificate in Medical Sciences
description:
A short postgraduate certificate aimed at graduates from non-medical backgrounds wanting a structured bridge into medical science postgraduate study, or as a standalone credential for allied health and science professionals wanting formal grounding in human biomedical sciences. It's not a pathway into Notre Dame's MD in the way the Assured Pathway biomedical degree is. It functions more as targeted upskilling or a stepping stone toward further postgraduate study.

Coursework compresses core biomedical science content (physiology, pathophysiology, pharmacology basics) into an intensive format, often taken part-time by people already working in health-adjacent fields.
curriculum:
Core subjects: Human Physiology, Pathophysiology, Pharmacology Foundations, Research Methods in Health Sciences
Structure: typically 4 subjects, completable in one semester full-time or across two part-time
Assessment: coursework-based, no thesis component
Progression: can articulate into further postgraduate medical science or health study for eligible students
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor degree in science or health-related field
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Juris Doctor
description:
Notre Dame's JD is a graduate-entry law degree run through the School of Law, built for people with an existing non-law bachelor's degree wanting to qualify for legal practice. It covers the full Priestley 11 core subjects required for admission in an accelerated postgraduate format, with practical legal skills, mooting, negotiation, a supervised legal clinic placement, woven through rather than left entirely to post-degree Practical Legal Training.

Notre Dame's law cohort is smaller than the big Sydney law schools, and the school leans into a values-based framing consistent with the university's Catholic character, which shows up in dedicated subjects on legal ethics and social justice rather than treating those as an afterthought elective.
curriculum:
Core (Priestley 11): Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, Equity and Trusts, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Evidence, Civil Procedure, Corporations Law, Professional Conduct and Ethics
Electives: minimum 4-6 subjects, options include international law, family law, employment law
Clinical option: supervised legal clinic placement (credit-bearing)
Capstone: research subject or moot, final semester
Leads to: eligibility for Practical Legal Training and admission as a legal practitioner
admission_requirements: Completed bachelor degree in any discipline (or equivalent); relevant work experience viewed favourably
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Notre Dame's MBA is a smaller, values-oriented program compared to the large AACSB-branded MBAs at bigger business schools: positioned toward professionals wanting leadership and management skills grounded in ethical decision-making, consistent with the university's mission, rather than competing primarily on rankings or alumni network size. Delivered in flexible formats aimed at working professionals, with core subjects in finance, strategy, and marketing alongside a distinctive emphasis on ethical leadership.

Cohorts are small, and the program leans on case-based and applied project work over large-lecture delivery, reflecting Notre Dame's teaching style across its postgraduate business offerings generally.
curriculum:
Core: Financial Management, Strategic Management, Marketing Management, Ethical Leadership, Organisational Behaviour, Business Analytics
Electives: choose from entrepreneurship, human resource management, international business
Capstone: applied business project or strategy report, final term
Delivery: part-time/flexible options for working professionals
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline), professional experience considered favourably (typical MBA entry bar, approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Education (Leadership and Management)
description:
Aimed at practising teachers moving into or already in school leadership roles (deputy principal, principal, head of department), this is a part-time-friendly postgraduate degree with an emphasis on Catholic and independent school sector leadership specifically, reflecting Notre Dame's institutional base, though the content applies across government schools too. Assessment leans on applied projects tied to students' own school contexts rather than purely theoretical coursework, on the assumption most students are working full-time in schools while studying.

Coursework covers educational leadership theory, school improvement and change management, and financial and human resource management within schools, with a research project or dissertation option for students wanting a pathway toward doctoral study afterward.
curriculum:
Core: Educational Leadership Theory, Managing Change in Schools, School Improvement and Data-Informed Practice, Human Resource Management in Schools
Electives: financial management in schools, curriculum leadership, pastoral care leadership, Catholic school leadership and mission
Capstone: applied leadership project based in the student's own school context, or research dissertation option
Delivery: part-time, intensive/block format common for working teachers
admission_requirements: Relevant bachelor degree in education or related field, typically with teaching experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Advanced Business (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Advanced Business (Honours) is the University of Queensland Business School's flagship four-year undergraduate degree, built for high-achieving students aiming at leadership careers in business, strategy or consulting. Honours is embedded in the degree rather than added on afterwards, and students choose two majors from six options, including accounting, finance and marketing, or opt for a research pathway that leads toward postgraduate study. Core courses in information systems for strategic advantage and business analytics and artificial intelligence sit alongside major-specific study such as auditing, behavioural finance or applied market research, and a capstone project closes out the degree. Cohort-exclusive courses and structured networking are built into the program to help students build lasting professional connections, and graduates who complete the accounting major with an extra elective can work toward CAANZ or CPA accreditation. Typical destinations include investment analyst, operations manager and analytics project manager roles.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. A sample of what you study includes: Information Systems for Strategic Advantage [Core course], Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence [Core course], Auditing & Public Practice [part of Accounting major], Behavioural Finance [part of Finance major], Applied Market Research [part of Marketing major], Business Industry Consultancy Project [Elective], Business Industry Placement [Elective], Operations manager. Core courses cover tools of economic analysis, microeconomics and financial management, with electives in the economics of international finance and competition policy and regulation, and the degree finishes with a supervised individual research thesis. name: Bachelor of Agribusiness

The degree was developed in close collaboration with Australia's agricultural and business sectors, so the transferable business skills it builds are recognised well beyond farming specifically. Graduates typically move into roles such as agribusiness analyst, agribusiness banker, export trader or farm management consultant, either in Australia or in their home country's agricultural or agribusiness sector.

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Science
description:
Agriculture at UQ runs primarily out of the Gatton campus, a genuine working farm and research station about an hour west of Brisbane rather than a token rural annex, and the Bachelor of Agricultural Science leans on that hard: students get direct access to livestock and cropping systems, UQ's own research farms, and industry connections into Queensland's cattle, grain, and horticulture sectors that are simply larger and more varied than what a metro-based agriculture program can offer.

The degree covers plant and animal production systems, agribusiness, and increasingly precision agriculture and sustainability units, reflecting real shifts in the industry toward data-driven farm management, and UQ's agricultural research strength (particularly in areas like plant breeding genetics and tropical agriculture, given Queensland's subtropical and tropical growing regions) feeds directly into elective and capstone project offerings.

Most students complete a substantial industry placement or work-integrated learning component, often with agribusiness employers, government agencies like the Department of Agriculture and Fisheries, or research organisations, and Gatton's genuinely rural setting (compared to a program run entirely from a capital-city campus) means students graduate having actually worked with production systems rather than only studying them in theory.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Agricultural Science, Soil Science, Plant Biology, Animal Biology, Agricultural Economics
Year 2: Crop Production Systems, Livestock Production Systems, Agricultural Business Management, Pest and Disease Management
Year 3: Precision Agriculture, Agribusiness and Marketing, Sustainable Farming Systems, work-integrated learning placement
Year 4: Capstone Agricultural Systems Project, electives (options include tropical agriculture, plant breeding, agricultural technology), industry placement
Delivered primarily at UQ Gatton campus
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 78+
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

Core courses include sustainability for global citizenship and foundation design studios, and the degree includes field trips and study tours to locations such as Japan and India. Teaching staff are a mix of academics and practising architects, so classroom projects stay connected to real practice. Graduates leave with an industry-ready design portfolio and typically move into roles such as architect, interior designer or urban designer.

name: Bachelor of Behavioural Science (exit award only)
description: The Bachelor of Behavioural Science is an exit award at the University of Queensland rather than a program you apply for directly. It is granted to students enrolled in the Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours) who choose, or need, to leave that program after 3 years of study rather than continuing into the honours year. The Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours) itself explores human behaviour, cognition and emotion through neurodevelopmental, social, cognitive, biological and abnormal psychology, and normally leads on to postgraduate study required for registration as a psychologist. A student who exits with the Bachelor of Behavioural Science still has a recognised university qualification covering the first 3 years of that coursework, useful for roles in human resources, community services, research support and further study in a related field, but without the honours research component or the direct line into psychologist registration that completing the full 4 year program provides.
curriculum: This is an exit award from UQ's Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours), not a program with its own separate course list. Students are awarded the Bachelor of Behavioural Science after completing the first 3 years of that program's coursework, which covers areas such as The Brain and Behavioural Sciences, Psychological Approaches to Complex Problems and Neuroscience for Psychologists, before the dedicated honours research year.
admission_requirements: There is no direct entry pathway for this award. Students reach it only by first being admitted to and enrolling in UQ's Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours), which for domestic school leavers requires Queensland Year 12 General English (Units 3 and 4, C) and a minimum ATAR of 89, or the International Baccalaureate equivalent of 34.75.
english_requirements: As an exit award, English language requirements match UQ's Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours): IELTS Academic overall 6.5, with 6.0 in each of reading, writing, speaking and listening. PTE Academic overall 64, with a minimum of 60 in each communicative skill.

Core courses include integrative cell and tissue biology, principles of anatomy and physiology, developmental biology and neuroscience, and microbiology and immunology, taught by award-winning biomedical researchers. Many students use the degree as a stepping stone into medicine or allied health postgraduate study rather than an endpoint qualification. Typical graduate roles include biomedical scientist, clinical trials research assistant and IVF scientist.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
UQ Business School holds the "triple crown" of business accreditations (AACSB, EQUIS, AMBA), a distinction only a handful of Australian business schools carry, and the Bachelor of Commerce is the school's flagship undergraduate degree: majors span accounting, finance, economics, and business analytics through to more specialised options like actuarial studies, one of the few undergraduate actuarial programs in the country accredited toward the Actuaries Institute pathway.

The degree draws a genuinely large international cohort, which shapes the classroom experience in group project units especially, and UQ Business School runs its own careers and mentoring programs that connect students directly to Brisbane's finance and professional services sector as well as national graduate programs at the big four accounting firms and major banks. Students can combine the Commerce degree with another (law, engineering, IT) as a dual degree, a common path for students wanting a technical-plus-business skill set.

Class delivery mixes large first and second-year lectures with smaller major-specific seminars from third year, and a capstone consulting-style project unit in most majors gives students a real client brief to work through in their final semester rather than a purely theoretical assessment.
curriculum:
Year 1: Economic Principles, Accounting for Decision Making, Quantitative Methods for Business, Introduction to Management, Business Law
Year 2: Major units begin (Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Analytics, Actuarial Studies, Marketing, or other majors), Corporate Finance, Business Statistics
Year 3: Advanced major units, Strategic Management, Capstone Business Project (client-based consulting project), electives
Dual degree options with Law, Engineering, IT, and other faculties extend the degree length
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 85+

Core courses include introduction to strategic communication, media and society, and public relations project work, and the degree can be combined into a dual program with business management. Graduates typically move into roles such as communications manager, communications adviser, public relations specialist or communication and engagement officer across corporate, government and non-profit sectors.

name: Bachelor of Criminal Justice (exit award only)
description: The Bachelor of Criminal Justice is an exit award at the University of Queensland rather than a program you apply for directly. It is granted to students enrolled in the Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice (Honours) who complete 48 units of the core and elective coursework in that program but choose, or need, to leave before the dedicated honours research year. The full honours program investigates justice related issues through advanced research methodology and criminology coursework, culminating in an independent thesis, and prepares graduates for policy analysis, intelligence and academic research roles. A student who exits with the Bachelor of Criminal Justice keeps a recognised qualification covering the substantive criminology and criminal justice coursework, which supports entry level roles in community corrections, youth justice, policy support and further study, without the honours thesis or the research credentials that come with completing the full program.
curriculum: This is an exit award from UQ's Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice (Honours), not a program with its own separate course list. Students are awarded the Bachelor of Criminal Justice after completing 48 units of that program's core and elective coursework in Level 2 and Level 3, before the dedicated honours year of Honours Research Thesis and Research Design courses.
admission_requirements: There is no direct entry pathway for this award. Students reach it only by first being admitted to and enrolling in UQ's Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice (or its Arts double-degree variant), and completing 48 units of Level 2 and Level 3 core courses with a grade point average (GPA) of 5.0.
english_requirements: As an exit award, English language requirements match UQ's Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice (Honours): IELTS Academic overall 6.5, with 6.0 in each of reading, writing, speaking and listening. PTE Academic overall 64, with a minimum of 60 in each communicative skill.

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice (Honours) at the University of Queensland is a one-year research program for students who want to investigate a justice-related issue in depth before moving into policy, further research or postgraduate study. Coursework in research methods and advanced criminology supports an independent honours thesis, developed with one-on-one guidance from an academic supervisor across the year. Core courses include the honours research thesis and research design across the humanities, arts and social sciences, building analytical and evidence-evaluation skills that go well beyond a standard undergraduate criminology degree. It suits students who have completed an undergraduate criminology or criminal justice degree and want to strengthen their research credentials before applying for postgraduate study or research-focused roles. Typical graduate roles include policy adviser, intelligence analyst, cyber crime investigator and criminology tutor.

name: Bachelor of Economics
description: The Bachelor of Economics at the University of Queensland is the only stand-alone economics degree of its kind in Queensland, training students to analyse, model and predict human and market behaviour to solve policy and business challenges. Core courses in introductory microeconomics, macroeconomics and tools of economic analysis build a foundation before students specialise in up to two majors and choose electives aligned with their career interests, whether in banking, government policy, health, technology or the environment. A professional placement builds practical work experience into the degree, and many students combine it into dual programs with law or business management. Because the degree teaches transferable statistical and analytical skills rather than a single fixed career path, graduates move into varied roles including economic consultant, investment analyst, regulatory affairs officer and business development manager.

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description: UQ's Bachelor of Education (Primary) trains students to teach across the full range of primary school subjects, from English and mathematics to science, the arts and humanities. Supervised school placements start from first year, building from observation and support work toward a final placement where students take substantial responsibility for a whole class. Core courses cover child development, inclusive classroom practice, Indigenous knowledge and education, and the Australian Curriculum, and students choose one of four minors, in English and literacy, humanities and social sciences, mathematics and numeracy, or science, to deepen their subject knowledge. Small cohort sizes are a deliberate feature of the degree, helping students build a support network alongside their studies. Because Queensland teacher registration requires a higher IELTS band than most UQ degrees, the program suits students who already have strong English proficiency. Graduates register as primary school teachers or move into curriculum planning and learning support roles.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
UQ Engineering carries real weight in mining, minerals processing, and chemical engineering specifically. The Sustainable Minerals Institute is a globally recognised research centre, and it's not unusual for chemical and mining engineering students to end up working on SMI-affiliated research projects for their thesis, something a lot of comparable engineering schools around the country can't offer at the same depth given Queensland's genuine resources industry base.

The Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) is a four-year, Engineers Australia accredited degree covering the standard range of majors (civil, mechanical, electrical, chemical, mining, software, and others), with all students completing a common first year before choosing a major, giving some flexibility to switch specialisations early without losing time. A mandatory professional practice component (minimum weeks of industry experience) is built into the degree, and UQ's engineering placement office benefits from strong ties to Queensland's resources and infrastructure sectors as well as multinational engineering firms with Brisbane offices.

Final-year thesis projects are individually supervised and, for students in minerals, energy, or water-related majors, frequently connect to one of UQ's larger applied research centres rather than being a purely academic exercise, which gives some graduates a direct route into industry-sponsored postgraduate research if they want it.
curriculum:
Year 1 (common to all majors): Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Mechanics, Engineering Modelling and Problem Solving, Chemistry and Materials for Engineers
Year 2: Major-specific core units begin (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, Mining, Software, or other majors), Engineering Design, Thermodynamics/Fluid Mechanics (major-dependent)
Year 3: Advanced major units, Professional Practice (industry placement component), Engineering Management, Sustainability in Engineering
Year 4 (Honours): Advanced design units, Engineering Thesis (individual research project, often SMI-affiliated for minerals/resources-related majors), technical electives
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 85+, prerequisite Mathematical Methods and Chemistry or Physics
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

The degree combines natural sciences with social and economic disciplines, decision-making and policy analysis, and includes a full semester of placement and practical experience alongside hands-on field and lab-based learning across Queensland's biodiversity hotspots, from coral reefs to World Heritage rainforests. Core courses include cultural heritage management, environmental impact assessment and conservation planning and management, with the embedded honours component adding a research dimension. Graduates typically move into roles such as environmental management consultant, sustainability adviser, natural resources manager or environmental planner in government or private consultancies.

Coursework spans biomechanics, anatomical basis of human movement, health and fitness through diet and exercise, and the professional context of healthcare, alongside 500 hours of hands-on placement with clients in a supervised environment. Students planning careers helping elite athletes optimise performance, supporting community health and fitness, or working in rehabilitation and research settings use this degree to build both the science background and the practical hours accreditation bodies expect. Graduates go on to roles across sports academies and institutes, rehabilitation clinics, hospitals and research centres, applying biomechanics, physiology and psychology to turn research into training and recovery plans for individuals and teams across Australia and internationally.

name: Bachelor of Laws (Honours)
description:
UQ Law School is consistently rated among the top two or three in the country, and the LLB (Honours) benefits from that reputation in ways that show up in specific programs: its Pro Bono Centre places students in real supervised legal work with community legal centres and Legal Aid Queensland, and the law school runs one of the more active international mooting programs in Australia, regularly sending teams to competitions like the Willem C. Vis arbitration moot in Vienna.

Students take the LLB combined with another degree (arts, commerce, science, and others are common pairings), which stretches the program to five years but means graduates leave with genuine breadth rather than a law-only credential. UQ also has particular research strength in areas like international law and human rights, taught by academics with real practice or UN-adjacent backgrounds, and third and fourth-year elective offerings reflect that rather than sticking to a generic elective list.

Brisbane's legal market is smaller than Sydney's or Melbourne's, but UQ graduates dominate hiring at the state's top-tier firms and at the Queensland Bar, and the law school's clerkship placement rates into those firms are a large part of why the program remains competitive to enter despite Queensland having several other law schools to choose from.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Legal Method and Reasoning, Contracts, Torts, Criminal Law, Property Law, plus first two years of paired degree (Arts, Commerce, Science, or other)
Years 3-4: Equity, Constitutional Law, Administrative Law, Corporations Law, Evidence, Civil and Criminal Procedure, continued paired degree units
Year 5 (honours): Advanced electives (options include International Law, Human Rights Law, Competition Law), honours thesis or advanced coursework, Professional Responsibility
Co-curricular: Pro Bono Centre placements, international mooting competitions
Practical Legal Training required post-graduation for admission as a solicitor
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 95+
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0

name: Bachelor of Mathematics
description: The Bachelor of Mathematics at the University of Queensland offers more than 60 mathematics and statistics courses, more than any other university in the state, letting students specialise in areas such as mathematical artificial intelligence, optimisation and operations research, mathematical physics or pure mathematics. The Mathematical Artificial Intelligence major covers machine learning, data science and algorithm development, while Optimisation and Operations Research focuses on solving real logistical and efficiency problems for industry. Students can gain practical, real-world experience through UQ's Summer Industry Experience Program, working on live projects rather than only theoretical coursework. Core courses include calculus and linear algebra, methods and models of applied mathematics, and abstract algebra and number theory. Graduates typically move into roles such as data scientist, statistician, quantitative analyst or bioinformatician across finance, technology, healthcare and government.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. A sample of what you study includes: Calculus & Linear Algebra II [Core course], Methods & Models of Applied Mathematics [part of Applied Mathematics major], Operations Research & Mathematical Planning [part of Optimisation and Operations Research major], Algebraic Methods of Mathematical Physics [part of Mathematical Physics major], Deep Learning [part of Mathematical Artificial Intelligence major], Abstract Algebra & Number Theory [part of Pure Mathematics major], Problems & Applications in Modern Statistics [part of Statistics and Mathematical Data Science major], Bachelors of Music / Mathematics. The exact core versus elective structure depends on the major, specialisation or study plan chosen, and is confirmed in UQ's official program and course list at enrolment.

name: Bachelor of Medical Science (Exit award)
description: The Bachelor of Medical Science (Exit award) is granted at the University of Queensland to students enrolled in the Bachelor of Medical Science / Doctor of Medicine dual degree who complete the 2 year pre-medicine component, and typically a further stage of the Doctor of Medicine, before choosing or needing to leave the combined program early, since UQ approves an early exit after 3 years of this pathway. The full dual degree lets students graduate as a doctor at least a year earlier than traditional postgraduate medicine pathways, combining tailored pre-medicine study with a 4 year Doctor of Medicine, and covers traditional science and biomedical science alongside public health, humanities and computer science or information technology. A student exiting with the Bachelor of Medical Science keeps a recognised science degree covering that coursework, useful for roles in biomedical research, health administration, science communication or further postgraduate study, without the clinical training and registration pathway that completing the full Doctor of Medicine provides.
curriculum: This is an exit award from UQ's Bachelor of Medical Science / Doctor of Medicine dual degree, not a program with its own separate course list. The first 2 years (pre-medicine) cover 8 core foundational courses in Year 1 and 5 core courses plus 3 electives in Year 2, spanning traditional science, biomedical science, public health, humanities and computer science or information technology, before transitioning into Doctor of Medicine clinical coursework in later years.
admission_requirements: There is no direct entry pathway for this award. Students reach it only by first being admitted to and enrolling in UQ's Bachelor of Medical Science / Doctor of Medicine, which for domestic school leavers requires an adjusted ATAR of 95 or equivalent, Queensland Year 12 General English and Mathematical Methods (Units 3 and 4, C), a competitive UCAT ANZ score, and a multiple mini-interview.
english_requirements: As an exit award, English language requirements match UQ's Bachelor of Medical Science / Doctor of Medicine: IELTS Academic overall 7.0, with 7.0 in each of reading, writing, speaking and listening. PTE Academic overall 72, with a minimum of 72 in each communicative skill.

name: Bachelor of Midwifery
description: UQ's Bachelor of Midwifery is a 3-year program developed with midwifery academics, industry partners and parents themselves, training students to support women through pregnancy, labour, birth and the postpartum period. Clinical placement rostered shifts and simulated learning begin in first year, building toward extended clinical placements in the final year that manage the transition from student to practising midwife. Core courses include introduction to midwifery practice and clinical midwifery practice, and students who want to also qualify as a registered nurse can complete UQ's combined Bachelor of Nursing/Midwifery dual degree with just one extra year of study. Graduates typically move into hospital midwifery, community midwifery, antenatal care or international aid work, in a profession facing sustained demand across Australia's health system.

A sample of what you study includes: Introduction to Midwifery Practice, Professional Practice 1, Bachelors of Nursing / Midwifery, Midwife, Community midwife, Antenatal midwife. The exact core versus elective structure depends on the major, specialisation or study plan chosen, and is confirmed in UQ's official program and course list at enrolment.

name: Bachelor of Music (Honours)
description: UQ's Bachelor of Music (Honours) is a research-focused year for musicians who want to explore a specialist area of music in depth before moving into a professional or academic music career. Students combine advanced coursework with planning and completing a substantial research or creative project, developing independent investigation skills alongside performance, analysis and research work under close academic supervision. Core courses include research design in arts and culture, and the honours research thesis itself, taught by nationally and internationally recognised music academics and performers. The program is designed as a direct pathway into postgraduate music study and research as much as into performance careers. Typical graduate roles include music researcher, music critic, music tutor and music producer, alongside performance and composition careers.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description: The Bachelor of Nursing at the University of Queensland prepares students to become registered nurses through 880 hours of supervised clinical practice in real hospitals and healthcare facilities across Australia. The program was developed with healthcare professionals, industry partners and patients, and uses a narrative and inquiry-based teaching approach that integrates evidence-based theory with clinical practice from the first year, when students begin rostered clinical placement shifts and skills simulation. Core courses cover health across the lifespan, clinical nursing practice, older adults' health and acute care nursing, and students can pursue a combined Bachelor of Nursing/Midwifery dual qualification. Registered nurse graduates from UQ move into diverse settings including paediatric, critical care, mental health, rural health and aged care nursing, a profession with strong ongoing demand in Australia.

name: Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours)
description: UQ's Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours) trains students to help people of all ages overcome barriers to everyday activities caused by injury, illness, disability or ageing, at what is considered one of Australia's leading schools for health and rehabilitation sciences. From first year, students gain practical experience across community and healthcare settings, including UQ's own on-site clinics, alongside coursework in systematic and applied anatomy, introduction to professional skills, and occupational therapy for children and youth. The degree builds knowledge across medical, social, behavioural and psychosocial sciences so graduates can modify tasks, environments or routines to suit an individual client's needs rather than applying a single fixed method. The embedded honours qualification is internationally recognised and can lead into further research or postgraduate study. Graduates typically register as occupational therapists, working in injury rehabilitation, disability services, aged care or paediatric settings.

name: Bachelor of Pharmaceutics and Therapeutic Science (exit award only)
description: The Bachelor of Pharmaceutics and Therapeutic Science (exit award only) is granted at the University of Queensland to students enrolled in the Bachelor of Pharmaceutics and Therapeutic Science / Doctor of Pharmacy dual degree who complete 48 units in years 1 to 3 but choose, or need, to leave before the Doctor of Pharmacy stage. The full 5 year dual degree trains students to work as registered pharmacists, with over 700 hours of supervised clinical placement across community pharmacy, hospital pharmacy and aged care beginning in year 2, and an optional major in Clinical and Experimental Therapeutics for students interested in a research project in areas like drug discovery. Honours is not available for this exit award. A student exiting after the bachelor stage keeps a recognised science qualification covering pharmaceutical and therapeutic science coursework and placement hours, useful for roles in pharmaceutical companies, laboratories or further study, but without the clinical training and registration that completing the full Doctor of Pharmacy provides.
curriculum: This is an exit award from UQ's Bachelor of Pharmaceutics and Therapeutic Science / Doctor of Pharmacy dual degree, not a program with its own separate course list. Students are awarded it after completing 48 units drawn from years 1 to 3 of that program, which include roughly 165 hours of supervised placement across community pharmacy, hospital pharmacy and aged care settings, before the Doctor of Pharmacy stage begins.
admission_requirements: There is no direct entry pathway for this award. Students reach it only by first being admitted to and enrolling in UQ's Bachelor of Pharmaceutics and Therapeutic Science / Doctor of Pharmacy, which requires Queensland Year 12 General English, General Mathematics, Mathematical Methods or Specialist Mathematics, and Chemistry (all Units 3 and 4, C), with Biology recommended.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) at the University of Queensland trains students to become registered pharmacists, teaching safe, effective, patient-centred use of medicines alongside the technical knowledge needed to work as a medicines expert. Teaching happens in UQ's roughly $100 million biomedical science centre at Dutton Park, purpose-built with laboratories, mock dispensaries and simulated pharmacies, and includes two 6-week clinical placements plus an interprofessional education program with other health disciplines. Core courses include pharmacy practice and medicines management, pharmaceutical sciences, and pharmacokinetics and medicines management, building toward registration as a community, hospital or industrial pharmacist. The honours component gives the degree a research dimension beyond standard pharmacy registration training, and graduates describe the program's cohort as a close-knit professional community rather than a large lecture-only degree.

A sample of what you study includes: Pharmacy Practice and Medicines Management 1A, Pharmaceutical Sciences 2A, Social Pharmacy and the Health System 2, Pharmacokinetcs and Medicines Management, Community pharmacist, Hospital/dispensary pharmacist, Research pharmacist, Industrial pharmacist. name: Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours)
description: UQ's Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours) trains students in the diagnostic and clinical skills needed to help patients recover from injury, manage chronic conditions and restore movement and function. Teaching combines clinical visits, seminars, practical skills sessions and supervised clinical practice with an award-winning simulated patient program run in UQ's hospital simulation ward and its own physiotherapy clinics. Coursework spans musculoskeletal, neurological and respiratory conditions, covering injury prevention, clinical reasoning and diagnosis, and therapeutic exercise prescription, building toward registration as a physiotherapist. The embedded honours qualification is internationally recognised and gives graduates the option of continuing into physiotherapy research after they finish. Typical graduate destinations include general physiotherapy practice, sports physiotherapy, community health physiotherapy or further clinical research.

name: Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics (Honours)
description: UQ's Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics (Honours) combines all three disciplines to prepare students for leadership careers in business, politics, the not-for-profit sector or academia. Core courses across introductory microeconomics, introduction to Australian politics, critical reasoning and introduction to ethics build a common foundation before students specialise in one area or continue across all three as a general path. A Work-Integrated Learning course lets students apply their theoretical knowledge to real business problems, and small, high-achieving cohorts create close academic relationships with teaching staff who hold a significant share of Australia's competitive research grants. A global study experience is built into the degree to give students an international network before they graduate. Typical graduate roles include economic policy adviser, political adviser, public commentator and diplomat.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours)
description:
UQ's psychology school is one of the largest and most research-active in the country, with active labs in areas ranging from clinical and cognitive psychology to social identity research, the latter a genuine UQ specialty, given the school is home to some of the researchers behind widely cited social identity and group processes theory that gets taught internationally. The Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours) is a four-year embedded honours degree rather than a separate bolt-on year, meaning honours entry (competitive, GPA-gated) is built into the program's structure from the start rather than treated as an optional extra.

Because the school is so large, students get access to a wide spread of research areas for their honours thesis, supervised individually, and the school's own on-campus clinics (including for things like the treatment of anxiety and other clinical presentations) give some students supervised client-facing experience during their degree, a step up from purely coursework-based training.

The degree is APAC accredited, positioning graduates for further postgraduate training: provisional psychologist registration, and eventually a masters or doctorate in clinical, forensic, or organisational psychology, areas where UQ's own postgraduate programs are strong and where honours graduates get a genuine leg up in admission.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Bases of Behaviour, Social and Developmental Psychology, Statistics for Psychology
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Personality and Individual Differences, Research Methods, Abnormal Psychology
Year 3: Advanced Research Design and Statistics, Psychological Assessment, electives across clinical, social, and cognitive streams
Year 4 (Honours, competitive entry): Supervised empirical thesis, advanced seminars, research placement options
APAC accredited — pathway to provisional registration and postgraduate clinical, forensic, or organisational training
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 88+

name: Bachelor of Rehabilitation Studies (exit award only)
description: The Bachelor of Rehabilitation Studies (exit award only) is granted at the University of Queensland to students enrolled in either the Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours) or the Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours) who complete 48 units drawn from years 1 to 3 of those programs but choose, or need, to leave before finishing the full honours qualification. Both parent degrees train students for allied health careers through more than 1,000 hours of supervised clinical practice across hospitals, schools and private practice, accredited by their respective national boards so that graduates can register with AHPRA. A student exiting with the Bachelor of Rehabilitation Studies keeps a recognised qualification covering the shared foundational coursework in anatomy, professional skills and client centred practice from either pathway, useful for allied health support roles or further study, but without the clinical placement hours or accreditation needed to register as an occupational therapist or physiotherapist.
curriculum: This is an exit award from UQ's Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours) or Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours), not a program with its own separate course list. Students are awarded it after completing 48 units drawn from years 1 to 3 of either parent program, which include courses such as Systematic and Applied Anatomy, Introduction to Professional Skills in Occupational Therapy, and Promoting Participation through Occupation and the Environment, before the honours clinical year.
admission_requirements: There is no direct entry pathway for this award. Students reach it only by first being admitted to and enrolling in UQ's Bachelor of Occupational Therapy (Honours) or Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Honours), which require Queensland Year 12 General English and one of Biology, Chemistry or Physics (Units 3 and 4, C), with a minimum adjusted ATAR of 95.5 for occupational therapy in recent intakes.

PTE Academic overall 72, with a minimum of 72 in each communicative skill.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
UQ's Bachelor of Science is a broad, major-driven degree, and the range of majors on offer reflects some genuinely distinctive UQ research strengths: marine biology students get access to the Moreton Bay Research Station on Stradbroke Island for fieldwork, and students interested in genetics or molecular biology sit close to major research institutes like the Institute for Molecular Bioscience and the Australian Institute for Bioengineering and Nanotechnology, both based on the St Lucia campus, giving undergraduates a rare chance to see (and sometimes join) frontier research as an elective or vacation project.

Students choose one or two majors from a long list spanning the physical, life, earth, and mathematical sciences, and the flexibility to combine, say, ecology with data science, or physics with a second science major, is a genuine structural feature rather than marketing language. The degree's unit planner is built around combinability. A capstone science project or thesis in third year is common across most majors, giving students a taste of independent research before deciding whether to pursue honours.

Because UQ's science faculty is large and spread across many buildings and even campuses (Gatton for agriculture-adjacent majors, St Lucia for most others), the actual day-to-day experience varies a lot depending on chosen major. That's a fairly typical feature of large comprehensive science degrees at big research universities, but worth knowing rather than assuming a single unified experience.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundational units across chosen majors (Chemistry, Biology, Physics, Mathematics, Earth Sciences typically among first-year choices), Introduction to Scientific Practice
Year 2: Major-specific core units (one or two majors selected from options including Marine Biology, Genetics, Ecology, Physics, Data Science, Geology, Chemistry), Research Methods
Year 3: Advanced major units, Capstone Science Project, electives
Optional Year 4: Honours year with individual research thesis (competitive entry based on GPA)
Distinctive majors: Marine Biology (fieldwork at Moreton Bay Research Station), Genetics/Molecular Biology (research institute proximity)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 80+, prerequisite Mathematical Methods
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0

name: Bachelor of Social Science
description: The Bachelor of Social Science at the University of Queensland examines social systems, inequality and human behaviour through disciplines including sociology, policy and community development, with strong links kept between theory and real-world practice throughout. Early courses cover social structures and policy before students specialise in one of three majors aligned with their career interests, and a supervised, year-long research project gives students hands-on experience conducting original social research. Core courses include introduction to the social sciences, political problems and public policy, and introduction to social research, and the degree can be combined with a Bachelor of Arts as a dual program. Teaching builds skills in policymaking, advocacy, public communication and project management that employers in the social and government sectors actively look for. Typical graduate roles include community development officer, social and government researcher, and community planning and policy adviser.

A sample of what you study includes: Society, Challenges and Solutions: Introduction to the Social Sciences, Political Problems and Public Policy, Research, Planning and Design, Introduction to social research, Bachelors of Arts / Social Science, Aid project officer, Community development officer, Community planning and policy adviser. Core courses include human development and social work, working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, and the moral and ethical foundations of social work, and teaching uses simulated client encounters so students can practise real-world responses before working with actual clients. Because the profession requires a higher IELTS band than most UQ undergraduate degrees, it is aimed at students with strong English proficiency. Graduates typically move into roles such as counsellor, child welfare worker, family therapist or community worker.

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Science (Honours)
description:
UQ's vet school is the oldest and one of the most internationally recognised in Australia, holding accreditation from the Australasian, American (AVMA), European, and Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons bodies simultaneously, a rare combination that lets graduates practice in a wider range of countries without extra certification than most other vet degrees allow. Most of the clinical years happen at the Gatton campus, about an hour west of Brisbane, where UQ operates its own teaching hospital plus large-animal and equine facilities that give students hands-on experience with production animals most city-based programs can't offer at the same scale.

The six-year Bachelor of Veterinary Science (Honours) folds a science-heavy first two years into increasingly clinical training, with extramural studies (externally supervised placements at private practices, zoos, and specialist referral hospitals) building up across the degree so students graduate with genuine caseload experience rather than only university clinic exposure. UQ's teaching hospital handles a real mixed caseload of companion animals, equine patients, and production animals, and students rotate through all three streams rather than specialising early.

Places are extremely competitive (among the hardest to gain entry to of any UQ program), and the honours research component in the final years gives students who want to go on to specialist veterinary residencies or research careers a genuine head start.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Animal Biology, Biochemistry, Anatomy, Physiology, Animal Husbandry, Veterinary Pathology foundations (largely St Lucia campus)
Years 3-4: Clinical Sciences (companion animal, equine, production animal streams), Veterinary Pharmacology, Diagnostic Imaging, Surgery foundations (transition to Gatton campus)
Years 5-6: Clinical rotations through UQ Veterinary Medical Centre (small animal, equine, production animal), extramural studies placements at external practices, Honours research project
Extramural studies (externally supervised clinical placement weeks) required throughout later years
Accredited by AVBC, AVMA, EAEVE, and RCVS
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with ATAR of approximately 99+, prerequisite Chemistry
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Technology
description: UQ's Bachelor of Veterinary Technology trains students as para-veterinary healthcare specialists, based at UQ's Gatton campus alongside its Small Animal Hospital and Equine Hospital. Core study covers basic sciences such as chemistry and biochemistry, animal handling, welfare and behaviour, applied and clinical nutrition, and diagnostic techniques for animal disease, with electives available in agribusiness, wildlife science and animal production. Students complete 14 weeks of clinical rotation and placement in third year, learning surgical and medical nursing principles and veterinary practice management alongside the small and large animal health curriculum. The program is taught by internationally regarded animal health academics and prepares graduates for a broad range of roles across clinical, commercial, research and diagnostic settings. Typical destinations include veterinary technician, veterinary nurse, laboratory technician and biosecurity officer roles.

name: Bachelor of Wildlife Science
description: The Bachelor of Wildlife Science at the University of Queensland combines zoology, ecology, conservation biology and animal husbandry to train students in protecting species, managing ecosystems and caring for animals in captivity. The first year is based at UQ's St Lucia campus, building a foundation in ecology and animal science, before students move between St Lucia and the Gatton campus in later years depending on their chosen major, such as Captive Wildlife Management. Field experience is built throughout the degree, drawing on Queensland's biodiversity and industry partnerships with Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary, Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary and Hidden Vale Research Station. A dedicated work-integrated learning course prepares students for the realities of wildlife careers rather than only classroom study. Typical graduate roles include environmental biologist, wildlife scientist, conservation officer and ecotourism guide.

name: Doctor of Clinical Dentistry
description: The Doctor of Clinical Dentistry at the University of Queensland is a 3-year postgraduate specialist training program for qualified general dentists working toward specialist registration in fields such as orthodontics, periodontics, prosthodontics, oral medicine or dento-maxillofacial radiology. Teaching and clinical placement take place at UQ's Oral Health Centre, a purpose-built $138 million facility on the Herston campus, with interdisciplinary patient care built into training from the first week. The periodontics stream is accredited by the European Federation of Periodontology, and the degree keeps a research focus running alongside clinical practice under academics with international standing in their specialty. Graduates move directly into specialist dental practice, working as orthodontists, periodontists, prosthodontists or dento-maxillofacial radiologists rather than as general dentists.

name: Doctor of Medicine (MD)
description:
UQ's MD is one of the largest medical programs in Australia by enrolment, which comes with a genuinely unusual feature: a long-running dual accreditation partnership that lets a portion of the cohort complete significant clinical training at Ochsner Health in New Orleans, a legacy of UQ's original push into US-facing medical education in the early 2000s. Most students, though, train through Queensland's own network: Brisbane's major tertiary hospitals (Royal Brisbane and Women's, Princess Alexandra) plus an extensive regional and rural clinical school system stretching to Toowoomba, Rockhampton, Bundaberg, and further afield, reflecting Queensland's genuinely dispersed population and UQ's role in training doctors who will actually work outside the southeast corner.

The four-year graduate-entry MD (after a relevant bachelor's, GAMSAT, and interview) replaced the old MBBS structure, and its first eighteen months are organ-systems based with early clinical exposure through longitudinal GP placements, before students move into full hospital-based clinical rotations for the remainder of the degree.

Because so much of the clinical training happens in regional and rural settings, and because of the Ochsner option for eligible students, the actual training experience varies more between UQ MD students than at a program that keeps everyone in one metropolitan teaching hospital, something prospective applicants should factor in rather than assuming a single uniform experience.
curriculum:
Years 1-2 (pre-clinical/early clinical): Foundations of Medicine (organ systems-based), Clinical Skills, Population and Social Health, longitudinal general practice placements
Years 3-4 (clinical): Core rotations in medicine, surgery, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynaecology, paediatrics, general practice, emergency medicine — delivered through metropolitan teaching hospitals, regional clinical schools (Toowoomba, Rockhampton, Bundaberg), and rural placements
Ochsner Clinical School pathway: eligible students complete extended clinical rotations in New Orleans, USA
Electives and selectives in later clinical years; final-year preparation for internship
Entry: relevant bachelor's degree, GAMSAT, interview (MMI format)
admission_requirements: Completed bachelor degree in any discipline with a competitive GPA, plus GAMSAT and MMI interview
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Architecture, creative arts, education, health, information technology, management and commerce, mathematical sciences, social and cultural studies)
description: This Doctor of Philosophy listing groups several broad University of Queensland research fields, including architecture, creative arts, education, health, information technology, business and commerce, mathematical sciences, and social and cultural studies. In practice UQ runs one PhD research degree and admits candidates by field and school rather than through separate program pages for each discipline group. A PhD at UQ is an internationally recognised research degree in which a candidate works independently, guided by an advisory team, to produce original research and an 80,000 word thesis, defended through an oral examination, typically over 3 to 4 years full-time. UQ enrols around 1,000 PhD candidates a year across its schools, with access to a Career Development Framework for building transferable research and professional skills alongside the thesis. Before applying, a prospective candidate needs to identify a research topic and either secure a supervisor or apply to join an existing project, since admission is assessed against that specific research proposal rather than a generic entry test.
curriculum: The Doctor of Philosophy is a research only degree with no set course list. Candidates work independently, guided by an advisory team, on an original research project in their chosen field, drawing on UQ's library, laboratory and research infrastructure, and complete an 80,000 word thesis plus an oral examination over roughly 3 to 4 years full-time. UQ also offers professional development through its Career Development Framework alongside the research itself.
admission_requirements: You need an approved university degree completed within the last 10 years, demonstrating research experience and capability. Acceptable qualifications include a Master of Philosophy or other research master's degree, a bachelor's degree with at least honours class IIA or equivalent, or a coursework master's degree with an overall grade point average (GPA) of 5.65 on UQ's 7-point scale.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5, with a minimum of 6.0 in each sub band, for most research fields; clinical research projects require an overall score of 7.0 with 7.0 in every sub band. See UQ's English language requirements page for accepted alternative tests.

name: Doctor of Veterinary Clinical Science
description: UQ's Doctor of Veterinary Clinical Science is a 3.5-year veterinary residency and doctoral program for already-qualified veterinarians working toward specialist certification. It combines clinical training in UQ's roughly $100 million veterinary facilities, including a small animal hospital, an equine specialist hospital and a diagnostic laboratory, with a research-based thesis of about 50,000 words. Coursework and supervised clinical work in a diagnostic laboratory or teaching hospital build specialist-level skills in areas such as case management, epidemiology and research methods, and count toward the degree alongside the thesis. UQ's veterinary program is accredited by the Australasian Veterinary Boards Council, the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons and the American Veterinary Medical Association, which supports international recognition of the qualification. Graduates typically become specialist veterinarians in fields such as anatomical pathology, anaesthesiology or equine surgery, in clinical practice, public health agencies or university research.
curriculum: This is UQ's veterinary residency doctorate: a 3.5-year, 56-unit program based at the Gatton campus combining supervised clinical training in an approved veterinary diagnostic laboratory or referral hospital with a research-based thesis of around 50,000 words. Coursework requirements are built around your clinical residency rather than a standard subject list, and the exact structure is confirmed with your supervisor and the UQ Graduate School before you enrol.

Applicants must satisfy the Head of School and Dean of the Graduate School that they are qualified for admission, and may be required to attend an interview. Applicants must be eligible for registration with the Veterinary Surgeons Board of Queensland. Prerequisites BVSc(Hons) with honours class IIB or higher; OR Postgraduate degree in Veterinary Science of at least one year full-time equivalent including relevant experience and an overall GPA of 5; OR BVSc or equivalent plus two years relevant experience, or one year internship under the supervision of a registered veterinary specialist.

name: Graduate Certificate in Agribusiness
description: The Graduate Certificate in Agribusiness is a half-year postgraduate program at UQ's St Lucia campus designed for recent business, agricultural or rural science graduates, and for established professionals moving into agribusiness. Over the program students gain specialised knowledge of agribusiness management alongside business and communication skills, taught by academics and industry experts who cover contemporary issues such as sustainability, globalisation, food security and international trade. Students learn how agribusinesses in different contexts can respond to global opportunities and challenges. It can serve as a standalone qualification or a pathway into the Graduate Diploma or Master of Agribusiness. Graduates work in agribusiness management, agricultural supply chains, trade and marketing, agri-finance and rural policy.

Students select from more than 20 courses across genetics, breeding, nutrition, biosecurity, agronomy, agribusiness and human-wildlife interaction, along with business electives that build management ability. The program develops leadership, research and problem-solving skills aimed at the global challenges of feeding the world and maintaining the environment, and can lead into further study. Graduates work in government, commercial, community and research roles across livestock production, animal nutrition, breeding and genetics, and biosecurity.

name: Graduate Certificate in Applied Linguistics
description: The Graduate Certificate in Applied Linguistics is a half-year postgraduate program at UQ's St Lucia campus that examines how language is structured, learned, used and analysed across cultural and social contexts. It suits educators, language professionals and people working across cultures, starting with language structure, communication and language learning, then moving into multilingualism, language teaching and language use in different settings. Learning combines research-based study with practical analysis tasks. The program can be a standalone qualification or a pathway into the Master of Applied Linguistics. name: Graduate Certificate in Learning Studies (Primary)
description: The Graduate Certificate in Learning Studies (Primary) is an exit award at the University of Queensland rather than a program you apply for directly. It is granted to students enrolled in UQ's Master of Teaching (Primary) who complete at least 8 units of that program's coursework and then choose, or need, to withdraw before finishing the full qualification. The certificate recognises the education theory and classroom foundations covered in the early part of the Master of Teaching (Primary), including child development, literacy and numeracy teaching and inclusive classroom practice, but it is not approved for teacher registration in Australia because it falls short of a full initial teacher education qualification. Students who want to teach in a Queensland primary school need to complete the full Master of Teaching (Primary) or an equivalent accredited program instead. Entry, coursework and English language requirements all mirror the parent Master of Teaching (Primary) program at the point a student is enrolled in it.
curriculum: This is an exit award from UQ's Master of Teaching (Primary), not a program with its own course list. Students are awarded the Graduate Certificate in Learning Studies (Primary) if they withdraw from the Master of Teaching (Primary) after successfully completing at least 8 units drawn from that program's course list, which covers areas such as contemporary theories of development and learning, introduction to teaching mathematics, building inclusive primary classrooms and teaching science. The certificate is not approved for teacher registration in Australia.
admission_requirements: There is no direct entry pathway for this certificate. english_requirements: As an exit award, English language requirements match UQ's Master of Teaching (Primary): IELTS Academic overall 7.5, with a minimum of 8 in speaking and listening and 7 in reading and writing. name: Master of Business Administration
description:
UQ's MBA runs through the triple-accredited UQ Business School, which puts it in the same accreditation tier as a small number of the most established MBA programs in the Asia-Pacific, and the program leans on that reputation with a genuinely international student mix and an emphasis on global business context in its core case studies rather than a purely domestic Australian focus.

The full-time MBA includes an international study tour as a core component in most cohorts. Students travel as a group to a partner region (destinations have included parts of Asia and Europe in past cohorts) for a short but intensive period of company visits and comparative business study, which is a more substantial global-exposure element than a lot of competing Australian MBAs offer as standard. A capstone consulting project, done in teams for a real client organisation, functions as the practical culmination of the degree.

The program can be completed full-time or part-time, and UQ's career development team runs dedicated MBA-specific coaching and employer engagement events, reflecting the fact that most MBA students are mid-career professionals looking for a deliberate career pivot or acceleration rather than a first postgraduate qualification.
curriculum:
Core units: Financial Management, Strategic Marketing, Managerial Economics, Leadership and Organisational Behaviour, Operations Management, Business Analytics and Decision Making
International component: Global Business Study Tour (company visits and comparative study in a partner region)
Electives: choose from streams including entrepreneurship, finance, marketing, health management
Capstone: Strategy Consulting Project (team-based, real client organisation)
Full-time (approx. 1.5 years) or part-time delivery available
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree plus minimum 2 years professional work experience; competitive candidates typically have 5+ years
english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
UQ's computer science research sits inside the School of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering, and the Master of Computer Science draws directly on ITEE's active groups in machine learning, computer vision, and data science rather than existing as a standalone teaching-only degree. Students in the AI-heavy specialisations regularly cross paths with PhD candidates and postdocs in shared labs, which is a genuinely different experience from a pure coursework master's.

The degree is designed as a professional entry qualification for computing, split into an extended (for students without a computing background) and standard pathway (for those with a relevant bachelor's), a structure UQ uses to funnel students from unrelated undergrad degrees, engineering, science, even arts, into software careers without demanding they redo an entire CS bachelor's. Specialisations include artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and software engineering, and the capstone project unit typically pairs students with either an academic research group or, less often, an industry partner sourced through UQ's employability programs.

St Lucia's tech employer proximity is modest compared to Sydney or Melbourne, but Brisbane's tech sector (particularly in gov-tech and health-tech, given Queensland Health's large IT footprint) has grown enough that local placement and graduate hiring pipelines are reasonably active for students who don't want to relocate after finishing.
curriculum:
Extended pathway (no computing background): foundation units in programming, data structures, and discrete mathematics before core coursework
Core coursework: Algorithms and Data Structures, Software Engineering Practice, Programming Languages, Database Systems, Computer Systems
Specialisation (choose one): Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, Data Science
Capstone: Master's Project (research-group or industry-partnered, one to two semesters depending on specialisation)
Standard pathway (relevant bachelor's): condensed core plus specialisation and capstone, typically 1.5 to 2 years
admission_requirements: GPA 5.0/7.0 in a bachelor's degree in computer science or software engineering (1.5-year track), or a bachelor honours degree with broader CS/IT discipline content (1-year track).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall; 6.0 minimum in each of reading, writing, speaking, listening.

The program covers cryptography, cyber criminology, cyber defence and leadership, developed in partnership with industry and government experts in response to Australia's projected shortfall of roughly 18,000 cyber security professionals by 2026. Students study alongside a cohort from diverse backgrounds spanning technology, business, mathematics, social science and law, then complete an industry or research-based project to build workforce-ready experience. It is one of the first Australian programs built around this deliberately interdisciplinary approach to cyber security rather than a purely technical curriculum. Typical graduate roles include cyber security analyst, security consultant, chief information security officer pathway roles and cyber policy adviser.

name: Master of Data Science
description:
UQ's Master of Data Science is a joint offering between the School of Mathematics and Physics and ITEE, which in practice means the curriculum leans more heavily on statistical theory and mathematical foundations than a lot of competing data science master's programs that are essentially applied-CS degrees with a statistics unit bolted on: students spend real time on probability theory and statistical inference before getting to the machine learning and big-data-systems units.

The program is designed to take students from varied undergraduate backgrounds (maths, science, commerce, engineering) through to job-ready data science skills, with an extended pathway for students needing foundational programming or statistics coursework first. UQ's genuine research strength in areas like computational biology and bioinformatics (there's a large research presence in these fields at UQ, including at the Institute for Molecular Bioscience) means some students end up doing capstone projects with an unusually strong life-sciences data flavour compared to the finance- or tech-heavy capstones typical elsewhere.

Brisbane's data science job market is smaller than Sydney's or Melbourne's, but Queensland Health, mining and agribusiness analytics, and a growing gov-tech sector provide a reasonably steady set of local capstone and graduate employer partners for students who complete the program.
curriculum:
Foundation units (extended pathway only): Programming Fundamentals, Introductory Statistics
Core coursework: Statistical Foundations of Data Science, Machine Learning, Big Data Management and Systems, Data Visualisation and Communication
Electives: options across computational biology/bioinformatics, business analytics, natural language processing, computer vision
Capstone: Data Science Project (industry or research-group partnered, one to two semesters)

description: This Master of Philosophy listing groups several broad University of Queensland research fields, including architecture, creative arts, education, health, information technology, business and commerce, mathematical sciences, and social and cultural studies. In practice UQ runs one Master of Philosophy research degree and admits candidates by field and school rather than through separate program pages for each discipline group. An MPhil is a research only postgraduate degree in which a candidate works with an advisory team on an original research project, culminating in a 40,000 word thesis and an oral examination, typically over 1.5 to 2 years full-time. UQ enrols around 500 MPhil candidates a year, and many go on to convert into a PhD once their research is underway. Before applying, a prospective student needs to identify a research topic and a confirmed thesis supervisor within the relevant school, since admission is assessed against that specific proposal rather than a generic entry test.
curriculum: The Master of Philosophy is a research only degree with no set course list. Candidates work independently, guided by an advisory team, on a single research project relevant to their field, drawing on UQ's library and research infrastructure, and complete a 40,000 word thesis plus an oral examination over roughly 1.5 to 2 years full-time.

name: Master of Public Health
description:
UQ's School of Public Health is one of the largest and most research-active in Australia, and the Master of Public Health draws on that scale to offer a genuinely wide set of specialisation streams, including epidemiology, health policy, global health, and environmental health, rather than the generic single-track MPH some smaller schools offer. A meaningful share of the cohort each year is international, often mid-career health professionals from across Asia and the Pacific, which shapes case discussions toward genuinely global health system comparisons rather than an Australia-only lens.

The program includes a substantial applied component: most students complete either a supervised field placement with a health organisation (government health departments, NGOs, or research units) or a research-based project, and UQ's public health research strength in areas like infectious disease modelling and Indigenous health gives some students access to genuinely active research groups for their placement or project supervision.

Because the degree can be tailored heavily through electives, two MPH graduates can come out with quite different skill profiles: one epidemiology and biostatistics-heavy, another policy and health systems-focused. That's a deliberate design feature for a workforce that includes clinicians, policy analysts, and program managers all under the one degree title.
curriculum:
Core units: Foundations of Public Health, Biostatistics, Epidemiology, Health Policy and Systems, Global Health
Specialisation streams (choose one or combine electives): Epidemiology, Health Promotion, Environmental Health, Global Health, Health Economics
Applied component: Field Placement (supervised with a health organisation) or Research Project
Capstone: Public Health Project or Practicum, integrating specialisation coursework
Delivered over 1.5 to 2 years full-time equivalent, part-time options available
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in any discipline plus 1 year relevant healthcare work experience, or graduate certificate/diploma in a relevant discipline, GPA 4.0/7.0
