name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description: The Master of Social Work (Qualifying) at the University of Queensland is a two year, full-time professional entry program for recent graduates and human services workers who want an accredited pathway into social work practice. It suits people with an undergraduate background in psychology, sociology, human services, counselling, criminology, Indigenous studies or a related field, since one year of full-time equivalent study in social and behavioural sciences is a prerequisite. The program combines professional practice courses in health and ageing, child, youth and family services, and mental health with roughly 1,000 hours of supervised practical placement, and coursework covers areas such as the legal and policy context for social work practice and direct practice skills. Graduates are eligible for accreditation with the Australian Association of Social Workers, opening roles in child protection, community development, correctional services, disability services, drug and alcohol services, health services, migrant and refugee support, private practice and youth justice across Australia.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. Sample courses include Lifespan, Culture and Disability, Introduction to Key Elements of Social Work, Direct Practice 1, and The Legal and Policy Context for Social Work Practice, alongside roughly 1,000 hours of supervised professional placement across health, ageing, child and family, and mental health settings. The exact course list is confirmed in UQ's official program and course database at enrolment.

A grade point average (GPA) of 4.0 on UQ's 7-point scale is required.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0, with 7.0 in each of reading, writing, speaking and listening. PTE Academic overall 72, with a minimum of 72 in each communicative skill. See UQ's English language requirements page for the full breakdown and alternative pathways.

name: Master of Software Engineering (Professional)
description: UQ's Master of Software Engineering (Professional) is a 2-year, provisionally Engineers Australia accredited degree covering software design, development and systems architecture at an advanced level. Students complete a research project as part of the program, working on real software engineering problems, and study courses including engineering innovation and leadership and information retrieval and management. The degree responds to strong global demand for skilled software professionals, and UQ notes graduates go on to work at organisations including SAP, Oracle, IBM, LinkedIn and Google. It suits computer science or IT graduates who want a professionally accredited engineering qualification rather than a general computing degree. Typical graduate roles include software engineer, information security analyst, software developer and network and systems engineer.

name: Master of Speech Pathology Studies

Students build on their existing qualifications, expanding theoretical knowledge and professional attributes while gaining the clinical and research skills to graduate with confidence. Graduates work as speech pathologists in hospitals, community and aged care, schools, private practice, disability services and research.

name: Master of Sustainable Energy
description: The Master of Sustainable Energy is a 1.5-year postgraduate program at UQ's St Lucia campus that builds the skills to tackle global energy challenges and the shift to a low-carbon future. Students learn from academics, researchers and industry practitioners about energy generation, distribution and supply, and the transition to sustainable energy, in a flexible structure designed to fit around work. Graduates work in energy policy and planning, renewable energy projects, energy analytics and management across utilities, industry, consulting and government.

name: Master of Teaching (Primary)
description: The Master of Teaching (Primary) at the University of Queensland is a 4-semester graduate-entry qualification for students who already hold an undergraduate degree and want to become registered primary school teachers. Early study covers child development, curriculum design and contemporary theories of learning, before extended professional placements, 60 days of supervised classroom experience in total, let students apply teaching approaches in real Queensland schools. Core courses include introduction to teaching mathematics, building inclusive primary classrooms and teaching science, taught by lecturers with national and international teaching awards. The program is accredited for teacher registration in Queensland and other Australian states, with the option to teach internationally afterwards. Because Queensland teacher registration requires a higher English band than most UQ postgraduate programs, applicants need stronger IELTS scores than a typical master's degree. Graduates typically register as primary school teachers or move into curriculum leadership roles.

name: Master of Urban Development and Design
description: UQ's Master of Urban Development and Design trains students to approach cities strategically and holistically, treating urban design as its own discipline rather than a specialism borrowed from architecture or planning. Core courses include urban design: urban futures, contemporary urbanism theory and practice, and urban design: responsive environments, alongside a course in managing organisational behaviour for students who will lead urban projects. The program is aimed at addressing growing global demand for urban designers who can respond to limited resources, population growth and climate change with a strategic view of how cities work rather than one-off design solutions. It suits both working professionals and graduates from architecture, planning or related fields who want to specialise further. Typical graduate roles include urban designer, urban strategist, community engagement consultant and landscape architect.
curriculum: UQ calls subjects "courses" within this program. A sample of what you will study includes: Urban Design: Urban Futures, Contemporary Urbanism Theory and Practice, Urban Design: Responsive Environments, Managing Organisational Behaviour. Relevant work experience must be supported by a signed employer letter detailing your role, duties and length of employment.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5; TOEFL iBT overall 87. UQ also accepts Cambridge C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency, OET and other approved English tests; see UQ's English language requirements page for the full sub band breakdown and alternative pathways.

name: Master of Urban Planning
description: The Master of Urban Planning at the University of Queensland is an accredited qualification from the Planning Institute of Australia, aimed at professionals or graduates ready to move into leadership and advisory roles in city planning. Students choose a field of study in Environment and Sustainability, Urban Analytics, or Research in Urbanism, and build advanced expertise across transport and infrastructure planning, environmental planning, statutory planning and community engagement. Coursework is built around authentic planning challenges worked through with industry, government and community stakeholders rather than only theoretical case studies, taught by academics who are also practising planners. It suits graduates of the Bachelor of Urban Planning or a related discipline who want formal accreditation and advanced skills rather than an entry-level qualification. Typical graduate roles include urban planner, strategic planner, urban strategist and research analyst in government planning departments or consultancies.
curriculum: This 32-unit program (2-year full pathway, or a 1.5-year pathway with 8 units of recognised prior learning) combines foundation courses such as Applied Demography, Urban Innovations, Urban Law and Regulation, and Transport Planning with core courses including Planning Systems and Governance, Planning for Social Change, Urban Infrastructure Transitions, Data Science and Technology for Planners, Urban Policy Impact Lab, and Urban Design: Urban Futures. Students then choose a Field of Study such as Environment and Sustainability, Research in Urbanism, or Urban Analytics, plus program or general electives.
admission_requirements: This program has two entry pathways. For the 2-year, 32-unit degree you need a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in any discipline, except qualifications accredited by the Planning Institute of Australia, with a GPA of 4.5 on a 7-point scale. For the accelerated 1.5-year, 24-unit degree (using recognised prior learning) you need a bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline such as urban or regional planning, architecture, urban design, environment, design, engineering or geography, or a bachelor's degree in a non-relevant discipline plus 2 years full-time equivalent relevant work experience in urban and regional planning, again with a GPA of 4.5.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5; TOEFL iBT overall 87. UQ also accepts Cambridge C1 Advanced, C2 Proficiency, OET and other approved English tests; see UQ's English language requirements page for the full sub band breakdown and alternative pathways.

name: Master of Urban Water Engineering (Professional)
description: The Master of Urban Water Engineering (Professional) at the University of Queensland is an Engineers Australia accredited degree that trains engineers to manage the whole urban water cycle, from drinking water supply through to wastewater treatment. Core courses cover drinking water supply source, treatment and distribution, and sewer network design, operation and maintenance, addressing a global shortage of engineers who understand how the different parts of the urban water system interact. The program responds directly to growing water stress in dense, urbanising cities, a trend UQ expects to continue rather than reverse. Students can select electives to complement their existing engineering background, and the degree suits civil or environmental engineers moving into water-specific specialisation. Typical graduate roles include wastewater treatment engineer, urban engineer and water infrastructure consultant.

name: Master of Writing, Editing and Publishing

Students learn from award-winning authors and publishing professionals, including UQ Press and Corella Press, building a foundation across publishing practice, workplace writing, editing techniques and digital storytelling before shaping their studies around creative or professional interests. Graduates work in publishing, editing, content, communications and freelance writing.

name: Associate Degree of Medical Laboratory Science
Bachelor of Agricultural Technology and Management
description:
UniSQ describes this as Queensland's first dedicated degree in agricultural technology and management, and the pitch is specific: it sits between traditional agricultural science and straight agribusiness, training students to apply precision-ag and digital technology to farm systems rather than just studying plant and animal science in the abstract or business theory divorced from paddock reality. Students based at Toowoomba get direct access to the working farming and agtech industries of the Darling Downs, one of Australia's most productive agricultural regions, and the course can also be completed externally for students already working in the sector.

At 24 units it's a leaner degree than most three-year bachelor's programs, built around agricultural science fundamentals (plant and animal production systems), the technology layer (precision agriculture, remote sensing, farm data systems), and the management side (agribusiness, supply chains, farm business decision-making). Work-integrated learning and industry placement units are built into the structure, which matters in a discipline where employers routinely rate practical exposure above classroom theory.

Graduates are aimed at roles in agronomy support, farm technology and precision-ag consulting, agribusiness management, and agricultural data analysis, a narrower but more targeted set of outcomes than a general agricultural science degree, reflecting the technology-and-management framing the course was actually built around.
curriculum:
Year 1: Plant production systems, animal production systems, introduction to agricultural technology, farm business fundamentals
Year 2: Precision agriculture and remote sensing, soil and water management, agribusiness and supply chains, agricultural data systems
Year 3: Farm business management and decision-making, industry placement/work-integrated learning, capstone agricultural technology project, elective units in a chosen specialisation
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, no specific ATAR cut-off; suited to students from rural and regional backgrounds, with articulation pathways from the Diploma of Agriculture and Environmental Science Studies.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
UniSQ's Bachelor of Business follows the standard flexible-major structure most Australian business schools use now: a shared first-year core across accounting, economics, marketing, and management, then students pick a major: accounting, marketing, management, human resource management, tourism, or a handful of others, and build the back two years around it. What sets the delivery apart is less the content than the mode: a large share of the cohort studies wholly online, and the university has built its systems around that being the default rather than an add-on for people who can't make it to campus.

The degree carries professional accreditation pathways relevant to its majors, the accounting major is designed to meet the academic requirements for CPA Australia and CA ANZ membership, for instance, so students with a specific professional body in mind can check their major choice against that requirement early rather than discovering a gap in final year.

A capstone business project or internship unit toward the end of the degree gives students a chance to apply what they've studied to an actual organisational problem, and the university's regional business networks around Toowoomba and southeast Queensland feed a reasonable number of those placements.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting principles, economics, marketing fundamentals, management and organisational behaviour, business law, business statistics
Year 2: Major core units (accounting, marketing, management, HR, or tourism strand), business analytics, financial management
Year 3: Advanced major units, strategic management, capstone business project or industry placement, elective units
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (Queensland Certificate of Education) or equivalent, ATAR of approximately 60-65 or equivalent; no prerequisite subjects required.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Design and Interactive Technologies
Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
Primary teaching at UniSQ is a four-year initial teacher education degree accredited against the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers, and it leads to registration as a primary school teacher on graduation. That's the standard shape for this qualification nationally, but UniSQ's version leans on its regional footprint for placement variety, with school partnerships across the Darling Downs, Ipswich, and wider southeast Queensland giving students a mix of regional and larger-town classroom experience rather than an exclusively metropolitan one.

Curriculum studies units cover the primary learning areas (literacy, numeracy, science, HASS, health and PE, the arts) alongside professional units in child development, inclusive education, and classroom management, with supervised professional experience placements building in length and responsibility each year, from observation-heavy early placements to a substantial final-year internship where students effectively run a classroom under a mentor teacher's supervision.

A sizeable share of the cohort studies externally, particularly students already working as teacher aides or in regional schools, and the degree is structured so placement blocks can be arranged around a student's existing location rather than requiring relocation to a university city.
curriculum:
Year 1: Child development, introduction to teaching and learning, foundations of literacy and numeracy, first professional experience placement
Year 2: Curriculum studies (English, mathematics, science), inclusive education, classroom management, professional experience placement
Year 3: Curriculum studies (HASS, the arts, health and PE), assessment and reporting, Indigenous perspectives in education, extended professional experience placement
Year 4: Advanced pedagogy, professional capstone unit, final internship placement (extended, near-autonomous teaching)
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, ATAR of approximately 60-65 or equivalent, plus satisfactory completion of the Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education (LANTITE) prior to final-year professional experience placement.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 7.0 (or equivalent), reflecting Queensland teacher registration standards.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Ask most Queensland engineering academics who teaches the most students by distance and UniSQ's name comes up first: the university has run distance-education engineering programs for more than four decades and is Australia's largest provider of engineering degrees delivered off-campus. The Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) is the degree that carries that reputation, and it shows in how the labs are built: UniSQ's Remote Access Laboratories let external students run real instrumentation and measurement experiments over the internet rather than substituting simulations for hands-on work.

Students choose a major from the usual spread (civil, electrical and electronic, mechanical, mechatronic, power, and others) and the degree is accredited by Engineers Australia, so graduates sit the same accreditation bar as anyone from a metro sandstone university. A supervised professional placement is built into the course, which matters more than it sounds for a program with a large external cohort: it's the mechanism that gets distance students onto an actual work site before graduation, not just into a classroom.

The university has also been ranked Australia's number one for graduate starting salary by the Good Universities Guide, a data point UniSQ leans on in its own marketing but which is at least consistent with an engineering-heavy graduate profile. Whether a given student is based in Toowoomba, Springfield, or studying entirely online from a mine site or a regional town, the course structure and assessment are designed to be identical, which is unusual enough among Australian engineering schools to be worth naming directly.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Engineering mathematics and mechanics, engineering materials, engineering computing, professional engineering practice, discipline foundation units (statics, thermofluids, circuits depending on major)
Year 3: Major-specific core units (e.g. structural analysis for civil, power systems for electrical, machine design for mechanical), engineering management, project management
Year 4: Capstone engineering project (two-part), professional placement/work-integrated learning, advanced major electives, engineering law and ethics
Throughout: Remote Access Laboratory sessions and residential schools for practical/lab components
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 with sound achievement in English and Mathematics (Methods or equivalent recommended), ATAR of approximately 70-75 or equivalent; a Preparatory year is available for students who do not meet prerequisites.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description:
This is the entry-level computing degree UniSQ builds its whole postgraduate IT pipeline around. Finish it and the university explicitly points graduates toward its Master of Information Technology, Master of Data Science, or Master of Cyber Security as the next step, which tells you something about how the undergraduate course is structured: broad enough in first year to let students discover which specialisation actually interests them, then increasingly focused from second year on.

Majors run through the usual spread for a modern IT degree, including software development, cyber security, networking, data science and analytics, and programming-heavy units are backed by UniSQ's long-running remote/online lab infrastructure, the same systems that support its distance engineering cohort, so external students aren't working with a lesser version of the practical content.

A professional placement or capstone project unit near the end of the course gives students something concrete to point to in job interviews beyond a transcript, and the degree's accreditation alignment with the Australian Computer Society matters for students planning to chase ACS-recognised professional status after graduation.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming fundamentals, computer systems, database fundamentals, web technologies, IT professional practice
Year 2: Major core units (software development, cyber security, networking, or data science strand), systems analysis and design, data structures and algorithms
Year 3: Advanced major electives, IT project management, capstone IT project or industry placement, emerging technologies elective
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent, ATAR of approximately 60-65 or equivalent; no specific prerequisite subjects, though Mathematics is recommended.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Nursing at UniSQ is delivered from a regional base (Toowoomba and Ipswich rather than inner-city Brisbane), which shapes where a lot of its clinical placements happen: students get real exposure to rural and regional health settings that metro-heavy nursing schools often can't offer as standard, alongside placements in larger hospital systems. The degree is accredited by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia, and graduates sit for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse on completion.

The course structure follows the pattern most Australian nursing degrees use: foundational anatomy, physiology, and pharmacology units in first year, building toward specialty clinical units (mental health, paediatrics, aged care, acute care) in second and third year, with supervised clinical placement hours threaded through every year rather than saved for the end. UniSQ's placement network covers regional Queensland health services as well as metropolitan hospitals, which is a genuine point of difference for students who want experience in under-served health systems before they graduate into them.

Students who want to keep studying can move directly into UniSQ's Master of Nursing for a postgraduate specialisation, and the university markets a fairly direct undergraduate-to-postgraduate nursing pipeline for exactly that reason.
curriculum:
Year 1: Anatomy and physiology, foundations of nursing practice, pharmacology basics, communication in health care, introductory clinical placement
Year 2: Mental health nursing, medical-surgical nursing, pathophysiology, health assessment, clinical placement blocks
Year 3: Acute and critical care nursing, aged care and chronic illness, paediatric and family nursing, transition to professional practice, capstone clinical placement
Throughout: Supervised clinical placements across regional and metropolitan health settings, professional experience portfolio
admission_requirements: Completion of Australian Year 12 (Queensland Certificate of Education) or equivalent, no specific ATAR cut-off, plus a Health Undertaking and National Police Check; relevant recognition of prior learning available for enrolled nurses.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 6.5, or equivalent (higher than most UniSQ programs due to nursing registration requirements).

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description:
UniSQ's Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) is a four-year, APAC-accredited sequence built for students who already know they want provisional registration at the end of it, not just a psychology-adjacent arts degree. The first three years share a common set of foundational units with the university's other psych-flavoured degrees, so students who start here and change their mind about the honours pathway aren't locked in early. The divergence happens later, once the fourth-year research component kicks in.

That fourth year is where the degree earns its name. Students complete an honours research project (PSY4000) alongside units in advanced research methods, ethical and professional practice, and applied assessment and intervention skills, working under the supervision of academic staff who are themselves practising or research psychologists. Because a large share of UniSQ's cohort studies externally, the clinical and assessment skills components are built around structured on-campus intensives and simulated client work rather than assuming everyone is walking past a psych clinic on campus daily.

Graduates come out eligible for provisional registration as a psychologist with AHPRA, which is the real value proposition of choosing the Honours pathway over a plain Bachelor's: it's the entry ticket to supervised practice or further postgraduate study toward general or clinical registration. UniSQ explicitly positions this degree as a pipeline into its own Master of Professional Psychology, so students planning that far ahead can map out a five-plus-one style progression from day one.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Biological Psychology, Lifespan Development, Social Psychology, foundational research methods and statistics units

Master of Business Administration
description:
UniSQ's MBA follows the generalist model most Australian MBAs use: core units across strategy, finance, marketing, leadership, and organisational behaviour, aimed at experienced professionals moving into or already working in management roles rather than fresh graduates. Where it departs from the metro-university MBA template is delivery: it's built primarily for students studying externally while working full-time, which shapes the assessment design around applied, workplace-relevant projects rather than assuming students have time for extended residential intensives.

Students typically bring several years of workplace experience into the cohort, and case studies and group assignments lean on that mix of industries and seniority levels rather than assuming a uniform corporate background. A capstone strategic management project toward the end of the degree asks students to apply the accumulated coursework to a real organisational problem, often drawn from their own workplace.

The degree doesn't chase the specific big-name accreditations (AACSB, EQUIS) that the most prestige-focused Australian MBAs market heavily, and is positioned instead as an accessible, flexible option for regional and remote professionals who need postgraduate business credentials without relocating or taking time off work.
curriculum:
Core units: Strategic management, managerial finance, marketing management, organisational behaviour and leadership, business economics, operations management
Elective units: Selected from specialisations such as project management, human resource management, or international business
Capstone: Strategic management project (applied, often workplace-based)
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree plus at least two years of professional work experience, or a graduate certificate/diploma in a related discipline; delivered fully online.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent.
intake_dates: February, April, July, September, November (online, multiple study periods)

name: Master of Data Science
description:
The Master of Data Science runs on twelve core ICT and analytics units rather than a long menu of loosely related electives, which keeps the degree tight: statistics, machine learning, big data systems, and data visualisation are treated as the spine of the course rather than optional add-ons bolted onto a generic IT masters. Students coming in with an undergraduate background outside computing typically pick up a set of foundation units first to bring their programming and stats up to postgraduate speed before moving into the specialist content.

What distinguishes it from a lot of similarly-named degrees elsewhere is that it's taught by a university that has spent decades building distance-delivery infrastructure, so the heavily technical, lab-based components (model building, data pipeline work, visualisation projects) are designed from the ground up for students working through them off-campus, often while employed full-time. A capstone project lets students apply the full analytics pipeline to a real or realistic dataset, which is the piece employers tend to ask about at interview.

Graduates leave positioned for data analyst, data engineer, or junior data scientist roles, and the degree sits alongside UniSQ's Master of Information Technology and Master of Cyber Security as one of three postgraduate computing options the university actively cross-promotes to its own IT undergraduates.
curriculum:
Foundation units (where required): Programming fundamentals, database systems, introductory statistics
Core: Data wrangling and management, statistical modelling, machine learning, big data technologies, data visualisation, data ethics and governance, cloud computing for data science
Capstone: Data science project (industry or research-based)
Maximum candidature: six years part-time, allowing for concurrent full-time work
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Education
description:
UniSQ's Master of Education is aimed at people already teaching, not career-changers looking for an initial qualification. It's a postgraduate degree for practising educators who want to specialise or move into leadership, and the course design assumes students are working full-time in schools while they study. Specialisation strands typically cover areas like educational leadership, TESOL, inclusive education, and curriculum studies, and students can usually shape a chunk of the degree around whichever of those matches their actual career direction.

Because the degree sits within a university whose delivery model has been built around distance and online study for decades, assessment is structured around what a working teacher can realistically produce alongside a full timetable: applied projects and research tied to the student's own school context rather than requiring long stretches of campus attendance.

A research-focused exit option (often a minor thesis or major project) exists for teachers considering a later move into doctoral study or educational research roles, alongside the more common coursework-only completion for those staying in the classroom or moving into middle leadership.
curriculum:
Core units: Educational research methods, contemporary issues in education, leading learning and teaching
Specialisation units (select strand): Educational leadership, TESOL, inclusive and special education, or curriculum and pedagogy
Elective units: Drawn from education specialisations or cross-disciplinary options
Exit options: Coursework-only completion, or research project/minor thesis pathway for those considering further postgraduate research
admission_requirements: A relevant bachelor degree, normally in education or a related field, or a bachelor degree plus relevant professional teaching experience; designed for practising teachers seeking specialisation or career progression.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0, or equivalent (reflecting teacher registration requirements).

name: Master of Nursing
description:
This is UniSQ's postgraduate specialisation route for registered nurses who've finished their undergraduate degree and want to move into advanced clinical practice, education, or leadership rather than staying at generalist RN level indefinitely. It's built for working nurses: the majority of the cohort studies externally while holding down clinical shifts. Specialisation strands typically include areas like nurse practitioner preparation, clinical leadership, or nurse education, depending on which stream a student enrols in.

Coursework covers advanced clinical assessment, evidence-based practice, and health systems leadership, with a research or applied project component that lets students investigate a genuine clinical or workplace issue rather than a hypothetical one. Given UniSQ's Bachelor of Nursing graduates are steered toward this degree as the next step, there's a reasonably well-worn pathway from RN registration through to postgraduate specialisation within the one institution.

Students pursuing the nurse practitioner stream complete additional advanced practice and prescribing units alongside supervised clinical hours, positioning them for endorsement as nurse practitioners, a role with growing demand in the regional and rural health services UniSQ's own placement network already covers.
curriculum:
Core units: Advanced health assessment, evidence-based practice, health systems and leadership, research methods for nursing
Specialisation strand: Nurse practitioner preparation (advanced pharmacology, diagnostics, prescribing) or clinical leadership/education strand
Applied/research component: Clinical project or minor research thesis
For NP stream: Supervised advanced clinical practice placements
admission_requirements: A bachelor degree in a health-related discipline (a non-nursing entry pathway is available), or a Bachelor of Nursing for registered nurses seeking advanced standing; current registration or eligibility for registration with AHPRA required for the nursing-entry stream.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 6.5, or equivalent, consistent with nursing registration standards.

name: Master of Professional Psychology
description:
This is the degree UniSQ points its own Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) graduates toward, and it functions as the next rung on the registration ladder for students who've done the four-year undergraduate sequence and want to keep moving toward broader practice rights rather than stopping at provisional registration. The course combines advanced coursework in assessment, intervention, and professional ethics with a substantial supervised practicum placement: the applied hours are the actual point of the degree, not a formality attached to it.

Students work with clients under supervision as part of the practicum component, building the direct-practice hours AHPRA expects to see before general registration, and the coursework side covers assessment techniques, evidence-based interventions, and the professional and ethical frameworks that govern psychological practice in Australia.

Because UniSQ runs a large distance cohort, the placement component is coordinated across a wider geographic spread of supervising psychologists and services than a metro-only program would need, which in practice means students in regional Queensland aren't stuck waiting for a city-based placement to open up.
curriculum:
Core coursework: Advanced psychological assessment, evidence-based interventions, professional ethics and practice standards, psychopathology
Applied component: Supervised practicum placement (staged across the degree, building client contact hours)
Research component: Applied research project or case-based research unit
Professional development: Practice management and supervision seminars
admission_requirements: An Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC) accredited four-year psychology qualification (e.g. Bachelor of Psychology Honours) with a credit average or better; competitive entry due to limited places.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, no band below 7.0, or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Advanced Computing
description:
The Bachelor of Advanced Computing at the University of Sydney is accredited by the Australian Computer Society and lets students specialise in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Software Development or Computational Data Science, combined with a shared pool of more than 100 majors. Core units build the design principles and programming skills behind technologies from intelligent drones and virtual reality to cybersecurity and the Internet of Things, alongside an Advanced Computing major and elective units.
Students can add a minor or second major from the disciplinary pool or elsewhere in the University. Graduates move into roles such as big data analyst, computer programmer, cybersecurity analyst, software architect and software project manager. Sydney is ranked first in Australia for computer science and information systems.

description:
The Bachelor of Agricultural Economics at the University of Sydney, delivered through the Bachelor of Agricultural Science, builds skills in crop production, animal production, soil science, food science and agricultural economics at Australia's first university for agricultural science. Core study covers agricultural science, biology, animal management, agronomy, agricultural markets, statistics, genetics and digital agriculture, alongside one of eight cognate majors and training in sensors, robotics and data analytics for modern farming.
The University of Sydney is ranked 18th globally in the QS World University Rankings 2025. Graduates move into roles including agricultural business manager, agricultural policy maker, consulting agronomist and food scientist.

The course suits students seeking fundamental and applied knowledge in animal bioscience as a pathway into veterinary and animal science industries, including research, policy, farm management and, with further study in Sydney's Doctor of Veterinary Medicine, veterinary practice itself.

The Bachelor of Applied Science (Exercise and Sport Science) Honours at the University of Sydney is a fourth year of study in which graduates of the pass degree design and complete an original research project under the supervision of a senior academic. Honours topics can focus on a specific area of health care practice, a topical health issue, or interventions that aim to improve health outcomes.
Students work closely with academic supervisors to design, implement and write up their research as a thesis, developing specialist knowledge and research skills that extend career options beyond the pass degree. Sydney is ranked fourth in the world for sports-related subjects.

The Bachelor of Architecture and Environments at the University of Sydney gives students a broad overview of the built environment through core units in design and architecture, urban planning, sustainability, building systems, and construction and property. The Bachelor of Biomedicine and Health at the University of Sydney gives students a comprehensive understanding of human biology, health, disease and treatment alongside approaches to public health and the health care system. Delivered at the University's Westmead campus within the Westmead Health Precinct, one of Australia's largest health zones, students learn alongside two major teaching hospitals and the largest pathology service in New South Wales.
The three-year course suits students building toward a range of health sector careers or further postgraduate study to become a health professional. Graduates move into health management, health promotion and related roles across the health care sector.

name: Bachelor of Education Studies
description: The Bachelor of Education Studies at the University of Sydney is delivered through the Bachelor of Education (Primary), an initial teacher education degree with in-school experience from the first semester, building to a fourth-year professional placement where students teach with minimal supervision. Graduates are prepared for registration and work as primary school teachers, and for leadership and reflective practice roles. Indicative international tuition is around 62,400 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Engineering
description:
The Bachelor of Engineering Honours (Flexible First Year) at the University of Sydney lets students explore different engineering disciplines before committing to a stream, starting with a common set of units in mathematics, computing and an introduction to engineering. At the start of second semester, students transfer into their chosen stream, from aeronautical, biomedical and chemical to civil, electrical, mechanical, mechatronic and software engineering.
The course suits students who are unsure which engineering discipline to pursue and want to explore before deciding. Career pathways depend on the chosen stream, spanning aeronautical, biomedical, chemical, civil, electrical, mechanical, mechatronic and software engineering roles.

name: Bachelor of Engineering Honours (Civil Engineering)
description:
The Bachelor of Engineering Honours (Civil Engineering) at the University of Sydney develops comprehensive technical knowledge to plan, design and test structures within the built and natural environment, from buildings and transport networks to water and irrigation systems. Core units in mathematics and computing are combined with multidisciplinary project units and embedded professional, managerial, organisational, financial and environmental skills, and the course is accredited by Engineers Australia.
One-year exchange programs are available with partner universities in Europe, Asia and North America. Graduates move into roles across construction, mining, municipal councils, transport systems, water and sanitation, and international infrastructure aid. Sydney is ranked second in Australia and 28th in the world for civil and structural engineering.

description:
The Bachelor of Engineering Honours (Software Engineering) at the University of Sydney covers all aspects of software production, from strategy and design to coding, quality and management, including programming languages, data structures, algorithms, databases and operating systems. The course is accredited by Engineers Australia, combining foundational core units in mathematics and computing with multidisciplinary project units and stream-specific software engineering units.
One-year exchange programs are available with partner universities in Europe, Asia and North America. Graduates move into roles including software analyst and engineer, information security specialist, database programmer, web developer and artificial intelligence specialist.

description: The Bachelor of Environmental Systems at the University of Sydney is delivered through the Bachelor of Science, which offers more than 40 science majors, programs and streams including environmental science, alongside shared majors and a flexible degree plan. Students gain essential knowledge in the fundamental sciences in first year before specialising. Graduates work in environmental science, research, consulting and government. name: Bachelor of Global Studies
description: The Bachelor of Global Studies at the University of Sydney is delivered through the Bachelor of International and Global Studies, a three-year full-time degree, with an honours year of advanced research-centred study available. Students study global political, economic, social and cultural issues and can undertake an in-depth research thesis in the honours year. Graduates work in diplomacy, policy, international development, business and research. Indicative international tuition is around 54,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of Health Sciences (Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Health Sciences (Honours) at the University of Sydney is a one-year research program for students who completed a Bachelor of Health Sciences, or an equivalent degree at another institution, before 2017. The year combines lectures and seminars with an individually supervised research project, giving students the chance to plan, conduct and report an original piece of health sciences research.
Honours topics can address a specific area of health care practice or a current health issue. Graduates move into health promotion, policymaking, project and case management, consultancy, business development and public relations roles.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Information Technology
description: The University of Sydney no longer admits new students to a standalone Bachelor of Information Technology. Its current undergraduate computing degree is the Bachelor of Advanced Computing, a four-year program in the Faculty of Engineering with majors in computer science, cybersecurity, software development and computational data science, which can also be taken combined with commerce, science, arts, law or the Dalyell scholars stream. Students who specifically want an information-systems focus can take the Bachelor of Commerce with a Business Information Systems major. For postgraduate study, Sydney offers the Master of Information Technology and the Master of Computer Science. This page is kept for reference because the Bachelor of Information Technology still appears in older listings and in the CRICOS register. International tuition for the Bachelor of Advanced Computing is around A$63,400 per year.
discontinued_note: This award now sits within the Bachelor of Advanced Computing, with specialisations in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Software Development and Computational Data Science.

name: Bachelor of Information Techonology (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Information Technology (Honours) at the University of Sydney is now offered through the Bachelor of Advanced Computing, an accredited degree covering IT, computer science and software engineering. Students learn the design principles and programming skills behind emerging information technologies, from intelligent drones and virtual reality to cybersecurity and the Internet of Things. Graduates work as software engineers, computing specialists and technology consultants. Indicative international tuition is around 60,600 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of International and Global Studies
description: The Bachelor of International and Global Studies at the University of Sydney is a three-year full-time degree examining global political, economic, social and cultural issues, with an honours year of advanced research-centred study available. Students take seminar classes and, in the honours year, research and write a substantial thesis with a specialist supervisor. Graduates work in diplomacy, policy, international development, business and research. Indicative international tuition is around 54,100 Australian dollars per year.

name: Bachelor of International Studies (Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of International Studies (Honours) at the University of Sydney is a one-year, full-time program developing research skills in international studies through a substantial original project, for students interested in languages, cultures, global politics and history. Students complete two seminar units from history, languages and cultures, or social sciences, plus an independent research project culminating in a thesis of around 20,000 words.
The course suits high-achieving Bachelor of International Studies graduates preparing for PhD-level research. Graduates move into roles including policy adviser, diplomat, trade negotiator, defence adviser, international business consultant and human rights advocate.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Languages
description:
The Bachelor of Languages at the University of Sydney immerses students in global languages and cultures, building high-level intercultural skills through a modern language major, translation theory and practical translation projects. Students can access exchange scholarships to study abroad with international partners, and pursue further study in business, economics, humanities or science through the University's shared pool of majors and minors.
The course is an endorsed qualification for the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters at the Certified Translator level. Graduates move into roles including translator, foreign affairs and trade officer, journalist, museum curator and public relations officer.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description: The University of Sydney does not offer a standalone undergraduate Bachelor of Laws for direct school-leaver entry. Its undergraduate law degree is available only as a combined degree, pairing the Bachelor of Laws with another bachelor's degree such as arts, commerce, economics, science, advanced studies or engineering honours. These combined programs run five years or more and total around 240 to 312 credit points, of which 144 credit points are law units, including 102 credit points of compulsory law study. Students who already hold a bachelor's degree in another field enter law through the graduate-entry Juris Doctor instead. This page is kept for reference because a standalone Bachelor of Laws appears in the CRICOS register and older course listings. International tuition for the law component is around A$58,000 per year.

The Bachelor of Liberal Arts and Science (Honours) at the University of Sydney is a stand-alone additional year of study open to graduates who have completed the pass degree, undertaken in any area of science or arts in consultation with one or more supervisors. Students design a research program that may span more than one discipline, such as physiology and biology, with additional coursework or technical training as required by the project.
The Faculty of Science has a strong record in postgraduate research funding and supervision. Graduates move into careers spanning academia, science media, administration, education and business, shaped by their chosen major.

The Bachelor of Liberal Arts and Science at the University of Sydney gives students a background in both the humanities and the sciences, with flexibility across a wide range of majors. Core and core selective liberal studies units cover academic writing, critical thinking and ethics, with a major chosen from the Arts or Science disciplinary pools plus supporting units from the other faculty.
The course suits curious students who want breadth across disciplines rather than a single specialised area. Graduates move into roles spanning academia, administration, education and business, shaped by their chosen major.

name: Bachelor of Mathematical Sciences
description:
The Bachelor of Mathematical Sciences at the University of Sydney builds a competitive edge in mathematics, computing, data analysis and problem-solving, with pathways in pure and applied mathematics, statistics, financial mathematics and data science. From the first year, students engage with core concepts in mathematics, statistics and data science, then tackle increasingly complex problems and group projects that require independent hypothesis formation and critical evaluation of evidence.
Graduates move into roles including business analyst, bioinformatician, data scientist, economic modeller, energy forecaster and quantitative analyst in banking. The University of Sydney is ranked 18th globally in the QS World University Rankings 2025.

The Bachelor of Media and Communications at the University of Sydney combines professional training in media production with an advanced education in the history, theory and professional practices of media. Students complete degree core units and a media studies major covering media production, the structure of media and communications industries, and contemporary legal and ethical issues, adding breadth through minors and electives.
The course includes hands-on learning and internships to launch students into careers as journalists, editors, producers, digital producers, content creators, social media managers and public relations consultants.

description:
The Bachelor of Medical Science (Honours) at the University of Sydney is a stand-alone research year available to students who have completed the University's Bachelor of Medical Science, combining a supervised independent research project with coursework units in experimental design and technical training. Honours projects are available across the Faculty of Science's schools, with the specific structure varying by discipline area.
The Faculty of Science has a strong record in postgraduate research funding and supervision. Graduates move into medical research, pathology, histology, physiology, microbiology, biochemistry, biomedical device design, and further study toward medicine or dentistry.

description:
The Bachelor of Music (Music Education) at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music prepares students to become music teachers in primary or secondary schools, combining performance, composition and the latest teaching techniques and technology. Students choose a study focus in performance, composition, contemporary music practice or musicology, alongside music education, choral and instrumental pedagogy, and music technology training.
Students also build information and communication technology competencies and an understanding of children with special educational needs. Graduates move into roles as music teachers, performing soloists, chamber musicians, orchestral players and community music educators.

description:
The Bachelor of Music Studies (Honours) at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music is an appended year open to graduates of a Bachelor of Music at the Conservatorium or an approved degree elsewhere, combining research seminars, classes and individual lessons with an independent research project. The year completes a music education while preparing students for postgraduate study such as a Doctor of Musical Arts or PhD.
Students specialise in their principal study while working with internationally recognised music academics at the Conservatorium. Honours graduates move into performance, teaching, research and other music-related career paths.

name: Bachelor of Nursing (Advanced Studies)
description:
The Bachelor of Nursing (Advanced Studies) at the University of Sydney prepares students for registered nursing practice with an added focus on leadership, critical decision-making and understanding of the local and global health landscape. Core study covers anatomy and pathophysiology, pharmacology, clinical and relational skills, and the sociological determinants of health, alongside clinical placements across varied nursing specialties.
The advanced curriculum builds engaged, globally aware health professionals ready for a wide range of practice areas. Graduates work in paediatric, intensive care, trauma, emergency and community health roles across metropolitan, regional and remote Australia and internationally.

description:
The Bachelor of Oral Health at the University of Sydney is a three-year degree that graduates students with a dual qualification in dental hygiene and dental therapy. The course develops skills to prevent disease and manage oral health conditions with an adult restorative scope of practice, and graduates are licensed to use diagnostic radiation on registration with the Dental Board of Australia.
Oral health therapists work across school and community dental services, hospitals, residential care and both general and specialist private practice. Sydney has invested in a dedicated dental simulation clinic for hands-on clinical training.

name: Bachelor of Pharmacy
description:
The Bachelor of Pharmacy (Honours) and Master of Pharmacy Practice at the University of Sydney is a vertically integrated degree preparing students for professional pharmacy practice, incorporating the Pharmacy Board of Australia's intern training program and supervised practice requirements. Over five years, students build a comprehensive understanding of how medicines are developed and how they affect the human body, combined with hands-on clinical experience.
Graduates are eligible for general registration as a pharmacist after completing the required examination, and go on to work in community and hospital pharmacy, primary care, clinical trials, research, regulatory affairs and manufacturing. Sydney is ranked 16th globally for pharmacy and pharmacology.

description:
The Bachelor of Pharmacy and Management (Honours) and Master of Pharmacy Practice at the University of Sydney combines the same vertically integrated pharmacy training as Sydney's standard pharmacy degree with a foundation in business practice. Over six years, students build a comprehensive understanding of medicines and how they affect the human body, plus the business skills to develop sustainable and innovative pharmacy practice models, including the Pharmacy Board of Australia's intern training and supervised practice requirements.
Graduates are eligible for general registration as a pharmacist and can move into community and hospital pharmacy, primary care or pharmacy business leadership. Sydney is ranked 16th globally for pharmacy and pharmacology.

The Bachelor of Political, Economic and Social Sciences (Honours) at the University of Sydney is an intensive, year-long program of advanced study built around an independent research thesis, developed in collaboration with a supervisor who specialises in the student's chosen field. Students take seminar classes alongside their research, extending the analytical, research and communication skills built during their undergraduate degree.
The honours year prepares some students for careers as professional researchers and academics, and serves as a capstone for others. Graduates move into roles including current affairs journalist, diplomat, government administrator, policy researcher and political adviser.

The Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy, and Economics at the University of Sydney builds intellectual skills for leadership, policymaking, business and advocacy across four disciplines: politics, philosophy, political economy and economics. Students choose one discipline as a major and one as a minor, developing critical thinking, data literacy, ethical decision-making and persuasive communication.
The course suits analytical thinkers aiming for leadership roles. Graduates move into policy analysis, business management, economics, diplomacy, public service, politics, lobbying and investment banking.

The Bachelor of Project Management at the University of Sydney gives students the fundamental project management skills, theories and methods needed to succeed in a complex business environment, from theory to real-world technical application. The course is accredited by the Project Management Institute's Global Accreditation Center, and students complete core project management units alongside a major from the project management or shared disciplinary pool, with an optional minor.
Industry placements and a team-based final-year project build practical, start-to-finish project delivery experience. Graduates move into roles such as construction project controller, events director, document controller and team leader across construction, government and start-up organisations.

The Bachelor of Psychology at the University of Sydney is an accredited three-year degree exploring the science of human behaviour, covering behavioural neuroscience, social psychology, personality theory, perception, intelligence, mental health and developmental psychology. Students complete a psychology program plus advanced psychology units, alongside non-psychology units including a junior mathematics unit and a minor from the shared pool, keeping career options open.
Students are taught by researchers using facilities including the Charles Perkins Centre and the Brain and Mind Centre. Graduates move into roles in advertising, market research, marketing, public relations, science journalism, public policy, and further study toward registration as a psychologist.

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
The Bachelor of Science at the University of Sydney offers more than 40 science majors, programs and streams spanning biology, chemistry, nanoscience and physics, plus a pool of shared majors from across the University. Students build foundational knowledge in the fundamental sciences in first year, then specialise in a chosen stream, program or major in second and third year, alongside a minor or second major and Open Learning Environment units.
Students are taught by scientists including Australian Academy of Science members and Australian Research Council Fellows, using facilities across the University. Graduates move into roles including agricultural scientist, astronomer, ecologist, marine scientist, medical scientist and nanoscientist.

description:
The Bachelor of Science and Doctor of Dental Medicine at the University of Sydney combines an undergraduate science foundation with the University's four-year Doctor of Dental Medicine, teaching students to become confident, ethical dentists through practice-based learning. Core dental units cover life sciences, clinical dentistry and research, alongside clinical and practical placements at Westmead and other Sydney and rural sites.
Sydney is Australia's oldest dental school. Graduates become eligible to register with the Dental Board of Australia and move into private practice, public hospitals, the defence forces, academia and oral health research.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission to the DMD in 2027, applicants must meet the following requirements: Satisfactory performance* in an eligible bachelor’s degree at the time of application, as indicated by Grade Point Average (GPA); and Satisfactory performance* in an admissions test - Domestic applicants must submit eligible Graduate Australian Medical School Admissions Test (GAMSAT) results with their application. International applicants must submit eligible GAMSAT, United States Dental Admission Test (DAT), or Canadian Dental Aptitude Test (CDAT) results with their application. *Satisfactory performance is defined in the relevant Admissions Guide. Eligible GAMSAT results: The University will ONLY accept GAMSAT results from one or more of the following tests for admission to the DMD in 2027: September 2024, March 2025, September 2025 and March 2026. name: Bachelor of Science and Doctor of Medicine
description:
The Bachelor of Science and Doctor of Medicine at the University of Sydney lets exceptional school leavers combine a three-year undergraduate science degree with the four-year Doctor of Medicine, building the scientific fundamentals that underpin clinical training. Students complete core science units and a major from the science disciplinary pool before progressing into the Doctor of Medicine's clinical and research training.
The pathway suits students drawn to biology, physics and chemistry with a passion for healthcare. Sydney is ranked 27th globally for medicine, and graduates move into general practice, specialist medicine, surgery, research and medical administration.
curriculum: Majors — Infectious Diseases, Food Science, Animal Production, Mathematical Modelling and Computation, Medicinal Chemistry, Immunology and Pathology, Biology, Animal Health, Disease and Welfare, Microbiology, Physics, and 24 more.

name: Bachelor of Science in Agriculture
description: The Bachelor of Science in Agriculture at the University of Sydney is delivered through the Bachelor of Agricultural Science, at Australia's first university for agricultural science. Students build knowledge across crop and animal production, soil science and hydrology, food science and agricultural economics, and learn contemporary agricultural technology including sensors, robotics and data analytics. Graduates work in agriculture, agribusiness, research and policy. Indicative international tuition is around 53,300 Australian dollars per year.
discontinued_note: This award now sits within the Bachelor of Agricultural Science.

name: Bachelor of Social Work
description:
The Bachelor of Social Work at the University of Sydney is an internationally recognised four-year degree that qualifies graduates as professional social workers while allowing two years of study in areas such as sociology, diversity studies or gender studies. Core units in sociology and social work are combined with electives from across Arts and Social Sciences, final-year field education placements, and an optional honours thesis.
The course develops reflective, versatile practitioners able to translate professional values into action across a changing field. Graduates work in health services, aged care, disability services, child and family services, migration and refugee services, and policy and advocacy roles.

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Biology (Exit Only)
description:
The Bachelor of Veterinary Biology (Exit Only) at the University of Sydney is the standalone science qualification available to students in the combined Bachelor of Veterinary Biology and Doctor of Veterinary Medicine pathway who complete the first two years of biomedical and animal science but do not progress into the full veterinary medicine degree. It covers the scientific foundations of veterinary science, including animal and biomedical sciences core units.
The award recognises the science component completed before clinical veterinary training begins, and can support further study or work in animal science, research or related industries.

name: Bachelor of Veterinary Science
description:
The Bachelor of Veterinary Biology and Doctor of Veterinary Medicine at the University of Sydney is a six-year combined degree building a scientific foundation before specialist clinical and medical training. The first two years cover the fundamentals of biomedical and animal sciences that underpin veterinary practice, before students progress into the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine's prescribed core units and clinical placements.
Graduates become veterinary medical professionals equipped for private practice in livestock, equine, small animal or mixed clinics, as well as corporate veterinary and research roles. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and 26th in the world for veterinary science.

name: Bachelor of Visual Arts
description:
The Bachelor of Visual Arts at the University of Sydney builds the conceptual, theoretical and technical skills to practise as an artist or work across the creative industries. Students complete six studio units across disciplines including ceramics, glass, jewellery, painting, photomedia, printmedia, screen arts or sculpture, plus four art history units and electives or a second major from across the University.
Students are taught by practising artists, writers and curators with extensive professional networks, using well-equipped studio production facilities. Graduates work as artists, curators, arts writers, digital artists, illustrators, filmmakers and museum educators.

name: Bachelor of Wildlife Conservation (Taronga)
description:
The Bachelor of Wildlife Conservation (Taronga) at the University of Sydney is delivered in partnership with Taronga Conservation Society Australia, combining ecology and conservation management with animal and veterinary science. Students are taught by researchers and practitioners from both institutions, developing expertise in wildlife conservation and the underlying scientific concepts needed to address global conservation challenges.
The University of Sydney is ranked 25th globally in the QS World University Rankings 2026. Graduates move into roles across wildlife conservation, sustainability, environmental consultancy, animal health and reproduction, government policy, and conservation-focused non-government organisations.
curriculum: Majors — Biology, Animal Health, Disease and Welfare, Environmental Studies, Marine Science, Genetics and Genomics.

name: Diploma of Music
description:
The Diploma of Music at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music gives vocational training in a principal study area, with options in performance, contemporary studies, digital and music technology, or composition. Principal studies include composition, contemporary music practice, digital music composition, historical performance, jazz performance, and orchestral or non-orchestral instrument performance.
The course suits students aiming for a professional career in music performance or music technology, and serves as a pathway into the Conservatorium's Bachelor of Music degrees. Located near the Sydney Opera House, graduates move into roles including artist agent, arts administrator, chamber musician, orchestra manager and concert soloist.

name: Doctor of Clinical Dentistry (Oral Medicine)
description:
The Doctor of Clinical Dentistry (Oral Medicine) at the University of Sydney trains qualified dentists to diagnose and manage the full range of oral mucosal and salivary gland diseases, facial pain, and the oral effects of systemic conditions such as HIV. Teaching is clinically based, with a research project each semester and close cooperation with the medical and surgical units at Westmead Hospital, including care for medically compromised patients such as transplant recipients.
The course is aimed at local and international dentists preparing for a career in clinical oral medicine, and graduates are prepared for specialist practice ranging from major hospitals to private clinics. Sydney has run its dental school for more than a century and has invested in a dedicated simulation centre for clinical training.

name: Doctor of Dental Medicine
description:
The Doctor of Dental Medicine at the University of Sydney is a four-year graduate-entry degree open to applicants from any undergraduate discipline who want to become a dentist. Students complete core units in life sciences, clinical dentistry and research, alongside clinical and practical placements at Westmead and other Sydney and rural sites, before becoming eligible to register as a dentist with the Dental Board of Australia.
Sydney is Australia's oldest dental school, and graduates go on to private practice, public hospitals, the defence forces, academia and oral health research, with further specialisation options available once they have professional and research experience.

name: Doctor of Medicine
description:
The Doctor of Medicine at the University of Sydney is a four-year, masters-level graduate-entry degree open to graduates of any discipline with a passion for healthcare. Students complete a prescribed course of core units across eight vertical themes covering basic and clinical sciences, and on graduation are eligible for provisional registration with the Medical Board of Australia as a medical practitioner.
A biomedical science background is not required, and a foundational knowledge course is available on enrolment. Most graduates choose their specialty, commonly general practice, during their second postgraduate year, then complete three to six years of supervised training with a specialist college such as the RACGP, RACP or RACS.
curriculum:
Years 1-2: Foundations of clinical practice (case-based and problem-based learning), Human Structure and Function, Population Health, early clinical placements in hospitals and general practice
Years 3-4: Core clinical rotations — medicine, surgery, psychiatry, obstetrics and gynaecology, paediatrics, general practice, emergency medicine — across metropolitan teaching hospitals (RPA, Westmead, Concord, Royal North Shore, Nepean) and the rural clinical school (Dubbo/Orange, extended placements)
Selective and elective terms in later clinical years, including options for overseas or research-based electives
Entry: completed bachelor's degree, GAMSAT, interview
