name: Doctor of Musical Arts
description:
The Doctor of Musical Arts at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music is a research-based professional doctorate in performance, conducting or composition, designed for professional musicians with strong scholarly ability. Candidates complete a supervised research program leading to a thesis with two components: a public presentation of creative work or a composition portfolio, and a written research dissertation of 25,000 to 35,000 words, supported by coursework in the first year of candidature.
The course suits candidates with a research background who want to extend their high-level creative and research abilities. Graduates pursue careers spanning innovative performance, conducting and composition practice.
admission_requirements: Admission requirement To be eligible to be admitted to candidature by the Dean or Associate Dean (Research Education), an applicant must: (a) hold or have completed the requirements for - (I) the degree of Bachelor of Music (Composition) or Bachelor of Music (Performance) from the University of Sydney, with first class honours, first division; or (II) a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, with first class honours, first division, in a related area of study; or (III) a master's degree from the University of Sydney, completed by research in a related area; or (IV) a master's degree from the University of Sydney, completed by coursework in a related area, with a weighted average mark of at least 80 and including a research component; and (b) perform successfully at a demonstration interview. (2) The Dean or Associate Dean (Research Education) may admit to candidature an applicant who does not meet the requirements of sub-clause (1), provided that the applicant holds a qualification or qualifications that, in the opinion of the Dean or Associate Dean (Research Education), are equivalent to those prescribed in sub-clause (1).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Engineering)
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy in Engineering at the University of Sydney lets candidates research and write a thesis making a substantial, original contribution across the Faculty of Engineering's key research areas, including complex systems, data science, energy, environment, healthcare, infrastructure, IoT and robotics. Candidates typically hold a bachelor's with first-class honours, a research-focused master's or an equivalent qualification, and can take additional coursework units to accelerate their research.
Research spans disciplines including aerospace, mechanical and mechatronic engineering, biomedical engineering, chemical and biomolecular engineering, civil engineering, and electrical and information engineering. Graduates pursue careers in industry, academia and research organisations.
admission_requirements: Admission criteria You must have completed the equivalent of one of the following in an area related to your proposed research: bachelor's degree with first class honours (or equivalent), master's degree by research, master's degree by coursework with an independent research component such as a thesis, dissertation or research project with a minimum overall distinction average. an equivalent qualification that demonstrates research experience, excellence and capability. Applicants who do not meet these admission requirements may be issued an offer of a place in the Master of Philosophy (Engineering) . Transfer from Master of Philosophy (Engineering) Outstanding candidates who successfully complete up to one year full-time or equivalent part-time of the University of Sydney's Master of Philosophy (Engineering) may apply for transfer into the Doctor of Philosophy (Engineering) and receive credit for work completed: with approval from the Supervisor and School, meeting all Higher Degree by Research progression requirements, providing evidence that their research is of a sufficient scope and depth to sustain a doctoral thesis.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Doctor of Philosophy in Agriculture
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy in Agriculture at the University of Sydney's Faculty of Science lets candidates pursue research across the faculty's agricultural and environmental science strengths, submitting an 80,000 word thesis over three to four years. Research areas include agricultural systems, food security, and the management of carbon, water and the environment, within a faculty that attracts researchers and top science students from across Australia.
Candidates typically hold a strong academic background and seek to deepen their expertise in a research area. Graduates pursue careers across banking, policy, marketing, analysis, academia and industry.
admission_requirements: To apply for a PhD, you need to demonstrate sufficient prior research experience and capability. In most cases, to be eligible to apply for a PhD you will have: a Bachelors degree with first class honours or; a Masters degree performed at a high academic standard, and which includes a substantial component of original research, or an equivalent qualification that demonstrates research experience, excellence and capability. These criteria constitute the minimum requirements for eligibility and do not guarantee admission. That remains at the discretion of the Associate Dean (Research Education) for a given Faculty. Inherent requirements In addition to the academic requirements set out in the Science Postgraduate Handbook , you may be required to satisfy a number of inherent requirements to complete this degree. Example of inherent requirement may include: confidential disclosure and registration of a disability that may hinder your performance in your degree; confidential disclosure of a pre-existing or current medical condition that may hinder your performance in your degree (e.g. heart disease, pace-maker, significant immune suppression, diabetes, vertigo,); ability to perform independently and/or with minimal supervision; ability to undertake certain physical tasks (e.g. heavy lifting); ability to undertake observatory, sensory and communication tasks; ability to spend time at remote sites (e.g. One Tree Island , Narrabri and Camden ); ability to work in confined spaces or at heights; ability to operate heavy machinery (e.g. farming equipment); hold or acquire an Australian driver’s licence; hold a current scuba diving license; hold a current Working with Children Check; meet initial and ongoing immunisation requirements (e.g. Q-Fever, Vaccinia virus, Hepatitis, etc.) You must consult with your nominated supervisor regarding any identified inherent requirements before completing your application. The academic requirements that are displayed are applicable to currently available degree only and are updated annually in October and may be changed without notice. The Handbooks Online and the University of Sydney Calendar are the official legal source of information relating to study at the University of Sydney, and you are referred to those documents.

name: Doctor of Philosophy in Architecture (Cotutelle)
description:

description:
The Doctor of Physiotherapy at the University of Sydney is a three-year graduate-entry degree combining clinical education and research training across the core areas of physiotherapy practice. The course takes a patient-centred, evidence-based approach and includes substantial work-integrated learning, with clinical placements at urban public and private clinics and rural health settings that give students hands-on experience with real clients throughout the course.
Graduates take up direct client care, education, research, management, advisory, regulatory and policy roles across hospitals, private practice, sports facilities, schools and aged care. Sydney is ranked fourth globally for sports-related subjects and in the top 20 universities worldwide.

Rural applicants as well as Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants must have a minimum average mark of 60 or equivalent. For domestic applicants, the Indigenous Facilitated Entry Scheme and the Rural Applicants Facilitated Entry Scheme are available for eligible applicants. description:
The Doctor of Veterinary Medicine at the University of Sydney is a four-year graduate-entry course open to applicants with a completed bachelor's degree who want to become registered veterinary practitioners. Teaching follows a One Health framework connecting veterinary health, human medicine and the environment, combining core units with preparatory clinical and farm placements, small-group tutorials and hands-on animal handling training.
Graduates work across private veterinary practice in livestock, equine, small animal and mixed-practice settings, as well as in the pharmaceutical industry and corporate veterinary medicine. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and 26th in the world for veterinary science.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course is based on the following criteria: Grade Point Average (GPA) from a completed Bachelor's degree, minimum credit (65) average required* Successful completion of prerequisite units (see below) Submit the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine Admission Statement A minimum of 30 days of relevant work experience and animal handling experience within the last five years, using the prescribed form Completion of both Situational Judgement Tests Kira Talent and Acuity Casper, is required. For Acuity Casper test, no later than 22 August 2026 for DOMESTIC students and 13 September 2026 for INTERNATIONAL students . For Kira Talent, no later than 29 July 2026 for BOTH DOMESTIC and INTERNATIONAL students . More information about the Situational Judgement Tests Kira Talent and Acuity Casper can be located below. *These are the minimum admission requirements for the DVM. As entry to this course is highly competitive, students who meet the minimum requirements are then ranked according to academic performance, admission statement and both situational judgement test results. For more information read the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine Admission Guide and the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine Admission Statement .
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Executive Master of Arts and Social Sciences
Graduate Certificate in Architectural Science
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Architectural Science at the University of Sydney is an entry point into the University's Building Performance and Sustainable Design program, focused on sustainable design and building performance for a low-carbon built environment. Core foundational units build technical knowledge in building science, with electives applying sustainable design theories to architecture, urban planning, building performance or project management.
The course develops the technical, collaborative and cultural competencies to contribute to world-leading environmental outcomes in interdisciplinary teams. Graduates move into roles such as environmentally sustainable design consultant, sustainable design advisor, and construction or urban planning specialist.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in Building Performance and Sustainable Design requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or in the absence of a bachelor's degree, evidence of three years’ full-time equivalent professional experience in a relevant field. Graduate Certificate students may apply to upgrade to the Diploma or Masters at the completion of their program (with an average mark of at least 70).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Art Curating
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Art Curating at the University of Sydney, taught partly at Sydney College of the Arts, combines core academic skills, historical knowledge and community-engaged experience across museums, galleries and the expanding field of contemporary curating. Students gain access to gallery spaces, art studios and collaboration with institutions including the Art Gallery of New South Wales and the Museum of Contemporary Art Australia.
The course prepares graduates for employment in a gallery or curatorial organisation, covering traditional exhibition spaces alongside artist-run spaces, public art projects and festivals.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Graduate Certificate in Art Curating requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification; or equivalent professional experience in a relevant field.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Art Curatorship
description: The Graduate Certificate in Art Curatorship at the University of Sydney, now offered as the Graduate Certificate in Art Curating, is a six-month full-time program combining academic skills, art historical knowledge, critical insight and community-engaged experience. Students study museums and galleries alongside contemporary and artist-run exhibition spaces. Graduates are prepared for employment in galleries and curatorial organisations. Indicative international tuition is around 45,000 Australian dollars per year.
discontinued_note: This award now sits within the Graduate Certificate in Art Curating.

name: Graduate Certificate in Bioethics
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Bioethics at the University of Sydney examines the ethical challenges that arise in health care, public health and the life sciences, including issues in genetic engineering, migrant and prisoner health, animal experimentation and clinical medicine. The course is directed through Sydney Health Ethics and draws on units shared with the Graduate Diploma in Bioethics.
Students come from backgrounds including philosophy, humanities, social science, law, science and health professions. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and tenth globally for public health, and graduates move into roles across medicine, nursing, allied health, pharmacy, health law and health policy.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in Bioethics requires: a bachelors degree from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification in the field of science, medicine, nursing, allied health sciences, philosophy/ethics, sociology, anthropology, history, law or other relevant field.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Biomedical Science (Infection and Immunity)
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Biomedical Science (Infection and Immunity) at the University of Sydney trains graduates in clinical laboratory techniques used in infectious disease research and the biomedical industry. Students complete 24 credit points, including core units in clinical laboratory science and immunology principles, plus stream selective units in virology, bacteriology, clinical immunology and immunotherapy.
The course suits recent science and health graduates as well as established scientists or clinicians. Sydney is ranked in the top 20 universities globally and second in Australia for medicine, and graduates gain the research and laboratory skills used in infectious disease containment, diagnosis and treatment.
admission_requirements: Admission to the course requires: a bachelors degree or higher award in science, medical or veterinary science, biomedical science, health science or a health-related discipline from the University of Sydney, or qualifications deemed by the Faculty to be equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Brain and Mind Sciences
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Brain and Mind Sciences at the University of Sydney prepares science, medical, nursing, psychiatry and psychology professionals to meet the needs of people with disorders of the brain and mind. Students complete 24 credit points, including core units linking basic neuroscience to clinical applications and elective units offering specialised training with current research methodologies.
The course is delivered through the Brain and Mind Centre. Sydney is ranked second in Australia and 25th in the world for medicine, and graduates move into science, research management and industry roles across biotech, pharmaceutical and government organisations.
admission_requirements: A successful applicant for admission to the Graduate Certificate in Brain and Mind Sciences will: hold a bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification and, where required, satisfactorily perform at an interview.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Building Performance and Sustainable Design
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Building Performance and Sustainable Design at the University of Sydney gives students a foundation in sustainable design and building performance for a low-carbon built environment. Core foundational units build technical knowledge in building science, with electives applying sustainable design theories and methods to architecture, urban planning, building performance or project management.
The course develops the technical, collaborative and cultural competencies needed to contribute to world-leading environmental outcomes in interdisciplinary teams and projects. Graduates move into roles such as environmentally sustainable design consultant, sustainable design advisor in architectural practice, and construction management.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in Building Performance and Sustainable Design requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or in the absence of a bachelor's degree, evidence of three years’ full-time equivalent professional experience in a relevant field. Graduate Certificate students may apply to upgrade to the Diploma or Masters at the completion of their program (with an average mark of at least 70).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business Administration
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Business Administration at the University of Sydney Business School is based on the part-time MBA but requires fewer units of study, giving experienced managers a faster route to core leadership and management skills. Core units cover leadership practice, growth strategy, data analytics and modelling, financial management, critical analysis, strategic marketing and managing people and organisations.
Graduates gain a stronger understanding of themselves as leaders, exposure to current thinking across major business disciplines, and the ability to turn theory into practical, real-world solutions. The course suits working managers who want postgraduate business credentials without committing to the full MBA.
admission_requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree or higher qualification or equivalent; and at least five years’ work with at least three years in a managerial role. Applicants must also: provide a one-page statement of motivation (outlining what will be achieved professionally and personally by completing the course); and complete a selection interview.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Clinical Dentistry (Hospital Dentistry)
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Clinical Dentistry (Hospital Dentistry) at the University of Sydney gives qualified dentists a structured entry into hospital-based clinical dental practice. Study covers oral medicine, oral pathology and the surgical and medical management of patients treated in a hospital setting, taught alongside a supervised clinical caseload and a research component.
The course suits local and international dentists who want to move into hospital dentistry or build toward specialist registration with the Australian Dental Board. It sits within a dental school that has trained practitioners for more than a century and is taught by clinicians active in hospital dental practice.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Clinical Epidemiology
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Clinical Epidemiology at the University of Sydney is a fully online course for clinicians and clinical researchers who want to design, run and interpret clinical research. Over 24 credit points of core and elective units, students build structured, end-to-end research skills covering concept development, study design, statistical analysis and translating findings into practice and policy.
The course is aimed at health professionals, clinical researchers and health decision makers, and credits toward the University of Sydney's Graduate Diploma and Master of Medicine (Clinical Epidemiology) for students who want to continue. Sydney is ranked first in Australia for public health.
admission_requirements: Admission to the course requires: a medical degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification; or a bachelors degree in a health-related discipline with first or second class honours from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification; or a pass bachelors degree in a health-related discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification. Applicants must have completed work equivalent to a first or second class honours bachelors degree or pass a preliminary examination(s) as prescribed by the Faculty; or completion of the first 4 years of an undergraduate medical degree that is accredited by the Australian Medical Council, and a letter of recommendation from the head of clinical school/medical program supporting concurrent enrolment while completing degree requirements. All students entering the program are expected to have some clinical experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Commerce
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Commerce at the University of Sydney Business School is a half-year qualification for graduates from another discipline, or applicants with relevant work experience, who want a global, adaptable business skillset. Students complete foundational units chosen from disciplines including accounting, business information systems, business analytics, economics, finance, global logistics, marketing, and strategy, innovation and management.
The course develops the advanced skills needed for high-level roles in industry, commerce and government, with career paths spanning accounting, marketing and a wide range of other business specialisations.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree or higher (or equivalent qualification) or appropriate qualifications and professional work experience in a relevant field (typically three years).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Computer Science
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Computer Science at the University of Sydney gives students foundational computer science units of study, preparing them for further postgraduate study or a career transition into IT. The course combines technical knowledge with problem-solving skills used to design, implement and evaluate computer science solutions.
The course suits professionals looking to build foundational IT skills for roles in business applications, websites, systems and IT environments across industries including IT companies, consulting firms and financial services. The University of Sydney is ranked first in Australia and 36th in the world for computer science and information systems.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: An Australian bachelor’s degree or higher award in any discipline with a minimum 60 percent average.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Computing
description: The Graduate Certificate in Computing at the University of Sydney, now offered as the Graduate Certificate in Computer Science, is a six-month full-time program for those seeking foundational computer science skills to advance their career or transition to further study. It combines technical knowledge, real-world experience and problem solving to develop solutions to technological challenges. Graduates move into technology roles or continue to the Graduate Diploma or Master of Computer Science. Indicative international tuition is around 50,500 Australian dollars per year.
discontinued_note: This award now sits within the Graduate Certificate in Computer Science.

name: Graduate Certificate in Creative Writing
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Creative Writing at the University of Sydney develops core skills in fiction, nonfiction, poetry and life writing, alongside a deep understanding of relevant literary theory and history. Students gain access to Sydney's literary life, including major cultural events such as the Sydney Writers' Festival, in a research environment run by the University's English Department, one of the world's leading centres for literary study.
The course suits writers building toward publication as well as those pursuing careers in adjacent fields. Graduates work as fiction and nonfiction authors, poets, journalists, reviewers, editors, publishers and media and communications writers.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in Creative Writing requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or equivalent professional experience in a relevant field. Portfolio You will need to include a portfolio of 1,500 to 3,000 words of prose writing or 10 to 15 pages of poetry with your application. These components are crucial to assessing your application.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 64. The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Cultural Studies
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Cultural Studies at the University of Sydney is the only cultural studies degree in Australia, covering popular culture, media, gender, sexuality, globalisation and consumer culture. Students complete four units of study, including three core electives, using real-world examples to analyse cultural forms and debate their significance, with a dissertation pathway available for students planning further research.
The course is taught within the Department of Gender and Cultural Studies by scholars including Professor Elspeth Probyn and Professor Catherine Driscoll. Graduates move into government, community, arts, education and communication roles.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Graduate Certificate in Cultural Studies requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, with a major in a relevant subject area in the humanities or social sciences, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Cybersecurity
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Cybersecurity at the University of Sydney gives professionals a foundational level of knowledge and skills in cybersecurity, along with an introductory understanding of present and emerging trends in the field. Two cybersecurity core subjects and two specialist elective subjects build the technical grounding needed to start a cybersecurity career.
The course suits professionals entering an industry projected to need over 15,000 additional cybersecurity professionals in Australia within five years. The University of Sydney is ranked first in Australia and 36th in the world for computer science and information systems.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: a three year Australian bachelor's degree in a cognate discipline with a minimum average of 60 percent, and a major or minor in information technologies (IT) or computer science, or equivalent in volume of learning as determined by the program directors is required for this discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Data Science
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Data Science at the University of Sydney gives professionals with a strong mathematical or quantitative background a foundational level of knowledge in data mining, machine learning and data visualisation. Two data science core subjects and two specialist elective subjects build the skills needed to guide strategic, data-driven decision making.
Graduates can pursue roles including analytics consultant, business analyst, business intelligence specialist, data analyst and data engineer. The University of Sydney is ranked first in Australia and 36th in the world for computer science and information systems.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: a three year Australian bachelor's degree in a cognate discipline that demonstrates a background in computer programming or statistics with a minimum average of 60 percent.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Design Science (Building)
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Design Science (Building) at the University of Sydney is an entry point into the University's Building Performance and Sustainable Design program, focused on sustainable design and building performance for a low-carbon built environment. Core foundational units build technical knowledge in building science, with electives applying sustainable design theories and methods to architecture, urban planning, building performance or project management.
The course develops the technical, collaborative and cultural competencies needed to contribute to world-leading environmental outcomes in interdisciplinary teams. Graduates move into roles such as environmentally sustainable design consultant, sustainable design advisor and construction management specialist.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in Building Performance and Sustainable Design requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or in the absence of a bachelor's degree, evidence of three years’ full-time equivalent professional experience in a relevant field. Graduate Certificate students may apply to upgrade to the Diploma or Masters at the completion of their program (with an average mark of at least 70).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Development Studies
description: The Graduate Certificate in Development Studies at the University of Sydney is offered within the Master of Social Justice (Development Studies). Students address development policy and debate with experts across anthropology, international relations, political economy, public health, human geography, economics and sociology, in a research-driven environment with industry connections. It suits people who want to make a practical, sustainable difference in developing nations and humanitarian crises. Indicative international tuition is around 51,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Graduate Certificate in Digital Communication and Culture
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Digital Communication and Culture at the University of Sydney examines internet platforms, social media, digital audiences, mobile media, online governance and computer games, building a critical understanding of how digital technologies shape communication and culture. Core units and electives from across Arts and Social Sciences, Sydney College of the Arts and other faculties let students tailor the program to their interests.
The course suits professionals moving into digital content, social media, mobile telecommunications and computer entertainment roles. Graduates work as creatives in television, radio and games, digital and print journalists, and educators.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Graduate Certificate in Digital Communication and Culture requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or equivalent institution; or equivalent professional experience in a relevant field.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Digital Health and Data Science
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Digital Health and Data Science at the University of Sydney is co-designed and co-taught by the School of Computer Science and the Faculty of Medicine and Health's Biomedical Informatics and Digital Health group, giving students advanced data science skills applied to healthcare. Two data science-related subjects and two digital health-related subjects build skills to develop, implement, evaluate and manage data-driven health technologies, taught alongside engineers and health professionals.
The course suits data science professionals moving into health, or health professionals expanding into digital health. Sydney is ranked second in Australia for medicine and first in Australia for computer science and information systems.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: A bachelor’s degree with honours in a cognate discipline.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Economic Analysis
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Economic Analysis at the University of Sydney is a challenging program for high-achieving students with a strong background in economics and quantitative methods, covering advanced core studies in microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics and mathematical economics. The course suits recent graduates and professionals seeking high-level training for career progression, and can serve as a pathway to the Master of Economic Analysis.
Graduates move into technical roles such as economist, analyst, adviser and consultant with employers including central banks, financial institutions and regulatory authorities. The School of Economics is taught by economists whose research influences policy at the Reserve Bank of Australia and the Treasury.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in Economic Analysis requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, including a major in Economics with a minimum distinction (75%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the Graduate Certificate in Economics from the University of Sydney with a minimum distinction (75%) average.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Economics
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Economics at the University of Sydney builds critical thinking, data analysis and problem-solving skills for a career in the public or private sector, suited to students with little or no prior background in economics. Foundation-level units give an in-depth introduction to microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics and quantitative methods, with a pathway to progress into the full Master of Economics.
Graduates move into roles such as analyst, researcher, adviser and consultant with financial institutions, regulatory authorities, government departments and consultancies. The School of Economics is taught by economists whose research influences policy at the Reserve Bank of Australia and the Treasury.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Graduate Certificate in Economics requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification; or evidence of a minimum of three years recent, relevant, professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Educational Studies
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Educational Studies at the University of Sydney lets trained teachers and education professionals choose units across educational management and leadership, educational psychology, international education, special and inclusive education, sports coaching, and teaching English to speakers of other languages. Students complete 24 credit points, drawn from core Master of Education units and selective units matched to their interests.
The course suits teaching professionals, educational administrators, researchers and policymakers who want to specialise within a specific area of education practice, with a pathway to progress into the full Master of Education.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: (i) a bachelor degree or higher in a cognate discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent; OR (ii) a bachelor honours degree or postgraduate qualification in a non-cognate discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification; OR (iii) a bachelor degree in a non-cognate discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification, and professional experience equivalent to two years full-time, in a field considered by the Faculty to be appropriate to the program of studies.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Engineeering
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Engineering at the University of Sydney lets engineering graduates complete a component of the higher-level specialisation needed to excel in a chosen field. Students complete two core units and two specialist units chosen from disciplines including automation and manufacturing systems, biomedical engineering, chemical and biomolecular engineering, civil engineering, electrical engineering and software engineering.
The course suits engineers seeking intermediate career advancement or testing their readiness for further postgraduate study, with a pathway to progress into a full master's degree in their chosen engineering discipline.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian Bachelor of Engineering degree in the relevant discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification or an Australian Bachelor of Engineering degree in the relevant discipline or equivalent, and five years relevant professional work experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in English Studies
description:
The Graduate Certificate in English Studies at the University of Sydney brings contemporary critical theory together with literary narratives, examining literature's resonance in the 21st century and its place in Australian culture. Students complete 24 credit points of core and elective units, with the option to take creative writing units in contemporary poetry, fiction and screenwriting.
The course suits research students, secondary school teachers and anyone studying English literature at an advanced level, spanning fields from medieval to modern and contemporary literature. Graduates move into secondary teaching, journalism, writing, literary criticism and academia.
admission_requirements: Admission to the course requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification; or equivalent professional experience in a relevant field.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Environmental Science
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Environmental Science at the University of Sydney is a flexible, half-year program that links environmental science disciplines such as ecology, climate change and chemistry with politics, law, project evaluation and conflict resolution. Students complete four selective units, choosing from electives including marine science, international development, law and the environment, and geographic information systems.
The course suits new graduates and professionals wanting formal environmental qualifications. Graduates work as analytical scientists, environmental indicator monitors, policy-makers and catchment managers, with alumni employed across state and federal government bodies including the National Parks and Wildlife Service.
admission_requirements: For admission into this course, you should have: a Bachelor of Science or higher with a credit average in one of the following disciplines: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Ecology, Climate and Atmospheric Sciences, Marine Science, Geology, Geography, Environmental Studies, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Economics, Environmental Archaeology, Sustainability, Agriculture, Forestry, and Natural Resource Management; or equivalent qualification; or a Bachelor of Science (Honours) or postgraduate qualification in a non-cognate disciplineor equivalent qualification; or a Bachelor's degree in a non-cognate discipline from the University of Sydney, or equivalent, and professional experience equivalent to two years full-time, in a field considered by the Faculty to be appropriate to the program of studies; or minimum 5 years equivalent experience which is considered to demonstrate the knowledge and aptitude required to undertake the units of study. A credit average means a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 65.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Heritage Conservation
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Heritage Conservation at the University of Sydney equips graduates to practise heritage conservation as an ethic of care grounded in intergenerational equity and cross-cultural understanding. Coursework develops core competencies in documenting and assessing culturally significant places, formulating heritage policy, and understanding the legal frameworks and professional methods that govern heritage practice.
The course engages with contemporary debates including sustainability and climate change alongside ethical and inclusive approaches to heritage. Graduates work as heritage consultants, planners, policy experts, educators and architectural conservation specialists across the public sector, private practice and community organisations.
admission_requirements: (a) a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification; or (b) in the absence of a bachelor's degree, evidence of a minimum of five years’ full time equivalent professional experience in a relevant field.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Human and Community Services
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Human and Community Services at the University of Sydney combines policy, practice and research to give students foundational knowledge for entry into the Australian human and community services sector. Students complete 24 credit points, including six core units and 18 elective units, with the option to focus on fields such as management, community work or violence against women, including Australia's only specialisation in domestic and family violence.
Graduates move into roles at human service organisations including neighbourhood centres, aged care and disability services.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature requires a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Human Resource Management & Industrial Relations
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Human Resource Management and Industrial Relations at the University of Sydney Business School gives students a sound understanding of employment issues and the skills to respond to changes reshaping local and international work practices. It suits graduates from another discipline, or applicants without a degree but with extensive practical HR or industrial relations experience, and provides a pathway to the graduate diploma or master's.
Core units cover the foundations of HRM and industrial relations, emerging workplace challenges, human resource strategy and HR data insights, with electives spanning cross-cultural management, employment law and leadership. Graduates move into roles such as human resource manager, workplace relations manager and industrial relations advisor.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree or higher (or equivalent qualification) or professional work experience in a relevant field (typically three years).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Human Rights
description: The Graduate Certificate in Human Rights at the University of Sydney is offered within the Master of Social Justice (Human Rights). Students gain a critical understanding of the roots of human rights violations and the tools and mechanisms used to promote and protect them, and develop skills in research, analysis, communication and advocacy for domestic, regional and international contexts. Graduates work in advocacy, policy, research and humanitarian roles. Indicative international tuition is around 51,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Graduate Certificate in Information Technology
description: The Graduate Certificate in Information Technology at the University of Sydney is now offered as the Graduate Certificate in Computer Science, a six-month full-time program for those seeking foundational computing skills to advance their career or transition to further study. It combines technical knowledge, real-world experience and problem solving to develop solutions to technological challenges. Graduates move into technology roles or continue to further computer science study. Indicative international tuition is around 57,900 Australian dollars per year.
discontinued_note: This award now sits within the Graduate Certificate in Computer Science.

name: Graduate Certificate in Information Technology Management
Graduate Certificate in Interaction Design and Electronic Arts
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Interaction Design and Electronic Arts at the University of Sydney introduces the fundamentals of human-centred design for products and systems, with a focus on interactive technologies and experiences. Students build core skills in human-centred design thinking, web and mobile interface design and software programming, learning to analyse and evaluate their application across a range of design contexts.
The course promotes a creative and critical approach within research-driven interaction design and user experience methodology. Graduates move into roles such as interaction designer, usability engineer, new media artist and creative director.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification. Graduate Certificate students may apply to upgrade to the Diploma or Masters at the completion of their program (with an average mark of at least 70).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in International Business
description:
The Graduate Certificate in International Business at the University of Sydney Business School is an entry point into the University's Master of International Business, developing the skills to devise and implement strategies for sustainable global corporate expansion. Core units cover the international business environment and global strategy, building knowledge and skills that transfer directly to careers in global management, consulting and trade.
The course suits students looking to accelerate an international career, with graduates moving into roles at organisations such as the World Bank, Austrade and the United Nations, or into global import and export management. The University of Sydney's international business program is ranked first in Australia in the QS International Trade Rankings 2026.
admission_requirements: Education To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in a related discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in an unrelated discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification and relevant professional work experience (typically three years), or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in a related discipline with less than a credit average (minimum 50 percent required) or equivalent qualification and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585) or equivalent Business School approved admissions test. Demonstrated commitment Applicants must demonstrate commitment by providing a statement of motivation that demonstrates clear evidence that the candidate has researched the program and has the capability and mindset to learn in an experiential environment. Selection interview All applications will be ranked according to academic merit after the application closing date. Successfully ranked applicants will be invited to participate in an interview.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in International Relations
description:
The Graduate Certificate in International Relations at the University of Sydney investigates relations among states and non-state actors and the evolution of the international system, through an intellectually rigorous, research-intensive program. Core units introduce key theories, concepts and institutions in international relations and the history of the international system, alongside a choice of selective units in specialist areas.
The course suits professionals looking to elevate their understanding of international relations and ground their existing career with practical, skills-building study. Graduates move into international business, consulting, government, journalism and international organisations including the United Nations, supported by the University's links to major Australian policy think tanks.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in International Relations requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in International Security
description:
The Graduate Certificate in International Security is the international security studies specialisation within the University of Sydney's Graduate Certificate in International Relations, investigating relations among states and non-state actors and the evolution of the international system. Core units introduce key theories, concepts and institutions in international relations and the history of the international system, with selective units focused on international security.
The course suits professionals looking to elevate their understanding of international security and ground their existing career with practical, skills-building study. Graduates move into government, defence, intelligence and international organisations, supported by the University's links to major Australian policy think tanks.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in International Relations requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

description:
The Graduate Certificate in International Studies at the University of Sydney examines relations among states and non-state actors and the evolution of the international system, through an intellectually rigorous, research-intensive program. Core units introduce key theories, concepts and institutions in international relations and the history of the international system, alongside a choice of selective units in specialist areas.
The course suits professionals looking to elevate their understanding of international relations and ground their existing career with practical, skills-building study. Graduates move into international business, consulting, government, journalism and international organisations including the United Nations, supported by the University's links to major Australian policy think tanks.

english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Learning Sciences and Technology
Graduate Certificate in Management
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Management at the University of Sydney Business School is an entry point into the University's Master of Management, a program styled like an MBA but designed for recent graduates from any field with no prior work experience required. Students explore core areas of business, from strategy formulation and decision-making to business negotiation and people management.
The course suits graduates from any discipline who want a fast, practical grounding in general management. The Master of Management this certificate feeds into is ranked first in Australia by the Financial Times, The Economist and QS.
admission_requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree or higher with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher with less than a credit average (minimum 50 percent required), and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585) or equivalent Business School approved admissions test.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Media Practice
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Media Practice at the University of Sydney focuses on media content production in a global context, strengthening written and verbal communication skills alongside print, broadcast and online production skills. Students complete four units of study, including two core units, chosen from approved electives in journalism, communications or a related field.
The course suits practising media professionals and marketing and communications workers who want to update their skills or explore a new career direction. Graduates have established careers across prominent national and international media organisations.
admission_requirements: Admission to the course requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification; or equivalent professional experience of no less than three years in a relevant field such as journalism, public relations, media relations or media research.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Medicine
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Medicine at the University of Sydney gives graduates from any discipline an entry point into postgraduate medical study, drawing on the same core units as the University's Doctor of Medicine. Teaching covers basic and clinical sciences across the vertical themes used throughout the MD, developing the foundations needed to progress toward provisional registration as a medical practitioner.
A biomedical science degree is not a prerequisite, and a foundational knowledge course is available on enrolment. The certificate suits students building toward the full Doctor of Medicine at the University of Sydney, one of Australia's leading medical schools.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Doctor of Medicine in 2027, applicants* must meet the following requirements: Satisfactory performance** in an eligible bachelor’s degree at the time of application, as indicated by Grade Point Average (GPA); and Satisfactory performance** in an admissions test - Domestic applicants must submit eligible Graduate Australian Medical School Admissions Test (GAMSAT) results with their application. International applicants must submit eligible GAMSAT or Medical College Admission Test (MCAT) results with their application. *Applicants applying via the Indigenous Facilitated Entry Scheme should refer to Part 3.1 of the Domestic Admissions Guide **Satisfactory performance is defined in the relevant Admissions Guide. Eligible GAMSAT results: The University will ONLY accept GAMSAT results from one or more of the following tests for admission to the MD in 2027: September 2024, March 2025, September 2025 or March 2026. Applicants for the Dubbo Stream must also provide a Personal Statement (docx, 61KB) in the template form demonstrating a genuine interest, intention and aptitude for practising medicine in rural and regional areas. Please note that the Dubbo Stream is available to domestic applicants only. The University reserves the right to ask applicants to participate in further assessment using other selection tools. Applicants will be given due notice of any additional requirements. Please click on the links below for the Admissions Guide: MD Domestic Admissions Guide (pdf, 1.28MB) MD International Admissions Guide (pdf, 696KB) Indigenous Facilitated Entry Scheme (For domestic applicants only) For Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants with a bachelor’s degree. (From 2027 entry onwards, the GAMSAT requirement will be waived for applicants applying via the Indigenous Facilitated Entry Scheme.) For Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants with a postgraduate degree Rural Applicants Facilitated Entry Scheme (For domestic applicants only) For Australian rural origin applicants as defined by the Australian government Please refer to the MD Domestic Admissions Guide (pdf, 1.28MB) for definitions and information on facilitated entry schemes. Important information Disclaimer Please note Sydney Medical School regularly reviews the admission criteria and application processes for its courses including the Doctor of Medicine. It reserves the right to change these criteria and processes without notice. Information on this website provides advice about the currently applicable criteria and processes, and may not be correct for future application periods. Applicants are advised to consult this website on a regular basis for any changes to entry criteria or program updates. Other requirements prior to commencement of the MD Students who accept a place in the MD will be required to provide a current approved First Aid Certificate and meet Clinical Compliance requirements. First Aid qualification (details are outlined in the Admissions Guide) NSW Ministry of Health Compliance Checking NSW Working with Children Check (WWCC) Post-degree Registration Requirements: Learn about registration, internships, and practice in Australia and other countries (pdf, 79KB). Additional costs Additional costs are involved pre-application and during the application process. Admission test fees - GAMSAT / MCAT Domestic UAC Qualifications Assessment Service (QAS) - GPA calculation (please refer to Part 6.3) International application processing fee (University) You can also expect further costs if you enrol in the program: First Aid Certificate and Clinical Compliance (see above). Specific equipment and supplies required for the course. Overseas health cover (international students only). The University provides a guide for living away from home costs . Deferral Applicants should be prepared and ready to commence the course in the year for which they have applied. Applications for deferral of enrolment following offer and acceptance of a place in the Doctor of Medicine will only be considered under exceptional circumstances that could not have been foreseen at the time of application, and require the approval of the relevant delegate. Transfer Transfer of enrolment between medical schools is not possible, other than in exceptional circumstances. Applications for transfer for 2027 close on 30 September 2026. Find more information on transfers and the Transfer Application Form (pdf, 92KB). Change in immigration status International applicants and students who change from international to domestic status can find the relevant rules here (pdf, 106KB). Disability and inclusion The University is dedicated to ensuring that all students have equal access to learning. You are not obligated to disclose a disability or medical condition to the University, but if you would like to access academic or environment-related adjustments, disclosing enables us to determine the kind of assistance that could be most useful to you. All MD students are required to meet the Inherent Requirements for Medicine: https://sydney.edu.au/students/student-responsibilities/inherent-requirements.html Applicants who require adjustments for their future MD studies should contact the Faculty Admissions Office at fmh.admissions@sydney.edu.au in the first instance. The team will guide you to the University’s Inclusion and Disability Services for further information. Impermissible conduct Sydney Medical School reserves the right, in its sole discretion, to reject an application for admission or to vary or cancel an offer of admission if an applicant’s conduct during the admissions process or prior to enrolment causes Sydney Medical School to form the view that the applicant is unsuitable for admission to the MD. Examples of conduct that might make an applicant unsuitable for admission to the MD include (but are not limited to): failure by the applicant to treat University of Sydney employees, students, applicants or other members of the University community with respect and courtesy, including failure to use appropriate language and tone in written or verbal communications; failure by the applicant to act honestly and ethically in their dealings with University of Sydney employees, students, applicants or other members of the University community; conduct that results in the applicant being excluded from another higher education institution, or from a course or program offered by another higher education institution; conduct that gives Sydney Medical School reasonable cause to believe that enrolling the applicant in clinical training may place them, their peers, or members of the public at risk of harm; and conduct that results in the applicant being charged with a criminal offence.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Museum and Heritage Studies
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Museum and Heritage Studies at the University of Sydney gives students a contextual understanding of core historical and theoretical developments in the field, alongside practical frameworks for managing collections and heritage sites. Students complete 24 credit points across core and elective units, drawing on the University's museum collections and ties to institutions including the Art Gallery of New South Wales and the Australian Museum.
The course suits students interested in how museums and heritage engage the public, including sites of trauma, commemoration and memorialisation. Graduates move into museum education, collection management, heritage site interpretation and cultural policy roles.
admission_requirements: Admission to the course requires: a bachelor's degree or higher award from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Peace and Conflict Studies
description: The Graduate Certificate in Peace and Conflict Studies at the University of Sydney is offered within the Master of Social Justice (Peace and Conflict Studies). Students explore the intellectual and practical challenges of attaining peace with justice, from justice and reconciliation after mass violence to the role of the United Nations in peacekeeping and peace building, and tailor the program to their interests and career goals. Graduates work in peacebuilding, humanitarian, policy and research roles. Indicative international tuition is around 51,300 Australian dollars per year.

name: Graduate Certificate in Political Economy
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Political Economy at the University of Sydney examines how political, institutional, social, cultural and historical factors shape economic life, exploring different theoretical traditions to question how markets, the state and households interact. Core units survey the history of economics, economic theory and Australian political economy, with selective units in specialist areas.
The course suits students seeking a career in social or policy analysis and research. The University of Sydney has the largest number of political economists in Australia, and graduates work in state and federal treasuries, research institutions, government and the media.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in Political Economy requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting at the University of Sydney Business School is an entry point into the University's Master of Professional Accounting and Business Performance, developed with input from industry and taught across seven Business School disciplines. Coursework builds analytics, technology and communication skills alongside technical accounting expertise, including experience with cloud-based accounting platforms.
The course suits students who want to pair deep accounting knowledge with broader business acumen. Graduates move into roles such as financial analyst, tax and estate adviser, and financial and management accountant, with a pathway to progress into the full master's degree.
admission_requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: Australian bachelor's degree or higher with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or Australian bachelor's degree or higher (minimum 50 percent required) or equivalent qualification, and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585), or University of Sydney Graduate Diploma in Professional Accounting and Business Performance with a credit average (65 percent).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting and Business Performance (Exit degree)
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting and Business Performance is an exit-level award within the University of Sydney's Master of Professional Accounting and Business Performance, recognising students who complete the certificate-level units of that program. Coursework, developed with industry input and taught across seven Business School disciplines, builds analytics, technology and communication skills alongside core accounting expertise.
The award suits students who complete part of the master's but choose to exit early with a recognised qualification. Careers span financial analysis, management accounting and business performance roles across a range of organisations.
admission_requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: Australian bachelor's degree or higher with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or Australian bachelor's degree or higher (minimum 50 percent required) or equivalent qualification, and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585), or University of Sydney Graduate Diploma in Professional Accounting and Business Performance with a credit average (65 percent).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Project and Program Management
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Project and Program Management at the University of Sydney's Faculty of Engineering is an entry point into the University's Master of Project Management, giving working professionals the fundamental methodologies, modelling and analytical techniques used to design and implement projects. The course is accredited by the Project Management Institute and draws on the John Grill Institute for Project Leadership.
Students complete technical, strategic and leadership-focused core units suited to managing successful projects across industries from construction and mining to IT and finance. Graduates move into project management roles locally and internationally, with a pathway to progress into the full master's degree.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: a bachelor's degree in any discipline with a minimum credit average (65 percent) or an Australian bachelor's degree (with honours), or equivalent qualification or a combination of a bachelor's degree and relevant industry experience and certifications or a University of Sydney Graduate Diploma/Graduate Certificate in Project Management with a credit average (65 percent)
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Project Management
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Project Management at the University of Sydney's Faculty of Engineering gives working professionals a foundation in the methodologies and analytical techniques used in project management, complementing on-the-job experience. Four core units build the platform for further study in the Graduate Diploma in Project Management, and a credit average allows students to upgrade directly into the diploma.
The course suits professionals without a recognised bachelor's degree who want a pathway into postgraduate project management study. It is accredited by the Project Management Institute, the world's leading specialised accrediting body in the field.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification or three years relevant industry experience and certifications (e.g. certification from the Project Management Institute) or similar
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Public Policy
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Public Policy at the University of Sydney gives students a critical, multidisciplinary perspective on public policy at the global, national and local level, amid growing public scrutiny, shrinking resources and new cross-border challenges. Core units cover the fundamentals of public policy and public administration, with selective units in specialist areas, and the course can serve as a pathway to the full Master of Public Policy.
The course suits people working in or aiming for government and the public sector, as well as those in non-government and private organisations who want to understand government's role in policymaking. Graduates move into policy analyst, government adviser and strategic planning roles.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Graduate Certificate in Public Policy requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney with a major in cognate discipline, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Graduate Certificate in Publishing
description:
The Graduate Certificate in Publishing at the University of Sydney gives students the skills needed for book, magazine, digital and online publishing, combining professional, vocational training with a scholarly understanding of publishing's history and cultural significance.
