Non-Australian qualifications (if relevant) The Australian Psychological Accreditation Council (APAC) provides information on APAC accredited psychology qualifications in Australia. The Australian Psychological Society (APS) assesses non-Australian qualifications for APAC equivalence. All qualifications obtained from a non-Australian Higher Education Provider must be assessed as equivalent by the Australian Psychological Society (APS) before an application may be submitted.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Commerce
description:
The Master of Commerce at the University of Sydney Business School is an 18-month postgraduate degree for graduates with prior business study or relevant professional experience who want advanced, industry-relevant expertise in a focused commerce discipline. Students build a foundation in core business areas in their first year, then specialise in one of eight commerce disciplines, add breadth through selective units, and complete a capstone project applying their learning to a real business situation.
Graduates move into advanced positions across private, public and non-profit organisations, including accounting, marketing and other specialist fields. Students can transfer between the Master of Commerce and its extension variant depending on how their study progresses.
curriculum:
Core units: Managerial Economics, Accounting for Managers, Quantitative Methods for Business, Business Ethics and Sustainability
Major coursework (choose one): Finance, Accounting, Marketing, Business Analytics, International Business, Human Resource Management
Electives within chosen major, plus cross-disciplinary electives
Capstone: Business Project or Internship unit (final semester)
Duration: 1.5 to 2 years full-time depending on prior qualifications
admission_requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree in commerce, business or related discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in commerce, business or related discipline (minimum 50 percent average) or equivalent qualification, and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585), or an Australian bachelor's degree in any discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification and a minimum of one-year relevant work experience, or an Australian bachelor's degree with honours or higher in any discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or the University of Sydney Graduate Diploma or Graduate Certificate in Commerce with a credit average (65 percent).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
The Master of Computer Science at the University of Sydney gives students the expertise to address challenges in generative AI, cybersecurity, programming, software engineering and network systems, from foundational knowledge through to specialised skills. Students complete foundation subjects, computing professional core subjects, specialist computing subjects and a professional capstone or research project, with an advanced-entry pathway available for applicants who already hold a computing qualification.
Graduates take on roles designing, implementing and evaluating computer science solutions across IT companies, consulting firms and financial services. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and 36th in the world for computer science and information systems.
curriculum:
Foundation units (extended pathway only): Introduction to Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms, Discrete Mathematics for Computing
Core coursework: Software Construction and Design, Computer Networks, Database Systems, Machine Learning Fundamentals
Specialisation streams: Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Software Development
Capstone: choose between Industry Project, Research Project (with academic supervisor), or Coursework Capstone Project
Standard pathway (relevant bachelor's): approximately 1.5 years; extended pathway: approximately 2 years
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have an Australian bachelor’s degree in any discipline with a credit average (65 percent), or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Contemporary Art
description: The Master of Contemporary Art at the University of Sydney is now offered through the Master of Fine Arts by research, delivered by Sydney College of the Arts as a supervised independent program of written work and studio research. Students develop their art practice through advanced research in one or more discipline areas. It suits visual arts graduates who want to elevate their practice through research-driven exploration. Graduates work as practising artists and pursue further research. Indicative international tuition is around 50,200 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Creative Writing
description:
The Master of Creative Writing at the University of Sydney develops core skills in fiction, creative nonfiction, poetry and other forms of writing through multi-genre workshops, alongside practice-based research methods and industry knowledge. Students complete core units in creative writing research and practice, specialist writing workshops, electives from across the University, and a capstone creative dissertation or project.
The course suits writers seeking expert guidance toward publication or further study, as well as teachers building their workshop skills and pedagogy. Sydney describes its program as Australia's most research-intensive in creative writing.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Creative Writing (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, including a major in a relevant subject area in the humanities or social sciences, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the requirements for the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Creative Writing with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Creative Writing (1 year full-time) requires: an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course with the relevant minimum average mark.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 64. The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Criminology
description:
The Master of Criminology at the University of Sydney examines contemporary questions about crime and social control in policy, theory and practice, comparing Australian and global perspectives, taught by leading Australian criminologists. Students complete eight units of study covering crime theories, psychology, public policy, social research and legal theory, building the knowledge to work with criminal justice and social welfare agencies.
The course welcomes students from backgrounds including social policy, psychology, public health, media and policing. Graduates work across criminal justice agencies, government policy, border protection and research institutions.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Criminology requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit average from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; and the applicant provides evidence of two years of relevant professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics
description:
The Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics at the University of Sydney examines the forms and functions of spoken and written language and how it connects with visual and digital contexts, applying linguistics and cross-cultural research to professional and social engagement. Core units build critical awareness of the connections between language, culture and society, finishing with a capstone professional practice unit.
The course suits students seeking to deepen their knowledge of linguistics and cross-cultural communication or pursue further research. Graduates move into roles spanning public relations, multilingual education, community engagement, TESOL teaching and doctor-patient communication in health settings.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 2 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (2 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average in a relevant discipline, calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate in Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or relevant professional work experience. Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Diploma in Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Crosscultural Communication
description:
The Master of Crosscultural Communication at the University of Sydney, known as the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics, gives students the concepts and methods of linguistics and cross-cultural research and applies them to marketing, education, TESOL, community relations, media, medicine and business. Core units build foundational knowledge of language, culture and society, finishing with a capstone professional practice unit and electives chosen from across the University.
Graduates work across public relations, multilingual education, community engagement, TESOL teaching, media and doctor-patient communication in health settings.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 2 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (2 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average in a relevant discipline, calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate in Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or relevant professional work experience. Admission to candidature for the Master of Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Diploma in Crosscultural and Applied Linguistics with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Cultural Studies
description:
The Master of Cultural Studies at the University of Sydney examines popular culture, media, gender, sexuality, globalisation and consumer culture, using real-world examples to analyse cultural expressions and their significance within socio-historical frameworks. Core units build conceptual and methodological skills, complemented by electives matched to the student's interests and a capstone research project.
The course suits students seeking to apply a deep understanding of cultural processes to their industry. Graduates move into government, community, arts, education and communication roles.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Cultural Studies (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney including a major in a relevant subject area in the humanities or social sciences, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Cultural Studies (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Cultural Studies with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Cybersecurity
description:
The Master of Cybersecurity at the University of Sydney gives professionals an expert-level understanding of leading attack and defence techniques, network security assessment, and organisational cybersecurity strategy. Students complete cybersecurity and computing professional core subjects, cybersecurity specialist electives, and a capstone or research project, with optional specialisations in cloud security, cryptography and blockchains, or data and information security.
The course is designed for professionals aiming to become leaders and technical experts in an industry projected to need 17,000 additional cybersecurity professionals in Australia within five years. Sydney is ranked first in Australia for computer science and information systems.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: a three year Australian bachelor's degree in a cognate discipline with a minimum credit average (65 percent), or the University of Sydney Graduate Diploma in Cybersecurity with a minimum credit average (65 percent), or a qualification deemed to be equivalent; or completed 24 credit points of the University of Sydney Graduate Diploma in Cybersecurity or Graduate Certificate in Cybersecurity with a minimum credit average (65 percent). The 24 credit points must include 12 credit points of Cybersecurity Core units and 12 credit points of Cybersecurity specialist elective units, and a major or minor in information technologies (IT) or computer science, or equivalent in volume of learning as determined by the program directors is required for this discipline
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Data Science
description:
The Master of Data Science at the University of Sydney develops the analytical and technical skills professionals with a strong mathematical or quantitative background need to use data science for strategic decision making. Students complete data science core subjects, computing professional core subjects, data science specialist electives, and a capstone project or research project, with optional specialisations in data engineering or machine learning.
Graduates apply data analysis, machine learning and statistical modelling across technology, finance, healthcare and government, with career outcomes shaped by their chosen specialisation and applied project experience. Sydney is ranked first in Australia for computer science and information systems.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: a three year Australian bachelor's degree in a cognate discipline that demonstrates a background in computer programming or statistics with a minimum credit average (65 percent), or the University of Sydney Graduate Diploma in Data Science with a minimum credit average (65 percent), or a qualification deemed to be equivalent; or completed 24 credit points of the University of Sydney Graduate Diploma in Data Science or Graduate Certificate in Data Science with a minimum credit average (65 percent). The 24 credit points must include 12 credit points of Data Science Core units and 12 credit points of Data Science specialist elective units. If you have the equivalent of an Australian AQF Level 8 degree or above in a cognate discipline, you may be eligible for a Reduced Volume of Learning (RVL) of up to 24 credit points or 0.5 years/1 semester.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Dental Public Health
description:
The Master of Dental Public Health at the University of Sydney focuses on preventing oral disease and improving oral health at a population level, particularly among vulnerable groups. Students complete core units in dental health services, population oral health and preventive dentistry, alongside a capstone and research project, developing skills in oral health surveillance, policy development and service delivery.
The course is designed for registered dentists seeking specialist recognition as well as other dental practitioners and non-dental professionals working in oral or public health. Sydney is ranked fourth in Australia and in the top 100 globally for dentistry and oral sciences.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Dental Public Health requires: a bachelor or doctoral degree (or equivalent) in dentistry; or a bachelor degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field, and a Master of Public Health (MPH) degree; or a qualification deemed by the faculty to be equivalent, and performance in an interview. In exceptional circumstances, applicants may be admitted without the master’s degree in public health who, in the opinion of the faculty, have qualifications and evidence of experience and achievement sufficient to successfully undertake the award.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Design
description:
The Master of Design (Design Innovation) at the University of Sydney gives designers the skills to develop the systems, organisations and services the world needs, through design-led innovation and inquiry. Core units introduce the principles and methods of design innovation, finishing with a capstone in industry or research and either a second capstone or elective units.
The course suits design professionals who want to use innovation across business and social domains to create value and impact. Graduates move into roles including design manager, digital innovation director, chief customer officer and chief design officer.
admission_requirements: Available places will be offered to qualified applicants in the order in which complete applications are received, according to the admissions criteria listed below. a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification with an average mark of 65, or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate diploma with an average mark of 70.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Design Science (Building)
description:
The Master of Design Science (Building) at the University of Sydney develops advanced technical, collaborative and cultural competencies to address environmental challenges in the built environment sector. Core foundational and advanced units mix theory and practice, equipping graduates for careers as environmentally sustainable design consultants or in other sustainability and building science-focused roles.
The course suits graduates aspiring to a sustainability-focused career as well as built environment professionals seeking formal qualifications in sustainable design. Graduates move into environmentally sustainable design consulting, property development, construction management and urban planning.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Building Performance and Sustainable Design requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the requirement of the graduate certificate with an average mark of at least 70; or completion of a recognised undergraduate program in architecture, engineering, project management or a related field from another institution with a credit average mark (equivalent to 65%) over the final two years of study.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Development Studies
description:
The Master of Development Studies at the University of Sydney, delivered as the Master of Social Justice (Development Studies), addresses development policy and debate with experts in anthropology, international relations, political economy, human geography, economics and sociology. Students complete core units in social justice alongside stream selective units in development studies, finishing with a capstone dissertation, vocational placement or independent research project.
The course suits students who want to make a practical, sustainable difference in developing nations and humanitarian crises. Graduates work in government, non-government and private sector organisations focused on development and poverty alleviation.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for this course requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65 percent) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, with a major in the humanities or social sciences, or or an equivalent level of performance in an equivalent qualification; or completion of the requirements for the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Social Justice with a minimum credit (65 percent) average, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Diagnostic Radiography
description:
The Master of Diagnostic Radiography at the University of Sydney trains graduate-entry students to use imaging technologies from mobile X-ray units to MRI, CT and cardiac imaging systems for patient diagnosis and treatment. Over two years, students work closely with radiologists across a range of imaging modalities, learning to produce high-quality medical images used to describe, diagnose, monitor and treat injury and illness.
The program is accredited by the Medical Radiation Practice Board of Australia, and graduates are eligible for general registration on completion. Sydney is ranked in the top 20 universities globally.
admission_requirements: To be eligible to apply you will need to fulfill the following criteria: a bachelor's degree, master's degree or PhD from an Australian institution or equivalent a minimum average mark of 60 out of 100 or equivalent. This does not guarantee an offer as the places are limited and offers are made based on academic merit. evidence of any other minimum standards specified by the Faculty of Medicine and Health. Prospective students must ensure that they understand the Medical Radiation Practice Board of Australia's (MRPBA) registration requirements for graduates of this program prior to enrolment. For domestic applicants, the Indigenous Facilitated Entry Scheme and the Rural Applicants Facilitated Entry Scheme are available for eligible applicants. Please refer to the Sydney School of Health Sciences Special Admission Pathways Guide for definitions and information on facilitated entry schemes.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 64. The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Digital Communication and Culture
description:
The Master of Digital Communication and Culture at the University of Sydney examines internet platforms, social media, digital audiences, mobile media, online governance and computer games, preparing students for transformations across communication, culture, politics, consumption and everyday life. Core units cover key themes in digital communication and culture, finishing with a professional project, internship or dissertation capstone examining an aspect of digital cultural change.
The course suits professionals moving into digital content, social media, mobile telecommunications and computer entertainment roles. Graduates work as creatives in television, radio and games, digital and print journalists, and educators.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Master of Digital Communication and Culture (1.5 years full-time) Admission to the Master of Digital Communication and Culture (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification. Master of Digital Communication and Culture (1 year full-time) Admission to the Master of Digital Communication and Culture (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Digital Communication and Culture with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Digital Health and Data Science
description:
The Master of Digital Health and Data Science at the University of Sydney is co-designed and co-taught by the School of Computer Science and the Faculty of Medicine and Health's Biomedical Informatics and Digital Health group, giving students advanced data science skills applied to healthcare. Core units cover implementation science in digital health, foundations of digital health, and applied and foundational healthcare data science, alongside further data science electives.
Graduates deliver data-driven solutions to complex health challenges in leadership roles across medical and health professions, including data scientist and solutions architect positions. Sydney is ranked second in Australia for medicine and first in Australia for computer science and information systems.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: A bachelor’s degree with honours in a cognate discipline with at least a credit average; or Completion of the requirements of the embedded Graduate Certificate in Digital Health and Data Science with a credit average.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Economic Analysis
description:
The Master of Economic Analysis at the University of Sydney develops research skills in economics or econometrics through advanced core and elective study in economic theory, culminating in a substantial independent research project and 12,000-word dissertation supervised by an academic staff member. The course suits students with a strong background in economics and quantitative methods, and can serve as a pathway to a PhD.
Small class sizes support close interaction with academic staff. Graduates move into technical roles such as economist, analyst, adviser and consultant with employers including central banks, financial institutions and international organisations.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Economic Analysis requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, including a major in Economics with a minimum high distinction (85%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate in Economic Analysis or Graduate Diploma in Economic Analysis with a minimum distinction (75%) average, or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course with the relevant minimum average mark.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Economics
description:
The Master of Economics at the University of Sydney builds critical thinking, data analysis and problem-solving skills for a career in the public or private sector, with foundation units for students new to the discipline and reduced course duration available for those with an undergraduate economics background. Core study covers advanced microeconomics, macroeconomics and econometrics, with a specialisation in econometrics, economics or financial economics and a capstone applying the knowledge gained.
Graduates move into roles such as analyst, researcher, adviser and consultant with financial institutions, regulatory authorities, government departments and consultancies. The School of Economics is taught by economists whose research influences policy at the Reserve Bank of Australia and the Treasury.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Economics (2 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the requirements for the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Economics with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification. Reduced volume of learning If you have completed previous studies in a related area or have relevant work experience, you may be able to reduce the duration of your studies based on the criteria below: Admission to the Master of Economics (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, with a major in Economics and with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or relevant professional experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to the Master of Economics (1 year full-time) requires: an Honours degree in Economics. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Education
description:
The Master of Education at the University of Sydney is taught by active researchers and designed for experienced educators and future education leaders, deepening understanding of educational theory, leadership, research and policymaking. Students complete core units building a strong foundation in advanced education practice, finishing with a capstone special project or dissertation, and can choose a specialised stream or an unstreamed program drawing from across offerings.
The course suits educators seeking their next professional challenge. Graduates move into teaching, educational administration, research and policymaking roles within specific areas of education practice.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: (i) a bachelor degree or higher in a cognate discipline from the University of Sydney, or equivalent; OR (ii) a bachelor honours degree in a non-cognate discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification; OR (iii) A graduate certificate or a graduate diploma in the same stream as that in which the applicant wishes to proceed, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Emergency Nursing
description:
The Master of Emergency Nursing is a specialisation stream within the University of Sydney's Master of Nursing, aimed at registered nurses and graduate-entry students building an emergency and trauma nursing career. It shares the Master of Nursing's core units in anatomy, pathophysiology, pharmacology and person-centred practice, with a concentration in emergency nursing.
The program is accredited by the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Accreditation Council, leading toward registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. Graduates work in emergency departments and trauma units across metropolitan, regional and remote health services in Australia and abroad.
admission_requirements: You must have: a previous Australian level bachelor degree (or equivalent) in any discipline other than nursing, AND this qualification has been completed within 10 years prior to applying Overseas nursing qualifications are acceptable. See our Master of Nursing Admissions Guide (pdf, 1.00MB) for more information.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Engineering
description:
The Master of Engineering (Software Engineering) at the University of Sydney gives qualified engineers specialised technical knowledge in software production, from strategy and design to coding, quality and management. Students complete core and elective software engineering units, engineering management and leadership units, and project or research pathway units, addressing the growing demand for skilled engineers across internet, mobile and embedded systems.
The course develops professional engineering skills aligned with current industry standards, opening up opportunities for career advancement as well as research and innovation roles.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian Bachelor of Engineering degree in the relevant discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or an Australian Bachelor of Engineering degree in the relevant discipline or equivalent, and five years relevant professional work experience, or the relevant University of Sydney Graduate Diploma in Engineering or Graduate Certificate in Engineering with a credit average (65 percent).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of English Language in Australia
Master of English Studies
description:
The Master of English Studies at the University of Sydney examines contemporary critical theory, the enduring significance of literature in the 21st century, and Australian literary works, spanning critical reading, literary history and English as a global literature. Students complete 72 credit points, including at least 24 credit points of core units and a capstone, drawing on a department ranked first in Australia and 18th globally for English language and literature.
The course suits research students, secondary school teachers and anyone studying English literature at an advanced level. Graduates move into teaching, publishing, writing and research roles that reward critical thinking and adaptability.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below. Admission to candidature for 1.5 years full-time requires: a bachelor's degree with a major in English Literature and a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature 1 year full-time requires: completion of the requirements for the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in English Studies with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Environmental Law
description:
The Master of Environmental Law at the University of Sydney Law School covers one of law's most rapidly expanding areas of specialisation, examining legal issues arising from natural resource protection, pollution prevention and urban planning across science and law. Students complete eight units of study, including the compulsory Environmental Law and Policy unit, with students who lack a law degree also completing a foundational legal reasoning unit.
The course suits environmental specialists from Australia and overseas, with or without a legal background. Graduates work in law, government agencies, private industry, international development and non-profit organisations.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Environmental Law requires: a bachelor's degree with a credit average (65 percent) from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification.; or a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; and the applicant provides evidence of two years of relevant professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Environmental Science
description:
The Master of Environmental Science at the University of Sydney is a launch pad into leadership for environmental sector professionals, drawing on a wide range of science-based disciplines including environmental chemistry, ecology, climate change, renewable energy and environmental policy. Over 1.5 years, students complete core units in environmental science and choose between an integrated environmental practice unit or a research project as their capstone, alongside electives matched to their interests.
The course suits new graduates and professionals seeking formal environmental qualifications. Graduates work as analytical scientists, environmental indicator monitors, policy-makers, environmental managers and catchment managers across government and industry.
admission_requirements: For admission into this course, you should have: a Bachelor of Science or higher with a credit average in one of the following disciplines: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Ecology, Climate and Atmospheric Sciences, Marine Science, Geology, Geography, Environmental Studies, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Economics, Environmental Archaeology, Sustainability, Agriculture, Forestry, and Natural Resource Management; or equivalent qualification or a Bachelor of Science (Honours) or postgraduate qualification in a non-cognate discipline or equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in this discipline, from the University of Sydney, or equivalent qualification. A credit average means a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 65.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Environmental Science and Law
description:
The Master of Environmental Science and Law at the University of Sydney combines complementary study in environmental science and environmental law, extending scientific knowledge into environmental policy and legal frameworks. Compulsory units in environmental law and policy and legal reasoning are paired with environmental science units chosen to suit the student's interests, linking science with politics, law and project evaluation.
The course suits science graduates who want to build environmental policy expertise. Graduates work in environmental management and policy development across private industry, government agencies, international development agencies, non-government organisations and research, though the degree does not itself qualify graduates to practise law.
admission_requirements: For admission into this course, you should have: a bachelors degree or higher with a credit average in one of the following disciplines: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Ecology, Climate and Atmospheric Sciences, Marine Science, Geology, Geography, Environmental Studies, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Economics, Environmental Archaeology, Sustainability, Agriculture, Forestry, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Policy, and Law, or equivalent qualification; or a bachelor honours degree or postgraduate qualification in a noncognate discipline, or equivalent qualification. A credit average means a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 65.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Exercise Physiology
description:
The Master of Exercise Physiology at the University of Sydney trains graduates to design, deliver and evaluate safe, effective exercise interventions for people with acute, sub-acute and chronic conditions, injuries or disabilities. Core units, a selective unit and a final-semester capstone project cover cardiovascular, metabolic, neurological, musculoskeletal, cancer, kidney and respiratory practice.
Graduates become eligible to work as accredited exercise physiologists in private and public health, rehabilitation, occupational health and safety, sport and research settings. The University of Sydney teaches in the purpose-built Susan Wakil Health Building, with dedicated clinical simulation and research facilities.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Exercise Physiology requires the applicant to have: A bachelor or master’s degree or a PhD in exercise science or a health-related discipline from the University of Sydney, or qualifications deemed by the faculty to be equivalent; and A minimum average mark of 60 out of 100 or equivalent (GPA of 4.5 out of 7) any other minimum standards specified by the Faculty of Medicine and Health. Evidence of*: a current Exercise Scientist Accreditation (AES) with Exercise and Sport Science Australia ; or completion of a bachelor or master’s degree accredited by Exercise and Sport Science Australia at the level of Exercise Science; or an approved Graduate Entry Assessment from Exercise and Sport Science Australia * by providing evidence of accreditation, applicants are also proving extensive pre-existing knowledge in human anatomy, human or exercise physiology and research design and statistics. For domestic applicants, the Indigenous Facilitated Entry Scheme and the Rural Applicants Facilitated Entry Scheme are available for eligible applicants. Please refer to the Sydney School of Health Sciences Special Admission Pathways Guide for definitions and information on facilitated entry schemes.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Facilities Management
description:
The Master of Facilities Management at the University of Sydney's Faculty of Engineering gives working professionals the fundamental methodologies, modelling and analytical techniques needed to manage complex buildings and built assets across their operational life. Technical, strategic and leadership-focused core units are combined with a capstone comprising either a research thesis or a professional project, and the course is accredited by the Project Management Institute.
Graduates move into facilities and asset management roles across construction, property, government and corporate real estate, drawing on the University's John Grill Institute for Project Leadership.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: a bachelor's degree in any discipline with a minimum credit average (65 percent) or an Australian bachelor's degree (with honours), or equivalent qualification or a combination of a bachelor's degree and relevant industry experience and certifications or a University of Sydney Graduate Diploma/Graduate Certificate in Project Management with a credit average (65 percent)
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Film and Screen Arts
description:
The Master of Film and Screen Arts at the University of Sydney gives students hands-on education in contemporary screen production, developing a film project from concept to screen. Core units cover story development, scripting, directing, art design, cinematography, editing and post-production, finishing with a capstone major moving image project for public exhibition and a choice between research or professional development pathways.
The University of Sydney has been a major training ground for NSW's contemporary artists, researchers and curators for more than four decades. Graduates move into roles as director, screenwriter, producer, editor, production manager and cinematographer across the film, screen arts and digital media industries.
admission_requirements: A successful applicant for admission to the Master of Film and Screen Arts will: hold a bachelor's degree or higher award in visual arts from the University of Sydney or a qualification deemed by the faculty to be equivalent; and present a portfolio* of creative work demonstrating the ability to undertake advanced art practice and coursework.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Fine Arts
description:
The Master of Fine Arts by research at the University of Sydney, delivered through Sydney College of the Arts, lets visual artists develop their practice through advanced research in one or more discipline areas. The degree is primarily a supervised independent study program of written work and studio research, with a research supervisor providing personalised guidance to produce original and speculative work.
The course suits students with an advanced degree in visual arts or a related field. Sydney College of the Arts has been Sydney's premier training ground for contemporary visual artists for more than 40 years, with strong research assessment results.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Master of Fine Arts, you must present a portfolio of work that demonstrates you have the level of art practice proficiency expected of an advanced research applicant. In addition, you must have completed the equivalent of one of the following in visual arts or other subject area related to your proposed research area: bachelor's degree with honours; or bachelor's degree and graduate diploma; or master's degree by coursework with an independent research component such as a thesis, dissertation or research project. These criteria constitute the minimum requirements for eligibility and do not guarantee admission. That remains at the discretion of the relevant supervisors and departments, and access to supervision remains highly competitive. The University must certify that there are sufficient supervisory and other resources and facilities available to enable your candidature to be completed successfully.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Global Health
description:
The Master of Global Health at the University of Sydney examines the social, environmental, economic and political processes that drive global health inequity, preparing graduates from health and non-health backgrounds to work on population health challenges internationally. Core units in global health concepts, biostatistics and epidemiology are paired with elective units and placement opportunities in specific global health subject areas.
Graduates move into roles such as monitoring and evaluation officer, public health policy analyst, and public health adviser for governments, non-government organisations and international aid agencies. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and tenth globally for public health.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Global Health degree requires: a bachelor's degree with honours or a graduate certificate or graduate diploma from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification or a bachelor's degree in the field of medicine, nursing, physiotherapy, occupational therapy, optometry, pharmacy, dentistry, veterinary science, psychology, biological science, medical science, international relations, international development, education, social science, political science, communication and journalism, civil engineering, law, economics or mathematics from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification or a bachelor's degree in an unrelated field and two years professional work experience in health or international development.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Health Law
description:
The Master of Health Law at the University of Sydney Law School is a flexible, specialist qualification covering legal and ethical issues in healthcare, including healthcare law, the impact of new technologies, professional regulation, litigation, public health law, mental health law and global health governance. Students come from backgrounds including legal practice, health professions, health administration and government.
The course suits lawyers and non-lawyers who want to upgrade their qualifications for career advancement. Graduates learn to identify, analyse and develop solutions to complex legal, ethical and policy issues affecting the health sector.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Health Law requires: a bachelor's degree with a credit average (65 percent) from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification.; or a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; and the applicant provides evidence of two years of relevant professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Health Policy and Planning
description:
The Master of Health Policy and Planning at the University of Sydney builds a comprehensive, practical understanding of health systems and policy-making, extending beyond administration into systems thinking, economic evaluation, health financing and the use of evidence in policy. Core units cover health policy, policy planning and health economics, including a health policy project, alongside electives in global and public health.
The degree is delivered flexibly to fit around work, and prepares graduates for senior roles across government, advocacy, health service leadership, strategy and regulation. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and tenth globally for public health.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: a bachelor's degree with first or second class honours from the University of Sydney, or equivalent qualification and a minimum of 1 year of work experience in a health or policy related field; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate certificate; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate diploma, or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Health Studies
description:
The Master of Health Studies at the University of Sydney gives working health professionals a flexible, research-informed grounding in health systems and policy, drawing on the same teaching used in the University's health policy and planning program. Students build practical understanding of systems thinking, health financing, politics and the use of evidence in health decision-making, delivered through an interactive learning environment that fits around full-time work.
The course suits practitioners and public servants who want to progress into health policy, planning or leadership roles. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and tenth globally for public health.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: a bachelor's degree with first or second class honours from the University of Sydney, or equivalent qualification and a minimum of 1 year of work experience in a health or policy related field; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate certificate; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate diploma, or equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Heritage Conservation
description:
The Master of Heritage Conservation at the University of Sydney equips graduates to practise heritage conservation as an ethic of care grounded in intergenerational equity and cross-cultural understanding. Coursework develops advanced competencies in documenting and assessing culturally significant places, formulating heritage policy, and understanding the legal frameworks and professional methods that govern heritage practice, engaging with debates such as sustainability and climate change.
Graduates work as heritage consultants, planners, policy experts, educators and architectural conservation specialists across the public sector, private practice and community organisations. The University of Sydney is ranked among the world's top 25 universities.
admission_requirements: a) a bachelor's degree or higher from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification with a credit average mark; or (b) completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate diploma with a credit average mark .
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Human Resource Management & Industrial Relations
description:
The Master of Human Resource Management and Industrial Relations at the University of Sydney Business School gives students a sound understanding of key employment issues and the skills to respond to changes reshaping local and international work practices and policies. Core and elective units cover human resource management and industrial relations in depth, finishing with a capstone project in the final semester.
The accredited program suits students building a career in people management, with graduates moving into roles such as human resource manager, workplace relations manager, diversity consultant, policy analyst and industrial relations advisor.
admission_requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree with honours or higher in any discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in a related discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification or an Australian bachelor's degree in an unrelated discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, and relevant professional work experience (typically two years) or any of the above combinations of qualifications and/or experience with less than a credit average (minimum 50 percent required) and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585) or equivalent Business School approved admissions test, or the University of Sydney Graduate Diploma or Graduate Certificate in Human Resource Management and Industrial Relations with a credit average (65 percent).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Human Rights
description:
The Master of Human Rights at the University of Sydney, delivered as the Master of Social Justice (Human Rights), builds a critical understanding of the roots of human rights violations and the tools deployed to promote and protect them. All students take four elemental core units offering an interdisciplinary grounding in development, peace and conflict, and human rights, tackling problems including poverty, conflict transformation and environmental crises.
The course suits people who want to work in policy, advocacy and research in human rights and humanitarianism at any scale. Graduates hold positions at organisations including UNICEF, the World Health Organisation, Amnesty International and government departments.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65 percent) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, with a major in the humanities or social sciences, or or an equivalent level of performance in an equivalent qualification; or completion of the requirements for the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Social Justice with a minimum credit (65 percent) average, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Information Technology
description: The University of Sydney's Master of Information Technology is a coursework degree for IT professionals extending their technical knowledge or moving into a new specialisation. It offers six majors across four areas, software, business, engineering and health, drawing on more than 25 IT specialist units plus units from electrical engineering and business, and every student completes a substantial project. Students can focus on one major or combine subjects from related majors, and the health and business majors sit alongside the more technical software and engineering streams. It suits people updating existing IT skills or crossing into a new area of computing. Graduates work as software engineers, systems architects, IT consultants, business analysts, data and cloud specialists and technical project leads. Indicative international tuition is around A$57,900 per year.
discontinued_note: This award now sits within the Master of Computer Science, which covers computer science and information technology together with an advanced-entry pathway for applicants with a computing qualification.

name: Master of Intensive Care Nursing
description:
The Master of Intensive Care Nursing is a specialisation stream within the University of Sydney's Master of Nursing, for registered nurses and graduate-entry students moving into critical care nursing. It shares the Master of Nursing's core units in anatomy, pathophysiology, pharmacology and culturally safe, person-centred practice, concentrated on intensive and critical care.
The program is accredited by the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Accreditation Council, leading to registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. Graduates work in intensive care units and high-dependency wards across Australian and international health systems.
admission_requirements: You must have: a previous Australian level bachelor degree (or equivalent) in any discipline other than nursing, AND this qualification has been completed within 10 years prior to applying Overseas nursing qualifications are acceptable. See our Master of Nursing Admissions Guide (pdf, 1.00MB) for more information.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Interaction Design and Electronic Arts
description:
The Master of Interaction Design and Electronic Arts at the University of Sydney introduces the fundamentals of human-centred design for products and services, aimed at people seeking a career in UX, UI, interactive products or the creative use of technology. Foundation and advanced core units, delivered as design studios and technical workshops, build analytical, design and communication skills, finishing with a capstone that can be a client-focused studio, research project or dissertation.
Graduates become proficient in the creative use of new technologies across a wide range of professional settings, moving into roles such as UX/UI designer, interaction designer, product designer and service designer.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Interaction Design and Electronic Arts requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification with a credit average mark across all units; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate diploma; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate certificate with an average mark of at least 70.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of International Business
description:
The Master of International Business at the University of Sydney Business School develops the skills to devise and implement strategic decisions that drive sustainable, global corporate expansion. Core units cover global business and strategy, including dedicated international business project units, complemented by elective units chosen to meet course requirements.
The program is ranked first in Australia in the QS International Trade Rankings 2026, and suits students looking to accelerate an international career. Graduates move into roles spanning global management, import and export management, and consulting for organisations such as the World Bank, Austrade and the United Nations.
admission_requirements: Education To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in a related discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in an unrelated discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification and relevant professional work experience (typically three years), or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in a related discipline with less than a credit average (minimum 50 percent required) or equivalent qualification and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585) or equivalent Business School approved admissions test. Demonstrated commitment Applicants must demonstrate commitment by providing a statement of motivation that demonstrates clear evidence that the candidate has researched the program and has the capability and mindset to learn in an experiential environment. Selection interview All applications will be ranked according to academic merit after the application closing date. Successfully ranked applicants will be invited to participate in an interview.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of International Business and Law
description:
The Master of International Business and Law at the University of Sydney combines the University's global business program with legal study, developing the skills to devise and implement strategic decisions for sustainable global corporate expansion alongside an understanding of the legal frameworks that govern international trade. Core units cover global business and strategy, including international business project units, alongside legal electives.
The course suits students accelerating an international career who want business strategy skills paired with legal literacy. Graduates move into global management, international consulting and trade roles with organisations such as the World Bank and the United Nations.
admission_requirements: Education To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in a related discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in an unrelated discipline with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification and relevant professional work experience (typically three years), or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher in a related discipline with less than a credit average (minimum 50 percent required) or equivalent qualification and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585) or equivalent Business School approved admissions test. Demonstrated commitment Applicants must demonstrate commitment by providing a statement of motivation that demonstrates clear evidence that the candidate has researched the program and has the capability and mindset to learn in an experiential environment. english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of International Law
description:
The Master of International Law at the University of Sydney examines the international rules governing relations between states, states and international organisations, and states and individuals, taught by faculty who integrate international relations, security studies and legal structure. Students complete a core unit in international law plus electives, including options from the Department of Government and International Relations or the Centre for International Law.
The course suits students who want an interdisciplinary understanding of international law alongside international relations and politics. Graduates work as barristers, judges, solicitors, diplomats and policy advisers across foreign affairs, global business and international organisations.
admission_requirements: Admission to this degree requires: a bachelor's degree with a credit average (65 percent) from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; and the applicant provides evidence of two years of relevant professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of International Relations
description:
The Master of International Relations at the University of Sydney examines the world's most pressing challenges, including war and peace, social and economic justice, development and environmental crises, through the study of relations among states and non-state actors. Core units cover key theories and institutions in international relations, with optional specialisations in international security studies, peace and conflict studies, or political economy, finishing with a capstone research project.
The program suits students building or advancing a career in international affairs. Graduates move into consulting, diplomacy, development, government, defence, immigration and international business roles, supported by the University's links to major Australian policy think tanks.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of International Relations (2 years full-time) requires: a bachelor’s degree from the University of Sydney with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in International Relations with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification. Reduced volume of learning If you have completed a qualification in a relevant discipline or have relevant professional experience, you may be eligible for a reduction in course requirements based on the criteria below. Admission to the Master of International Relations (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor’s degree from the University of Sydney with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, including a major in the humanities, social sciences, or law, or an equivalent qualification; or relevant professional experience and a bachelor’s degree with a minimum credit (65%) average. Admission to the Master of International Relations (1 year full-time) requires: an honours degree in the humanities, social sciences, or law. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s, you may be able to enter via the Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of International Security
description:
The Master of International Security is the international security studies specialisation within the University of Sydney's Master of International Relations, examining the world's most pressing security challenges through the study of relations among states and non-state actors. Core units cover key theories and institutions in international relations, with selective units focused on international security, finishing with a capstone research project.
The program suits students building or advancing a career in defence, intelligence or international security policy. Graduates move into government, defence, intelligence agencies and international organisations, supported by the University's links to major Australian policy think tanks.

name: Master of Labour Law and Relations
description:
The Master of Labour Law and Relations at the University of Sydney combines expertise from the Law School, Business School and Department of Political Economy, and is open to students with or without a law degree. Over 48 credit points, students complete compulsory units in labour law and industrial relations policy, with students lacking a law background also completing a legal reasoning foundation unit.
The interdisciplinary qualification suits legal and human resource professionals who want to specialise in employment and industrial law, drawing at least 24 credit points from Sydney Law School units. Graduates work across law and human resources in roles that bridge legal practice and industrial relations.
admission_requirements: Admission to the degree requires: a bachelor's degree with a credit average (65 percent) from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification.; or a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; and the applicant provides evidence of two years of relevant professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Laws
description:
The Master of Laws at the University of Sydney lets law graduates and Juris Doctor holders specialise and diversify their legal expertise, choosing electives from areas including administrative law and policy, business law, criminology, environmental law, health law, international law, jurisprudence, labour law and taxation law. Students complete a capstone long research essay in at least one chosen elective area.
The degree deepens expertise for legal professionals working across practice, government, business, policy and international organisations, with career outcomes shaped by prior experience and chosen specialisation.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for this course required a Bachelor of Laws or Juris Doctor with a credit average (65 percent) from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification.
