english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Logistics and Supply Chain Management
description:
The Master of Logistics and Supply Chain Management at the University of Sydney Business School develops specialist skills in one of the world's fastest-growing business sectors, with a strong focus on resilience, analytics, sustainability, ethics and responsible management. Core and elective units cover concepts and techniques applicable across procurement, warehousing, manufacturing, shipping, airlines and retail, finishing with a project capstone unit.
Graduates are in high demand around the world, moving into roles such as logistics manager, supply chain director, export manager and procurement manager. The University of Sydney's logistics and supply chain program is ranked highly in the ShanghaiRanking Global Ranking of Academic Subjects.
admission_requirements: To be considered for admission to the Master of Logistics and Supply Chain Management, an applicant is required to have: a bachelor’s degree with honours or higher qualification in any discipline with a minimum credit average (or equivalent) at an institution approved by the Business School; or a bachelor's degree in a cognate discipline, as defined by the Business School, with a minimum credit average (or equivalent) at an institution approved by the Business School; or a bachelor's degree or higher qualification in a non-cognate discipline with a minimum credit average (or equivalent) at an institution approved by the Business School and a minimum of two years relevant work experience; or completion of the qualifications and experience specified in (1), (2) or (3) with a minimum pass average (or equivalent) and performance in an admissions test approved by the Business School to a standard considered satisfactory by the Business School; and satisfaction of the English language requirements; and any other minimum standards specified by the Business School; or completion of the requirements of either the Graduate Certificate or the Graduate Diploma in Logistics and Supply Chain Management from the University of Sydney with a credit average, or equivalent qualification. In exceptional circumstances, the Business School may admit applicants without these qualifications who, in the opinion of the Business School, have qualifications and evidence of experience and achievement sufficient to successfully undertake the award.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Management
description:
The Master of Management at the University of Sydney Business School is ranked first in Australia and styled like an MBA but designed for a younger market, requiring no prior work experience and open to graduates from any discipline. Over 15 months full-time or two years part-time, a hand-picked cohort of around 50 students completes six core units in leadership, strategy, financial management, business tools, digital transformation and the future of business, plus a capstone project with corporate partners.
The program builds the skills businesses demand from future leaders through direct company engagement and interactive learning. Graduates move into change management, executive management, government and non-profit management roles around the world.
admission_requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree or higher with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher with less than a credit average (minimum 50 percent required), and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585) or equivalent Business School approved admissions test.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Marine Science and Management
description:
The Master of Marine Science and Management at the University of Sydney gives students hands-on experience at leading Australian coastal field sites, including One Tree Island on the Great Barrier Reef, covering coastal management, environmental modelling, marine law, marine biology, reef science and climate change. Students take a coursework or research pathway, building both theoretical understanding and applied skills to manage dynamic marine environments.
The course suits graduates passionate about ocean conservation seeking marine science careers. Graduates move into roles including marine ecologist, fisheries scientist, oceanographer, marine policy analyst and aquaculture manager.
admission_requirements: For admission into this course, you should have: a Bachelor of Science with a credit average in one of the following disciplines: biology, chemistry, physics, mathematics, ecology, climate and atmospheric sciences, marine science, geosciences, geography, geology environmental studies, environmental engineering, civil engineering, aquaculture, agriculture or natural resource management; or a Bachelor of Science with Honours in one for the disciplines listed above. A credit average means a minimum Grade Point Average (GPA) of 65.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Media Practice
description:
The Master of Media Practice at the University of Sydney covers content production across the global field of media and communications, including broadcast and online journalism, writing for media, social media, and the ethical and legal issues involved. Core units cover media industries, audiences and the global media environment, finishing with a capstone professional research project, internship or dissertation, and an internship component giving students hands-on experience and industry contacts.
Graduates move into multiplatform journalism, content production, editing, social media, podcasting and video production, with alumni working across prominent national and international media organisations.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Master of Media Practice (1.5 years full-time) Admission to the Master of Media Practice (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification. Master of Media Practice (1 year full-time) Admission to the Master of Media Practice (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Media Practice with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Medical Physics
description:
The Master of Medical Physics at the University of Sydney provides specialist postgraduate training in radiation physics, artificial intelligence, dosimetry, imaging, radiobiology and radiation protection for medical conditions including cancer, setting graduates on the path to becoming a clinical medical physicist. Students complete core units in radiotherapy physics, medical imaging physics and nuclear medicine physics, finishing with a final-year research project.
Sydney's School of Physics is the country's leading physics department, with access to supercomputers and modern laboratories. Graduates work as trainee medical physicists in hospital departments, dosimetry laboratories, radiation protection agencies and health-related government departments.
admission_requirements: Admission to this course requires: a bachelor's degree in Science or Engineering with a minimum credit average and a major in physics or equivalent; or completion of the requirements for the Graduate Diploma in Medical Physics with a credit average or better.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Medicine (Clinical Epidemiology)
description:
The Master of Medicine (Clinical Epidemiology) at the University of Sydney is a fully online degree for clinicians and clinical researchers who want to generate and interpret high-quality clinical research. Students complete two core units in introductory clinical epidemiology and biostatistics, a capstone unit, and five elective units chosen to fit their own research interests.
Graduates can apply for continuing professional development points with relevant medical colleges, and the course builds the end-to-end research skills used across the clinical research pathway, from study design through analysis to translating evidence into practice. Sydney is ranked first in Australia for public health.
admission_requirements: Admission to the course requires: a medical degree from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Mental Health Nursing
description:
The Master of Mental Health Nursing is a specialisation stream within the University of Sydney's Master of Nursing, for registered nurses and graduate-entry students building a career in mental health care. It shares the Master of Nursing's core units in anatomy, pathophysiology, pharmacology and culturally safe, person-centred practice, concentrated on mental health nursing.
The program is accredited by the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Accreditation Council and leads toward registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. Graduates work in mental health wards, community mental health teams and specialist services across Australia and internationally.
admission_requirements: You must have: a previous Australian level bachelor degree (or equivalent) in any discipline other than nursing, AND this qualification has been completed within 10 years prior to applying Overseas nursing qualifications are acceptable. See our Master of Nursing Admissions Guide (pdf, 1.00MB) for more information.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Museum and Heritage Studies
description:
The Master of Museum and Heritage Studies at the University of Sydney develops a deep understanding of the core historical and theoretical developments in museum and heritage studies, current practice and debates. Core units cover managing collections and heritage sites, finishing with a capstone internship project or dissertation, alongside electives matched to the student's interests.
The course suits students interested in how museums and heritage sites, including sites of trauma and commemoration, engage the public. Graduates move into museum education, collection management, heritage site interpretation and cultural policy roles.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Museum and Heritage Studies (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a major in one of Anthropology, Archaeology, Art History, Classics and Ancient History, Cultural Geography, Cultural Studies, Education, English, Gender Studies, History, Indigenous Studies or another major with an equivalent skills and knowledge base; and a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Museum & Heritage Studies (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the requirements for the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Museum and Heritage Studies with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Music (Performance)
description:
The Master of Music (Performance) at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music lets students with a performance-focused music degree develop high-level, research-based creative work culminating in a public performance presentation and a written dissertation. Candidates receive training and supervision to develop their performance practice, demonstrating independence of thought, critical awareness and interpretative capacity through a recital, lecture recital, recording or other creative format.
The course suits aspiring musicians aiming for scholarly and high-level performance careers, articulating how their creative work extends the boundaries of the discipline of performance.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, you must have completed the equivalent of a Bachelor's degree in music with a major in performance. In exceptional circumstances the Dean or Associate Dean may admit an applicant who does not meet this requirement provided that the applicant has exceptional qualifications and presents evidence of having the aptitude required for undertaking the course. The University must certify that there are sufficient supervisory and other resources and facilities available to enable your candidature to be completed successfully.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Music Studies (Performance)
description:
The Master of Music Studies (Performance) at the Sydney Conservatorium of Music develops command of performance technique and musical communication across orchestral and solo instruments, early music, jazz and contemporary music. Students choose a principal study area, presenting recitals and participating in ensembles and chamber groups throughout the course, culminating in a final-semester public performance.
The Conservatorium has some of the best music facilities in the Asia-Pacific region, located near the Sydney Opera House. Graduates reach the levels of excellence demanded by the profession, moving into careers as performing soloists, chamber musicians and orchestral or ensemble players.
admission_requirements: Admission requires: a master's degree in an appropriate discipline as determined by the Sydney Conservatorium of Music; or a pass bachelor's degree with a credit average, or an honours bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or equivalent qualification in an appropriate discipline as determined by the Conservatorium; or an award of graduate diploma from the University of Sydney, or equivalent qualification in an appropriate discipline as determined by the Conservatorium; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate diploma in this discipline from the University of Sydney, or equivalent qualification; and successful completion of an audition. Available places will be offered to qualified applicants in the order in which complete applications are received, and according to the admissions criteria. Applicants who do not have a recognised tertiary award but who demonstrate an equivalent musical ability and maturity at the audition and interview, and who can show considerable performing experience may be admitted.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 73; PTE Academic 60 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Nursing
description:
The Master of Nursing at the University of Sydney is a graduate-entry degree for non-nursing degree holders who want to become registered nurses, and the base program behind the University's family of specialised nursing masters. Core units cover anatomy and pathophysiology, pharmacology, clinical and relational skills, and nursing practice informed by Indigenous knowledges, alongside professional clinical placements across the lifespan and diverse patient populations.
The course is accredited by the Australian Nursing and Midwifery Accreditation Council, and graduates register with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. Sydney's nursing graduates work across paediatric, intensive care, trauma, emergency, mental health and community settings in Australia and abroad.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (writing 7.0); PTE Academic 72. The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Nutrition and Dietetics
description:
The Master of Nutrition and Dietetics at the University of Sydney is a two-year course for science graduates that builds on human biochemistry and physiology to cover the role of nutrients and diet in health and disease. Core units in the first year prepare students for public health nutrition, individual patient case management, food service management, and nutrition research and evaluation.
Graduates are qualified to work as dietitians and nutritionists across public health, medical nutrition therapy, food service, communication and research. Sydney is ranked 25th globally for life sciences and medicine.
admission_requirements: Admission to the degree requires a Bachelor of Science degree with a credit average. The applicant must also have successfully completed the following prerequisite units of study within the last 10 years: 12 credit points of junior chemistry, or equivalent; and 12 credit points of junior human biology, or equivalent; and 12 credit points of intermediate or senior Biochemistry and/or Molecular Biology, or equivalent; and 12 credit points of intermediate or senior Human Physiology, or equivalent; and 6 credit points of intermediate or senior Nutrition Science, or equivalent; and 6 credit points of intermediate or senior Food Science, or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Occupational Therapy
description:
The Master of Occupational Therapy at the University of Sydney prepares graduate-entry students to help people with physical, social or emotional challenges participate fully in daily life, through practical learning and extensive clinical placements. The course is recognised by the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency, and teaching takes a collaborative, strengths-based approach to helping people overcome barriers from disability, injury or ongoing conditions.
Graduates work in multidisciplinary teams across hospitals, rehabilitation centres, private practice, occupational health, schools and aged care. Sydney is ranked fourth in the world for sports-related subjects and in the top 20 universities globally.
admission_requirements: To be eligible to apply you will need to fulfill the following criteria; A bachelor's degree, master's degree or PhD from an Australian institution or equivalent. A minimum average mark of 60 out of 100 or equivalent. This does not guarantee an offer as the places are limited and offers are made based on academic merit. Evidence of any other minimum standards specified by the Faculty of Medicine and Health. For domestic applicants, the Indigenous Facilitated Entry Scheme, the Rural Applicants Facilitated Entry Scheme, and Applicants Living with Disabilities Facilitated Entry Scheme are available for eligible applicants. Applicants under the facilitated entry scheme must upload the required supporting documentation at the time of application.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Peace and Conflict Studies
description:
The Master of Peace and Conflict Studies at the University of Sydney, delivered as the Master of Social Justice (Peace and Conflict Studies), examines the intellectual and practical challenges of attaining peace with justice, from post-conflict reconciliation to the United Nations' role in peacekeeping. Students complete core units offering an interdisciplinary grounding in development, peace and conflict, and human rights, plus stream selective units, finishing with a capstone dissertation, placement or research project.
The course suits people seeking careers with the United Nations, non-government organisations, media, the private sector or government agencies. Graduates hold positions such as international programs officer, mediator and reporter.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Social Justice (Peace and Conflict Studies) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65 percent) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, with a major in the humanities or social sciences, or or an equivalent level of performance in an equivalent qualification; or completion of the requirements for the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Social Justice with a minimum credit (65 percent) average, or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Pharmacy
description:
The Master of Pharmacy at the University of Sydney is an accredited two-year graduate-entry program that prepares students for the full scope of pharmacy practice, including leadership in evidence-based care. Core units cover professional practice and experiential placement, with a capstone unit in the final semester, and graduates become eligible to register with the Pharmacy Board of Australia after completing supervised practical training and an intern training program.
Careers span community pharmacy, hospital pharmacy, research and the pharmaceutical industry, including drug production and marketing. Sydney is ranked 20th globally for pharmacy and pharmacology.
admission_requirements: Admission requirements from 2026: To be eligible to apply for the Master of Pharmacy applicants will need to fulfill the following criteria: A bachelor's degree from an Australian institution or equivalent A minimum Grade Point Average (GPA), currently 5.0 over 7.0 (equivalent to 65% at USYD), or Graduate Australian Medical Admissions Test (GAMSAT), currently 55 with 50 in each section, or Medical College Admission Test (MCAT), currently 8 (previous test version) / 500 (new test version). 36 credit points, or equivalent, in five prerequisite subjects at university level (see below) English language proficiency of IELTS 7.0 overall with 6.5 in each band (if relevant) Admission pathway Course transfers from current Master of Pharmacy programs across Australia will be considered. Subject exemptions are assessed on a case-by-case basis. International pharmacy graduates with registration from outside of Australia are accepted provided pharmacy registration has been within the last ten years. It is not a requirement to have a GPA, MCAT or GAMSAT for this application. Applicants with relevant professional experience (eg pharmaceutical industry or related research area) within the last ten years will be considered on a case-by-case basis. It is not a requirement to have a GPA, MCAT or GAMSAT for this application.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Philosophy (Architecture, Design and Planning)
description:
The Master of Philosophy (Architecture, Design and Planning) at the University of Sydney lets candidates undertake research and advanced specialisation in any area of scholarship pursued by the Sydney School of Architecture, Design and Planning, alongside required coursework. Students access a range of specialist units supporting research development, including analytical methods, professional development and discipline-specific subjects.
The course suits candidates with a bachelor's degree with honours or a master's degree in architecture, design or a related field, aiming for leadership roles in academia, design practice or industry. Graduates gain deeper subject expertise plus analytical, problem-solving and project management skills.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Master of Philosophy (Architecture, Design and Planning), you must have completed the equivalent of one of the following in a subject area related to your proposed research area: bachelor's degree with first class or second class honours or, master's degree These criteria constitute the minimum requirements for eligibility and do not guarantee admission. That remains at the discretion of the relevant supervisors and departments, and access to supervision remains highly competitive. The University must certify that there are sufficient supervisory and other resources and facilities available to enable your candidature to be completed successfully.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Physiotherapy
description:
The Master of Physiotherapy at the University of Sydney is a graduate-entry degree combining clinical education and research training across the core areas of physiotherapy practice. Teaching takes a patient-centred, evidence-based approach, with hands-on clinical placements at urban public and private clinics and rural health settings that give students real-world experience with patients from professional practice week one.
Graduates take on direct client care, education, research, management and policy roles across hospitals, private practice, sports facilities, schools and aged care. Sydney is ranked fourth globally for sports-related subjects and in the top 20 universities worldwide.
admission_requirements: To be eligible to apply you will need to fulfill the following criteria; A bachelor's degree, master's degree, or a PhD from an Australian institution or equivalent, completed before 1 January of the year in which the applicant intends to commence the Doctor of Physiotherapy. Academic performance in an eligible degree - the standard requirement to be eligible to apply is a minimum average mark of 65 or equivalent. Rural applicants as well as Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants must have a minimum average mark of 60 or equivalent. For domestic applicants, the Indigenous Facilitated Entry Scheme and the Rural Applicants Facilitated Entry Scheme are available for eligible applicants. Please refer to the Doctor of Physiotherapy Special Admission Pathways Guide for definitions and information on facilitated entry schemes.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Political Economy
description:
The Master of Political Economy at the University of Sydney examines how political, institutional, social, cultural and historical factors shape economic life, developing critical analysis and communication skills for engaging with public policy debates. Core units survey the history of economics and Australian political economy, with optional specialisations in country risk assessment or social and environmental policy.
The University of Sydney has the largest number of political economists in Australia, with affiliations to scholars including former Greek finance minister Yanis Varoufakis. Graduates work as policy analysts and researchers across government, business, research institutions and the media.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Political Economy (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree,including a major in the social sciences, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Political Economy with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification. Reduced volume of learning If you have completed a qualification in a relevant discipline or have relevant professional experience, you may be eligible for a reduction in course requirements based on the criteria below. Admission to the Master of Political Economy (1 year full-time) requires: an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s, you may be able to enter via the Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Primary Health Care
description: The Master of Primary Health Care at the University of Sydney is delivered through the university's medicine offering in general practice and primary health care, extending knowledge and skills across areas such as dermatology, diabetes and metabolic health, paediatrics, internal medicine, mental health and clinical teaching. It is designed for doctors across all levels of experience. Graduates strengthen their general practice and primary care work. Indicative international tuition is around 41,000 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description:
The Master of Professional Accounting at the University of Sydney Business School gives graduates from non-accounting disciplines a pathway into the accounting profession, developing the technical and professional skills needed for accredited practice. The course covers core accounting, finance and business knowledge alongside the analytics and communication skills employers expect from modern accountants.
Graduates are prepared for professional body recognition and roles across public practice, corporate accounting and financial management. The University of Sydney Business School's accounting programs are taught across seven specialist disciplines with strong industry input.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 64. The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Professional Accounting and Business Performance
description:
The Master of Professional Accounting and Business Performance at the University of Sydney Business School is an accredited postgraduate degree developed with industry and taught across seven Business School disciplines, pairing deep technical accounting expertise with analytics, technology and communication skills. Core units and a capstone build experience in enterprise performance management and cloud-based accounting technology platforms.
Graduates are well equipped for roles including chief financial officer, financial controller, company secretary, financial analyst, forensic accountant, and tax and estate adviser across a wide range of organisations.
admission_requirements: To be considered for admission, an applicant is required to have: Australian bachelor's degree or higher with a credit average (65 percent) or equivalent qualification, or Australian bachelor's degree or higher (minimum 50 percent required) or equivalent qualification, and satisfactory performance in the GMAT (for guidance, the class average score is 630) or GMAT Focus Edition (for guidance, the class average score is 585), or University of Sydney Graduate Diploma in Professional Accounting and Business Performance with a credit average (65 percent).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Professional Engineering
description:
The Master of Professional Engineering (Software Engineering) at the University of Sydney is designed for people transitioning from a science or mathematics career into engineering, or engineers changing specialisation, giving them an advanced understanding of software production from strategy and design to coding, quality and management. Students study advanced computer architecture, real-time computing, internet software platforms and object-oriented design across an extensive core and elective unit structure with a project or research pathway.
Graduates move into roles across information technology, database management, telecommunications, internet programming, control systems, biomedical systems and artificial intelligence, with professional accreditation supporting registration as an engineer.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian Bachelor of Engineering degree with a 65 percent average, or equivalent qualification or an Australian bachelor's degree in a non-Engineering discipline with a 65 percent average, with studies equivalent to 48 credit points (equivalent to 1 year full time study load) in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, geology, computing or statistics, as related to the stream sought for admission.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Project and Program Management
description:
The Master of Project and Program Management at the University of Sydney's Faculty of Engineering gives working professionals the fundamental methodologies, modelling and analytical techniques needed to design and implement major projects across industries. Technical, strategic and leadership-focused core units are combined with a capstone comprising either a research thesis or a professional project.
Graduates move into senior project manager, program director and chief project officer roles across sectors including construction, mining, IT, finance, manufacturing and environmental consultancy, locally and internationally.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: a bachelor's degree in any discipline with a minimum credit average (65 percent) or an Australian bachelor's degree (with honours), or equivalent qualification or a combination of a bachelor's degree and relevant industry experience and certifications or a University of Sydney Graduate Diploma/Graduate Certificate in Project Management with a credit average (65 percent)
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Project Management
description:
The Master of Project Management at the University of Sydney's Faculty of Engineering gives working professionals advanced, hands-on project management skills through technical, strategic and leadership-focused core units. Students finish with a capstone comprising either a research thesis or a professional project, alongside elective units chosen to meet course requirements.
The program is accredited by the Project Management Institute and draws on the University's John Grill Institute for Project Leadership. Graduates move into senior project manager, program director and chief project officer roles across industries from construction and mining to IT and finance.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: a bachelor's degree in any discipline with a minimum credit average (65 percent) or an Australian bachelor's degree (with honours), or equivalent qualification or a combination of a bachelor's degree and relevant industry experience and certifications or a University of Sydney Graduate Diploma/Graduate Certificate in Project Management with a credit average (65 percent)
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Public Administration
description:
The Master of Public Administration at the University of Sydney gives students a critical, multidisciplinary perspective on public policy at the global, national and local level, amid growing public scrutiny, shrinking resources and new cross-border challenges. Core units cover the fundamentals of public policy and administration, with optional specialisations in economic policy, political economy or social policy, finishing with a capstone research project or supervised dissertation.
The course suits people working in or aiming for government and the public sector, as well as those in non-government and private organisations who want to understand government's role in policymaking. Graduates move into policy analyst, government adviser and strategic planning roles.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Public Policy requires: a bachelor’s degree from the University of Sydney with a minimum credit (65%) average, calculated over the whole degree, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Public Policy with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s, you may be able to enter via the Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Public Health
description:
The Master of Public Health at the University of Sydney builds the knowledge and skills needed to manage community health problems and improve population health outcomes, for students from medical, non-medical, academic and professional backgrounds. Core units cover epidemiology, biostatistics, health promotion, research and ethics, and students can use their elective allowance to complete an optional area of specialisation.
Graduates take on hands-on and research-oriented public health roles, including government health officer, health educator, health promotion officer and clinical researcher. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and tenth globally for public health.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Public Health requires: completion of the requirements for the embedded Graduate Diploma with at least a credit average in the core units of study; or a bachelor’s degree in public health, medicine, medical science, nursing, allied health (including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, optometry), dentistry, veterinary science, education, communication and journalism, science, arts, psychology, social science, political science, policy analysis, government, international relations, engineering, architecture, mathematics, law, economics, commerce, business, accounting and marketing from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Public Policy
description:
The Master of Public Policy at the University of Sydney gives students a critical, multidisciplinary perspective on public policy at the global, national and local level, amid growing public scrutiny, shrinking resources and new cross-border challenges. Core units cover the fundamentals of public policy and administration, with optional specialisations in economic policy, political economy or social policy, finishing with a capstone research project or supervised dissertation.
Certain units can be completed intensively over four days rather than across a full semester. Graduates move into policy analyst, government adviser and strategic planning roles across administration, research and education.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Public Policy requires: a bachelor’s degree from the University of Sydney with a minimum credit (65%) average, calculated over the whole degree, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Public Policy with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s, you may be able to enter via the Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Publishing
description:
The Master of Publishing at the University of Sydney gives students the skills needed for the evolving world of print, digital and audio publishing, combining professional training with a broad understanding of publishing's cultural and technological context. Core units cover publishing and online editing, print and website production, design and marketing, finishing with a capstone professional research project, internship or dissertation.
The course is taught by industry practitioners and publishing scholars, covering commissioning, acquisition, editing and production. Graduates move into publishing houses, freelance work, and roles bringing publishing expertise to any organisation.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Publishing (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, including a major in the humanities or social sciences, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Publishing (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Publishing with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Science
discontinued_note: Sydney no longer offers a generic Master of Science; the degree is now offered as named specialisations such as Master of Science in Coaching Psychology and Master of Science in Medicine (various streams).

name: Master of Science in Coaching Psychology
description:
The Master of Science in Coaching Psychology at the University of Sydney is an applied positive psychology program sitting at the intersection of counselling, clinical and organisational psychology, giving students the skills to enhance productivity and quality of life for individuals, organisations and communities. Students can complete the degree via a coursework or research pathway, using a client-centred approach across career development, executive coaching, leadership growth and organisational change.
The University of Sydney's coaching psychology program is the world's first and longest-running of its kind. Graduates move into human resource development, private practice, organisational consultancy and executive coaching roles.
admission_requirements: Admission to this degree requires: An undergraduate degree with Honours in Psychology or a postgraduate degree in a cognate discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent institution; and a minimum of three years relevant employment experience* *Relevant work experience may include counselling, experience in organisational learning and development, management experience, employment in applied psychology settings, professional coaching or other areas directly related to coaching.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 105; PTE Academic 78 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Science in Medicine (Clinical Epidemiology)
description:
The Master of Science in Medicine (Clinical Epidemiology) at the University of Sydney is a fully online, 48 credit point degree for health professionals and clinical researchers who want deep training in clinical research methods. Twelve credit points of core units, a capstone and 30 credit points of electives give students structured, end-to-end research skills from study design and biostatistics through to translating findings into practice and policy.
The course is designed around busy clinical schedules and suits health care professionals, clinical researchers and health decision makers. Sydney is ranked first in Australia and tenth globally for public health.
admission_requirements: Admission to the course requires: a bachelor's degree in a health-related discipline with first or second class honours from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification; or a pass bachelor's degree in a health-related discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification. Applicants must have completed work equivalent to a first or second class honours bachelor's degree or pass a preliminary examination(s) as prescribed by the Faculty; or completion of the first 4 years of an undergraduate medical degree that is accredited by the Australian Medical Council, and a letter of recommendation from the head of clinical school/medical program supporting concurrent enrolment while completing degree requirements. All students entering the program are expected to have some clinical experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Social Justice
description: The Master of Social Justice at the University of Sydney is an eighteen-month full-time degree offered with streams including human rights, peace and conflict studies, and development studies. Students gain a critical understanding of social justice issues and the tools and mechanisms used to address them, and develop skills in research, analysis, communication and advocacy for domestic, regional and international contexts. Graduates work in advocacy, policy, research and humanitarian roles. Indicative international tuition is around 51,800 Australian dollars per year.
discontinued_note: Sydney no longer offers a generic Master of Social Justice; the degree is now offered as named streams such as Master of Social Justice (Human Rights), (Peace and Conflict Studies) and (Development Studies).

name: Master of Social Work
description:
The Master of Social Work (Qualifying) at the University of Sydney equips graduates to become professional social workers in health, community services or the non-government sector, developing expertise in social work values and holistic client-centred practice. Core units cover practice with Indigenous Australians, mental health, child protection, violence against women, ageing and social exclusion, finishing with a capstone integration-of-learning unit.
The course responds directly to the AASW accreditation process's priority learning areas, including cross-cultural practice and standards for working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. Graduates take on leadership roles across social work and related professions.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Social Work (Qualifying) requires: a relevant Australian bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification; and evidence of the ability to meet the required prerequisite knowledge in relation to human development and of society; and evidence of relevant employment history in human and community services industry (generally evidence of at least 2 years is required). In exceptional circumstances, the Dean may admit applicants without a bachelor's degree who, in the opinion of the faculty, have qualifications and evidence of experience and achievement sufficient to successfully undertake the award. This may include evidence through publications or authorship of official documents.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.5 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 105; PTE Academic 78 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Speech Language Pathology
description:
The Master of Speech Language Pathology at the University of Sydney is a graduate-entry degree open to candidates from any prior discipline who want to assess and treat communication and swallowing difficulties across all ages and cultures. Core units in speech pathology theory and practice lead to eligibility for practising membership of Speech Pathology Australia on graduation.
Graduates work with children and adults experiencing difficulties with speech, language comprehension, reading, writing, voice, stuttering or swallowing, across hospitals, private practice, schools and early childhood services. Sydney is ranked 25th in the world for life sciences and medicine.
admission_requirements: To be eligible to apply you will need to fulfil the following criteria: An Australian bachelor's degree, master's or PhD from an Australian institution or equivalent. A minimum average mark of 60 out of 100 or equivalent (GPA of 4.5 out of 7). This does not guarantee an offer as the places are limited and offers are made based on academic merit. Evidence of any other minimum standards specified by the Faculty of Medicine and Health. For domestic applicants, the Indigenous Facilitated Entry Scheme and the Rural Applicants Facilitated Entry Scheme are available for eligible applicants. Please refer to the Sydney School of Health Sciences Special Admission Pathways Guide for definitions and information on facilitated entry schemes.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 7.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 72 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Strategic Public Relations
description:
The Master of Strategic Public Relations at the University of Sydney covers corporate, government, media, investor, community, political and environmental relations, taking a critical approach to how practitioners exert and experience influence. Core units cover strategy selection in corporate PR, crisis communication, political public relations, and public opinion and policy, finishing with a capstone special project or year-long dissertation.
The course suits career changers moving into public relations as well as media professionals extending their skillset. Graduates hold roles including public relations adviser, media and communications officer, public affairs consultant and social marketing coordinator.
admission_requirements: Entry in the 1 year or 1.5 year degree program is determined by the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) criteria below: Admission to candidature for the Master of Strategic Public Relations (1.5 years full-time) requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average calculated over the whole degree, from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification. Admission to candidature for the Master of Strategic Public Relations (1 year full-time) requires: completion of the embedded Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in Strategic Public Relations with a minimum credit (65%) average, or an equivalent qualification; or an Honours degree in a relevant discipline; or relevant professional work experience and a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit (65%) average or an equivalent qualification. If you do not meet the requirements listed above for direct entry to the Master’s degree, you may be able to enter via a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma in the same subject area and upgrade to the Master’s after successful completion of the shorter course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Studio Art
description: The Master of Studio Art at the University of Sydney is now offered through the Master of Fine Arts by research, delivered by Sydney College of the Arts as a supervised independent program of written work and studio research. Students develop their art practice through advanced research in one or more discipline areas. It suits visual arts graduates who want to elevate their practice through research-driven exploration. Graduates work as practising artists and pursue further research. Indicative international tuition is around 40,500 Australian dollars per year.

name: Master of Sustainability
description:
The Master of Sustainability at the University of Sydney builds expertise in conservation, population health, food security, sustainability policy and analysis tools through coursework and an industry placement, addressing complex global sustainability challenges. Core units build foundational sustainability knowledge, finishing with a capstone research project and electives chosen to suit the student's career path.
The course suits professionals diversifying into environmental science, finance, law, urban planning, sustainable building design or public health. Graduates help public and private organisations understand and implement sustainable practices across industries.
admission_requirements: For admission to this course, you should have a bachelor's degree or higher from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification. Applicants who do not meet the requirements for admission into the Master of Sustainability may wish to consider applying for entry into the Graduate Diploma in Sustainability or the Graduate Certificate in Sustainability .
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Taxation
description:
The Master of Taxation at the University of Sydney Law School is a specialist qualification in Australian tax law, drawing on the Law School's internationally respected taxation program taught by academics and practitioners recognised as leaders in the field. Students choose elective units matching their interests, with the option to complete an independent research project.
The degree suits Australian and international law graduates from professional firms, industry, the private sector and government who want to build a high level of specialist tax expertise, whether as lawyers, accountants, public administrators or academics.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature for the Master of Taxation requires: a bachelor's degree with a minimum credit average from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or a bachelor's degree from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification and evidence of two years of relevant professional experience.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Teaching
description:
The Master of Teaching (Secondary) at the University of Sydney is a graduate-entry professional qualification to teach one or two secondary school subjects, including English, mathematics, science, HSIE, creative arts or languages, based on an applicant's undergraduate background. Core units in education and curriculum are combined with professional units and specialisation in chosen teaching areas, alongside training in Aboriginal education, diversity and educational technology.
Graduates become accredited teachers in New South Wales and other Australian jurisdictions, qualified to teach across a wide range of secondary school subjects, from biology and business studies to drama and modern history.
admission_requirements: Admission to candidature requires: a bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification; and completion of the teaching area specialisation requirements specified by the Faculty; and completion of any additional qualifying courses prescribed by the Faculty. Applicants who are one unit of study (equivalent to one quarter of a semester of full-time study or 0.125 EFTSL) short of meeting the prerequisites for admission to the Master of Teaching (Secondary) may be given special permission to study the deficient unit in another faculty or institution during their first semester while undertaking their Master of Teaching.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (writing 6.0); PTE Academic 64. The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
description:
The Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages at the University of Sydney builds advanced expertise in English language education across diverse age groups and learning contexts, using the latest research and pedagogy. Core and selective units cover second language acquisition, effective teaching methodology and the cultural dimensions of language learning, finishing with a capstone special project or research dissertation.
The course suits current or aspiring English language teachers of children, adolescents or adults. Graduates move into roles including English language teacher, academic language adviser, curriculum developer and instructional designer.
admission_requirements: A successful applicant for admission to the Master of Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages will: hold a bachelor degree or higher in a cognate discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification and professional experience equivalent to one year full-time in English language teaching; or a bachelor honours degree or postgraduate qualification in a non-cognate discipline from the University of Sydney or equivalent qualification and professional experience equivalent to one year full-time in English language teaching.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Transport
description:
The Master of Transport at the University of Sydney is Australia's first interdisciplinary degree covering the engineering, urban planning and business management of transport. Students complete core units from the transport discipline, electives, and a capstone project, developing skills to analyse and design transport systems and the interdisciplinary judgement to work across engineering, planning and policy.
The course draws on the University's Institute of Transport and Logistics and its transport engineering research strengths. Graduates move into roles such as transport and infrastructure consultant, global fleet manager, transport engineer and urban and regional planner.
admission_requirements: To be eligible for admission, an applicant is required to have: an Australian bachelor's degree or higher qualification, with a credit average (65 percent) in a cognate discipline, or an equivalent qualification or an Australian bachelor's degree or higher qualification, with a credit average (65 percent) in a non-cognate discipline, and three years of relevant work experience
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Urban and Regional Planning
description:
The Master of Urban and Regional Planning at the University of Sydney is accredited by the Planning Institute of Australia and develops an understanding of how cities and sites are constructed physically, socially and environmentally. Core units build communication, reasoning and analytical skills for the policy, technical and regulatory aspects of planning, finishing with a capstone planning report or research dissertation.
The course suits graduates with a background in human geography, design or a related field, or graduates of Sydney's Bachelor of Architecture and Environments, as well as working planners extending their skills. Graduates work in the public, private and not-for-profit sectors guiding urban and regional change.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Urban and Regional Planning requires: a bachelor's degree in design, human geography or related field from the University of Sydney or an equivalent qualification with a credit average mark across all units; or completion of the requirements of the embedded graduate diploma with an average mark of at least 70.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Urban Design
description:
The Master of Urban Design at the University of Sydney develops leadership and expertise in urban design and urbanism with a strong emphasis on sustainability, quantification and implementation. Core foundational units in urban design practice, theory and spatial analysis are paired with electives from the Sydney School of Architecture, Design and Planning focused on urban form and design thinking.
The course suits professionals and graduates in architecture, landscape architecture or urban planning extending their expertise. Graduates are sought after by consulting firms, developers, and local and state governments to prepare and evaluate urban design policies, strategies and master plans.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Urban Design requires: an undergraduate degree in architecture, landscape architecture, urban planning, town planning, urbanism, geography or a related field; or completion of the requirements of the embedded Graduate Certificate with an average mark of at least 65. Based on the applicant's undergraduate performance, the Program Director reserves the right to require a portfolio of work indicating relevant design interests and capabilities for admission to the Master of Urban Design. A portfolio should only be provided if requested by the Program Director.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Urbanism
description:
The Master of Urbanism at the University of Sydney introduces contemporary planning theories and debates while building expertise in urban design, planning and policy, bridging the concerns of architecture and planning. An integrative core covers the factors shaping the planning, policy-making and urbanisation of future cities, with an Urban Design stream offering the program's core urban design studio unit and electives to deepen or broaden study.
Graduates become highly sought-after professionals across development, policymaking and design of the built environment, able to think strategically, appreciate scale and place, and communicate urban design principles to varied audiences.
admission_requirements: Admission to the Master of Urbanism requires: a bachelor's degree in design, human geography or related field from the University of Sydney, or an equivalent qualification; or completion of an approved graduate Diploma course.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); TOEFL iBT 85; PTE Academic 64 (minimum 60 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Veterinary Clinical Studies
description:
The Master of Veterinary Clinical Studies at the University of Sydney, open to domestic students, is a combined coursework and research degree giving veterinarians practical advanced clinical training in disciplines including small animal medicine and surgery, avian health, equine medicine, and veterinary anaesthesia and diagnostic imaging. Candidates typically hold a Bachelor of Veterinary Science or Doctor of Veterinary Medicine and want to enhance their clinical skills or pursue specialist status.
The Sydney School of Veterinary Science delivers the program alongside impactful veterinary research with global significance. Graduates move into specialist veterinary practice across their chosen clinical discipline.
admission_requirements: Admission requirement To be eligible for admission to the Master of Clinical Veterinary Science, you must have completed the equivalent of a Bachelor of Veterinary Science, or Doctor of Veterinary Medicine. Additional application requirements You will be required to upload all the following documents when you submit your application: certified academic transcripts for all your previous tertiary study, if they were not completed at the University of Sydney CV, providing a summary of your work experience two academic reference reports cover letter outlining your reasons for applying research proposal evidence that your supervisor supports your application. This can be PDF copies of emails between you and your supervisor proof of your Australian residency status (a certified copy of the main page your Australian passport, or a certified copy of the main page(s) of your own passport with evidence of your permanent resident visa) English language qualifications (if your prior study was completed at an institution where English is not the medium of instruction).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: Master of Veterinary Studies
description:
The Master of Veterinary Studies at the University of Sydney is the coursework component of a combined clinical residency program taken alongside the Master of Veterinary Clinical Studies, open only to veterinarians offered a place in one of the University's designated clinical streams. Candidates complete 48 credit points of supervised elective units in a chosen stream, from small animal medicine and surgery to equine sports medicine, avian health and veterinary oncology.
The program gives working veterinarians practical, advanced clinical training toward specialist status. Sydney's veterinary science program is ranked first in Australia and among a small number of schools outside North America accredited by the American Veterinary Medical Association.
admission_requirements: Available places will be offered to qualified applicants based on academic merit and relevant professional experience, according to the following admissions criteria: A Bachelor of Veterinary Science with Honours or equivalent, such as a masters degree which is recognised by the NSW Veterinary Practitioners Board (relevant professional experience in the relevant stream is desirable). Full registration, or Registration with conditions, or Limited Registration with the NSW Veterinary Practitioners Board for the entire duration of the candidature. Admission to candidature will be conditional upon the appointment of an appropriate clinical supervisor and associate supervisor. Merit factors and professional experience required include: Grade point average (GPA) or Weighted Average Mean Average (WAM) of veterinary degree (essential). Honours mark or equivalent (essential). Membership of Australian and New Zealand College of Veterinary Scientists is equivalent to Hons I. ‘Accepted’ or published papers in Web of Knowledge listed journals or respected open access on-line journals (not essential, but desirable). Presentations/abstracts at national and international veterinary conferences (not essential, but desirable). Other esteem factors e.g. awards, veterinary positions held since graduation (not essential, but desirable). A minimum experience of a one year rotating internship or equivalent practice experience (essential). Two referees’ reports (essential). Applications will be ranked (in the same manner as for all USYD applicants applying for Australian Postgraduate Awards) within each of the disciplines seeking residents at that time. The highest ranked applicants within each of the disciplines seeking residents at that time, will be requested to attend an interview with the Faculty Academics that oversee this program. Final selection will be made after the interview.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 7.0 (minimum 6.5 in each band); TOEFL iBT 96; PTE Academic 72 (minimum 64 in each band). The University of Sydney also accepts its Sydney International College and USYD College pathway programs.

name: University of Sydney Foundation Program - Standard Course
discontinued_note: The University of Sydney Foundation Program is delivered through Sydney's pathway partners rather than the main course finder; see sydney.edu.au/study/pathways-and-foundation-studies for current entry into this pathway.

name: University of Sydney Foundation Program - Standard Intensive
discontinued_note: The University of Sydney Foundation Program is delivered through Sydney's pathway partners rather than the main course finder; see sydney.edu.au/study/pathways-and-foundation-studies for current entry into this pathway.

name: Advanced Diploma of Applied Science (Nautical Science)
description: The Advanced Diploma of Applied Science (Nautical Science) at the University of Tasmania, delivered through the Australian Maritime College in Launceston, is for students planning a career at sea as navigating (Deck) Officers and Masters on commercial vessels. It provides the knowledge and skills to safely manage and operate vessels, covering navigation and vessel handling, cargo and passenger transport, vessel management, marine legislation and shipboard safety. The program integrates classroom study with sea time, and takes a minimum of 3.5 years to complete.

name: Associate Degree in Arts
description: The Associate Degree in Arts at the University of Tasmania gives students the opportunity to interpret human culture and behaviour from different perspectives and periods, to explore contemporary questions about society, and to engage with creativity, performance and innovation. The course is designed to be flexible: it can serve as the first two years of a Bachelor of Arts, or as a standalone qualification. It takes a minimum of two years full-time and is available at the Hobart, Launceston and Cradle Coast campuses.

name: Associate Degree in Global Logistics and Maritime Management
description: The Associate Degree in Global Logistics and Maritime Management at the University of Tasmania, offered through the Australian Maritime College, lays the groundwork for problem-solving in logistics and maritime operations. Students gain essential knowledge in logistics, business management and shipping to work within the specialised industries of global trade. The course can be studied part-time by distance and takes a minimum of two years full-time, based in Launceston or online. It provides a pathway into the Bachelor of Global Logistics and Maritime Management.

name: Associate Degree in Music
description: The Associate Degree in Music at the University of Tasmania is a two-year full-time qualification (up to five years part-time) grounded in the School of Creative Arts and Media. Based in Hobart, students use the recording, rehearsal and performance spaces at the Hedberg and join a learning community that values and explores diverse forms of music. The degree is closely aligned with the Bachelor of Music and can serve as a pathway into that degree or as a standalone qualification.

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Science
description: The Bachelor of Agricultural Science at the University of Tasmania prepares students to address the complex challenges facing modern agriculture through science, innovation and evidence-based decision making. Drawing on the biological and physical sciences, students develop the knowledge and skills to understand how agricultural systems function and how they can be improved to support productive, sustainable and resilient food production. The degree takes a minimum of three years full-time and is based in Hobart, with strong links to Tasmania's agricultural industries.

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Science with Honours
Bachelor of Agriculture (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Agriculture with Honours at the University of Tasmania is a one-year (full-time) to three-year program for high-achieving students ready to deepen their expertise through research. Honours combines advanced study with a significant research project in the student's chosen agricultural field, developing specialised analytical skills that boost employability or provide a pathway to a PhD. It is available at the Hobart, Launceston and Cradle Coast campuses and builds on an undergraduate agriculture or agricultural science degree.

name: Bachelor of Agriculture and Agribusiness
description: The Bachelor of Agriculture and Agribusiness at the University of Tasmania prepares students to address the challenges and opportunities facing modern agriculture, food production and agribusiness management. Combining agricultural science with business, innovation and food systems knowledge, students develop the skills to understand the complete agricultural value chain, from on-farm production through to processing, marketing and consumers. The degree takes a minimum of three years full-time and is based in Launceston, with strong connections to Tasmania's farming and food sectors.

name: Bachelor of Applied Science (Marine Engineering)
description: The Bachelor of Applied Science (Marine Engineering) at the University of Tasmania, delivered through the Australian Maritime College, prepares students for a career as a Marine Engineering Officer. It combines engineering knowledge with practical maritime training for work on commercial vessels, covering how to operate, maintain and manage the complex engineering systems that keep ships running safely and efficiently, including marine engineering systems and ship operations. The degree takes a minimum of four years full-time and is based in Launceston, with online study options.

name: Bachelor of Architecture & Built Environments
description: The Bachelor of Architecture and Built Environments at the University of Tasmania develops ideas and forms that enrich experience and imagination with reference to environmental, social and economic realities. The course fosters innovation in design, addressing contemporary environmental and social challenges through hands-on learning with a focus on community impact and creative freedom.
