The Bachelor of Behavioural Science (Psychology) is UniSC's standard three-year accredited pathway into professional psychology, structured so graduates who want to keep going can move directly into the one-year Honours program, which is separately APAC-accredited and required for anyone continuing toward registration as a psychologist. The Honours year is genuinely research-heavy: students complete a dissertation (PSY408A/B) alongside advanced coursework in statistics, ethics, and the legislative framework governing psychological practice in Australia, rather than honours being a token add-on year.

UniSC also runs a combined Behavioural Science (Psychology) / Counselling degree for students who want dual accreditation pathways (APAC alongside the Australian Counselling Association and PACFA), which is a slightly unusual offering. Most universities keep counselling and psychology as fully separate degrees rather than building a combined pathway.

The standard bachelor's on its own doesn't lead to registration; it's the first stage of a longer pathway (Honours, then postgraduate training or supervised practice) that mirrors the national psychology registration requirements everywhere in Australia, so students need to plan the full sequence rather than assuming the bachelor's alone gets them into practice.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time (Bachelor), plus 1 year Honours (APAC-accredited)
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods, Biological Bases of Behaviour, Social Psychology
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Statistics for Psychology
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Personality Theory, advanced electives, research preparation
Honours (optional 4th year): PSY400 Research Methods and Analysis, PSY401 Advanced Theoretical Issues, PSY402 Professional Practice of Psychology, PSY403 Ethical and Professional Issues, PSY408A/B Research Dissertation
Combined pathway available: Bachelor of Behavioural Science (Psychology) / Bachelor of Counselling (dual APAC/ACA/PACFA accreditation)
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business at UniSC is a fairly standard generalist business degree in structure (foundation year, then a major, then advanced electives and a work-integrated learning component), but it's worth knowing in context of where UniSC sits: a regional Queensland university whose graduate outcomes lean heavily on Sunshine Coast and Brisbane employers rather than the big multinational graduate programs that Group of Eight business schools feed into more directly.

Majors typically include accounting, marketing, management, tourism and event management (reflecting the region's genuine tourism economy), and human resource management. The tourism and event management option in particular draws on UniSC's location. The Sunshine Coast is a real tourism and hospitality economy, not just a marketing backdrop, and placement partners for that major include local tourism boards and event companies rather than purely hypothetical case studies.

Accounting students need to check their specific subject selection against CPA Australia or Chartered Accountants ANZ requirements if they want the degree to satisfy those professional accreditation pathways directly, since not every accounting-adjacent subject in the course automatically counts.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Accounting Principles, Economics for Business, Marketing Fundamentals, Management, Business Statistics
Year 2: Major subjects begin (Accounting / Marketing / Management / Tourism and Event Management / Human Resource Management), Business Law
Year 3: Advanced major electives, Work-Integrated Learning placement or industry project, capstone strategy course
Majors (choose one): Accounting, Marketing, Management, Tourism and Event Management, Human Resource Management
CPA/CAANZ accreditation pathway available depending on major and subject selection
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Communication
description:
UniSC's Bachelor of Communication runs students through the standard media, journalism, and public relations foundations before letting them specialise, and the degree leans on the university's growing profile in regional and digital media rather than pretending to compete head-on with the big-masthead placement networks that Sydney or Melbourne journalism schools can offer. Students get exposure to regional broadcasters, local papers, and the Sunshine Coast's expanding digital content and marketing sector, which is a genuinely different professional network than what a capital-city program would provide.

The course covers writing, media law and ethics, and digital content production, with students able to lean toward journalism, public relations, or social media and digital communication depending on their career direction. A work-integrated learning placement in the final year is standard, and UniSC has been building out its digital media production facilities on campus in recent years as student demand shifts away from traditional broadcast toward content creation and social platforms.

Graduates typically move into roles in regional media, corporate communications, digital marketing agencies, or government and not-for-profit communications teams.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Introduction to Communication and Media, Writing for Media, Media Law and Ethics, Digital Media Production
Year 2: stream selection (Journalism / Public Relations / Digital and Social Media), Media Research Methods, Content Strategy
Year 3: Advanced stream subjects, Work-Integrated Learning placement, capstone communication project or portfolio
Streams: Journalism, Public Relations, Digital and Social Media
Capstone: industry placement-linked portfolio or campaign project
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Justice
description:
Criminology and Justice at UniSC covers the expected sociological and legal foundations of the field (theories of crime, criminal justice systems, victimology), but the program has a practical bent toward the actual justice sector employers in Queensland: police, corrections, youth justice, and community services organisations. Students typically complete a work-integrated learning placement in their final year with one of these agencies rather than finishing the degree on coursework alone.

The Sunshine Coast region's demographic mix (a growing population, a significant retiree community, and pockets of real socioeconomic disadvantage inland from the coast) gives the program's community and justice case studies a genuinely local texture rather than pulling every example from interstate or overseas.

Graduates commonly move into policy or operational roles in corrections, youth justice, victim support services, or further study toward psychology, social work or law, and the degree is often taken as one half of a combined degree (paired with criminology and psychology, or with justice and legal studies) for students who know early they want a specific combination of skills.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Introduction to Criminology, Australian Legal System, Sociology of Crime, Research Methods
Year 2: Criminal Justice Systems, Victimology, Youth Justice, Policing and Society
Year 3: Corrections and Community Justice, Work-Integrated Learning placement (justice sector agency), capstone research project, electives
Elective areas: Family Violence, Cybercrime, Restorative Justice
No separate thesis; capstone is placement-linked applied project
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
UniSC's Bachelor of Education (Primary) requires 80 days of supervised professional experience delivered as four full-time placement blocks, plus 40 hours of separate wider field experience, a structure that front-loads real classroom time earlier and more heavily than some equivalent degrees. Students need a Blue Card before their first placement, with applications needing to go in a full twelve weeks ahead of the block start, which is a scheduling constraint that shapes first-year enrolment planning more than students often expect going in.

From second year, students choose between an English or STEM specialisation, a fork that reflects the two national curriculum priority areas primary schools have been under the most pressure to strengthen over the past several years, particularly STEM given well-documented national concerns about numeracy outcomes.

The degree leads to provisional registration with the Queensland College of Teachers on graduation (subject to standard requirements), and UniSC's placement network draws heavily on Sunshine Coast and wider regional Queensland schools, giving graduates a practical head start on employment in regional and rural postings that some metropolitan-based teaching degrees don't emphasise as strongly.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time
Year 1: Foundations of Teaching, Child Development, Literacy Foundations, Numeracy Foundations, first professional experience block
Year 2: specialisation choice (English or STEM), Curriculum and Pedagogy, Inclusive Education, ongoing professional experience blocks
Year 3: Advanced specialisation subjects, Classroom Management, Assessment and Reporting, professional experience block
Year 4: Capstone professional experience block (extended), Professional Practice seminar, graduate readiness subjects
Total: 80 days Supervised Professional Experience (4 full-time blocks) + 40 hours Wider Field Experience
Requirement: Blue Card required before first placement, application 12 weeks in advance
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent, Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) - Civil Engineering
description:
UniSC's Civil Engineering (Honours) degree is accredited at Professional Engineer level by Engineers Australia and structured around 384 total units across four years, with the honours classification calculated from the mean mark across the 96 units of AQF8-level (400-coded) courses in the final stage of the degree, a fairly transparent way of determining honours class compared to some universities' more opaque weighting systems.

Core subjects run through the full range of civil engineering practice: structural design, road and traffic engineering, concrete design and technology, water and wastewater systems, and environmental engineering, with two dedicated engineering project courses providing the capstone research and design component. Students must also complete a minimum of 60 days of approved industry work experience, which UniSC treats as a hard requirement rather than an optional add-on.

The Sunshine Coast's rapid regional growth (new housing estates, transport corridors, and coastal infrastructure under constant development) gives students a genuinely active local pipeline of real projects and employer placements, rather than relying purely on textbook case studies from elsewhere in the country.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time, 384 total units
Year 1: Engineering Fundamentals, Mathematics for Engineers, Physics for Engineers, Introduction to Civil Engineering
Year 2: Structural Design, Water and Wastewater Engineering, Engineering Mechanics, Surveying
Year 3: Road and Traffic Engineering, Concrete Design and Technology, Structural Modelling, Environmental Engineering
Year 4 (AQF8, 400-coded, 96 units): Advanced Structural Analysis and Design, Sustainable Transport Systems, Engineering Management, two Engineering Project courses (capstone)
Requirement: minimum 60 days approved industry work experience
Accreditation: Engineers Australia (Professional Engineer level)
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Information and Communications Technology
Bachelor of Laws
description:
UniSC's law degree covers the standard Priestley 11 academic requirements for legal practice admission in Australia, including Contracts, Torts, Property, Constitutional Law, Equity and Trusts, Corporations Law, Evidence, Administrative Law and the rest, but distinguishes itself with two courses that put students in front of real legal problems before graduation. LAW423 Community Legal Practice has students shadowing practising lawyers and assisting with actual client work, and LAW400 Negotiation and Dispute Resolution runs as a simulated clinic where students work in fictional firms resolving hypothetical client disputes.

Because UniSC is a regional university without the long institutional pedigree of the sandstone law schools, the program leans on this practical-exposure angle as its point of difference, along with combined degree options (Bachelor of Laws / Bachelor of Business, /Bachelor of Arts, /Bachelor of Environmental Management) that let students pair legal training with another discipline rather than studying law in isolation.

Graduates still need to complete a separate period of practical legal training after finishing the degree before admission as a legal practitioner. The degree itself satisfies the academic component only, consistent with how legal admission works across Australia.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time (or as a combined degree, e.g. with Business, Arts, or Environmental Management)
Core courses: Foundations of Australian Law, Criminal Law and Procedure, Torts, Contracts, Property, Constitutional Law, Equity and Trusts, Corporations Law, Civil Procedure, Evidence, Administrative Law, Professional Conduct
Practical courses: LAW423 Community Legal Practice (WIL placement shadowing practitioners), LAW400 Negotiation and Dispute Resolution (simulated clinic)
Electives: Commercial Law, Children and the Law, Intellectual Property, Employment Law, Family Law
Post-graduation requirement: separate practical legal training period before admission as a legal practitioner
admission_requirements: ATAR 70 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Nursing Science
description:
UniSC's nursing degree requires a minimum of 800 clinical placement hours for NMBA registration eligibility, delivered in consecutive-week blocks that students find out about roughly ten weeks ahead of time, a scheduling rhythm that shapes how students plan work and life around the degree more than most other bachelor programs would. Placements begin in first year and run across hospital, aged care, community and primary health settings, with a Clinical Placement Office handling allocation separately from the academic teaching team.

The teaching model blends clinical simulation labs and virtual reality environments with the placement hours themselves, and electronic medical records training is built in from early in the course rather than left for graduates to pick up on the job. UniSC's health teaching facilities on the Sunshine Coast campus are relatively new, built with simulation wards designed to mimic hospital layouts rather than generic classroom space.

A graduate-entry pathway exists for students who already hold a related degree, compressing the timeline, and the standard degree can also lead into an honours year for students interested in nursing research rather than moving straight into clinical practice after graduation.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time (graduate-entry pathway available for eligible students)
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, first clinical simulation and placement block
Year 2: Adult Health Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, Child and Family Health, ongoing block placements
Year 3: Complex and Critical Care Nursing, Aged Care Nursing, Community and Primary Health, Transition to Practice, final placement block
Total clinical placement: minimum 800 hours across hospital, aged care, community and primary health settings
Optional: Honours year (research-focused) available after completion of the standard degree
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) with an ATAR of approximately 65 or QTAC selection rank; competitive selection with National Police Check and vaccination/immunisation requirements for clinical placements
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with no band below 7.0, or equivalent (required for AHPRA registration as a nurse)

name: Bachelor of Nursing Science: Graduate Entry
Bachelor of Recreation and Outdoor Environmental Studies
Bachelor of Science
description:
UniSC's Bachelor of Science is a flexible, major-based science degree rather than a narrowly specified single-discipline qualification, letting students choose from majors spanning environmental science, biology, chemistry, marine science, and similar fields depending on the year's offering. Given the campus's location, the environmental and marine science options draw genuine advantage from proximity: the Sunshine Coast sits between coastal reef and estuary systems and the Great Sandy biosphere region, and UniSC's own research strengths (the university has notable output in coastal ecology and marine science) filter down into undergraduate field trips and lab work in a way a landlocked science faculty couldn't replicate.

First year is common core across majors (general biology, chemistry, and quantitative methods) before students specialise from second year, with an increasing share of major electives and a capstone research or field project in the final year.

Graduates typically move into environmental consultancy, laboratory and research assistant roles, government environmental agencies, or further postgraduate study, with the university's regional environmental science reputation being a genuine drawcard for that particular major relative to some metropolitan competitors.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: General Biology, Chemistry Fundamentals, Quantitative Methods for Science, Earth and Environmental Systems
Year 2: Major selection (Environmental Science / Biology / Chemistry / Marine Science), major core subjects, Research Methods in Science
Year 3: Advanced major electives, field-based subjects (marine or environmental fieldwork depending on major), capstone research project
Majors (choose one): Environmental Science, Biology, Chemistry, Marine Science
Capstone: independent research or field project supervised by faculty
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science
description:
The Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Science at UniSC is accredited at Exercise Science level with Exercise and Sports Science Australia, meaning graduates can call themselves accredited exercise scientists on completion rather than needing further study to use that title. It sits on the Sunshine Coast campus, which gives the program unusually direct access to elite outdoor training environments. The region's surf, running and triathlon culture feeds into applied placements that a landlocked campus couldn't replicate as easily.

The degree requires a minimum of 270 supervised professional practice hours, with 140 of those specifically counting toward ESSA membership requirements, so the practical component isn't an afterthought tacked onto lecture-heavy science subjects. Students are out doing supervised assessment and program design work well before final year.

Course subjects like Exercise Prescription and Programming and Introduction to Coaching Science sit alongside the expected anatomy and physiology base, and UniSC also offers pathway degrees (Clinical Exercise Physiology, Clinical Exercise Science) for students who decide partway through that they want the higher clinical accreditation rather than stopping at exercise science.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: HLT140 Think Health, LFS112 Human Physiology, LFS122 Human Anatomy, SCI110 Science Research Methods, SPX100 Physical Activity and Health, SPX101 Introduction to Sport and Exercise Science
Year 2: SPX102 Introduction to Coaching Science, SPX121 Exercise Prescription and Programming I, Biomechanics, Nutrition for Performance
Year 3: Exercise Prescription and Programming II, Sport Psychology, supervised professional practice placements (minimum 270 hours total, 140 hours toward ESSA)
Accreditation: Exercise and Sports Science Australia (Exercise Science level)
No separate thesis; assessment via essays, reports, seminar presentations and supervised practice
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent) with an ATAR of approximately 60 or QTAC selection rank; Mathematics and a science subject recommended but not required
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 overall, no band below 6.0, or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Urban Design and Town Planning (Honours)
Master of Business Administration
description:
UniSC's MBA is a smaller, regionally-rooted program compared to the metropolitan MBA heavyweights, and it markets that directly: smaller cohorts, closer contact with teaching staff, and case material drawn from Queensland regional business as much as from ASX-listed multinationals. It suits students already working, often in management roles in regional businesses, government, health, or education sectors along the Sunshine Coast and wider South East Queensland corridor, rather than assuming a purely career-break, full-time cohort.

The course covers the expected core spine of strategy, finance, marketing and leadership, with a capstone project that's typically applied to the student's own organisation or a local industry partner rather than a purely theoretical case competition, reflecting the practical, work-integrated bent that runs through most of UniSC's postgraduate business offerings.

Delivery is flexible, with online and block-intensive options available for the substantial share of students studying part-time while working, and the program doesn't assume a finance or consulting background walking in the door the way some more competitive-entry MBAs do.
curriculum:
Duration: 1.5–2 years part-time (or accelerated full-time option)
Core subjects: Strategic Management, Financial Management, Marketing Management, Leading and Managing People, Business Analytics
Elective block: choose from Innovation and Entrepreneurship, Project Management, Health Management, or Public Sector Management streams
Capstone: applied strategy or consulting project, often based in student's own organisation or a regional industry partner
Delivery: online and block-intensive options for part-time students
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus relevant work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Business Intelligence and Analytics
Master of Civil Engineering
description: The University of the Sunshine Coast Master of Civil Engineering can be completed in 12 months across eight courses, combining online learning with on-campus intensive sessions. It suits recent civil engineering graduates and practising engineers who want to deepen their technical expertise or refresh their qualifications while continuing to work. Entry requires a completed four-year bachelor degree in civil engineering or a relevant discipline, or equivalent; work experience is not required and there is no application fee. The degree is seeking provisional accreditation from Engineers Australia. Indicative international tuition is around A$38,500 per year. Graduates apply advanced civil engineering knowledge to the planning, design, construction and maintenance of infrastructure such as buildings, bridges, roads and water systems.

name: Master of Climate Change Adaptation by Research
Master of Cyber Security and Forensics
Master of Information and Communications Technology
description:
UniSC's Master of ICT is built for people entering tech from somewhere else, and the program is upfront about it: 14 courses covering cybersecurity, data analytics, programming, and AI, deliverable in 14 months if a student pushes through fast or closer to two years at a normal pace. It runs across the Sunshine Coast, Adelaide, and online campuses simultaneously, which is a bit unusual for a postgrad ICT degree and reflects UniSC's broader push into flexible, multi-campus delivery over the last several years as it's grown from a regional university into a larger multi-state one.

The course is professionally accredited by the Australian Computer Society, and UniSC embeds vendor certifications directly into coursework rather than treating them as optional add-ons: Microsoft Security, Compliance and Identity Fundamentals shows up as a named credential students pick up along the way, which matters to employers scanning a resume for something concrete.

Students without an IT background start with foundational programming and systems courses before moving into the data-and-security-heavy back half of the degree, and the specialisation option lets students lean further into data management and analysis if that's the direction they're aiming for.
curriculum:
Duration: 14 months–2 years, 14 courses total
Foundation courses (non-IT background entrants): Programming Fundamentals, IT Systems and Infrastructure
Core courses: Data Analytics, Cybersecurity Fundamentals, Software Development, Research Methods for ICT
Specialisation option: Information and Communications Technology Specialisation (data management and analysis focus)
Embedded certifications: Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals and other vendor credentials
Capstone: applied ICT project or research course in final term
ACS professional accreditation
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant or any discipline (typical Australian postgrad IT/CS entry bar used as approximate default, not program-specific verified).
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (typical postgrad bar used as approximate default, not program-verified).

name: Master of Regional Planning by Research
Master of Robotics and Automation Engineering
Master of Social Work by Research
Master of Sport and Exercise Science by Research
Master of Sports Nutrition by Research
Bachelor of Advanced Computer Science (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Advanced Computer Science (Honours) at the University of Western Australia covers areas from mobile data and cloud computing to artificial intelligence and advanced software development, giving students the tools and techniques to embrace technological challenges and devise innovative solutions. Students can specialise in Artificial Intelligence, International Cybersecurity, Computing and Data Science, or Quantum Computing, gaining practical skills, knowledge and connections. Graduates forge careers developing new technologies and advanced programming to overcome challenges in business, science and society.

name: Bachelor of Agribusiness
description: The Bachelor of Agribusiness at the University of Western Australia prepares students for employment in areas related to agriculture, including finance, marketing, policy formation, business management and rural development. Students learn the business and economics skills needed to assume managerial and leadership roles, taking 12 core units with the opportunity to take electives to pursue their interests. Graduates work in agribusiness management, agricultural finance and marketing, policy and rural development roles.

name: Bachelor of Agricultural Science
description: The Bachelor of Agricultural Science at the University of Western Australia prepares students for the agricultural systems of the future, integrating the rapidly developing field of agricultural technology with key agricultural science subjects. Students develop skills in digital agriculture, agricultural economics, soil science, and crop and livestock production, learning to integrate agricultural systems with new digital technologies for improved farm efficiency and productivity. Graduates work in agronomy, agribusiness, research, consulting and government roles across the agricultural sector.

name: Bachelor of Art History and Curatorial Studies
description: The Bachelor of Art History and Curatorial Studies at the University of Western Australia blends knowledge of art history with practical curatorial skills, cultivating transferable skills in visual and spatial analysis, critical thought, and oral and written communication. The major combines art historical knowledge with curatorial methods, and offers opportunities for foreign study, industry placements and object-based learning, activating art history through hands-on engagement with exhibitions and curatorial practice. Graduates work in arts management, museum and gallery curation, art criticism and analysis, and across the wider cultural sector.

name: Bachelor of Art History and Curatorial Studies (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Art History and Curatorial Studies (Honours) at the University of Western Australia blends art historical knowledge with practical curatorial skills, giving students the opportunity to work in arts management, museum and gallery curation, and art criticism and analysis. The degree offers opportunities for foreign study, industry placements and object-based learning, activating art history through hands-on experience and engagement with exhibitions and curatorial practice. The honours year adds an independent research project. Graduates work in galleries, museums, auction houses, arts organisations and as writers and critics, and are prepared for research higher degree study.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
UWA's Bachelor of Arts is a broad-based humanities and social sciences degree with majors spanning history, literature, politics, anthropology, linguistics, Asian studies and more, built on UWA's New Courses curriculum structure that lets students combine a major with a genuinely broad set of electives rather than locking into a narrow single-discipline pathway from first year, the way older-style Australian arts degrees used to.

Being based in Perth, the degree has some specific regional strengths worth naming directly. Asian studies and Indian Ocean-focused international relations content benefit from Perth's geographic position closer to Southeast Asia than any other Australian capital, and Indigenous studies units draw on UWA's location on Noongar country and long-running partnerships with WA Aboriginal communities.

Graduates go into a wide range of fields, including media, public policy, government, education pathways via further study, and the arts and cultural sector, with the degree's broad structure making it a common double-degree partner alongside commerce, law or science at UWA rather than a purely stand-alone qualification.
curriculum:
Year 1: broad elective units across humanities and social sciences, introductory major unit(s), academic writing and research skills unit
Year 2: major units (chosen from history, politics, literature, anthropology, Asian studies, linguistics and others), second major or broadening units
Year 3: advanced major units, capstone research or thesis unit, further electives
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 80+.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Biological Science
description: The Bachelor of Biological Science at the University of Western Australia equips students with skills and knowledge valued by employers around the globe and enables them to understand the vulnerabilities and resilience of life on our planet. Students explore the growth, reproduction, adaptation and evolution of living organisms and discover how species and ecological communities can be managed, conserved and restored. Graduates work in conservation, ecological management, research and environmental roles.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science at the University of Western Australia is a comprehensive undergraduate degree designed to meet growing global demand for graduates with expertise across a range of health science disciplines. Students specialise in one or two of the 10 majors available, or combine a biomedical science major with another from Arts, Commerce or Science, tailoring their studies to their career goals. It is a practical, flexible degree covering subjects from biochemistry to physiology. Graduates work in medical research, laboratory science and health roles, or progress to health professional degrees.

name: Bachelor of Biomedicine (Specialised)
description: The Bachelor of Biomedicine (Specialised) at the University of Western Australia is a practical degree providing learning across a broad arena of health and medical disciplines, designed to articulate with UWA's health professional degrees. Multiple specialisations within the biomedical disciplines enable breadth and depth of learning, including Aboriginal Health, Human Biology, Genetics, Biochemistry, Physiology, Pharmacology, Microbiology and Pathology. Graduates progress to health professional study or to research and laboratory roles.

name: Bachelor of Business
description: The University of Western Australia Bachelor of Business is a three-year degree of 144 points (24 six-point units, normally eight per year). Students major in Business Management, Global Business, or Enterprise and Innovation, covering business reporting, economics, marketing and management principles alongside communication and data-literacy skills, an international business context, or entrepreneurship and innovation. The degree emphasises practical skills and access to real-world industry experience through internships and work-integrated learning, and is noted as well suited to students who want to launch a start-up or small business. Entry requirements, including ATAR thresholds and international equivalents, are set out on the UWA admissions pages, and international students must meet the UWA English requirement of IELTS 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0. International tuition is about A$50,700 per year.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description:
The Bachelor of Commerce is UWA's core business degree, run through the UWA Business School, which holds the AACSB and EQUIS dual accreditation that puts it among a small number of Australian business schools recognised at that level internationally. Majors span accounting, finance, economics, marketing, management and human resources, and students combine a major with a broad-based commerce core before specialising.

Perth's economy gives the degree a distinct regional flavour compared with a Sydney or Melbourne commerce degree: resources sector finance, mining company accounting and corporate roles tied to WA's energy and minerals sector feature more prominently in local graduate outcomes and industry connections than they would at an eastern-states business school, alongside the standard banking, consulting and professional services pathways common to any commerce degree.

Graduates pursue chartered accounting, finance and banking, corporate roles in the resources sector, and general management pathways, with UWA Business School's international accreditation carrying weight for graduates who look toward global rather than purely domestic careers.
curriculum:
Year 1: Economic Principles, Accounting Principles, Business Statistics, Introduction to Management
Year 2: major units begin (Accounting, Finance, Economics, Marketing or Management stream), Business Law, Organisational Behaviour
Year 3: advanced major units, capstone business strategy or applied project unit, optional industry placement
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 85+.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
description: The Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice at the University of Western Australia teaches students about the role criminology plays in understanding crime and how society deals with it, as well as effective criminal justice interventions. Students draw on knowledge and perspectives from criminology, law, psychology, history, anthropology, geography and forensic science, learning about contemporary explanations for crime and criminality, the structure of the criminal justice system, and transnational and international crime. Graduates work in policy, research, corrections, policing and community roles.

name: Bachelor of Design
description:
The Bachelor of Design at UWA is the university's studio-based creative degree, covering streams that typically include architecture-adjacent design, interior architecture, urban and landscape design, and product or visual design depending on current stream offerings, taught through project-based studio work rather than conventional lecture-and-exam assessment for most of its core content.

It functions as UWA's foundation pathway into the Master of Architecture and related postgraduate design qualifications, which is the standard structure in Australia now that architecture is a postgraduate accredited qualification rather than a single undergraduate degree, so most Bachelor of Design students intending to become registered architects treat this as stage one of a longer combined pathway rather than a terminal qualification.

Graduates who don't continue into a design-specific master's move into design-adjacent roles in urban planning, construction and design consultancy, while those continuing typically progress into UWA's Master of Architecture or a related postgraduate design degree to complete their accreditation pathway.
curriculum:
Year 1: Design Studio I, Visual Communication, Design History and Theory, Digital Design Tools
Year 2: Design Studio II (stream specialisation begins), Structures and Materials, Design Studio III
Year 3: advanced Design Studio units, capstone design project, portfolio development for postgraduate progression
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 85+; portfolio not typically required.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Earth Science
description: The Bachelor of Earth Sciences at the University of Western Australia is ideal for students curious about the complex system that comprises the solid Earth, its oceans and atmosphere, and the place of Earth in the solar system and beyond. Earth scientists have a key role in understanding environmental challenges and the sustainability of resources in a changing world, and the degree provides knowledge and skills highly valued by employers. Graduates work in resources, energy, environmental, geoscience and research roles.

name: Bachelor of Economics
description: The University of Western Australia Bachelor of Economics is a concentrated three-year program for students who want to become professional economists. Students major in Economics or Financial Economics, both grounded in micro and macroeconomics and econometrics. The course requires an ATAR of 90 and Mathematics Applications as a prerequisite, with Mathematics Methods recommended; a bridging course is available for students who have not done the prerequisite maths, and alternative entry pathways exist for those who do not meet the standard requirements. Graduates work as specialist economists in government and business, and as economic consultants, analysts and policy advisers, with UWA reporting graduates employed at the Australian and State Treasuries and the Reserve Bank as well as in consultancies and major companies. Students can continue to honours, a specialist Master of Economics, or a PhD. International tuition is about A$54,500 per year.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
UWA's Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) is a four-year accredited degree: engineers here graduate with honours built in as standard, in line with the Washington Accord structure most Australian engineering schools now use rather than treating honours as an optional extra year. Perth's economy leans heavily on resources and energy, and UWA's engineering school reflects that: mining, mechanical, chemical and civil engineering all have direct pipelines into the state's mining and oil and gas sector, alongside newer strength in areas like renewable energy engineering as the WA economy diversifies.

Students choose a specialisation stream after common first-year engineering foundations, and the degree includes mandatory industry-relevant project work and, depending on the stream, placement or work-integrated learning components that connect directly to WA's resources employers, a genuine local advantage given how concentrated mining and energy company headquarters and operations are in Perth compared with the eastern states.

Graduates move into mining, oil and gas, civil infrastructure and increasingly renewable energy roles, with strong graduate starting salaries in the resources-linked specialisations reflecting sustained WA industry demand for locally trained engineers.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Mechanics, Introduction to Engineering Design, Chemistry or Physics foundation
Year 2: specialisation stream begins (Civil, Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Mining or Software Engineering), Thermodynamics or equivalent core unit, Engineering Computation
Year 3: advanced specialisation units, industry-based project or internship, Professional Engineering Practice
Year 4: capstone engineering design project, further advanced electives, honours thesis or major design project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 90+ with prerequisite Mathematics Methods and Physics or Chemistry.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Environmental Design
description: The Bachelor of Environmental Design at the University of Western Australia is a broad study area that involves design and planning in relation to natural and constructed environments. Students choose from degree-specific majors and build a foundation for professional practice and further study in architecture, landscape architecture, urban and regional planning and related fields. Graduates progress to accredited master's degrees or to roles across the design, planning and built-environment sectors.

name: Bachelor of Environmental Science
description: The Bachelor of Environmental Science at the University of Western Australia teaches understanding, rational analysis and improvement of human impacts on the natural world, through critical review of current knowledge, systematic observation, experimentation, modelling and rigorous data analysis. Graduates have strong theoretical knowledge combined with practical and creative skills, equipping them to solve diverse and emerging environmental problems and communicate unbiased information to the wider community. Graduates work in environmental management, consulting, policy and research roles.

name: Bachelor of Geographical and Spatial Science
description: The Bachelor of Geographical and Spatial Science at the University of Western Australia develops fundamental spatial science skills, knowledge and techniques to solve the world's biggest environmental issues. The course has a strong focus on understanding the environmental processes, including climate and hydrology, that interact with landscapes and people and drive economies, along with broader geography principles, demography and regional development. Graduates work in GIS and spatial analysis, environmental management, planning and research roles.

name: Bachelor of Hospitality Management
description: The Bachelor of Hospitality Management at the University of Western Australia builds a foundation in business and hospitality management, combining core areas such as leadership, marketing, economics and global business practices with specialised hospitality studies. This integrated approach ensures students develop both the theoretical understanding and practical capability required in a service-driven industry. Graduates work in management roles across hotels, events, tourism, food and beverage and the wider hospitality sector.

name: Bachelor of Human Rights
description: The Bachelor of Human Rights at the University of Western Australia is a unique, interdisciplinary program that equips students with the knowledge and skills necessary to engage with real-world issues in human rights and related areas such as social justice. Students examine human rights ideas from legal, historical, political, practical and philosophical perspectives, as a complex set of global institutions has evolved around human rights alongside a flourishing field of academic inquiry. Graduates work in advocacy, government, international organisations, law and policy roles.

name: Bachelor of Human Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Human Sciences at the University of Western Australia gives students an interdisciplinary understanding of human function and behaviour, including variation, and how humans adapt to challenging and disruptive change. The degree houses a suite of majors that examine the biology of being human in the contemporary world, with an emphasis on how biology and behaviour are influenced by genetic, developmental, ecological and cultural factors. Students build skills in analytical thinking, critical thinking and complex problem-solving. Graduates work in health, research, policy and analytical roles.

name: Bachelor of Human Sciences (Pharmaceutical Health) and Doctor of Pharmacy
Bachelor of International Relations
description: The Bachelor of International Relations at the University of Western Australia is a professional and practice-oriented program that provides the conceptual knowledge and real-world experience required to tackle pressing global challenges, from pandemics and conflict to supply chain disruptions and climate-related emergencies. Students develop a rigorous understanding of international relations from political, legal, historical and sociological perspectives, with unique training focused on the Indo-Pacific and Indian Ocean regions. Graduates work in diplomacy, government, international organisations, NGOs and research.

name: Bachelor of Marine Science
description: The Bachelor of Marine Science at the University of Western Australia offers the full breadth of the marine science discipline, combining knowledge of marine life with a solid understanding of the physical environment across all levels of biological organisation. Students learn about the complex interactions in marine ecosystems and how to manage these systems in a changing world through lectures, laboratory exercises and field excursions, using UWA's nationally unique facilities. Graduates gain skills valued by employers worldwide and clear pathways into master's study, and work in marine research, conservation and management.

name: Bachelor of Mathematics
description: The Bachelor of Mathematics at the University of Western Australia provides high-achieving students with a solid foundation in the fundamental concepts and theories of mathematics. It covers core subjects like calculus, linear algebra and statistics while exploring advanced topics in complex systems, networks, abstract algebra, analysis, topology, probability theory and numerical methods. Students develop problem-solving skills and analytical reasoning, preparing them for careers as mathematicians, data scientists, statisticians and analysts, filling strong demand for graduates who can apply mathematical techniques to real-world problems.

name: Bachelor of Media and Communication
description: The Bachelor of Media and Communication at the University of Western Australia offers applied learning opportunities and skills for those interested in working directly in media and communication industries. Focused on the core techniques of ideation, engagement and impact, the interdisciplinary program spans media production, journalism, strategic communication and digital storytelling, developing versatile skills in media development and analysis. Graduates are ready to navigate the dynamic digital culture and work across media production, communication, journalism and content roles.

name: Bachelor of Modern Languages
description: The Bachelor of Modern Languages at the University of Western Australia enables students to study two languages in depth, achieving high competency in reading, listening, speaking and writing while acquiring transferable skills such as communication, teamwork and problem-solving. Students choose from Chinese, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean and Spanish, all available to absolute beginners, and combining the degree with fields like engineering, science or business provides a competitive advantage. Graduates work in translation, international business, government, education and diplomacy.

name: Bachelor of Molecular Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Molecular Sciences at the University of Western Australia develops an understanding of life at the molecular level, including the complex functioning of cells, tissues and organisms. Training in current laboratory technologies equips students with the tools to tackle challenges in the biological and health sciences, and the degree serves as an excellent stepping stone into careers in the biosciences. Graduates work in laboratory research, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals and health-related roles.

name: Bachelor of Music
description: The Bachelor of Music at the University of Western Australia allows students to work with professional musicians to develop their skills as emerging artists, with specialisations for composers, performers and musicologists as well as those focused on creative music technology. This highly practical degree means students learn performance by performing, and make industry connections with leading players in Western Australia and internationally, including the West Australian Symphony Orchestra and West Australian Opera. Graduates pursue performance, composition, teaching and music technology careers.

name: Bachelor of Philosophy (Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Philosophy (Honours) is UWA's flagship program for its highest-achieving school leavers, and it isn't a philosophy degree despite the name. "Bachelor of Philosophy" here is used in the older, broader sense (as in Oxford's PPE-adjacent BPhil tradition) rather than referring to the discipline. Students design an individualised, interdisciplinary program across UWA's schools, take small specialist seminars capped well below normal first-year lecture sizes, and complete an honours-level research project earlier than students in a standard single-discipline degree would.

Entry is competitive and typically requires an ATAR near the top of the state's distribution, and the program functions as UWA's answer to the flagship honours colleges that several other Group of Eight universities run: a way of keeping high-achieving students who might otherwise look interstate or overseas, by offering genuine academic flexibility and research exposure from first year rather than making them wait until an honours year bolted onto the end of a conventional degree.

Graduates typically go on to competitive postgraduate study, research careers, or professional pathways in law, medicine or policy, carrying an honours-level research thesis completed years earlier than most of their undergraduate peers.
curriculum:
Year 1: foundation seminars across chosen disciplines, research skills and academic writing intensive, individualised program design in consultation with academic mentors
Year 2: advanced disciplinary units, interdisciplinary seminar series, preliminary research proposal
Year 3: specialised units in the student's chosen area(s), continued interdisciplinary coursework, honours thesis research and writing, final oral presentation
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of 98+ typically required, plus a supplementary application and interview.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Philosophy, Politics and Economics
Bachelor of Psychology
description: The University of Western Australia Bachelor of Psychology is a three-year degree of 144 points (24 six-point units, normally eight per year) built around a 14-unit extended major in psychology. The degree is accredited at Level 1 by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC), and an APAC-accredited honours year serves as the fourth year of psychology needed to progress toward registration. Students satisfy any prerequisites for their chosen majors, and combined degrees pairing psychology with arts, commerce or science are also available. A psychology degree prepares graduates for a wide range of work, from personnel selection and market research to human-computer interface design, and for postgraduate professional training in industrial and organisational psychology, business psychology, clinical psychology and clinical neuropsychology. International tuition is about A$53,300 per year.

name: Bachelor of Science (Agriculture)
description:
The Bachelor of Science (Agriculture) sits inside a state where agriculture is a genuinely dominant export sector (Western Australia produces roughly half the nation's wheat), and UWA's agriculture program leans directly into that regional weight, covering plant and animal production, soil science, agricultural economics and increasingly agtech and precision agriculture content, with field-based practical components that draw on WA's actual grain, livestock and horticultural industries rather than generic textbook agriculture.

The degree is taught with strong links to WA's Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development and to grower groups and agribusiness employers across the Wheatbelt and southwest, giving students industry contact that a purely metropolitan science degree elsewhere in the country typically can't offer at the same scale.

Graduates move into agronomy, agribusiness management, agricultural research and government agricultural policy roles, with strong local graduate demand given the size and continued growth of WA's grains, livestock and horticultural export sectors.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Agricultural Science, Soil Science, Plant Biology, Chemistry foundation
Year 2: Crop and Pasture Production, Animal Production Systems, Agricultural Economics, Field Practicum
Year 3: Precision Agriculture and Agtech, Agribusiness Management, capstone research or industry placement project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 75-80.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Science (Marine Science)
description:
The Bachelor of Science (Marine Science) at UWA benefits from an unusually good stretch of coastline right on its doorstep: Perth sits between the temperate Indian Ocean reefs of Rottnest and the Ningaloo Reef further north, one of the largest fringing coral reefs in the world and considerably less studied and less crowded than the Great Barrier Reef, which gives UWA marine science students field research opportunities in relatively pristine reef systems that eastern-states marine science programs simply don't have local access to.

The course combines core marine biology and oceanography with UWA's own strengths in areas like fish ecology and coral reef research, and field components take advantage of WA's marine research stations and the university's own vessel-based and reef-based fieldwork rather than relying purely on aquarium or lab-based teaching.

Graduates move into marine research, fisheries and conservation management roles, often with WA state agencies managing the Ningaloo and Rottnest marine parks, as well as into further postgraduate marine science research both in Australia and internationally.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Marine Science, Biology foundation units, Chemistry, Earth and Ocean Systems
Year 2: Marine Ecology, Oceanography, Marine Invertebrate and Vertebrate Biology, field-based practical units
Year 3: Coral Reef Ecology, Fisheries Science, Marine Conservation and Policy, capstone field research project
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (WACE or equivalent); ATAR of approximately 85+ with prerequisite Mathematics Methods and a science subject.
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent).

name: Bachelor of Social and Environmental Sustainability
description: The Bachelor of Social and Environmental Sustainability at the University of Western Australia provides a unique blend of social sciences, humanities, environmental studies and policy for students passionate about creating a sustainable future. Students study the latest research and best practices in sustainability, hear from community and industry leaders, and gain hands-on experience tackling complex social and environmental challenges, with the option to take one of 10 interdisciplinary science minors. Graduates work in sustainability, environmental policy, community development and advocacy roles.

name: Bachelor of Social Work (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Social Work (Honours) at the University of Western Australia develops students' skills and knowledge to bring about positive change and socially just outcomes in the wellbeing of individuals, organisations and communities, equipping them to advocate for and improve the lives of individuals, families and communities. Built in collaboration with industry, the degree includes supervised field education placements. Graduates work in child protection, health, mental health, community development and policy, and are eligible for membership of the Australian Association of Social Workers.

name: Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Sport and Exercise Sciences at the University of Western Australia takes a multidisciplinary approach to examine humans' relationship with sport, exercise and physical activity, helping tackle major health challenges by understanding the effects of physical activity on human health and performance. Theory is combined with hands-on laboratory and practical work so students develop technical and communication skills, choosing from four degree-specific majors. Graduates work in exercise science, strength and conditioning, sports performance and health promotion, or progress to clinical exercise physiology.

name: Diploma in Computer and Data Science - 12 months
Diploma in Computer and Data Science 8 Months
Doctor of Clinical Dentistry
description: The Doctor of Clinical Dentistry at the University of Western Australia is a three-year full-time specialist training program for qualified dentists. It is a degree by coursework that includes a supervised research project and report, with coursework covering biostatistics, research methodology, oral and maxillofacial radiography and radiology, and the practical aspects of specialist dentistry. The program combines didactic teaching, weekly seminars, journal clubs and clinics with a supervised research project, and offers interdisciplinary teaching and research opportunities. Graduates practise as registered dental specialists.

name: Doctor of Dental Medicine
description: The Doctor of Dental Medicine at the University of Western Australia is delivered by Western Australia's only tertiary dental school, which has trained dentists for more than 75 years. The course consists of 20 units within modularised streams covering comprehensive clinical care, developmental and behavioural sciences, diagnostic and surgical sciences, and restorative and rehabilitative sciences. Core modules cover fundamental dental and medical sciences, while clinical practice modules cover patient care, preventive and conservative dentistry, restorative dentistry, and child and adolescent dental health. Graduates are qualified to register and practise as dentists.

name: Doctor of Medicine
description: The Doctor of Medicine at the University of Western Australia aims to produce graduates committed to the wellbeing of the patient, community and society as responsible, accountable, scholarly, capable and caring doctors. The course prepares graduates with the clinical and professional attributes required for successful internships and future training. In the first year students gain background knowledge in biomedical sciences, and in years two and three they undertake clinical attachments in wards and clinics. Graduates enter internship and prevocational training on the pathway to registration as a medical practitioner.

name: Doctor of Optometry
description: The Doctor of Optometry at the University of Western Australia is a three-year program that combines on-campus teaching and clinical placements. Students are trained in the early detection, diagnosis, treatment and management of eye diseases and the rehabilitation of conditions of the visual system. Course content and teaching are based on the competency standards for optometrists in Australia and New Zealand, covering professional responsibilities, communication, patient examination, diagnosis and management, and health information management. Graduates are qualified to register and practise as optometrists, detecting and managing eye conditions across the community.

name: Doctor of Pharmacy
description: The Doctor of Pharmacy at the University of Western Australia is accredited by the Australian Pharmacy Council and approved by the Pharmacy Board of Australia as a qualification leading to registration as a pharmacist in Australia. Delivered intensively over two years, the course integrates advanced pharmaceutical sciences with immersive practical training in community and hospital pharmacy, covering pharmacy practice, clinical pharmacy, pharmaceutics, medicinal chemistry, pharmacology, pharmacotherapy and health systems. It is designed to prepare graduates for dynamic roles in contemporary and emerging pharmacy practice.

name: Doctor of Philosophy and Master of Clinical Audiology
Doctor of Philosophy and Master of Clinical Neuropsychology
Doctor of Philosophy and Master of Clinical Psychology
Doctor of Philosophy and Master of Industrial and Organisational Psychology
Doctor of Podiatric Medicine
description: The Doctor of Podiatric Medicine at the University of Western Australia is a three-year program for entry into professional practice as a podiatrist. It aims to produce graduates able to treat and educate their patients effectively and appropriately in a professional and responsible way, using teaching methods including lectures, tutorials, practical training and directed self-learning. Case-based and problem-based learning emphasise patient-focused practice, and clinical practice begins in second year and continues into third year. Graduates register and practise as podiatrists, diagnosing and treating conditions of the foot and ankle.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business at the University of Western Australia covers the cornerstone areas of modern business, equipping participants with the skills to advance their careers and reach decision-making roles in their chosen industry or profession. The course consists of four units covering accounting, economic management, marketing and organisational behaviour, and can be studied full-time, part-time or online. It is designed for graduates of non-business disciplines and experienced professionals, and can serve as an entry pathway to the MBA. Graduates use it to move into management roles across sectors.

name: Graduate Certificate in Commerce
description: The Graduate Certificate in Commerce at the University of Western Australia comprises four units in accounting, economics, management and marketing. It is a standalone qualification that can also serve as an entry point into the Master of Commerce, and is ideal for graduates who do not hold an undergraduate degree in business. A postgraduate qualification in commerce from the internationally accredited UWA Business School can boost employment opportunities globally. Graduates use it to build business knowledge and progress toward specialist and management roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Finance
description: The Graduate Certificate in Finance at the University of Western Australia is designed to provide a practical grounding in financial affairs for careers in corporate banking and finance, stock-market trading, insurance and investment management. The course equips students to apply technical knowledge and skills to a variety of finance problems, such as capital investment decisions and investment analysis. It can be taken as a standalone qualification or as a pathway into further postgraduate finance study. Graduates work in banking, corporate finance, investment and analysis roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Forensic Anthropology
description: The Graduate Certificate in Forensic Anthropology at the University of Western Australia is designed to acquaint students with current developments in basic forensic sciences, particularly the medical and social sciences of direct relevance to forensic anthropology. Forensic anthropology has practical applications in forensic investigations as well as humanitarian efforts for the investigation of both living and deceased individuals. The course can be taken on its own or as a pathway into the Graduate Diploma and Master of Forensic Anthropology. Graduates work in forensic, investigative and humanitarian settings.

name: Graduate Certificate in Health Professional Education
description: The Graduate Certificate in Health Professional Education at the University of Western Australia addresses fundamental issues in health professional education by fostering interdisciplinary discussion and collaboration while participants develop knowledge and skills as educators within their field. The course comprises three core units covering the principles of teaching and learning, assessment, evaluation and research methods in health professions education, plus one elective unit that lets students explore an area of educational interest in more detail. Graduates take on teaching, supervision and curriculum roles across the health professions.

name: Graduate Certificate in International Relations
description: The Graduate Certificate in International Relations at the University of Western Australia is a professionally oriented postgraduate course studied over one semester full-time equivalent. It offers the opportunity to gain expertise in international relations with a particular focus on the dynamic Indo-Pacific and Indian Ocean regions, providing knowledge, skills and networks for a career in foreign affairs and diplomacy, government, international and non-governmental organisations, the media and education. The course offers credited internship options and engagement in professional networks.

name: Graduate Certificate in Population Health Studies
description: The Graduate Certificate in Population Health Studies at the University of Western Australia provides a pathway for those who wish to enrol in a Master of Public Health but who do not have the required educational background. Students gain an introduction to the fundamental concepts of public health and learn how public health works to create healthier populations, covering epidemiology, biostatistics, qualitative research methods, health economics and health promotion, plus the biological, environmental, economic and social determinants of health. Graduates progress to further public health study or to entry-level roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Public Policy
description: The Graduate Certificate in Public Policy at the University of Western Australia gives students a multidisciplinary understanding of how governments work to create a better future. Students who study public policy work across all levels of government, the not-for-profit sector, consulting firms and international organisations, as social entrepreneurs, policy analysts, consultants to government or holders of public office. The course helps students understand, design and evaluate economic and public policies, and can articulate into the Master of Public Policy.

name: Graduate Certificate in Rural and Remote Medicine
description: The Graduate Certificate in Rural and Remote Medicine at the University of Western Australia is a broad-based course for those wishing to pursue a career in teaching or research focused on rural and remote medicine, with Indigenous health a special focus. As rural and remote medicine is a generalist discipline, the range of relevant topics is wide, from large-scale epidemiological studies to educational, qualitative and clinical studies. The course can articulate into higher degrees. Graduates work in rural and remote clinical, teaching and research roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Social Policy Practice
description: The Graduate Certificate in Social Policy Practice at the University of Western Australia enables practising social workers to build on their knowledge of advanced social work theory, practice and research methods. The course is open to graduates with a bachelor degree, and students may proceed to the Graduate Diploma in Advanced Social Work on completion. Graduates apply advanced social policy knowledge in practice, management and advocacy roles across human services.

name: Graduate Certificate in Strategic Communication
description: The Graduate Certificate in Strategic Communication at the University of Western Australia gives students a preliminary overview of the skills, knowledge and capabilities required to participate in the contemporary communications environment across industry, government agencies and community organisations. Students gain practical skills and understanding relevant to a broad range of communications and media roles, and advance their capabilities for developing effective communication strategies and projects across digital and traditional formats. The course can articulate into the Graduate Diploma and Master of Strategic Communication.

name: Graduate Certificate in Studies
description: The Graduate Certificate in Studies at the University of Western Australia allows students to create their own course, undertaking four postgraduate units of optional breadth from across all faculties before deciding whether to articulate into the Master of Studies. In consultation with a course adviser, students complete 24 points of breadth from units available across the University. The course suits students who want a flexible, self-directed postgraduate qualification tailored to their academic, professional or personal goals.

name: Graduate Certificate in Translation Studies
description: The Graduate Certificate in Translation Studies at the University of Western Australia provides foundational knowledge about translation theory and practice and develops students' skills in translating between English and a chosen language: Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese or Spanish. Lecturers are both academics and professional translators, so teaching is enriched with theoretical and practical experience. The course can articulate into the Master of Translation Studies. Graduates pursue bilingual and multilingual careers across sectors.

name: Graduate Certificate in Urban Design
description: The Graduate Certificate in Urban Design at the University of Western Australia, delivered by the Australian Urban Design Research Centre, provides a preliminary overview of the urban design discipline and an introduction to its core principles, theories and practices. Students develop techniques of urban analysis and design propositions oriented to the traditions, aims and means of urban design. The course serves as a top-up qualification for professional practitioners and graduates of related fields, or an introduction for graduates from unrelated fields, and can articulate into the Graduate Diploma and Master of Urban Design.

name: Graduate Diploma in Advanced Social Work
description: The Graduate Diploma in Advanced Social Work at the University of Western Australia involves two compulsory units and a choice from a range of other advanced social work units, depending on availability. The course is open to social work graduates with a minimum of two years' experience as a professional social worker. Areas available for study include family-based practice, community and statutory practice, gender and cultural issues, disability, and management. Graduates advance into senior practice, supervision and management roles across human services.

name: Graduate Diploma in Building Information Modelling
description: The Graduate Diploma in Building Information Modelling at the University of Western Australia is designed by construction professionals for the next generation of professionals, and is beneficial to anyone working in engineering, construction, quantity surveying, architecture, project management or associated industries. The course extends practice into powerful and valuable applications of digitally based, data-rich building information models, helping students create innovative solutions for technological, economic and built futures. Graduates apply BIM skills to major infrastructure and building projects.

name: Graduate Diploma in Clinical Psychology
description: The Graduate Diploma in Clinical Psychology at the University of Western Australia is a bridging course for practitioners who have completed a master's degree or equivalent in clinical neuropsychology and are qualified with the Psychology Board of Australia, allowing them to upskill in clinical psychology. On completion, graduates are eligible for endorsement as a clinical psychologist with the Psychology Board of Australia and AHPRA. It is usually taken as a two-year part-time course, which suits practitioners who are working while they study.

name: Graduate Diploma in Forensic Anthropology
description: The Graduate Diploma in Forensic Anthropology at the University of Western Australia acquaints students with current developments in basic forensic sciences, particularly the medical and social sciences of direct relevance to forensic anthropology, and enables students to undertake advanced studies in the field. Forensic anthropology has practical applications in forensic investigations as well as humanitarian efforts for the investigation of both living and deceased individuals. Graduates work in forensic, investigative and humanitarian settings, or progress to the Master of Forensic Anthropology.

name: Graduate Diploma in Health Professions Education
description: The Graduate Diploma in Health Professions Education at the University of Western Australia addresses fundamental issues in health professional education by fostering interdisciplinary discussion and collaboration while participants develop knowledge and skills as educators within their field. The course comprises core units in the principles of teaching and learning, assessment, evaluation and research methods, plus elective units that allow students to explore an area of educational interest in further detail. Graduates take on teaching, supervision and curriculum leadership roles across the health professions.

name: Graduate Diploma in Infectious Diseases
description: The Graduate Diploma in Infectious Diseases at the University of Western Australia is aimed at science-based and medical professionals intending to work in hospital diagnostic or research laboratories, medical clinics, government health departments and international agencies. Units in the course have a practical emphasis enhanced by classes in the adjacent PathWest laboratories. Graduates apply their knowledge to the diagnosis, prevention and management of infectious diseases across laboratory, clinical and public health settings.

name: Graduate Diploma in International Relations
description: The Graduate Diploma in International Relations at the University of Western Australia is a professionally oriented postgraduate course studied over two semesters full-time equivalent. It offers the opportunity to gain expertise in international relations with a particular focus on the dynamic Indo-Pacific and Indian Ocean regions, and prepares students for a career in foreign affairs and diplomacy, government, international and non-governmental organisations, the media and education. The course offers credited internship options and engagement in professional networks.

name: Graduate Diploma in Law
description: The Graduate Diploma in Law at the University of Western Australia is designed to equip practising lawyers and law graduates with an advanced understanding of the law to meet the challenges of the dynamic workplace. Students learn from experienced teaching staff and study alongside the next generation of leaders in legal practice, government, business and the not-for-profit sector. The course consists of four postgraduate option units chosen from an extensive list. Graduates deepen their specialist legal knowledge and advance their careers.

name: Graduate Diploma in Natural Resources Law
description: The Graduate Diploma in Natural Resources Law at the University of Western Australia is ideal for those looking to expand their knowledge of the mining, energy and natural resources sector or to move into this highly regulated industry. The course is available for law and non-law graduates, and depending on qualifications it may articulate into the Master of Resources and International Commercial Law or the Master of Mining and Energy Law. Graduates work in legal, compliance, policy and advisory roles across the resources sector.

name: Graduate Diploma in Ocean Technology and Engineering
Graduate Diploma in Strategic Communication
description: The Graduate Diploma in Strategic Communication at the University of Western Australia enables students to develop the skills, knowledge and capabilities required to participate in the contemporary communications environment in industry, government agencies and community organisations. The course is tailored to advance creative and organisational capability, developing practical skills relevant to communication strategy and managing communication projects across digital and traditional media formats. It can articulate into the Master of Strategic Communication. Graduates work across communication, media and campaign roles.

name: Graduate Diploma in Urban Design
description: The Graduate Diploma in Urban Design at the University of Western Australia is delivered by the Australian Urban Design Research Centre and provides a focused year of urban design history, theory, implementation strategy and studio-based learning. Building on the Graduate Certificate, students gain experience as individual designers and in interdisciplinary groups working on the complex nature of urban issues, and gain preliminary experience in conducting independent research.
