name: Diploma of Arts, Social Science and Humanities
Doctor of Medicine
description: The Doctor of Medicine at the University of Wollongong aims to produce knowledgeable, caring and competent graduates who are well prepared to commence vocational training in any area of medicine. The MD is a four-year full-time degree, with each academic year approximately 42 weeks long, using a combination of face-to-face teaching, clinical placements, blended and online learning, and self-directed learning. Teaching takes place at the Wollongong, Shoalhaven and Southern Highlands campuses and one of eight rural hubs, giving the program a strong community and rural health emphasis. Graduates enter internship and prevocational training toward registration as a medical practitioner.

name: Graduate Certificate in Applied Finance
description: The Graduate Certificate in Applied Finance at the University of Wollongong is an introductory course providing a general understanding of areas in applied finance such as financial statement analysis, managerial finance, statistics and corporate governance. The course values prior learning and work experience, and mature-age working professionals without an undergraduate degree can still apply and have their relevant qualifications or substantial professional experience assessed. Domestic students can study on campus or by distance. Graduates use it to formalise finance skills and progress toward further postgraduate study or finance roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business at the University of Wollongong is for those who want to advance their career, formalise their industry experience or move into a business-focused role within their field. The course covers key business areas including accounting, financial management, organisational behaviour and marketing management. It caters for professional and lifestyle commitments by offering study on campus at Wollongong or Sydney CBD, or online through distance or fully online delivery modes. Graduates use it to build business knowledge and progress toward management roles or further master's study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Business Administration (Executive)
description: The Graduate Certificate in Business Administration at the University of Wollongong is designed for professionals ready to sharpen their strategic capabilities and lead with purpose in complex business environments. Fully embedded within the MBA, the course focuses on diagnosing real organisational challenges through the disciplines that drive business performance, developing the analytical rigour and ethical framework needed to make decisions that matter. Learning is grounded in practical real-world examples, industry input and collaborative assessment. Graduates advance into management and leadership roles or continue into the MBA.

name: Graduate Certificate in Computing
description: The Graduate Certificate in Computing at the University of Wollongong provides a postgraduate introduction to computing for students without prior knowledge of IT and computing. As occupations in data science, cyber security, IT management, health informatics and software engineering grow in demand, the course allows graduates and professionals from a non-IT background to add a recognised computing qualification to their skill set. It includes a selection of core computing and information technology subjects related to programming and systems. Graduates progress into IT roles or into further postgraduate computing study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Education
description: The Graduate Certificate in Education at the University of Wollongong is designed for educators seeking a short, flexible degree that can be tailored to their needs and interests. It suits graduates and professionals looking to diversify or change career direction into fields such as staff training and development or policy and planning. The course has one core subject and three electives chosen from the Master of Education specialisations, including educational leadership, digital technologies for learning, and TESOL, and can articulate into the Master of Education. Graduates apply it across teaching, training and education support roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Engineering
description: The Graduate Certificate in Engineering at the University of Wollongong is designed to train and enhance professional practice, advance technical and specialist skills, and provide the opportunity to apply theory through applied projects. It provides a foundation for the more intensive theoretical and practical work of the graduate diploma and master's degrees. The course consists of four subjects: engineering research methods plus three technical subjects in a specialisation such as civil, mining and environmental; electrical, computer and telecommunications; or mechanical, materials and mechatronic engineering. Graduates advance their engineering careers or continue to further study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Financial Technology
description: The Graduate Certificate in Financial Technology at the University of Wollongong is built on the intersection of finance and information technology, a field growing exponentially and transforming the future of business. The course is aimed at students seeking to upgrade existing finance skills or aspiring to a career in the growing FinTech field. Students learn to consider the impact of technology on banking and global payment systems, the insurance industry and trading in financial markets, and how blockchain technology facilitates more transparent transactions. Graduates work in FinTech, banking, payments and financial services roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Fisheries Policy
description: The Graduate Certificate in Fisheries Policy at the University of Wollongong is tailored for individuals seeking to specialise in fisheries policy, management or representation within the fisheries sector, including fisheries policy officers, junior managers and government enforcement officers, as well as industry and non-government organisation representatives. The course provides a broad understanding of the international legal and policy framework within which fisheries resources are managed, conserved and developed, and examines the principles of fisheries management. Graduates work in fisheries and marine resource management, policy and compliance roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Indigenous Trauma and Recovery Practice
description: The Graduate Certificate in Indigenous Trauma and Recovery Practice at the University of Wollongong responds to issues of particular relevance in Australian Indigenous communities. It is a multidisciplinary program in which students apply critical thinking, collaborative practice and judgement when working with individuals who have experienced trauma. The course focuses on applying Indigenous social and emotional wellbeing principles, practices and healing frameworks, using both Aboriginal and Western concepts of trauma and considering the historical and cumulative impact of trauma. Graduates work in health, community, social and emotional wellbeing, and healing roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in International Relations
description: The Graduate Certificate in International Relations at the University of Wollongong offers a focused introduction to international relations for graduates from any discipline. Students build in-demand skills in critical thinking, policy analysis and professional communication that transfer across industries, deepening their understanding of complex global systems and how to respond to real-world international issues. The course prepares students to contribute across government, business and the not-for-profit sector, and can articulate into further international relations study.

name: Graduate Certificate in Law of the Sea
description: The Graduate Certificate in Law of the Sea at the University of Wollongong covers the international law governing the rights and duties of stakeholders in maritime environments, including the rights and obligations of coastal states, navigational rights and responsibilities, conservation and use of marine resources, and maritime security. It is designed to meet the early and mid-career education requirements of legally qualified professionals working in a maritime policy or operational context. Graduates work in maritime law, ocean governance, policy and enforcement roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Maritime Studies
description: The Graduate Certificate in Maritime Studies at the University of Wollongong deals with policy, law and security issues related to the world's oceans, including maritime trade routes, the ocean as a natural habitat, and its role as a source of both international tension and cooperation. Students gain an understanding of maritime enforcement, maritime security threats and solutions, marine environmental law, regulation of shipping and marine resources management, and learn to analyse the legal, political and operational factors that shape the law of the sea and maritime policy. Graduates work in maritime policy, security and governance roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting
description: The Graduate Certificate in Professional Accounting at the University of Wollongong is an introductory course providing a general understanding of accounting and related areas in business, including accounting, finance, economics and business law. Successful completion provides a pathway to the Master of Professional Accounting or Master of Professional Accounting Advanced with credit for four subjects, and progression to other master's degrees including the MBA may also be possible. Graduates use it to enter the accounting profession or to build toward a professional accounting qualification.

name: Graduate Certificate in Public Health
description: The Graduate Certificate in Public Health at the University of Wollongong is a flexible program providing a broad introduction to public health, enabling graduates to work with communities to contribute to effective and sustainable public health practices nationally and internationally. Students gain insight into the challenges of improving the health of vulnerable communities and the range of career opportunities in public health, studying two core public health subjects plus two electives. The course can articulate into the Master of Public Health. Graduates work in health promotion, policy and program roles.

name: Graduate Certificate in Science and Management
Graduate Certificate in TESOL
description: The Graduate Certificate in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages at the University of Wollongong is a specialist qualification for people who want to teach English to speakers of other languages in Australia or overseas, and for current primary or high school teachers who want additional ESL qualifications. The course offers sound theoretical and empirical foundations and extensive practical skills, including exploring teaching methods and common grammar issues and undertaking a supervised professional experience placement in an ESL classroom. Graduates teach English across language schools, secondary and vocational settings, and overseas.

name: Graduate Diploma in Business Administration (Executive)
description: The Graduate Diploma in Business Administration at the University of Wollongong is designed to build responsible, strategic leaders who can make confident decisions and drive meaningful change in complex global business environments. The course grounds students in the fundamentals that matter, from economics and finance to marketing, artificial intelligence, supply chain, and people and culture. Through case studies drawn from contemporary organisations and input from industry experts, students develop the strategic thinking and ethical framework required to lead organisations that are commercially successful and socially responsible. Graduates advance into management roles or continue into the MBA.

name: Graduate Diploma in Occupational Health and Safety
description: The Graduate Diploma in Occupational Health and Safety at the University of Wollongong is for students holding an undergraduate degree or graduate certificate in occupational health and safety or occupational hygiene. Developed with industry to address the complex nature of workplace health and safety, the course covers advanced WHS risk management, applied human factors and ergonomics, industrial epidemiology and toxicology, occupational health and safety theories and systems, work health and safety law, and workplace hazards and hygiene. Graduates work as WHS advisers, managers and consultants across industry and government.

name: Graduate Diploma in TESOL
description: The Graduate Diploma in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages at the University of Wollongong is designed for TAFE or vocational education teachers whose employers require an in-depth qualification, and for experienced educators seeking a higher specialist qualification in ESL teaching. The course offers sound theoretical and empirical foundations and extensive practical skills, providing the skills to teach English with a focus on international and local contexts and catering for diversity in the classroom. Graduates teach English across vocational, secondary and adult education settings in Australia and overseas.

name: Master of Applied Finance
description: The Master of Applied Finance at the University of Wollongong builds advanced understanding of applied finance for careers in financial statement analysis, managerial finance, corporate governance and related areas. The course values prior learning and professional experience, and develops the analytical and decision-making skills finance professionals need across corporate finance, investment and risk. Graduates work in banking, corporate finance, investment and financial analysis roles.

name: Master of Business
description: The Master of Business at the University of Wollongong allows students to choose subjects that are of most interest to them and their career, building fundamental business knowledge and skills through core subjects and completing a research capstone. It can be combined with another business master's degree through the double master's program, earning two master's degrees in two years and building expertise in two in-demand areas. Graduates gain knowledge across a broad range of business areas and move into a variety of business careers.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
UOW's MBA runs through the Faculty of Business and Law and is AACSB-accredited. It targets working professionals: most units are offered in intensive or evening/weekend formats so people can study alongside full-time jobs, and the cohort skews toward students with several years' work experience rather than fresh graduates.

Core coverage is standard MBA territory (strategy, finance, marketing, leadership), but the elective structure lets students build a concentration: options have included international business and innovation/technology management, reflecting the region's manufacturing and steel industry links. A consulting-style capstone project replaces a traditional thesis for most students, usually done with a real host organisation.
curriculum:
Core: Managerial Economics, Financial Management, Strategic Management, Marketing Management, Organisational Leadership, Business Analytics for Decision Making
Electives: choose 4, options include International Business, Innovation Management, Human Resource Strategy, Entrepreneurship
Capstone: applied strategy/consulting project with a partner organisation, final session
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus 2 years relevant work experience
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Business Administration Advanced
description: The Master of Business Administration (MBA) Advanced at the University of Wollongong is designed to shape responsible, strategic leaders who can navigate complexity, drive innovation and make confident data-informed decisions in rapidly evolving organisations. The advanced course allows students to specialise in an area of interest by completing additional subjects, and is grounded in the Principles of Responsible Management Education so that graduates lead ethically and sustainably. Students study economics, accounting, marketing, finance, people and culture, artificial intelligence, project management and supply chain management. Graduates progress into senior management and leadership roles.

name: Master of Business Analytics
description: The University of Wollongong Master of Business Analytics builds skills in descriptive, predictive and prescriptive analytics for working with large volumes of business data. Foundation subjects are completed in the first two sessions, followed by Advanced Business Analytics and a Business Analytics Research Capstone in the final sessions, with two 900-level electives chosen from across the Faculty of Business and Law. On completion, students receive the SAS Joint Certificate and the Advanced SAS Joint Certificate. The course is offered on campus and by distance. Overseas qualifications must be assessed as equivalent to an Australian bachelor degree, and international students must show English proficiency. Indicative international tuition is around A$37,100 per year. Graduates apply analytics and the associated tools and technologies to support business decision-making.

name: Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology
description: The Master of Clinical Exercise Physiology at the University of Wollongong is for graduates of exercise science who want to upgrade their qualifications and work with individuals with chronic diseases and disabilities. On completion, students have the technical expertise to restore good health and physical capability to people after illness or injury, and develop their skillset in data gathering and analysis as it applies to human movement, physiological systems integration and the processes underpinning unhealthy individuals. Graduates work as accredited exercise physiologists in clinical, hospital and community settings.

name: Master of Computer Science
description:
UOW's Master of Computer Science runs out of the School of Computing and Information Technology, based across the main Wollongong campus and the SMART Infrastructure Facility building on the eastern side of campus. It's built for people switching into computing from another background as much as CS graduates topping up their qualification: there's a foundation stream covering programming and data structures for anyone without a CS undergrad, then the degree proper moves into data management systems, network design, and software architecture. Wollongong's CS group has a long-standing research strength in wireless networking, and that shows up in elective options around network and system security.

Class sizes are smaller than at the Group of Eight campuses in Sydney, and a fair chunk of the cohort is international, drawn partly by post-study work rights and partly by regional-campus fee settings that undercut the big Sydney universities. The degree finishes with an individual capstone project, supervised one-on-one, which functions as a portfolio piece students bring to interviews with Illawarra-region and Sydney tech employers.
curriculum:
Foundation session (waived with a relevant CS background): Programming and Data Structures, Data Management Systems
Core: Software Construction and Design, Advanced Database Systems, Strategic Network Design, Security, Ethics and Professionalism
Electives: choose from cloud computing, machine learning, mobile application development, distributed systems
Capstone: individual major project, supervised by CSIT faculty, final session
Optional: internship/WIL subject in place of one elective for eligible students
Duration: 24 months full-time or 48 months part-time
admission_requirements: A recognised bachelor's degree in any field with a weighted average mark (WAM) of 60% or above; applicants with other qualifications plus relevant professional experience may also be considered.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, minimum 6.0 in each band.

name: Master of Computing
description: The Master of Computing at the University of Wollongong develops the next generation of computing professionals with broad knowledge and a deep understanding of the technical, managerial and ethical aspects of computing practice. The data analytics specialisation focuses on applying current technologies to deliver data-driven insights and intelligence. The degree suits graduates with a computing background who wish to upskill and graduates without a computing background who wish to enter the field, and incorporates academic learning with practical application. Graduates work as computing and data professionals across industry.

name: Master of Data Science
description:
Housed in the School of Computing and Information Technology, this is a conversion-friendly degree: people with a quantitative but non-CS background (maths, engineering, science, even some commerce graduates) can enter through the foundation stream. Coursework runs through statistics, machine learning, big data systems, and data visualisation, with more weight put on applied projects using real or realistic datasets than on pure theory.

UOW markets this partly on Wollongong's growing data-analytics employer base and partly on affordability relative to Sydney's data science masters programs, a genuine consideration for the international cohort making up a large share of enrolments.
curriculum:
Foundation session (background-dependent): Programming for Data Science, Statistics for Data Science
Core: Machine Learning, Big Data Management, Data Visualisation, Data Mining
Electives: deep learning, natural language processing, business analytics (varies by session offering)
Capstone: applied data science project, industry or research-based, final session
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree in a related discipline
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of Earth and Environmental Sciences
description: The Master of Earth and Environmental Sciences at the University of Wollongong is for students who wish to extend their knowledge and diversify their skills across sub-disciplines of the earth and environmental sciences, including environmental science, earth science, life sciences and conservation. The degree emphasises the interconnectedness of these sub-disciplines through common core subjects, and is designed through the lens of global perspectives in science, with students using drones, artificial intelligence and coding. Graduates work in environmental science, conservation, consulting and research roles.

name: Master of Education
description: The Master of Education at the University of Wollongong is a higher degree for teachers and educators wishing to pursue advanced studies in their area of interest. Many subjects require the application of research and theoretical insights to actual practice, and it is desirable that students have some workplace or teaching experience. Specialisations include digital technologies for learning, educational leadership, interdisciplinary studies and TESOL. Graduates advance into leadership, curriculum, policy and specialist roles across the education sector.

name: Master of Education Extension
description: The Master of Education Extension at the University of Wollongong is a higher degree for professional educators and for those interested in a career in teaching English to speakers of other languages or in educational leadership. The two-year program extends the learning outcomes of the Master of Education and offers candidates the opportunity to specialise in either TESOL or educational leadership, introducing contemporary trends and issues in research, theory and practice, with flexible online or classroom study. Graduates advance into specialist, leadership and TESOL teaching roles.

name: Master of Engineering
description: The Master of Engineering at the University of Wollongong delivers the expert skills and applied competencies required for the professional engineer. Designed to train and enhance professional practice and advance technical and specialist skills, the degree provides the opportunity to put theory into practice through applied projects and research, while building communication, strategic and project management skills. It is professionally accredited by Engineers Australia apart from the Management major. Graduates practise as professional engineers across a range of engineering sectors.

name: Master of Engineering Management
description: The Master of Engineering Management at the University of Wollongong is a professional degree for engineers who see their careers progressing into management, including senior management positions. The degree provides a strong grounding in modern management thinking applicable to engineering industries, and is offered in conjunction with the Sydney Business School so that professional, technical and environmental aspects of engineering projects are accompanied by current management thinking. Students study engineering logistics, project management, modelling of engineering management systems and strategic management. Graduates move into engineering management and leadership roles.

name: Master of Financial Technology
description: The Master of Financial Technology at the University of Wollongong is aimed at students aspiring to pursue a career in the growing FinTech field, built on the intersection of finance and information technology. Students explore technology and its impact on banking and global payment systems, the insurance industry and trading in financial markets, learning through a blend of theoretical knowledge and practical application as organisations across industries seek graduates who can identify opportunities to disrupt markets and drive positive change. Graduates work in FinTech, banking, payments, insurance and financial services.

name: Master of Financial Technology Extension
description: The Master of Financial Technology Extension at the University of Wollongong is aimed at students aspiring to a career in the growing FinTech field, built on the intersection of finance and information technology. The extended degree covers the impact of technology on banking and global payment systems, the insurance industry and trading in financial markets, and adds advanced FinTech skills and data programming expertise. Organisations across industries seek graduates who can identify opportunities to disrupt markets and drive positive change. Graduates work in FinTech, banking, payments and financial services roles.

name: Master of Fisheries Policy
description: The Master of Fisheries Policy at the University of Wollongong is designed for fisheries or environmental policy officers, mid-level managers and enforcement officers, and for those wanting to pursue a career in fisheries and marine resources management. The degree provides a broad understanding of the law of the sea and the issues facing the fisheries sector, including fisheries management; monitoring, control and surveillance; fish trade; and regulatory compliance. Students analyse the relationships between fisheries law, policy, science, economics and trade. Graduates work in fisheries management, policy and compliance roles.

name: Master of Global Science and Management
Master of Human Resource Management
description: The Master of Human Resource Management at the University of Wollongong is designed to prepare professionals for the evolving landscape of people and culture. The specialised degree equips individuals with essential skills for working through the demands of the contemporary workplace, examining organisational structures, systems, culture and leadership dynamics, and providing a comprehensive understanding of how to leverage competitive advantage in the global marketplace. It addresses hybrid work models, digital transformation and sustainability. Graduates work in human resources, people and culture, and organisational development roles.

name: Master of Information and Communication Technology Advanced
Master of Information Technology
description: The University of Wollongong Master of Information Technology develops an in-depth understanding of the organisational, economic, regulatory and socio-technical issues in implementing and applying IT in business, and how to manage them. Students specialise in Information Design and Analysis, Information Systems Development, or Enterprise Systems. It suits both graduates moving into IT from another field and those extending an existing computing background into management and analysis roles. The degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society at professional level, and the ACS reciprocal agreements give that recognition internationally. Indicative international tuition is around A$40,300 per year. Graduates work as IT managers, business and systems analysts, enterprise systems specialists and IT consultants.

name: Master of International Business
description: The Master of International Business at the University of Wollongong is designed to enhance the capabilities of business managers within the global business landscape. Students develop knowledge and skills in identifying and analysing global business strategy issues and providing sustainable recommendations, studying topics such as multinational financial management and cross-cultural management and learning how to develop international business strategies to achieve business objectives. It can be combined with another business master's degree through the double master's program. Graduates work in international business, trade, strategy and management roles.

name: Master of International Relations Extension
description: The Master of International Relations Extension at the University of Wollongong provides advanced knowledge and skills needed to respond to the complex and globalised international environment. Students critically engage with key theories and issues in international relations through elective subjects and specialisations, developing knowledge and skills in one of four areas: research, public health, maritime security and policy, or international policy and skills. The two-year degree is aimed at graduates of any discipline and offers an interdisciplinary, practical understanding of international relations. Graduates work in government, international organisations, NGOs and policy roles.

name: Master of Laws
description: The Master of Laws at the University of Wollongong provides law graduates with specific knowledge and skills in a specialised area of law and policy. The degree is designed for early or mid-career legally qualified professionals working in a particular area of policy or operational context, or those intending to pursue a career in a specialised field. Students gain knowledge of areas such as jurisdiction, law enforcement, and legal regulation and frameworks, and learn to analyse the legal, political and operational factors that shape the development of law and policy. Graduates advance into specialist legal and policy roles.

name: Master of Maritime Policy
description: The Master of Maritime Policy at the University of Wollongong deals with policy, law and security issues related to the world's oceans, including maritime trade routes, the ocean as a natural habitat, and its role as a source of international tension and cooperation. The degree is designed to meet the early or mid-career education requirements of maritime professionals working in a policy or operational context, providing a broad understanding of the law of the sea, ocean governance and maritime security. Graduates work in maritime policy, security, governance and operational roles.

name: Master of Marketing
description: The Master of Marketing at the University of Wollongong equips students with the knowledge and skills to thrive in a marketing landscape shaped by digital transformation and emerging technologies. Students explore how artificial intelligence, big data and digital media are redefining how businesses connect with their audience, and through subjects such as AI-Driven Digital Marketing and Big Data and Marketing Analytics learn to use data and technology to design strategies that deliver real business impact. Guided by leading academics and industry experts, graduates move into marketing strategy, digital marketing and analytics roles.

name: Master of Mathematical Sciences
description: The Master of Mathematical Sciences at the University of Wollongong is designed for graduates with a background in mathematics and statistics, providing the opportunity to consolidate and expand existing knowledge while being equipped to apply mathematics in other disciplines such as computer science, business, science and psychology. Students develop skills in undertaking research on mathematical or statistical problems that arise in other disciplines, learn to communicate and synthesise complex information, and complete a research or coursework-focused capstone project. Graduates work as mathematicians, statisticians, data scientists and analysts.

name: Master of Medical Biotechnology
description: The Master of Medical Biotechnology at the University of Wollongong is designed for students who seek knowledge and technological expertise in specific areas of cell and molecular biology, the basis for modern biotechnological research and development. Subjects introduce the basic elements of modern cell and molecular biology before intensive training in current biotechnology and its application to medicine, agriculture and molecular biology, with tutorials and laboratory-based practical work. Graduates work in biotechnology, pharmaceutical, research and laboratory roles.

name: Master of Medicinal Chemistry
description: The Master of Medicinal Chemistry at the University of Wollongong provides advanced training across various fields of medicinal chemistry and significant skills in the drug discovery and development processes, responding to high demand for graduates in medicinal and pharmaceutical chemistry. The degree brings together chemistry and biology to understand the causes of disease and to design, synthesise, characterise and develop medicines, and integrates science communication and science management to prepare graduates for diverse careers. Graduates work in pharmaceutical research, drug development and chemistry roles.

name: Master of Nursing
description: The University of Wollongong Master of Nursing prepares nurses for senior roles in nursing and the health system. It requires 48 credit points: 24 credit points of core subjects plus 24 credit points made up of electives or, for students who choose it, a major research project. Entry requires a Bachelor of Nursing of at least three years or a Graduate Certificate in Nursing from a recognised institution, and international students need IELTS 6.5 overall with at least 6.0 in every band. This is a post-registration degree and does not by itself lead to registration; those seeking to register as a nurse take the Bachelor of Nursing or the Master of Nursing (Pre-Registration). Indicative international tuition is around A$35,600 per year. UOW also offers specialist graduate certificates and master degrees in areas such as mental health nursing and gerontology.

name: Master of Nursing International
description: The University of Wollongong's Master of Nursing International is a two-year degree for internationally qualified nurses: entry requires a recognised Bachelor of Nursing. It is a post-registration professional development degree, not a pathway to first registration for people who are not already nurses. The course builds on the School of Nursing's strengths in primary health, mental health, aged and dementia care, clinical excellence, and research principles and methods, and is delivered through weekly online learning activities in each subject. It gives nurses an academic route to advance their knowledge and apply evidence-based practice in their own health systems. Estimated total tuition is around A$59,400 for the degree.

name: Master of Nutrition and Dietetics
description: The Master of Nutrition and Dietetics at the University of Wollongong prepares graduates to be professional dietitian-nutritionists who apply the science of food and nutrition to promote health, prevent and treat disease, and optimise the health of individuals, groups and communities. Students study medical nutrition therapy, translating the science of nutrition into personalised dietary advice, and are prepared to work in community and public health nutrition, clinical dietetics, food service management and research. The course is accredited. Graduates work as dietitians across hospitals, private practice, community health and industry.

name: Master of Occupational Health and Safety
description: The Master of Occupational Health and Safety at the University of Wollongong provides an integrated teaching and research program with the objective of promoting the highest level of safety and inspiring the next generation of occupational health and safety professionals. The knowledge and skills developed allow graduates to confidently address complex workplace health and safety issues through technical knowledge and application, with an emphasis on the communication skills and techniques needed to implement WHS strategies. The degree was developed with industry. Graduates work as WHS managers, advisers and consultants.

name: Master of Occupational Health and Safety Extension
description: The Master of Occupational Health and Safety Extension at the University of Wollongong provides an integrated teaching and research program, giving students the opportunity to focus on health promotion or occupational health and safety research and to address complex workplace issues through specialised technical knowledge and application. Students study advanced WHS risk management, workplace hazards and hygiene, occupational health and safety systems, applied human factors and ergonomics, and industrial epidemiology and toxicology. Graduates work as senior WHS professionals, researchers and consultants.

name: Master of Occupational Hygiene
description: The Master of Occupational Hygiene at the University of Wollongong uses science and engineering to measure exposure to physical, chemical and biological workplace hazards, communicate these to employers and employees, and design and implement control strategies to prevent ill health caused by the working environment. The degree has a flexible delivery mode combining online content with three to five days of on-campus block teaching that uses UOW's well-resourced facilities. Graduates work as occupational hygienists across industry, consulting and government.

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description: The University of Wollongong Master of Professional Accounting is recognised by CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand; students seeking membership apply directly to those bodies for recognition of their prior undergraduate study and should start that process before enrolling. The degree covers the core accounting disciplines and suits graduates who want an accredited accounting qualification, including those without an accounting background. An Advanced version runs two years and includes further study for students without a business background. Entry is based on a recognised bachelor degree, with English language, individual qualification assessment and relevant professional experience among the criteria considered. Indicative international tuition is around A$37,100 per year. Graduates work in professional accounting, audit, tax and financial-management roles across the private and public sectors.

name: Master of Professional Accounting Advanced
description: The Master of Professional Accounting Advanced at the University of Wollongong is a two-year course designed for non-accounting graduates who want a career in the accounting profession and want to enhance their learning by including another discipline specialisation. The learning experience is focused on the practice of accounting, and students choose one of three specialisations depending on their career aspirations, such as financial management or international business. Graduates work in accounting, finance and advisory roles and toward professional accreditation.

name: Master of Professional Psychology
description: The Master of Professional Psychology at the University of Wollongong is for graduates who have completed four years of APAC-accredited study in psychology or an international equivalent. The primary aim is to provide a one-year comprehensive program of study of the professional practice of psychology, including assessment, intervention, communication and ethics, preparing candidates for a final year of supervised internship on the pathway toward general registration as a psychologist. Graduates progress to supervised practice and registration.

name: Master of Project Management
description: The Master of Project Management at the University of Wollongong explores how efficient management provides organisations with an improved ability to plan, implement and control their business activities. The course provides comprehensive project management skills across the full project lifecycle, from initiation and planning to execution and closing, and teaches strategies for dealing with a broad range of issues encountered within organisations. It can be combined with another business master's degree through the double master's program. Graduates work as project and program managers across sectors.

name: Master of Public Health
description: The University of Wollongong's Master of Public Health is a one-year full-time degree built from four foundational core subjects plus electives or a chosen specialisation: Social Systems, Big Data and Decision Science, Indigenous Health, Public Health Practice, Public Health Research, or Climate and Environment. It includes work integrated learning, industry connections and practical placements, and can be studied in a flexible mode with fortnightly on-campus tutorials or fully by distance. Entry requires a bachelor degree with a 65 percent weighted average plus further study or experience, and IELTS 6.5 with no band below 6.0. Graduates work in health policy, program design and evaluation, research, and government and non-government health organisations. Indicative international tuition is around A$39,000 for the full course in 2026.

name: Master of Public Health Extension
description: The Master of Public Health Extension at the University of Wollongong provides a comprehensive introduction to public health, with the extended degree allowing students to tailor their learning to their career aspirations through additional specialisations or elective subjects. Students study four foundational subjects in public health and can specialise in areas such as social systems, big data and decision science, Indigenous health, public health practice, public health research, or climate and environment. Graduates work in public health policy, program, research and practice roles across government and non-government organisations.

name: Master of Social Work (Qualifying)
description: The Master of Social Work (Qualifying) at the University of Wollongong prepares students for a career that drives meaningful social change across health, community services and government. Designed for graduates from a range of backgrounds including social sciences, psychology, health and human services, education, and arts and humanities, the degree provides an accredited pathway to become a professional social worker in Australia. Students build the skills and knowledge to support individuals, families and communities through the study of social policy, ethics and practice, with supervised field education. Graduates work across health, child protection, community and government settings.

name: Master of Supply Chain Management
description: The Master of Supply Chain Management at the University of Wollongong is aimed at those seeking to develop or expand their skills in supply chain management and the key business functions of procurement and logistics. Students learn how to implement a variety of strategies relevant to contemporary supply chains, developing capabilities in forecasting, analytics, continuous improvement and logistics management. It can be combined with another business master's degree through the double master's program. Graduates work in supply chain, procurement, logistics and operations roles.

name: Master of Teaching (Primary)
description: The Master of Teaching (Primary) at the University of Wollongong is for university graduates from non-teaching courses who want to become primary school teachers from Kindergarten to Year 6. The degree produces high-quality teachers with an understanding of diversity in the classroom and strong connections to school communities. Students build teaching skills through professional experience immersion programs starting within the first month and continuing in weekly blocks, completing 60 days of professional experience including the option of a placement in a rural or remote area of New South Wales. Graduates are qualified to teach in primary schools.

name: Bachelor of Actuarial Studies
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Actuarial Studies is a direct foundation for entering the actuarial profession, structured so that students achieving the required academic standard in their actuarial courses gain exemption from the Actuaries Institute's Foundation Program professional examinations, along with Validation by Educational Experience credit recognised by the US Society of Actuaries and Casualty Actuarial Society. Actuarial Studies (Co-op) students and those in dual degrees may also gain exemption from university accreditation components of the Actuary Program's professional examinations, and students planning to complete UK actuarial qualifications can access Transfer of Prior Learning credit for subjects already covered. It suits students who've decided on an actuarial career from the outset of their studies and want their undergraduate degree to count directly toward professional actuarial accreditation, rather than treating actuarial study as one specialisation within a broader commerce degree.
curriculum: Students must complete 144 UOC when taken as a standalone program. These UOC are made up of: Level 1 Actuarial Studies Core Courses (48 UOC) Level 2 Actuarial Studies Core Courses (24 UOC) (Please note: ACTL2131 may be substituted by MATH2901 and MATH2931, please see below) Level 3 Actuarial Studies Core Courses (6 UOC) Level 3 Actuarial Studies Electives (18 UOC) Free electives (36 UOC) General Education (12 UOC) For single and related double degrees please see Progression Plan
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); PTE Academic 64 overall. UNSW also accepts TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency Cambridge English and its own UNSW College pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Advanced Computer Science (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Advanced Computer Science (Honours) is built for talented students with exceptional analytical skills who want to build the technologies of the future, covering core fundamentals in programming, software engineering, computer hardware, data structures and algorithms before moving into computing electives and an in-depth Honours thesis in a chosen specialisation. Free electives let students pursue other interests alongside their core computing training, and the degree provides strong preparation for postgraduate study, joining or building a technologically innovative organisation, or making a substantial contribution to IT in any field. It suits high-achieving students who know computer science is their career direction and want genuine depth and research experience woven into their undergraduate degree, rather than a standard computer science degree without the honours research component.
curriculum: Advanced Computer Science (Honours) Specialisations: COMPTH Theoretical Computer Science, COMPCH Computer Science, COMPIH Artificial Intelligence, COMPYH Security Engineering. Optional Minor: MATHC2 Mathematics.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); PTE Academic 64 overall. UNSW also accepts TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency Cambridge English and its own UNSW College pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Advanced Science (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Advanced Science (Honours) suits innovative thinkers with exceptional scientific ability who want genuine flexibility to tailor their degree around their own interests, studying foundation courses across biology, chemistry, physics and mathematics before choosing a major to explore in depth. The embedded fourth-year honours component involves a supervised research project and, in some cases, advanced coursework, giving students genuine research experience before they graduate rather than saving it for postgraduate study. Outstanding honours students can continue directly into a higher research degree, making this a real pathway into an academic or research career for talented science students. It suits high-achieving science students who want more flexibility, advanced-level content and built-in research training than the standard Bachelor of Science provides.
curriculum: Students must complete 192 UOC when taken as a standalone program. Students in the Advanced Science (Honours) program are expected to complete the following requirements. 144 UOC of Science courses : - At least one approved Bachelor of Advanced Science (Honours) major - SCIF1001 and SCIF2001 - 48 UOC Honours year - Science elective courses. Science courses are defined in "Table 1" in the Additional Information section. 36 UOC Free Electives . These courses can be taken from any Faculty of the University at any stage of your program. 12 UOC General Education courses . Please see the rules regarding General Education below. These courses can be taken at any stage in your program. Please click the Sample Programs link below to view a typical enrolment pattern for this program.
admission_requirements: UNSW Students may be granted Recognition for Prior Learning (RPL) which may or may not reduce the amount of learning required to achieve a degree at UNSW. Generally, RPL is only granted based on the completion of tertiary-level studies, but in exceptional circumstances may also include non-formal or informal learning such as professional experience. RPL will not be granted based on partly completed tertiary courses. All applications for RPL at UNSW are subject to UNSW Recognition of Prior Learning (Coursework Programs) Policy and Procedures. Students seeking credit for courses completed at another university are required to submit documentary evidence (course outlines, academic transcripts) to support their application, and to nominate the course(s) for which they seek credit. In addition, the following conditions apply for all UNSW Science programs (including the Science component of...
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); PTE Academic 64 overall. UNSW also accepts TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency Cambridge English and its own UNSW College pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Architectural Studies
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Architectural Studies centres on studio-based learning, introducing students to real-world design challenges like climate-responsive architecture, housing and cultural safety from day one rather than delaying practical design work until later years. The curriculum integrates environmental sustainability, construction principles and digital design skills, with a strong focus on architecture in practice through engagement with industry professionals and real projects, building understanding of design processes, construction methods and professional legal and social responsibilities. Students explore First Nations knowledge and perspectives throughout, ensuring their design work respects cultural heritage and fosters inclusive communities. Graduates can move into diverse architecture and design-based careers or continue into UNSW's accredited Master of Architecture, the recognised pathway to professional architectural registration. It suits students who want a genuinely studio-driven, practice-connected introduction to architecture as both a design and social discipline.
curriculum: Students must complete 144 UOC when taken as a standalone program. This is comprised of the following: Core Courses: 120 UOC Free Electives: 12 UOC General Education: 12 UOC
admission_requirements: Applicant may be required to do an interview as part of the admission process. UNSW Built Environment recognises that your academic results may not reflect your potential in creative thinking and making. We have therefore introduced an optional alternative admission scheme to give applicants for our design programs an opportunity to submit a portfolio to be considered in conjunction with their academic achievements. More information about this scheme is available at: https://www.be.unsw.edu.au/future-students/alternative-admission-scheme Applicant can submit a portfolio to showcase talent and boost the chance of admission.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); PTE Academic 64 overall. UNSW also accepts TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency Cambridge English and its own UNSW College pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Art Theory
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Art Theory (Honours) is a one-year advanced degree for high-achieving students who've already completed an undergraduate degree in art history and theory or a related field, deepening their critical and scholarly skills through a significant independent research thesis supported by coursework in art theory. The program builds highly sought-after analytical, problem-solving and research skills alongside deep art history and theory knowledge, providing a genuine pathway into higher degree research programs like an MPhil or PhD as well as diverse careers across the arts and cultural sectors. It suits art history and theory graduates who performed strongly in their undergraduate studies and want research training before either continuing into further academic study or moving into cultural sector careers requiring genuine scholarly depth, distinguishing this honours pathway from purely practice-based creative arts study.
curriculum: Core Courses: DART4300 Contemporary Art Research Methods, DART4301 Art Theory Honours Research Project, ADAD4020 Art and Design in Practice.
admission_requirements: Applicants are required to have completed (or to be eligible to complete) a Bachelor of Art Theory or other bachelors degree in art history, art theory, visual culture, cultural studies, or related fields. Applicants may be graduates either of UNSW or another recognised institution. A weighted average mark (WAM) or equivalent of 70 or higher is an entry requirement. Admission is subject to the WAM requirements as well as supervisory capacity in the Faculty as determined by the Program Authority. Applications should be submitted via the UNSW Apply Online portal and include a 500-word research proposal sent directly to the Program Authority. This proposal should outline the topic and area of interest so that an appropriate supervisor can be assigned.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in each band); PTE Academic 64 overall. UNSW also accepts TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency Cambridge English and its own UNSW College pathway programs.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Arts builds critical thinking, communication and research skills through deep exploration of human existence, societies, cultures and histories, taught by academics working across diverse humanities and social science disciplines. Students combine deep specialisation in at least two disciplinary areas with a wide range of elective courses and genuine industry engagement opportunities, rather than following one narrow single-discipline path. Employers value UNSW Arts graduates for their creativity and ability to develop innovative solutions to contemporary problems, reflecting the degree's emphasis on transferable analytical and communication skills alongside disciplinary depth. It suits students who want genuine breadth and depth across humanities and social science disciplines, combining flexibility in course choice with the option to specialise seriously in two chosen areas rather than staying purely generalist.

name: Bachelor of Arts and Social Sciences (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Arts and Social Sciences (Honours) is a one-year advanced degree for high-achieving students who've completed an undergraduate pass degree in Arts, Social Sciences, Politics Philosophy and Economics, International Studies, or Social Research and Policy, deepening research and analytical skills within their existing major specialisation. The honours year develops higher-order critical thinking, reflection and analysis specific to the student's chosen discipline, understanding of relevant disciplinary methods and their assumptions, and an appreciation for ethics within both private and public life. Available full-time or part-time, the program builds genuine research capability that applies interdisciplinary perspectives and historical or comparative frameworks where relevant to the student's field. It suits arts and social science graduates who performed strongly in their pass degree and want deeper research training before entering the workforce or continuing into further postgraduate research study.

name: Bachelor of Aviation (Flying)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Aviation (Flying) trains students to become professional pilots while also developing them as future aviation industry leaders, combining the science behind aviation with actual flight training delivered through UNSW Aviation's own Flying Operations Unit at Bankstown Airport. Students train to Commercial Pilot Licence standard with a multi-engine instrument rating and complete Air Transport Pilot Licence theory subjects, while also studying aviation management topics including human factors and safety, airworthiness management, commercial operations and airline management. The program includes direct mentoring from professional industry pilots, and students can access the Qantas Aviation Career Enrichment Program, which builds professional skills during second year and provides a recruitment pathway into Qantas after graduation. It suits students specifically committed to a professional piloting career, since the block-based flight training structure means teaching periods run differently from standard academic terms and the flying component must be completed full-time.

name: Bachelor of Biotechnology (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Biotechnology (Honours) applies living cells and biochemical molecules like proteins, DNA and RNA to real-world problems, covering pharmaceutical and food production, improved crops and livestock, environmental clean-up and forensic science, grounded in molecular genetics and molecular cell biology. Students learn how recombinant DNA technology enables creating and improving industrial organisms and producing useful proteins at scale, underpinning biopharmaceuticals like hormones, vaccines and new cancer therapies that are actively reshaping medicine. The degree also covers how genomic and proteomic techniques are generating new drug targets, and how microorganisms are being modified to control plant and animal diseases and pests. It suits students drawn to the practical, product-focused application of modern biology, positioning graduates for careers in pharmaceutical development, agricultural biotechnology, forensic science, diagnostics or environmental biotechnology.

name: Bachelor of City Planning (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of City Planning (Honours) is a four-year, full-time embedded honours program leading to accredited professional planning qualifications, combining core disciplinary courses with electives and a practice year of genuine work-integrated learning in the workplace. The final year includes a plan-making studio and a research thesis, letting students pursue specialist interests in depth before graduating, reflecting the profession's real work: collecting and analysing information, forecasting, preparing policies and plans, exercising development control and communicating outcomes to diverse stakeholders. Using Sydney and New South Wales as a working laboratory placed in global planning context, the program builds analytical, collaborative and communication skills valued well beyond planning itself. It suits school leavers who've decided on planning as a career from the outset, wanting a fully accredited, practice-integrated undergraduate pathway into the profession.
curriculum: Students must complete 192 UOC when taken as a standalone program.

name: Bachelor of Commerce
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Commerce is built around an Integrated First Year where students learn how organisations actually operate in complex environments while developing professional skills alongside academic content, before choosing up to two majors from a comprehensive, industry-advised list including accounting, business analytics, economics, finance, fintech, HR, information systems, international business, marketing and taxation. Students get exclusive access to UNSW Business School's Career Accelerator program, with completion of at least one for-credit Career Accelerator course a signature feature of the degree, alongside a personalised myBCom roadmap and a digital graduate portfolio showcasing academic and practical career-ready skills. Many majors fulfil professional accreditation requirements directly, and high-performing students can continue into an honours year or postgraduate study. It suits students who want a comprehensive, career-focused business degree with genuine industry connections built into the curriculum rather than added as optional extras, backed by access to UNSW Business School's 90,000-strong alumni network.
curriculum: Optional Interdisciplinary Major: COMMI1 AI in Business and Society.
admission_requirements: ATAR 92 or equivalent

name: Bachelor of Commerce/Design
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Commerce/Design is a four-year double degree combining a fully valued business qualification with training for careers in design across a wide range of fields, or for understanding design's role within contemporary business more broadly. The Commerce component builds core business fundamentals and lets students explore a chosen business discipline, while the Design component provides strong design fundamentals with flexibility to explore multiple design specialisations. It suits students who see genuine value in combining commercial literacy with creative and design skills, whether they're aiming for a career as a practising designer who understands business, or a business role where design thinking and product sense matter, such as digital product management, brand strategy or design-led innovation consulting.

name: Bachelor of Computational Design
description: UNSW's honours year within the Bachelor of Computational Design lets students who've performed well at undergraduate level deepen their knowledge of design methods, literature and history through a significant independent research project, connecting undergraduate study to supervised research. The honours program consolidates and extends work from the standard undergraduate degree, providing an academic foundation for students planning to continue into a professional master's, a research master's or a PhD. Alongside the independent research project and coursework, students complete research literacy and integrity training, OH&S and safety training in the faculty's Squarehouse studios, and present at faculty research seminars. It suits high-achieving computational design students who want genuine research experience and an academic credential beyond the standard degree before moving into further postgraduate study or specialised computational design practice.
curriculum: Thesis: CODE4200 Honours Thesis. Core Courses: BENV4000 Research Methods in the Built Environment, CODE4100 Critical Review of the Literature.
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in Computational Design with the equivalent of a UNSW Credit average.

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description:
Run through the School of Computer Science and Engineering, this is one of the most selective computing degrees in the country by ATAR cutoff, reflecting demand from Sydney's tech and finance sectors. Students can specialise from second year into streams like artificial intelligence, computer graphics and games, security, or programming languages and compilers, with a well-worn path into UNSW's CSE research groups for honours.

The degree carries a mandatory industrial training requirement (typically a placement over a summer break), and the school has a well-known extracurricular hackathon and competitive programming culture that a meaningful chunk of students plug into outside timetabled hours.
curriculum:
Year 1: Programming Fundamentals, Data Structures and Algorithms, Mathematics for CS, Computer Systems Fundamentals
Year 2: Software Engineering, Databases, Operating Systems, Theory of Computation
Year 3: specialisation electives (AI, security, graphics, systems), Professional Issues and Ethics
Mandatory: minimum 60 days industrial training
Capstone: research or industry-linked project course, final year
admission_requirements: ATAR 96 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Construction Management and Property
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Construction Management and Property is a three-year program building foundational knowledge across construction management, property development and quantity surveying, covering industry regulations, construction and property management technologies, sustainability principles and professional ethics. Close industry ties mean students can enrol in a dedicated work-integrated learning course, alongside site visits, guest lectures and overseas study opportunities woven through the curriculum. After completing the base degree over nine terms, students can pursue a one-year honours program either continuing broadly in construction management and property or specialising specifically in building, property development or quantity surveying. It suits students aiming for management careers across construction and property-related organisations, wanting a genuinely industry-connected degree rather than a purely theoretical construction or property qualification.
curriculum: Students must complete 144 UOC when taken as a standalone program.

name: Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice offers a critical, interdisciplinary exploration of crime, justice and social change, drawing on criminology, sociology, law, public health, youth work and policy studies rather than treating criminology as a narrow standalone discipline. Students engage with diverse perspectives, including from people with lived experience of the criminal justice system, examining criminalisation, policing, incarceration, alternative justice systems, and the impacts of colonisation and systemic inequality on justice outcomes. Two integrated core curricula, the Criminology and Criminal Justice Core and the Social Science Core, build both deep criminological theory and practical social research and policy analysis skills, supplemented by work-integrated learning, internships or one of four available double degree options. It suits students who want a genuinely critical, research-grounded approach to criminology rather than a purely descriptive study of crime, positioning graduates for careers across justice, policy, advocacy and community sectors.

name: Bachelor of Cyber Security
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Cyber Security directly addresses the cyber skills gap, building a strong computer science technical foundation with emphasis on machine and software understanding alongside human factors and vulnerabilities that attackers actually exploit. Students learn from both an attack and defence perspective with a genuine engineering mindset toward security, combining applied and theoretical elements to build a well-rounded pipeline of cyber professionals capable of contributing to Australia's sovereign cyber capability. The program uses Universal Design for Learning principles and a hybrid flexible delivery model integrating online, in-person, laboratory and industry-based experiences. It suits students who want dedicated cyber security training from the start of their degree rather than treating security as one specialisation within a broader computer science or IT program, positioning graduates for roles as security analysts, penetration testers or security engineers.
curriculum: Students must complete 144 Units of Credit (UOC) to attain a Bachelor of Cyber Security, including: 66 UOC Core Courses 30 UOC Cyber Electives 36 UOC Free Electives 12 UOC General Education

name: Bachelor of Data Science and Decisions
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Data Science and Decisions trains students to meet strong current and future demand for data scientists and analysts, building coherent knowledge across mathematics and statistics, computer science, and economics before students pursue deeper knowledge in one of three specialisation streams. Beyond technical data skills, the program deliberately builds critical reading, logical thinking, clear communication and teamwork, alongside genuine ethical grounding for working with data and its real-world consequences. Students learn to apply mathematical and computational techniques alongside genuine business sensibility to real-world problems involving complex data sets, rather than treating data science as a purely technical exercise divorced from its business or social context. It suits students who want a genuinely interdisciplinary data science degree spanning mathematics, computing and economics, rather than a narrower computer-science-only or statistics-only data program.

name: Bachelor of Design (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Design (Honours) offers flexible, wide-ranging specialisations across Computational Design, Industrial Design and Integrated Design, letting students craft a design career around their own goals and the challenges society will face in the future rather than following one fixed design track. The practical, hands-on studio culture gives students access to making workshops, digital facilities and advanced research labs, learning directly from award-winning entrepreneurs, studio-based designers, industry professionals and futurists across two campuses, Paddington and Kensington. Conceptual, technical and theoretical coursework combine to prepare genuinely job-ready graduates capable of contributing imaginatively and thoughtfully to real design challenges. It suits students who want design training with genuine specialisation choice and hands-on studio access, rather than a narrow single-discipline design degree, positioning graduates for careers spanning product, digital, computational and industrial design.

name: Bachelor of Design/Education (Secondary)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Design/Bachelor of Education (Secondary) is a four-year, nationally accredited double degree for students who want to become secondary school design and technology or visual arts teachers, combining design training with 80 days of supervised professional teaching experience across two secondary schools. Depending on which design specialisation a student chooses, Computational Design, Industrial Design or Integrated Design, they gain teaching accreditation in different combinations of subjects: Design and Technology, Enterprise Computing, Graphics and Multimedia Technology, Visual Arts, or Textiles and Design, as either a first or additional teaching area. It suits students who know from the outset that they want to teach design-related subjects in secondary schools, giving them both genuine design expertise and a fully accredited teaching qualification in one combined program, rather than completing a design degree followed by a separate teaching qualification afterward.

name: Bachelor of Economic (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Economics (Honours) explores how the decisions of institutions and individuals interact to determine outcomes for the economy and society, covering traditional economic issues like unemployment, taxation and trade policy alongside genuinely pressing human challenges including inequality, climate change, corruption and access to education and healthcare. The honours pathway adds a research dimension on top of the standard degree, developing highly transferable analytical skills valued across policy, government, private sector and international organisation careers. Students can choose from three economics specialisations, build their own program, or combine economics with other business and commerce study, including through double degree options, and gain practical experience through internships, group consulting projects and global practicums. It suits high-achieving economics students who want genuine research training and deeper analytical rigour before entering the workforce or continuing into further postgraduate economics study.
curriculum: Students must complete 144 UOC when taken as a standalone program. Courses for the major are taken once but also meet core and elective course rules where listed. Students completing the degree as a standalone program may also choose to complete optional majors and minors from outside Economics by using their business electives, free electives and / or general education electives as appropriate. name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) - Software Engineering
description:
A four-year, 168-unit accredited engineering degree combining engineering design fundamentals with computing depth. It starts with the same common engineering core as UNSW's other engineering majors (Engineering Design and Innovation, first-year maths and computing) before specialising into software architecture, systems design, and software project management from second year. Distinct from the standalone CS degree in its engineering accreditation and heavier emphasis on large-scale system design and formal engineering process.

The degree requires a minimum of 60 days of industrial training, which the faculty helps place, often with Sydney's large tech, finance, and telecommunications employers given UNSW's location and industry relationships.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Design and Innovation, Programming Fundamentals, Mathematics 1A/1B, engineering foundations
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Software Engineering Design and Construction, Database Systems, Computer Architecture
Year 3: Software Architecture, Requirements Engineering, Systems Design Project, electives

Hands-on creative practice is balanced with studies in the histories and theories of each discipline, helping students understand how creativity and culture intersect with the social, ethical and global contexts of contemporary life. The three-year program builds a genuine creative community for deep engagement in practice, honing both creative and professional skills to prepare graduates for industry pathways or further study. It suits students who know they want a genuinely practice-focused fine arts education with real specialisation depth, rather than a broad, generalist creative arts degree, whichever of the four specialisations matches their creative direction.

name: Bachelor of Food Science (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Food Science (Honours) is a four-year professional degree preparing students for careers as food scientists, offered in two disciplines: Food Science and Technology, focused on product design and processing, or Food Science and Nutrition, focused on the chemistry, biochemistry, health and nutrition dimensions of food. Students build a solid natural and applied science foundation before specialising in areas including food chemistry, microbiology, toxicology, biotechnology, processing, packaging, preservation and product development, culminating in a research thesis project. An optional minor in Humanitarian Science and Technology lets students apply their food science knowledge toward UN Sustainable Development Goals, adding a genuine social-impact dimension to the technical training. Both streams lead to a Bachelor of Science (Honours) recognised by the Institute of Food Technologists, giving graduates internationally recognised professional standing in food science careers spanning product development, food safety and nutrition consulting.

Building on the disciplinary foundation from the standard bachelor's degree, the honours year develops academic excellence, social engagement and global perspective to prepare graduates for transition into professional practice, while also connecting undergraduate study to supervised independent research for those considering a research master's or PhD afterward. It suits high-achieving industrial design students who want a genuine research credential and deeper design exploration before entering professional practice, as well as those keeping the door open to further postgraduate research study in design.

name: Bachelor of Information Systems
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Information Systems trains students in the interaction between technology, people and processes needed to achieve business goals, spanning internal applications like enterprise networks and IT services through to external technology products and user experience. The degree includes an Integrated First Year alongside other business school students, building professional skills and organisational understanding before moving into core Information Systems content across design and development, organisational IS, data and information management, and technology and security. A work-integrated learning course lets students apply their skills in real workplace settings before graduating, and core study concludes with a capstone project synthesising learning across the whole degree. It suits students who want a genuinely 'business savvy' technology qualification, positioning graduates for careers in digital transformation, IT consulting, UX design, cybersecurity consulting or database administration, with an optional honours year available for high performers wanting deeper research training.
