name: Bachelor of Interior Architecture (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Interior Architecture (Honours) treats interior architecture as research-led creative practice, focused on the design and agency of inhabited interiors across scales from a single room to an entire city, and across permanent to temporary spaces. The program treats the interior as a dynamic, open-ended conceptual space through which the human experience of private and public urban environments can be interrogated and reimagined, grounded in material and spatial assembly informed by environmental, cultural and historic context. Students develop an agile, critical approach to design inquiry balanced with genuine creative risk-taking, aiming to produce graduates capable of ethical, collaborative, multi-disciplinary practice as global demands reshape future interior spaces. It suits design students drawn to interiors as a genuinely intellectual and research-grounded discipline, rather than a purely decorative or styling-focused approach to interior design.

Students combine a regional or language specialisation (options have included Chinese, Spanish, French, Japanese, Korean) with a disciplinary stream in international relations, politics, or global development.

It suits students drawn to landscape architecture as a critical design profession shaping public spaces in cities and regions, rather than gardening or horticulture-focused study.

name: Bachelor of Laws
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Laws cannot be studied as a standalone degree; it's only offered in combination with another approved undergraduate degree as a double degree, satisfying the academic requirements for admission as a legal practitioner in NSW. The law-specific component comprises 144 units of credit covering compulsory core courses, a prescribed theory elective and law electives, while breadth comes from whichever second degree a student pairs it with, and double degree LLB students don't need to complete general education courses separately. Students cannot transfer from a double degree LLB enrolment into a single LLB enrolment, though transferring out of the double degree into just the non-law program may be possible depending on that program's own rules. It suits school leavers who've decided on a legal career and want to pair law study with another discipline, such as arts, commerce or science, from the start of their degree.

name: Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics combines three distinct intellectual disciplines to help students understand and act on pressing contemporary issues like justice, inequality and climate change, rather than studying any one discipline in isolation. Alongside a carefully chosen combination of existing courses from Politics and International Relations, Philosophy, and Economics, the program includes courses specifically designed to explore the synergies and tensions between these three fields and assess their combined relevance to humanity's hardest problems. PPE graduates globally are recognised leaders across government, political parties, the public service, NGOs and social activism, as well as banking, consultancy and corporate strategic advising, reflecting the degree's reputation for producing versatile, analytically rigorous graduates. It suits students who want genuinely interdisciplinary training in how political, philosophical and economic thinking intersect, rather than a single-discipline social science degree.

name: Bachelor of Psychological Science
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Psychological Science provides an integrated education across developmental, social, cognitive, biological, physiological and abnormal psychology, building both scientific research understanding and applied practice skills alongside genuine research methods training. The APAC-accredited three-year sequence lets students choose electives in specialist areas like psychology and law, psychology and work, developmental disorders, psychopathology, health psychology or neuroscience, and pair psychology with a complementary major in a related discipline such as behavioural economics, criminology, linguistics, neuroscience or vision science. Career paths span clinical, correctional, counselling, educational and organisational psychology settings, as well as academic research, health research, ergonomics, personnel selection and marketing. It suits students who want a genuinely accredited psychology foundation combined with a complementary discipline, keeping open the option of a fourth-year Honours program for those who qualify.

name: Bachelor of Psychology (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Psychology (Honours) builds an integrated education across learning, memory, cognition, perception, motivation, lifespan development, personality, social interaction and abnormal psychology, combining scientific research training with applied practice skills. In the fourth honours year, students complete a year-long, 30-credit-point independent research project across areas including psychopathology, behavioural neuroscience, cognitive science, forensic psychology or social and developmental psychology, culminating in a thesis independently assessed by two academics other than their own supervisor. Alongside the research project, students complete 18 credit points of advanced coursework covering the history, professional ethics and evidence-based practice foundations of psychology, plus contemporary issues reflecting current staff research specialisations. It suits high-achieving psychology students who want genuine research experience and a thesis-based honours qualification, positioning graduates for clinical, forensic, health or organisational psychology careers as well as further postgraduate psychology study.

name: Bachelor of Science - Computer Science
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Science in Computer Science studies the design, construction and use of computer systems, covering how data and data structures are represented and how algorithms are designed for automatic information manipulation through programming languages and machine systems. The program focuses on the design and development of hardware and software tools that enable computer applications, rather than the applications themselves, though non-computing factors like human interface design and psychological aspects are acknowledged as genuinely shaping whether computing systems actually succeed in practice. UNSW places particular emphasis on understanding the basic principles behind computing tools, operating systems, compilers and translators, and computer hardware, building foundational understanding rather than only applied programming skill. It suits students who want a genuinely science-oriented computer science education grounded in fundamental computing theory, rather than a more applied IT or software engineering degree.

name: Bachelor of Science (Computer Science) / B Arts
description: UNSW's combined Bachelor of Science (Computer Science) and Bachelor of Arts lets students complete both a genuine computer science qualification and a full Bachelor of Arts from the Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture, requiring 192 units of credit across the combined 5-year program. Students must satisfy entry requirements for both components separately, reflecting the genuine depth expected in each half of the double degree rather than a diluted combination of the two. It suits students who want serious computer science technical training paired with substantive humanities, social science or creative arts study, rather than choosing between a purely technical degree or a purely arts-based one, positioning graduates for careers where technical skill and humanities perspective combine, such as technology policy, digital humanities, UX design or technology journalism.

name: Bachelor of Science (Medicine) Honours
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Science (Medicine) Honours is a one-year research program available to high-achieving year 4 students in the six-year Medicine program or the Arts/Medicine double degree, letting students step out of standard medical training to complete supervised research. Since 2022, students choose between a coursework-intensive option, reducing the research project to 18 units of credit alongside coursework from an approved specialisation and General Practice units, or an Extended Research option with a larger 36-unit research project. The year builds appreciation for research's role in medical science, experience presenting scientific findings, and grounding in research philosophy and technique that can support a future specialised medical research career, alongside developing the ability to interpret evidence underpinning clinical practice. It suits medical students who've performed strongly enough to be eligible and want genuine research experience woven into their medical training rather than treating research as separate from clinical education.

name: Bachelor of Social Science
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Social Science (Honours) is a one-year advanced degree for high-achieving students who've completed an undergraduate pass degree in Social Science, deepening understanding within their chosen policy specialisation through a significant independent research thesis. The honours year develops the highly sought-after analytical, problem-solving and research skills that distinguish honours graduates from standard bachelor's graduates, typically completed within the same policy specialisation pursued in the pass degree rather than starting fresh in a new area. Available full-time or part-time, the program can serve as a genuine pathway into PhD study for students who want to continue in social science research. It suits social science graduates who performed strongly in their pass degree and want deeper research training before entering the workforce or continuing into doctoral study.
curriculum: Core Courses: ARTS4266 Puzzles, Planning, and Presentation for Honours in the Social Sciences, ARTS4268 Methodologies in the Social Sciences: Questions and Quandaries. Thesis: SOSS4052 Social Science Honours, SOSS4053 Social Science Honours, SOSS4051 Social Science Honours.

name: Bachelor of Social Sciences
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Social Sciences builds capacity to contribute to real-world social, political and cultural change, focusing on contemporary global and local challenges taught using new and digital technologies for a flexible, rich learning experience. Students combine in-depth disciplinary knowledge in one or more social science disciplines with specialisation in national or international policy-making and the skills to identify and apply evidence in professional practice and policy contexts. The degree explicitly develops professional communication, analysis, ethical decision-making and teamwork skills, demonstrated through strong work-integrated learning and exchange options with industry partners. It suits students who want social science training explicitly oriented toward employability and real-world policy impact, rather than purely academic social science study, positioning graduates for careers in policy, government, NGOs and international organisations.

name: Bachelor of Social Work (Honours)
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Social Work (Honours) is an accredited program leading to eligibility for membership of the Australian Association of Social Workers, covering social work practice, social and behavioural sciences, and specific fields of practice including work with Aboriginal communities, counselling skills, community and group work, mental health, trauma and child protection. Students build research skills throughout the degree and complete either an independent research thesis or a professional practice portfolio as their honours capstone, drawing on the extensive expertise of qualified social work practitioners who teach the program. Two separate field placements in years three and four give students substantial practical experience before graduation, with the Honours Thesis pathway requiring a 70 weighted average mark while the Advanced Practice Honours Portfolio has no such cutoff. It suits students who want a fully accredited social work qualification combining genuine scholarly rigour with substantial hands-on field experience.
curriculum: Students must complete 192 UOC when taken as a standalone program. The UNSW BSW (Hons) can be completed full-time in Single mode (normally 4 years) or in Double Degree mode alongside Bachelor degrees in Criminology, Arts, Social Policy or Law. The basic requirements of the program are simple. The BSW has a depth component and a breadth component. Students enrolled in Single mode do both the depth and breadth component while students enrolled in Double Degree mode only complete the depth component. If you study in either the single or double degree mode, you will complete: Core courses comprising 168 UOC (24 courses) If you study in single mode, you will also complete: 12 UOC of Free Electives (2 courses) 12 UOC of General Education (2 courses)

name: Bachelor of Vision Science
description: UNSW's Bachelor of Vision Science studies the sensory processes underlying vision alongside the development of vision-related technologies, covering optics and lens design, ocular anatomy and physiology, eye disease, sensation and perception, and research design across a genuinely broad discipline. Graduates are positioned for growing sectors including vision and ophthalmic research, assistive and rehabilitative technologies, virtual and augmented reality development, ocular imaging and diagnostics, and the design of new healthcare devices and models, going well beyond a narrow pre-optometry pathway. Students who complete the degree may be eligible to transfer into the Master of Clinical Optometry, making it a genuine dual-purpose degree for students interested in vision science broadly as well as those aiming specifically for optometry practice. It suits students interested in the science of vision and its technological applications, whether that leads toward clinical optometry, biomedical technology industries, or further vision science research.
curriculum: Students must complete 144 UOC when taken as a standalone program. 120 UOC Core courses in Stages 1 to 3 12 UOC General Education Courses 12 UOC Free Elective Courses Please check 3181 Vision Science for optimal order of term based course enrolment.

name: Diploma in Architecture
description: UNSW's Diploma in Architecture is a 12-month pathway into second year of Architectural Studies, Interior Architecture (Honours), or Landscape Architecture (Honours), the latter only via Term 1 intake, letting students complete eight courses, seven first-year equivalents plus one general education elective, that count directly toward the destination degree. Delivery runs at a slower pace than standard first-year study, with longer 12-week terms and greater contact hours giving students more opportunities for consultation, practice and revision as they adjust to university-level design studio learning. It suits students who want to study architecture, interior architecture or landscape architecture at UNSW but need a supported, slower-paced entry point before committing to full first-year design studio coursework, with successful completion leading directly into second year of the chosen destination degree.

name: Diploma in Business
description: UNSW's Diploma in Business is a 12-month pathway into the Bachelor of Commerce, letting students complete eight business courses plus a communication and academic literacy course, all equivalent in content to first-year UNSW courses but delivered at a slower pace with more face-to-face contact hours. Credit is granted toward the Bachelor of Commerce for each course achieved at the specified level, so successful completion of all nine courses leads directly into commerce degree study rather than requiring a separate application process. The program is deliberately structured to ease the transition into university learning styles, lectures, tutorials and problem-solving workshops, with additional support built in throughout, though the economics and information systems streams aren't currently available. It suits students who want a Monash-style university experience and support structure before committing to full undergraduate commerce study, particularly those without strong prior advanced mathematics who may also benefit from a mathematics bridging course beforehand.

description: UNSW's Master of Biomedical Engineering is only available to students already enrolled in specific double degree pathways, either the Engineering (Honours)/Biomedical Engineering or Materials Science and Engineering (Honours)/Biomedical Engineering programs, rather than as a standalone qualification students can apply for directly. The degree applies engineering principles to healthcare technology and problems across an unusually broad range of applications, spanning implantable bionics, drug delivery systems, medical imaging, radiotherapy, orthopedic devices, telemedicine, robotic surgery, tissue engineering and physical rehabilitation. Because it only exists within these double degree structures, students planning a biomedical engineering career at UNSW need to enrol in the relevant combined program from the outset rather than adding biomedical engineering as an afterthought. It suits engineering students who know early on that they want to apply their technical training specifically to healthcare and medical technology problems.

name: Master of Built Environment
description: UNSW's Master of Built Environment is a research-only degree letting students develop expert knowledge in a chosen area of built environment research, involving an original investigation more limited in scope than a doctorate but still genuinely research-driven. Running 1.5 to 2 years full-time, students produce a thesis of up to 75,000 words under supervision, with all candidates required to complete a research seminar course in their first session to build appropriate research methodology from the outset. Because the degree is entirely research-focused, the specific built environment topic, whether in architecture, planning, construction or another related field, depends on the individual student's interests and available supervision. It suits built environment graduates with a genuine research question who want a formal research credential, often as a pathway toward a PhD or a specialised research role in the built environment sector, rather than students seeking a taught postgraduate qualification.

description: UNSW's AGSM MBA prepares students for general management and executive leadership roles across business, government, startups and the social-impact sector, combining facilitated class discussions with experiential activities and case studies taught by academics with genuine international industry experience. The 12-month program runs across three consecutive terms with no program leave permitted, reflecting its design for professionals who can take a full year away from work to concentrate entirely on their development, supported by AGSM's international offerings and a strong peer cohort of high-performing leaders from around the world. A dedicated Career Accelerator team works with students throughout the program on career goals and access to AGSM's alumni network, and scholarship offerings recognise the sacrifice of taking a year away from paid work. Entry is based on a portfolio assessment including an undergraduate degree plus at least two years of professional or managerial experience, or at least six years of professional work experience without a degree, alongside a Graduate Management Admission Test score, making this suited to established professionals with genuine leadership experience rather than recent graduates.

A problem-based learning approach teaches ethics, brain function and disorders, assessment and intervention based on real client presentations, combining weekly asynchronous lectures with case-based tutorials. name: Master of Clinical Optometry
description: UNSW's Master of Clinical Optometry combines the theoretical discipline of vision science, covering optics, ocular physiology and the neuroscience of vision, with the clinical practice of primary eye care, including diagnosing and managing ocular disease, dispensing spectacles and contact lenses, and caring for patients with special vision needs. Graduates are eligible to register as optometrists in Australia, with the qualification also recognised in New Zealand and most of Asia, reflecting strong and growing job demand driven by an ageing population and the high visual demands of modern computer-based work. Students in the dual Bachelor of Vision Science/Master of Clinical Optometry award graduate with specialised knowledge spanning both clinical practice and vision science research capability. It suits vision science graduates or those with a related science background who want to become practising optometrists, combining rigorous scientific training with genuine clinical registration pathway.

As the number of places available each year is limited and will vary from year to year, entry into the program is competitive. name: Master of Commerce - All Specifications
description: UNSW's Master of Commerce is a long-established, broad-based postgraduate business degree that lets students specialise across a comprehensive range of business disciplines, suiting both non-business graduates building commercial skills from scratch and business graduates wanting to broaden their expertise into new areas. Because the degree covers many possible specialisations, the exact content varies significantly depending on which discipline a student chooses to focus on, whether that's accounting, finance, marketing, business analytics or another business field offered through UNSW Business School. Entry requires a recognised undergraduate degree with a credit average, though applicants without an undergraduate qualification may be eligible through alternative pathways UNSW Business School assesses individually. It suits students who want a genuinely flexible business postgraduate qualification and are prepared to choose their own specialisation path, rather than a pre-set curriculum, making UNSW's Business School advising resources important for shaping the degree around individual career goals.

Entry requires a recognised undergraduate degree with a credit average, with alternative pathways available for applicants without a qualifying undergraduate degree through UNSW Business School's own assessment process. It suits students who want the same flexibility as the standard Master of Commerce but need or want the longer extension format, whether for a deeper specialisation, additional foundational coursework, or a more gradual course load.

name: Master of Construction Project Management
description: UNSW's Master of Construction Project Management applies project management principles across the full construction development cycle, covering how to manage time, cost, quality, safety and sustainability outcomes on real construction projects. Available full-time or part-time, the program is aimed at improving the proficiency of practitioners already working in construction to meet current and future industry challenges, covering both general management principles and their specific application to construction project delivery. It suits construction industry professionals who want formal project management credentials to progress into more senior project leadership roles, as well as graduates from engineering, architecture or related fields moving specifically into construction project management. The program's practical, industry-facing focus distinguishes it from a general project management qualification not tailored to construction's specific technical and regulatory demands.

name: Master of Construction Project Management/Property and Development
description: UNSW's combined Master of Construction Project Management and Master of Property Development is a two-year, seven-term program giving students knowledge across both construction project management and property development and investment, rather than specialising in just one. The concise, combined structure suits people seeking careers spanning construction management, project management, design management, and property development, investment and infrastructure management, as well as architects, engineers, urban planners and lawyers wanting a broader base for their existing careers. Because the program deliberately straddles two related but distinct industries, graduates leave with genuinely dual expertise rather than a construction qualification with a token property module or vice versa. It suits people who want career flexibility across both construction delivery and property investment and development, rather than committing to a narrower single-discipline postgraduate qualification.

name: Master of Curating and Cultural Leadership
description: UNSW's Master of Curating and Cultural Leadership builds connections between curating, audience engagement, policy, management, critical writing, promotion and production, treating contemporary curating as a dynamic profession that sets cultural agendas rather than a purely administrative gallery function. Built on more than 20 years of UNSW Art & Design postgraduate experience in this field, the program is delivered in close collaboration with UNSW Galleries and a broad range of Australian and international industry partners, giving students genuine professional networks alongside academic training. Fully online study is available, though only for domestic students not on an international student visa. It suits both people with existing backgrounds in museums, galleries, arts organisations or art practice, and career-changers entering curating or cultural leadership from other professional backgrounds, preparing graduates as independent professionals able to lead across curating, exhibition, arts policy and management contexts.

name: Master of Cyber Security (Research)
description: UNSW's Master of Cyber Security (Research) lets students contribute new knowledge within cyber security through a genuine research project, developing critical research skills and methodologies alongside original scientific insight rather than following a purely taught curriculum. The program builds the experience and expert knowledge needed to confidently approach a research career in cyber security, distinguishing it from taught cyber security master's degrees focused on applied professional skills. It suits computer science, engineering or related graduates with a genuine cyber security research question who want a formal research credential, often as a pathway toward a PhD or a specialised research role in security research institutions, government cyber agencies, or industry security research and development teams, rather than students seeking a taught professional cyber security qualification.
admission_requirements: (1) A candidate for the degree shall have been awarded at a standard not below Honours Class 2 an appropriate degree of Bachelor from The University of New South Wales or a qualification considered equivalent from another university or tertiary institution. (2) In exceptional cases an applicant who submits evidence of such other academic and/or professional qualifications as may be approved by the Committee may be permitted to enrol for the degree. (3) If the Committee is not satisfied with the qualifications submitted by an applicant the Committee may require the applicant, before being permitted to enrol, to undergo such examination or carry out such work as the Committee may prescribe. name: Master of Data Science and Decisions
description: UNSW's Master of Data Science and Decisions trains current and future data scientists and analysts to meet strong workforce demand, building broad, advanced knowledge across mathematics and statistics, computer science, and economics before students specialise more deeply in one of four available areas. Two pathways accommodate different statistics backgrounds: Option 1 covers foundational probability and statistical theory for students with limited prior exposure, while Option 2 assumes existing knowledge of probability, hypothesis testing and estimation methods, letting students skip straight to more advanced coursework. Research and communication skills are developed through genuine project work rather than only classroom instruction, reflecting how data science actually gets applied in industry settings. It suits graduates from any quantitative background who want genuinely interdisciplinary data science training, with the flexible statistics pathway accommodating both newcomers to formal statistical theory and those who've already studied it.

name: Master of Design
description: UNSW's Master of Design combines core design studio and contextual courses, covering critical approaches to design, sustainable practice, entrepreneurship and design research methods, with electives letting students specialise in Communication Design, Design Leadership, Immersive Design, Interaction and UX Design, Materials and Object Design, or Spatial and Experience Design. The industry-engaged, intellectually rigorous program develops both the creative skills and strategic thinking needed to lead in design, rather than focusing purely on technical execution within one narrow discipline. Because students choose their elective specialisation, the degree can lean toward digital product design, physical object design, spatial design or design leadership depending on individual career goals. It suits design graduates or professionals who want genuine specialisation choice alongside rigorous contextual and critical design theory, positioning graduates for design leadership roles across a range of industries rather than one narrow design niche.

name: Master of Development Studies
description: UNSW's Master of Development Studies builds theoretical knowledge and practical skills to analyse and address major global development challenges, grounded in participatory, rights-based and community-centred approaches that draw on the expertise of local communities rather than imposing external solutions. Students build critical understanding of forced migration, gender-based violence, human rights, global health, disaster justice, food insecurity, environmental governance and climate change, taught by academics with genuine practical development experience locally and internationally. The program develops transferable skills in critical analysis, policy formulation and advocacy, preparing students to engage meaningfully with affected communities at local, national and global levels while accessing development industry networks. It suits students who want to work in international development, humanitarian response, or policy roles addressing global inequality, rather than a purely academic study of development theory.

name: Master of Economics
description: UNSW's Master of Economics is a specialist program providing advanced theoretical and applied training across modern economics and econometrics, building in-depth knowledge of current thinking in microeconomics, macroeconomics and econometric methods. Unlike the broader Master of Applied Economics, this program leans more theoretically rigorous, suiting students who want deep economic theory training rather than a more practically oriented economics qualification. It suits economics or related quantitative graduates who want genuinely advanced economic theory and econometric technique, positioning graduates for roles in economic research, policy analysis, financial institutions or further doctoral study in economics. The specialist framing distinguishes it from generalist business or commerce postgraduate degrees that touch on economics as one component among several.

name: Master of Education
description: UNSW's Master of Education deepens working education professionals' understanding of teaching, learning and educational systems through genuine engagement with educational theory, research and practice, building the capacity to critically analyse educational issues and reflect on professional practice across varied contexts. The program supports not just classroom teachers but curriculum specialists, educational leaders, policymakers and learning support professionals, with flexible specialisations and electives letting students tailor their studies to their specific professional context. It's important to note this program doesn't provide teaching accreditation for NSW or Australian schools; students seeking that qualification should look at the Bachelor of Education or Master of Teaching programs instead, and fully online study isn't available to international students on a student visa. It suits practising education professionals who want deeper theoretical and research grounding to complement existing teaching or education experience.

name: Master of Health Professions Education (Research)
description: UNSW's Master of Health Professions Education (Research) is designed for teachers and educational administrators working within the health professions who want to build genuine research skills, requiring an original investigation under supervision for a minimum of three academic sessions full-time or four sessions part-time or external, culminating in a thesis. Candidates can enrol as internal students at a campus or teaching hospital, or as external students spending a minimum of 14 weeks in the School during the program, with external research work requiring a co-supervisor at the host institution where necessary. Because the degree is entirely research-driven, the specific health education research question depends on the individual candidate's interests and available supervision. It suits health professions educators with a genuine research question about how health professionals are taught and trained, who want a formal research credential rather than a taught postgraduate education qualification.

name: Master of International Relations
description: UNSW's Master of International Relations builds a strong theoretical and practical understanding of contemporary world politics, introducing the major theoretical traditions used to explain state behaviour and international actors before applying them to real issues like the conduct of war, the pursuit of international security, global economics and environment, international law and diplomacy, and human rights. Students examine current concerns including regional conflicts, great power rivalry, economic uncertainty, environmental threats, humanitarian crises and terrorism, extending existing knowledge with advanced research and analytical thinking skills. It suits graduates and professionals aiming for careers in diplomacy, international organisations, government foreign policy roles, think tanks or international NGOs, as well as those who want deeper theoretical grounding in world politics to complement an existing career touching international affairs.

The program covers legal, medical, business, community and conference interpreting specialisations, taught by leading researchers and practitioners and complemented by real professional practice experience. Beyond interpreting-specific skills, students build oral comprehension, public speaking, discourse analysis and project management capabilities relevant across professional interpreting settings. Language combinations, offered subject to demand, span Chinese (Mandarin and Cantonese), French, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Serbian, Spanish and Turkish, with fully online study available only to domestic students not on an international student visa.

name: Master of Journalism and Communication
description: UNSW's Master of Journalism and Communication builds a professionally relevant and academically rigorous portfolio of media practice skills spanning print, radio, television, online media, media relations and corporate communication, grounded in interdisciplinary understanding of the social, economic and political role of media locally and internationally. Students develop critical thinking and research skills for ethical, reflective media practice, drawing on international journalism and communication scholarship, and can choose either research or practice pathways at the advanced disciplinary level depending on career direction. Community engagement is built into both coursework and assessment, with some tasks involving genuine cooperative partnerships with NGOs and industry organisations. It suits graduates and working professionals who want comprehensive journalism and communication training with real emphasis on the research-practice connection, positioning them for careers across journalism, corporate communication and media production.

name: Master of Landscape Architecture
description: UNSW's Master of Landscape Architecture uses the Sydney region as its landscape laboratory, building research-informed design skills for equitable, adaptive and sustainable urban and regional environments through a core sequence of design studios, each paired with a supporting skills or knowledge course. Students' design process is grounded in research and critical analysis of real landscape sites and systems, tested through modelling and dialogue rather than developed in the abstract, with electives available in specialised interdisciplinary areas including urban design and city analytics. The program culminates in a final-year capstone studio sequence where students undertake an independent, research-based design project. It suits design graduates who want landscape architecture training grounded in genuine research methodology and real site analysis, encouraged throughout to connect global landscape issues to local, Sydney-based design practice.

name: Master of Laws
description: UNSW's Master of Laws by Coursework lets graduates expand and deepen their legal expertise through a flexible structure that tailors the degree to each student's personal interests, emphasising a genuine mix of domestic, international and comparative legal perspectives. Students select eight courses from a wide range taught within and outside the Faculty of Law and Justice, building expert legal knowledge alongside genuine legal and research skills, delivered in a range of formats spanning term-length and intensive courses, primarily face-to-face with online and hybrid options available. Course availability varies year to year depending on student interest and teacher availability, so not every course runs annually. It suits practising lawyers wanting to specialise further in a particular area of law, as well as law graduates from other jurisdictions wanting genuine exposure to Australian and comparative legal perspectives.

name: Master of Marine Science and Management
description: UNSW's Master of Marine Science and Management is a joint program with three Sydney Institute of Marine Science partner universities, covering coastal management and engineering, climate change, marine ecology and conservation, physical oceanography and modelling in a genuinely interdisciplinary structure. Running 12 to 18 months full-time depending on recognition of prior learning, students can complete the program in a shorter 48-credit-point format if they hold a relevant Bachelor of Science (Honours) or equivalent industry experience. A compulsory course delivered at SIMS in Chowder Bay uses real data streams from the Integrated Marine Observing System, and students can complete up to two courses at partner universities, giving genuine cross-institutional exposure. It suits science graduates or industry professionals who want combined marine science and management training, positioning graduates for careers in coastal management, marine conservation, fisheries management or ocean policy roles.

name: Master of Materials Technology
description: UNSW's Master of Materials Technology offers the widest selection of postgraduate materials science and engineering courses in Australia, built for graduates in chemical or physical sciences, engineering or related fields who want deeper understanding of the microstructure-property-performance relationship across major material classes and how they're transformed into eco-friendly products through sustainable manufacturing. The flexible curriculum runs one to two years full-time depending on prior study, normally 96 credit points over two years, though recognition of prior learning in materials science can shorten it to 18 months or one year. The program aims to produce socially aware graduates equipped for careers in materials science and engineering broadly, rather than narrowly training for one specific materials application. It suits both recent science and engineering graduates and working professionals who want to deepen materials expertise, with the flexible duration accommodating candidates at different starting points.

name: Master of Medicine - research
description: UNSW's Master of Medicine (Research) is the Faculty of Medicine's main postgraduate research degree, requiring candidates to submit a thesis based on original investigation under the direction of a UNSW-appointed supervisor. Candidates can enrol full-time, part-time, or as external students working at an affiliated teaching hospital or research facility, with annual progress reviews by the faculty's Higher Degree Committee and the possibility of a co-supervisor at an external institution where research is based outside UNSW itself. Because the degree is entirely research-driven, the specific medical field and research question depend on the individual candidate's interests and available supervision, spanning the full breadth of medical research the Faculty of Medicine supports. It suits medical or science graduates with a genuine research question who want a formal research credential, often as a pathway toward a PhD or a specialised medical research career, rather than students seeking a taught postgraduate medical qualification.
curriculum: Students must complete 96 UOC when taken as a standalone program.
admission_requirements: A candidate for the degree shall have been awarded an appropriate degree of Bachelor from the University of New South Wales or a qualification considered equivalent from another university or tertiary institution at a level acceptable to the Committee. An applicant who submits evidence of such other academic or professional attainments as may be approved by the Committee may be permitted to enroll for the degree. When the Committee is not satisfied with the qualifications submitted by an applicant the Committee may require the applicant, before being permitted to enroll, to undergo such examination or carry out such work as the Committee may prescribe. For further information, see the Admission to Higher Degree Research Programs Procedure .

name: Master of Mining Engineering
description: UNSW's Master of Mining Engineering combines theoretical knowledge and practical industry experience across 72 credit points of core courses, prescribed electives and a research project, built for people already working in mining or planning to enter the field. Many courses run in modular block format, face-to-face or online, specifically designed so working mining professionals can attend without interrupting their employment, though some electives are only offered every two years and international students on a student visa can complete only a third of the program online. The program covers the full breadth of mining engineering practice while building research skills that prepare graduates for leadership roles in the sector. It suits mining professionals wanting a comprehensive, industry-relevant postgraduate qualification that accommodates continued full-time work, as well as career-changers with a related technical background moving into mining engineering specifically.

name: Master of Philosophy - Engineering
description: UNSW's Master of Philosophy in Engineering is a research degree combining an original research thesis with a coursework component of three courses (18 units of credit), including a research methods course and two advanced disciplinary knowledge courses, completed within the first four terms of enrolment. The thesis component requires original investigation, design or engineering development work, giving students genuine research training that goes beyond a purely coursework-based engineering master's while still including structured coursework support. It suits engineering graduates who want a taste of independent research and thesis writing without committing to a full PhD, either as a standalone research credential or as a stepping stone toward doctoral study. Because it's research-focused, the specific engineering discipline and project depend entirely on the individual student's interests and available supervision, with one advanced disciplinary course able to be substituted for a standard disciplinary course with Program Authority approval.

name: Master of Philosophy Arts and Social Sciences
description: UNSW's Master of Philosophy in Arts and Social Sciences offers interdisciplinary research training built for twenty-first-century researchers and leaders, combining three compulsory courses, a common foundational course, a specialisation-specific course and a discipline-specific course, with a 25,000-word research thesis supervised by academic experts. Rather than following traditional academic majors, the specialisations align closely with the faculty's actual research strengths, staff expertise and the employment market, giving students a genuinely current grounding in contemporary problems from cross-disciplinary perspectives. It particularly suits people with an undergraduate degree who want to return from the workforce and develop research skills, with successful completion potentially qualifying graduates for doctoral-level research admission. It works well for career-changers moving into research-oriented roles as well as those testing whether doctoral study suits them before committing to a full PhD.

name: Master of Physical Oceanography
description: UNSW's Master of Physical Oceanography gives science, engineering and related graduates advanced training in the theory and physical processes of the ocean, equipping them with skills demanded by employers in Australia's growing Blue Economy and forming the largest program in an articulated suite of nested Physical Oceanography qualifications at UNSW. Beyond coursework reflecting current oceanography practice, students complete a major research project bringing together coursework knowledge and extending their investigative skills, developing quantitative, computational and technical capabilities applied to real industry problems. The program provides a genuine foundation for students wishing to continue to PhD level. It suits science and engineering graduates aiming for careers in marine industries, oceanographic research, environmental consulting or government agencies working on ocean and coastal issues, wanting deeper training than the Graduate Diploma provides.

name: Master of Population Health (Research)
description: UNSW's Master of Population Health (Research) recognises successful, original research contributing significantly to knowledge in an approved population health area, with the thesis normally submitted within two years of full-time equivalent study. Candidates typically work at a UNSW campus, teaching hospital or affiliated research facility under a Committee-appointed supervisor, though periods working elsewhere can be approved where genuinely necessary to the research program. Because the degree is entirely research-driven, the specific population health topic and methodology depend on the individual candidate's research question and available supervision, rather than following a set taught curriculum. It suits population health graduates or professionals with a genuine research question they want to pursue, often as a pathway toward further research study or a specialised research role in public health policy, epidemiology or health services research.

It suits psychology honours graduates who want registration as a clinical psychologist through a program with a genuinely evidence-based, empirically grounded approach to clinical training, distinguishing it from clinical psychology programs with a different theoretical orientation. The program's decades-long track record gives it an established reputation within Australian clinical psychology training.

name: Master of Public Health (Extension)/Infectious Diseases Intelligence
description: UNSW's dual Master of Public Health (Extension) and Master of Infectious Diseases Intelligence is a two-year program combining broad public health training in epidemiology, biostatistics, health promotion and policy with specialised infectious disease surveillance, outbreak investigation and mitigation skills. The Public Health Extension component adds research methodology and an advanced research project on top of standard public health coursework, while the infectious diseases component builds specific expertise in controlling disease spread across populations, requiring a genuinely multisectoral understanding given the ongoing threat of emerging disease outbreaks. Graduates typically work in government, military and first-responder organisations, primary care and community health services in Australia and internationally. It suits public health professionals who want combined depth in both research methodology and infectious disease response specifically, rather than a general public health qualification or a narrower infectious diseases-only credential.

name: Master of Taxation
description: UNSW's Master of Taxation is a specialist program for taxation professionals dealing with complex tax issues in business decisions and transactions, taught by leading tax academics with exposure to complex aspects of the discipline and critical understanding of the Australian taxation system. Three compulsory core courses and a compulsory capstone in tax policy form the backbone of the degree, with four elective courses letting students tailor the program toward personal tax and financial planning, indirect taxes, corporate and commercial tax, or international tax depending on career interests. Assessment emphasises sustained analytical writing on current problem areas, encouraging genuine contributions to professional debate on key tax issues rather than only reproducing existing knowledge. All courses are offered in online distance learning or hybrid mode, and the program can be studied full-time or part-time, suiting working tax professionals who need flexible delivery around existing employment.

name: Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management
description: The Advanced Diploma of Hospitality Management (SIT60322) at Victoria University TAFE qualifies graduates for senior management positions in the hospitality industry. Students learn and apply skills in VU's fully equipped hospitality training centre under industry experts, developing advanced skills in hospitality operations and leadership including human resource management, financial management, marketing strategies and business planning. Students also learn to manage hotel front office operations, including creating reservations, managing accounts and check-out. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Associate Degree in Hospitality and Hotel Management
description: The Associate Degree in Hospitality and Hotel Management at Victoria University develops management and leadership capabilities to improve prospects of securing a senior position in the industry. Students build business management potential, gain hands-on experience in VU's hospitality training centre, and develop an understanding of industry trends and issues, learning from teachers directly involved in the industry. Skills developed include hotel operations management, food, wine and catering operations, accounting principles for management, marketing and business communications, contracts, risk and business law, resort management, and rooms division management. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Accounting
description: The Bachelor of Accounting at Victoria University produces career-ready graduates with technical and professional skills and a strong knowledge of global trends in accounting. Based at VU's City Tower in the Melbourne CBD, students develop the skills to qualify for accreditation with CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand. The degree develops the ability to execute case studies and business plans, complete evidence-based projects with real clients, and adapt cross-disciplinary knowledge in accounting, data analytics and finance, along with professional skills in critical thinking, problem solving, teamwork and communication.

name: Bachelor of Applied Music
description: The Bachelor of Applied Music at Victoria University blends creativity with real-world application, preparing students for careers in music teaching, production, performance, mixed-media arts and community projects, and setting them up for further study in music education, music therapy, community development, youth work and social work. The course focuses on four interconnected areas: music teaching, creative digital music production including video, streaming and AI music, music for life and music for change covering wellbeing and social change, and performance skills. It explores the power of music to support emotional, cultural and social wellbeing and to engage with Indigenous and social-justice issues. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Architectural Design
description: The Bachelor of Architectural Design at Victoria University focuses on sustainable building design that responds to community needs, incorporating circular-economy ideas such as reusing, repurposing, refurbishing, recycling and repairing to reduce waste. Students apply these methods to real projects, visiting sites, taking measurements and collaborating with local communities, and participate in design studio classes focused on real-world challenges in architecture and construction. Graduates have the skills to work as building designers in government and private planning and construction sectors, and can continue into a Master of Architecture to become a registered architect. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description: The Bachelor of Arts at Victoria University offers broad flexibility, letting students choose their area of focus based on their interests and career goals. After a first-year introduction to the humanities, students study one or two majors from communication studies, digital media, history, literary studies, psychology, sociology, visual art and writing, and can choose from 14 minors including Aboriginal Yulendj (Knowledge) and Community. The degree develops sought-after employability skills such as communication, problem solving, teamwork and analytical thinking. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical and Exercise Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical and Exercise Science at Victoria University is a dual-disciplinary degree that integrates biomedical science and exercise science in the contexts of physical activity, sport and health research. Students study the fundamentals of anatomy and physiology, pathophysiology, biochemistry, biomechanics, kinesiology and psychology, and how the structure and function of the body are influenced by exercise and impacted by disease. They apply theoretical knowledge in practical and clinical scenarios and develop research skills through active participation in research teams, using VU's medical research facilities at Sunshine Hospital. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Biomedical Science
description: The Bachelor of Biomedical Science at Victoria University develops a strong foundation in the medical sciences and advanced laboratory skills, preparing graduates for careers in biomedical research or entry into postgraduate health courses. Combining hands-on experimentation with interactive online learning, students gain in-depth knowledge of how the human body works, covering physiology, anatomy and cell biology and the causes, diagnosis and treatment of disease at molecular, cellular and system levels. Study areas include anatomy and physiology, nutrition, biochemistry, cell biology, medical microbiology, immunology, molecular biology, human genetics and pharmacology. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.
curriculum: Biological Systems (HBM1002, 12CP), Mathematics and Statistics for Biomedicine (HHH1001, 12CP), Functional Anatomy of the Trunk (RBM1100, 12CP), Functional Anatomy of the Limbs (RBM1200, 12CP), Human Physiology 1 (RBM1518, 12CP), Human Physiology 2 (RBM1528, 12CP), Chemistry 1A (RCS1601, 12CP), Chemistry 1B (RCS1602, 12CP)

A study score of 20 of one of the following: Biology, Chemistry, Health and Human Development, any Mathematics or Physical Education. OR:. Completion of an Australian Advanced Diploma or Diploma (or equivalent). PLUS:. IELTS (or equivalent): Overall score or 6.0 (with no band less than 6.0 in Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking). OR:. Completion of a Foundation course or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS (or equivalent): Overall score or 6.0 (with no band less than 6.0 in Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking). OR:. Completion of a Foundation course or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Biomedicine
description: The Bachelor of Biomedicine at Victoria University provides a strong foundation for a career in medicine or allied health and prepares students for entry into postgraduate medicine and courses such as physiotherapy, pharmacy and dietetics, including essential physiology, anatomy and biochemistry prerequisites. The course has a particular focus on the role of exercise and nutrition in medicine, and students design and analyse research methods and undertake a research project that can be a platform for a research degree. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Building Surveying
description: The Bachelor of Building Surveying at Victoria University is the only degree of its kind in Victoria and prepares students for roles improving the safety and quality of the built environment. Study is delivered online and in real time without traditional classrooms or labs. Graduates are ready to work as registered building surveyors accredited by the Victorian Building Authority and the Australian Institute of Building Surveyors, and with three years of relevant experience can work on buildings of any size and height. Students specialise in building and construction legislation and auditing, inspection procedures, building codes and regulations, professional practice standards, building safety and fire safety, and sustainable construction techniques.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
VU's general business degree lets students pick a major (accounting, marketing, human resource management, management or international business among them) after a common first-year foundation, and like the rest of VU's undergraduate offering it's delivered block-mode, one unit over four weeks rather than a full timetable of subjects running in parallel.

The course is aimed squarely at Melbourne's west: a large share of VU's business students are first-in-family university attendees or came through pathway diplomas, and the degree includes built-in study support and a Professional Year option that matters to the substantial number of international students in the cohort chasing skilled migration points after graduation. There's also a work-integrated learning unit in most majors, connecting students with local employers rather than leaving placement entirely up to students to arrange.

It's not a prestige-brand business degree in the way a Melbourne or Monash commerce degree might be, and VU doesn't pretend otherwise: its pitch is accessibility and a direct line into local industry rather than an elite cohort experience.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Business, Economic Principles, Marketing Fundamentals, Business Communication
Year 2: Business Law, Quantitative Methods, Major units begin (Accounting, Marketing, HRM, Management, or International Business), Work-Integrated Learning unit
Year 3: Advanced major units, Strategic Management, Business Capstone Project
admission_requirements: ATAR 55 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Community Development
description: The Bachelor of Community Development at Victoria University gives students the skills and knowledge for roles in local community development, with units focused on practical skills to become an effective community worker and an advocate for change. Students benefit from extensive placements in community development organisations, with opportunities to travel overseas, and from university partnerships that enable study abroad and help build capacity to work in diverse communities. This combination of knowledge and practical experience prepares graduates for a rewarding and ethical career. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours)
description: The Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours) at Victoria University prepares graduates to take a leading role in large-scale building and civil-engineering projects, managing residential, commercial and industrial construction from design through development, construction and operation. Students gain skills in planning and managing the construction process, assessing documents for compliance with codes and standards, assessing plans for constructability, communicating with architects and engineers, formulating project cashflows and budgets, preparing tender documents and contracts, and supervising sites and personnel. Students can add a minor in building compliance or quantity surveying. The degree is closely connected to industry and offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Criminal Justice
description: The Bachelor of Criminal Justice at Victoria University equips students with the knowledge, skills and hands-on experience to make an impact on community safety and social justice. Students examine how crime, law and inequality intersect, including the role of mental health, trauma, substance use, poverty and systemic disadvantage, and study criminal justice theories, human rights and ethical frameworks, exploring how policing, courts and prisons operate and how policy, practice and reform can shape fairer outcomes. In the final year, students complete an industry placement preparing them for careers in law enforcement, corrections, courts and legal services, youth justice, and community support. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Criminal Justice and Psychological Studies
description: The Bachelor of Criminal Justice and Psychological Studies at Victoria University combines a deep understanding of criminal behaviour with study of the systems that respond to it. Students examine the social, political and psychological factors that shape behaviour, including trauma, inequality and mental health, while developing knowledge in counselling theory, family dynamics, research and ethics. This interdisciplinary course prepares graduates for work across justice, welfare and community sectors, including victim support and advocacy, child protection and family services, corrections and rehabilitation, mental health and wellbeing, and policy development. In the final year students complete an industry placement. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description: The Bachelor of Criminology at Victoria University develops the knowledge and practical skills to critically examine crime, justice and the operation of the criminal justice system. Students explore why people commit crime by examining social, political, cultural, psychological and economic factors, and through practical learning and real-world case studies gain experience identifying crime-related problems and developing evidence-based policy reform recommendations. Specialist subjects include crime and inequality, policing and offending, victimology, digital criminology, transnational and international crime, early intervention and crime prevention, corporate crime, environmental crime, and justice policy and reform. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Cyber Security
description: The Bachelor of Cyber Security at Victoria University builds in-demand skills to protect data and information systems. Students first study information technology, preparing for careers in software development or networking, then focus on specialised cyber security units. They learn cyber-threat detection and risk management, cyber security technologies such as digital signatures, public key infrastructure, VPNs, firewalls, intrusion detection and encryption, ethical hacking and digital forensics, vulnerability analysis and control, enterprise security, and cyber security regulation, policy and law, along with software development and network design. The degree is internationally recognised. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Data Science
description: The Bachelor of Data Science at Victoria University teaches students to identify, organise and analyse big data using specialised computational and statistical techniques to generate insights for complex problems. With industry-focused practices, real-world datasets and hands-on tools, students build an in-depth understanding of deep learning, data management, data mining and decision making, and learn to wrangle, analyse, visualise and predict from data. Targeted expertise includes machine learning, deep learning, big data management, data mining, predictive and prescriptive analysis, data visualisation, and business- and cyber security-oriented data analytics. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Dermal Sciences
description: The Bachelor of Dermal Sciences at Victoria University qualifies graduates for a career performing evidence-based skin treatments in the growing dermal therapies industry. Students get hands-on experience in VU's Dermal Clinic at the City Campus in Melbourne, learning under expert dermal clinicians to safely perform laser and light-based treatments, resurfacing procedures and lymphatic procedures. Designed with industry and the Australian Society of Dermal Clinicians, the degree is the only one of its kind in Australia and provides comprehensive knowledge across all areas of dermal science.

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education
description: The Bachelor of Early Childhood Education at Victoria University prepares students to become in-demand early childhood teachers, with strong projected job growth in the sector and Victorian Government scholarships and incentives available. The degree prepares graduates for a career nurturing the development and wellbeing of children from birth to five years, teaching students to support young children's foundations for success, involve families as contributors to learning, and support effective transitions to school. Students build a strong sense of social justice and ethical, inclusive teaching practice. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Early Childhood Education and Leadership
description: The Bachelor of Early Childhood Education and Leadership at Victoria University is the only course of its kind that dedicates four years of study to early childhood education with a focus on leadership, setting graduates up for advanced career opportunities. Students prepare for a career nurturing the development and wellbeing of children from birth to five years, learning to support young children's foundations for success, involve families as contributors to learning, and support transitions to school, while developing leadership capability, an understanding of child development, and ethical professional teaching practice that includes Indigenous perspectives. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood and Primary)
description:
This is a dual-qualification degree: graduates come out eligible for registration to teach both early childhood settings and primary school classrooms, which broadens job options in a way a single-sector teaching degree doesn't. VU runs the course through its College of Sport, Health, Engineering (education sits within VU's broader teaching college structure) with mandatory professional experience placements spread across multiple year levels rather than backloaded into the final year.

Students complete placements in both long day care/kindergarten settings and primary classrooms, which means the practical component runs longer in total than a primary-only degree, offset by the broader employment scope it opens up afterward. VU has increasingly focused its teaching pathways on the acute teacher shortages in Melbourne's growth corridors to the west, and a fair number of placement partnerships sit in those newer school communities rather than established inner-city schools.

Coursework covers child development, literacy and numeracy pedagogy, curriculum planning, and inclusive education, with a research or capstone project in the final year addressing a self-chosen classroom practice question.
curriculum:
Year 1: Child Development, Introduction to Early Childhood Education, Literacy Foundations, Numeracy Foundations
Year 2: Curriculum and Pedagogy (Early Childhood), Curriculum and Pedagogy (Primary), Professional Experience Placement 1
Year 3: Inclusive Education, Assessment and Reporting, Professional Experience Placement 2
Year 4: Professional Experience Placement 3 (extended), Research Project in Teaching Practice, Professional Studies Capstone
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent, Working with Children Check required
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0)

name: Bachelor of Education Studies
description: The Bachelor of Education Studies at Victoria University develops the skills to lead learning programs outside the traditional classroom and is also an alternative path into teaching. Graduates can work in mentoring and tutoring programs, community programs, public and welfare services, after-school care and teacher aide positions. Students can steer their career toward an area of interest with a major or minor in options including physical education, arts, community, English and teaching English as an additional language, humanities, ICT, maths, outdoor education and science. This course does not provide the prerequisites for teacher registration. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description:
Engineering at VU runs on problem-based learning rather than the standard lecture-then-lab format: students in the College of Engineering and Science are handed open-ended engineering problems from early in the course and work through them in teams, with staff acting more as facilitators than lecturers delivering content. It's accredited by Engineers Australia across its specialisations (civil, mechanical, electrical and electronic, and architectural engineering are the usual streams), so graduates come out eligible for graduate membership straight away.

The four-year honours degree includes a substantial industry placement component, and VU's location in Melbourne's west, close to manufacturing, construction and infrastructure projects rather than the CBD, shapes a lot of the applied project work students get assigned. It's a smaller, less internationally ranked engineering school than the sandstone universities, but the trade-off VU offers is smaller class sizes in the specialist years and a teaching style built around solving real problems rather than sitting exams on theory alone.

Students choose their specialisation after a shared first year of core mathematics, physics and engineering fundamentals, then move into discipline-specific design and project units.
curriculum:
Year 1: Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Physics, Introduction to Engineering Design, Engineering Mechanics
Year 2: Specialisation core units begin (Civil, Mechanical, Electrical and Electronic, or Architectural Engineering), Materials Science, Thermodynamics or Structures
Year 3: Advanced specialisation units, Industry Placement, Engineering Project Management
Year 4: Capstone Engineering Design Project (Honours thesis-equivalent), Professional Practice, Advanced electives
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science
description: The Bachelor of Exercise and Sport Science at Victoria University is a hands-on, science-based degree that equips students to support health and wellbeing, enhance athletic performance, and prevent or manage injury and chronic conditions. Students gain experience working with diverse populations and can tailor their studies toward clinical health or sport performance. Through classroom learning, laboratory work and industry placements, students explore movement and performance screening, exercise prescription and delivery, injury prevention and rehabilitation, and coaching for skill development. Accreditation pathways and industry connections prepare graduates for careers in exercise science, fitness and health promotion. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

name: Bachelor of Health Science
description: The Bachelor of Health Science at Victoria University focuses on improving the health of populations and prepares students for a range of health and science careers. Through VU's collaborations with health institutes, universities and community organisations, students gain real-world experience and graduate ready to work on government health programs, private-practice initiatives and with NGOs. Students study core bioscience, research and public-health topics with a major in Public Health, and from second year choose areas of interest, graduating with expertise in disease and injury prevention, health research, health promotion and epidemiology. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.

OR:. Completion of a Foundation course or equivalent.
english_requirements: IELTS (or equivalent): Overall score or 6.0 (with no band less than 6.0 in Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking). OR:. Completion of a Foundation course or equivalent.

name: Bachelor of Human Nutrition
description: The Bachelor of Human Nutrition at Victoria University gives students a solid foundation in nutrition, food and related science subjects, beginning with eight core units before progressing to targeted study. In the second and third years, students choose a specialisation from Biomedical Nutrition, Public Health Nutrition, or Exercise and Nutrition, broadening their learning and employment opportunities in the community nutrition and public health sector or as preparation for postgraduate study. It is offered at VU in Melbourne.
