name: Bachelor of Architectural Design
description: Design the spaces where people live, work and connect Great architecture shapes the way we experience the world. From sustainable homes and vibrant public spaces to iconic buildings and thriving communities, architects combine creativity, technology and critical thinking to design places that improve how we live. Every project begins with an idea-and the ability to transform that idea into a space that inspires people. Western's Bachelor of Architectural Design combines studio-based learning with hands-on making, digital technologies and real-world industry experience to prepare you for a career in architecture and the built environment. You'll explore architectural design, spatial thinking, digital modelling, construction technology, history and theory while developing the creative and technical skills used by contemporary architects. The program includes opportunities for internships and work-integrated learning, and provides a pathway to the Master of Architecture (Urban Transformation) for students pursuing registration as an architect. Graduate with a professional portfolio that demonstrates your creativity, technical capability and ability to design spaces that respond to the challenges of tomorrow.
curriculum: accredited by the NSW Architects Registration Board and currently appears on the list of Accredited Architecture Qualifications published by the Architects Accreditation Council of Australia. Students who complete the Master of Architecture (Urban Transformation) will be eligible to become registered architects after undertaking relevant practical experience and successfully completing the Architectural Practice Examination.

name: Bachelor of Arts
description: Work. Travel. Learn. We've redesigned the Bachelor of Arts so you can get the most out of this program. Step outside the classroom and get real world experience with an internship. Travel overseas and get credit towards your degree with a study abroad program. Find a meaningful community service project. At Western, you're not just learning how to make a difference in the world. You're doing it. Our new delivery mode combines traditional classroom learning with 24-hour access to program materials online. This gives you greater flexibility and more time to discuss ideas and collaborate in class. Depending on your major, there are opportunities for practical experience and international placements. We've also got facilities like our own recording studio, multimedia labs and digital suites. Effective communication and critical thinking skills are valued in all industries. That's why there are so many career pathways in this program. Communication and media, education, psychology, social policy, writing and publishing are just some of the career opportunities our graduates pursue.

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business at Western Sydney University is built around a broad first year of shared foundation subjects before students commit to a major. Accounting, finance, marketing, management, international business, and a few others are typically on offer, with the option to combine two majors within the same degree rather than being locked into one professional identity from day one.

WSU's School of Business runs primarily out of Parramatta City campus, in the heart of what's increasingly called Sydney's "second CBD," and the course leans on that location for placement and internship partnerships with the growing corporate and government presence that's moved into Parramatta over the last decade (several state government departments have relocated headquarters there, along with a number of corporate regional offices).

A work-integrated learning subject is standard in the final year, and accounting-track students need to check their specific subject combination against CPA Australia or CAANZ requirements to ensure it satisfies those professional body pathways, since the degree's flexible major system means not every combination automatically ticks every accreditation box.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Accounting Principles, Economics for Business, Marketing Principles, Management, Business Statistics
Year 2: Major subjects begin (Accounting / Finance / Marketing / Management / International Business), Business Law
Year 3: Advanced major electives, Work-Integrated Learning subject, capstone strategy subject
Majors (choose one or combine two): Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management, International Business, Human Resource Management
CPA/CAANZ accreditation pathway available depending on major selection
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Business Analytics and AI Management
description: Bachelor of Business Analytics and AI Management This inter-disciplinary course brings together advanced applied analytics capabilities and AI fluency with business professional competencies. The curriculum builds business fluency with contemporary generative AI and machine learning tools. Learning at the intersection of technology and social purpose, students gain skills to optimise organisational performance safely, critically, and responsibly. Through industry relevant, technology-enabled learning, students will excel at identifying, extracting, and visually modelling complex data and creating actionable executive insights. Graduates emerge uniquely prepared to lead data driven innovation and problem-solving, translate advanced data analytics and AI outputs into sustainable organisational performance, and step directly into a broad range of emerging roles. This course is delivered by Western Sydney University.
curriculum: The curriculum builds business fluency with contemporary generative AI and machine learning tools. Learning at the intersection of technology and social purpose, students gain skills to optimise organisational performance safely, critically, and responsibly.

name: Bachelor of Clinical Science (Medicine) (Exit Only)
description: The Bachelor of Clinical Science (Medicine) at Western Sydney University is a three-year qualification offered as an exit award within the five-year Bachelor of Clinical Science (Medicine) and Doctor of Medicine program, an undergraduate-entry pathway to becoming a medical intern in Australia and New Zealand. The parent program is taught through purpose-built clinical schools with access to research facilities. Graduates use the exit award as a science degree or as credit toward completing the combined program. Indicative international tuition is around 85,500 Australian dollars per year. The course holds CRICOS registration 097592B.

name: Bachelor of Communication
description:
WSU's Bachelor of Communication covers journalism, public relations, and digital/social media as its main specialisation streams, taught with a practical, portfolio-building emphasis rather than a purely theoretical media studies approach. The program's Sydney-wide industry placements pull from both metropolitan mastheads and broadcasters and Western Sydney's own growing local and community media outlets, giving students exposure to a genuinely different regional media landscape alongside the standard capital-city options.

The course includes media law and ethics, writing and content production, and research methods subjects across the early years, before students specialise and undertake a work-integrated learning placement in their final year. WSU has also built out digital content and social media production facilities across its campuses in recent years, reflecting the shift in graduate employment away from traditional broadcast roles toward digital-first content and communications work.

Graduates commonly move into journalism, public relations, corporate and government communications, or digital marketing roles across both Sydney metropolitan employers and organisations based in the growing Western Sydney business corridor.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Introduction to Communication and Media, Writing for Media, Media Law and Ethics, Media Research Methods
Year 2: stream selection (Journalism / Public Relations / Digital and Social Media), Content Strategy, Media Industries
Year 3: Advanced stream subjects, Work-Integrated Learning placement, capstone portfolio or campaign project
Streams: Journalism, Public Relations, Digital and Social Media
Capstone: industry placement-linked portfolio or campaign project
admission_requirements: ATAR 60 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Computer Science
description:
WSU's Bachelor of Computer Science covers the expected core sequence (programming, data structures, algorithms, systems and databases), with the option to specialise later in areas like software engineering, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity or networking. The degree is taught primarily out of the Kingswood and Parramatta campuses, and WSU has invested in growing its cybersecurity and cyber-physical systems research groups over recent years, which flows down into some of the specialisation electives available to undergraduates.

The university draws a large proportion of its student cohort from Greater Western Sydney itself, meaning many computer science students are first-in-family university attendees, and WSU's course design leans on strong first-year academic support (peer mentoring, transition subjects) to account for that rather than assuming a cohort that arrived with strong prior computing exposure.

A final-year capstone or industry project subject gives students a portfolio piece for graduate job applications, and placement partnerships lean on Western Sydney's logistics, health, and government-services employers as much as CBD tech firms.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time
Year 1: Introduction to Programming, Discrete Mathematics, Computer Systems Fundamentals, Web Technologies
Year 2: Data Structures and Algorithms, Database Systems, Software Engineering Principles, Networks
Year 3: Specialisation electives (Artificial Intelligence / Cybersecurity / Software Engineering / Networking), Capstone Project
Capstone: industry or research-based final-year project
Electives available across cross-disciplinary computing subjects
admission_requirements: ATAR 65 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours)
description: Bachelor of Construction Management at Western Western's Bachelor of Construction Management (Honours) prepares you for a career in the building industry. Along with the full suite of theory and practical knowledge that enables you to develop a broad-based view of how the construction industry operates, you will gain a strong understanding of construction technology, construction economics, construction law, and construction project management through this degree. You can also opt to specialise either in quantity surveying, building or building surveying by undertaking relevant suite of electives under each specialisation pathway. Construction Management at Western offers students a future-focused learning experience. With Western Sydney as one of the fastest-growing economic regions in Australia, students are uniquely positioned to take advantage of opportunities to learn and gain practical experience in an expanding construction landscape where skills demand is booming. Programs are shaped in collaboration with industry, ensuring graduates are job-ready with the skills employers need. With 1,200 hours of industry-based experience required before graduating, the program is offered with flexible and condensed timetables to enable you to undertake industry cadetships and other work-integrated learning activities.

name: Bachelor of Creative Leadership
description: Bachelor of Creative Leadership The Bachelor of Creative Leadership (BCL) provides transformative educational experience, internships, student-led projects, and community engagement opportunities that will expand your ability to examine and influence current and future paradigms. You will emerge with a sound balance of theory, practical experiences, and leadership skillsets - so you can take your career further than you ever thought possible. Are you ready to enter the industry with refined critical thinking and high level leadership qualities? Are you ready to create an impact through your leadership skills? In the BCL, you will engage with innovative assessments that prepare you for work-related challenges and gain experience by participating in a diverse range of real-world opportunities. Students learn to articulate their ideas into innovative strategies that address complex contemporary and future challenges. The skills learned in the BCL are transferable to any discipline and are what the employer of tomorrow will be seeking in a graduate in various roles including global workplaces. You will have an opportunity to apply skills and knowledge gained from this degree in a workplace setting, through an internship or an engaging work-integrated learning experience. The Bachelor of Creative Leadership is a concurrent degree that is designed to be. This course is delivered by Western Sydney University.
curriculum: The Bachelor of Creative Leadership is a concurrent degree that is designed to be combined with any Bachelor degree at Western. The BCL degree consists of eight subjects that can be taken concurrently with subjects in your discipline-based degree. The subjects are designed with flexibility in-mind and delivered in intensive mode in the week prior to the commencement of Autumn and Spring sessions. This allows students to take a BCL subject in addition to the four discipline-based subjects in a semester, and/or complete BCL subjects during Summer sessions*. * Not all subjects are available during Summer sessions

name: Bachelor of Criminal and Community Justice
description: Bachelor of Criminal and Community Justice at Western The degree draws upon disciplinary areas such as Criminal Justice, Criminology, Psychology, Social Work and Welfare in order to provide a theoretical framework for those who work with offenders. This degree is a specialised degree which targets a range of central themes and issues that are paramount for those who work with victims and also offenders, both in terms of their treatment and management. As well as providing a theoretical framework, the program equips our students with the knowledge and skills to develop and evaluate practice with a view to enhancing work with offenders and victims. The Bachelor of Criminal and Community Justice can be described as an 'applied degree' insofar as the teaching within the program will link theory to practice. It is important to note that this degree does not guarantee direct employment into Corrective Services or related fields. Our academics who teach in the program have had first-hand experience working directly with offenders and victims in a variety of settings including prisons, courts and a community setting. This is reflected in some of the specialised subjects, including Assessment and Treatment of Offenders and Managing Offenders in the Community.

name: Bachelor of Criminology
description: Become a force for good Western's Bachelor of Criminology allows you to study crime and criminal justice in a conceptual and applied way, and gain an understanding of how these things affect society. It gives you the skills and knowledge you need to take on a career in the police force, corrective services, and the criminal and community justice systems. You will learn about law enforcement and surveillance, violence, gender and crime, restorative and international criminal justice, cultural depictions of crime, and contemporary debates in criminology. Examples of minors include Child and Community Studies, Psychological Studies or Sociology. Ultimately, you will emerge with the specialist skills and knowledge to make a difference in the world and be a force for good.

name: Bachelor of Cyber Security and Behaviour
description: Digital Defender Western's Bachelor of Cyber Security and Behaviour is the only cyber security degree in Australia that analyses both the technical and human side, and places you at the centre of a fast-changing digital world. With a focus on hands on learning led by industry experts, you'll use advanced technology to develop skills in programming and hacking and build your understanding of usable security and privacy by design - two skills that are highly sought after worldwide. You'll be introduced to cyber risk management frameworks and how to think dynamically to respond to cyber threats. Learn the behavioural science behind online fraud and advanced hacking, and use this knowledge to protect data against cyber attacks. We've partnered with leading Australian and global organisations to offer industry based training, your final year will include a half-year placement at the Western Centre for Cybersecurity Aid & Community Engagement working on cyber security problems for local businesses, followed by an industry lead project or placement with a partner organisation.

Graduates work as visual communicators, brand and UX designers across industry. Indicative international tuition is around 34,800 Australian dollars per year. Today's designers don't just create products or spaces-they design digital experiences, emerging technologies and innovative solutions that improve the way people live, work and connect. As industries continue to evolve, organisations are looking for creative thinkers who can combine design, technology and innovation to tackle complex challenges. Western's Bachelor of Design and Technology combines studio-based learning with emerging technologies, digital design and real-world industry experience to prepare you for careers across the creative industries. You'll explore design thinking, user experience, digital technologies, interaction design and creative problem-solving while developing the practical and technical skills needed to thrive in an increasingly digital world. Graduate with a professional portfolio that showcases your creativity, technical capability and ability to develop innovative solutions for real-world challenges.

description: Become a primary school teacher at Western Be a highly sought-after primary-school teacher by gaining your initial teaching degree at Western Sydney University. This degree prepares our graduates to teach Kindergarten to Year 6 (K-6) in government and non-government primary school settings and other educational fields in Australia. The Bachelor of Education (Primary) provides deep engagement in primary education through innovative approaches to teaching and learning combining on-campus and online learning experiences. These superior experiences underpinned by research evidence produce high quality graduates who are active at advancing the status of the teaching profession. To fully prepare you for your school-based professional experience placements, you study foundation subjects such as sociology for educators and educational psychology; teaching content knowledge with emphasis on building capacity in literacy, numeracy and science; and the full suite of primary curriculum subjects and pedagogy subjects. You may choose to study electives such as inclusive education, sustainability or science as part of your studies with a blended learning approach with both online and on campus program delivery. You will also be involved in engaged and work integrated learning, through working with a school from your first year and professional experience in a variety of primary schools..

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours)
description: Engineer the Future From sustainable infrastructure and renewable energy to robotics, advanced manufacturing and smart cities, engineers solve the challenges that shape our world. Western's Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) prepares you to design, build and improve the systems, technologies and infrastructure that support modern society. You'll develop strong technical knowledge alongside practical problem-solving skills and industry experience. The degree allows you to explore different engineering disciplines before choosing a specialisation, giving you the flexibility to discover where your interests and strengths lie. Areas of study include Advanced Manufacturing, Civil, Construction, Electrical, Materials Engineering, Mechanical, Robotics & Mechatronics and Sustainability. You'll apply your knowledge through hands-on projects, industry engagement and professional experience. Before graduation, you'll complete 450 hours of industry-related employment, helping you build practical skills, industry connections and career confidence. Accredited by Engineers Australia, this degree prepares graduates for professional engineering careers recognised both nationally and internationally. Note: At the Sydney City campus, this program is available for full-time study only, and only in the specialisations Civil, Electrical and Mechanical. Sydney City Campus semesters commence in March, July and October. Not all subjects are available on all campuses. Please refer to our handbook for more information.

name: Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) - Civil Engineering
description:
WSU's Civil Engineering (Honours) degree is taught out of the Penrith (Kingswood) campus and is accredited at Professional Engineer level with Engineers Australia, covering the standard civil engineering spine (structures, geotechnical, water, transport) with an emphasis on infrastructure that reflects the region's own construction boom. Western Sydney has been the site of enormous infrastructure investment over the past decade (the new international airport, associated road and rail corridors, new housing release areas), and the program's project-based subjects and industry placements draw directly on that pipeline rather than needing to import case studies from elsewhere.

Students complete mandatory industry work experience as part of the accreditation requirements, and the degree's honours component is built into the standard four-year structure rather than requiring an additional year, with the fourth-year engineering project functioning as the capstone research and design piece.

Graduates commonly move into roles with the major infrastructure contractors and state government agencies working on Sydney's western growth areas, which gives the degree a genuinely strong local employment pipeline relative to some engineering programs based further from where the actual construction is happening.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time
Year 1: Engineering Fundamentals, Mathematics for Engineers, Mechanics, Introduction to Civil Engineering
Year 2: Structural Analysis, Geotechnical Engineering, Fluid Mechanics, Surveying
Year 3: Structural Design, Transport Engineering, Water Engineering, Construction Management
Year 4: Advanced Structural Design, Engineering Project (capstone), Professional Practice, electives
Requirement: mandatory industry work experience placement
Accreditation: Engineers Australia (Professional Engineer level)

description: Bachelor of Lead through health and movement The Bachelor of Health, Physical Education, and Sport brings together our previous Bachelor of Health and Physical Education and Bachelor of Sport into one flexible, future-focused degree. With a strong focus on young people, you'll build contemporary health knowledge and the confidence to lead informed conversations around important and emerging health issues - supporting positive decision-making among young people. You'll also develop movement expertise and practical teaching capabilities, equipping you to design and deliver engaging physical education experiences at school that foster lifelong participation in physical activity. Across the degree, there is a strong emphasis on rethinking sport and physical activity to be more inclusive, creative, and accessible, enabling you to make a meaningful impact across schools, clubs, and communities. You can prepare for a career in Health and Physical Education teaching while also gaining broader knowledge across the sport sector, opening pathways beyond the classroom. name: Bachelor of Laws
description:
Western Sydney University's Bachelor of Laws covers the full Priestley 11 sequence required for admission to legal practice in NSW, taught out of the Parramatta campus where the university's law school sits close to the Parramatta courts precinct, genuinely useful for students who want to sit in on real proceedings as part of their studies rather than relying purely on moot exercises. The school runs a legal clinic where students under supervision provide advice to real clients from the local community, which functions as both a practical skills subject and a piece of access-to-justice work given the significant unmet legal need across Greater Western Sydney.

WSU Law markets itself around social justice and diversity in the profession. A meaningful share of its cohort are the first in their family to study law, and the school has built subjects and support structures (including an Indigenous-focused unit and community legal partnerships) around that reality rather than assuming a cohort of students already embedded in legal or professional family networks.

As with all Australian law degrees, graduates need to complete practical legal training after finishing the academic component before being admitted as a solicitor or barrister.

Duration: 4 years full-time

Practical subjects: Legal Clinic (supervised real-client casework), Dispute Resolution
Electives: Family Law, Immigration Law, Native Title and Indigenous Legal Issues, Employment Law
Post-graduation requirement: Practical Legal Training before admission as a legal practitioner
Final year typically combines electives with clinic or advanced practice subjects

name: Bachelor of Medical Science
description:
WSU's Bachelor of Medical Science lets students choose one of three primary majors: Biomedical Science, Anatomy and Physiology, or Human Nutrition. The flexible elective structure means students can add a second major (80 credit points) or minors like Environmental Health, Infectious Diseases, or Microbiology from the university's broader science and health offerings. It's a three-year science degree rather than a clinical or professional program, aimed at students heading toward postgraduate medicine, allied health, research, or laboratory science careers rather than direct clinical registration.

The Biomedical Science major builds an integrated foundation across biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, physiology and anatomy, while Anatomy and Physiology leans specifically into the structural and functional basis of human health and disease. WSU's science teaching draws on strong ties to Western Sydney's public hospital network for research placements and honours pathways, given the university's location across a region served by several major teaching hospitals.

Students completing the degree with strong results commonly progress into a fourth-year Honours program or graduate-entry medicine, dentistry, or other health professional degrees, with the flexible major/minor structure letting students shape their science background toward whichever pathway they're aiming for.

Duration: 3 years full-time (6 years part-time)
Core subjects: Human Biology, Biochemistry, Cell Biology, Physiology, Research Methods in Science
Major (choose one): Biomedical Science / Anatomy and Physiology / Human Nutrition
Electives: second major (80cp) or minors (40cp each) — Environmental Health, Infectious Diseases, Microbiology available
Final year: advanced major subjects, independent research or laboratory-based project subject
Pathway options after completion: Honours year, graduate-entry medicine/dentistry, allied health postgraduate study

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
WSU's Bachelor of Nursing is a 240-credit-point degree made up of 24 nursing subjects, with a minimum of 800 clinical placement hours (excluding public holidays) required across the three years to meet AHPRA registration requirements. Skills and knowledge are built first in on-campus simulated clinical settings before being consolidated in real placements across hospitals, aged care facilities, general practice, and community health teams. It's a staged model rather than throwing students into full clinical settings from day one.

Given Western Sydney's rapidly growing population and its multiple major public hospitals (Westmead among them being one of the largest hospital precincts in the state), students get placement exposure to a genuinely high-acuity, high-volume health system, and the university's nursing program has consistently ranked well nationally partly on the strength of those clinical partnerships.

An Enrolled Nurse pathway variant exists for students who already hold EN qualifications, letting them complete the degree on a accelerated timeline with credit for prior clinical experience, which is a meaningfully different cohort experience from the standard-entry three-year structure.
curriculum:
Duration: 3 years full-time, 240 credit points, 24 nursing subjects
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy and Physiology, Health Assessment, on-campus simulated clinical practice
Year 2: Adult Health Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pharmacology, Child and Family Health, clinical placement blocks begin
Year 3: Complex Care Nursing, Aged Care, Primary Health Care, Professional Practice Experience, final placement block
Total clinical placement: minimum 800 hours across hospitals, aged care facilities, GP practices, community health teams
Alternate pathway: Enrolled Nurse entry with accelerated/credit-bearing structure

From the beginning of the degree, you'll develop a strong grounding in biomedical sciences-such as anatomy, physiology, and the fundamentals of podiatry-while also building essential communication skills, academic literacy, cultural capability, and an understanding of the Australian health care system and interprofessional practice. As you progress, your studies expand into podiatry specific areas including biomechanics, musculoskeletal podiatry, gait analysis, and pre clinical skills. description: The Bachelor of Psychological and Social Sciences at Western Sydney University is a three-year full-time degree that gives students a thorough scientific understanding of psychology alongside social sciences study. name: Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours)
description:
The Bachelor of Psychological Science (Honours) at WSU is an APAC-accredited four-year sequence that folds the honours research year into the standard degree, meaning students don't need to apply separately or complete an additional bolt-on year to get the accredited honours qualification required to continue toward psychologist registration. The final year centres on an independent research thesis, supervised individually, alongside advanced coursework in psychological assessment, ethics, and professional issues.

WSU's psychology research strength includes work in areas like mental health, addiction, and Indigenous psychology, and honours students often end up attached to active faculty research programs for their thesis rather than working in isolation, which gives some students a pathway into PhD study or research assistant roles straight after graduation.

As with all APAC-accredited honours degrees in Australia, completion is the first of several steps toward registration as a psychologist: graduates still need to complete further supervised practice or postgraduate training (a Master's or the 4+2 internship pathway) before they can register and practise independently.
curriculum:
Duration: 4 years full-time (Honours embedded)
Year 1: Introduction to Psychology, Research Methods 1, Biological Psychology, Social Psychology
Year 2: Cognitive Psychology, Developmental Psychology, Psychological Assessment, Research Methods 2
Year 3: Abnormal Psychology, Personality and Individual Differences, advanced electives, research preparation
Year 4 (Honours): Advanced Research Methods, Professional and Ethical Issues in Psychology, Honours Thesis (independent supervised research)
APAC-accredited; graduates proceed to further supervised practice or postgraduate training for registration

You will develop knowledge and skills to understand and explain human behaviour and experience. You will have the option to include in your study program electives such as Introduction to Digital Mental Health; Behaviour and Environment; Psychology, Crime and Law; and Applied Psychology. The dynamic and flexible learning experience are just some of the reasons why students choose to study Psychology at Western. Upon completion of your first three years within this accredited psychology program you may be eligible to progress into our elite Honours Program. name: Bachelor of Social Science
description: Influence the world you'll live in Western's Bachelor of Social Science allows you to choose your own majors and minors, including Child and Community, Geography and Urban Studies, Heritage and Tourism, Peace & Development Studies, Sociology, Disability Studies, and Criminology & Criminal Justice. You will gain a greater understanding of the social world in three ways: through social theory, social research and the applications of these ideas and knowledge to practice through social engagement. The program caters to individual interests, while also preparing graduates for employment in a complex, culturally diverse and ever-changing social environment. Optional placement subjects provide opportunities to develop valuable work-place skills in research and communication, analysis, data and digital literacy, and community engagement. Emerge with a wide base for understanding issues in the complex, culturally diverse and ever-changing social environment of the 21st century. Create a degree as specialised or as broad as your desired career path. Note: Sydney City start times are March, July and November. Some majors available online. WSU Online start times are February, June and September.
curriculum: You can choose from the following majors: Anthropology Available on Liverpool and Kingswood Campuses. Social Anthropology is the study of humans and the cultures they create. The major in Anthropology within the Bachelor of Social Science offers students the opportunity to examine social patterns and practices across cultures, to discover similarities and differences between cultures, and to understand the processes by which humans organise and create meaning. Areas of focus include the development of anthropology as a discipline; globalisation and culture; power and politics; gender and sexuality; identity and belonging; ethnography and ethnographic methods; indigenous peoples and nation.

name: Bachelor of Teaching/Bachelor of Education (Primary)
description:
WSU's combined Bachelor of Teaching/Bachelor of Education (Primary) is a 320-credit-point program built around embedding professional experience from the very first year rather than saving classroom placements for later in the course. Students are in schools observing and assisting well before they're leading lessons themselves. Before students can undertake Professional Experience subjects, they need Working with Children clearance and Child Protection Awareness training, and the National Literacy and Numeracy Test for Initial Teacher Education students has to be cleared before the final placement subject, both NESA requirements rather than university-specific hurdles.

WSU trains a very large share of NSW's primary teaching workforce, particularly for schools across Greater Western Sydney, and the program's placement network reflects that. A meaningful number of graduates end up placed, and later employed, in the same public school systems across Western Sydney where the university itself draws much of its student body from.

The degree is NESA-accredited and meets the national Australian Professional Standards for Graduate Teachers, qualifying graduates to teach Kindergarten to Year 6 in NSW government and non-government schools.

Duration: 4 years full-time, 320 credit points

Year 2: Curriculum studies (English, Mathematics, Science, HASS), Inclusive Education, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Education, ongoing placements
Year 3: Advanced curriculum and pedagogy subjects, Classroom Management, Assessment and Reporting, Professional Experience block
Year 4: Capstone Professional Experience (extended placement), Professional Practice seminar
Requirements: Working with Children Check, Child Protection Awareness training, NESA Literacy and Numeracy Test (before final placement)
NESA-accredited; meets Australian Professional Standards for Graduate Teachers

name: Bachelor of Youth Work
description: Bachelor of Youth Work at Western The Bachelor of Youth Work is a program that trains professional youth workers, bringing together the best intelligence from across the humanities and social sciences to understand why things are the way they are for young people - and to do something about it. Based on a commitment to work with young people not as 'a problem' but as people who face challenges and barriers, the programme draws on the University's core commitment to social justice and inclusion. Because youth workers typically work with high degrees of autonomy, the course trains students to make their own decisions and take responsibility for them, to take initiative in solving problems and designing new approaches, and to ground their practice firmly in the ethics of their profession. Intensely practical, the program provides skills for working with young people as well as opportunities to engage with young people and communities under the supervision of experienced youth workers.

name: Diploma in Criminal and Community Justice (Exit Only)
description: Criminal and Community Justice at Western The degree draws upon disciplinary areas such as Criminal Justice, Criminology, Psychology, Social Work and Welfare in order to provide a theoretical framework for those who work with offenders. This degree is a specialised degree which targets a range of central themes and issues that are paramount for those who work with victims and also offenders, both in terms of their treatment and management. As well as providing a theoretical framework, the program equips our students with the knowledge and skills to develop and evaluate practice with a view to enhancing work with offenders and victims. The Bachelor of Criminal and Community Justice can be described as an 'applied degree' insofar as the teaching within the program will link theory to practice. It is important to note that this degree does not guarantee direct employment into Corrective Services or related fields. Our academics who teach in the program have had first-hand experience working directly with offenders and victims in a variety of settings including prisons, courts and a community setting. This is reflected in some of the specialised subjects, including Assessment and Treatment of Offenders and Managing Offenders in the Community.

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Western Sydney University's MBA runs out of the Parramatta City campus and is pitched deliberately at working professionals across Greater Western Sydney's public sector, health, education and logistics employers rather than assuming a Sydney CBD finance-and-consulting cohort. Case material and guest teaching draw heavily on the region's own major employers. Western Sydney has become a genuine economic centre in its own right, particularly with the new Western Sydney Airport precinct under construction and the associated business and government investment that's followed it.

The core spine covers strategy, finance, marketing and leadership as any MBA would, but WSU frames its differentiator as a stronger focus on public sector and not-for-profit management alongside standard corporate strategy, reflecting the composition of its actual student cohort more than it does at some private-sector-oriented MBA programs.

Most students complete the degree part-time while working, with evening and block-intensive delivery options, and the capstone is typically an applied strategy project connected to the student's own workplace or a partner organisation rather than a purely theoretical case study exercise.
curriculum:
Duration: 1.5–2 years part-time, or accelerated full-time option
Core subjects: Strategic Management, Financial Management, Marketing Management, Leading People and Organisations, Business Analytics, Public Sector and Not-for-Profit Management
Elective block: Finance, Marketing, Health Management, or Entrepreneurship streams
Capstone: applied strategy project, often based in student's own workplace or partner organisation
Delivery: evening and block-intensive options for part-time cohort
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree plus relevant work experience

name: Master of Information and Communications Technology
description:
Western Sydney University's Master of ICT is aimed squarely at career-changers and international graduates entering the tech workforce through Sydney's western suburbs corridor, an area that's absorbed a lot of the city's newer data centre and logistics-tech investment as space in the inner city has run out. The course structure typically opens with foundation subjects for students without a computing background, then narrows into a specialisation (software development, networking, data analytics or cybersecurity are common options) before a final applied project.

WSU's tech teaching happens across its Parramatta and Kingswood campuses, and the university has been building out partnerships with western Sydney's expanding business park tenants (logistics, health tech, government shared-services) as placement and project partners, which gives the program's industry project component a genuinely regional flavour rather than defaulting to CBD finance-sector case studies the way an inner-Sydney university's ICT masters might.

Graduates commonly move into systems analyst, network administrator, or junior software developer roles, with the degree also functioning as a stepping stone toward permanent residency pathways for many international students given its alignment with the skilled occupation list.

Duration: 1.5–2 years full-time, depending on entry background

Core subjects: Systems Analysis and Design, IT Project Management, Enterprise Architecture
Specialisation (choose one): Software Development, Networking and Security, Data Analytics, Cybersecurity
Capstone: industry-based ICT project or research subject in final term
Electives drawn from cross-faculty computing subjects

name: Master of Teaching (Secondary)
description: Be the teacher they remember At Western, we know the value a great teacher brings to the classroom as well as the challenges you'll face. That's why we've built our Master of Teaching (Secondary) around giving you practical tools to provide inspiration and direction to high-school students. Offering a mix of on-campus theory and school-based placements, this program helps you turn your specialist undergraduate degree into an inspiring career path. The aim is to produce teachers with strong academic knowledge and skills, excellence in professional practice, commitment to equity and social justice, and dedication to personal and professional growth. The dual degree of an undergraduate degree and postgraduate teaching degree gives you enormous flexibility when it comes to your career. You can apply for roles as a secondary school teacher with government and non-government schools in Australia and most other countries. You can also pursue career interests in the field of your undergraduate degree, like education policy, curriculum development and education administration or even generalist positions, since many of the skills from your teaching degree - teamwork and leadership, communication and organisation - are highly valued by employers. Finally, to help you juggle your busy work, career and personal life.

Bachelor of Culinary Management
description:
This degree sits on top of Angliss's core reputation: the institute has trained generations of Melbourne's professional chefs, and its commercial kitchens run as genuine working production and training spaces rather than teaching-only mockups, supplying the institute's own training restaurant and bakery outlets that serve the public. Culinary Management students aren't just cooking in class; they're working alongside vocational chef apprentices and trainees in kitchens that operate under real commercial kitchen conditions and food safety obligations.

The degree is built for students aiming at kitchen leadership and food business management roles rather than a pure culinary arts (hands-on cooking) qualification. It layers business management, food cost control, and menu engineering on top of solid practical culinary skills, positioning graduates for head chef, food and beverage manager, or hospitality business owner pathways rather than line-cook roles. Angliss's placement network into Melbourne's restaurant, hotel, and catering scene (a city with a genuinely dense and competitive food industry) gives students access to kitchens ranging from high-volume hotel operations to smaller chef-driven restaurants.

Because Angliss's culinary teaching culture is built by working chefs as much as academics, expect assessment that includes live food production under time pressure and real cost-control exercises, not only written business case assignments.
curriculum:
Year 1: Culinary Fundamentals and Kitchen Operations, Food Safety and Hygiene, Introduction to Menu Planning, Hospitality Business Fundamentals, kitchen placement (short block)
Year 2: Advanced Culinary Techniques, Food and Beverage Cost Control, Menu Engineering, Kitchen Team Leadership, extended kitchen/restaurant placement
Year 3: Culinary Business Management, Supply Chain and Procurement for Food Service, Sustainable and Ethical Food Practices, Capstone Culinary Business Project, final industry placement
Practical training delivered in William Angliss's working commercial kitchens and training restaurant
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent; prior culinary certificate preferred
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Event Management (Diploma to Degree Pathway)
description:
This is a stacked pathway degree: students complete a diploma-level qualification first (Angliss's diploma in event management is itself a well-regarded vocational credential in the Victorian events industry) before articulating into the bachelor's degree, which means graduates come out with both a completed diploma and a full bachelor's, a structure aimed at students who want a recognised qualification milestone partway through rather than a single long commitment.

Melbourne's genuine events economy, with major sporting events (the Australian Open, Melbourne Cup Carnival, AFL grand final), large conventions, and a dense festival calendar, gives Angliss event management students access to real, large-scale event placements that a lot of smaller event management programs elsewhere in the country simply can't offer. The diploma stage focuses heavily on operational event delivery skills (run sheets, vendor coordination, on-the-day logistics), and the degree stage builds on that with strategic event business management, marketing, and larger-scale project planning.

Because the pathway structure means students transition from a TAFE-style diploma delivery model into more strategic degree-level units partway through, the shift in workload and assessment style between the two stages is genuinely noticeable. Angliss's course advisors flag this directly to students moving between the diploma and degree components rather than treating it as a seamless continuation.
curriculum:
Diploma stage: Event Operations and Logistics, Event Marketing and Promotion, Risk Management for Events, Vendor and Stakeholder Coordination, supervised event placements
Degree stage Year 1 (post-diploma articulation): Strategic Event Management, Event Business Planning, Sponsorship and Partnership Management, Financial Management for Events
Degree stage Year 2: Large-Scale Event Project Management, Sustainable and Ethical Event Practice, Capstone Event Project (often tied to a real Melbourne event), final industry placement
Graduates receive both the diploma and bachelor's qualification through the articulated pathway
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent; first year delivered as Diploma of Event Management
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Resort and Hotel Management
description:
Angliss built this degree specifically around hotel and resort operations rather than the broader tourism-industry framing of some of its sister degrees, and the practical bent shows in the assessment style: students work through actual front office, housekeeping, and food and beverage operational scenarios using the institute's on-campus training facilities, which include a working commercial kitchen, bakery, and bar rather than only lecture-based case studies.

Placement is heavily weighted in this degree, and Angliss's long-standing relationships with major international hotel brands operating in Australia (a legacy of the institute's decades as the primary trainer for Melbourne and Victoria's hospitality workforce) mean students typically get placed into genuine hotel operations roles rather than administrative shadowing. Resort management units draw on case material from both Australian coastal and regional resort operators and international examples, reflecting graduates' genuine spread of career destinations: some go into city hotel management, others into regional or international resort operations.

Because Angliss's teaching culture leans so heavily on people who've worked the industry themselves, students should expect assessment that mirrors real operational pressure (rostering problems, service recovery scenarios, revenue management under real seasonal demand curves) rather than purely theoretical management frameworks.
curriculum:
Year 1: Hotel and Resort Operations, Front Office Management, Food and Beverage Service Operations, Customer Experience Management, industry placement (short block)
Year 2: Rooms Division Management, Resort Facilities and Recreation Management, Financial Management for Hospitality, Human Resource Management, extended industry placement
Year 3: Revenue and Yield Management, Strategic Hotel and Resort Management, Sustainable Resort Operations, Capstone Industry Project, final industry placement
Practical training delivered through William Angliss's on-campus commercial kitchen, bakery, and bar facilities
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Tourism
description:
Angliss's Bachelor of Tourism leans toward destination management, tourism marketing, and sustainable tourism planning rather than the operations-heavy hospitality focus of the institute's hotel and resort degrees. It suits students aiming at roles with tourism boards, destination marketing organisations, tour operators, or the travel sector rather than on-property hotel management.

Victoria's tourism industry (Melbourne's major-events calendar, regional tourism across the Great Ocean Road and wine regions, and Victoria's state tourism agency presence) gives Angliss tourism students placement and project opportunities genuinely grounded in a real, active state tourism economy rather than abstract global tourism theory. The degree includes units on sustainable and responsible tourism, reflecting increasing industry and government focus on managing tourism's environmental and community impact, particularly relevant given Victoria's push on regional and nature-based tourism.

Because Angliss is fundamentally an industry-training institute rather than a research university, the tourism degree's teaching staff mix includes people who've worked in destination marketing organisations and tour operations, and assessment tends toward applied projects, such as actual destination marketing plans and tourism product development pitches, rather than purely theoretical tourism studies essays.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Tourism Systems, Destination Studies, Tourism Marketing Fundamentals, Customer Service in Tourism, industry placement (short block)
Year 2: Sustainable and Responsible Tourism, Tourism Product Development, Digital Marketing for Tourism, Tourism Policy and Planning, extended industry placement
Year 3: Destination Management Strategy, Tourism Business Management, Capstone Tourism Project (often tied to a real Victorian destination or operator), final industry placement
Grounded in Victoria's active tourism economy — Melbourne major events, regional and wine tourism, state tourism agency partnerships
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

name: Bachelor of Tourism and Hospitality Management
description:
This degree runs through the same campus that trains Angliss's chefs and baristas, which means tourism and hospitality management students aren't learning service standards purely from textbooks. The institute's commercial training restaurant, bakery, and bar operate as real, publicly trading venues, and management students do rotations through front-of-house operations there alongside the vocational trainees, giving them direct exposure to how a service business actually runs on a given shift rather than only studying it in case format.

Angliss has decades-deep relationships with Victoria's tourism and hospitality employers, and industry placement is a substantial, credit-bearing part of the degree rather than an optional add-on: students typically complete placements with hotel groups, tourism operators, or event companies across multiple points in the degree, building a genuine employment track record before graduating. The institute's location in Melbourne, a city with a real convention, major-events, and hospitality economy, gives students access to large-scale operations (major hotel chains, the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre precinct, and a dense CBD hospitality strip) that a regional or suburban-based hospitality school couldn't match.

The degree covers both the tourism-destination-management side and hands-on hospitality operations management, and Angliss's teaching staff mix includes industry veterans as much as academics, which shows up in how practically the coursework is pitched: a lot of assessment is scenario and operations-based rather than purely essay-driven.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Tourism and Hospitality Industries, Hospitality Operations, Customer Service Management, Tourism Destination Studies, industry placement (short block)
Year 2: Rooms Division and Hotel Operations Management, Food and Beverage Management, Tourism Marketing, Human Resource Management for Hospitality, extended industry placement
Year 3: Revenue Management, Strategic Management in Tourism and Hospitality, Sustainable Tourism, Capstone Industry Project, final industry placement
Delivered with direct access to William Angliss's own training restaurant, bakery, and bar operations
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.0 (no band below 6.0)

description:
Angliss pitches this at people already working in hotel operations who want to move into senior leadership roles without doing a full master's. It's a shorter, more intensive credential than the Master of International Hotel Leadership, aimed at hospitality professionals who need the qualification bump for a promotion or an international transfer rather than a broad career change into the industry.

The teaching draws directly on Angliss's international hotel industry connections, built over decades of the institute supplying trained staff and managers into major hotel brands across the Asia-Pacific region, and a meaningful share of each cohort is already mid-career, often studying part-time or in block-intensive mode while continuing to work in hotel operations. Coursework covers revenue management, international hotel operations standards, and leadership, with case material drawn from real branded hotel operating models rather than generic hospitality management theory.

Because the cohort skews toward working professionals, delivery is typically more flexible (block or intensive formats) than a standard academic-year degree structure, and students often complete assessments directly tied to problems from their own current workplace rather than hypothetical scenarios.
curriculum:
Core units: International Hotel Operations and Standards, Revenue and Yield Management, Leadership in Hospitality Organisations, Financial Management for Hotels
Applied units: Strategic Human Resource Management for Hotels, International Hospitality Marketing, Change Management in Hotel Operations
Capstone: Applied Leadership Project (typically addressing a real problem from the student's own workplace)
Delivered in block/intensive format to suit working hotel industry professionals
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)

name: Master of International Hospitality Entrepreneurship
description:
William Angliss doesn't run this as an academic hospitality-theory degree. It's built for people who already have some industry background and want to launch or scale their own venture, whether that's a restaurant group, a boutique accommodation brand, or a food and beverage startup. Classes are small and run out of the institute's Melbourne CBD campus, which has its own working training restaurant, bars, and bakery on site, so the teaching staff are frequently people who've actually run venues rather than career academics, and guest lecturers tend to be working hospitality operators and investors from Melbourne's genuinely dense hospitality scene.

The degree centres on a business venture project: students develop an actual business plan or concept across the program, often one they intend to launch for real, and it gets pressure-tested against real costing, supply chain, and staffing constraints rather than treated as a hypothetical case study. Angliss's industry placement network (built over decades of supplying trained chefs, managers, and baristas to Melbourne hospitality) gives students access to venue owners and hospitality investors most standalone business schools can't offer.

Because the cohort is small and heavily practitioner-taught, the pace and flavour of each intake varies with who's enrolled and who's teaching that trimester. This isn't a large standardised MBA-style program, and Angliss is upfront that a lot of the value comes from the industry network and mentorship as much as from the coursework itself.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Hospitality Entrepreneurship Fundamentals, Financial Management for Hospitality Ventures, Market Analysis and Concept Development
Trimester 2: Supply Chain and Operations for Hospitality Businesses, Marketing and Brand Strategy, Venture Feasibility Study
Trimester 3: Leadership and People Management in Hospitality, Legal and Regulatory Frameworks for Hospitality Ventures, Business Venture Project (part 1)
Trimester 4: Investment and Growth Strategy, Business Venture Project (part 2 — capstone business plan or launched concept), industry mentorship placement
Delivered at William Angliss Melbourne campus, drawing on the institute's working training venues and hospitality industry network
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline) typically required (approximate, typical bar, not program-page-verified)
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall (typical bar for postgrad at private AU providers, approximate)

name: Master of International Hotel Leadership
description:
This is Angliss's senior credential for hotel industry professionals, longer and more research-oriented than the Graduate Diploma of International Hotel Leadership, and it's pitched at people aiming for general manager or regional leadership roles within international hotel brands rather than a first entry into hospitality management. The program draws on Angliss's genuinely deep international hotel industry relationships, built over decades of training staff who go on to work across branded hotel groups throughout the Asia-Pacific region.

Coursework moves from operational hotel leadership topics into higher-level strategic and international business content: cross-cultural management, international hotel branding and franchise models, and hospitality investment and asset management, reflecting the reality that senior hotel leaders increasingly need to understand ownership and brand-management structures, not just day-to-day operations. The capstone research or applied project typically has students examining a real strategic problem in international hotel operations, often connected to their own employer or a target market.

Given the practitioner-heavy cohort (most students are already working in hotel management), Angliss runs the degree with flexible block and intensive delivery options, and it's common for students to be sponsored or part-supported by their current employer as part of a leadership development plan, which shapes both the applied focus of assessments and the seniority of typical classroom discussion.
curriculum:
Core units: International Hotel Leadership and Strategy, Cross-Cultural Management in Hospitality, Hotel Branding and Franchise Models, Financial and Asset Management for Hotels
Advanced units: Hospitality Investment and Development, Global Hotel Operations Standards, Strategic Human Resource Leadership
Capstone: Applied Research Project or Strategic Business Project (often connected to the student's own employer or target market)
Delivered in block/intensive format for working international hotel industry professionals
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent, hospitality industry experience preferred
english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0)
